A workflow connects the steps of an analysis. The steps run as one unit, in the same way each time. A usual sequence is: do a check of the data, decide what to do, prepare the data, choose settings, fit, and test against benchmarks. Then select the best model, do the governance checks and write a report. Each step is a node. The arrows between the nodes carry typed results.

A workflow is a document (kind: Workflow, YAML or JSON). It has versions, the same as a spec. The platform validates it before it runs. A workflow can run on a schedule, or each time that a dataset gets a new version.

Status

The contracts are in mapi_spec.workflow, mapi_spec.workflow_nodes, mapi_spec.workflow_templates, mapi_spec.expr, mapi_spec.splitplan and mapi_spec.stattests. The engine and the node implementations are in mapi_workflows. The endpoints are in the HTTP API reference. The workflows guide gives the practical walkthrough and cookbook.

docs.title: The canonical example
docs.text:
Most forecasting projects need the template ts_readiness_arimax:

flowchart LR
  D[(data)] --> ADF[ADF] & KPSS[KPSS] & PP[PP] & ZA[Zivot-Andrews] & S[Seasonal strength]
  ADF & KPSS & PP & ZA --> W{Difference?}
  S --> SS{Seasonal difference?}
  SS -- then --> SD[Seasonal difference]
  W -- then --> DF[Difference]
  SD --> DF
  DF --> ACF[ACF/PACF]
  D --> O[AR/MA order search]
  D --> F[Expanding-window folds]
  O & F --> BT[ARIMAX backtest]
  F --> N[Naive benchmarks]
  BT & N --> C[Compare] --> SEL[Select] --> G[Governance] --> R[Report]
  1. Unit-root tests. ADF and Phillips-Perron ask "does the series wander?". KPSS asks the opposite question. Zivot-Andrews permits one sudden break.
  2. Decisions. One branch differences the series only if the tests show that it wanders. A different branch seasonally differences the series only if the season is strong.
  3. Orders. ACF/PACF shows how many past values are important. An information-criterion grid search selects the AR and MA orders. It gets the differencing decision as an input.
  4. A correct backtest. An expanding-window plan refits ARIMAX on each fold. The plan has an optional gap (for late data) and some horizons (1, 4 and 8 weeks ahead).
  5. Benchmarks. The same folds score naive and seasonal-naive forecasts. The comparison and the selection keep ARIMAX only if it is better than the benchmarks.
  6. Governance and report. The selected model goes through the policy checks. A plain-language report explains each decision.

docs.title: The document
docs.text:
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata: {name: ts-readiness, project: growth}
params:
  alpha: {type: number, default: 0.05}
  season: {type: integer, default: 52}
inputs:
  data: {type: dataset}
nodes:
  - {id: adf, use: test.adf, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, with: {alpha: {$param: alpha}}}
  - {id: kpss, use: test.kpss, inputs: {data: inputs.data}}
  - id: wanders
    use: branch.if
    with: {condition: "not nodes.adf.reject or nodes.kpss.reject"}
  - {id: diff, use: transform.difference, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, when: wanders.then}
  - id: order
    use: search.arma_order
    inputs: {data: inputs.data}
    with: {d: {$expr: "if(nodes.wanders.value, 1, 0)"}, max_p: 3, max_q: 3}
outputs: {orders: order.table}
Field Meaning params Run-time parameters with a type, a default (or required: true), bounds and permitted values. A run can override them. inputs The items that the workflow uses: dataset, model_version, split_plan... with an optional default reference nodes[].use The node implementation (below), optionally with a version range nodes[].inputs Port bindings: inputs.<name> or <node>.<port>. For a single-value port, a list gives alternatives. The port uses the first alternative whose node ran. For a multiple port (compare.models candidates, report items), a list collects all sources that ran. nodes[].with Parameters. The platform checks them against the JSON Schema of the node. A value can be {$param: name} (a workflow parameter) or {$expr: "..."} (calculated from upstream results). nodes[].when <branch>.then or <branch>.else. The node runs only on that arm. nodes[].retries, timeout, cache, on_failure Execution settings for each node. With on_failure: continue, the platform treats a failure as a skip. outputs Named results of the workflow (<node>.<port>). A parent workflow reads these results from a sub-workflow.

If a node is gated by an arm that the workflow did not take, the node is skipped. All nodes that need that node are also skipped, unless their input has an alternative. This is how "difference only if necessary" goes into the next step: data: [diff.data, inputs.data].

docs.title: Typed ports
docs.text: Each edge carries one of these types: dataset, test_result, split_plan, model_version, metrics, table, plot, report or evidence (mapi_spec.workflow_nodes.PortType). If you bind a test_result to a dataset port, you get a validation error before a node runs.

docs.title: Conditions: a safe expression language
docs.text:
Branch conditions and $expr values use a very small language (mapi_spec.expr). A hand-written parser parses it, and the platform evaluates it over JSON. The platform never gives it to the Python eval. It never reads an attribute of a Python object. All inputs have limits: 2000 characters, 400 tokens, nesting depth 32 and 10 000 evaluation steps.

nodes.adf.p_value < params.alpha and not nodes.kpss.reject
nodes.seas.strength >= 0.64 or 'seasonal' in params.flags
[nodes.order.best_p, if(nodes.wanders.value, 1, 0), nodes.order.best_q]
coalesce(nodes.search.best_score, 0) < 500 and exists(nodes.za.details.break_at)
  • Values: numbers, 'text' or "text", true, false, null, and lists [a, b].
  • References: nodes.<id>.<field> (the result of a node), params.<name>, inputs.<name> and run.<field>. Index with [0] or ['5%'].
  • Operators: == != < <= > >=, in, not in, and, or, not, + - * / %, unary - and parentheses. You cannot chain comparisons. The language refuses a < b < c. Write a < b and b < c.
  • Functions: abs, min, max, len, round, any, all, exists, coalesce and if(condition, a, b). The if function evaluates only the selected value.

A condition can also read the results of a Bayesian fit. These examples read the results of model.summary (node s) and evaluate.ppc (node ppc):

coalesce(nodes.s.max_rhat, 99) < 1.01 and nodes.s.min_ess >= 400
nodes.s.params['beta[north]'].hdi_low > 0
nodes.s.focus.excludes_zero and nodes.ppc.ok

A condition cannot make an entry name from a parameter. Thus, to read a value that a workflow parameter names, set the focus parameter of model.summary. The result field focus then gives the mean, sd, HDI bounds, p_positive and excludes_zero of that value. R-hat is null when the fit has only one chain, so use coalesce for it.

The rules are strict. Thus, a condition means exactly what it says:

  • and/or/not need true or false. Numbers are not "truthy".
  • An order comparison compares numbers with numbers and text with text.
  • A missing result is an error, unless it is in exists or coalesce.

Static validation makes sure that each referenced node runs before the branch. It also makes sure that the node produces the field (its result_fields).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
POST /v1/workflows:validate runs mapi_spec.workflow.validate_workflow. Each saved revision also runs it. It reports each problem with a JSON pointer:

Check Example message Unknown implementation /nodes/0/use: node 'adf' uses 'test.nope', which is not in the node catalog Parameters /nodes/0/with/alpha: 2 is greater than or equal to the maximum of 0.5 Missing or unknown ports /nodes/4/inputs: node 'order' needs input 'data' (dataset) Port types /nodes/4/inputs/data: expects dataset but adf.result is test_result References /nodes/2/with/condition: nodes.adf.p_valu: test.adf results have no field 'p_valu' Cycles /nodes: the workflow has a cycle: a -> b -> a Unreachable nodes /nodes/6: node 'x' can never run: it needs both the then and the else arm of 'wanders' Unused results (warning) /nodes/5: the result of 'lone' is not used by any node or output Models /nodes/7/with/model: no catalog model matches 'ts.sarimx@^1'

The platform stores a revision with errors, thus you can correct it. But the revision cannot run (409 WORKFLOW_NOT_RUNNABLE).

docs.title: Runs, caching and automation
docs.text:
A run (POST /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs) is a parent run of kind workflow. The orchestrator goes through the graph in topological order. It does these actions:

  • It evaluates branches and selections itself, on JSON results only (orchestrator nodes). It records a BranchDecision with the values that the condition read.
  • It sends tests, transforms, splits, order searches, backtests, forecasts, summaries, scores, plots, evaluations, comparisons with Diebold-Mariano or stacking, and governance checks to sandboxed workflow_node child runs. Only the sandbox decodes user data.
  • It starts fits as usual fit child runs, and sub-workflows as child workflow runs (see where nodes run).

The identity of each node is a cache key (node_cache_key). The key contains the resolved implementation, its resolved parameters and the content of its inputs. If a node did not change, it uses its earlier result again (status cached). For example, if you change only the final report and run the workflow again, only the report runs again. Each node records its status, attempt, result, outputs, child runs and cost.

Schedules run a workflow on a cron expression in a time zone (@daily, 0 6 * * 1). The shortest interval is 15 minutes. The schedule handles daylight-saving gaps. Triggers run a workflow each time that a dataset gets a new version. A trigger has a binding to one of the inputs of the workflow. Terminal runs send a notification to webhooks.

Some nodes give a plot output: plot.render, model.forecast and evaluate.residuals. The server puts each plot output through the plot sanitizer when it collects the output. An unsafe plot fails its node with PLOT_UNSAFE. report.summary has a plots input and puts each plot into a section of the report. The run view of the web app and the JSON report show these plots.

docs.title: The node catalog
docs.text:
GET /v1/catalog/workflow-nodes lists all implementations. For each implementation, it gives its ports, parameter schema, result fields and an About card.

Kind Implementations Statistical tests test.adf, test.kpss, test.pp, test.zivot_andrews, test.johansen, test.engle_granger, test.ljung_box, test.jarque_bera, test.breusch_pagan, test.white, test.arch_lm, test.granger, test.acf_pacf, test.seasonal_strength, test.vif, test.cusum, test.chow Data processing transform.difference, transform.seasonal_difference, transform.log, transform.box_cox, transform.steps (all catalog preprocessing steps), transform.select Train/test plans split.holdout, split.rolling_origin, split.expanding_window, split.blocked_kfold, split.purged_kfold, split.geo_holdout, split.nested Searches search.arma_order, search.sarima_order, search.var_lag_order, search.coint_rank, search.grid Models model.fit (all catalog models), model.backtest, model.forecast, model.summary, model.score, model.lift_test Evaluation evaluate.metrics, evaluate.baseline, evaluate.residuals, evaluate.ppc Comparison and selection compare.models, compare.diebold_mariano, compare.stacking, select.best, select.threshold Governance governance.policy, governance.check (see Governance) Reports report.summary, report.evidence_pack Plots plot.render (all catalog plot recipes) Control branch.if, subworkflow.run

Each test returns a StatTestResult. It contains these items:

  • The statistic and the p-value
  • The decision at the significance level: reject, and a label such as unit_root or stationary
  • The verdict in plain words
  • For panels, the result for each series

The null hypothesis of KPSS is the "good" case. Thus, its labels are the opposite of the labels of ADF. mapi_spec.stattests.decide keeps them correct.

docs.title: Bayesian models in a workflow
docs.text:
Five nodes work on the draws of a Bayesian fit:

Node What it gives model.summary The mean, sd, HDI, R-hat and bulk ESS of each parameter, max_rhat, min_ess and the number of divergent transitions evaluate.ppc A posterior predictive check: the coverage of the 50% and 90% ranges, the PIT distance from uniform, Bayesian p-values and ok compare.stacking Stacking weights (or pseudo-BMA+ weights) of some fits, from the pointwise elpd_loo that model.fit keeps for data of up to 10 000 points model.score A score mode (predict, simulate, forecast or counterfactual) as a dataset that later nodes can use plot.render Any recipe of the plot catalog as a plot output. source is auto, data, model or predictions.

model.lift_test v0.13 reads the impact group of a causal model version (causal.impact, causal.synthetic_control or causal.did). It gives a LiftTest for the calibration of mmm.bayesian: the total effect over the effect window, with its sd and HDI. The calibration parameter of model.fit takes it, for example {lift_tests: {$expr: "[nodes.lift.lift_test]"}}.

Validation finds the recipe of plot.render in the bundled recipes and in the plot catalog. An unknown recipe gives REF_UNRESOLVED.

docs.title: Tree datasets in a workflow
docs.text:
model.fit and model.backtest have the parameters nodes and join. They have the same meaning as data.nodes and data.join of a spec (Tree datasets). If nodes is not set, the node reads the root node of the tree. model.score, model.forecast and plot.render with source: predictions send a tree input as a full tree. plot.render with source: data keeps the groups of a tree input.

Known gaps

  • A backtest of a tree dataset gives the full tree to each fold. A tree-input model that reads its target from the tree can see the test window. The node shows a warning.
  • search.grid has no nodes parameter.
  • Nodes that fit again on changed flat data, and the ablations of governance checks, do not give a tree to tree-input models.
  • The HTML report does not show plot sections. Only the JSON report and the web run view show them.

docs.title: Train/test plans
docs.text:
A SplitPlan describes many folds at one time (mapi_spec.splitplan). Window plans have these fields: horizons (scored separately), a step between origins, a gap between training and test, n_folds and an anchor. By default, the last test window ends at the last period. The platform calculates folds from the number of periods only. Thus, the web app shows the folds before a node runs.

expanding_window and rolling_origin match the scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit. An expanding fold is exactly the existing as_of split with its gap. geo_holdout holds out full markets, optionally only over their last periods. nested runs an inner plan in each outer training window, for correct tuning.

docs.title: The gallery
docs.text:
Template What it automates ts_readiness_arimax Unit-root tests, differencing that branches decide, order search, an expanding-window backtest against naive benchmarks, selection, governance and a report var_vecm_cointegration A Johansen test. If the series are tied together, a VECM with the selected rank. If not, differences, a lag search and a VAR. Granger tests and a report. mmm_governed Driver collinearity, the mmm-framework marketing mix model with a holdout, the governance policy, a report and an evidence pack geo_lift_mmm A Bayesian synthetic control of a geo-lift test, the lift test that it gives (model.lift_test), mmm.bayesian calibrated with that lift test, the plots of the test and of the calibration, and a report. See the cookbook. forecast_bakeoff A backtest of SARIMAX, ETS, Theta and the smooth-trend model on the same folds, against benchmarks. The platform fits the best model again. sci_spatial_ladder sci.areal_bym2 with iid, ICAR and BYM2 area effects, compared by elpd_loo and stacking weights. The best model, the range of its covariate effect, fits with wider and narrower priors when the effect is clear, a convergence check, a risk map and a report. See the cookbook. sci_network_ladder sci.network_latent_space with covariates, sociality and a latent space, compared by elpd_loo and stacking weights. The pair effects of the best model, a network plot, simulated networks with their statistics and a report. See the cookbook. sci_phylo_signal Four fits of sci.phylo_regression (no tree, Brownian motion, Pagel's lambda, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck), ranked by elpd_loo and weighed by stacking. A branch on the slope of one predictor of the winner: does its range exclude zero? A plot of the tree and a report. See the cookbook. sci_calibrate_then_design A fit of sci.heat_plate with one calibration run held out. A branch on the error on that run and on R-hat. If the calibration is good enough, the predicted temperature field of a new heater layout, as a map. A report. See the cookbook. bayes_workflow_audit Any Bayesian model: a fit with prior draws, a convergence gate, the posterior predictive check, prior sensitivity, the recovery of known values, the plots and a report. See the cookbook. sci_image_model_check An image model: a fit, residual maps, the observed image next to predicted images, the posterior predictive check and a report. See the cookbook.

To make a workflow from a template, use POST /v1/workflows with {"template": "<id>"}. Then edit its parameters or nodes, the same as for all other workflows. The complex workflows tutorial shows the patterns of the science recipes in the workflow editor.

Known gaps of the science recipes

  • governance.check with sensitivity.prior cannot find the prior widths of sci.areal_bym2, so the check is skipped. sci_spatial_ladder fits the model again with these widths in its place.
  • The graph check of sci_network_ladder plots the statistics of the simulated networks only. The plot does not mark the statistics of the observed network.
  • core.prior_predictive cannot draw the prior draws of sci.heat_plate. Some science models (for example sci.cmb_field and sci.phylo_regression) keep no prior draws. bayes_workflow_audit then shows a failed prior plot and continues.
  • Only sci_spatial_ladder ran end to end on a live dev stack and in a browser. The six science and audit recipes run through the server orchestrator in a slow test, with small fits.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
You can start in five ways. All five use the same spec format, steps, models and bundles.

  • Guided mode, no code v0.4

    This way is for analysts. Select a template, upload a spreadsheet and answer some questions. You get a report, a sanity scorecard and what-if sliders. You need a platform that runs: the platform of your team, or make dev below.

    Your first MMM in Guided mode

  • Run the platform v0.2

    Start the API, the job queue, the sandboxed runner and the web app on your laptop with make dev. Then fit and score from the browser, the CLI, Python or HTTP.

    Quickstart: zero to first model in 10 minutes

  • Automate an analysis v0.5

    Start a gallery workflow. Examples are unit-root tests to a backtested, governed ARIMAX, VAR/VECM, a forecast bake-off and a governed MMM. Run it from the browser, with mapi workflows run --watch or with Python.

    Workflow cookbook

  • Fit a science model v0.9

    Do the analysis of a pymc-challenges notebook in the web app. Export the data with python -m mapi_plugin_science.export, upload it, fit a sci.* model and run the recipe of the case. Images, fields, maps and graphs are available.

    pymc-challenges in the web app

  • Use the library in your own process

    Use import mapi_sdk in a notebook, a script or a test suite. You can validate specs, fit, score and write bundles in-process. You can also test your own plugins with the contract kit.

    Your first model in Python

The library and the platform both need Python 3.12 and uv. The platform also needs Node.js 22+ with pnpm for the web app. Docker is optional (Deployment).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
From a clone (today)Into your own project (once published)

We develop the packages together in one uv workspace. Clone the repository. Then sync all the packages and the developer tools:

git clone <repository-url> modeling-api
cd modeling-api
uv sync --all-packages        # or: make install (also installs the web app)
uv run python -c "import mapi_sdk, mapi_spec; print(mapi_sdk.__version__)"

To open a notebook in the same environment, use uv run --with jupyterlab jupyter lab.

Each package is a separate distribution. Install only the packages that you need:

uv add mapi-sdk mapi-steps                 # the runtime and the built-in steps
uv add mapi-pymc                           # PyMC models
uv add mapi-sklearn                        # scikit-learn and xgboost models
uv add "mapi-plots[recipes]"               # plot recipes (Altair, Plotly)
uv add mapi-plugin-mmm mapi-plugin-ts mapi-plugin-tabular   # the built-in models
uv add mapi-plugin-statsmodels "mapi-workflows[runtime]"    # statsmodels models, workflows
uv add mapi-plugin-science                 # science models (sci.*) and the export helper

Not on PyPI yet

We will publish the distributions with the first tagged release. Until then, you install from the workspace, as the first tab shows.

docs.title: What each package does
docs.text:
Package Import What it gives you Heavy dependencies mapi-spec mapi_spec The contracts: DataSchema, ModelSpec, ScoreRequest, capabilities, error codes, static validation and JSON Schemas none (pure Pydantic) mapi-sdk mapi_sdk The runtime: steps, pipelines, coord plans, summaries, bundles, the in-process executor and the contract kit xarray, numpy, zarr mapi-steps mapi_steps 28 built-in preprocessing steps and the split catalog – mapi-pymc mapi_pymc PyMCModel: you write build(). You get engines, diagnostics, new levels and counterfactuals. PyMC mapi-sklearn mapi_sklearn SklearnModel: you write estimator(). You get stacking, safe persistence and uncertainty. scikit-learn, xgboost, skops mapi-plots mapi_plots The JSON-only plot sanitizer and templates. Recipes come with the recipes extra. Altair, Plotly (extra) mapi-plugin-* mapi_plugin_* Built-in models: marketing mix (mapi-plugin-mmm, on mmm-framework), time series, statsmodels time series (mapi-plugin-statsmodels), tabular and science (mapi-plugin-science: 15 sci.* models for images, fields, maps and graphs) as above; mmm-framework, statsmodels, scipy mapi-workflows mapi_workflows The workflow engine, the node implementations and a local runner for notebooks (guide) The engine has none (pure Python, safe for the control plane). The node implementations are the runtime extra (numpy, xarray, scipy, statsmodels and the plot recipes of mapi-plots[recipes]). mapi-conformance mapi_conformance The conformance corpus and its runner all of the above mapi-client mapi_client A typed Python client for the HTTP API (guide) httpx (xarray optional) mapi-cli mapi_cli The mapi command line (guide) typer, rich mapi-server mapi_server The control plane: API, orchestrator and executors (AGPL or commercial) FastAPI, SQLAlchemy; no numpy mapi-runner mapi_runner The sandboxed run harness: supervisor and worker (AGPL or commercial) the SDK, in the worker only mapi-gcs-shim mapi_gcs_shim A local emulator of the Cloud Storage features that the platform uses Starlette

Plugins register themselves through Python entry points (mapi.steps, mapi.models, mapi.plots). Thus mapi_sdk.default_registry() finds all the installed plugins.

    This page shows the platform from start to end. Use make dev and make seed. Then fit, examine and score from the browser. It takes about ten minutes.

docs.title: Runs and executors
docs.text:
fit_spec and score_bundle are plain functions. The platform does the same work as runs. A run is a JSON-only submission that goes to an executor. The executor sends progress as events. It also returns a status, and the status is the source of truth. The in-process executor uses that protocol inside your Python process. Thus notebooks, tests and the local-process and docker executors of the platform use one code path.

sequenceDiagram
    participant You as Notebook / API
    participant Ex as Executor
    participant H as Harness (fit_spec / score_bundle)
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: fit, payload: spec}, nonce)
    Ex->>H: resolve dataset refs, fit
    H-->>Ex: progress events
    Ex-->>You: event stream (state, progress, complete)
    You->>Ex: wait(handle) → SUCCEEDED
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: score, payload: request + bundle})
    Ex->>H: score_bundle
    Ex-->>You: result: xr.DataTree

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
The executor uses a resolver to find the datasets for the dataset:// references in specs and requests. Here, the resolver is a mapping to in-memory datasets. The built-in tabular plugin contains the store-demand data and the spec that this page uses.

import asyncio

from mapi_plugin_tabular.datasets import (
    STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA,
    STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
    store_demand_dataset,
)
from mapi_sdk import InprocExecutor
from mapi_spec.executor import ExecState, RunEventType, RunKind, RunSubmit

history = store_demand_dataset(stores=4, skus=2, weeks=60, seed=1)
recent = history.isel(week=slice(-8, None))  # a window of fitted weeks to re-score

executor = InprocExecutor(
    # dataset refs in specs and requests resolve to in-memory datasets
    resolver={
        "dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest": history,
        "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1": recent,
    },
)
print(executor.caps().isolation.name)  # NONE: your own code, in your own process

docs.title: Submit, wait, score
docs.text:
async def main() -> None:
    fit = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="fit-001",
            kind=RunKind.FIT,
            payload={
                "spec": STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
                "raw_schema": STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-fit-0001",  # resubmitting the same nonce returns the same run
    )
    status = await executor.wait(fit, timeout=300)
    print(status.state)  # succeeded
    for event in executor.events(fit):  # the same event stream a cloud run will produce
        if event.type is RunEventType.PROGRESS:
            print(event.seq, event.payload.get("message"))  # 2 validated the spec and the data

    executor.put_bundle("store-demand@1", executor.result(fit))
    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

succeeded
2 validated the spec and the data
3 split the data
4 fitted quantile model 1
5 persisting the fitted estimators
6 fitted on the training data
7 evaluated the holdout through the score path
8 fitted quantile model 1
9 persisting the fitted estimators
10 fit complete
{'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}

Look at these points:

  • Payloads are JSON. The spec goes as YAML text or as a dict. The raw schema goes as a dict. Data goes only as references. This is exactly what the API will store and what a sandboxed runner will receive.
  • Submissions are idempotent. If you submit again with the same nonce, you get the same handle. Thus an API call that you try again never starts a second fit. adopt(nonce) finds a run after a restart.
  • Status is the source of truth. Events are for progress bars. status() and wait() tell you if a run succeeded. Failures come back as RFC 7807 problems with a stable code.
  • Cancellation is cooperative. The executor checks cancel(handle) between the phases of the pipeline and inside long fits.

docs.title: Isolation levels
docs.text:
Each executor declares how strongly it isolates a run. The platform does not send untrusted code to an executor that is not sufficiently strong.

Executor Isolation For Status InprocExecutor NONE Notebooks, tests and your own trusted code available Local process / Docker PROCESS / GVISOR Local platform, CI v0.2 Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) MICROVM Hosted runs, one new sandbox for each run v0.3

Never run untrusted code in-process

The in-process executor runs plugins in your interpreter, with your permissions. Use it only for code that you wrote or that you trust. Public plugins run only in the sandboxed executors.

For the sandbox design, see the roadmap.

docs.title: Your first model
docs.text:
In this walkthrough, you fit a demand model for three stores and two products. You forecast the next four weeks, and the forecast includes a store that is not open yet. You also see the errors that stop dishonest answers. You run all the code in a notebook, one cell at a time. The complete script is docs/snippets/quickstart.py. The test suite runs it on each change.

flowchart LR
    D["1. Labelled data<br/><code>xr.Dataset</code>"] --> S["2. Schema<br/>dims, roles, policies"]
    S --> P["3. Spec<br/>pipeline + model"]
    P --> V["4. Static check<br/>no data touched"]
    V --> F["5. Fit<br/>evaluate, then refit"]
    F --> SC["6. Score<br/>forecast, new store"]
    SC --> B["7. Bundle<br/>write, read, verify"]

docs.title: 1. Labelled data
docs.text:
Your data is an xr.Dataset. Each variable has named dims, and each dim has coordinates (labels). No later part of the process uses the sequence of stores or products.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

Coming from pandas?

A long DataFrame with one row for each store, sku and week becomes this dataset with df.set_index(["store", "sku", "week"]).to_xarray().

docs.title: 2. Describe it with a schema
docs.text:
A DataSchema tells what each dim is. It also tells what can occur to the dim when you score:

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)
Dim Policy At score time store new_levels (pooled) Stores that the fit did not see are permitted. They get the pooled prediction. sku fixed Only the fitted products. All other products are UNSEEN_LEVELS. week extend New weeks must continue the fitted range. Gaps are not permitted.

If you do not write the schema, mapi_sdk.infer_schema(data, targets=[...]) makes a draft. In the draft, time dims become extend and all other dims become fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the spec
docs.text:
A ModelSpec does these things:

  • It names the dataset.
  • It binds your names to the canonical names of the model.
  • It selects a train/holdout split.
  • It lists the preprocessing steps.
  • It selects the model.
from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")
  • bind maps canonical names onto the names in your dataset. Steps and models use the canonical names. Outputs come back with your names.
  • core.calendar adds week-of-year features. core.log1p models log(1 + units). The pipeline inverts it automatically on the way out.
  • tabular.regressor is a built-in quantile model (xgboost underneath). It stacks its rows from the labelled dims. Store and sku become categorical features.

docs.title: 4. Check it before you fit it
docs.text:
This is the same static check that the API does before it accepts a job. It reads no data, and it takes milliseconds.

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)

The check finds these errors, among others:

  • An incorrect variable name.
  • A split on a dim that does not exist yet.
  • A stateful step before the split.

Each error has a stable code and a JSON pointer, for example /pipeline/1/with/vars/0.

docs.title: 5. Fit
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

With the default fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, fit_spec does these steps:

  1. It fits each stateful step and the model on the first 44 weeks.
  2. It scores the last 8 weeks through the score path, exactly as a forecast. It calculates rmse, mape and coverage_80 in units sold (it undoes the log1p).
  3. It fits again on all 52 weeks, so that a forecast starts from the latest data. It links the evaluation fit in the bundle.

docs.title: 6. Forecast, with a new store
docs.text:
Supply the plan for the next four weeks. Prices and promotions are future_required. The target is not necessary. The fit did not see west.

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

The result is an xr.DataTree. summary holds the statistics that you asked for, along a stat dim, with your dim names. Its attributes tell you how to read it:

Attribute Value here Meaning representation quantiles Quantiles for each cell. You can read them, but you cannot add them. output_space {"y_hat": "raw"} The pipeline inverted the values through each value step, back to the space of the raw data. issues UNSEEN_LEVELS (info) The model scored west with the pooled strategy.

docs.title: 7. The errors that protect you
docs.text:
These requests fail before model code runs. Each failure has a stable code:

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))

MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE - forecasting needs future values of ['promo'] at stage 'raw'
CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED - cannot aggregate 'quantiles' output: Quantiles are marginal per cell; summing quantiles is not a quantile of the sum.
UNSEEN_LEVELS - 1 level(s) of 'sku' were not seen at fit and the dim's policy is 'fixed'

So how do I get a total over stores?

Use a model that has a representation that supports totals. sklearn.tabular_bootstrap returns joint draws, and you can add them for each draw. Bayesian models return posterior draws. See Representations.

docs.title: 8. Save and reload the bundle
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

A bundle holds these items:

  • The spec and the binding.
  • The state and the context tail of each step.
  • The fitted groups and the native artifacts of the model (here, the xgboost model as JSON).
  • A manifest with the size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of each file.

The bundle contains no pickled objects. See Bundles.

docs.title: The whole script
docs.text:
docs/snippets/quickstart.py 
"""Getting started: fit and score a labelled demand model in a notebook.

Every section between ``--8<--`` markers is included verbatim in the docs, and
``conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py`` runs this file top to bottom.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)
assert check.ok, check.errors

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks
assert set(bundle.metrics.values) == {"rmse", "mape", "coverage_80"}
assert bundle.metrics.n_holdout == 48

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'
assert set(summary["store"].values) == {"north", "south", "east", "west"}
assert summary.sizes["week"] == 4

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))
assert code_1 is ErrorCode.MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE
assert code_2 is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED
assert code_3 is ErrorCode.UNSEEN_LEVELS

from mapi_sdk import CoordPlan
from mapi_spec import load_score_request, validate_score_request

# What the API stores next to a model version: JSON only, no arrays, no plugin code.
meta = CoordPlan(load_score_request(FORECAST), bundle.resolved, bundle.fit_coords).metadata()
print(f"{len(meta.model_dump_json()) / 1024:.0f} KiB of metadata")

request = load_score_request(FORECAST + "output: {summary: [hdi_90], draws: 100}\n")
for issue in validate_score_request(request, meta):  # no data, no model: milliseconds
    print(issue.code, issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE /data - forecasting needs future values of ['price', 'promo'] ...
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/draws - draws were requested but the model's
#                                        representation is 'quantiles'
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/summary/0 - summary 'hdi_90' cannot be computed from
#                                            'quantiles' output
assert any(
    i.code is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED for i in validate_score_request(request, meta)
)

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

print(manifest.role, manifest.plugin["id"], manifest.spec_hash[:19])
# production tabular.regressor sha256:...
print(manifest.files["bundle.zarr.zip"])  # size, crc32c, md5 (GCS forms) and sha256
print(manifest.lineage["evaluation_bundle"])  # the train-only fit behind the metrics

tree = again.to_tree()  # the whole bundle as one xr.DataTree
print(sorted(tree.children))
# ['binding', 'fit_coords', 'model', 'native', 'preprocess', 'schema', 'spec']
print(sorted(tree["preprocess"].children))  # ['cal', 'logy']: one node per step
assert {"model", "preprocess", "native", "spec"} <= set(tree.children)

  • To learn why the split occurred at that position, read Pipelines and stages.

docs.title: Quickstart: zero to first model in 10 minutes v0.2
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you start the platform on your own machine and load a demo dataset. Then you fit a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model from the web app. You read its scorecard and plots, and you score an 8-week forecast. You do not need Docker or a cloud account. PostgreSQL is embedded, and the object storage is a local emulator of Google Cloud Storage.

Step What occurs Time on a laptop 1. Install Python and JavaScript dependencies 2–5 min the first time 2. Start the stack Database, object store, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox about 10 s 3. Load the demo Three datasets and a model spec, through the API about 40 s 4. Fit from the browser A sandboxed fit run that you watch live 20–60 s 5. Inspect Scorecard, diagnostics, plots, provenance – 6. Score An 8-week forecast. The run uses the fitted preprocessing again. about 10 s

We did exactly these steps on a new clone when we wrote this page. The time from make dev to a scored forecast was less than three minutes. The screenshots below come from that run.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need these items:

  • macOS or Linux, with about 2 GB of free disk space.
  • uv. If necessary, it installs Python 3.12 for you.
  • Node.js 22 or newer, with pnpm. corepack enable gives the pinned pnpm version.
  • git. If you want to follow the HTTP examples later, you also need jq and curl.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url> modeling-api
cd modeling-api
make install          # uv sync --all-packages, then pnpm install

make install puts all the Python packages of the workspace into .venv. It puts the dependencies of the web app into node_modules. It installs nothing globally.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
make dev

make dev runs all the services in the foreground. Each output line starts with the name of its service. When the stack is ready, make dev shows all 6 services up. Do not stop make dev. To stop all the services, push Ctrl+C.

The first start also puts a sandboxed describe run in the queue. This run exports the catalog of installed models and steps. It finishes in a few seconds.

Service Address Web app http://127.0.0.1:5173 API http://127.0.0.1:8000 (OpenAPI document at /openapi.json) Plot sandbox (a separate origin, on purpose) http://127.0.0.1:5174 GCS shim (signed URLs point here) http://127.0.0.1:4443

Port 8000 (or any other) already taken?

Export the applicable variable before make dev. Also export it in each other shell that you use:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174

make dev, make seed, the CLI, the Python client and the web app all read the same variables. We made this page on exactly these ports. Troubleshooting gives more data.

docs.title: 3. Load the demo
docs.text:
In a second shell, type this command:

make seed

API http://127.0.0.1:8000 is ok (version 0.15.0)
uploading eu_media_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v1 ready
uploading fx_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/fx_daily@v1 ready
uploading holidays_eu (7 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/holidays_eu@v1 ready
spec spec://default/eu-geo-mmm@r1: valid

make seed uses only the public API. For each table, it does these steps:

  1. It asks for a signed upload URL.
  2. It sends the file directly to object storage.
  3. It starts a sandboxed ingest run. The run opens the file and checks it against its schema. Then it stores an immutable, content-addressed version.

Then make seed saves the model spec and validates it.

The data is the E33 example of the conformance corpus. It contains these tables:

  • 30 weeks of daily spend for each market and channel, for NL, DE and UK.
  • Daily revenue for each market (UK in GBP).
  • An FX table.
  • A holiday calendar.

To score, you need the spend that you plan for the next weeks. Upload it with the CLI:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/     # the demo tables, score payloads and spec
uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future

docs.title: 4. Fit from the browser
docs.text:
1. Open http://127.0.0.1:5173.
  2. Go to Build.
  3. Click the eu-geo-mmm row.

When the editor opened, it validated the spec on the server. All dataset:// references, all steps and the model settings resolve. The panel on the right shows what each step of the pipeline does to the data. The split into training and holdout weeks is after the weekly step. The reason is that a week exists only from that stage on.

Push Fit. The run page follows the run through server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the supervisor of the run read its one-time bootstrap object. It deleted the object before model code started.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is usual on a laptop. The local executor cannot run the model code as a separate user. Containers and the cloud executor can.
  • The progress bar and the message come directly from the sampler.

The spec uses very small sampler settings, so the fit takes much less than a minute. On a new machine, the first fit also compiles PyTensor code. When the fit succeeds, the platform does these steps:

  1. It checks each file that the run wrote against the checksums of the storage.
  2. It copies the files to a location that runs cannot get to.
  3. It signs a manifest.

Push Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The scorecard flags R-hat and effective sample size. Two chains of 100 draws are not sufficient to converge. Each warning tells you what to do. The metrics come from the 8 holdout weeks. The model scored these weeks through the same code path as a forecast. This occurred before the model was fitted again on all the data (fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit).

Open Plots → Contribution by channel:

Each plot is a Vega-Lite or Plotly spec that the server sanitized. The plot shows inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> that comes from the own origin of the plot sandbox. Provenance shows the signed manifest, each stored object with its generation, and the lineage.

docs.title: 6. Score a forecast
docs.text:
Push Score (top right). What this model needs lists the inputs that the model reads and the data that it was fitted on. The form shows only the modes that this model supports.

  1. Keep Forecast and 8 periods.
  2. Under Values to score, select Use a dataset.
  3. Type dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1. Alternatively, keep Type values and type the planned spend into the grid. Then you do not need an upload.
  4. Under Advanced, keep the fx side table at the version that the fit used. It covers the forecast weeks.
  5. Push Forecast.

The run did not fit the model again. It used the fitted preprocessing again: currency conversion, weekly resampling, scaling, and the last weeks of spend that each market carries into the adstock. Then it inverted the result back to weekly EUR. The output_space of the result tells you this.

docs.title: Stop, and start again later
docs.text:
make stop             # or Ctrl-C in the make dev shell
make dev              # everything you loaded is still there (.local/)
make clean-local      # delete the local database and objects, start from scratch

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Tour every page of the web app

    Datasets and CSV mapping, revisions and dry-runs, run controls, the data tree and counterfactuals.

  • Do the same from the command line

    mapi datasets upload, mapi fit --remote @, mapi score and --json for scripts.

  • Or from Python

    mapi_client.Client: uploads, live events, model versions and xr.DataTree results.

  • Understand what happened

    The control plane, the run sandbox, storage integrity and the event path.

docs.title: Administration v0.3
docs.text:
From v0.3, one deployment serves many organisations. This guide is for the persons who manage the deployment. It tells who can do what, and how the platform limits compute and charges for it. It also tells what to do when a problem occurs. For the concepts, see Tenancy and authentication and Quotas and cost. For sign-in, see Authentication.

There are three administrative jobs, and the platform keeps them separate:

Who Holds Works in Does Platform operator A verified e-mail in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in Admin console, mapi admin …, /v1/admin/* Creates and suspends tenants. Sets trust tiers and quotas. Sets kill switches. Monitors executors. Reads all audit logs. Never reads tenant content (datasets, specs, models, plots). Tenant admin The admin role, tenant-wide Members, Usage (Organisation), /v1/tenants/{tenant}/… Creates projects. Adds and removes persons. Reads the bill and the audit log of the tenant. Project admin The admin role in one project Members, Tokens, Usage Manages the members, endpoints, plugins and the tokens of all persons in that project.

All examples on this page come from one walkthrough, docs/snippets/admin_tour.sh. The test suite runs it against a development stack (make dev). The walkthrough signs in two times through the development identity provider. It signs in as admin@dev.local (a platform operator). It also signs in as analyst@dev.local, who becomes the admin of the new tenant.

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
export MAPI_URL=$API
dev_login() {  # dev profile only: an ID token for one seeded account, valid for an hour
  python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))' "$API" "$1"
}
OPERATOR=$(dev_login admin@dev.local)          # a platform operator
TENANT_ADMIN=$(dev_login analyst@dev.local)    # becomes the new tenant's admin below
MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR mapi whoami

On a real deployment, each person runs mapi login instead (see Authentication). Operator commands always need a sign-in. An API token never has operator powers, also when its owner is an operator.

docs.title: Tenants
docs.text:
A tenant is an organisation. It is the boundary for bills, isolation and quotas. PostgreSQL row-level security keeps the rows of each tenant separate. Each storage key starts with t/{tenant}/. Only operators create tenants:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin tenants create "$TENANT" --name "Acme Retail" --tier verified \
    --residency eu --admin-email analyst@dev.local --yes
mapi admin tenants ls
Field Values Effect id A lowercase slug (acme) Part of each reference (dataset://growth/eu_media_daily is in a project of a tenant) and of each storage key. You cannot change it. Trust tier internal, verified, public, self-hosted-trusted Where the runs of the tenant can execute, and its default quotas (below) Status active, suspended, deleting suspended: persons can read and download. They cannot create, change or run anything. deleting: there is no access. Data residency eu, us, asia or one region (europe-west1) The platform puts runs only on executors in a region that matches. A change applies only to new runs. Admin e-mail Any address The platform invites this person as tenant admin. The person claims the invitation at the first sign-in with that verified e-mail.

The Admin console lists each tenant with its tier, status and residency. Only operators can use it. Other persons see an explanation. New tenant and Edit do the same as the commands above. To suspend or delete a tenant, you must give a reason and type the id of the tenant.

To stop an organisation in a reversible way, suspend it. Its persons keep read access to their work. The platform refuses each change, upload and run with 403 FORBIDDEN. Operators can still do actions on the tenant.

mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status suspended --reason "contract ended" --yes
mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status active --yes

docs.title: Trust tiers
docs.text:
The tier controls where the code of a tenant can run. The dispatcher enforces this in code. Tenant configuration never controls it. The dispatcher never submits a run to an executor that does not have the isolation that the tier needs. It fails the run with INFRA_ERROR and a detail that tells what is necessary. An example is verified tenants require an executor with isolation >= gvisor and enforced egress/DNS. The tier also sets the default quotas of the tenant, until an operator overrides them.

Tier Executor must provide vCPU-s / day vCPU-s / month Concurrent runs Fan-out tasks Largest class Storage Egress / month Requests / min internal isolation ≥ process — — 100 1,000 — — — 6,000 self-hosted-trusted isolation ≥ process — — — — — — — — verified isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 86,400 1,000,000 20 256 L 100 GiB 100 GiB 600 public isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 3,600 36,000 2 16 S 2 GiB 5 GiB 60

Platform-wide (global) defaults: concurrent_runs = 700. A dash means no limit at that level.

Which executors can take verified and public tenants today

Shared tiers need an executor with gVisor or microVM isolation and enforced egress and DNS. In v0.3, these executors can do this:

  • cloudrun-jobs, when MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED=true. The default is false. The reason is that nobody has verified the DNS response policy against a real Cloud Run Jobs execution yet. This is the first item of the M0 checklist. Until then, verified and public runs fail at dispatch. They do not run on a weaker executor.
  • docker-gvisor, only with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=none. This setting needs an HTTPS bootstrap URL. Thus it is not available with the local GCS shim.

internal and self-hosted-trusted tenants run on all executors, also on local-process. (local-process does not start under MAPI_PROFILE=multi-tenant.)

docs.title: Projects and members
docs.text:
A project is a workspace inside a tenant. It is the unit of access control. Tenant admins create projects and control who works in them. There is no CLI command for members yet. Thus the walkthrough uses the HTTP API:

as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects" \
    -d '{"id": "growth", "name": "Growth marketing"}' | jq -c '{tenant_id, id, name}'
as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    -d '{"email": "viewer@dev.local", "role": "runner"}' | jq -c '{project_id, email, role}'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t(tenant-wide)"'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t\(.project_id // "(tenant-wide)")"'

A membership grants one role. The role applies to one project, or tenant-wide (to the tenant and all its projects). In a project, the effective role of a person is the higher of the two. The platform reads membership at each request. Thus, when you remove a person from a project, their sessions and their tokens in that project stop immediately.

Members shows the members of the project. With Organisation, it shows the tenant-wide grants. Admins can change a role in the list or remove a member. They can also use Add member with an e-mail address. If nobody has signed in with that address, the platform makes an invitation. The person claims it at the first sign-in. A grant with the mark organisation comes from a tenant-wide membership. You change it in that membership.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
There are four roles. Each role includes the role before it. Permission to run is above permission to edit on purpose. The reason is that compute costs money. Thus you can let a person edit a spec, but not start a 200-task sweep.

Role Adds viewer Read all items in the project. Validate specs. Mint tokens for themselves. editor Create and change datasets, specs and saved plots. runner Spend compute: submit, cancel and retry runs, score models and endpoints, and render plots. admin Manage members, endpoints, plugins and the tokens of other persons. Delete items.

Since v0.5, the workflow and governance rules use the same sequence of roles. Editors write workflows. Runners run workflows and submit models for validation. Project admins edit policies, and tenant admins edit the tenant-wide policies. Admins also deprecate validated versions.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A capability is a grant in addition to a role, for each project membership. At this time, the only capability is reviewer. A reviewer is the second person who approves model validations when a governance policy asks for it (Validate models with governance policies). Admins grant it in the Reviewer column of Members, or with capabilities on the membership. Project admins have it implicitly. Viewers cannot have it. Nobody can approve their own submission or approve through an API token.

Capability Needed for What it allows reviewer model approve Approve or reject model validations that wait for a second person (POST /v1/validations/{id}/approvals), never the member's own submissions (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and never through an API token. Granted per project membership (capabilities on the membership, or the Reviewer column of Members); viewers cannot hold it.

This is the complete matrix. It comes from mapi_spec.tenancy.PERMISSIONS, the table that each component checks. tenant-wide means that only a tenant-wide grant counts. The platform refuses a pair that is not in the list to all persons:

Resource Action viewer editor runner admin Operator tenant read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ update ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ delete ✓ manage (tier, status, residency, identity verification) ✓ tenant_member read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ tenant-wide delete ✓ tenant-wide project read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ delete ✓ tenant-wide member read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ token read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ delete (own tokens; manage covers everyone's) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ manage (list and revoke other members' tokens) ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ run read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ delete ✓ validate (submit, resubmit or cancel a governance validation) ✓ ✓ approve (needs the reviewer capability; never the submitter, never a token) ✓ with reviewer ✓ with reviewer ✓ update (deprecate a validated version) ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ manage (override a promotion gate;
