The Permissions reference has the same matrix. It shows the token scopes and the permissions of the operators next to it.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs use API tokens. Examples are the Python client, the CLI in CI and BI exports. A person mints a token in one project. The token is bound to that project. It acts as that person, but its scopes limit what it can do. All persons with a role can mint tokens for themselves. Project admins can list and revoke the tokens of all persons.

export MAPI_TOKEN=$TENANT_ADMIN
mapi use "$TENANT/growth"
mapi tokens create nightly-report -s models:read --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 60 \
    --budget 3600 --budget-period day > nightly-report.token   # the secret, once
mapi tokens ls

New token asks for these items:

  • A name.
  • The scopes.
  • Optional endpoint aliases.
  • An expiry. The default is 90 days. The maximum is 365 days.
  • A limit of requests for each minute.
  • A vCPU-second budget for each day or month.

The form also shows your role. Your role is the maximum that your tokens can do.

The platform shows the secret one time only. The server stores only an HMAC of it. Thus, if you lose a token, you revoke and replace it. You cannot get it back. A revocation has an effect on the next request.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Scopes can only make a token more limited. A token can never do more than the role of its owner. The role and the scope must both permit an action. admin covers all that the role of the owner permits. This table comes from mapi_spec.tokens.scope_allows:

Resource Action models:read runs:create score:* plugins:publish datasets:write endpoints:promote webhooks:manage workflows:write workflows:run models:validate policies:manage runs:write project read ✓ ✓ ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ ✓ run read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ update ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ ✓ validate ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ plot read ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ webhook read ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ plugin read ✓ create ✓ delete ✓ usage read ✓ ✓ ✓ workflow read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ ✓ run ✓ cancel ✓ policy read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓

score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:geo-mmm-prod). score:* covers all endpoints of the project. A token can never do tenant-level actions (members, the bill, the audit log) or operator actions.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text:
The platform limits compute in vCPU-seconds. It checks three levels, in this sequence:

  1. The limits of the token.
  2. The policy of the tenant, or the defaults of its tier (above).
  3. The platform-wide limits that protect the cloud project.

The first limit that a request would exceed answers 429 with QUOTA_EXCEEDED or RATE_LIMITED. The answer has a detail that names the level and the limit. It also has Retry-After with the time when the limit resets. Quotas and cost explains each limit. Operators override the defaults of a tenant:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin quotas set tenant "$TENANT" --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 \
    --concurrent-runs 40 --max-fanout-tasks 256 --storage 200GiB \
    --note "private beta customer" --yes
mapi admin quotas ls

set replaces the policy. It removes the limits that you do not give. For those limits, the tier default applies again. mapi admin quotas rm tenant acme removes the override.

docs.title: Cost and usage
docs.text:
When you submit a run, the platform makes an estimate of its cost. It checks the estimate against the quotas. When each attempt ends, the platform meters the run. It uses the vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds of the resource class of the run, at the versioned price table of the deployment. It writes the result to an append-only cost ledger. Amounts are exact integer micros of a currency. Each amount names the price table that it used. The page of a run and mapi runs get show its cost. Usage pages add the costs.

mapi usage --group-by resource_class             # the selected project, this UTC month
mapi usage --tenant "$TENANT" --period day       # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)

Usage shows the cost, compute, runs and memory of a project for a UTC day or month. With Organisation, it shows these values for the full tenant. It also shows these items:

  • A daily chart.
  • How near each quota is. It gives warnings at 70 % and 90 %.
  • The totals for each token and for each resource class.

All persons in a project can see its usage. The tenant-wide view needs a tenant-wide admin. The amounts are an estimate of compute cost at list prices. They are not an invoice.

docs.title: Kill switches
docs.text:
Two platform-wide switches stop compute quickly. The platform audits both, and both need a reason:

Switch Effect Uploaded code (untrusted_execution_enabled) Off: the platform does not accept or lease runs of plugin code that a tenant uploaded. Built-in models continue to work. Global spend cap When the spend of the platform in the current UTC day or month gets to the cap, no new compute starts. Only internal tenants can still start compute. 
mapi admin kill-switches set --spend-cap 500 --spend-cap-period month \
    --reason "private beta budget" --yes
mapi admin kill-switches get

The first step of the sandbox-escape runbook (ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md) is to turn off uploaded code. At 70 % of the cap, spend opens a ticket. At 90 %, it pages a person (Observability).

docs.title: Executors
docs.text:
Executors in the admin console (and mapi admin executors ls) show these data for each execution backend:

  • Health and isolation.
  • Resource classes.
  • Work that runs and work in the queue.
  • Failures in the last hour.
  • The jobs.run rate against the limit.
  • If it passed the executor conformance suite.

trusted tenants only marks an executor that never gets runs of verified and public tenants.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
The platform adds security-relevant actions to an audit log. These actions are:

  • Sign-ins, and sign-ins that failed.
  • Changes to tenants, projects and memberships.
  • Token creation, revocation and failed use.
  • Changes to quotas and kill switches, and quota denials.
  • Run creation and cancellation.
  • Integrity failures.
  • Artifact links and dataset downloads.
  • Refused run events.

Each entry records who did the action, and if that person was an operator. It records what the action was, on which resource, the result and a problem code. The platform keeps IP addresses and user agents only as keyed hashes. You can correlate entries, but you cannot get the original values back.

mapi admin audit --tenant "$TENANT" -n 10        # operators: any tenant
# tenant admins: their own tenant's log
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/audit?limit=5" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.ts)  \(.action)  \(.resource_kind):\(.resource_id)  \(.outcome)"'

Tenant admins read the log of their own tenant (GET /v1/tenants/{tenant}/audit). Operators read the logs of all tenants in the Audit log tab or with mapi admin audit. They can filter by tenant, project, actor, action, result and time.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Authentication: browser sign-in, the development IdP, Identity Platform, API tokens and the CLI.
  • Permissions: the generated matrices.
  • CLI reference: all mapi admin and mapi tokens options.
  • HTTP API: multi-tenant API: the endpoints.
  • Observability: the metrics, alerts and runbooks for the kill switches and quotas.

docs.title: Authentication v0.3
docs.text:
A v0.3 deployment answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to all callers that it does not know. There are three ways in, one for each type of caller:

Caller Signs in with Sends Reference A person in a browser The identity provider of the organisation (OpenID Connect) An HttpOnly session cookie. The app never sees a token. Browser sign-in A person in a terminal mapi login: the same provider, from the command line The ID token of the provider as Authorization: Bearer The command line A program Nothing. A person mints an API token for it. Authorization: Bearer mapi_… API tokens

In all three ways, the caller is a user (usr_…) with roles in projects. The platform checks each request against those roles at that time (Administration). This page is for the persons who sign in and who set up sign-in. For the protocol details (cookies, CSRF, PKCE, JWKS, the database roles), see Authentication and tenant isolation.

docs.title: Browser sign-in
docs.text:
If you open the web app without a session, it shows Sign in to your workspace. Continue to sign in goes to /auth/login on the API. The API sends the browser to the identity provider. After the sign-in at the provider, the browser comes back to the page where it started.

The API does all the OpenID Connect work. This work is the authorization code with PKCE, a nonce, and the verification of the ID token against the keys of the provider. The API keeps the tokens. The browser holds only two cookies: a __Host- session cookie that scripts cannot read, and a CSRF token. A session ends after 2 hours without activity or after 12 hours in total. It also ends when you click Sign out.

After you sign in, the project switcher at the top left lists each tenant and project where you have a role. It shows that role and the trust tier of the tenant. All that the app shows and does applies to the selected project. The app sends the project as X-Mapi-Project on each request. The avatar menu shows who you are. A shield marks a platform operator.

The first sign-in of a person creates their user from the (issuer, subject) of the provider. If the provider tells that the e-mail is verified, the platform also claims all invitations to that address. Invitations come from Add member (a tenant admin) or --admin-email (an operator). A person with no membership yet sees You are not in a project yet.

docs.title: The development IdP
docs.text:
make dev (and Docker Compose) run the servers in the dev profile. This profile mounts a small OpenID provider inside the API at /dev/idp. Then sign-in works offline, through exactly the same code path as a real provider. It uses RS256-signed ID tokens, PKCE and single-use codes.

There are no passwords. All persons who can get to a dev API can sign in as any listed account. The accounts come from MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS:

Account Gets at start-up admin@dev.local Admin of the default tenant and a platform operator analyst@dev.local runner in default/default viewer@dev.local (and all other addresses) viewer in default/default

Scripts sign in without a browser with mapi_client.oidc.dev_idp_login(api_url, email). This function does the same flow and returns an ID token that is valid for an hour. make seed, the end-to-end tests and the walkthroughs on this page use it. A server in any other profile answers 404. Thus you cannot use the function against production. The walkthrough below is docs/snippets/auth_tour.sh. The test suite runs it against make dev:

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'anonymous: %{http_code}\n' "$API/v1/me"      # 401: sign in first
# dev profile only: what `mapi login` gets from a real identity provider, without a browser
ID_TOKEN=$(python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], "analyst@dev.local"))' "$API")
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" \
  | jq -c '{email: .principal.email, auth, operator,
            projects: [.tenants[].projects[] | "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id) \(.role)"]}'

anonymous: 401
{"email":"analyst@dev.local","auth":"session","operator":false,"projects":["acme/growth admin","acme/retail admin","default/default runner"]}

MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant make dev turns off sign-in fully. This is the v0.2 behaviour: each request acts as the local administrator of default.

docs.title: Set up a real identity provider
docs.text: The API can sign in persons with any OpenID Connect provider that has the authorization-code flow. The provider needs an issuer whose /.well-known/openid-configuration lists an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint and a JWKS.

docs.title: Google accounts
docs.text:
Google accounts are the default of the Google Cloud deployment. They are the simplest selection for an organisation on Google Workspace.

  1. In the Google Cloud console (APIs & Services → Credentials), create an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Set the authorized redirect URI to https://<your app domain>/auth/callback.
  2. Give the id to Terraform (oidc_client_id in terraform.tfvars). Give the secret as the ephemeral variable TF_VAR_oidc_client_secret, with oidc_client_secret_version = 1 (step 4 of the deployment).
  3. If you do not use Terraform, set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET on the API.
  4. Put the e-mails of the operators in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS.
  5. Create the tenant of each organisation with an --admin-email (Administration).

MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS='{"hd": "acme.com"}' selects a Workspace domain in advance in the account chooser of Google. It is only a hint. Memberships control who can do what. The e-mail domain never controls it.

docs.title: Identity Platform
docs.text:
Terraform also enables Identity Platform in the control project (infra/terraform/modules/control/identity.tf). It registers the domain of the app as an authorized domain. It turns off anonymous sign-in and, by default, e-mail/password sign-in. You add SAML and OIDC providers for enterprise single sign-on in Identity Platform. Add them in the console, or with google_identity_platform_*_idp_config resources outside the module. Keep these resources outside the module, because their secrets must not be in its state.

Known gap in v0.3

The sign-in of the API cannot use the tokens of Identity Platform yet. You get those tokens (issuer https://securetoken.google.com/<project>) with the client SDK of Identity Platform. That issuer has no authorization-code endpoint for the API to redirect to. Until that adapter exists, point MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER at Google (above). As an alternative, point it directly at the own OpenID provider of the organisation (below). Until then, the Identity Platform configuration that Terraform creates causes no problems.

docs.title: Other providers
docs.text:
Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0 and all other standard providers work in the same way:

  1. Register a web client with the redirect URI https://<your app domain>/auth/callback.
  2. Set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER to its issuer.
  3. If its discovery document is not under the issuer, set MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL.
  4. Set MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.

ID tokens must have a signature with an asymmetric algorithm (MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS, default RS256,ES256).

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
mapi login signs in with the same provider, from the terminal:

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • With a browser, it opens the page of the provider. It listens one time on 127.0.0.1 for the redirect (authorization code with PKCE).
  • --device shows a short code. Type the code on a different device. This works with providers that support the device flow.
  • --with-token reads an API token from standard input and stores it instead (CI).

The CLI keeps the sign-in in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600). It sends the ID token of the provider as Authorization: Bearer. The API accepts such a token only when its audience is one of MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS (default mapi-cli). Register the CLI with your provider as a public installed app client. Use a loopback redirect, PKCE and the openid email scopes. The installed-app clients of Google need a client secret. The CLI reads it from MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and never shows it.

To sign in against the development IdP, use this command:

mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost \
           --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp

Then select the project where commands act. Use mapi use <tenant>/<project>, --project or MAPI_PROJECT. mapi whoami shows who you are, how you signed in and your projects. See The command line.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs never sign in. A person mints a token for them in one project, with only the scopes that the program needs. The token then acts as that person, but only in that project. Its scopes limit what it can do. To mint a token, use one of these methods:

  • In the web app, use Tokens → New token (Administration).
  • From the CLI, use mapi tokens create.
  • Over HTTP, use this request:
CREATED=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" \
  -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "auth-guide", "scopes": ["models:read"], "expires_in_days": 1}')
TOKEN=$(jq -r .secret <<<"$CREATED")             # shown once: store it now
TOKEN_ID=$(jq -r .token.id <<<"$CREATED")
jq -c '.token | {id, display, scopes, project: "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id)", expires_at}' \
  <<<"$CREATED"

{"id":"tok_01m50mxfqh4k95ed2dv2jc005v","display":"mapi_hhb9gjzf_…","scopes":["models:read"],"project":"default/default","expires_at":"2026-10-16T20:44:02.161164Z"}

The secret (mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>) is in the response one time only. The server keeps only an HMAC of it. Lists show the prefix (mapi_hhb9gjzf_…). Clients and secret scanners use the built-in checksum to reject an incorrect or invented token. They do not have to ask the server.

A program sends the token as a bearer. The token is bound to its project, so it does not need an X-Mapi-Project header:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{auth, operator}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/runs?limit=2" \
  | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.id) \(.kind) \(.state)"'   # bound to its project: no header needed

The Python client accepts the token as Client(token=…) or MAPI_TOKEN. The CLI accepts it as --token, MAPI_TOKEN or mapi login --with-token (Python client). Both refuse to send a token over plain HTTP to an address that is not a loopback address.

docs.title: What a token cannot do
docs.text:
Scopes can only make a token more limited. A models:read token cannot start a run, also when its owner is a runner. A token cannot act in a different project. No token has operator powers:

# models:read cannot spend compute, even though its owner is a runner
curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"kind": "fit", "spec": "spec://default/eu-geo-mmm"}' \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
# a token never acts outside its project, or as an operator
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth' "$API/v1/runs" \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/admin/tenants" | jq -c '{status, code}'

{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}

Tokens expire. The default is 90 days, and the maximum is 365 days. If you revoke a token, or remove its owner from the project, the token stops at the next request:

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'revoke: %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/v1/tokens/$TOKEN_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{status, code}'   # at once

revoke: 204
{"status":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}

The platform writes failed uses of a known token to the audit log as token.auth_failed. Examples are an incorrect secret, or an expired or revoked token. No error ever shows the token.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: Browser session mapi login API token Identity The person The person The person who minted it Projects Each project with a role (select one for each request) Same Only the project where it was minted Permissions The role The role The role and the scopes Operator powers Yes, for operators Yes, for operators Never Needs CSRF token Yes, for changes No No Ends 2 h without activity, 12 h total, sign-out mapi logout. If the provider gave a refresh token, the CLI uses it to renew the ID token. If not, use mapi login again. Expiry or revocation

docs.text:

  • Authentication and tenant isolation: the view of the operator, with cookies, CSRF, row-level security and Pub/Sub push authentication.
  • Tenancy and authentication: the concepts and the request-authorization pipeline.

docs.title: Measure the effect of a change v0.13
docs.text:
This guide tells you how to measure the effect of a campaign, a launch or a price change. It has three procedures:

  1. Measure the effect of a change on one series (causal.impact).
  2. Run a geo-lift test: a campaign in some markets only (causal.synthetic_control).
  3. Feed the result of the geo-lift test to the marketing mix model (mmm.bayesian).

Causal models gives the settings, the bundle groups and the math of each model.

docs.title: Select the model
docs.text:
Your data Model Guided template One series. The change touched all of it from one date. causal.impact campaign_impact - Effect of a campaign The same number for many markets. The campaign ran in some markets only. causal.synthetic_control geo_lift - Geo-lift test The same number for many units. Some units got the change, at the same time or at different times. Some units never got it. causal.did none (use the spec editor)

All three models compare the actual values with a prediction of the values without the change. The prediction is only as good as the information that the model has:

  • causal.impact uses the history of the series and the control series. A control series must not change because of the change.
  • causal.synthetic_control uses the markets without the campaign.
  • causal.did uses the units that never got the change.

Look at the causal.pre_fit chart before you use an effect. Before the change, the actual values must be in the band of the prediction.

docs.title: Measure the effect of a change on one series
docs.text:
1. Upload a dataset with a date column, the result (for example weekly sales) and optional control columns. The data must start a minimum of 3 periods before the change. Two years before the change is better, because the model then learns the yearly pattern.
  2. In Guided mode, select Effect of a campaign.
  3. Select the result column and the date column.
  4. Select the control columns. Use series that the change did not affect, for example the sales in other countries or searches for the category. You can select no column.
  5. Type the start date of the change as YYYY-MM-DD.
  6. If the change stopped, type the end date. If it did not stop, leave the field empty.
  7. Fit the model.

The report shows these items:

  • causal.impact: the actual values, the values without the change, the effect in each period and the cumulative effect. The caption gives the total effect with its 90% interval, the relative effect and the probability that the effect is more than zero.
  • causal.pre_fit: the fit before the change, with its error.
  • core.convergence: the convergence of the sampler.

The same model as a spec:

data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest
  bind: {dims: {time: week}, vars: {y: sales}}
model:
  use: causal.impact@^1
  settings:
    intervention_start: "2024-03-04"
    intervention_end: "2024-04-28"
    controls: [sales_de, category_searches]
    seasonality: [{period: 52.18, harmonics: 3}]
  fit: {mode: train_only, tune: 500, draws: 500, chains: 4, seed: 20261020}
outputs:
  plots: [causal.impact, causal.pre_fit, core.convergence]

Use train_only

The effect is the result of the fit. A holdout removes the periods that you want to measure. Thus the causal templates fit once on all periods.

docs.title: Run a geo-lift test
docs.text:
A geo-lift test changes the spend of one channel in some markets (the test markets) for some weeks. The other markets stay as they were. causal.synthetic_control makes a weighted mix of the other markets that follows each test market before the test. During the test, the mix gives the value without the campaign.

  1. Upload a dataset with a date column, a market column and the result. Include a minimum of 10 weeks before the test, and all weeks of the test.
  2. In Guided mode, select Geo-lift test.
  3. Select the result column, the date column and the market column.
  4. Type the names of the test markets as they are in the market column. Separate the names with commas, for example Leeds, Bristol.
  5. Type the start date and the end date of the test as YYYY-MM-DD.
  6. Fit the model.

The report shows causal.impact (summed over the test markets), causal.donor_weights (the weight of each market in the mix) and causal.pre_fit. If one market has almost all of the weight, the result depends on that market only.

Do not use a test market that is larger than all other markets with the simplex weights

A positive mix of smaller markets cannot follow it. The pre-period chart then shows a bad fit. Use normalize: mean (the default) and intercept: true, or select other test markets.

docs.title: Feed the result to the marketing mix model
docs.text: The total effect of a geo-lift test is a lift test for mmm.bayesian. A lift test tells the model: "this extra spend on this channel in these weeks added this quantity of the KPI". The model then agrees with the test (see Guided modelling).

docs.title: From the Guided report
docs.text:
1. Open the report of the geo_lift fit.
  2. In the Lift test for your marketing mix card, type the channel of the test.
  3. Type the spend change in the test. Type a negative number for a holdout (less spend).
  4. Copy the YAML entry.
  5. Paste the entry into calibration.lift_tests of the spec of your marketing mix model.
  6. Fit the marketing mix model again.

The card does not change the spec of the marketing mix model for you.

docs.title: With the workflow template geo_lift_mmm
docs.text:
The workflow template geo_lift_mmm does all steps in one run:

  1. geolift: model.fit of causal.synthetic_control on the data of the experiment.
  2. lift: model.lift_test makes the lift test from the impact group. kpi_delta is the mean of the total effect and se is its sd.
  3. impact_plot: the causal.impact chart.
  4. mmm: model.fit of mmm.bayesian with calibration.lift_tests from the lift node.
  5. lift_plot: the mmm.lift_tests chart. It shows if the model agrees with the test.
  6. report: a report of the lift test, the metrics and the two charts.

The template has two inputs: experiment (the KPI for each market and week around the test) and data (the data of the marketing mix model). It has the parameters treated, test_start, test_end, channel and spend_delta.

mapi workflows create --template geo_lift_mmm
mapi workflows run geo-lift-mmm \
  -i experiment=dataset://growth/geo_test@latest \
  -i data=dataset://growth/eu_media_weekly@latest \
  -p 'treated=["Leeds", "Bristol"]' -p test_start=2024-03-04 -p test_end=2024-04-14 \
  -p channel=tv -p spend_delta=50000 --watch

These rules apply:

  • The dates of the test must be in the data of the marketing mix model.
  • With one test market, the lift test has the geo of that market. That market must be a geo of the marketing mix model.
  • With two or more test markets, the lift test is national (geo: null).
  • The time labels of the experiment must be dates.

docs.title: Before and after, with a comparison group
docs.text:
Use causal.did when some units (stores, markets, products) got a change and other units never got it. Make a treatment column: 0 before a unit got the change, 1 from the period of the change.

data:
  bind: {dims: {unit: store, time: month}, vars: {y: sales, treatment: new_layout}}
model:
  use: causal.did@^1
  settings: {design: event_study, leads: 4, lags: 8}
  fit: {mode: train_only, tune: 500, draws: 500, chains: 4, seed: 20261020}
outputs:
  plots: [causal.event_study, causal.impact, causal.pre_fit, core.convergence]

The causal.event_study chart shows one coefficient for each period before and after the change. The coefficients before the change must include zero. If they do not include zero, the units moved differently before the change, and the effect is not reliable.

If the units got the change at different times, the model gives the warning STAGGERED_ADOPTION. The estimate can then be wrong when the effect is different for each group of units.

docs.title: What the fit logs
docs.text: Each causal fit logs the total effect, its interval, the relative effect and the error before the change as tracking metrics. Thus you can compare tests on the Runs page. See What a causal fit logs.

docs.title: Choosing a model v0.5
docs.text: You do not need to know what "SARIMAX" means to select a good forecast model. Also, you do not need to read a statistics textbook to know when not to use one. Each model, preprocessing step, workflow node, governance check and template has an About card in plain words. Help me choose asks some questions about your goal and your data. Then it gives a ranked shortlist with the reasons. This page shows the two tools. Then it compares the model families, for persons who want the details. For the contract behind the tools, see About cards and choosing.

docs.title: Answer a few questions
docs.text:
There are eight questions. All are optional. The goal has the most weight:

Question Answers What do you want to do? measure what marketing adds · plan a budget · measure the effect of a campaign, a launch or a test · forecast · understand drivers · predict per item · understand choices · find regimes · see series move together · check data · validate a model · make a map or an image from measurements · fit a physical model to measurements · put items or images into classes (v0.14) What does your data look like? one number over time · a few related numbers · the same numbers for many markets, stores or products · purchases or choices · a table without time · a map, an image or values on a regular grid · images, pictures of the same size (v0.14) How often do you record the data? daily · weekly · monthly or less often · not over time How much history? under a year · one to three years · more Other columns that could explain it? yes (prices, promotions, weather, spend) · no Do you need a range? essential · it would be good · one number is enough How much do you know about statistics? new to it · the basics · expert How quickly do you need results? seconds · minutes · can wait TerminalPythonHTTPWeb app 
mapi choose                                   # questions, one at a time; Enter skips one
mapi choose -a goal=forecast -a data_shape=one_series -a drivers=yes -a experience=beginner
mapi about ts.sarimax                         # one item's About card
mapi about ts.sarimax --expert                # ... with the maths and references

mapi choose asks the questions one at a time. Type a number. For questions that accept more than one answer, type more than one number. To skip a question, push Enter. The command shows the shortlist, and then the About card of the first three items. This is the result for the four answers above, on a local stack (shortened):

Recommended for you

Smooth trend forecast  model ts.hsgp_trend
Forecasts one regular series with a smooth, flexible trend and a repeating seasonal pattern, and gives a range of likely values.
difficulty: beginner   typical time: minutes
…
unanswered (answer them to sharpen the ranking): frequency, history, uncertainty, speed

The answer "new to it" (statistics) has an effect. Models that need more experience have a caution, and they rank below the models for beginners. Examples are ts.ardl above and ts.sarimax in position six. The models for beginners include the readiness workflow, which selects the settings of an ARIMAX for you. If you answer experience=intermediate, or skip the question, ts.ardl and ts.sarimax come first. These are the models that use the drivers.

from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()  # MAPI_URL, the `mapi login` sign-in (or MAPI_TOKEN) and MAPI_PROJECT

result = api.catalog.recommend(
    goal="forecast", data_shape="one_series", drivers="yes", experience="beginner", limit=3
)
for item in result.items:  # best first, with the reasons in plain words
    print(f"{item.score:.0%}  {item.title}  ({item.kind.value} {item.id})")
    for reason in item.reasons_plain:
        print("     +", reason)
    for caution in item.cautions_plain:
        print("     !", caution)

card = api.catalog.about("ts.sarimax", kind="model")  # any item's About card
print(card.summary_plain)
print("use it when:", "; ".join(card.use_when))
print("pick something else when:", "; ".join(card.avoid_when))

api GET "/v1/catalog/chooser"        # the questions
api GET "/v1/catalog/recommendations?goal=forecast&data_shape=one_series&drivers=yes&experience=beginner&limit=3"
api GET "/v1/catalog/abouts?kind=model"

Help me choose on the model, template and workflow pickers asks the same questions. It shows the same ranking. Each card has About. About shows the plain explanation first. The expert details are folded away.

The ranking is deterministic, and you can see why each item has its position:

  • An answer that matches adds the weight of the question. An answer that does not match subtracts it.
  • Items that are more difficult than your experience lose points. Items that are slower than your answer for speed also lose points.
  • Each recommendation lists its reasons ("Suits: forecast the future").
  • Each recommendation lists its cautions ("Needs expert-level statistics knowledge", "Usually takes long").

Without a kind, the candidates are the items that you start from: models, guided templates and workflow templates. --kind step, node or check ranks only one type of item.

docs.title: Read an About card
docs.text:
mapi about ts.ets

Exponential smoothing forecast  ts.ets
Forecasts a series by giving recent values more weight than older ones, with optional trend and
seasonality, and is quick and robust.
difficulty: beginner   typical time: seconds
Use it when
  • You need a fast, reliable baseline forecast
  • The level, trend and seasonality shift slowly
Pick something else when
  • Outside drivers explain most of the movement
It needs
  • One number over time at a regular frequency
It assumes
  • Recent history is the best guide to the near future
You get
  • A forecast with a range
  • Level, trend and seasonal parts
Example: Forecast monthly demand 12 months ahead with a damped trend.
Related: ts.theta, ts.arima, evaluate.baseline
(--expert shows the maths and references)

Each card has the same parts:

  • A summary of one or two sentences, without jargon.
  • When to use the item, and when not to use it.
  • The data that it needs, and what it assumes.
  • What you get.
  • How difficult it is, and how long it usually takes.
  • A very small example, and related items.

--expert (or Expert detail in the web app) adds the maths and the references. The platform refuses catalog items that do not have a complete card. Thus each model that you can select explains itself. This also applies to your own plugins (the About check).

docs.title: The model families, compared
docs.text:
You want to Start with Why Then consider Measure what each marketing channel adds. Plan budgets. mmm.bayesian Pooled over markets. Adstock and saturation, business priors and lift tests. Ranges on all values. Budget optimisation. mmm.frequentist for a quick first look. The mmm_governed workflow to gate it on null tests. Measure marketing effects that go through visits, searches or awareness mmm.nested Direct and indirect effect of each channel. A measure can have empty periods, for example a monthly survey. National data. The mediated_mmm Guided template. mmm.bayesian when price or promotions change sales much (it takes controls). Measure marketing effects on two or more results, such as related products mmm.multivariate One budget, several results with correlated noise, and the effects between the results (associations, not causes). National data. The multi_kpi_mmm Guided template. One mmm.bayesian model for each result when the results do not interact. Measure marketing with a count (orders, sign-ups) or a share as the result mmm.bayesian with likelihood: poisson, negative_binomial or beta The predictions stay whole numbers or between 0 and 1 normal when the counts are large. ROI priors and lift tests need it. Measure the effect of a campaign, a launch or a price change on one series v0.13 causal.impact The actual values against a prediction without the change, from the history and control series. The effect in each period and in total, with a range. The campaign_impact Guided template. causal.synthetic_control when you have the same number for many markets. Measure a geo-lift test (a campaign in some markets only) v0.13 causal.synthetic_control A weighted mix of the other markets follows each test market. The result is a lift test for the MMM. The geo_lift Guided template. The geo_lift_mmm workflow calibrates mmm.bayesian with the test. Measure a change that some units got and other units never got v0.13 causal.did Unit and time effects, and one effect for each period before and after the change (event study) causal.synthetic_control when only a few units got the change Forecast one series with known drivers (price, promotions) ts.sarimax Past values, season and drivers. Prediction intervals. Forecasts from planned drivers. The ts_readiness_arimax workflow. It selects the differencing and orders, and proves that the model is better than naive. Forecast without drivers, fast and robust ts.ets or ts.theta Strong, simple baselines that are difficult to beat The forecast_bakeoff workflow, which lets them compete See the trend under the noise ts.unobserved_components Level, trend, season and noise as separate parts ts.hsgp_trend for a Bayesian smooth trend. ts.bsts for the same parts with ranges, gaps in the data and a filter mode. Know how an effect builds up over weeks ts.ardl Lags of the drivers, selected automatically ts.ecm when the result and drivers have the same trend Several series that drive each other ts.var Impulse responses, variance decompositions, Granger tests ts.vecm when they are tied in the long run. The var_vecm_cointegration workflow decides. Find regimes (normal or caused by promotions) ts.markov_switching Probability of each regime for each period ts.gaussian_hmm for a Bayesian hidden-state model Predict a value for each store, product or customer sklearn.tabular_regressor Gradient boosting or forests. Quantiles and conformal intervals. tabular.hierarchical_glm when groups must borrow strength Understand which product people select choice.multinomial_logit Price and promotion effects, household effects Predict yes or no for each row v0.14 sklearn.tabular_classifier The probability of yes. Logistic regression, forests, xgboost, histogram boosting, LightGBM or CatBoost. sklearn.multiclass_classifier for three or more classes Put each row into one of three or more classes v0.14 sklearn.multiclass_classifier The probability of each class. ROC and precision-recall curves for each class, and a confusion matrix. tabular.hierarchical_glm with family: ordinal when the classes have an order Classify small images v0.14 tabular.image_logistic A Bayesian model on the main patterns of the pixels. A range for the probability of each class. sklearn.multiclass_classifier on features that you calculate first, for larger images. See Image data. Classify thousands of images or more v0.15 dl.cnn_classifier A neural network that trains on all images of a collection. Training curves, early stopping and checkpoints. The GPU class makes it faster. dl.finetune_classifier when you have pretrained weights. See Deep learning. Classify images with few labels and a pretrained network v0.15 the step dl.embed and sklearn.multiclass_classifier Image features from a frozen network, then a fast classifier tabular.image_logistic with input: features for a range on each probability Predict a value or a class for each row of a large table with a neural network v0.15 dl.mlp Relations that are not linear. Training and validation curves. Draws from the last layer. sklearn.tabular_regressor first: on most tables, boosted trees are as good and faster Model counts with many zeros, shares or positive amounts v0.14 tabular.hierarchical_glm with family: zero_inflated_poisson, negative_binomial, beta or gamma Group effects with sharing, and a likelihood that fits the data Check data before you model it the Data Explorer Stationarity, cross-correlation with the KPI, STL, VIF, quality warnings Make sure that you can trust a model a governance policy Null tests, benchmarks, residuals, stability, signs

For the details of each family, see these pages: Marketing-mix models, statsmodels time-series models, forecasting, tabular models and the built-in models.

docs.title: Science models, compared
docs.text:
The science models (sci.*, package mapi-plugin-science) come from the pymc-challenges case studies. They are for maps, images, fields, graphs, trees and angles. All of them are Bayesian and give a range for each value. The base-bayes runner image contains them. The chooser shows them only when the catalog has the plugin.

To find them with Help me choose, answer the goal "Make a map or an image from measurements" or "Fit a physical model to measurements". Then answer the data shape "A map, an image or values on a regular grid". The graph, tree and angle models use the goal "Understand what causes changes in a number" with the data shape "A table of items without a time order". Most of these models need expert-level statistics knowledge. Thus, if you answer "new to it", they rank lower and show a caution.

api GET "/v1/catalog/recommendations?goal=map_fields&data_shape=grid&kind=model"
Your data Use When to use it Counts of events in each cell of a map, for each period sci.lgcp_grid You want a map of the rate and a forecast of the next periods Counts of cells across a scratch, at some times sci.fisher_kpp You want the speed at which cells move, divide and close the wound A map of the movement of a gel under cells sci.traction_force You want the force map and the strain energy A telescope image of a lens galaxy with a ring or arcs sci.strong_lens You want the Einstein radius and the source galaxy without the lens Temperatures at some points of a heated plate sci.heat_plate You want the heat properties and the temperature map of a new heater layout Images of a pattern of spots or stripes that starts to grow sci.turing_pattern You want the reaction and diffusion rates and the probability of a Turing pattern Raw frames of a STORM or PALM microscope (EMCCD camera) sci.storm_localisation You want the position of each molecule in nm, with an error bar Many small images of the same size sci.ibp_features You want the parts that the images share, or to fill in hidden pixels The colour names that the speakers of one language gave to colour chips sci.colour_naming You want the boundaries between the colour words and a map of the words A CMB temperature map of a small flat patch, with a mask sci.cmb_field You want the sky behind the mask and the bandpowers Counts of cases and expected counts for each area of a map sci.areal_bym2 You want a map of the risk that borrows strength from the neighbour areas Ties between pairs of nodes (yes or no) sci.network_latent_space You want the effect of pair covariates and the chance of a tie for each pair The same variables, measured on many samples sci.graphical_model You want the direct links between the variables, with a probability for each link One trait value for each species, and a tree of the species sci.phylo_regression You want a slope across species that does not count shared ancestors many times Angles: wind directions or times of day sci.circular_regression You want the most probable direction for each hour and season, or the activity of species

The About card of each model tells when not to use it. For example, sci.areal_bym2 cannot predict areas that are not on the map, and sci.cmb_field is not correct for a patch of more than about 20 degrees. For all settings, see Scientific models.

The workflow gallery has recipes that compare science models or check them:

Recipe What it does sci_spatial_ladder Fits sci.areal_bym2 with iid, ICAR and BYM2 area effects and keeps the best model by elpd_loo and stacking weights sci_network_ladder Fits sci.network_latent_space with covariates, sociality and a latent space and keeps the best model sci_phylo_signal Fits sci.phylo_regression with four residual kinds and keeps the best model sci_calibrate_then_design Fits sci.heat_plate with one run held out, and predicts a new heater layout only if the holdout error and R-hat are in their limits sci_image_model_check Shows residual maps and predicted images next to the observed image of an image model bayes_workflow_audit Does the checks of a careful Bayesian workflow for each model that gives draws

For the documents of these recipes, see the workflow cookbook.

docs.title: When the chooser is not enough
docs.text:
• Compare. Do not guess. Fit two candidates and compare them on the same holdout. Use mapi explore compare model://growth/a@v1 model://growth/b@v1 (metrics, ranking and Diebold-Mariano tests). Alternatively, run a bake-off workflow.
  • Let the data decide the details. The readiness workflow selects differencing and ARMA orders with tests and information criteria. It records the reasons.
  • Make "good enough" explicit. A governance policy changes "it looks fine" into checks. The checks have thresholds, evidence and the approval of a second person.

docs.title: The command line v0.2
docs.text:
mapi (package mapi-cli, Apache-2.0) works in two locations:

  • Locally, without a server. You scaffold a spec, check it, fit it and score it in your own Python process, with the installed plugins (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec).
  • Remotely, against the HTTP API of a platform that runs. You upload datasets, fit, follow runs and score model versions (datasets, runs, and --remote on check, fit, score and catalog).

The generated CLI reference lists all commands and options. The examples on this page are scripts that the test suite runs. The default suite runs the local scripts. make e2e runs the remote scripts.

Running the commands

make install puts mapi into the workspace environment. You can activate the environment (source .venv/bin/activate). Alternatively, you can put uv run before each command (uv run mapi --help).

docs.title: Without a server
docs.text:
Scaffold a spec from a template. --with-data also writes the sample data of the conformance fixture that matches. This option needs the mapi-conformance package. The workspace has this package.

mapi new tabular -o spec.yaml --with-data     # an XGBoost demand model plus its sample data
Template What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Hierarchical geo MMM (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend and seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02

Check the spec statically against the installed plugins and the schema of the data. --stages shows the schema after each pipeline step. If there are errors, the exit status is 1. Thus the command works in CI:

mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --stages

Fit in-process. The bundle goes to bundles/<name>/. It contains the zarr zip, sidecars, plots, metrics and the evaluation bundle of evaluate_then_refit. --side-table NAME=PATH supplies side tables:

mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip       # in-process: writes bundles/<name>/
ls bundles/tabular

mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/<name> --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip scores a local bundle with a ScoreRequest document.

Local means trusted

Local fit and score import and run the plugins in your own process (isolation NONE), exactly as a notebook does. Use them only with code and data that you trust. On the platform, the same work runs in a sandbox.

Inspect the catalog of installed plugins. Upgrade spec documents across apiVersions:

mapi catalog models
mapi --json catalog steps | jq -r '.steps[].id' | head -n 5
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check           # exit 0: already the current apiVersion

mapi plugin init NAME scaffolds a plugin package (model, entry point, contract-kit tests). mapi plugin test NAME runs its tests. See Write a plugin.

docs.title: With a server
docs.text: First, start the stack (make dev, then make seed). See the quickstart.

docs.title: Select the API
docs.text:
Each remote command finds the API in the same way as the Python client. The first match in this list wins:

  1. --url and --token. These are global options. Put them before the command: mapi --url http://… runs ls.
  2. MAPI_URL, MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE. If MAPI_URL is not set, the CLI uses MAPI_API_URL, the name that make dev uses.
  3. The selected profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml. If $MAPI_CONFIG or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml is set, the CLI uses that file.
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.
# ~/.config/mapi/config.toml
profile = "local"

[profiles.local]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

[profiles.other-ports]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:18000"
timeout = 60

mapi config show shows the resolved URL, profile, project and credentials. It also shows the source of each value. It never shows a token. An API token shows as mapi_<prefix>_…. A sign-in shows as the person who signed in and the time when the sign-in ends. mapi config path shows the location of the file.

mapi config set KEY VALUE and mapi config unset KEY change the selected profile. The selected profile is --profile. If you do not give it, it is MAPI_PROFILE, and then the default of the file. These commands write the file again with mode 0600. They do not keep comments. You cannot set secrets in this way. Use mapi login --with-token.

--remote @ on check, fit, score and catalog means "the configured API". --remote URL overrides it for one command.

Tokens

v0.2 is single-tenant and has no authentication. The API listens only on 127.0.0.1. When MAPI_TOKEN is set, the client sends it as a bearer token. The client refuses to send it over plain HTTP to an address that is not a loopback address.

docs.title: Sign in and choose a project v0.3
docs.text:
A multi-tenant API (v0.3) needs credentials and a project (Tenancy and authentication).

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • mapi login opens the identity provider in your browser. It uses OpenID Connect and the authorization code with PKCE. The provider redirects to a one-time listener on 127.0.0.1.
    • --device signs in with a code that you type on a different device.
    • --no-browser only shows the address.
    • The CLI saves --issuer, --client-id and --discovery-url in the profile. Thus later logins do not need them.
    • Against a local MAPI_PROFILE=dev stack, use mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp. Then select an account on the page that opens.
    • The CLI keeps the sign-in in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600). It renews the sign-in automatically with its refresh token. It sends the sign-in only to the API that it was made for.
  • mapi login --with-token reads an API token from stdin and checks its checksum. Thus it finds an incorrect character before it sends a request. Then it verifies the token with GET /v1/me and saves it in the profile. It writes the config file again with mode 0600. An API token in the profile or in MAPI_TOKEN has priority over a browser sign-in.
  • mapi whoami shows who you are and how you signed in. It also shows each project where you can act, with your role there.
  • mapi logout removes the sign-in and revokes its refresh token at the identity provider. It also removes the token of the profile. --revoke also revokes that token on the server.

Each v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) is now in a project. mapi use checks that you are a member. Then it saves the selection in the profile. The CLI sends the project as X-Mapi-Project, but only on project-scoped requests. --project overrides it for one command. MAPI_PROJECT overrides it for one shell. An API token acts only in its own project.

mapi use acme/growth                            # sent as X-Mapi-Project from now on
mapi --project acme/retail runs ls              # another project, for one command
mapi use                                        # show the selection and where it came from

docs.title: Tokens, usage and cost v0.3
docs.text:
mapi tokens create budget-planner -s score:geo-mmm-prod -s models:read \
    --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 120 > planner.token   # the secret, once, on stdout
mapi tokens ls
mapi tokens revoke tok_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0      # asks first; --yes for scripts
mapi usage --group-by resource_class            # this month: cost, compute, quota headroom
mapi usage --tenant acme --period day           # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)
mapi runs get run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0    # includes the run's metered cost

mapi tokens create shows the secret of the new token one time, alone on stdout. Thus, if you redirect stdout to a file, the file contains exactly the token. --save stores the token in the profile instead. No other command ever shows a token. Lists, whoami and config show use the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_….

mapi usage shows these data:

  • The exact cost of the period, in integer micro-units of the currency. A named price table gives the prices.
  • The vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds behind the cost.
  • How much of each quota is used, and when it resets.

mapi runs get and mapi runs ls show the cost of each run. While the cost is still an estimate, it has a ~.

When the API answers 429, the client does these actions:

  • For RATE_LIMITED, the client waits and then tries again. It waits for the Retry-After of the server, and then uses exponential back-off.
  • For QUOTA_EXCEEDED, the client stops immediately. It shows the reason and the time when the quota resets (retry after 1h 30m). With --json, it also gives retry_after_seconds.

docs.title: Operators v0.3
docs.text:
Platform operators use mapi admin to manage tenants, quotas, kill switches and executors. Each change shows a before-and-after table and asks for confirmation. For runbooks, --yes skips the confirmation. The server audits each change. Kill-switch changes need --reason.

mapi admin kill-switches set --untrusted-code off --reason "incident 2026-10-15"
mapi admin quotas set tenant acme --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 --concurrent-runs 40 \
    --storage 200GiB --note "beta customer"
mapi admin tenants update acme --status suspended --reason "payment overdue"
mapi admin executors ls
mapi admin executors disable cloudrun-jobs --reason "incident 2026-10-15: contain"
mapi admin audit --tenant acme --action token.create --since 2026-10-01

mapi admin quotas set replaces the full policy of a subject. It removes the limits that you do not give. The tier defaults and the other levels still apply.

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
mapi datasets upload does these steps:

  1. If the dataset does not exist, it creates the dataset.
  2. It sends the file to the signed URL that the API returns.
  3. It starts the sandboxed ingest run.
  4. It waits until the version is ready.

CSV and Parquet files need --mapping mapping.yaml. This file is an IngestMapping that gives the column of each dim and variable:

python scripts/seed.py --export demo/      # the E33 tables, score payloads and spec
mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future
mapi datasets ls

docs.title: Fit and follow
docs.text:
mapi fit SPEC --remote @ creates the spec. If the text changed, it adds a revision. Then it submits a fit run and follows its event stream until the run ends. It shows warnings, diagnostics and metrics when they arrive. With --no-wait, the command returns after it submits the run. mapi runs watch RUN follows a run at a later time.

mapi check demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @   # the server's static validation
mapi fit demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @     # create or revise the spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --kind fit --limit 3

mapi runs cancel RUN asks for cancellation. mapi runs retry RUN --resource-class L starts a new run from a run that failed.

From v0.11, mapi runs watch and mapi fit --remote also show the metrics that the model logs. They show a maximum of one metrics line each 5 seconds, for example metrics loss=1.23 (step 400).

docs.title: Track metrics, params and tags v0.11
docs.text:
Each run keeps metrics, params, tags, a name and a note. To see them, do these steps:

  1. Show the metric series of a run: mapi runs metrics RUN.
  2. Show the points of one key: mapi runs metrics RUN --key step_size --points 200.
  3. Show the params: mapi runs params RUN.

You can add values to a run, also after it finished. You need the runner role. A token needs the runs:write scope.

mapi runs log-metric RUN revenue_lift 0.042 --label region=north
mapi runs log-param RUN analyst kim
mapi runs tag RUN stage=production team=growth --delete old_tag
mapi runs rename RUN "weekly sales, adstock 4"
echo "Holiday weeks removed." | mapi runs note RUN -

To find runs by their tracking data, use the options of mapi runs ls:

mapi runs ls --filter 'metric.rmse < 12' --filter 'param.fit.engine = nutpie' \
  --order-by metric.rmse --column metric.rmse --column param.settings.adstock.l_max
mapi runs ls --tag stage=candidate --name adstock --parent RUN

For the grammar of --filter, --order-by and --column, see Search runs.

docs.title: Media, experiments and comparison v0.14
docs.text:
mapi runs media RUN                                  # key, labels, step, kind, size, caption
mapi runs media RUN --key samples --download out/    # files KEY-LABELS-STEP.EXT
mapi runs log-image RUN holdout_map map.png --step 3 --label split=val --caption "Holdout error"

mapi experiments create "adstock length study" --description "Adstock 2, 4 and 8 weeks."
mapi experiments add "adstock length study" RUN RUN
mapi experiments ls
mapi experiments show "adstock length study"
mapi experiments rename "adstock length study" "adstock study"
mapi experiments archive "adstock study"            # unarchive makes it accept runs again
mapi experiments remove "adstock study" RUN
mapi experiments rm "adstock study"                 # the runs stay
mapi fit spec.yaml --remote @ --experiment "adstock study"
mapi workflows run weekly-readiness -i data=dataset://growth/sales@latest \
  --experiment "adstock study"                     # the node runs join it too
mapi runs ls --experiment "adstock study" --column metric.rmse

mapi runs compare RUN RUN RUN --key loss --key rmse --agg min
mapi runs views save "best fits" --filter 'metric.rmse < 12' --order-by metric.rmse \
  --column metric.rmse
mapi runs views ls
mapi runs ls --view "best fits"
mapi runs views rm "best fits"

An experiment argument (EXP) is an id or the exact name of the experiment. mapi runs compare shows a table of the metrics (one column for each run), then the params that are different (--all-params shows all params). mapi runs ls --view uses the search of the view. The other options add to the search or replace a part of it. mapi runs watch shows a line for each image that the run logs (a maximum of one line each 5 seconds).

docs.title: Image collections and weights v0.15
docs.text:
mapi datasets missing-images product_photos ./photos            # new and present images
mapi datasets upload-images product_photos ./photos --label-from-folder --size 64x64 --wait
mapi datasets upload-images product_photos ./photos --manifest labels.csv \
  --label-column label --split-column split --state photos.upload.json
mapi datasets upload-images product_photos ./photos --no-base   # upload all images again
mapi datasets upload-weights tiny-resnet resnet.safetensors --arch arch.json

upload-images uploads only the images that the base version does not have (by default the latest ready collection version). If the upload stops, type the same command again. With --state, the command skips the parts that arrived and signs the expired URLs again. The options are in Image data: collections.

upload-weights uploads a safetensors file as a weights dataset (the mapping {format: safetensors}). --arch gives the architecture when the file has no mapi_arch metadata. Read Deep learning.

--resource-class accepts GPU wherever the CLI offers the option.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
cat > forecast.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
data: dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest
side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90]}
EOF
# the CLI has no `models` command yet: take the model id and version from the API
# (with the same credentials as the CLI when MAPI_TOKEN is set)
AUTH=(-H "X-Mapi-Project: ${MAPI_PROJECT:-default/default}")
[ -z "${MAPI_TOKEN:-}" ] || AUTH+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN")
MODEL=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}/v1/models" \
  | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
mapi score forecast.yaml --remote @ --model "$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")" \
  --version "$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")" -o forecast.zarr.zip

mapi score --remote @ sends Prefer: wait=60. To change the time, use --wait. If the run takes longer, the command follows the run. It shows the outputs with their sizes and CRC32C. With -o, it downloads the result tree and checks it against that CRC32C.

The request must give data to score: data, inline values, a scenario dataset or a forecast horizon. If it gives none of them, the server refuses the request before a run starts (SCHEMA_INVALID on /data, "the score request has no data").

docs.title: Endpoints, webhooks and sharing v0.4
docs.text:
mapi endpoints promote geo-mmm-prod model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3   # asks first; --yes skips
mapi endpoints ls
mapi endpoints schema geo-mmm-prod --example > call.json           # a valid score call
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod call.json -o result.zarr.zip
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --mode forecast --periods 8 --draws 100
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --data plan.nc                   # inline XrJSON (≤ 5 MB)
mapi endpoints snippets geo-mmm-prod -l python > score.py
mapi endpoints rollback geo-mmm-prod --reason "v3 over-forecasts"

promote goes through the promotion gate. A scorecard with warnings needs --override --reason TEXT from a signed-in project admin. The gate blocks a scorecard that fails. Promotions and rollbacks change what each integration that calls the alias receives. Thus both commands show the current version and ask before they act.

score sends a JSON EndpointScoreCall. The call comes from a file, from stdin (-) or from --example. Flags set these values:

  • The mode and the horizon.
  • --data/--scenario: a dataset:// reference, an XrJSON .json, a .zarr.zip or a netCDF file. The command sends the file inline.
  • --draws.

score waits in the same way as mapi score --remote. -o downloads the result tree. With one --language, snippets shows only the code.

mapi endpoints schema ts-forecast                           # the Input table's columns
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv               # actuals + blank-target future rows
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast --actuals new.csv --periods 6
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast --actuals new.csv --future 1961-04-01 --future 1961-05-01
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv --dry-run     # print the call, send nothing

forecast sends actuals and the dates to forecast without a new fit. The CSV has a header row with the columns of the input table of the endpoint: the time column, the target and the drivers. schema lists them.

  • Rows with a target value are actuals.
  • Rows after the actuals with an empty target are the forecast.
  • If there are no such rows, the command adds --periods (default 8) after the last actual.
  • The command carries empty drivers on future rows forward (--future-covariates).

The command shows the data that the forecast used ("Forecast updated with 3 actuals …") and the summary table. score also shows them.

mapi webhooks create https://hooks.example.com/mapi -e endpoint.promoted -e run.failed > hook.secret
mapi webhooks ls
mapi webhooks deliveries WEBHOOK_ID --status failed
mapi webhooks replay WEBHOOK_ID DELIVERY_ID
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID --enable           # back on after --inactive or an auto-disable
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID -e run.failed --description "on-call"
mapi webhooks rotate WEBHOOK_ID > hook.secret      # asks first; the old secret signs for 24 h
mapi webhooks rm WEBHOOK_ID                        # asks first

create and rotate show the signing secret of a webhook one time, alone on stdout, as for tokens. Lists show whsec_…<last 4>. update changes the events, --url or --description. -e replaces the full list of events. --enable/--disable turns deliveries on or off.

A webhook that you created with --inactive goes back on with --enable. This also applies to a webhook that the platform disabled automatically after many failures. --enable also resets the failure count. Delivery responses are the text of the receiver. The CLI shows them with control sequences removed. Receiving webhooks tells how to verify deliveries.

mapi plots render --model MODEL_ID --version 3 --plot mmm.response_curves -f pdf -o curves.pdf
mapi plots render --saved PLOT_ID --width 1200
mapi plots embed PLOT_ID --expires-in-days 30 --allow-origin https://bi.example.com
mapi plots embeds PLOT_ID
mapi plots revoke PLOT_ID EMBED_ID                 # asks first

render draws the plot in the sandbox (vl-convert) and downloads the file. embed shows the link one time. The link contains its token (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Guided mode and business priors v0.4
docs.text:
mapi guided templates [geo_mmm]
mapi guided detect geo_mmm --csv media.csv          # or --dataset dataset://growth/media@v2
mapi guided draft geo_mmm --name eu-geo-mmm --dataset eu_media --csv media.csv --detect \
    -a spend=tv_spend,search_spend -a holdout_periods=8 --yaml-out spec.yaml
mapi priors preview --beliefs beliefs.yaml --spec SPEC_ID --revision 2 -o priors.json

detect and draft --csv profile the file locally. They find the types, counts, ranges and some sample values of each column. They send only those summaries, as the web app does.

  • --detect fills each answer that detection is sure of.
  • -a QUESTION=VALUE answers one question, or overrides the answer. Use a,b,c for lists and JSON for numbers.

A draft stores nothing. Examine spec.yaml. Then upload the data with the mapping (--mapping-out) and fit. priors preview changes ROI ranges or contribution-share ranges into model priors in a sandboxed run. It shows what the model then believes, for each channel (Guided modelling).

docs.title: Sign-up and your workspace v0.4
docs.text:
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example signup --email ana@acme.example --name "Ana Analyst" --accept-terms
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example verify-email mev_…   # the token from the e-mail link
mapi tenant status                                       # verification, any scheduled deletion
mapi tenant export -o acme-export.zip                    # GDPR export, waited for and downloaded
mapi tenant delete                                       # type the tenant id to confirm
mapi tenant delete --cancel                              # within the grace period

signup and verify-email send no credentials. tenant delete tells what the platform purges and what it keeps. Then it asks you to type the tenant id. Scripts give --confirm TENANT. The tenant is --tenant. If you do not give it, the tenant is the tenant of the selected project. If there is no selected project, it is your only tenant (Deleting and exporting data).

docs.title: Workflows, governance and explorers v0.5
docs.text:
Help me choose and About cards, in the terminal:

mapi choose                                   # questions, one at a time; Enter skips one
mapi choose -a goal=forecast -a data_shape=one_series -a drivers=yes -a experience=beginner
mapi about ts.sarimax                         # one item's About card
mapi about ts.sarimax --expert                # ... with the maths and references

Workflows: start from the gallery and check the file on the server. Then save it, run it and watch each node live. If the run fails, --watch exits with status 1. Thus it works in CI:

mapi workflows templates                      # the gallery, in plain words
mapi workflows init ts_readiness_arimax --name weekly-readiness   # writes weekly-readiness.yaml
mapi workflows validate weekly-readiness.yaml # checked by the server: pointers to every problem
mapi workflows apply weekly-readiness.yaml -m "first version"     # create, or save a revision
mapi workflows run weekly-readiness \
  --input data=dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  --param 'drivers=["price"]' --param window=104 \
  --watch                                     # live node status; exit 1 if the run fails

validate and apply show the sequence in which the nodes will run. This output is from a local stack, with the document of the cookbook:

weekly-readiness.yaml: valid (23 nodes)
order: adf → kpss → pp → za → seas → folds → holdout → wanders → seasonal → naive → order → sdiff → backtest → fit → diff → compare → dm → acf → select → governance → report → trusted → pack

The cookbook shows the live board of --watch and the summary at its end. Then examine a run, one node at a time:

RUN=$(mapi --json workflows runs weekly-readiness -n 1 | jq -r '.[0].run_id')
mapi workflows status "$RUN"                  # nodes, what each found, decisions, outputs
mapi workflows node "$RUN" order              # one node: parameters, result, outputs
mapi workflows output "$RUN" diff data --out diff.zarr.zip   # a derived dataset, verified

 node        order
 uses        search.arma_order@1.0.0
 status      succeeded
 attempt     1
 child runs  run_01m53hawz719exdgb6kcw5ysp3
 params      {"d": 1, "exog": ["price"], "max_p": 3, "max_q": 3, "trend": "c", "criterion": "aic"}
 result      {"best_p": 1, "best_q": 1, "best_order": [1, 1, 1], "criterion": "aic",
              "best_score": 430.4823790539326, "n_failed": 0, "suggested_p": 0, "suggested_q": 0}
 outputs     table: table

This is the output of mapi workflows node "$RUN" order. Here, we folded the JSON onto fewer lines. The differencing decision gave d = 1 to the search, and the run gave the price driver. The search selected ARIMA(1, 1, 1) by AIC.

mapi workflows schedules add weekly-readiness "0 6 * * 1" --tz Europe/Berlin \
  --input data=dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest
mapi workflows triggers add weekly-readiness dataset://growth/weekly_sales --debounce 600
mapi workflows schedules ls weekly-readiness

-i name=ref binds a workflow input. When the run starts, the platform pins @latest to a version. -p name=value sets a parameter. If the value parses as JSON, the CLI sends it as JSON (-p 'horizons=[1,4,13]'). The workflow cookbook has complete documents that you can start from.

Since v0.9, mapi workflows templates also lists the recipes for Bayesian and science models. Start each one with mapi workflows init <id>. The cookbook shows the commands for each one:

Template Cookbook section sci_spatial_ladder Disease map: which spatial model? sci_network_ladder Network ties: which model? sci_phylo_signal Trait regression across species sci_calibrate_then_design Calibrate, then design bayes_workflow_audit Bayesian workflow audit sci_image_model_check Image model check

To get the data of a science case study, use python -m mapi_plugin_science.export <case>. Then upload the file with mapi datasets upload.

Governance: the check catalog, policies, validations and approval by a second person. mapi validate model waits for the checks. It shows each result in plain words with the suggested action. mapi approve needs a signed-in reviewer who did not submit the model:

mapi governance checks                        # what a policy can require
mapi governance checks --about null.permutation_target --expert
mapi governance policies ls                   # in force here: tenant-wide first
mapi governance policies create forecast-policy.yaml
mapi validate model model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1   # runs the checks, waits
mapi validations ls --queue                   # reviewers: what waits for a decision
mapi approve "$VALIDATION" --comment "Null tests convincing; beats naive by 25%"
mapi validations pack "$VALIDATION" --out evidence.html          # for the auditor

Explorers and budget plans:

mapi explore dataset dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  -s overview -s stationarity -s ccf -s stl --kpi sales --out views/
mapi explore dataset weekly_sales --show stationarity            # one view as JSON
mapi explore model model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1 -s params -s residuals
mapi explore compare model://growth/arimax@v3 model://growth/ets@v1 --horizon 4

mapi optimize model://growth/geo-mmm@v7 --change-pct 0 \
  --channel 'tv={"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}' \
  --objective p10 --frontier 8

These are the forms of a model reference: model://project/name@vN, name@vN, name with -v N, or a model id. Dataset references have the same forms with dataset://. All commands accept --json.

docs.title: Use --json in scripts
docs.text:
--json is a global option. It shows one JSON document on stdout instead of tables. runs watch --json and workflows watch --json show one JSON event on each line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1. Usage errors exit with status 2.

RUN=$(mapi --json runs ls --kind score --limit 1 | jq -r '.[0].id')
mapi --json runs get "$RUN" | jq '{state, attempt, kind}'
mapi runs logs "$RUN" | tail -n 5

The CLI removes ANSI and control sequences from text that came from the server, a plugin or a run log. Thus a hostile log line cannot write over your terminal.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev. It does the database migrations. Then it runs the API and the orchestrator in one process. It uses an embedded PostgreSQL, unless DATABASE_URL is set. It uses an in-process GCS shim, unless a shim already listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. This is the smallest way to get an API for the CLI or the client. If you also want the web app, use make dev (Local deployment).

docs.title: Conformance corpus
docs.text:
The corpus is how the platform defines "supported". It is a set of small, realistic modelling problems. These problems are ports of pymc-challenges and of the examples of the plan. They must continue to work, from start to end, after each change. Each fixture goes through exactly the same process as the model of a user:

  1. validate: The runner checks the spec statically against the step, model and plot catalogs. The API does the same before it accepts a run.
  2. fit: The runner does a fit run on the in-process executor. It obeys fit.mode (also evaluate_then_refit).
  3. score: The runner does each request in score_requests.yaml as a score run. For requests that must fail, it checks the typed error code (for example HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT or UNSEEN_LEVELS).
  4. evaluate: The runner scores the holdout through the score path. The metrics must be equal to the metrics that the fit calculated.
  5. contract: The runner does the full check_model contract kit.
  6. plots: The runner renders the outputs.plots of the spec from real outputs.
  7. expectations: The runner does the own checks of the fixture (for example, recovered effects or the terminal state).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
python -m mapi_conformance list
python -m mapi_conformance run                         # every fixture at size tiny
python -m mapi_conformance run --fixture e24 --fixture c08
python -m mapi_conformance run --size full --json corpus.json
make conformance                                       # the same as `run` at size tiny
make conformance FIXTURE=e33                           # one fixture
make conformance-full                                  # every fixture at size full
python -m mapi_conformance list --deferred             # plus the plan fixtures not ported yet

The runner shows one row for each fixture. If a step failed, the exit status is not zero:

fixture           model                           validate  fit  score   evaluate  contract  plots   expectations  ...  result
----------------  ------------------------------  --------  ---  ------  --------  --------  ------  ------------       ------
e02               tabular.hierarchical_glm@1.0.0  ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
c08               ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0             ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e24               ts.gaussian_hmm@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 15/15  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
xgb_store_demand  tabular.regressor@1.0.0         ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 16/16  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e33               mmm.bayesian@1.0.0              ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 17/17  ok 4/4  ok                 PASS
mmm_frequentist   mmm.frequentist@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 4/4  ok        ok 18/18  ok 1/1  ok                 PASS

--size tiny is the default, and pytest -m conformance uses it. It keeps the data small and the MCMC short. --size full uses the own fit settings of the spec and larger data.

docs.title: Through a stack that runs
docs.text:
The default runner does not use the control plane. --stack sends the same fixtures through the API of a stack that runs (make dev), as a user does: spec → ingest → fit → score.

  1. The runner uploads the data, the side tables and the score payloads as dataset versions. It uses a signed PUT, and then a sandboxed ingest run.
  2. The spec points at the uploads. The platform validates it, creates it and fits it through the dispatcher, the runner and FINALIZING.
  3. Each score request runs against the registered model. An expected typed error can come from the failed run. It can also come from the API, if the API refuses the request at the start.
  4. The runner checks the holdout metrics and the stored plots on the model version.
  5. The runner downloads the bundle through signed URLs and verifies each hash. Then the bundle goes through the check_fit of the fixture.
python -m mapi_conformance run --stack http://127.0.0.1:8000 --fixture e33 --fixture xgb_store_demand
uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_corpus_stack.py   # E33, xgboost and sklearn (`make e2e`)
