The contract kit does not run in this mode. It needs the plugin in-process.

docs.title: The fixtures
docs.text: Fixture Model Exercises e02 tabular.hierarchical_glm Long layout, shuffled county labels, new counties from the hyperprior, LOO, CRN counterfactual c08 ts.hsgp_trend Sentinel codes, max_extension from anticipated coords, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, contiguity e24 ts.gaussian_hmm Padded data with a mask, terminal state, forecast and filter, relabelling, LOO that is not valid xgb_store_demand tabular.regressor Pooled new stores, refused quantile aggregation, covariates that must have future values sklearn_store_demand sklearn.tabular_conformal The same panel with plain scikit-learn (histogram boosting, skops): split-conformal intervals, refused interval aggregation, pooled new stores e33 mmm.bayesian FX (supplied) and holiday (pinned) side tables. Split after resample. mmm-framework owns scaling and carry-over (history added before the data at score time). New market from the hyperprior. Weekly EUR plan through inputs_stage. CRN counterfactual (intervention and baseline-vs-scenario). Derived quantities in EUR. mmm_frequentist mmm.frequentist The ridge estimator of mmm-framework with bootstrap draws. A model that owns scaling, carry-over and units. A score window is equal to the same weeks of the full series. e84_lite choice.multinomial_logit A ragged household × trip panel with a text target. last_per_group split. Products off the shelf. New households from the fitted spread. A price-rise counterfactual. Next trips. Categorical holdout metrics (hit rate against the naive guess, log score, Brier). guided_mmm mmm.bayesian The draft of the geo_mmm Guided template with business priors (ROI, contribution share, baseline share). The fit translates the priors, and a lift test is in the likelihood. Both agree with the simulation. ROI, baseline share and lift are checked against the truth. A forecast and the channel-off preset. e13_bsts v0.13 ts.bsts The plan fixture E13. Monthly sales with missing months and a price driver. A forecast with future prices, predictive draws, the filter mode that returns an updated terminal state, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED for counterfactual, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE without future prices. LOO that is not valid. causal_impact v0.13 causal.impact Weekly sales with two control series and a simulated lift. The impact group and a total effect more than zero. predict over the data (the values without the change and the effect), a forecast of 4 weeks with the control series, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE without them, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED for counterfactual geo_lift v0.13 causal.synthetic_control Weekly sales of 12 markets. One test market is a mix of the other markets. The impact and donor_weights groups and the simulated lift. A score needs the donors without gaps. A new market is refused. No forecast. did_event_study v0.13 causal.did Monthly sales of stores, some with a new layout. The event-study coefficients, the counterfactual mode (treatment set to 0), no month after the fit (the time effects are fixed), a missing treatment. No forecast. sm_arimax ts.sarimax Weekly sales for each geo with price and promotion drivers. An ARIMAX model for each series (statsmodels) sm_vecm_macro ts.vecm US real GDP, consumption and investment in log levels. A VECM with the Johansen cointegration rank e07_lgcp sci.lgcp_grid Earthquake counts on a space-time grid. A log-Gaussian Cox process with a 2-D HSGP map e18_areal sci.areal_bym2 A disease map on a graph of areas (BYM2). The polygons stay for the map e50_kpp sci.fisher_kpp A scratch assay as a Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion PDE that the model solves e51_heat_plate sci.heat_plate A heated plate, calibrated with the 2-D steady heat equation that the model solves e60_traction sci.traction_force Traction force microscopy. A Gaussian inverse problem in Fourier space e80_lens sci.strong_lens A galaxy-scale strong lens. A forward model of each pixel of a mock image e61_turing sci.turing_pattern Schnakenberg kinetics from early images of a Turing pattern e58_storm sci.storm_localisation Molecule positions in raw STORM frames (a Gaussian PSF with Poisson counts) e31_ibp sci.ibp_features Binary features of small images. An Indian buffet process e77_colour_naming sci.colour_naming Colour names of one language as a softmax over CIELAB values e79_cmb sci.cmb_field A masked CMB map. A Gibbs sampler for the sky behind the mask and the bandpowers e21_network sci.network_latent_space The ties of a graph, with sociality and a latent space e19_ggm sci.graphical_model A Gaussian graphical model. Partial correlations and edge probabilities of proteins e23_phylo sci.phylo_regression A regression across primate species, with residuals that the phylogeny correlates e81_circular sci.circular_regression Wind directions on the circle. A von Mises regression

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text:
The corpus of the plan also lists fixtures that need plugins or run kinds that do not exist yet. mapi_conformance.fixtures.DEFERRED lists them with the reason. A test makes sure that the list of the plan, the fixtures and the deferrals agree:

Plan fixture Waits for E82-slim GP Bayesian optimisation The recommend mode and Campaign runs (planned) E45 A plugin for its model (vetted plugins, planned)

docs.title: Time to port
docs.text:
The M0 exit criteria ask for the time to port each fixture. The target is less than one day for each fixture, for the model plugin and the fixture. This time is a measure of human effort. Thus you cannot get it from the code or from commit timestamps. Record it here when you port a fixture, or port it again.

Fixture Time to port Recorded e02 not measured yet – c08 not measured yet – e24 not measured yet – xgb_store_demand not measured yet – sklearn_store_demand not measured yet – e33 not measured yet – mmm_frequentist not measured yet –

docs.title: Add a fixture
docs.text:
1. Create a package conformance/src/mapi_conformance/fixtures/<id>/.
  2. Put <id> in the list in fixtures/__init__.py.
  3. Add the files below to the package.

data.py makes the data:

def generate(seed: int = 0, size: str = "tiny") -> tuple[xr.Dataset, dict[str, xr.Dataset]]:
    """The dataset and its side tables (name -> dataset)."""

def schema() -> DataSchema:            # optional: the raw schema (else inferred)
    ...

def payload_new_store(data, seed, size) -> xr.Dataset:   # optional payload builders
    ...

spec.yaml is a usual ModelSpec with the fit settings of a full run.

score_requests.yaml lists the requests to score. The runner fills in apiVersion, kind and model for you:

- name: forecast_with_new_store
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}}
  payload: new_store          # none | fit_data | "tail:<n>" | a payload_<name> builder
  drop_targets: true          # remove target variables from the payload (default)
  side_tables: true           # pass the fixture's side tables to the run (default)
  expect: {vars: [y_hat], sizes: {week: 4}, issues: [UNSEEN_LEVELS], groups: [summary]}
- name: quantiles_are_not_summed
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}, output: {aggregate: {over: [store_id]}}}
  payload: new_store
  expect_error: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED

expectations.py (optional) adds checks for the fixture. To make a check fail, raise AssertionError:

TINY_FIT = {"tune": 150, "draws": 100, "chains": 2}       # fit overrides at size tiny
TINY_SETTINGS = {"m": 20}                                  # model-settings overrides
MODEL_CHECKS = None                                        # or a subset of check_model checks

def check_fit(bundle, data): ...
def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data): ...
def check_evaluate(tree, bundle, data): ...

A hook that declares a keyword ctx parameter also receives a FixtureContext. The context holds the seed, the size, the registry, the side tables and results. results holds the trees of the score requests that succeeded before this one. Use it to compare requests. E33 does this. It checks that a weekly EUR plan forecasts exactly the same as the raw daily path:

def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data, *, ctx):
    if name == "weekly_eur_plan" and "forecast_8w" in ctx.results:
        ...

A side table can have score_policy: supplied. Then each score request that replays its step must name the side table (request.side_tables). The runner supplies the data with that name.

From Python, mapi_conformance.run_fixture("e24") returns a FixtureReport. run_corpus() returns a CorpusReport with .table() and .to_json().

docs.title: Deleting data and exporting it v0.4
docs.text: A tenant admin can export all the data that the workspace stored (GDPR access). The tenant admin can also delete the full workspace (GDPR erasure). Both actions need a signed-in session of a tenant admin. API tokens never administer a tenant. The HTTP API reference gives the HTTP operations. The configuration reference gives the settings.

docs.title: Export first
docs.text:
# queue the export (everything by default: metadata, datasets, models, audit, usage)
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
# poll it; once "ready", download_url is a signed link valid for 15 minutes
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports/exp_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0"
# every export of the workspace, newest first (any admin, any browser)
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports"

Settings > Data shows the newest export from that list. Thus a different admin (or a different browser) sees an export that the platform still makes. That admin can also download a finished export. The Python client has client.tenants.exports("acme").

The orchestrator makes the archive in the background, usually in less than a minute. The archive is a zip:

Path Content README.txt, manifest.json What is in the archive, with the size and SHA-256 of each file metadata/<table>.jsonl Each record of the workspace, with one JSON object on each line. Examples are projects, members, API tokens, datasets and versions (schemas, profiles), specs and revisions (YAML), runs, models and versions, plots, endpoints and webhooks. The maximum total is MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES (256 MiB). If the export stops a table early, skipped lists the table with the rows that it wrote. datasets/<dataset>/v<n>/... The stored dataset objects, byte for byte. The maximum total is MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES (256 MiB). manifest.json lists the remaining objects under skipped, with sizes and checksums. models/<model>/v<n>/manifest.json, model_version.json The signed bundle manifest, lineage, diagnostics, scorecard and metrics of each model version audit/audit_events.jsonl, usage/cost_ledger.jsonl The audit log and the metered usage of the workspace

The platform never exports credentials. Token hashes, signing keys, nonces and webhook secrets show as [redacted]. The platform reads the records through the own row-level-security session of the workspace. Thus an archive can contain only the rows of its own workspace.

One export runs at a time. The maximum is MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY (3) each day. More exports get 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The platform deletes an archive after MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S (7 days). A suspended workspace can still export. This includes a workspace with a scheduled deletion.

docs.title: Request the deletion
docs.text:
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"confirm": "acme", "reason": "closing the account"}'

confirm must contain the tenant id again. A deployment can also make a recent sign-in necessary (MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S). Older sessions get 401 and must sign in again. You cannot delete the own tenant of the platform.

The platform schedules the deletion for the end of a grace period (MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S, 7 days). These things occur immediately:

  • The platform suspends the workspace. You can still read all its data. You cannot create or run new items, and nothing spends compute.
  • The platform cancels the unfinished runs of the workspace.

Until the grace period ends, the admin can still export. The admin can also cancel the deletion:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X DELETE "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion"

When you cancel, the workspace gets back the status that it had before. This is not the case if an operator changed the status after the request. The audit log records tenant.deletion_request and tenant.deletion_cancel.

docs.title: What happens when the grace period ends
docs.text:
The deletion becomes deleting. You cannot undo this. The platform does these steps:

  1. The status of the tenant becomes deleting. The platform refuses each request for the tenant, from its members and from its tokens. Operators can still read the progress of the deletion.
  2. The platform revokes the API tokens of the tenant. It ends the browser sessions of persons who belong to no other workspace. Components that give links (webhooks, embed links) revoke their links.
  3. The platform cancels the unfinished runs again. The purge waits for them to stop, for a maximum of MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S (one hour). After that time, a run that has not stopped can possibly continue to upload results under the prefix of the workspace. It can do this while its signed upload links are valid (its timeout plus 30 minutes). Thus the purge then waits for those links to expire before it deletes anything. The detail of the queue store shows the time until which it waits.
  4. The platform cancels exports that are in the queue or that it still makes (state failed). The purge waits for a build in progress to end. The maximum wait is the MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S lease of the build. A cancelled build never uploads its archive. If an archive arrived after the purge listed the objects, the build deletes it.

Then the purge goes from store to store. GET /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion shows the progress of each store:

Store What is purged queue Background jobs of the runs of the tenant, and their bootstrap objects database Each record of the workspace in each table, children before parents. The platform also deletes persons who belonged only to this workspace. object_store Each object under t/<tenant>/ in the quarantine, runs, bundles and data buckets: uploads, run scratch, model bundles, dataset versions and export archives logs Not purged (see below) webhooks The platform sends the tenant.deletion.completed webhook to the endpoints that were registered before the purge.

When all stores are complete, the deletion is purged. The audit log gets the tombstone event tenant.purged. This event contains the tenant id, but no content.

docs.title: What is kept, and why
docs.text: Record Kept Audit log 1 year after deletion, pseudonymised: actor ids and keyed digests of client addresses, no content Cost ledger 7 years for tax law: amounts and run ids, no content The own record of the deletion Its ids, dates and counts for each store The tenant id A tombstone row (status deleting, no name), so that nobody can use the id again Sign-up records Only the keyed digests that the platform uses against repeated abuse. The platform erases the e-mail, name and organisation. Platform logs Not purged: see below

docs.title: Retention locks
docs.text: Model bundles are in a bucket with a retention policy (Terraform bundle_retention_days, 30 days, locked in production). Nobody can delete an object that is younger than that. The purge records each such object with the time when it can be deleted (time_created plus MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS). It shows object_store as running, with a plain explanation. When the retention expires, the purge continues automatically. All the other data is already gone, and nobody can get access to the workspace.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
You cannot delete Cloud Logging entries one at a time. Thus a deletion does not purge logs. The platform keeps tenant content out of the logs. Structured log lines contain tenant, project, run and request ids, and keyed digests of client addresses. They never contain request bodies, data or tracebacks of tenant code.

The logs expire with the retention of their bucket. Terraform sets the _Default log bucket of the control project to log_retention_days (30 days by default, infra/terraform/modules/control/logging.tf). The run-event sink only sends events to Pub/Sub and stores nothing. Thus 30 days after a deletion, its logs are also gone.

docs.title: When a store fails
docs.text:
If a store fails, the deletion becomes failed. The orchestrator tries it again with back-off. The back-off starts at 5 minutes and doubles each time, up to 6 hours. The maximum is MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS (8) attempts. After that, an operator examines last_error in the logs and starts the deletion again:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST \
  "$API/v1/admin/tenants/acme/deletion/retry"

The purge is idempotent. A new attempt starts where the last pass stopped.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text:
• The scheduler runs in the orchestrator (mapi-server worker) each MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S. Purges and exports run as procrastinate jobs on the lifecycle queue, one at a time for each deletion or export. If a worker stops unexpectedly, the platform puts the job in the queue again.
  • An export build can take MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S (one hour). After that, it fails. Possibly, an export is still running five minutes after that time. Then it belongs to a process that stopped unexpectedly (an OOM kill, a lost orchestrator). The scheduler makes the export one more time. If that build also stops, the scheduler fails the export. Thus a workspace can always ask for a new export.
  • The orchestrator makes the archive in memory. Give the orchestrator memory for MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES plus MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES.
  • Where the request-path role can delete database rows, the platform deletes them through the own row-level-security session of the tenant. Thus a purge cannot touch the rows of a different tenant.
  • Components that own credentials or links of a tenant register a mapi_server.services.trust.TenantRevoker. The webhooks component gives the DeletionNotifier that sends tenant.deletion.completed.

docs.title: Explore a dataset v0.5
docs.text:
The Data Explorer answers the questions to ask before you fit a model. It answers these questions:

  • What is in the data, and how does it move over time?
  • What is the shape of the data: series over time, images, a map, a network, a tree or directions?
  • Where are values missing or unusual?
  • Which drivers move with the result, and with how much delay?
  • Do series wander, or do they return to a level?
  • How strong is the season?
  • Which drivers overlap?
  • What must you correct first?

The sandbox calculates each view. The control plane never reads your data. Each view comes with Vega-Lite plots and captions in plain language. The web app shows all views. The other parts of this guide use the HTTP API, which the web app calls.

docs.title: In the web app
docs.text:
1. Open a dataset.
  2. Click Explore this version. Alternatively, go to /datasets/<dataset>/versions/<n>/explore.

The page starts with the About of the dataset. It has 22 sections in four groups:

  • The basics: overview, structure, data quality, distributions, over time, missing values and unusual values.
  • Pictures of the data: images and fields, gallery (v0.14), profiles and spectra, map, network, tree, directions and times of day, and points. Refer to Scientific data.
  • Relationships: correlations, leads and lags, overlapping drivers and group comparison.
  • Time patterns: memory (ACF/PACF), stable or wandering, and trend and season.

The list shows only the sections that apply to the data. The structure of the data sets the sequence of the sections. Thus a dataset of images starts with Images and fields, and a weekly panel starts with the overview and Over time. The sections that do not apply go in the closed list Not for this data below the other sections. Open this list to see each of these sections and the reason. A link to one of these sections (?section=) continues to open it.

A tick marks a section that is ready. An empty circle marks a section that the platform calculates when you ask for it. A dash marks a section that cannot show a result for this data, for example because a series is too short. The dash shows the reason.

Datasets from an earlier release

The index of a version that you ingested before this change does not give the reasons. For these versions, the list shows the thirteen sections of the earlier releases.

To add the new sections to a version from an earlier release, click Run the deeper checks (Guided) or Compute the remaining views (Expert).

  • Guided mode shows the plain summary of each section first ("4 series return to a stable level, 3 series wander (model their changes)…"). To see the numbers, click Show the statistics. Run the deeper checks calculates all the sections that the ingest did not calculate. It uses sensible defaults (the target of the dataset as the KPI).
  • Expert mode shows all statistics: test statistics and p-values, quantiles, VIFs and the condition number, and the significant lags. It also shows All series: the plots of the platform that are ready for export (ui/explore/plots/<section>.json). Explore with options sets the request of the run. The request contains the sections, the KPI and the dimensions that split the series. It also contains the lags, the season length, α, the correlation and outlier methods, and prewhitening.
  • Pickers select the variable or series that a plot shows. Examples are one line for each market, the STL decomposition of a series, or the cross-correlation of a driver with the KPI. The plots render in the isolated plot sandbox, as all plots do.
  • A section that is not calculated yet has a Compute it now button. This button starts an explore run for this section and for the other missing sections. The id of the run goes in the address (?run=). Thus you can share or reload the page. If you ask again with the same options, the platform answers immediately from the cached run.

docs.title: From Python and the command line
docs.text:
ds = api.datasets.find("weekly_sales")
assert ds is not None and ds.latest_version is not None
api.datasets.describe(ds.id, "Weekly sales and price by region, from the finance warehouse")
print(api.datasets.about(ds.id).summary_generated)  # "Weekly data from ... for 5 regions ..."

explored = api.datasets.explore(  # computed in the sandbox; the same request is cached
    ds.id,
    ds.latest_version,
    sections=["overview", "stationarity", "ccf", "stl", "quality"],
    kpi="sales",
    max_lag=12,
)
for section in explored.index.sections if explored.index else []:
    print(section.section, section.status, section.message_plain or "")
stationarity = api.explorations.view(explored, "stationarity")  # the view, as JSON

mapi explore dataset dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  -s overview -s stationarity -s ccf -s stl --kpi sales --out views/
mapi explore dataset weekly_sales --show quality      # one view as JSON

docs.title: Views written at ingest
docs.text:
Each ingest writes the quick sections next to the dataset: overview, distributions, timeseries, missingness, outliers, correlation and quality. It also writes structure and each picture section that applies to the data. Get the index, and then any view, through the artifact route:

api "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/artifacts/ui/explore/index.json"
api "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/artifacts/ui/explore/quality.json"

Each answer is a signed link (ArtifactLink) to the JSON view. The index lists each section with its status:

  • ok.
  • skipped, with the reason in plain words. An example is "the data has no time dimension". The field reason gives the type of reason:
    • not_applicable: the section is not for this data. The web app puts the section in Not for this data.
    • insufficient_data: the section applies, but the data is too small. An example is a series with fewer than 16 periods.
    • needs_option: the section needs an option of the request.
  • error.

The index also gives shapes (the data shapes that the explorer found, see How the explorer finds the structure) and order (the sections in the sequence that the web app shows them). An index without these fields comes from an earlier release.

The plots for a section are at ui/explore/plots/<section>.json. This file is a list of PlotSpecs to render in the plot sandbox.

Tree datasets v0.8. For a tree dataset, ui/explore/ holds the views of the default node: the root, or the first node with variables. The views of each node with variables are under ui/explore/nodes/<slug>/, where the slug is ~root for the root, or the node path with ~ in place of / (sales~weekly for /sales/weekly). ui/explore/nodes/index.json gives the default node and the index of each node. An explore run takes "node": "/sales" in its request. The default is the default node.

docs.title: Everything else, on demand
docs.text:
The heavier sections run as an explore run. These sections are stl, stationarity, ccf, acf_pacf, vif and groups. All sections with other options also run as an explore run:

api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/explore" -d '{
  "sections": ["stationarity", "stl", "ccf", "vif"],
  "kpi": "revenue",
  "facet_by": ["geo"],
  "max_lag": 12,
  "prewhiten": true
}'

The answer (202) is an Exploration with the run. Poll GET /v1/explorations/{run_id}. When the state is done, it holds the index and a signed link for each view. If you ask again with the same request, the platform answers 200 from the last run. Thus, after the platform calculates the explorers one time, they are instant.

Option Default Meaning sections all 22 The sections to calculate vars each numeric variable The variables to include kpi the target variable The result that the cross-correlations use time_dim the time dim of the schema The dimension that "over time" means facet_by none (each series) A maximum of two dims that split the series. For spend, media and the target, the platform adds the other dims. For all other variables, it calculates the average. group_by the first categorical dim The dim that groups compares max_lag 26 The lags for ACF/PACF and cross-correlations period from the frequency (52 weekly, 12 monthly, 7 daily) The season length for STL alpha 0.05 The significance level of the tests correlation pearson Or spearman outliers, outlier_threshold mad, 3.5 The robust score (mad, iqr or zscore, all on a standard-normal scale) and its threshold prewhiten true Filter the two series with the own AR model of the driver before the cross-correlation. To see the raw correlations, turn it off. max_series 50 The number of series in each view. The platform counts the other series as omitted. hints none Corrections to the structure that the explorer finds. Refer to Correct the structure.

docs.title: The sections
docs.text:
Section What you see Read it like this overview Dims, variables, roles, the fraction of missing values, a summary and a quality score "104 weeks for 3 markets; 2 data problems to look at." distributions For each variable: histogram, mean, spread, skew, quantiles and fraction of zeros Heavy tails or many zeros can need a transform or a different likelihood. timeseries Each variable over time, in facets It is easier to see breaks, level shifts and gaps than to test for them. missingness A heatmap of the fraction of missing values by variable and period, and the longest gap You cannot impute long gaps reliably. outliers Values that are far from the typical value, with their coordinates Are they errors or real events? For real events, add a control variable. correlation The correlation matrix with p-values It is difficult to separate drivers that move almost together. ccf The correlation of each driver with the KPI at each lag. A positive lag means that the driver leads. A peak at lag 2 means that the effect shows two periods later. Prewhitening is on by default. The significance band uses the formula of Bartlett for two autocorrelated series. Thus the platform does not flag two smooth but unrelated series at half of their lags. acf_pacf Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation with the significance band, and suggested AR/MA orders Bars outside the dashed band are more than chance. stationarity ADF and KPSS for each series, with one verdict stable, difference (it wanders: model the changes), trend_stable or unclear (the tests do not agree: look at the plot). stl Trend, season and remainder, with their strengths (0 to 1) If the seasonal strength is more than about 0.6, model the season explicitly. vif The variance inflation for each driver, and the condition number Above 10, the model cannot identify the separate effect of the driver well. groups Each variable across markets or stores, with an ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test Very different groups can need a hierarchical model. quality Warnings in plain language, the most serious first. Each warning has a suggested action. Correct errors before you model. Look at the warnings.

The data.quality governance check also counts the quality warnings (see Validate models with governance policies).

The sections for images, maps, networks, trees, directions and points are in Scientific data.

docs.title: Scientific data
docs.text: The Data Explorer is not only for data over time. It also shows images, fields on a grid, profiles and spectra, maps of areas, networks, trees, directions, times of day and points. The datasets of the pymc-challenges tutorials are examples of each shape. Each tutorial has a step "Explore the data" that tells you what to look at.

docs.title: How the explorer finds the structure
docs.text:
The runner finds the structure from the dims, the coords, the roles and the units of each variable. You do not give settings. For each dataset, and for each node of a tree dataset, the runner finds one or more shapes. The section Structure shows the shapes, the role of each dim and how the explorer uses each variable. The overview shows each shape as a link to its section.

Shape The explorer finds it when Example Section Image or field A variable has two spatial dims: row and col, y and x, lat and lon, also with a prefix or a suffix (y_cm, psf_row). Another dim of the variable gives the frames. Dims with other names are an image only when the data has no time dim and no media, spend or control variables, the two dims have 8 or more levels, and one dim is not more than 4 times longer than the other. E07 quakes on quarter, row and col: one frame for each quarter Images and fields Vector field An image has a dim of two components (x and y, or u and v) E60 displacement Images and fields Profile or spectrum A variable is on a numeric dim with five or more values that is not time E50 cells along position, one line for each hour. E79 reference_dl along multipole. Profiles and spectra Map of areas The variables ring_x and ring_y on (area, vertex) give the border of each area. A variable on (area, area_) gives the neighbours. E18, 56 districts Map Network A numeric variable is on two dims of the same size, X and X_ E21 cowork on lawyer and lawyer_ Network Tree An integer variable parent gives the parent of each node (−1 for the root) E23, 452 nodes and 186 species Tree Directions and times of day The units of a variable are degrees or radians, or the variable has the attribute circular. For hours, days and months, the name must also tell the time of day or the day of the year (hour_lst, clock_time, day_of_year). A duration (hours_open), a temperature, a latitude and a longitude are not directions. E81 wind_from (deg), clock_time (h) Directions and times of day Points Two numeric variables on one dim that is not time have names of positions: col, lon or easting and row, lat or northing, also with a prefix such as wcs_. For the names x and y (also pos_x or x_km), the values must be integers, the units must be a length or degrees, or the dim must name points (site, station). A target, media, spend or a control is never a position. E77 the 330 colour chips at wcs_col and wcs_row Points Table A numeric variable is on (item, column), with 64 columns or fewer and 30 items or more E19 level on cell and protein Correlations (one column for each protein) Time series A dim has kind: time in the schema, or its coords are dates. Also a dim with policy: extend and numbers that increase, when its name is week, day, month, quarter, year, date, period or time. A weekly panel Over time and the time patterns Sequence A dim has policy: extend, and its coords are numbers that increase. A list of ids (coords 0 to n−1 or 1 to n) is a sequence only when its name tells a step in time (step, t), or media or spend change along it. E61 t, E24 step Over time

Some variables are not data. The explorer uses them to draw the pictures, but it does not use them in the statistics (distributions, unusual values, correlations and quality):

  • Geometry: ring_x, ring_y and the neighbour matrix of a map, parent, branch_length, is_tip and tip_label of a tree, and the positions of points (wcs_row, wcs_col). The empty values (NaN) at the end of a border are not missing values.
  • Masks (the role mask). The images show a mask as a layer on the image.
  • Weights (the role weight) are images of their own.

docs.title: The sections for scientific data
docs.text:
Section What you see Read it like this structure (Structure) The shapes. A matrix of the variables and the dims, with the role of each dim (time, frame, y, x, area, node and other roles) and its size. How the explorer uses each variable: data, geometry, mask, weight, index or label. The section that shows each shape. "2 images of 81 x 81 pixels and 1 of 31 x 31 pixels." If the explorer reads a dim incorrectly, correct the structure. images (Images and fields) Each image in the field viewer, with a colour bar, a frame slider and the value of the cell below the pointer. A vector field shows the magnitude and arrows. A mask shows as a layer. For each variable: the mean, the spread, the minimum and the maximum of each frame on a line, a histogram of all cells, and the fraction of missing and saturated cells. For a label coord on the frames (E31 label), the mean image of each class. When a few cells are much brighter than the others (E58), the colours cover 98% of the values. Select Colours for the full range to use the colours for all the values. Look for frames that are not the same as the others, and for many cells at the maximum value (a saturated detector). A colour map with two colours (blue and red) shows values on the two sides of zero. gallery (Gallery, v0.14) Thumbnails of the images of one variable (a maximum of 64 pixels on each side), with chips for each label and split, and the number of images for each value. See Gallery. Look for images with the wrong label, empty images and classes with few images. profiles (Profiles and spectra) One line for each frame along the axis (position, multipole, wavelength or frequency), with the peak of each line. A picker selects the frame. The axes are logarithmic when the values cover a large range. A peak that moves from frame to frame shows a front or a wave (E50). map (Map) Each variable in colour on the areas, and the lines between neighbours. When the data has a target and an exposure, the map also shows their ratio (E18: cases / expected), and the map starts with this ratio. The areas with no neighbour. Moran's I for each variable, with a p-value from 999 permutations. A positive Moran's I with a small p-value shows that neighbour areas have similar values. Then a spatial model (ICAR or BYM2) is useful. For a variable with frames (one value for each area and year), Moran's I uses the mean of each area over the frames. network (Network) The matrix of ties, with similar nodes next to each other (140 nodes or fewer). A node-link graph of the nodes and the edges. A histogram of the degree of the nodes. The density, the transitivity, the reciprocity (directed networks) and the components. For each attribute of the nodes, the fraction of ties in the same group. Blocks on the diagonal of the matrix show groups. If the fraction of ties in the same group is much more than the expected fraction, the attribute explains the ties (homophily). tree (Tree) The tree, with the traits of the tips next to it. A trait with positive values that go across two orders of magnitude or more has a logarithmic axis. The number of nodes and of tips, the depth, and if all tips are at the same distance from the root. How the explorer matched the tips to the traits: by label, by count or by sequence. The phylogenetic signal of each trait (Moran's I with the inverse distance on the tree, 999 permutations). A small p-value shows that near species have similar traits. Then a model that uses the tree is necessary (E23). circular (Directions and times of day) A rose for each group, with the mean direction as a line of length R. The circular spread and the Rayleigh test. For two circular variables on one dim (E81 the hour and the wind direction), a heat map of the two and their circular correlation. A small Rayleigh p-value shows a preferred direction or time. R near 1 shows values near one direction. R near 0 shows values in all directions, or in opposite directions. points (Points) The points, or the cells of a lattice. A picker sets the colour: the colour of a CIE Lab triple, the most frequent answer, the agreement of the answers, or a numeric variable. For points that are not on a lattice, the Clark-Evans R. R less than 1 shows clusters. R more than 1 shows points at regular distances. For E77, the agreement shows where the speakers do not agree on the name of a colour.

In Expert mode, All series also shows the export plots of the science plot recipes: the map (sci.area_map), the network (net.graph) and the roses (sci.rose). These plots are Plotly plots. The other export plots are Vega-Lite plots.

docs.title: Gallery and colour images v0.14
docs.text:
The Gallery section shows small pictures (thumbnails) of the images of a dataset, for example a dataset from an image folder upload. It applies when a variable is an image with a frame dim of 2 or more levels, for example pixels on image, y, x and channel.

  • Each thumbnail is a maximum of 64 pixels on each side. The platform uses the mean of blocks of pixels for larger images. For images with numbers that are not 0 to 255, the platform uses the minimum and the maximum of each image.
  • The chips above the gallery are the facets: the variables and coordinates on the image dim with 2 to 64 values, for example label and split (a maximum of 8). Each chip shows the number of images. Click a chip to show only these images.
  • When the dataset has more than 240 images, the gallery shows a sample. The sample has the same number of images from each label and split, where possible. A note tells you the number of images that the gallery shows.
  • The gallery shows 48 thumbnails on each page. Click a thumbnail to see a larger picture and its values. The values come from your data. The app shows them as text only.

Colour images. When the channel dim of an image has 3 or 4 levels, or the levels r, g and b (red, green and blue), Images and fields shows the image in colour. A fourth channel (alpha) is not used. The statistics and the histogram use the brightness (0.299 r + 0.587 g + 0.114 b). The mean image of each class is also in colour. A label variable on the frames (for example label on image) gives the classes, as a label coordinate does.

docs.title: The time sections on scientific data
docs.text:
The explorer uses the time sections only when the data has a real time dim:

  • A dim is time only when the schema gives kind: time, or when its coords are dates.
  • A dim with policy: extend and coords that are numbers that increase is time when its name is a calendar word (week, month, quarter, year, day, date, period, time). Else it is a sequence.
  • A list of ids (coords 0 to n−1 or 1 to n) with policy: extend is a sequence only when its name tells a step in time (step, t), or media or spend change along it. A list of observations (report in E81, record in E81b) is never time.
  • Over time shows a time or a sequence dim. For an image with frames in time, the explorer adds (or averages) all cells of each frame to make one series. It does not make a series for each cell. E07 gives one series: the earthquakes in all cells for each quarter.
  • Memory (ACF/PACF), Stable or wandering, Trend and season and Leads and lags need a time dim and 16 periods or more in each series.
  • Group comparison compares only real groups: a categorical dim with 2 to 50 levels, or a variable that gives a group (an index with index_of, or an integer variable with 12 values or fewer). It never compares rows of pixels, cells, nodes or ids.
  • Correlations, Distributions and Unusual values use the dim with the most data variables. For E23, these sections use the traits brain, body and group_size of the species, not the tree. For E19, the correlations use the 11 proteins as columns.
  • Missing values without a time dim shows the frames of an image, or the units of the data (areas, species, nodes).
  • Unusual values and the OUTLIERS check of Data quality do not use an indicator: a variable with the values 0 and 1 (for example the ties of a network), or with two values that each occur in 5 % of the rows or more. One spike in a constant series is an unusual value. They also do not use a profile or a spectrum (E79 reference_dl): each value is a point of a curve, thus the peak is not an unusual value.
  • Data quality does not give SHORT_HISTORY for data without a time dim. It has these new warnings:
    • GEOMETRY_INVALID: an area without a border, or a border that is not closed.
    • TREE_INVALID: a cycle, more than one root, or a negative branch length.
    • NETWORK_ASYMMETRIC (information): the ties have a direction.
    • ANGLE_RANGE: values out of the period.
    • IMAGE_SATURATED: 1 % of the cells or more are at the maximum value of a detector. The check looks only at measured values with 32 or more different values. The maximum must be a detector limit (1.0, 255, 4095), or many more cells must be at the maximum than just below it. A setting, such as the power of a heater, does not get this warning.

A change for data with policy: extend

In earlier releases, the explorer used each dim with policy: extend as time. Now a list of ids (coords 0 to n−1, or no coords) is not time, except for the names in the list above. A week dim of an MMM panel with the numbers 1 to 104 continues to be time.

If your data uses a list of ids as time, give time_dim in the request.

docs.title: The Tree section and tree datasets
docs.text: The section Tree shows a tree that is in the data, for example the variables parent and branch_length of a phylogeny. A tree dataset is a different thing: it is a dataset with nodes (HDF5 groups), and the node picker (?node=) selects one node. The explorer finds the shapes of each node of a tree dataset separately.

docs.title: Correct the structure: hints
docs.text:
If the explorer reads a dim or a variable incorrectly, give hints. In the web app, open Explore with options (Expert mode) and set the fields under Shape of the data (hints). Through the API, give the field hints of the request:

api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/explore" -d '{
  "hints": {
    "y_dim": "lat",
    "x_dim": "lon",
    "frame_dim": "month",
    "angle_vars": {"heading": "deg"}
  }
}'
Hint Meaning y_dim, x_dim The two dims of the image. Give the two hints together. frame_dim The dim that gives the frames of the images node_dim The dim of the nodes of a network angle_vars Variables that are angles or times, with their units: deg, rad, h (hour of the day), d (day of the year) or month time_dim The dim that is time. If the request also has time_dim, the two values must be the same.

A hint changes only the variable or the dim that it names. The other rules stay the same.

docs.title: Dataset About
docs.text:
GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/about describes the latest version in plain words. It uses the schema and the coordinates of the version ("Weekly data from 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-29 (104 weeks) for 10 markets …"). The response also shows the own description of the owner. PATCH changes that description:

api -X PATCH "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/about" \
  -d '{"description_user": "Weekly media spend and revenue from the finance warehouse."}'

In the web app, the dataset page and the Data Explorer show the two descriptions next to each other (About this dataset). Editors change the description on the page with Edit.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Views have limits. The maximums are 200 series in each view, 5,000 points in each series, 256 variables and 200 lags. The platform thins longer series evenly and flags them downsampled.

  • The picture sections also have limits:

    View Maximum Images and fields 8 images, 160 × 160 cells in each frame (for a larger image, the platform shows the mean of blocks of cells), 24 frames, 1,000,000 cells in the view. The statistics of each frame cover up to 5,000 frames. The histogram uses an even sample of up to 5,000,000 cells. The mean image of each class covers up to 12 classes. The ingest does not calculate this section when the images have more than 50,000,000 cells: click Run the deeper checks to calculate it. Profiles and spectra 60 lines in each profile, 5,000 points in each line Map 2,000 areas, 20,000 border points in all (the platform keeps each k-th point of a border, and the first and the last point), 20,000 neighbour lines Network 300 nodes in the node-link graph (the nodes with the highest degree), 140 nodes in the matrix, 3,000 edges (the strongest) Tree 5,000 nodes. The phylogenetic signal uses up to 1,000 tips. Directions and times of day 72 bins, 12 groups Points 5,000 points (an even sample). Above this number, the view also has a 64 × 64 grid of counts. Gallery 240 thumbnails of a maximum of 64 × 64 pixels, 8 facets with a maximum of 64 values each (the other values are counted as (other)) - The statistical tests come from statsmodels and scipy. The test suite validates them against their reference outputs. - Strings in views come from your data. Render them only as text.

docs.title: Deep learning v0.15
docs.text:
The mapi-jax package adds neural networks to the platform. The networks use JAX, Flax (the nnx API) and Optax. They train in the same sandboxed runs as the other models. They give draws, so the scorecard, the plots and the comparisons work as for a Bayesian model.

Model or step Use it for dl.mlp A value or a class for each row of a table dl.cnn_classifier The class of each image, trained from the start dl.finetune_classifier The class of each image, from a pretrained network dl.embed (step) Image features from a pretrained network, for a scikit-learn or a Bayesian head See also Image data Image collections: large image sets for the networks Track metrics, params and tags The metrics and media that the training logs Spec format fit.checkpoint.every_epochs, data.collection, the GPU class Model catalog The settings of each model

docs.title: Choose a model
docs.text:
Use the table to select a model:

Your data Labels Model A table with thousands of rows A number or a class dl.mlp Up to a few thousand small images A class tabular.image_logistic, or dl.embed and a head Thousands of images or more A class dl.cnn_classifier Images, and a network that learned on similar images A class dl.finetune_classifier

For a few hundred rows, a neural network is not better than a regression or a tree model. See Choosing a model.

docs.title: Train an image classifier
docs.text:
1. Upload the images as an image collection, or as an image folder for a few thousand small images.

  2. Write a spec with dl.cnn_classifier:

    apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: products, project: default}
data:
  dataset: dataset://default/product_photos@v5
  split: {kind: column, dim: image, column: split, holdout: [test]}
model:
  use: dl.cnn_classifier@1
  settings:
    image_size: [64, 64]
    widths: [32, 64, 128]
    blocks: [2, 2, 2]
    augment: {flip_x: true, crop_pad: 4, brightness: 0.1}
    train:
      epochs: 30
      batch_size: 128
      learning_rate: 0.001
      early_stopping: {monitor: val_loss, patience: 5}
  fit:
    seed: 7
    checkpoint: {every_epochs: 2}
evaluate:
  metrics: [accuracy, accuracy_naive, log_score, brier]
execution: {resource_class: GPU, timeout: 6h}

  3. Submit the spec. Open the run and look at the Metrics tab while the network trains.

A collection dataset takes no pipeline steps. Put augmentation in the augment setting of the model. The split of a collection must be a row split: column, stratified or leave_group_out.

docs.title: Settings of the image models
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning pixels, target, image_dim pixels, label, image The names in the dataset image_size the size of the collection The height and width that the network reads. Necessary when the images have different sizes and the collection has no size. mode auto gray, rgb or auto (the mode of the collection) widths [16, 32, 64] The channels of each stage of the network blocks [1, 1, 1] The residual blocks of each stage groups 8 The maximum number of GroupNorm groups stem_stride 1 The stride of the first convolution (1 or 2). Use 2 for large images. dropout 0.1 The dropout rate before the last layer normalize unit unit (pixels / 255) or standardize (the mean and the standard deviation of the training images) augment none The random changes to the training images (see below) train see below The training settings uncertainty Laplace How the model makes draws (see Draws) class_order sorted labels The classes in a fixed sequence

augment changes each training image at random. The validation and the scored images do not change.

Field Default Change flip_x, flip_y false Turn the image left to right, or top to bottom rotate90 false Turn the image by 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees crop_pad 0 Add this number of edge pixels, then cut a random part of the original size (0 to 64) brightness, contrast 0 The maximum change (0 to 1) noise 0 The standard deviation of random noise, in units of 0 to 1 (a maximum of 0.5)

docs.title: Training settings
docs.text:
All dl models use the same train block:

Field Default Meaning epochs 20 The maximum number of passes through the training data (1 to 10 000) batch_size 64 Rows or images in each step optimizer adamw adamw, adam or sgd learning_rate 0.001 The step size weight_decay 0.0001 The weight decay of adamw schedule warmup_cosine constant, cosine or warmup_cosine warmup_epochs 1.0 The epochs that increase the learning rate from zero grad_clip 1.0 The maximum norm of the gradient (none: no limit) label_smoothing 0 Classification only val_fraction 0.1 The share of the training rows for validation, stratified by class val_split_value val If the data has a split coordinate, the rows with this value are the validation data early_stopping on See Stop early log_every_steps automatic How often the training logs the batch metrics (about 1000 points for each run) eval_every_epochs 1 How often the training calculates the validation metrics media_every_epochs automatic How often the training logs images (a maximum of 20 times) max_steps none Stop after this number of steps

Note

The validation data is a part of the training rows of the spec split. The holdout of data.split stays for the evaluation of the scorecard. The network never sees it during the training.

docs.title: Read the training
docs.text:
The training logs metrics with the label split. The Metrics tab of the run shows one line for each split:

Metric Labels When loss split=train Every log_every_steps steps (the batch value) loss split=val At the end of each evaluation epoch accuracy (classification), rmse and mae (regression) split=train, split=val As loss lr, grad_norm none With the batch metrics epoch none At the end of each epoch

At the end of each epoch, the Logs tab shows one line with the fields epoch, train_loss, val_loss and images_per_second. The speed is not a metric, because it changes from one fit to a different fit with the same seed.

The run also logs the params dl.arch.*, dl.train.*, dl.backend (cpu or gpu), dl.device and dl.parameters (the number of weights).

The Media tab shows two images at a maximum of 20 epochs:

  • val_predictions: up to 16 validation images with the true class and the predicted class.
  • confusion: the confusion matrix of the validation data.

The fit adds three plots to the run:

Plot Shows ml.training_curves The loss and the accuracy (or the error) for the training data and the validation data. The caption gives the best validation value and tells you when the network starts to overfit. ml.confusion_epochs The confusion matrix at up to 6 epochs: the first, some epochs between, the best and the last ml.misclassified Up to 24 validation images that the network classifies incorrectly, from the best epoch

Read Plots for the settings of these plots.

docs.title: Stop early
docs.text:
Early stopping stops the training when the validation metric does not become better. The fit then keeps the weights of the best epoch.

Field Default Meaning monitor val_loss val_loss, val_accuracy or val_rmse patience 5 The number of evaluations without a better value before the training stops min_delta 0 The smallest change that counts as better restore_best true Keep the weights of the best epoch, not of the last epoch

To turn early stopping off, set early_stopping: null.

docs.title: Checkpoints and resume
docs.text:
A long training can save a checkpoint every N epochs. If the run stops (for example, the executor stops the machine), you can resume the run. The new attempt starts from the epoch after the last checkpoint.

  1. Set fit.checkpoint.every_epochs in the spec:

    model:
  fit:
    checkpoint: {every_epochs: 2}

  2. If a run stops with the state partial, open the run and click Resume. From Python, call api.runs.resume(run_id).

A checkpoint holds the weights, the state of the optimizer, the epoch, the early-stopping state and the history of the metrics. The log of the new attempt shows "Resumed from epoch N." A resumed fit gives the same weights as a fit that did not stop.

Samplers use checkpoint.every_draws. A checkpoint has every_draws or every_epochs, not both. If the model cannot save checkpoints, validation shows a warning and the run ignores the setting.

docs.title: Draws
docs.text:
Every dl model gives draws with the dims (chain, draw) (one chain). The uncertainty setting selects how:

method Draws laplace (default) A Laplace approximation of the last layer. The other weights stay at their trained values. mc_dropout Passes through the network with dropout on. Each pass is one draw. none One draw: the trained network Field Default Meaning draws fit.draws, else 100 The number of draws (1 to 1000) hessian auto full or diag. auto uses full when (features + 1) × outputs ≤ 2048. max_rows 20 000 The training rows for the Laplace approximation prior_precision automatic The prior precision of the last layer. Automatic: the value with the largest evidence on a grid from 0.0001 to 10 000.

The draws show how sure the network is about its last layer. They do not include the uncertainty of the other weights. A network trained by gradient descent has no pointwise likelihood, so elpd_loo is not valid for the dl models.

docs.title: Use the GPU class
docs.text:
The resource class GPU gives a run one NVIDIA L4 GPU, 8 vCPU and 32 GiB of memory. Use it for dl.cnn_classifier and dl.finetune_classifier with thousands of images.

execution: {resource_class: GPU, timeout: 6h}
  • Validation refuses the GPU class when the model does not use a GPU. For example, dl.embed in front of a sklearn.* model runs on a CPU class, because the model of the spec sets the image and the class.
  • Validation shows a note when the model can use the GPU but the spec selects a CPU class.
  • The GPU class is not in the retry ladder. After RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, the platform offers the next CPU class only.
  • Quotas: the public and verified tiers stop at class S and class L. Only the internal and the self-hosted tiers can use the GPU class by default. An administrator can change the quota of a tenant.

When no GPU is available, the run uses the CPU. This occurs in local development, with the local-process executor, and with the Docker executor when MAPI_DOCKER_GPUS is not true. The run then shows the warning GPU_UNAVAILABLE: "The run asked for the GPU class, but no GPU is visible. It runs on the CPU." The param dl.backend tells you what the run used.

Warning

The GPU path is not tested. The project has no GPU and no GCP project to test it. The base-dl image and the Cloud Run GPU job are written to the documentation of Docker, NVIDIA and Cloud Run, but they are not verified. Do a test with a small run before you use them. See Cloud Run.

docs.title: Pretrained weights
docs.text:
A sandbox has no internet access. Thus a network cannot download pretrained weights during a run. Upload the weights as a dataset first. Then give the dataset to the model as a side table.

  1. Save the weights as a safetensors file. The tensor names and shapes must match the mapi-jax ResNet layout (backbone.*). Put the architecture in the metadata mapi_arch of the file, or give it with --arch.

  2. Upload the file:

    mapi datasets upload-weights tiny-resnet resnet.safetensors --arch arch.json

    From Python, use the mapping {"format": "safetensors"}:

    from mapi_spec import IngestMapping, WeightsOptions

mapping = IngestMapping(format="safetensors", weights=WeightsOptions())
version = api.datasets.upload("resnet.safetensors", dataset="tiny-resnet", mapping=mapping)

  3. Name the dataset as a side table in the spec:

    data:
  dataset: dataset://default/leaf_photos@v2
  side_tables:
    pretrained: {ref: dataset://default/tiny-resnet@v1, score_policy: pinned}
  split: {kind: stratified, dim: image, by: label, fraction: 0.2, seed: 1}
model:
  use: dl.finetune_classifier@1
  settings:
    pretrained: pretrained
    freeze: none
    head_epochs: 1
    backbone_lr_scale: 0.1
    train: {epochs: 10, learning_rate: 0.0005}

The weights dataset has one variable weights(param) (float32) and the tensor table in its attributes. The ingest reads the file in a sandbox. It refuses a header of more than 8 MiB, tensors that overlap, and more parameters than max_parameters (200 million by default).

Setting of dl.finetune_classifier Default Meaning pretrained pretrained The name of the side table freeze none none trains all weights. backbone trains only the last layer. head_epochs 1 The epochs that train only the last layer before all weights train backbone_lr_scale 0.1 The learning rate of the backbone, as a fraction of learning_rate

Gray images in a network for RGB images use the gray channel three times. A side table that only the model reads is not necessary when you score: the model version keeps the trained weights.

Note

There is no conversion from PyTorch or TensorFlow checkpoints. The weights must use the mapi-jax ResNet layout. mapi_jax.testing.tiny_pretrained() writes a small example file.

docs.title: Image features and a simple head
docs.text:
The step dl.embed changes each image into a short list of numbers (an embedding) with a frozen pretrained network. A simple model after the step then learns the classes. This is fast, and it works with a few hundred labelled images.

With a scikit-learn head:

data:
  dataset: dataset://default/leaf_photos@v2
  side_tables:
    backbone: {ref: dataset://default/tiny-resnet@v1, score_policy: pinned}
  split: {kind: stratified, dim: image, by: label, fraction: 0.25, seed: 3}
pipeline:
  - id: embed
    use: dl.embed@^1
    with: {weights: backbone}
model:
  use: sklearn.multiclass_classifier@1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: sklearn.LogisticRegression}
    target: label
    rows: [image]
    time_kind: none

With a Bayesian head, use tabular.image_logistic with the features input:

model:
  use: tabular.image_logistic@^1.1
  settings: {input: features, pixels: embedding}
Setting of dl.embed Default Meaning pixels pixels The pixel variable weights weights The name of the side table with the weights out embedding The name of the new variable embedding(image, feature) feature_dim feature The name of the feature dimension image_dim image The image dimension size the network size The height and width that the network reads batch_size 64 Images in each batch keep_pixels false Keep the pixel variable after the step

The step runs in the image of the head model, on the CPU. A collection dataset takes no pipeline steps. For a collection, set data.collection to read a sample of the images, or use dl.finetune_classifier with freeze: backbone for all images.

docs.title: Tables: dl.mlp
docs.text:
dl.mlp is a small neural network for tables. It reads number variables along the row dims of the target. It standardises them with the mean and the standard deviation of the training rows.

model:
  use: dl.mlp@1
  settings:
    target: delivery_hours
    rows: [order]
    features: [distance_km, weight_kg, hour]
    task: regression
    hidden: [64, 64]
    train: {epochs: 50, batch_size: 256}
Setting Default Meaning target y The target variable rows necessary The dims of one row (1 to 8), for example [order] or [store, week] target_dtype float64 The type of the target: float64 (numbers), str or int64 (class labels) features all number variables The variables that explain the target (a maximum of 256 variables and 4096 columns) task auto regression, classification or auto (text and integer labels are classes) new_levels pooled What to do with new row levels when you score: pooled, zero or error hidden [64, 64] The width of each hidden layer dropout 0.1 The dropout rate class_order sorted labels The classes in a fixed sequence train, uncertainty As for the image models

A regression gives y_hat(chain, draw, row dims). For the kind predictive, the draws add noise with the residual variance of the training. A classification gives y_hat(chain, draw, row dims, class) with the probability of each class.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text:
A fit with the same seed, the same data and the same image gives the same weights on the CPU:

  • The network, the dropout, the validation split and the order of the batches use the seed of fit.seed.
  • The loader gives each image its random changes from the seed, the epoch and the position of the image. The number of threads does not change the result.
  • All batches have the same shape, so the network compiles one time.

On a GPU, some operations can give small differences between runs. The base-dl image sets XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true to decrease them. This is not verified.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The GPU path (the base-dl CUDA image and the Cloud Run GPU job) is not tested on a GPU or on GCP.
  • One GPU for each run. There is no training on more than one GPU or more than one machine.
  • Pretrained weights must use the mapi-jax ResNet layout. There is no conversion from PyTorch checkpoints.
  • dl.embed on a collection reads only a sample (data.collection). Use dl.finetune_classifier with freeze: backbone for all images.
  • The draws come from the last layer (Laplace) or from dropout. They are approximations.

docs.title: Endpoints and webhooks v0.4
docs.text:
An endpoint gives a model version a stable name, endpoint://<project>/<alias>. Other applications call this name. You can promote a better version, or roll back a bad version, and the applications do not change. A webhook tells another application when an event occurs in a project. For example, a run finished, a model version is ready, or an endpoint changed.

This guide uses curl for endpoints and webhooks. Integrations gives the concepts: the promotion gate, signatures and the SSRF policy. The HTTP API reference lists all the operations.

In the examples, MAPI_TOKEN holds an API token and MAPI_PROJECT holds the <tenant>/<project> for the token. API holds the base URL:

export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
api() { curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: $MAPI_PROJECT" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$@"; }

docs.title: Promote a model version
docs.text:
PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} makes the alias, or points the alias at a different version. Give the version by reference or by id:

api -X PUT "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod" \
  --data '{"model": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3", "expected_revision": 0}'

{
  "alias": "geo-mmm-prod",
  "ref": "endpoint://growth/geo-mmm-prod",
  "model_ref": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3",
  "revision": 1,
  "evaluation_policy": {"fit_mode": "evaluate_then_refit", "schema_change": "block"},
  "gate": {"outcome": "allowed", "scorecard_overall": "pass", "reasons": []},
  "overridden": false
}

expected_revision makes the call safe if a colleague promotes at the same time:

  • 0 means "the alias must be new".
  • N means "the alias must still be at revision N".
  • If the alias does not agree, the answer is 409 CONFLICT.

If you send the same body again, nothing changes.

The promotion gate decides if the version can serve:

The version Answer Its scorecard passes, the fit used evaluate_then_refit, and it takes the input that the callers of the endpoint send Promoted Its scorecard warns, or it has no scorecard. Or it had no score on a holdout (no data.split). Or a check that its guided template asks for did not run (NOT_EVALUATED) 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED, unless a project admin overrides Its scorecard fails, the fit stopped before it finished, or the fit used train_only 409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED It expects different input (for example, a removed dim or a new necessary variable) Blocked by default. The schema_change policy of the endpoint can change this to warn or allow

A less strict evaluation_policy on the endpoint stops the gate, as an override does. For example, schema_change from block to warn or allow, or fit_mode to train_only. Thus only a signed-in project admin can send a less strict policy. An endpoints:promote token gets 403 FORBIDDEN. The token can send the same policy or a stricter policy. The audit event of the promotion records the policy before and after.

Each refusal gives the reasons of the gate in the errors of the problem. Each reason has the scorecard check that caused it:

{
  "code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED",
  "status": 409,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED", "severity": "warning",
     "message": "Holdout error: The forecast error on the holdout periods was 14%.",
     "context": {"gate_code": "SCORECARD_WARN", "check": "holdout.mape"}}
  ]
}

Evaluated, then refitted. An endpoint serves versions with a fit that evaluated the holdout and then fitted again on all the data. This is fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, the default of all specs. Thus forecasts start from the full history. The two steps occur in the same fit run. The lineage of the version links the evaluation. To serve an exploration fit, give the endpoint the policy {"fit_mode": "train_only"}.

docs.title: Overriding
docs.text:
An override is a human decision. A signed-in project admin sends override: true with a reason. The admin sends it from the web app or from a session. An API token cannot override, for all scopes:

{"model_version_id": "mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0", "override": true,
 "reason": "Holdout MAPE is high because of the strike in week 41; accepted by the CMO."}

The endpoint history and the audit log (endpoint.promote_override) keep the reason. The reason is next to the checks that warned.

docs.title: History and rollback
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/history"
api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/rollback" \
  --data '{"reason": "v4 over-forecasts after the price change"}'

A rollback points the alias at the version of an earlier revision. By default, this is the last revision that served a different version. to_revision selects a revision. A rollback is a new revision, and the audit log records it with its reason. The gate does not run again. DELETE /v1/endpoints/{alias} removes the alias and its history. The model versions stay.

docs.title: Score an endpoint
docs.text:
Ask the endpoint what it expects. The answer has the input schema from the time of the promotion. It also has an example body that is valid:

api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/schema" | jq .example

{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
 "future_covariates": "carry_last", "output": {"kind": "expected", "summary": ["mean", "hdi_90"]}}

Then score the endpoint. Prefer: wait=60 waits for a maximum of one minute:

  • If the run finished, the answer is 200 with links to the outputs.
  • If the run did not finish, the answer is 202 with the run.

A finished answer also has the numbers in summary. There is one table for each output. The table has the coordinate columns, then one column for each statistic. By default, the statistics are the mean and the 90% HDI. Thus a spreadsheet or a shell script does not need a zarr or Arrow reader. If a result has more than 100,000 cells, the server cuts it (truncated). score.zarr.zip always has all the data.

"summary": {"tables": [{"variable": "revenue",
                        "columns": ["geo", "time", "mean", "hdi_90_lower", "hdi_90_upper"],
                        "rows": [["de", "2026-01-05", 1520.4, 1402.1, 1633.9]]}],
            "truncated": false}

A table of a circular output (an angle, for example a wind direction) has the field period (one turn, for example 360). Its statistics are on the circle: mean is the circular mean, and each interval is centred on it. All values are from 0 to period. An interval with lower more than upper crosses the seam (for example, from 350 to 10 degrees).

api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score" \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H 'Idempotency-Key: plan-2026-11' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last"}'

To get a result that took more time, send the same call again with the same Idempotency-Key. The answer is for the run that the first call started. If you ask, the call waits again. This works with the smallest token, score:<alias>. This token can read and score one endpoint and nothing more.

docs.title: Inline data
docs.text:
data and scenario can be dataset:// references. They can also be small datasets that you send inline as XrJSON. XrJSON has the shape of xr.Dataset.to_dict(), with a maximum of 5 MB each. Thus scripts and spreadsheets do not need an upload.

A caller that cannot read datasets (a score:<alias> token) sends data inline. Or it gives the dataset that the model of the endpoint was fitted on. All other references get the same 403 FORBIDDEN. A reference to a dataset that does not exist also gets 403 FORBIDDEN. Thus such a token cannot score the other datasets of the project. It also cannot find which datasets exist:

{
  "mode": "predict",
  "data": {
    "coords": {
      "market": {"dims": ["market"], "data": ["de"]},
      "channel": {"dims": ["channel"], "data": ["search", "tv"]},
      "date": {"dims": ["date"], "data": ["2025-12-30"]}
    },
    "data_vars": {
      "spend_local": {"dims": ["market", "channel", "date"], "data": [[[1200.0], [5300.0]]]}
    }
  }
}

Before a run starts, the server checks the payload against the input contract of the endpoint:

  • Each variable must be a variable that the endpoint takes, with its dims.
  • Coordinates must be dims of the input.
  • A predict call must send all the inputs.

Then the server does the usual coordinate checks: modes, horizon, unseen levels and future covariates. For these checks, it reads only the coordinates of the payload. The sandboxed score run decodes the values. The API never decodes them. The score run gives each coordinate the type of the dim of the model. Dates arrive as ISO strings. Thus an inline payload gives the same score as the same rows in an uploaded dataset.

The input contract (GET …/schema → snapshot.input_schema) uses the dim and variable names that the spec uses after data.bind. For example, if the spec binds time: week and y: revenue, an inline payload sends a time dim, not week. The score run changes the payload names to the names of the dataset before it scores. The results use the names of the dataset, as for all scores. POST …/validate does the same checks and answers 200 with the issues. It does not run anything.

The server refuses bodies of more than 10.25 MB with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. For larger data, upload a dataset and give its reference.

docs.title: Forecasts with your latest actuals
docs.text:
A forecasting endpoint takes two things in one call, without a new fit (Forecasts with actuals):

  • The actuals that arrived after the fit.
  • The dates to forecast.

Send inline data along the time dim. Fill the target on the periods that you have. Leave the target empty (null) on the periods to forecast.

api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/ts-forecast/score" -H 'Prefer: wait=60' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "t", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last",
           "data": {"coords": {"t": {"dims": ["t"], "data": ["1961-01-01", "1961-02-01",
                                     "1961-03-01", "1961-04-01", "1961-05-01"]}},
                    "data_vars": {"y": {"dims": ["t"], "data": [417, 391, 419, null, null]}}}}'

This call updates the model with January to March. It forecasts April and May, the two empty rows. A warning tells you that the server did not use horizon.periods. If you send only the three actuals, the server forecasts the 8 periods after March. The summary.conditioning of the answer tells what occurred. It tells this in fields (conditioned, n_actuals, actuals_through, fit_end, horizon_source, details for each series) and in words (message).

GET …/schema gives the same table for spreadsheets and scripts:

  • input_table lists the columns: the time column first, then the target, the drivers and other inputs. The periods after the fit are empty rows.
  • snapshot.conditions_on_actuals tells if the model can use actuals.
  • actuals_example is a call over those periods that is ready for you to fill.

If a model cannot use actuals, it refuses target values in a forecast with 422 ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. It does not ignore them. For inline data, it refuses before a run starts. Actuals get 422 ACTUALS_INVALID if they have a gap that the model cannot filter. They also get it if they do not have the drivers that were observed with them.

In Python, api.endpoints.forecast("ts-forecast", rows) takes the same table as a DataFrame or a list of rows. You can also give actuals= and future= separately. result.conditioning.message tells what the forecast used. In a terminal, mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv reads the table from a CSV file (The command line). In Google Sheets, the table is the Input sheet (Connect Google Sheets).

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/snippets?language=python&language=curl"

This call gives code that is ready to run for these languages:

  • Python
  • TypeScript
  • curl
  • R
  • Google Sheets (Apps Script)
  • A notebook cell.

The code has the address of this server and the example payload of the endpoint. For a forecasting endpoint, it also has a call over the periods after the fit, for you to fill with actuals. It also has an Apps Script that reads the actuals from an Input sheet. base_url= puts a different address in the code, for example a public address behind a proxy. Snippets read the token from MAPI_TOKEN and never contain a secret.

In Python, Client().endpoint("geo-mmm-prod").score(ds) sends an xr.Dataset and returns an xr.Dataset (The Python client). The CLI has mapi endpoints score. To optimise a budget, use the model version (Optimise a budget).

docs.title: Tokens for integrations
docs.text:
Scope For score:geo-mmm-prod An application that scores this endpoint. It can also read the schema and snippets of the endpoint score:* All endpoints and models of the project endpoints:promote CI that promotes versions that pass and rolls back. It never overrides webhooks:manage A script that manages webhooks

Each call counts against the rate limit of the token (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After). Each score run counts against the vCPU-second budget of the token (429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED). These limits are in addition to the limits of the tenant.

docs.title: Subscribe
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks" \
  --data '{"url": "https://hooks.example.com/mapi",
           "events": ["run.succeeded", "run.failed", "endpoint.promoted"]}'

The answer holds the signing secret, whsec_…. You see it only one time. Keep the secret with the receiver. To manage webhooks, you need the project admin role, or a webhooks:manage token of an admin. The reason is that deliveries show what a project does.

The URL must be https on port 443 or 8443, and it must give a public host. The server resolves the host. It refuses (422 WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED) a host with an internal address. This includes private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses. The server checks again at each delivery. It connects only to the address that it checked. Thus a DNS answer that changes later cannot send a delivery into the platform.

docs.title: What a delivery looks like
docs.text:
POST /mapi HTTP/1.1
Host: hooks.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: mapi-webhooks/1
Mapi-Signature: t=1792000000,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd
Mapi-Event-Id: evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0
Mapi-Event-Type: run.succeeded
Mapi-Webhook-Id: whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0
Mapi-Delivery-Id: whd_01jaf3m1n2p3q4r5s6t7v8w9x0

{"api_version":"v1","created":"2026-10-15T09:30:00Z","data":{"kind":"fit","model_version_id":"mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0","run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"succeeded"},"id":"evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0","project":"growth","tenant":"acme","type":"run.succeeded"}
Event data run.succeeded, run.failed run_id, kind, state, model_version_id. Failures also have failure_class and code model.version.ready model_id, model_version_id, ref, scorecard_overall endpoint.promoted alias, ref, revision, model_version_id, overridden, action (promote or rollback) score.completed run_id, model_version_id, outputs (names), and endpoint (alias, ref, revision) if the score came through an endpoint tenant.deletion.completed deletion_id, requested_at, completed_at

The server records each event in the same database transaction as its cause. Thus the server sends an event only if the event occurred, and always if it occurred. Delivery is at least once. Use Mapi-Event-Id to remove duplicates. Envelopes have ids and states. They never have data, signed URLs or secrets. Use the API to get the results.

No plot attachments. Webhooks do not attach rendered plots. The platform plan had them as an option. A receiver is a third party on the internet. It is frequently a chat or automation service that logs or sends on what it gets. Thus a chart in the body, or a signed link to a chart, would publish model results outside the project.
