docs.title: Bonus: a preprocessing step
docs.text:
Steps use the same pattern. A step has settings, an optional state, fit / transform / inverse, and a static effect_template. The effect_template tells the control plane how the schema changes.

from typing import ClassVar

from mapi_sdk import Step, StepContext, StepSettings, StepState
from mapi_spec import StepKind
from pydantic import Field, JsonValue


class ScaleSettings(StepSettings):
    vars: list[str]
    over: list[str] = Field(default=[])  # plain defaults: the exported JSON Schema keeps them
    unseen_levels: str = "error"  # error | pooled | fill: what a new level's scale becomes
    fill_value: float = 1.0  # the scale used by 'fill'


class ScaleStep(Step[ScaleSettings, StepState]):
    """Divide each variable by its mean absolute value over `over` (learned on train)."""

    id = "acme.scale"
    version = "1.0.0"
    kind = StepKind.VALUE
    Settings = ScaleSettings
    State = StepState  # stateful: fitted on the training data only
    invertible = True
    var_params = ("vars",)  # settings that name variables ...
    dim_params = ("over",)  # ... and dims, so the control plane can check them
    unseen_levels_param = "unseen_levels"
    effect_template: ClassVar[dict[str, JsonValue]] = {  # static: how the schema changes
        "template_params": ["vars"],
        "updates": {"{*vars as v}": {"units": "1"}},
    }
    summary = "Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims"  # catalog and UI text
    summary_plain = "Puts each series on a comparable scale"

    def fit(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, ctx: StepContext) -> StepState:
        return StepState(arrays=xr.Dataset({f"scale__{v}": abs(ds[v]).mean(s.over) for v in s.vars}))

    def _scale(self, v: str, ds: xr.Dataset, s: ScaleSettings, st: StepState, ctx: StepContext):
        state = st.array(f"scale__{v}")
        return ctx.align_state(state, ds, s.unseen_levels, fill_value=s.fill_value)

    def transform(self, ds, s, st, ctx):  # never learns; skips absent vars (the target at score)
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] / self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

    def inverse(self, ds, s, st, ctx):
        return ds.assign({v: ds[v] * self._scale(v, ds, s, st, ctx) for v in s.vars if v in ds})

from mapi_sdk import infer_schema
from mapi_sdk.testing import check_step

report = check_step(
    ScaleStep,
    data,
    {"vars": ["spend"], "over": ["time"], "unseen_levels": "pooled"},
    schema=infer_schema(data, targets=["y"]),
)
print(report.summary())
# contract kit: step acme.scale@1.0.0
#   [PASS] catalog_entry: exported acme.scale@1.0.0
#   [PASS] transform_never_learns: ...
#   ...

The step kit does a check of these items:

  • The exported catalog entry
  • A deterministic and pure fit
  • That transform never learns
  • The bundle round trip of the state
  • That the declared schema effect agrees with the real output
  • That the step accepts a missing target
  • The inverse round trip
  • The equivalence of the context window for steps that look back
  • Each policy for unseen levels

For more information, see Write a step or model plugin.

docs.title: Ship it
docs.text:
Register your plugins through entry points in the pyproject.toml of your package. The value can be a class, a tuple of classes or a function that returns them:

[project.entry-points."mapi.models"]
acme = "acme_models.plugins:PLUGINS"      # PLUGINS = (Radon, GeoBaseline)

[project.entry-points."mapi.steps"]
acme = "acme_models.steps:STEPS"          # STEPS = (ScaleStep,)

mapi_sdk.default_registry() then finds them. The runner images of the platform also find them.

Checklist

  • schema_template in canonical names, with correct dim policies
  • capabilities: representation, score modes, contribution scale
  • outputs with units_of, so that the results come back in the units of the user
  • grid on outputs that are images or maps, and circular: true (with a period attribute) on outputs that are angles
  • score_modes that list only the modes that score can do
  • rules that join settings in a model_validator, not in fit
  • a log_likelihood group if users compare variants by elpd_loo, or loo_valid=False with a reason
  • settings as a ModelSettings subclass with defaults and descriptions (they become the form in the UI)
  • a tiny spec, and check_model passes in CI
  • no pickle: native artifacts as skops, xgboost JSON or safetensors

For the full guides with examples, see PyMC, scikit-learn and xgboost and steps and custom models.

docs.title: Bring a PyMC model
docs.text:
With mapi_pymc.PyMCModel, you write one method, build(). It returns a pm.Model. The platform does the rest of the work:

  • It fits the model with the engine that the spec names.
  • It keeps the ArviZ groups that you ask for.
  • It changes the convergence checks into scorecard items.
  • It predicts on new data, because it builds your model again: new geos, forecast horizons and counterfactual scenarios.

You never work with coordinates, pm.set_data or the records of the posterior.

docs.title: A hierarchical model in 30 lines
docs.text:
This example is the classic radon model (intercepts that change by county) in the long layout. Each obs row has a county_idx that points into the county coordinate.

from typing import Any, ClassVar

import pymc as pm
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc import BuildContext, PyMCModel
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA  # dims obs (extend) + county (new_levels)
from mapi_sdk import ModelSettings
from mapi_spec import Capabilities, Representation
from pydantic import Field


class RadonSettings(ModelSettings):
    beta_sigma: float = Field(1.0, gt=0)


class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    """log radon ~ Normal(a[county] + b * floor, sigma), with partially pooled a."""

    id = "acme.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    capabilities = Capabilities(
        inference="mcmc",
        representation=Representation.DRAWS,
        score_modes=frozenset({"predict", "counterfactual", "evaluate"}),
    )
    schema_template = RADON_SCHEMA
    outputs: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected: ClassVar[dict[str, str]] = {"y": "mu"}  # output -> Deterministic for E[y]
    pad_extend = False  # long layout: no positional time axis

    def build(self, ds: xr.Dataset, s: RadonSettings, ctx: BuildContext) -> pm.Model:
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as model:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")  # new counties come from the hyperprior
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0.0, s.beta_sigma)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            sigma = pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1.0)
            pm.Normal("y", mu, sigma, observed=ctx.observed("y"), dims="obs")
        return model

mapi_pymc.examples.RadonModel is a version that you can run, with synthetic data.

docs.title: What the ctx helpers do
docs.text:
Helper At fit At score ctx.coords() The labels of the data Adds <dim>__fit and <dim>__new when unseen levels come in ctx.data(name) pm.Data over the training values pm.Data over the score values (the platform builds the model again) ctx.observed(name) The target A zero placeholder of the correct shape (never imputed) ctx.hier_effect(name, dim) name ~ Normal(mu, sigma) over dim (non-centred by default) The fit levels from the posterior, then name__new for unseen levels ctx.position(dim) 0, 1, 2, … along an extend dim The same positions, continued into the horizon ctx.anticipated_coords The fit labels and max_extension future labels The same

The new_level_strategy of the dim controls new levels:

  • hyperprior: each posterior draw gets a new level mu + sigma * z from the fitted hyperprior. The noise z stays the same for each seed. Thus, if you score two times, you get the same answer.
  • pooled: the population mean mu.
  • zero: 0.
  • error: the platform rejects the request with UNSEEN_LEVELS.

Your model can use a new_levels dim as the index of a plain parameter (pm.Normal("a", dims="county")). If you then score a new county, the score fails with a clear UNSEEN_LEVELS error. The error tells you to use ctx.hier_effect.

docs.title: Choosing an engine
docs.text:
Set model.fit.engine in the spec:

Engine What you get nutpie (default) Fast NUTS with parallel chains. A seed does not make the result the same bit for bit. pymc The NUTS of PyMC. A seed makes the result the same. It has segmented sampling. map pm.find_MAP: one point (1 chain, 1 draw). advi Mean-field ADVI. tune is the number of optimization steps (default 10,000). pathfinder Pathfinder from pymc-extras (one chain). Install the extra mapi-pymc[pathfinder]. The runner images mapi/base-bayes and mapi/base-forecast have it. Without the extra, the fit stops with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. numpyro, blackjax The JAX bridges of PyMC, if the image has them. 
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit:
    engine: pymc
    tune: 1000
    draws: 2000
    chains: 4
    seed: 20261014
    checkpoint: {every_draws: 500}      # segmented sampling
    keep: {log_likelihood: true, posterior_predictive: {thin: 4}}
    prior_predictive: {draws: 500}

You can add these optional groups:

  • prior and prior_predictive (prior_predictive: {draws: N})
  • log_likelihood, which LOO and WAIC need
  • A thinned posterior_predictive

The bundle always contains posterior, sample_stats, observed_data and constant_data.

To get elpd_loo, keep the log-likelihood (keep: {log_likelihood: true}) and list elpd_loo in evaluate.metrics. The fit then also keeps the pointwise values in MetricsReport.elpd, for data of up to 10,000 points. The workflow node compare.stacking uses these values to calculate stacking weights. If LOO is not correct for your model (for example, all observations share one latent field), declare loo_valid=False and the reason in loo_invalid_reason in the Capabilities of the model. The fit then skips elpd_loo with that reason.

docs.title: The loss history of ADVI v0.10
docs.text:
An ADVI fit keeps the loss of each optimization step in the fit_history group of the bundle. The loss is the negative ELBO. A lower value is better. The group has one variable, loss, over the dim step (1 to the number of steps). If the fit has more than 5,000 steps, the group keeps 5,000 evenly spaced steps and the last step. The attr thinned_from then gives the number of steps of the fit.

The fit run adds the plot core.loss_curve to each fit that has this group. The plot shows the raw loss and a moving average. If the moving average still goes down by more than 1% over the last 10% of the steps, the caption tells you so. Then increase tune and fit again.

map and pathfinder do not keep a loss history.

From v0.11, ADVI also sends the loss to the run while it optimises. The run gets the metric loss with the optimisation step as its step. For a fit of more than 5,000 steps, it sends each k-th step, k = ceil(steps / 5000), and the last step. The Metrics tab of the run page shows the curve while the fit runs.

docs.title: Live chains and step metrics v0.11
docs.text:
While nutpie or the PyMC NUTS sampler makes draws, the fit sends the progress of each chain to the run. The run page shows one lane for each chain, with its draws, divergences and step size. The fit also logs these step metrics, with the label chain:

Engine Keys Step nutpie step_size, num_steps (leapfrog steps of the latest draw), divergences (cumulative) The draws that the chain finished, with tuning (starts at 1) pymc (NUTS) step_size, tree_depth, num_steps, divergences (cumulative) The draw index, with tuning (starts at 1). If a chain has more than 5000 draws, each k-th draw and the last draw, k = ceil(n / 5000)

The evaluation fit of evaluate_then_refit adds the label fit=evaluation. Thus its curves do not mix with the curves of the final fit. Its params get the prefix evaluation.. Your model code can log its own metrics, params and tags with ctx (see Track metrics, params and tags). The SDK does not build the step metrics when no tracker records them, for example in a notebook fit without a recorder.

docs.title: Segmented sampling and checkpoints
docs.text:
With engine: pymc and checkpoint.every_draws, the sampler tunes one time. Then it makes the draws in chunks. After each chunk, it writes a checkpoint with three items:

  • The draws until that time
  • The position of each chain
  • The full state of the sampler (step size, mass matrix and random state), encoded as JSON. The sampler never uses pickle.

If a run stops and starts again, it continues from the end of the last chunk. The result is the same as the result of a run that did not stop.

nutpie cannot export its adaptation state. Thus its checkpoints are snapshots. A snapshot contains the draws until that time. This is sufficient for a partial result. But when the run starts again, the sampler starts from the beginning.

Each engine reports the progress of each chain ("chain 2/4: sampling 150/500, 0 divergences").

docs.title: Start every chain at one point
docs.text:
By default, each MCMC chain starts at the initial point of the model with a random jitter. Some posteriors have a trap near that point. An example is a feature model where all the features switch off. For such a model, set two fields of EnginePlan (mapi_pymc):

  • initvals: the start values, by the name of each free variable, on the constrained scale (as pm.sample(initvals=...)).
  • jitter: False starts each chain at exactly that point. The default is True.

engine: pymc, nutpie and the external NUTS bridges (numpyro, blackjax) use the two fields. map, advi and pathfinder ignore them. PyMCModel.fit does not set them. Thus a model that needs a start point builds its pm.Model in a CustomModel and calls run_engine itself, as sci.ibp_features does:

from dataclasses import replace
from mapi_pymc import EngineHooks, EnginePlan, run_engine

plan = EnginePlan.from_config(cfg, default_engine="nutpie", seed=seed)
plan = replace(plan, initvals={"A": a0, "nu": nu0}, jitter=False)
result = run_engine(model, plan, EngineHooks(progress=ctx.progress, cancel=ctx.cancel))
posterior = result.group("posterior")

The convergence checks then need a call of mapi_pymc.convergence_diagnostics in the diagnostics hook of the model (see Write a step or a model plugin).

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
Each MCMC fit adds these items to the sanity scorecard. Each item has a message for experts, a message in plain language and a suggested action:

  • RHAT: the rank-normalised split r̂ is less than 1.01.
  • ESS_BULK and ESS_TAIL: each chain has 100 effective draws or more.
  • DIVERGENCES
  • TREE_DEPTH

docs.title: Expected vs predictive, and counterfactuals
docs.text:
output.kind: expected returns the Deterministic that you named in expected (without observation noise). output.kind: predictive returns draws of the observed variable.

Predictive draws use common random numbers: y = F⁻¹(U). The seed and the cell set the uniforms U, and they do not change. A counterfactual uses mode: counterfactual with interventions. In a counterfactual, the scenario and the baseline thus use the same noise. The delta then shows only the intervention, not two independent noise draws. Some distributions do not have an inverse CDF (Poisson, negative binomial). For these distributions, the platform uses the seeded stream of the sampler. The noise attribute of the output records the method that the platform used.

The governance check recovery.simulated uses these predictive draws. For a Bayesian model with a predict mode, it makes each simulated dataset from one posterior draw and the noise of the model (predict with kind: predictive). Then it fits the model again and finds the values of that draw. If the model gives no predictive draws, or if the draws have the attribute kind: expected, the check adds residuals to the fitted values. If the target holds counts and the model has no predictive draws, the check is skipped. Thus give real predictive draws, also for counts.

docs.title: Fast scoring with a FrozenPredictor
docs.text:
If you declare a FrozenPredictorSpec, the platform can compile one PyTensor function. This function calculates your responses for many inputs and scenarios at the same time. Use it for response curves and what-if grids:

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from mapi_pymc.examples import RADON_SCHEMA, RADON_SPEC_YAML, RadonModel, radon_dataset
from mapi_pymc.testing import check_fast_score
from mapi_sdk import Registry, fit_spec

registry = Registry()
registry.register(RadonModel)  # declares fast_score_spec = FrozenPredictorSpec(
#                                  response_exprs={"y": "mu"}, input_vars=["floor"])
data = radon_dataset()
bundle = fit_spec(RADON_SPEC_YAML, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA)

model = RadonModel()
predictor = model.frozen_predictor(bundle.model, data, num_samples=200, seed=1)
floors = xr.DataArray(
    np.outer([0.0, 0.5, 1.0], np.ones(data.sizes["obs"])),
    dims=["scenario", "obs"],
    coords={"scenario": ["basement", "mixed", "ground floor"]},
)
grid = predictor.predict({"floor": floors})  # one compiled call for every scenario
print(grid["y"].dims)  # ('sample', 'scenario', 'obs')

report = check_fast_score(model, bundle.model, data)  # fast path == exact path within MCSE
print(report.ok)  # True

The contract check mapi_pymc.testing.check_fast_score(plugin, fitted, ds) makes sure that the fast path agrees with the exact scores within the Monte Carlo error.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
Use the contract kit of the SDK:

from mapi_pymc.examples import radon_dataset
from mapi_sdk import Registry
from mapi_sdk.testing import ModelFixture, check_model

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: radon, project: demo}
data: {dataset: dataset://demo/radon@latest}
model:
  use: acme.radon@^1
  fit: {mode: train_only, engine: pymc, tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, seed: 3}
"""
report = check_model(
    Radon, ModelFixture(spec=SPEC, data=radon_dataset(), raw_schema=RADON_SCHEMA, registry=Registry())
)
print(report.summary())

Keep the test fits very small (tune: 100, draws: 100, chains: 2, engine: pymc). Then the tests are fast and give the same result each time.

docs.title: The Python client v0.2
docs.text:
mapi-client (mapi_client, Apache-2.0) is a typed client for the /v1 HTTP API. It uses httpx. Each request and each response is a Pydantic model from mapi_spec.api. The server uses the same models. Thus, if a field name has a typo, your editor shows the error before production. Errors come back as mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses with the stable error code of the server.

The mapi CLI, make seed and the end-to-end tests use this client. This page shows one script, docs/snippets/client_tour.py. make e2e runs this script against a live stack. The outputs on this page come from that script. Some outputs are shorter than the real outputs.

uv add mapi-client              # or, for xr.Dataset uploads and xr.DataTree results:
uv add "mapi-client[xarray]"

The workspace already has the two packages. The examples need a live stack and the demo files:

  1. Run make dev.
  2. Run uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_API_URL, a profile, or http://127.0.0.1:8000
health = api.ready()
print(api.config.base_url, health.status, health.version)

http://127.0.0.1:8000 ok 0.15.0

Client() finds its settings in the same sequence as the CLI:

  1. The arguments (Client("http://…", token=…, project=…)).
  2. MAPI_URL (or MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN, MAPI_PROJECT and MAPI_PROFILE.
  3. A profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml.
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.

api.config.sources tells where each value came from. Use the client as a context manager (with Client() as api:), or call close().

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
versions = {}
for name in ("eu_media_daily", "fx_daily", "holidays_eu", "eu_media_future"):
    versions[name] = api.datasets.upload(f"demo/{name}.zarr.zip", dataset=name)
    print(versions[name].ref, versions[name].status.value, versions[name].sha256[:19])

dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v2 ready sha256:3062fa82622c
dataset://default/fx_daily@v2 ready sha256:7f27db4a2ac4
dataset://default/holidays_eu@v2 ready sha256:11abf028d5f5
dataset://default/eu_media_future@v2 ready sha256:2db88e1af79d

datasets.upload does all the steps of an upload:

  1. If the name is new, it makes the dataset.
  2. It opens an upload session.
  3. It PUTs the bytes to the signed URL. It does not send your API credentials to that URL.
  4. It starts the ingest run in the sandbox with a new idempotency key.
  5. It waits until the version is ready. If the ingest fails, it raises the error of the ingest.

It accepts a path, bytes or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). CSV and Parquet files need a mapping=IngestMapping(…). Zarr zips and netCDF files describe themselves.

The version has the schema that the ingest run checked:

schema = versions["eu_media_daily"].data_schema  # the DataSchema the ingest run checked
print({dim: spec.policy.value for dim, spec in schema.dims.items()})
print({var: spec.role.value for var, spec in schema.vars.items()})

{'date': 'extend', 'market': 'new_levels', 'channel': 'fixed'}
{'spend_local': 'spend', 'revenue_local': 'target'}

docs.title: Validate a spec
docs.text:
with open("demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    spec_yaml = fh.read()

check = api.specs.validate(spec_yaml)
print("valid" if check.valid else [(i.code, i.pointer) for i in check.issues])
for stage in check.stages:  # the schema after every pipeline step, and where the split is
    if stage.data_schema is not None:
        print(stage.name, sorted(stage.data_schema.dims), "<- split" if stage.split else "")

valid
raw ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
to_eur ['channel', 'geo', 'time']
weekly ['channel', 'geo', 'time'] <- split
hols ['channel', 'geo', 'time']

Validation is synchronous and static. The server never imports plugin code. It returns all the issues at one time, each with a JSON pointer (/pipeline/2/with/over). It also returns the schema at each stage. Here, the schema uses the canonical names of the dataset (geo, time) after binding. The marketing-mix model (mmm.bayesian, on mmm-framework) scales the data and carries spend over. Thus, the pipeline stops at the currency, weekly and holiday steps.

docs.title: Fit and follow the run
docs.text:
from mapi_client import RunEnd, RunEventFrame, RunLiveFrame

revision = api.specs.upsert(spec_yaml)  # creates the spec, or adds a revision if it changed
run = api.runs.fit(revision.spec_id, revision.revision)

for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE; resumes with Last-Event-ID
    match item:
        case RunLiveFrame(name="progress", event=event):  # live only, never replayed
            print("  ", event.payload.get("message"))
        case RunEventFrame(name=name, event=event):  # persisted, with an event id
            p = event.payload  # state, warning, diagnostic, metric, complete, error
            print(name, p.get("code") or p.get("name") or "", p.get("message") or p.get("value"))
        case RunEnd(run=final):  # the stream closes after this frame
            print("end:", final.state.value)

run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
print(run.state.value, run.output_model_version_id)

state  bootstrap object read and deleted
warning DEV_MODE_ISOLATION worker isolation is reduced (development mode): …
state  downloading the dataset
state  fitting the pipeline and the model
   validated the spec and the data
   sampling (pymc)
   posterior ready
   fit complete
   posterior ready
state  rendering plots and views
   explorer: params
diagnostic RHAT 1.0485957785967657
diagnostic ESS_BULK 70.61247760811287
diagnostic ESS_TAIL 51.394768720375154
diagnostic DIVERGENCES 0.0
diagnostic PARETO_K_HIGH 3.0
metric coverage_90 0.9583333333333334
metric elpd_loo 89.0564020582058
metric mape 2.53957229942099
state  uploading outputs
complete  None
state  complete manifest uploaded
end: succeeded
succeeded mv_01m53hmgdhfby1esy1xe341hvh

(We got this output on a laptop against make dev. The demo spec has very small sampler settings on purpose. "posterior ready" shows two times. First, the model fits on the training weeks. Then it does an evaluation on the holdout. Then it fits again on all the weeks.)

runs.stream_events follows the server-sent event stream. It yields four types of items:

Item When Notes RunSnapshot First, and after each change of state The full Run RunEventFrame Persisted events: state, warning, diagnostic, metric, checkpoint, complete, error Has an id. The stream sends it again after a reconnect. RunLiveFrame progress and log Live only. The stream never sends it again. RunTrackingFrame tracking (v0.11): the metric series, params or tags changed Live only. A TrackingFrame with the changed series summaries. RunEnd One time, when the run is terminal Then the stream closes.

If the connection stops, the client continues it with Last-Event-ID. Thus, no persisted event is lost or repeated. runs.wait polls (with backoff) and does not use the stream. With raise_on_failure=True, it raises the error of the run. runs.logs(run_id) gives the captured output and the structured user lines page by page (include_user=False gives only the captured output).

docs.title: Inspect the model version
docs.text:
model = next(m for m in api.models.list() if m.name == "eu-geo-mmm")
mv = api.models.version(model.id, model.latest_version)
print(mv.ref, mv.scorecard.overall if mv.scorecard else None)  # pass | warn | fail
print(mv.metrics)
for item in mv.scorecard.items if mv.scorecard else []:
    print(f"{item.status:4} {item.code}: {item.message_plain}")

model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1 fail
{'mape': 2.53957229942099, 'elpd_loo': 89.0564020582058, 'coverage_90': 0.9583333333333334}
warn RHAT: The chains mostly agree, but not fully (R-hat 1.05).
fail ESS: Only 71 independent draws: the numbers are not stable.
pass DIVERGENCES: The sampler explored the model without problems.
pass HOLDOUT_MAPE: The forecast error on the holdout periods was 3%.
pass HOLDOUT_COVERAGE: 96% of held-out values fell inside the 90% range, as expected.
pass NEGATIVE_ROI: No channel is likely to have a negative return.
pass ROI_ABSURD: The highest channel return (4.34 per unit spent) is believable.
pass SHARE_OUTLIER: No single channel explains most of the KPI.
pass BASELINE_SHARE: The baseline (KPI without media) is 84%, a plausible share.
pass PRIOR_OVERLAP: The data moved every parameter away from its prior.
pass DATA_MISSING: Only 0% of the values are missing.
fail DATA_HISTORY: Only 0.6 years of history: too short to separate media from seasonality.
pass SPEND_VARIATION: Every channel's spend varies enough to measure its effect.

The scorecard works correctly here. The demo spec samples 100 draws on 2 chains from about half a year of weekly data. This keeps the tour fast. The scorecard tells this in plain words: too few independent draws and too little history. If a scorecard fails, you cannot promote the model version to an endpoint (PROMOTION_BLOCKED). If a scorecard only warns, an admin must give an audited reason (the promotion gate).

A ModelVersion also has the signed manifest, the diagnostics, the capabilities, the lineage and the list of artifacts. You can download each of them:

metrics = api.models.download(model.id, mv.version, "metrics.json")  # bytes, CRC32C-checked
api.models.download(model.id, mv.version, "bundle.zarr.zip", dest="eu-geo-mmm.zarr.zip")

The API checks the signature of the manifest before it makes the short-lived signed URL. The client compares the download with the CRC32C and the size that the object store calculated. mapi_sdk.bundle.Bundle opens the downloaded bundle.zarr.zip in a notebook.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
result = api.models.score(
    model.id,
    mv.version,
    {
        "model": mv.ref,
        "mode": "forecast",
        "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
        "side_tables": {"fx": "dataset://default/fx_daily@latest"},  # score_policy: supplied
        "output": {"kind": "expected", "summary": ["mean", "hdi_90"]},
    },
)
print(result.run.state.value, [link.name for link in result.outputs])
summary = result.tree["summary"]  # an xr.DataTree (needs the `xarray` extra)
print(result.tree.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "model-owned", ...}: weekly EUR
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="mean", market="NL").round(0).values)

succeeded ['plots.json', 'result.json', 'score.zarr.zip', 'summary.json', 'ui/guided/forecast.json', 'ui/summary.arrow']
{"contributions": "model-owned", "y_hat": "model-owned"}
[272645. 254447. 259143. 258366. 265242. 269497. 268112. 266377.]

model-owned means that the model returned its answers in the units of its own stage. The units attribute of each variable records these units. Here, the units are weekly EUR. The pipeline converted and resampled the data before the model.

models.score sends the request with Prefer: wait=60. If the run is not complete at that time, the client sends the same request again with the same idempotency key. The server answers with the run that it made before. Thus, a slow score never becomes two runs. With the xarray extra, the client downloads the result tree, does a check of it and puts it in result.tree.

The request is a ScoreRequest as a dict, a YAML string or the Pydantic model. The client fills in apiVersion and kind.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
from mapi_spec.errors import MapiError, ModeNotSupported

request = {
    "model": mv.ref,
    "mode": "forecast",
    "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
    "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
}
try:  # the fx side table has `score_policy: supplied`, and this request does not supply it
    api.models.score(model.id, mv.version, request)
except MapiError as err:
    print(err.code, err)  # SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE, with a JSON pointer: /side_tables/fx

try:  # this model cannot filter (that is for state-space models)
    api.models.score(model.id, mv.version, {**request, "mode": "filter"})
except ModeNotSupported as err:
    print(err.code)  # MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, raised before any run is created

SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE validation failed with 1 error; first at /side_tables/fx: side table 'fx' has score_policy 'supplied' and must be provided for stage 'raw'
MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED

The client changes each RFC 7807 problem from the server into a MapiError. The error can also be a subclass, for example ModeNotSupported, ValidationFailed, CoordPlanError, QuotaExceeded or IntegrityFailure. It has the stable code, the HTTP status, the JSON pointer and the individual issues. The two requests above failed in the static checks, before the server made a run. Transport failures raise mapi_client.TransportError. If the client cannot parse a response, it raises UnexpectedResponse.

The client tries idempotent calls again on 502, 503, 504 and connection errors. Idempotent calls are GETs, and POSTs with an idempotency key. The client obeys Retry-After (ClientConfig.max_retries, default 2). For 429 answers, see Quotas and rate limits.

docs.title: Projects, tokens and usage v0.3
docs.text:
On a multi-tenant API, the client needs credentials and a project (Tenancy and authentication). The credentials come from an API token (Client(token=…), MAPI_TOKEN or the profile). If there is no token, they come from the sign-in that mapi login stored for the profile. The client renews that sign-in automatically. It sends the sign-in only to the API that made it.

The project comes from Client(project=…), MAPI_PROJECT or the profile (mapi use). The client sends the project as X-Mapi-Project, only on the requests for a project:

me = api.me()
for tenant in me.tenants:
    for project in tenant.projects:
        print(f"{project.tenant_id}/{project.project_id}: {project.role.value}")
api.use("acme/growth")  # X-Mapi-Project on every project-scoped request from now on

Make a token for a program. The API returns the secret only one time. The secret does not show in repr:

created = api.tokens.create(
    "budget-planner",
    ["score:geo-mmm-prod", "models:read"],
    expires_in_days=30,
    rate_limit_per_minute=120,
)
print(created.token.display, created.token.expires_at.date())
secret = created.secret  # the only copy: put it in your secret store now

Usage reports and runs have exact costs in integer micro-units of the currency:

report = api.usage.get(period="month", group_by="resource_class")
print(report.totals.amount_micros / 1e6, report.totals.currency)
for quota in report.quotas:
    print(quota.limit_name.value, f"{quota.fraction_used:.0%}", quota.resets_at)
run = api.runs.get("run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0")
print(run.cost.amount_micros, run.cost.currency, run.cost.estimated)

api.tenants contains the calls for tenants, projects and members. api.admin contains the operator endpoints: tenants, quotas, kill switches, executors and the audit log. See the reference.

docs.title: Quotas and rate limits
docs.text:
A 429 answer has one of two codes:

  • RATE_LIMITED: The server refused the request before it did work on it. Thus, the client waits and sends the request again, for all methods. It waits for Retry-After, then for an exponential back-off with a small jitter. It raises RateLimited only after RetryPolicy.rate_limit_retries attempts. If the server asks for a wait longer than max_rate_limit_wait, the client raises RateLimited immediately.
  • QUOTA_EXCEEDED: The client raises QuotaExceeded immediately. retry_after_of(exc) tells when the quota window starts again. It is None when capacity becomes free only after the work that runs now is complete.
try:
    api.runs.fit("spc_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0", 1)
except QuotaExceeded as exc:
    wait = retry_after_of(exc)  # seconds until the quota window resets (None: no reset)
    print(exc.code.value, exc.detail, wait)

Use a RetryPolicy to change this behavior. With max_quota_wait, the client can also wait until a short quota window ends:

patient = Client(
    config=config,
    retry=RetryPolicy(rate_limit_retries=8, max_rate_limit_wait=300, max_quota_wait=0),
)

docs.title: Endpoints, webhooks and sharing v0.4
docs.text: The examples in this section come from docs/snippets/client_integrations.py. This script runs offline against a substitute API. For the concepts, see Integrations.

docs.title: Promote a model version to an endpoint
docs.text:
endpoint = api.endpoints.promote(
    "geo-mmm-prod",
    "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3",
    expected_revision=3,  # 409 CONFLICT if someone else promoted in between
)
print(endpoint.ref, "->", endpoint.model_ref, endpoint.gate.outcome)

endpoint://growth/geo-mmm-prod -> model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3 allowed

A promotion goes through the promotion gate. If the scorecard of a version warns, the call raises MapiError with code OVERRIDE_REQUIRED. Then a signed-in project admin must do the call again with override=True, reason="…". Nobody can override PROMOTION_BLOCKED. api.endpoints also has list, get, history, rollback(alias, reason, to_revision=…) and delete.

docs.title: Score an endpoint into xarray
docs.text:
api.endpoint(alias) returns a RemoteEndpoint:

  • schema() tells what to send.
  • validate(ds) does a check of a payload, but does not run it.
  • score(ds) sends an xr.Dataset inline (as XrJSON, up to 5 MB) and returns the scored xr.Dataset.
geo_mmm = api.endpoint("geo-mmm-prod")
schema = geo_mmm.schema()
print(sorted(schema.snapshot.input_schema.vars))

plan = xr.Dataset(
    {"spend_local": (("market", "channel", "date"), np.array([[[1200.0], [5300.0]]]))},
    coords={"market": ["de"], "channel": ["search", "tv"], "date": ["2025-12-30"]},
)
result = geo_mmm.score(plan, wait=60)  # inline XrJSON in, xr.Dataset out
print(result["revenue_local"].sel(stat="mean").values)

['revenue_local', 'spend_local']
[[13260.]]

score returns the summary group. This group has a stat dim (mean, hdi_90_lower, hdi_90_upper and more). For posterior draws along sample, pass group="draws" with output={"draws": 100}. For a counterfactual, pass group="delta/summary". Each other EndpointScoreCall field is a keyword, for example mode="forecast", horizon={"dim": "time", "periods": 8}, scenario=plan_ds and future_covariates="carry_last".

Like models.score, it sends Prefer: wait=60. It sends the call again with the same idempotency key until the run is complete. timeout= sets the maximum wait. Thus, a slow score never makes two runs. api.endpoints.score(alias, call) is the lower-level call. It returns a ScoreResult with the run, the output links and the downloaded tree. ScoreResult.summary holds the summary as tables. Each table gives dims (its coordinate columns) and time_dim (the dim that is time, or None). Inline payloads need the xarray extra. If the data is larger, upload it as a dataset and send it as data="dataset://growth/plan@v2".

mapi_client.xrjson.encode(ds) changes an xr.Dataset into the XrJSON payload. decode(payload) changes the payload back into an xr.Dataset. XrJSON is the wire format of the SDK. It has dates as ISO strings and NaN as null. The client does a check of the size before it sends data.

docs.title: Forecast with your latest actuals
docs.text:
api.endpoints.forecast(alias, rows) sends actuals and the dates to forecast in one call. It does not fit the model again. rows is a long table in the input layout of the endpoint (schema().input_table). This layout has the time column, the target and the drivers. rows can be a pandas DataFrame, a list of row mappings or a mapping of columns. Rows that have a target value are actuals. The model forecasts the rows after them that have no target value:

import pandas as pd

rows = pd.DataFrame({
    "t": ["1961-01-01", "1961-02-01", "1961-03-01", "1961-04-01", "1961-05-01"],
    "y": [417, 391, 419, None, None],
})
result = api.endpoints.forecast("ts-forecast", rows)
print(result.conditioning.message)
# Forecast updated with 3 actuals (1961-01-01 to 1961-03-01) after the fitted history, which
# ends 1960-12-01; the model's parameters were not re-estimated. 2 periods forecast from
# 1961-04-01 to 1961-05-01.

You can also give the two parts separately:

  • actuals=: the rows with the target.
  • future=: the dates to forecast, rows with their driver values, or a number of periods to add after the last actual (future=6).

The client carries empty driver values on future rows forward (future_covariates="carry_last", the default here). If a model cannot use actuals, it refuses them with ActualsNotSupported (422 ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED). api.endpoint(alias).forecast(rows) does the same and gets the schema one time. mapi_client.forecast_call(schema, rows, ...) only makes the call. ScoreResult.conditioning is the record for each forecast. If you sent no actual, it has conditioned=False and the end of the fitted history.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
python = api.endpoints.snippets("geo-mmm-prod", ["python"]).items[0]
print(python.code.splitlines()[2])

api.endpoints.snippets(alias, languages) returns the code that the Integrations hub shows. The languages are Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script and a notebook cell. The Python snippet is the same as the api.endpoints.score(...) call above. The notebook cell uses the api.endpoint(alias).score(...) form. The two snippets run without changes. The tests of the client run them.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
created = api.webhooks.create(
    "https://hooks.example.com/mapi", ["model.version.ready", "endpoint.promoted"]
)
signing_secret = created.secret  # the only copy: store it with the receiver
print(created.webhook.id, created.webhook.secret_hint)

create and rotate_secret return the signing secret only one time. The secret does not show in repr. api.webhooks also has list, get, update, delete, deliveries(id, status=…) and replay(id, delivery_id). For the checks of deliveries on the receiver side, see Receiving webhooks.

docs.title: Render a plot
docs.text:
render = api.plots.render(
        model_id="mdl_01jaf3c1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9n0",
        version=3,
        plot_id="mmm.response_curves",
        format="png",
        width=1200,
    )
    path = api.plots.download_render(render, Path(tmp) / "response_curves.png")

plots.render accepts a PlotSpec, a saved plot (saved_plot_id=) or a plot of a model version. Like a score, it waits for the render in the sandbox. download_render gets the file and does a CRC32C check. plots.save, saved, get_saved and delete_saved manage saved plots. create_embed returns a read-only embed link one time. Also see embeds, revoke_embed and the public embed(token) view. See Sharing plots.

docs.title: Sign-up, verification, deletion and export
docs.text:
export = api.tenants.export("acme")
    archive = api.tenants.download_export("acme", export.id, Path(tmp) / "acme-export.zip")

download_export waits until the export is ready. Then it downloads the export through the storage client to a temporary file. It never uses your API credentials for this download. When the size is correct, it renames the file to its final name.

api.tenants also has verification, request_deletion(tenant_id, confirm=tenant_id), deletion and cancel_deletion. api.signup(...) and api.verify_email(token) are the public sign-up calls. The client sends them without credentials. Operators have api.admin.signups, review_signup, set_verification and retry_deletion. See Deleting and exporting data.

docs.title: Guided mode
docs.text:
api.guided controls Guided mode from code. It has these calls:

  • templates() and template(id).
  • detect_roles(template_id, columns=[…] | dataset="dataset://…").
  • draft(template_id=…, name=…, dataset=…, answers={…}). This returns the ingest mapping, the ModelSpec and its YAML. It does not store data.
  • compile({...}). This returns the ScoreRequest for a what-if, a forecast or a preset.
  • preview_priors(business_priors, spec_id=…, revision=…). This starts a translate_priors run in the sandbox and waits for it.

docs.title: Workflows, governance and explorers v0.5
docs.text: All the v0.5 calls are on the same client. The mapi_spec DTOs give their types. The documentation tests run the tour below, without changes, against a real server.

docs.title: Help me choose
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()  # MAPI_URL, the `mapi login` sign-in (or MAPI_TOKEN) and MAPI_PROJECT

result = api.catalog.recommend(
    goal="forecast", data_shape="one_series", drivers="yes", experience="beginner", limit=3
)
for item in result.items:  # best first, with the reasons in plain words
    print(f"{item.score:.0%}  {item.title}  ({item.kind.value} {item.id})")
    for reason in item.reasons_plain:
        print("     +", reason)
    for caution in item.cautions_plain:
        print("     !", caution)

card = api.catalog.about("ts.sarimax", kind="model")  # any item's About card
print(card.summary_plain)
print("use it when:", "; ".join(card.use_when))
print("pick something else when:", "; ".join(card.avoid_when))

docs.title: Run a workflow and follow it live
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

check = api.workflows.validate(Path("weekly-readiness.yaml"))  # on the server; saves nothing
for issue in check.issues:  # every problem with a JSON pointer into the document
    print(issue.severity.value, issue.pointer, issue.message)
print(" -> ".join(check.order))  # the order the nodes will run in

from mapi_client import WorkflowEnd, WorkflowEventFrame, WorkflowSnapshot

# create the workflow, or save the file as its next revision when it changed
workflow, revision = api.workflows.upsert(Path("weekly-readiness.yaml"))
run = api.workflows.run(
    workflow.id,
    inputs={"data": "dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest"},  # pinned to a version at start
    params={"drivers": ["price"], "window": 80, "max_p": 2, "max_q": 2},
)
for item in api.workflows.stream_events(run.run_id):  # server-sent events, resumable
    match item:
        case WorkflowSnapshot(run=now):
            print(f"{len(now.nodes)} nodes, {now.status.value}")
        case WorkflowEventFrame(event=e) if e.type.value == "workflow.branch.decided":
            print(f"  {e.node_id}: took the {e.data['arm']} arm")
        case WorkflowEventFrame(event=e) if e.node_id is not None:
            print(f"  {e.node_id}: {e.type.value.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]}")
        case WorkflowEnd(status=status):
            print("run", status.value if status else "ended")

stream_events yields these items:

  • WorkflowSnapshot: the run with all its nodes. It comes first on each connection.
  • WorkflowEventFrame: a node is queued, started, succeeded, cached, skipped, failed or retrying, or a branch is decided.
  • WorkflowEnd.

If the connection stops, the client continues it with Last-Event-ID. api.workflows.wait(run_id) polls and does not use the stream. It raises the error of the node that failed.

run = api.workflows.wait(run.run_id)  # raises the run's error if it failed
nodes = {n.node_id: n for n in run.nodes}
print(nodes["adf"].result["verdict_plain"])  # e.g. "The series wanders: consider differencing it."
for d in run.decisions:
    print(d.node_id, d.arm, d.inputs)  # every branch with the values its condition read
order, d = nodes["order"].result, 1 if nodes["wanders"].result["value"] else 0
print(f"ARIMA({order['best_p']}, {d}, {order['best_q']})")  # chosen by information criterion
print(nodes["dm"].result["verdict_plain"])  # is ARIMAX's edge over naive more than luck?
print(nodes["select"].result["reason_plain"])  # kept only if it beats the benchmarks
model_ref = run.outputs["model"].ref  # model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1
report = run.outputs["report"].inline  # mapi.report/v1: every test, decision and table

Since v0.9, a node can give a plot output (plot.render, model.forecast and evaluate.residuals). api.workflows.node(run_id, node_id).outputs["plot"].inline is the PlotSpec document of the plot. The server puts it through the plot sanitizer each time it sends it. If the plot is not safe, inline is None. The gallery also has recipes for Bayesian and science models, for example sci_spatial_ladder and bayes_workflow_audit. The workflow cookbook shows how to run each one with the client.

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
gov = nodes["governance"].result  # the policy in force, measured on the selected model
print("passed" if gov["passed"] else f"failed: {gov['failed_checks']}")
validation = api.validations.get(gov["validation_id"])  # recorded because submit: true
print(validation.status.value)  # validated, or awaiting_approval when a reviewer must sign
for r in validation.results:
    print(f"{r.check:28} {r.status.value:7} {r.message_plain}")
api.validations.download_evidence_pack(validation.id, "evidence.html")  # for the auditor

import yaml

with open("forecast-policy.yaml", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    policy = api.governance.create_policy(yaml.safe_load(fh))
print(policy.id, policy.version, [c.check for c in policy.checks])

# edit and save the next version (refused with 409 if someone saved one meanwhile)
stricter = api.governance.update_policy(
    policy.id, policy.model_copy(update={"approvals_required": 2}), expected_version=1
)
for p in api.governance.policies():  # in force in the project: tenant-wide first
    print(p.scope, p.name, f"v{p.version}")

validation = api.models.validate(model_id, version, note="Q4 refresh", wait=True)
print(validation.status.value)  # validated, awaiting_approval or checks_failed
for r in validation.results:
    print(r.check, r.status.value, r.message_plain, r.suggested_action or "")
if validation.status.value == "checks_failed":
    validation = api.validations.resubmit(validation.id, note="refitted on clean data")

# a reviewer, signed in with `mapi login` (never the submitter, never an API token)
reviewer = Client(project=os.environ.get("MAPI_PROJECT"))
for pending in reviewer.validations.list(status="awaiting_approval"):
    evidence = list(reviewer.validations.evidence(pending.id))
    if all(r.status.value in ("pass", "skipped") for r in evidence):
        reviewer.validations.approve(pending.id, comment="Evidence reviewed")
    else:
        reviewer.validations.reject(pending.id, "The null test is not convincing yet")

docs.title: Explorers and budget optimisation
docs.text:
ds = api.datasets.find("weekly_sales")
assert ds is not None and ds.latest_version is not None
api.datasets.describe(ds.id, "Weekly sales and price by region, from the finance warehouse")
print(api.datasets.about(ds.id).summary_generated)  # "Weekly data from ... for 5 regions ..."

explored = api.datasets.explore(  # computed in the sandbox; the same request is cached
    ds.id,
    ds.latest_version,
    sections=["overview", "stationarity", "ccf", "stl", "quality"],
    kpi="sales",
    max_lag=12,
)
for section in explored.index.sections if explored.index else []:
    print(section.section, section.status, section.message_plain or "")
stationarity = api.explorations.view(explored, "stationarity")  # the view, as JSON

model_id, version = "mdl_01jaf3c1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9n0", 3
explored = api.models.explore(
    model_id, version, sections=["params", "residuals", "forecast"], horizon=13
)
residuals = api.explorations.view(explored, "residuals")

compared = api.models.compare(
    ["model://growth/arimax@v3", "model://growth/ets@v1", "model://growth/theta@v2"], horizon=4
)
table = api.explorations.view(compared, "comparison")  # metrics, ranking, Diebold-Mariano

plan = api.models.optimize(  # mmm-framework's planner on the posterior; waits for the plan
    model_id,
    version,
    budget_change_pct=0,  # reallocate today's total
    channels={"tv": {"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}},
    objective="p10",  # plan for a cautious outcome, not the average one
    frontier={"n_points": 8},
)
assert plan.result is not None
for a in plan.result.allocation:
    print(f"{a.channel:10} {a.current_spend:>12,.0f} -> {a.optimal_spend:>12,.0f}")
uplift = plan.result.uplift
print("uplift", uplift.mean if uplift else None, "P(better)", plan.result.prob_positive_uplift)

docs.title: Schedules and triggers
docs.text:
weekly = api.workflows.schedule(
    workflow.id,
    "0 6 * * 1",  # Mondays at 06:00
    timezone="Europe/Berlin",
    inputs={"data": "dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest"},
    params={"drivers": ["price"]},
)
on_upload = api.workflows.trigger(

)
print(weekly.next_run_at, on_upload.id)

docs.title: Track metrics, params and tags v0.11
docs.text:
You can add metrics, params and tags to a run, also after the run finished. For example, log a business KPI that you measured after you deployed the model. The writes need the runner role. An API token needs the runs:write scope.

run_id = "run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0"

api.runs.log_metric(run_id, "revenue_lift", 0.042, labels={"region": "north"})
api.runs.log_metrics(run_id, {"mae": 3.1, "rmse": 4.2}, labels={"split": "post_launch"})
api.runs.log_params(run_id, {"analyst": "kim", "holdout_weeks": 8})
api.runs.set_tags(run_id, {"stage": "production", "old_tag": None})  # None deletes the tag
api.runs.update(run_id, name="weekly sales, adstock 4", note="Holiday weeks removed.")

with api.runs.track(run_id) as t:
    for week, value in weekly_kpi:
        t.log_metric("weekly_lift", value, step=week)
Call What it does runs.update(run_id, name=…, note=…, tags=…) PATCH /v1/runs/{run_id}. Only the arguments that you give change. None clears the name or the note. runs.log_metric(run_id, key, value, step=None, labels=None, ts=None) Log one point runs.log_metrics(run_id, values, step=None, labels=None) Log a dict of values, or a list of MetricPointIn. The client sends a maximum of 1000 points in each request. runs.log_params(run_id, params) Log params (500 in each request). A different value for a stored key raises a CONFLICT error. runs.set_tags(run_id, tags) Set tags. None deletes a tag. runs.track(run_id, flush_every=500) A context manager with log_metric, log_metrics, log_param, log_params, set_tag and set_tags. It sends the points in batches and when the block ends. runs.metrics(run_id, key=None, attempt=None) The series of the run with their summaries (MetricSeries) runs.metric_history(run_id, key, max_points=1000, attempt=None, labels=None) The points of one key (MetricHistory), downsampled runs.params(run_id, prefix=None) The params (RunParam)

runs.list can search by the tracking data. The client does a check of each filters, order_by and columns value before it sends the request:

for run in api.runs.list(
    filters=["metric.rmse < 12", "param.fit.engine = nutpie"],
    tags=["stage:candidate"],
    order_by="metric.rmse",
    columns=["metric.rmse", "param.settings.adstock.l_max"],
):
    print(run.id, run.name, run.columns)

The other filters of runs.list are kind, state, spec_id, parent_run_id, name and (v0.14) experiment_id. For the grammar, see Search runs. For the logging API inside a model, see Track metrics, params and tags.

docs.title: Media, experiments and comparison v0.14
docs.text:
# images and tables of a run
api.runs.log_image(run_id, "holdout_map", "map.png", caption="Holdout error by region")
api.runs.log_table(run_id, "lift", {"region": ["north", "south"], "lift": [0.04, 0.02]})
for item in api.runs.media(run_id, key="samples"):
    png = api.runs.download_media(run_id, item)   # checks the size, CRC32C and SHA-256

# experiments
exp = api.experiments.create("adstock length study", description="Adstock 2, 4 and 8.")
api.experiments.add_runs(exp.id, [run_a, run_b])
run = api.runs.fit(spec_id, revision, experiment_id=exp.id)
api.runs.update(run_c, experiment_id=exp.id)        # move one run (None: no experiment)

# compare and save a search
cmp = api.runs.compare([run_a, run_b], keys=["loss"], media_keys=["samples"])
view = api.run_views.create(
    "best fits", {"filters": ["metric.rmse < 12"], "order_by": "metric.rmse"},
    experiment_id=exp.id,
)
runs = api.runs.list(experiment_id=exp.id, columns=["metric.rmse"])
Call What it does runs.media(run_id, key=None, kind=None, attempt=None, links=True) The images and tables of a run (RunMedia). With links, each item has a signed url. runs.media_keys(run_id, attempt=None) The media series with their counts and steps (MediaKeySummary) runs.get_media(run_id, media_id) One item with a new signed url runs.download_media(run_id, media) The bytes. The client does a check of the size, the CRC32C and the SHA-256. runs.log_image(run_id, key, image, step=None, labels=None, caption=None) Log PNG or JPEG bytes or a file path. With mapi-sdk, also a numpy array, a Pillow image or a DataArray. A maximum of 4 MiB. runs.log_table(run_id, key, table, step=None, labels=None, caption=None) Log a DataFrame, a dict of columns or a list of records runs.track(run_id) Also has log_image and log_table (sent immediately) runs.keys(experiment_id=None, prefix=None) The metric series, param keys and tag keys of the runs (RunKeys) runs.compare(run_ids, keys=(), media_keys=(), max_points=300, params=True) Compare 2 to 10 runs (RunCompare) experiments.list(name=None, archived=None), get, find(name_or_id) Find experiments experiments.create(name, description=None), update(id, name=…, description=…, archived=…), delete(id) Manage experiments experiments.add_runs(id, run_ids), remove_runs(id, run_ids) Move runs (a maximum of 200 in each request) run_views.list(experiment_id=None), find, create(name, query, experiment_id=None), update(id, name=…, query=…), delete(id) Saved views of the runs table

The async client has the same calls. For the web app and the CLI, see Compare runs and use experiments.

docs.title: Image collections and weights v0.15
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_spec import CollectionOptions, IngestMapping

# how many images are new? (the client calculates the SHA-256 of each image)
plan = api.datasets.missing_images(dataset_id, ["9f86d0…", "60303a…"])  # a ds_… id
print(plan.present, len(plan.missing))

# upload a folder: only the missing images, in parts, with a state file to continue later
version = api.datasets.upload_collection(
    "product_photos",
    Path("photos"),
    label_from_folder=True,
    options=CollectionOptions(size=(64, 64)),
    state_file=Path("photos.upload.json"),
    wait=True,
)
print(version.layout, version.collection.n_images, version.collection.new_images)

# pretrained weights as a dataset
weights = api.datasets.upload(
    "resnet.safetensors", dataset="tiny-resnet", mapping=IngestMapping(format="safetensors")
)
Call What it does datasets.upload_collection(dataset, root, *, manifest=None, label_from_folder=False, options=None, base_version=None, part_bytes=DEFAULT_PART_BYTES, state_file=None, message=None, wait=False, timeout=None, progress=None) Upload a folder of images as a collection version (DatasetVersion). dataset is a name (the client makes the dataset when it does not exist) or a ds_… id. It uploads only the images that the base version does not have. With state_file, a second call continues the upload: it skips the parts that arrived and renews expired URLs. datasets.missing_images(dataset_id, shas, *, base_version=None) BlobMissing. The client sends the digests in groups of 5000 and merges the answers. datasets.get_upload(dataset_id, upload_id) An UploadSession with received datasets.renew_upload(dataset_id, upload_id) A fresh signed PUT for an upload whose file did not arrive

mapi_client.collections has the parts of upload_collection that do not need a server: scan_images(root, manifest, path_column=..., label_from_folder=...), write_parts(plan, missing, out_dir, part_bytes) and client_manifest_csv(plan). The parts are zip files with no compression. The same images always give the same bytes.

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
AsyncClient has the same resources and arguments. Use await for the calls. Use async for for the lists:

import asyncio

from mapi_client import AsyncClient


async def recent_fits(n: int = 3) -> list[str]:
    async with AsyncClient() as aapi:  # same resources and arguments, awaited
        found: list[str] = []
        async for run in aapi.runs.list(kind="fit", limit=n):  # follows next_cursor lazily
            found.append(f"{run.id} {run.state.value}")
            if len(found) == n:
                break
        return found


print(asyncio.run(recent_fits()))

The v0.5 resources work in the same way:

import asyncio

from mapi_client import AsyncClient


async def main() -> None:
    async with AsyncClient() as aapi:
        wf = await aapi.workflows.find("weekly-readiness")
        assert wf is not None
        run = await aapi.workflows.run(
            wf.id, inputs={"data": "dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest"}, wait=True
        )
        async for node in aapi.workflows.nodes(run.run_id):
            print(node.node_id, node.status.value)


asyncio.run(main())

List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor. api.health() and api.ready() call /healthz and /readyz. api.me() calls /v1/me. api.use(project) changes the selected project. api.signup(), api.verify_email() and api.endpoint(alias) are v0.4. mapi_client.webhooks verifies deliveries. mapi_client.xrjson encodes inline payloads.

The platform optimizes budgets (see Optimise a budget). For the DTOs, see mapi_spec. For the endpoints, see the HTTP API reference.

docs.title: Compare runs and use experiments v0.14
docs.text:
When you try different settings of a model, you get many runs. This guide tells you how to find the runs that you need, how to compare them, and how to keep related runs together.

  • Find runs. The runs table shows metrics, params and tags as columns. You can filter and sort the table by these values.
  • Saved views. A saved view keeps a search of the runs table (the filters, the sort order and the columns) under a name. All members of the project can use it.
  • Compare runs. The compare page shows 2 to 10 runs side by side: metric curves, metric bars, the params that are different, the plots and the images.
  • Experiments. An experiment is a named group of runs, for example "adstock length study".

The runs must log their metrics, params and tags first. See Track metrics, params and tags.

See also HTTP API: Comparison, experiments and saved views The endpoints and the DTOs Search runs The grammar of filters, sort orders and columns Images, figures and tables Log images that the compare page shows

docs.title: Find runs
docs.text:
Open Runs in the web app. The toolbar has these controls:

  • Experiment: show only the runs of one experiment.
  • State and Kind: show only the runs in one state or of one kind.
  • Name: show only the runs with this text in their name.
  • Filters: type a filter and push Enter. Each filter shows as a chip. Click the cross on a chip to remove the filter.
  • Columns: add metrics, params and tags as columns of the table.
  • Views: apply, save, rename or delete a saved view.

The address of the page holds the search. Thus you can copy the address and send it to a colleague, or reload the page.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
A filter compares a value of each run with a value that you type. Examples:

Filter Shows the runs where metric.rmse < 3 The last value of the series rmse is less than 3 metric.loss{split=val}.min < 0.3 The minimum of the loss series with the label split=val is less than 0.3 param.lr = 0.01 The param lr has the text 0.01 param.fit.draws >= 1000 The param fit.draws is a number of 1000 or more tag.team = growth The tag team has the value growth name ~ adstock The name contains adstock (case is ignored)

A run that does not have the metric, the param or the tag does not match. The web app does a check of each filter when you type it. If the server does not accept a filter, its message shows below the filter bar. For the full grammar, see Search runs. A search has a maximum of 8 filters.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
Click Columns to open the column picker. The picker lists the metric series, the param keys and the tag keys of the runs of the project (or of the experiment), the most frequent first. Type to find a key.

  • For a metric, select the value to show: last (the default), min, max or count.
  • A metric series with labels is one column, for example metric.loss{split=val}.
  • The table has a maximum of 16 tracked columns.

Click the header of a tracked column to sort the runs by it. Click again to change the direction. A third click removes the sort. Runs that do not have the value go to the end. Click Load more runs to show more runs.

Note

Params and tags are text from the runs. The table shows them as text only.

docs.title: Saved views
docs.text:
A saved view keeps the search of the runs table: the experiment, the state, the kind, the name, the tags, the filters, the sort order and the columns.

  1. Set the search in the runs table.
  2. Click Views, then Save as a new view.
  3. Type a name. Names are unique in a project (case is ignored). The name of a view in an experiment must be unique in the experiment.
  4. Click Save.

To apply a view, click Views and select the view. The app writes the search of the view in the address. To change a view, change the search, then click Views and Save the changes to the view.

A project has a maximum of 200 saved views. The server does a check of each filter, sort order and column when you save the view. When you delete an experiment, the server also deletes the views of the experiment.

docs.title: Compare runs
docs.text:
1. In the runs table, select 2 to 10 runs with the check boxes.
  2. Click Compare.

The compare page (/runs/compare?runs=...) has a chip for each run in a fixed colour. Click a chip to open the run. Click the cross on a chip to remove the run. Click Add run to add a run. The page has these sections:

Section What it shows Curves One chart for each metric key, with one line for each run. Select a label (for example split) to draw each value of the label with a different dash. The default keys are the 12 keys that most of the runs have. Use the key picker to change them. Select the log scale for values that cover a large range. Metric bars A bar for each run for each metric, with the value that you select: last, min or max. The best run has a mark. For keys such as loss, error, rmse, mae, mape and brier, the best value is the minimum. For other keys, it is the maximum. The text below the chart tells which rule it used. Params A table with one row for each param key and one column for each run. Show only differences (on by default) hides the params that have the same value in all runs. An empty cell is a param that the run did not log. Plots The plots that two or more of the runs have, side by side. One row for each plot, one column for each run. Media The images that the runs logged. Select a media key. Move the step slider: each run shows its image at the largest step that is not more than the slider.

The server sends a maximum of 300 points for each curve. It keeps the shape of the curve, the first point and the last point.

docs.title: Compare runs from Python and the command line
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()
cmp = api.runs.compare(["run_01…", "run_02…"], keys=["loss", "rmse"], media_keys=["samples"])
for p in cmp.params:
    if p.differs:
        print(p.key, p.values)
for metric in cmp.metrics:
    for s in metric.series:
        print(metric.key, s.run_id, s.labels, s.values[-1])

mapi runs compare run_01… run_02… --key loss --key rmse --agg min

The command shows a table of the metrics (one row for each key, one column for each run). Then it shows the params that are different. --all-params shows all params.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text: An experiment is a named group of runs in a project. A run is in one experiment or in no experiment. Use an experiment for a study: for example, the runs that compare three adstock lengths, and the benchmark model that you compare them with.

docs.title: Why an experiment and not the spec
docs.text:
The runs table can also filter by spec. But the runs of a study often do not have the same spec:

  • Score runs, workflow nodes, search.grid trials and runs that you log from a notebook have no spec, or a different spec.
  • To compare two models (an MMM and a benchmark), you compare runs of two specs.
  • An experiment has a name and a description. It also has its own saved views.
  • You can move a run into an experiment or out of it at any time. You cannot change the spec of a run.

Tags are not a good replacement: a tag has no description, no list of all groups, and a typo makes a new group.

docs.title: Make an experiment and add runs
docs.text:
In the web app:

  1. Open Experiments.
  2. Click New experiment.
  3. Type the name and, if necessary, a description. Click Create.
  4. In the runs table, select the runs. Click Add to experiment and select the experiment.

The experiment page shows the description, the runs table of the experiment and its saved views. To move one run, open the run, go to the Notes tab and select the experiment.

From the command line:

mapi experiments create "adstock length study" --description "Adstock 2, 4 and 8 weeks."
mapi experiments add "adstock length study" run_01… run_02… run_03…
mapi fit spec.yaml --remote @ --experiment "adstock length study"
mapi runs ls --experiment "adstock length study" --column metric.elpd_loo
mapi experiments ls

From Python:

exp = api.experiments.create("adstock length study")
api.experiments.add_runs(exp.id, ["run_01…", "run_02…"])
run = api.runs.fit(spec_id, revision, experiment_id=exp.id)
runs = api.runs.list(experiment_id=exp.id, columns=["metric.elpd_loo"])

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Experiment names are unique in a project (case is ignored). A name has a maximum of 200 characters.
  • A workflow node run goes into the experiment of its workflow run. Name the experiment when you start the workflow run: experiment_id in POST /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}/runs, experiment_id= in api.workflows.run, or mapi workflows run --experiment. If you move a workflow run later, the node runs that it already started stay where they are.
  • A retry goes into the experiment of the run that it retries.
  • An archived experiment does not accept new runs. You can still list, filter and compare its runs. To add runs again, unarchive it. This includes retries: the server refuses to retry a run of an archived experiment (409).
  • When you delete an experiment, its runs stay. They are then in no experiment. The server deletes the saved views of the experiment.
  • One request adds or removes a maximum of 200 runs. The server ignores ids that are not runs of the project and lists them in missing.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Experiments and saved views use the permissions of runs. A viewer can see them. To make, change or delete them, you need the runner role (or a higher role), or an API token with the runs:write scope. See Tenancy and authentication.

docs.title: Sweeps
docs.text: The Sweep document is retired in v0.14. The server does not accept new Sweep documents. Use a workflow with a search.grid node. Each grid point of the node logs its scores as metrics with the step of the point (see Workflow nodes). Open the search run to compare the points in the Metrics tab, or compare the runs of two searches on the compare page.

docs.title: Sharing plots: saved plots, images and embed links
docs.text:
The plots of a model are in the web app. The isolated plot sandbox renders them. You can use a plot in a different place, for example a slide, a report, a BI dashboard, a Notion page or a Slack thread. To do this, you can:

  1. save the plot with a title (POST /v1/plots),
  2. render the plot to PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox (POST /v1/plots:render), or
  3. embed the plot with a link that has a token, is read-only and expires (POST /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds).

The three actions need a signed-in caller or an API token of the project. The embed link is public. All persons who have the link can see that one plot. They can see it until the link expires or until you revoke it.

Use the correct method for each tool:

  • BI tools and Notion put an embed link in a frame and show the live chart.
  • Chat tools, for example Slack and Teams, never put a page in a frame. They change a link into a card from the tags of its page. The tags of the embed page are the same for all links: a "Shared chart" card with no plot name and no image. Thus, post a rendered PNG to a Slack thread. If people must open the live view, also add the link.

docs.title: Save a plot
docs.text:
To save a plot of a model version, name its source. The API first does a check of the signed bundle manifest of the model version. Then it sends the plot through the sanitizer again:

curl -s -X POST "$MAPI_URL/v1/plots" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "title": "EU response curves (v3)",
        "source": {"model_id": "mdl_01jaf3c1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9n0", "version": 3,
                   "plot_id": "mmm.response_curves"}
      }'

The answer is a SavedPlot. Its embeddable field tells if you can share the plot with a link (see what can be embedded).

You can also save a plot that you wrote ("spec": {...}, a PlotSpec). The plot must pass the same sanitizer. If it does not pass, the answer is 422 PLOT_UNSAFE. The plot must also contain its data inline. data_ref datasets belong to a model version. Thus, to save that type of plot, use source. The platform always records a hand-written plot with author provenance. The value in its provenance field has no effect.

  • GET /v1/plots lists the saved plots of the project (newest first).
  • GET /v1/plots/{plot_id} returns one plot with its spec.
  • DELETE /v1/plots/{plot_id} deletes the plot and its embed links.

docs.title: Render an image
docs.text:
POST /v1/plots:render changes one plot into a file. You can identify the plot by saved_plot_id, by source (a plot of a model version) or inline (plot):

curl -s -X POST "$MAPI_URL/v1/plots:render" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Prefer: wait=30" \
  -d '{"saved_plot_id": "plt_01jaf3n1p2q3r4s5t6v7w8x9y0", "format": "pdf", "width": 1200, "height": 600}'
Field Default Meaning format png png, svg or pdf scale 2 The pixel density of PNG and PDF (0 < scale ≤ 8). SVG ignores it. width, height The size of the plot The size in CSS pixels before scale (16–4096). For a composite plot (facets, concatenations), it is the size of each panel.

A PNG or a PDF contains a maximum of 50 megapixels. This is the width x height x scale² of the plot after layout, with all panels. If a request is larger, the answer is 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE at the start. Sometimes only the layout shows the size. Then the render run fails with that code before it draws the plot. If you get this error, make the scale or the size smaller.

A render is a render run in the sandbox. Thus it counts against your quotas, as all small runs do. You can send Prefer: wait=N (a maximum of 60 seconds). If the run finishes in that time, the answer is 200 with signed links to renders/<plot>.<format>. If not, the answer is 202 with the run. Then poll GET /v1/plots/renders/{run_id} until done is true. The links expire after a short time. Download the file. Do not keep the URL.

Vega-Lite only, for now

vl-convert renders Vega-Lite plots. Plotly plots need kaleido and a Chrome or Chromium in the runner image. The images of the platform do not include them. Thus Plotly renders answer 422 MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, unless the operator enables them (MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED). You can export a Plotly plot from the plot viewer.

docs.title: Rendering never fetches anything
docs.text:
The renderer gets the sanitized plot and its data as pinned inputs of the run:

  • The API writes the plot as the plots.json of the run. It pins each bundle dataset of the plot (data_ref) to the verified object generation, as run inputs with the names plotdata.<n>.
  • The sanitizer refused URL data, href encodings, image marks, and Plotly layout images or tile maps before. The runner refuses them again before it draws.
  • vl-convert runs with no network access (allowed_base_urls=[]). Also, the sandbox has no egress.

An image has a limit of 32 MiB. The run has a time limit of MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S (5 minutes by default).

docs.title: Embed links
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$MAPI_URL/v1/plots/plt_01jaf3n1p2q3r4s5t6v7w8x9y0/embeds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"label": "Q4 board deck", "expires_in_days": 90,
       "allowed_origins": ["https://acme.notion.site"]}'

The answer (PlotEmbedCreated) is the only time that you see the link:

{
  "embed": {"id": "emb_01jaf3p1q2r3s4t5v6w7x8y9z0", "display": "mpe_7k2m9q…", "status": "active", "...": "..."},
  "url": "https://plots.mapi.example/embed/mpe_7k2m9q4x0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz",
  "token": "mpe_7k2m9q4x0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz"
}

The platform keeps only a keyed hash of the token, as it does for API tokens. Paste the url into the tool that shows the plot, or put it in a frame:

<iframe src="https://plots.mapi.example/embed/mpe_7k2m…" width="900" height="520"
        style="border:0" loading="lazy" title="EU response curves"></iframe>
Option Default Meaning expires_in_days 30 1 to 365 days label none Your note. The list of links shows it. allowed_origins all sites The https sites (https://host[:port], a maximum of 10) whose pages can show the plot in a frame. If you open the link directly, it always works.
  • GET /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds lists the links of a plot. It shows their status (active, expired or revoked), the view count and the last view. It never shows their tokens.
  • DELETE /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds/{embed_id} revokes one link. If you revoke a link two times, no problem occurs.

The audit log records each new link and each revoked link (plot.embed_create, plot.embed_revoke).

docs.title: What can be embedded
docs.text:
You can embed only the plots that a model version drew with one of the platform's own recipes (core.*, mmm.*, ml.*, ts.*, choice.*, causal.*). The science pack (sci.*) and the network pack (net.*) are not in this list. Thus you cannot embed their plots. Share them in the project, or render them to an image. The platform refuses plots from a model plugin and plots that a person wrote. The answer is 422 EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED. This rule exists because a shared link runs the spec of the plot in the browser of a stranger. Also in the sandbox, a spec can navigate its own frame. Thus shared views run only specs that the platform wrote. Share other plots in the project, or render them to an image.

A model version that you fit with uploaded plugin code (a dev overlay or a vetted overlay) can embed none of its plots. The recipe that a plot names has no effect. The reason: the worker that writes the plot documents also runs that code. Thus the server decides from the lineage of the version, not from what a plot tells about itself. Existing links to these plots stop and do not show them.

An embed also contains its data inline. Thus you cannot embed a dataset that is larger than 1.5 MB.

docs.title: The embed page
docs.text:
The link opens a page of the plot sandbox (/embed/<token>). The page reads the plot from the public GET /v1/embeds/{token} of the API. It draws the plot with the same safeguards as the plot frames of the app:

  • The request sends no cookie or credential. If the API gets one, the API ignores it.
  • The Content-Security-Policy of the page lets it fetch only the /v1/embeds/ path of the API. The API answers cross-origin reads only from the origin of the plot sandbox.
  • The browser validates the answer again (inline data only, and the same checks for unsafe constructs as the plot frames of the app). The page writes all text as text.
  • If a site that is not in allowed_origins puts the page in a frame, the page shows a notice and not the plot.

If you can start render runs (the runner role), the platform renders a PNG of the plot when you create the link. The page then shows an Open as PNG link, for tools that cannot show interactive content. Editors can also create links, but without that image.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Status Code When 404 NOT_FOUND The token does not exist, or a person deleted its plot. 410 LINK_EXPIRED The link expired, or a person revoked it, or its tenant is suspended. 429 RATE_LIMITED This link has too many views (MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE), or one address sent too many requests (MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE). Wait for the time in Retry-After.

docs.title: Hosting the embed page
docs.text:
The build of the plot sandbox has two pages: index.html (the plot frames of the app) and embed.html. The server sends embed.html for each /embed/<token> path. The embed page needs the origin of the API:

  • In development, the build includes VITE_API_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8000).
  • The mapi/web image builds the page with a placeholder. When nginx serves the page, it puts MAPI_API_URL in the placeholder. It also adds the headers of the page (CSP with connect-src … $MAPI_API_URL/v1/embeds/, frame-ancestors 'self' https:).

The API allows cross-origin reads of /v1/embeds/ only from MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN. Thus that setting must be the origin from which the server sends the embed page.

docs.title: Tabular models with scikit-learn and xgboost
docs.text:
