S (2 vCPU, 8 GiB) M (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) L (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) base-bayes (mmm.*, sci.*, tabular.*, ingest, describe) mapi-prod-base-bayes-s mapi-prod-base-bayes-m mapi-prod-base-bayes-l base-ml (sklearn.*) mapi-prod-base-ml-s mapi-prod-base-ml-m mapi-prod-base-ml-l base-forecast (ts.*, causal.*) mapi-prod-base-forecast-s mapi-prod-base-forecast-m mapi-prod-base-forecast-l base-dl (dl.*, v0.15) mapi-prod-base-dl-s mapi-prod-base-dl-m mapi-prod-base-dl-l

From v0.15, the inventory also has one GPU Job: mapi-prod-base-dl-gpu (see GPU jobs). Only a GPU base (base-dl) has a GPU Job. A spec of the GPU class for a model of another namespace is refused at placement: "only dl models run on the GPU class".

The names use MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE (default mapi-{env}-{base}-{class}). The infrastructure must make exactly these Jobs. Each Job must have:

  • max-retries = 0 (the platform decides about retries).
  • The execution service account (get and delete on the bootstrap bucket, and no other permissions).
  • The static environment MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL=gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce}.
  • The deny-all network and the restricted Google APIs VIP.

XL runs are for the GKE executor (planned). The dispatcher refuses XL runs for cloudrun-jobs.

docs.title: GPU jobs v0.15
docs.text:
Not verified

The GPU Job is written to the Cloud Run documentation, but it is not applied or tested against GCP. The base-dl CUDA image is not tested on a GPU. Do a test with a small run before you use it.

The resource class GPU runs on the Job {base-dl, GPU}:

Field Value Image base-dl (mapi-jax[cuda12]: jax[cuda12] from pip wheels on python-slim, no NVIDIA base image) Resources cpu = "8", memory = "32Gi", nvidia.com/gpu = "1" Node selector accelerator = "nvidia-l4" Zonal redundancy off (gpu_zonal_redundancy_disabled = true) Other fields The same service account, network, environment and max_retries = 0 as the CPU Jobs

To make the Job:

  1. Select a region that has Cloud Run GPUs (L4) and request the GPU quota for the project.
  2. Build and push the base-dl image. It is about 3 GB, because of the CUDA wheels.
  3. In Terraform, set images["base-dl"] and gpu_jobs = true in the exec module. The default is false.
  4. Apply. Set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_GPU_JOBS=true on the orchestrator. Without it, the executor does not offer the GPU class.
  5. Submit a small dl.cnn_classifier run of the class GPU.
  6. Open the run. Make sure that the param dl.backend is gpu and that the run has no GPU_UNAVAILABLE warning.

The cost of a GPU attempt adds accelerator_seconds (wall time × 1) at the price of the class GPU in the price table (the default is the Cloud Run L4 list price, [verify]).

docs.title: What one attempt looks like
docs.text:
1. The dispatcher writes the intent row (run, attempt, nonce) and the bootstrap object bootstrap/<nonce>. The bootstrap object is the RunSpec with signed URLs and the HMAC key.

  2. The dispatcher calls jobs.run on the selected Job with only these overrides:

    • MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE.
    • taskCount.
    • The task timeout. This is the timeout of the run plus MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S. Thus the supervisor can flush checkpoints before the backstop.

    Nothing goes in args. 3. The metadata of the operation names the execution. The dispatcher keeps the execution name as the handle of the attempt, and it logs the operation name. 4. The supervisor reads and deletes its bootstrap object. It runs the worker and prints events with HMAC signatures. The events go from Cloud Logging to Pub/Sub to POST /internal/events. 5. The reconciler polls executions.get. After the execution is complete, it also polls tasks.list for the exit codes. If there are no events, the reconciler only marks the run stalled. The status from the executor decides if the run is alive.

Execution outcome Reported as Run outcome All tasks succeeded succeeded, exit 0 finalized after the complete event Supervisor exit 16 (checkpoints flushed) failed or cancelled, exit 16 finalized as partial Exit 137, or "memory limit exceeded" failed, exit 137 failed (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), retry with the next larger class Task timeout failed, exit 143 failed (TIMEOUT) Cancelled through executions.cancel cancelled cancelled, or partial if it flushed Execution not found unknown cancelled and confirmed gone, then retried as an infrastructure failure

docs.title: Orphans and duplicates
docs.text:
Cloud Run selects the execution names. Thus the nonce identifies an execution. The dispatcher can stop after jobs.run but before it keeps the handle. If this occurs, the reconciler calls adopt(nonce). It lists the recent executions of each Job in the inventory. Then it finds the MAPI_NONCE override in the execution template [verify M0].

If two executions have the same nonce, the reconciler keeps the oldest and cancels the others. A duplicate that starts finds no bootstrap object, because the first execution deleted it. The duplicate then stops and does no work.

A jobs.run call can fail in a way that is not clear, for example a timeout or a 5xx after the dispatcher sent the request. The dispatcher never retries this call without a check. The next submit of that nonce adopts first.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
jobs.run has a limit for each project and region (180 calls a minute [verify M0]). Each orchestrator keeps a token bucket at MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE (default 150). Divide the quota between the orchestrator replicas.

A 429 answer means that Cloud Run made nothing. The executor then does these steps:

  1. It puts all submitters into a shared cool-down. This is an exponential back-off from MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S. It is at least the Retry-After of the server, but never more than MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S.
  2. It counts the answer as an alarm. The alarm shows in these locations:
    • ALARM cloudrun-jobs: jobs.run answered 429 in the log.
    • throttled_last_hour in the executor health.
    • mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total{executor} at /metrics. The MapiJobsRun429 alert monitors this metric.
  3. It retries the same nonce.

After MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES answers in sequence, the run goes back to the queue for a new attempt. This does not use one of its MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES. Thus a large quantity of throttled calls makes runs late, but it never makes them fail.

While a dispatcher works through a batch, it extends the leases of the runs that it has not submitted yet. Thus the reconciler never takes a run whose submit is only slow. If one submit stops for more than ten lease lengths, the renewals stop. The leases then expire. The reconciler adopts what jobs.run made (by nonce), or it retries the attempt.

docs.title: Fan-out with taskCount
docs.text:
Homogeneous children of a fan-out parent can run as the tasks of one execution (RunSubmit.task_count). Homogeneous children have the same kind, class, base and timeout. Each task i does these actions:

  • It reads its own bootstrap object at a nonce. The nonce comes from the execution nonce and CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX (mapi_server.executors.tasks.task_nonce).
  • It gives numbers to its events from task_seq(i, 0). Thus the event dedupe keeps the events of all tasks.
  • It writes its outputs under .../a{n}/tasks/{i}/.

The execution succeeds only when all tasks succeed. A cancel stops all of them. Fan-out parents (SBC, Backtest) can use tasks. The executor side is ready. v0.14 retired the Sweep document: a sweep is a workflow with a search.grid node.

docs.title: Events: authenticated Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
A Cloud Logging sink with the filter jsonPayload.mapi_event:* publishes the event lines of the supervisors to a topic. A push subscription with OIDC authentication sends them to POST /internal/events. Configure the expected token:

export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE=https://api.example.com/internal/events
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=mapi-events-push@mapi-prod-control.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS=projects/mapi-prod-control/subscriptions/mapi-run-events-push

The server then does a check of each push in this sequence, before it reads the body:

  1. The RS256 signature of the bearer token, against the JWKS of Google. The server keeps the JWKS in a cache, as Cache-Control tells. An unknown key id causes a maximum of one new fetch each 30 s. If the JWKS is not available for a short time, the cached keys continue to work.
  2. The claims of the token. The issuer is Google, and the audience is ours. The push service account has a verified e-mail. The token is not expired (60 s leeway).
  3. The subscription name, against MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS.

If a check fails, the server answers 401/403, and Pub/Sub retries. Configure a dead-letter topic. The server then decodes the message: the base64 Cloud Logging entry, jsonPayload.mapi_event and the run.googleapis.com/execution_name label. The server verifies the HMAC of the event with the key of its attempt. It removes duplicates on (run, attempt, seq) and merges the event into the progress row of the run.

If an event is forged or replayed, the server acknowledges it (200) and changes nothing. It counts the event as a sandbox violation.

In the multi-tenant profile, the endpoint refuses all requests until you configure push authentication. For a local setup, you can set MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN instead.

docs.title: Bundle signatures with Cloud KMS
docs.text:
export MAPI_SIGNER=kms
export MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION=projects/mapi-prod-control/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/mapi/cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/2
export MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS=projects/.../cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/1

The server sends only the SHA-256 digest of a manifest to asymmetricSign (EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256 or RSA_SIGN_PSS_*_SHA256). It does a check of the response for verified_digest_crc32c, the key version name and signature_crc32c. It verifies the signature locally before it keeps it. At startup, the server loads the public keys of the active and trusted versions. Thus, before the server mints URLs, it verifies a manifest locally and never waits for KMS.

To rotate the key, do these steps:

  1. Make a new key version.
  2. Set MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION to the new version.
  3. Keep the old version in MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS until no model version that it signed is in use.

With Terraform, these settings are control.kms_key_version and control.kms_trusted_key_versions (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md).

docs.title: Cloud Storage
docs.text:
GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run(...) signs V4 URLs and POST policies through the IAM Credentials signBlob API. It uses a token that it refreshes (the control-plane service account). It signs create-only POST policies as an uploader account. This account can make objects, but it cannot delete them. GCS POST forms do not accept a generation precondition. Thus an account that cannot delete cannot overwrite.

The URLs are byte-identical to the URLs from the V4 signer of google-cloud-storage. The store does a check of each write against the CRC32C and MD5 that Cloud Storage calculated. Copies pin the source generation and compare the result. Refer to GCS shim.

docs.title: Executor conformance and load
docs.text:
An executor gets shared tiers only after it passes two suites. These are the executor conformance suite (mapi_spec.conformance_executor) and the security suite. The conformance suite has these cases:

  • Submit, and orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash.
  • Duplicate submit, and cancel during a run.
  • Timeout, and stalled-not-lost.
  • Confirmed cancel before retry, and checkpoint resume.
  • OOM classification and fan-out.
  • Generation verification and 429 back-off.
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py      # fake-cloudrun, local-process
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py -m docker   # needs a daemon
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_load_cloudrun.py -s           # 100 fits; prints metrics

Each case runs the real dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and finalizer. It does a check of the exact sequence of run states, which a database trigger records. The load test sends 100 concurrent fits through cloudrun-jobs over the fake backend. It has these conditions:

  • The outputs are on the GCS shim.
  • The events come as Pub/Sub pushes that are late and duplicated.
  • There are three 429 answers and two lost jobs.run responses.

At the default of 150 submits a minute, the test measures a p95 time-to-running of about 46 s. No run is lost, and each run has exactly one execution. Real Cloud Run cold starts add more time.

docs.title: The shared-tier gate
docs.text:
The code enforces the gate. The dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on an executor only when these two conditions are true:

  1. The caps of the executor permit it: an isolation of gVisor or higher, with egress and DNS enforced.
  2. A passing executor-conformance report and a passing security-suite report are on record. They must be for exactly the caps that the executor reports now. Neither report can be older than MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S. The default is 3 days, so the nightly suites keep the gate open.

A security-suite report is evidence of enforced egress and DNS only under one condition. The http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes must run, and the executor must stop them. A skipped probe is not evidence. Record results with PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence (only operators, with an audit record). Include the target of the suites:

curl -X PUT "$API/v1/admin/executors/cloudrun-jobs/evidence" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"target": {"executor": "cloudrun-jobs", "caps": <caps from GET /v1/admin/executors>,
                  "remote_control_api": true, "enforces_memory_limit": true},
       "conformance": <ConformanceReport>, "security": <mapi-security --json output>}'

Until you record the evidence, the dispatcher keeps verified and public runs in the queue. It never makes them fail because evidence is missing. GET /v1/admin/executors shows shared_tiers_enabled: false, with the reason in message. It also shows conformance_passed and security_passed.

The executor stays enabled for the trusted tiers. enabled and the disabled status are the switch of the operators (PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}, incident containment). They are never the switch of the evidence gate. Evidence for other caps does not count, for example after a change to the region list or to MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED. The gate does not apply to internal and self_hosted_trusted tenants.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT — Exec project that holds the Job inventory (necessary) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 Region of the inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} Rule for Job ids MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, sci, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts, causal: base-forecast; dl: base-dl (v0.15) Plugin namespace to base (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes Base for runs without a plugin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_GPU_JOBS false v0.15: the inventory has the GPU Job of base-dl. Runs of the class GPU go to it MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 Token bucket in front of jobs.run (maximum 180) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 Number of 429 answers in sequence before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 Exponential back-off after a 429 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + margin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false The DNS response policy is verified for Jobs [verify M0]. verified and public tenants need the two settings, and also recorded evidence MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption looks MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT — Expected push token (set the two) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any Accepted subscriptions (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL Google's The source of the OIDC signing keys MAPI_SIGNER local local (PEM key file) or kms MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION, MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS — Active key versions and key versions that are still trusted

docs.title: Configuration reference v0.3
docs.text:
You configure each component with environment variables. Only three components read a config file: the CLI and the Python client (~/.config/mapi/config.toml), and Docker Compose (.env). This page lists each MAPI_* variable in the code base, in groups for the component that reads it. A test (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py) looks for the variables in the source tree. If a variable is not on this page, the test fails.

Each docs build makes two tables from the code:

  • The server settings: each mapi-server field with its type and default.
  • The index of environment variables: each MAPI_* name in the code, the images, the Terraform and the deploy scripts. The index tells which files use the name, and which section below explains it.

New in v0.3

Sign-in and tenancy (MAPI_PROFILE, MAPI_OIDC_*, MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, MAPI_SERVER_SECRET, the two database roles), quotas and cost (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH, MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED), the Cloud Run Jobs executor (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_*), Cloud Storage and KMS (MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs, MAPI_SIGNER=kms), Pub/Sub push authentication and observability (MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN, MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT). On Google Cloud, Terraform sets them (the deployment contract).

The short version

For a local stack, you need only the four addresses, and only when a different process uses a port: MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN. Export the same values in each shell that runs make dev, make seed, make e2e, mapi or the Python client. Troubleshooting has an example.

docs.title: Topology (every component)
docs.text:
These variables come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev. This is the one contract that these components share: the API, worker, runner, GCS shim, make dev, make seed, the end-to-end tests and (through VITE_*) the web app. Thus all components agree about the location of each service.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_ENV local Environment name. The buckets are mapi-{env}-quarantine, -bootstrap, -runs, -bundles, -data DATABASE_URL (or MAPI_DATABASE_URL) unset A postgresql:// URL. If unset, make dev and mapi serve start an embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver) in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/pg MAPI_API_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 The address where the API listens and where clients connect. make dev gets the host and port of the API from it MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT http://127.0.0.1:4443 The object store (the GCS shim). Signed URLs point here MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5173 The origin of the web app. The API and the shim permit it for CORS MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The origin of the plot sandbox. Must be different from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN. All components refuse a configuration where they are equal MAPI_DATA_DIR .local Local state: pg/, gcs/ (objects and the keys of the shim), keys/ (the bundle-signing key), executions/, dev/

docs.title: mapi-server (API and worker)
docs.text:
mapi-server api, worker, migrate and dev read mapi_server.settings.Settings. Each field is the variable MAPI_<FIELD>. These are the variables in addition to the topology above:

Identity and API

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev (multi-tenant with the built-in development identity provider). The local-process executor refuses multi-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID, MAPI_PROJECT_ID default The tenant and project of the platform. They are the only tenant and project of a single-tenant installation. Platform runs, for example describe, are in them MAPI_API_HOST, MAPI_API_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8000 The bind address of mapi-server api when you start it without --host/--port MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS 127.0.0.1,localhost,api The Host header values that the API answers (comma-separated). The host of MAPI_API_URL is always permitted. * turns the check off. This is the DNS-rebinding guard of the unauthenticated M1 API MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES unset The addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of the API, comma-separated. Examples are the load balancer, the Cloud Run front end and the /v1/ proxy of the web container. For a request from one of these proxies, the client address is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy. The limits for each address (sign-up, verification, embed views), the Sybil same_ip check and the audit fingerprints use this address. none: clients connect directly, and the server ignores X-Forwarded-For. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile. make dev sets none for its multi-tenant stack MAPI_DEBUG false Put tracebacks into the untrusted_text of problem documents. Never use this in production MAPI_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warning or error MAPI_LOG_JSON true One JSON object for each log line (structlog, with trace_id/span_id and the context of the request, run and tenant). false gives a console format for persons MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics (refer to Observability) MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset The bearer that a scraper must send on GET /metrics. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile, which refuses scrapes without it (the series contain tenant ids and spend) MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 Serve the GET /metrics of the worker (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer series) on this address. The same bearer rule as the API applies MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Make OpenTelemetry spans for requests, outgoing HTTP calls and runs MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset The OTLP/HTTP collector that gets the spans. The server also reads it from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. If unset, the server makes spans but does not export them MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN unset If set (and Pub/Sub push authentication is not set), POST /internal/events needs this bearer token. A multi-tenant profile with neither refuses all pushes MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset Set the two to make POST /internal/events need an OIDC token that Google signed for the service account of the push subscription. Refer to Authentication and the Cloud Run settings below MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S 15 The seconds between : keepalive comments on event streams MAPI_SSE_POLL_S 5 The fallback poll of an event stream when no PostgreSQL NOTIFY comes MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S 60 How frequently an open event stream does a check of the credential of its caller again. Revoked tokens, ended sessions and lost access close the stream MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES 8 MiB The largest JSON sidecar (plots.json, diagnostics.json, …) that the control plane parses

MAPI_PROFILE means two things

Do not export a client profile name in a shell that starts make dev or mapi-server. The server refuses all values other than single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev. The CLI and the Python client read MAPI_PROFILE as the name of a config-file profile. The server reads it as the deployment profile.

Database

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE 10 Request-path connections for each process (and the same number of overflow connections) MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_POOL_SIZE 5 Platform-role connections for each process (the orchestrator) MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_POOL_SIZE 5 Gateway-role connections for each process (the API and events service) MAPI_DB_ECHO false Log each SQL statement MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL unset The dedicated login of the request-path role (row-level security applies). If unset: DATABASE_URL with the start-up option role=$MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL unset The dedicated login of the platform role. It is the only role that bypasses row-level security. The dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and housekeeper of the orchestrator use it. The API never needs it. If unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL unset The dedicated login of the gateway role. The API and events service use it for look-ups before they know the tenant (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, pushed events). Row-level security applies. If unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE, MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE mapi_app, mapi_system, mapi_gateway The three runtime roles that mapi-server migrate makes and grants (refer to Authentication)

Authentication (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_AUTH_REQUIRED on, but not for single-tenant Make all routes that are not public need a session or API token. You cannot turn it off in a multi-tenant profile MAPI_SERVER_SECRET from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH The root secret of the API-token pepper, the audit fingerprints and the key that seals webhook secrets. All API and worker instances must share it. If you change it, all tokens and webhook secrets become invalid MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH server-secret next to the bundle-signing key The file that holds the root secret (0600). mapi-server migrate makes it. Compose keeps it on the keys volume MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE on when MAPI_API_URL is https Session cookies with the __Host- prefix and Secure. Off: mapi_session/mapi_csrf for development with plain HTTP MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER unset The OpenID provider (for example https://accounts.google.com). If unset outside the dev profile, browser sign-in is off, but tokens still work MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration The location of the metadata of the provider MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET unset The OAuth client that you registered for the BFF. The secret is optional for public clients. The server always uses PKCE MAPI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI $MAPI_API_URL/auth/callback The registered redirect URI MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS RS256,ES256 The ID-token algorithms that the server accepts (only asymmetric) MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS mapi-cli Public OIDC clients of the same issuer. The API accepts their ID tokens as Authorization: Bearer (what mapi login sends). Comma-separated. If empty, the API accepts only API tokens. In the dev profile, these clients can also use the built-in IdP with a loopback redirect MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS {} More authorization parameters as JSON, for example {"hd": "acme.com"} MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS unset The verified e-mails that sign in as platform operators (comma-separated) MAPI_DEFAULT_TENANT_ADMINS unset The e-mails that the server invites as admins of the default tenant at start-up. The user gets the invitation at the first sign-in with that verified e-mail MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS admin@dev.local,analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local The accounts of the dev profile. The first is an operator and tenant admin, the second is a runner, and the other accounts are viewers

Quotas and cost (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH unset A JSON PriceTable. If unset: list prices like Cloud Run prices (mapi_spec.cost.DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE) MAPI_ESTIMATE_WALL_S fit 300, score 30, ingest 60, … For each run kind, the wall time in seconds that the server charges against vCPU-second quotas until it meters the run (JSON). The maximum is the timeout of the run MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED true Enforce requests_per_minute at token, tenant and global level MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES 500 The queued runs that the fair-share planner of the dispatcher looks at in each pass. This does not include runs that are held by a suspended tenant, the kill switches or the spend cap MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT 50 The maximum number of these runs for each tenant. Thus the held runs of one tenant cannot push out the runs of other tenants MAPI_EXECUTOR_REPORT_INTERVAL_S 10 How frequently each dispatcher reports executor health for /v1/admin/executors MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S 259200 (3 days) How long a recorded conformance or security-suite report lets an executor take verified and public tenants (the shared-tier gate)

Plot rendering and embed links (v0.4)

Refer to Sharing plots.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S 300 The wall-clock limit of a POST /v1/plots:render run. The sandbox stops the run after this time MAPI_INSPECT_TIMEOUT_S 300 The wall-clock limit of an upload inspect run (POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/inspect). The run reads only the metadata of the file MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED false Accept Plotly plots for static rendering. This needs kaleido and a Chrome or Chromium in the runner image. The base images do not include them. While this setting is off, the server refuses Plotly renders with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE 300 The public views in each minute for one embed link. More views get 429 RATE_LIMITED MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE 120 The public embed requests in each minute from one client address, valid or not valid. This makes token guesses slower MAPI_EMBED_CACHE_S 60 How long an API instance uses the resolved plot of an embed again. The server still does a check of expiry and revocation on each request. Responses are Cache-Control: private, no-cache. Thus a revoked link stops on the next load MAPI_EMBED_IMAGE_URL_TTL_S 900 The life of the signed URL of the PNG fallback of an embed

Object storage

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim shim (the GCS shim at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT), gcs (real Cloud Storage. It needs the gcp extra, MAPI_URL_SIGNER and MAPI_URL_UPLOADER) or memory (only for tests) MAPI_GCP_PROJECT unset With gcs: the project of the Cloud Storage client (default: the project of the environment) MAPI_URL_SIGNER unset With gcs: the service account that signs URLs through IAM signBlob. Thus no key file is necessary MAPI_URL_UPLOADER unset With gcs (necessary): the account that signs create-only upload policies. Each run uses these policies for its outputs. It must be different from MAPI_URL_SIGNER. It can make objects, but it must never delete them. A GCS POST form has no generation precondition. Thus only a signer without storage.objects.delete makes the form create-only. The server does not start without this account MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT The base URL in signed URLs, when browsers or containers connect to the shim with a different host name MAPI_GCS_ROOT $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs The state directory of the shim. The server reads the key files of the principals under _shim/keys/ MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE $MAPI_GCS_ROOT/_shim/keys/control.json The key file of the principal of the control plane MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN from exec.json The bearer token of the exec principal of the shim. The server gives it to local runs (only local executors, never in the cloud)

Executors

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process local-process, docker, docker-gvisor or cloudrun-jobs (Cloud Run Jobs executor, with its own settings) MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND mapi-runner next to the interpreter The command line of the supervisor (shell-quoted) for local-process MAPI_EXECUTOR_WORKDIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/executions The scratch directory of the local executor for each run MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE mapi/base-bayes:<version> The runner image of the docker executors for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES mmm, sci, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts, causal: base-forecast; dl: base-dl (v0.15) Plugin namespace to runner image (JSON), with the tag of the workspace version MAPI_DOCKER_GPUS false v0.15: give a run of the class GPU one NVIDIA GPU (a Docker device request). The host needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. With false, a GPU run uses the CPU and shows GPU_UNAVAILABLE (docker) MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK none The network of the run containers: container:<gcs-shim container>, or an internal network that contains only the shim. The server refuses none while the bootstrap URL is HTTP MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED false Declare that MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK is an internal network with only the shim. Then docker-gvisor reports enforced egress and DNS. verified and public tenants also need a recorded security-suite run in which the network probes were stopped (docker) MAPI_DOCKER_RUNTIME_GVISOR runsc The OCI runtime of docker-gvisor MAPI_CANCEL_GRACE_S 10 The seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when you cancel a run

Dispatcher and reconciler

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DISPATCH_RATE_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_DISPATCH_BURST 180, 10 The token bucket in front of the executor (the jobs.run quota of Cloud Run) MAPI_DISPATCH_BATCH, MAPI_DISPATCH_POLL_S 10, 1 The queued runs that the dispatcher leases in each pass, and the pause between passes MAPI_DISPATCH_LEASE_S 120 How long the lease of a dispatcher on a run lasts. While the run waits for submission, a live dispatcher extends the lease after each third of this time. The maximum is ten lease lengths for each submit MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS all The trust tiers whose runs this orchestrator leases (comma-separated). If many orchestrators serve different exec pools, they need lists with no common tiers. If not, each orchestrator leases the runs of all tenants MAPI_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S 10 The level-triggered loop of the reconciler MAPI_STALL_INTERVALS 15 A run is stalled (a warning) after this number of progress intervals without events MAPI_COMPLETE_EVENT_GRACE_S 60 How long to wait for the complete event of a run after the executor reports an exit MAPI_LOST_EXECUTION_GRACE_S 60 How long an execution can be missing from the executor before the attempt is lost MAPI_DEADLINE_GRACE_S 60 The extra time after the timeout of a run before the reconciler stops it MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES 2 The automatic retries after infrastructure failures MAPI_HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_S 300 The sweep of expired upload intents (the server deletes their quarantine objects), expired browser sessions and abandoned sign-ins MAPI_TRACKING_RETENTION_DAYS unset v0.11. The days after a run finishes that the server keeps its metric points and its user log lines (1 to 36500). The housekeeping sweep deletes older rows in batches. The server always keeps the metric summaries, the value of each metric without a step, the params, the tags, the name and the note, thus search and comparison continue to work. If you do not set it, the server keeps the points while it keeps the run. See Track metrics, params and tags. MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_WINDOW_S 1800 No automatic retry of a run that has continued for longer than this time MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR 2 No automatic retry when the cost of a run is this multiple of its estimate MAPI_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 The attempts of the finalizer job before a run fails

Catalog and signing

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CATALOG_PATH unset A catalog JSON that the image build exports. If unset, the worker puts a sandboxed describe run in the queue MAPI_IMAGE_DIGEST sha256 of uv.lock The digest of the runner image. The catalog cache uses it as the key MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH found above the working directory The uv.lock whose hash is the image digest. When it is unset, the digest of a source checkout also hashes packages/*/src and plugins/*/src, so make dev makes a new catalog after a code change MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH $MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem The EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests (in place of Cloud KMS). The worker signs and the API verifies, thus the two must load the same file. mapi-server migrate makes it MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS none Old bundle-signing keys (PEM files, public or private, comma-separated) whose signatures still verify. Thus a key rotation does not break the models that the old key signed (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md) MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE true Make the key at the first use if it is missing. Compose turns it off for api and worker. Thus, if the key is missing, start-up fails, and the server does not mint a new key MAPI_SIGNER local local: the key file above. kms: a Cloud KMS asymmetric key version signs (gcp extra) MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION unset With MAPI_SIGNER=kms: the projects/…/cryptoKeyVersions/N that signs new manifests MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS none Older key versions whose signatures still verify (comma-separated, for rotation)

Cloud Run Jobs (MAPI_EXECUTOR=cloudrun-jobs; refer to Cloud Run Jobs executor)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT unset (necessary) The exec project that holds the Job inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 The region of the inventory MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY derived The data residency of the platform tenant, of tenants that the migrations adopt, and of tenants that you make without a residency. Default: with cloudrun-jobs, the multi-region of MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION (eu for europe-west1). If not, us MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} The rule for Job ids. It must agree with the Jobs that the infrastructure makes MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, sci, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts, causal: base-forecast; dl: base-dl (v0.15) Plugin namespace to base image family (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_GPU_JOBS false v0.15: the inventory has the GPU Job of base-dl (Terraform gpu_jobs). Then runs of the class GPU of dl models go to it. With false, the executor does not offer the GPU class. Not verified against GCP (GPU jobs) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes The base for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 The token bucket in front of jobs.run for each orchestrator (maximum 180, the regional quota) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 The number of 429 answers in sequence before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 The exponential back-off after a 429 (never shorter than Retry-After) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + this margin. The reconciler stops runs at their deadline. This margin is the backstop MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress, but not the restricted Google APIs VIP MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false We verified that the DNS response policy applies to Jobs (the M0 DNS red-team gate). The dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on the executor only when the two settings are true and passing suite evidence is on record (the shared-tier gate). verified is the default tier. Until then, the server refuses their runs at submission MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption lists executions

Webhooks (v0.4) (refer to Endpoints and webhooks)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S 2 How frequently the relay of the worker looks for due deliveries. The relay gives them to the webhooks procrastinate queue MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 The tries for each delivery (1 to 8). Retries wait 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h, plus a jitter of up to 10% MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER 20 Disable a webhook after this number of consecutive events that the server could not send. A 410 Gone disables it immediately. The audit log records webhook.disabled MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_PER_PROJECT 25 The maximum number of webhooks for one project (more get 409) MAPI_WEBHOOK_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The days that the server keeps events and their delivery logs MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE unset An extra PEM CA bundle that the server trusts for receivers (a private CA). The server always uses the system trust store MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP false Only for development: accept http:// URLs for the hosts in MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST. Refused in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST none Only for development: host names (comma-separated, optionally host:port) that the SSRF address and port checks do not apply to, for example a receiver on localhost. Refused in the multi-tenant profile

The server seals webhook signing secrets with a key from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET. If you change the server secret, you cannot use the webhook secrets. Rotate them after the change.

Workflows (v0.5) (refer to Workflows)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WORKFLOW_TICK_S 1 How frequently (seconds) the workflow loop of the orchestrator moves active workflow runs forward, and fires due schedules and debounced triggers MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS 20 The workflow runs that one project can have at the same time, with sub-workflow runs. More runs get 429. A subworkflow.run node over the limit fails with QUOTA_EXCEEDED MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_SCHEDULES 20 The active cron schedules for each project MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_TRIGGERS 20 The active dataset-version triggers for each project MAPI_WORKFLOW_NODE_TIMEOUT_S 1800 The timeout of the child run of a node when the node sets no timeout MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_JSON_OUTPUT_BYTES 1048576 The largest JSON output (tables, metrics, reports, plots) that a node can return. A larger output fails the node (INTEGRITY_FAILURE)

Pub/Sub push events (POST /internal/events)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE unset The expected audience of the OIDC token of the push subscription. When set, each push needs a token that Google signed MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset The service account that the subscription signs as (set it together with the audience) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any The accepted subscription names (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs The OIDC signing keys of Google

Sign-up, e-mail and abuse controls (v0.4) (refer to Sign-up and abuse controls)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED on in dev and multi-tenant when a mailer works, off in single-tenant Self-service sign-up at POST /auth/signup. If you set it on without a mailer that works, the server does not start MAPI_MAILER outbox in dev, smtp in multi-tenant, console in other profiles console (log the message), outbox (JSON files that you read at GET /dev/outbox in dev), smtp or none. multi-tenant refuses console and outbox while sign-up is on, because each person who reads the logs or the disk could verify all addresses MAPI_MAIL_FROM modeling-api <no-reply@mapi.localhost> The From: header MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/outbox The directory where the outbox mailer writes (mode 0600, the newest 200 messages stay) MAPI_SMTP_HOST, MAPI_SMTP_PORT unset, 587 The SMTP server. Without a host, the smtp mailer is off, and sign-up is also off MAPI_SMTP_TLS starttls starttls (necessary, not opportunistic: the server refuses an SMTP server without it) or ssl (implicit TLS, port 465). The server verifies the certificate against the system trust store MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME, MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD unset SMTP authentication (keep the password in a secret store) MAPI_SMTP_TIMEOUT_S 10 The connection and command timeout MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN/verify-email?token={token} The link that the server sends in the e-mail for a sign-up. The server replaces {token} MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS none The e-mail domains that the server refuses, in addition to the built-in disposable list (comma-separated, subdomains included) MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH unset A file of disposable domains, one on each line (# comments), for example a public list that a group keeps current MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR 5 The sign-ups that the server accepts for each client address in each hour MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY 25 The verified sign-ups for each e-mail domain in each day. Unverified sign-ups do not count. The shared free-mail domains are exempt MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR 500 The verified sign-ups in each hour on the whole platform (unverified sign-ups do not count) MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS built-in list (gmail.com, outlook.com, ...) Free-mail domains that persons with no relation share (comma-separated, replaces the built-in list). These domains have no cap for each domain and no domain_burst flag MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE 20 The e-mail verification attempts for each client address in each minute MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS 30 The look-back of the Sybil heuristics MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD 3 The workspaces from one client address, browser or e-mail in the window. After this number, the server flags the next workspace for review. The server flags a domain at two times this number in one hour MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND false Suspend the workspace of a flagged sign-up until an operator approves it. Default: the workspace works and waits in the review queue MAPI_SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The server deletes unverified sign-ups, with their e-mail, after this number of days MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED false Cut line B (planned): let identity-verified public tenants run uploaded code. Off: public tenants run only built-in models and declarative specs

Tenant deletion and GDPR export (v0.4) (refer to Deleting data)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S 604800 (7 days) The grace period of a deletion. During this period, the tenant is suspended and can cancel the deletion MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S unset To request a deletion, also need a sign-in that is not older than this number of seconds. If unset, only the confirmation phrase is necessary MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S 3600 How long a purge waits for the cancelled runs of the tenant to stop before it continues MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 The automatic retries of a failed purge, with back-off from 5 minutes to 6 hours. After this, an operator retries MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The retention period of the bundles bucket (Terraform bundle_retention_days). It tells when a purge retries the objects that a retention lock kept MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S 15 The interval of the deletion and export scheduler of the orchestrator MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES 256 MiB The dataset bytes in an export archive. The manifest lists the remaining bytes MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S 604800 (7 days) How long the server keeps an export archive MAPI_EXPORT_LINK_TTL_S 900 The life of the signed download link of an export (a new link on each GET) MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY 3 The exports that a tenant can request in each day (one at a time) MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES 256 MiB The metadata rows in an export archive. The manifest lists the tables that are not complete MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S 3600 The maximum time of an export build. If a build is still running five minutes after this time (its process stopped), the server builds it again one time. Then the build fails

docs.title: The runner (per run)
docs.text:
Executors start mapi-runner with exactly these variables. Its arguments contain nothing secret. Never set these variables manually.

Variable Meaning MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE The run, and the 256-bit nonce of its one-time bootstrap object MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL A template with {nonce}: the location where the supervisor reads (and deletes) the bootstrap object MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN Only local executors: the exec principal of the shim. It can only get and delete bootstrap objects MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The interpreter of the worker (default: the interpreter of the supervisor) MAPI_BASE_IMAGE The base image in the lineage of the run MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION The docker executor sets it to 1. The supervisor then fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION, and it does not run the worker in dev mode MAPI_TRACEPARENT The W3C traceparent of the dispatching span. Thus the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor contain the trace id of the run. Nothing goes out of the sandbox MAPI_LOG_JSON 1 (the default) makes the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor JSON lines. 0 makes plain text

The supervisor gives the untrusted worker only an allow-list of variables (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale and thread-count variables, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, XLA_FLAGS, …). The supervisor removes all MAPI_* variables.

In the runner images, MAPI_CACHE_SEED (/opt/mapi/cache) is the read-only PyTensor and Numba cache that the image build makes. MAPI_CACHE_DIR (/tmp/mapi-cache) is the writable symlink farm that the entry point builds over it (Container images).

docs.title: The GCS shim
docs.text: mapi-gcs-shim serve gets its defaults from the topology: MAPI_DATA_DIR (state in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs), MAPI_ENV (bucket names), MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT (host and port) and MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN (the CORS origin). Each has a command-line flag. Refer to the GCS shim reference. If you set MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS, it is also the locked retention of the bundles bucket in days when the shim makes its state. 0 means no retention. If unset, the bucket is write-once, for about 100 years.

docs.title: The CLI and the Python client
docs.text:
Variable Meaning MAPI_URL The API. If unset, the client uses MAPI_API_URL, then the profile, then http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_TOKEN An API token (mapi_…), sent as Authorization: Bearer. It has priority over a stored mapi login sign-in. The client never sends it over plain HTTP to a host that is not loopback MAPI_PROJECT The project to act in, <tenant>/<project> (v0.3). The client sends it as X-Mapi-Project on project-scoped requests. It has priority over mapi use MAPI_PROFILE The profile of the config file to use (refer to the warning above) MAPI_CONFIG The config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml, if not set ~/.config/mapi/config.toml) MAPI_CREDENTIALS The file where mapi login keeps sign-ins (default credentials.json next to the config file, mode 0600) MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER The identity provider for mapi login (https, or plain http on a loopback address for a local development provider) MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID The OIDC client id of the CLI (default mapi-cli) MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL The location of the discovery document of the issuer, when it is not under the issuer. The built-in IdP of the dev profile has the issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost. It serves its document at <api>/dev/idp MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Only for identity providers that need a secret from installed apps (for example Google "desktop" clients). The CLI never prints it

Arguments (--url, --token, --project, --profile, or Client(base_url=…, token=…, project=…)) have priority over the environment. The environment has priority over the file. mapi config show prints the result and the source of each value. mapi login, mapi use and mapi config set write the config file again atomically with mode 0600.

docs.title: make dev
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py reads the topology variables and these variables:

Variable Meaning MAPI_STACK_PROFILE The MAPI_PROFILE of the servers. dev is the default: sign-in through the built-in development IdP, the default tenant and project, and the seeded accounts of MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS, with admin@dev.local as tenant admin and platform operator. The other values are single-tenant (the M1 API without credentials) or multi-tenant. The name is different, so a CLI MAPI_PROFILE in your shell never goes to the servers MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN Outside the single-tenant profile, the script makes a random bearer for POST /internal/events in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/internal-token. It gives the bearer to the servers. The end-to-end suite reads it there MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE, MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST If you do not set them, the dev profile writes a temporary CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/ (ca.pem, cert.pem, key.pem). It trusts the CA and puts the two hosts on the allow-list. Thus webhooks can get to an HTTPS receiver on your machine (the receiver of the M3 end-to-end suite) MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD Replace the command of one service (shell-quoted). <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS, for example MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --port 8000" NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR Disable or force coloured service prefixes

make dev ONLY=api and make dev WITHOUT=web,plots select services. make seed SIZE=full loads the large demo. These are make arguments, not environment variables.

make seed, make e2e and python -m mapi_conformance run --stack sign in to a stack that needs sign-in. If MAPI_TOKEN is set, they use it. If not, they sign in through the development IdP as MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT (default admin@dev.local). They act in MAPI_PROJECT (default default/default).

docs.title: The web app and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
These are Vite build-time variables. make dev sets them from the topology. For a production build, set them yourself.

Variable Default Meaning VITE_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:8000 The API that the app calls (it must permit the origin of the app) VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox. It must be different from the app origin VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS http://127.0.0.1:4443 The origins of signed storage URLs. The CSP connect-src of the app permits them VITE_APP_ORIGINS (sandbox) http://127.0.0.1:5173,http://localhost:5173 The origins that can frame the sandbox and send messages to it VITE_AUTH_BASE VITE_API_BASE The location of the sign-in routes (/auth/*), when they are not on the API base VITE_TERMS_URL /terms The terms of service that sign-up links to (an http(s) URL or a path on the origin of the app). The default is the plain-language summary in the app VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL /acceptable-use The acceptable-use policy that sign-up links to, in the same way. A public installation must publish its own versions of the two documents

The Playwright smoke suite of the web app serves the app on 5173 and the sandbox on 5174. If other processes use these ports, set MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT and MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT. The suite then builds the app for that sandbox origin. It exports the origin to the specs as MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_ORIGIN.

The index.html of the sandbox has a %MAPI_CSP% placeholder. Its Vite build replaces the placeholder with the Content-Security-Policy. It is not a variable that you set.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example).

Variable Default Meaning POSTGRES_PASSWORD necessary The database password. Compose does not start without it MAPI_VERSION the workspace version The mapi/* image tag (make compose-up sets it) MAPI_ENV local The same as above MAPI_STACK_PROFILE dev The MAPI_PROFILE of the servers, the same as for make dev MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process The executor of the worker MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY, MAPI_WORKER_CPUS 4g, 12g, 4 The /tmp of the worker (the scratch of each local-process run), the memory limit and the CPUs DOCKER_GID 0 With the docker executor override: the group that owns the Docker socket

docs.title: The mapi/web image (nginx)
docs.text:
The container puts these variables into the nginx configuration when it starts. It replaces only MAPI_* variables.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT the local defaults The origins in the CSP and frame-ancestors headers MAPI_API_UPSTREAM http://api:8000 The location where nginx sends /v1/ (a URL without a path) MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES 127.0.0.1 localhost The host names that the app server answers (space-separated). All other Host values get no response. Keep it in step with MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA empty Extra script-src sources for the app. A wider CSP needs a review NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR /etc/nginx/templates/all …/web or …/plots serves only one of the two apps

docs.title: Image build arguments
docs.text:
Use docker build --build-arg NAME=value. The Makefile gives VERSION, VCS_REF and BUILD_DATE. The defaults define each image. Change them only to build a variant.

Argument Meaning MAPI_PACKAGES The workspace packages that the build installs into the image (mapi-runner mapi-steps mapi-pymc …) MAPI_WORKER_PACKAGES The packages that the worker target adds to base-bayes (mapi-plugin-ts mapi-plugin-causal mapi-server[docker]) MAPI_NO_INSTALL The distributions that the build never installs (the 300 MB nvidia-nccl-cu13) MAPI_APT_PACKAGES The system packages of the runtime stage (tini, and g++ for PyTensor) MAPI_XLA_PREALLOCATE, MAPI_XLA_FLAGS v0.15: the values of XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE and XLA_FLAGS in the image (empty by default). base-dl sets false (GPU memory on demand) and --xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true (deterministic GPU operations). Not verified on a GPU MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT, MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT The distributions that must be installed, and that must not be installed. If not, the build fails MAPI_IMAGE_NAME, MAPI_DESCRIPTION OCI labels, and the name that the catalog export records PYTHON_IMAGE (and the other base images) Base images, pinned by tag and digest (make docker-pin)

docs.title: Deploying to Google Cloud
docs.text:
The deploy scripts under deploy/gcp/ get their settings as flags (--help on each). One variable changes the location of their local files:

Variable Meaning MAPI_DEPLOY_OUT The local scratch directory of deploy/gcp/*.sh: images files, saved plans and Terraform outputs. The default is deploy/gcp/.out, with one directory for each environment. Never commit it MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL A repository secret of the nightly workflow: the Pushgateway that gets mapi_security_probe_unexpected from the security jobs. If unset, the jobs do not push (ops/README.md)

Deploy to Google Cloud lists the variables that Terraform sets on the Cloud Run services (the deployment contract with mapi-server).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_E2E pnpm --filter @mapi/web e2e sets it: run the Playwright @e2e suite against a stack that runs MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT The development-IdP account that make seed and the end-to-end suites sign in as (default admin@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_ACCOUNTS The two development-IdP accounts that the M2 tenancy suite makes tenant admins (default analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_UI_ACCOUNT The tenant admin of the M2 browser flow and the fit burst (default analyst@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS Opt-in: the number of concurrent real fits that tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py submits (M2 verification) MAPI_E2E_SIGNUP_ACCOUNT The address that the M3 trust-lifecycle suite (tests/e2e/test_m3_trust_stack.py) uses to sign up. It must be a development-IdP account, so that it can sign in (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_GUIDED_ACCOUNT The address that the M3 journey (tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py) uses to sign up. It is a development-IdP account (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_KEEP 1 keeps the project that the M3.5 journeys make (tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py, apps/web/e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts). It also keeps the project of the forecasts-with-actuals journey (tests/e2e/test_forecast_actuals_stack.py). Thus you can look at the project in the app (M3.5 verification) MAPI_E2E_WEBHOOK_TLS_DIR The location where the webhook receiver of the M3 journey finds cert.pem and key.pem (default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls) MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS 1 makes the contract snapshot of mapi_spec and the Guided catalog fixture of the server tests again (make snapshots) MAPI_HYPOTHESIS_EXAMPLES The examples for each property in the wire-format round-trip tests (default 60) MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA The data/ directory of a local copy of pymc-challenges. The from_challenges loaders of mapi-plugin-science read the real data files there, and the tests that use them run. If it is not set, these tests are skipped MAPI_E21_DRAWS The draws for each chain in the real-data sociality fit of sci.network_latent_space (plugins/science/tests/test_network.py, default 300)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_DOCS_SPEC The spec that scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs (make docs-screenshots) opens and fits, default eu-geo-mmm. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN MAPI_DOCS_PROJECT The project that scripts/docs_screenshots_admin.mjs (make docs-screenshots-admin) selects after it captures the project switcher, default Default project. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL and MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT MAPI_SCIENCE_DATA The folder of the exported datasets that scripts/docs_screenshots_science.mjs (make docs-screenshots-science) uploads, default .local/science: scotland_lip.nc, heat_plate_e51.nc and lazega_coworkers.nc for the tutorials, and also unc13_dstorm.nc, primates301.nc and bci_camera_traps.nc for the Data Explorer. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL and MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT MAPI_GUIDED_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/guided-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the screenshots of the Guided tutorial from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-guided sets it, with MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT/MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT at the defaults 15173/15174. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_EXPLORER_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/explorer-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the explorer, About-card and budget-plan screenshots of the docs from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-explorers sets it, with the same port defaults. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_WORKFLOW_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/workflow-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the screenshots of the docs for workflows (gallery, editor, run monitor, schedules, Guided recipe) and governance (policies, policy editor, review queue, validation, evidence), from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-workflows sets it, with MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT/MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT at the defaults 15183/15184. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_SHOTS_DIR A directory. When set, the workflow and governance smoke specs (apps/web/e2e/workflows.spec.ts, governance.spec.ts) also save full-page screenshots of their screens there MAPI_EMBED_VIEW The EmbedView JSON that scripts/docs_screenshots_tutorials.mjs (make docs-screenshots-tutorials) serves to the embed page of the plot sandbox. scripts/docs_embed_view.py writes it (default .local/embed-view.json). The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (default ports 15173/15174) MAPI_EMBED_API The API origin where the embed page asks for the view in that script. Playwright answers (default http://127.0.0.1:8000, the VITE_API_URL of the sandbox dev server). No process must listen there

docs.title: Docker Compose v0.2
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml runs the container images of the platform as a local stack on one machine. It uses the dev profile, the same as make dev (sign in as admin@dev.local, refer to signing in). It runs the same services as make dev, on the same ports, but from the exact images that production uses.

You do not need Docker for development (refer to Local, without Docker). Use compose to do a full check of the images, or to run a self-contained demo. Container images tells what is in each image, how the build makes it, and the build-time checks.

cp .env.example .env               # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD
make docker-build                  # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make compose-up                    # docker compose up -d --wait
make seed                          # load the E33 demo through the API
open http://127.0.0.1:5173
make compose-logs SERVICE=api      # follow one service
make compose-down                  # VOLUMES=1 also deletes the database and objects

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph ns["shared network namespace (gcs-shim)"]
        shim["gcs-shim :4443"]
        api["api :8000"]
        worker["worker<br/>(local-process runs)"]
    end
    pg[("postgres :5432")]
    web["web :8080"]
    plots["plot-sandbox :8081"]
    browser(("browser")) -->|127.0.0.1:5173| web
    browser -->|127.0.0.1:5174| plots
    browser -->|"127.0.0.1:4443 (signed URLs)"| shim
    web -->|/v1/ proxy| api
    api --> pg
    worker --> pg
    migrate["migrate (one-shot)"] --> pg
Service Image Published on the host postgres postgres:16 (pinned by digest) not published. Refer to the override example gcs-shim mapi/gcs-shim 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 (the API, which shares this namespace) migrate mapi/server, migrate. Compose waits until it stops with status 0 — api mapi/server, api through gcs-shim worker mapi/worker, mapi-server worker, MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process — web mapi/web with only the app server block 127.0.0.1:5173 plot-sandbox mapi/web with only the sandbox server block 127.0.0.1:5174

Why api, worker and gcs-shim share one network namespace. Signed URLs contain the address of the object store. The bootstrap URL template also contains it for runner processes. The API could connect to the shim as gcs-shim:4443, while the browser needs 127.0.0.1:4443. Then each URL would need a public form and an internal form. With a shared namespace, 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 mean the same thing to the browser, the API, the orchestrator and each runner subprocess. This is exactly the make dev topology, and it agrees with the LocalDev defaults. The web container connects to the API as api:8000, which is a network alias of the container of the shim.

Durable state. Three named volumes stay after the containers stop: pgdata (the database), gcsdata (the objects and principal key files of the shim) and keys (the bundle-signing key). The finalizer of the worker signs each bundle manifest. The API verifies that signature before it gives an artifact link, a ui/ view or a plot. It also verifies the signature before it accepts a score request. Thus the two services must load the same key, and the key must stay after restarts.

migrate makes the key one time at /var/lib/mapi/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH). api and worker mount the volume read-only, with MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false. Thus, if the key is missing, start-up fails with a clear error, and the services do not mint a new key without a message. MAPI_DATA_DIR (/tmp/mapi-data) is the scratch directory of each container.

Caution

Do not delete the key without the database and the objects. A new key cannot verify old bundles. make compose-down VOLUMES=1 deletes the key together with the data.

Hardening. Each mapi/* service runs as a non-root user, with a read-only root filesystem, a tmpfs on /tmp, all Linux capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges. Compose publishes ports on 127.0.0.1 only. The PostgreSQL password comes from .env, and compose does not start without it. The official postgres image is the one exception. It starts as root to set the owner of the data directory, then it changes to the postgres user.

Host names. The M1 API has no authentication. An attacker can point the host name of a web page at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding). The page is then same-origin to itself, so CORS does not stop it. Thus the API answers only the Host names in MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (default 127.0.0.1, localhost, api, and also the host of MAPI_API_URL). For all other names, it returns 400.

The nginx server of the app answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (default 127.0.0.1 localhost). It closes the connection for all other hosts. The GCS shim does the same, for loopback names and the hosts of its endpoints (--allowed-host adds more). If you connect to the stack with a different name, for example a LAN host name, add it to the two variables.

docs.title: Executor choice: local-process vs docker
docs.text:
The compose worker runs the local-process executor inside a runner-capable image. Each run is a mapi-runner subprocess of the worker container. This is the default, because it needs no Docker socket and works with all daemons. The two executors have these differences:

local-process in mapi/worker (default) docker executor (compose.override.example.yml) Isolation Process only: runs share the uid, filesystem (with its keys, refer to the text below), /tmp and memory limit of the worker One container for each run, from the exact runner image, with its own limits and a network that connects only to the shim Images One large image with all plugins and the control plane mapi/worker for the orchestrator. For each run, the mapi/base-* image that contains the plugin of the run (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES) Privileges Only the privileges of the worker The worker mounts /var/run/docker.sock, which is root-equivalent on the host Networking Runs connect to 127.0.0.1:4443 directly Run containers join the gcs-shim network namespace (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=container:mapi-gcs-shim) Use it for Daily development, demos, CI A full check of the production images, and self-hosted setups (gVisor runsc in v0.3)

Docker executor settings. MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES maps a plugin namespace to its runner image. mmm.*, sci.* and tabular.* (also tabular.image_logistic, v0.14) run in mapi/base-bayes, sklearn.* (with LightGBM and CatBoost from v0.14) in mapi/base-ml, and ts.* and causal.* in mapi/base-forecast. A workflow node run goes to the image of the model that it runs. This is its model parameter (for example a backtest or search of ts.sarimax). If there is no model parameter, it is the plugin of the model version that is bound to the node. Examples are a forecast, an evaluation or a governance check of a fitted model. Runs without a model plugin (ingest, describe, statistical tests) use MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE. The defaults are the tags that make docker-build makes for the current version.

Deep learning and the GPU class v0.15. dl.* runs in mapi/base-dl. This image has mapi-jax[cuda12]: JAX with the NVIDIA CUDA wheels from pip, on python-slim (no NVIDIA base image). It is about 3 GB. mapi/base-bayes and mapi/base-ml also have mapi-jax for the CPU, so the step dl.embed works in front of their models.

The docker executor accepts the resource class GPU:

  • With MAPI_DOCKER_GPUS=true, the executor asks Docker for one NVIDIA GPU (a device request with the driver nvidia and the capability gpu). The host needs the NVIDIA driver and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
  • With MAPI_DOCKER_GPUS=false (the default), the run gets the CPU and memory of the GPU class and no GPU. JAX uses the CPU. The run shows the warning GPU_UNAVAILABLE.

The local-process executor also accepts GPU and always uses the CPU.

Warning

The GPU path of mapi/base-dl is not tested. The project has no GPU. Do a test with a small run and make sure that the param dl.backend is gpu.

MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK must give the run a path to the object store, because the bootstrap object and each signed URL point at it. In compose, the run joins the network namespace of the shim (container:mapi-gcs-shim). An internal Docker network that holds only the shim also works, if MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT names the shim on that network. With none, the runner cannot get its bootstrap object. Thus the worker does not start with none.

docker-gvisor for verified and public tenants. Shared tiers need an executor with egress and DNS enforced. You cannot use none. Thus, do these steps:

  1. Make an internal network that holds only the shim (docker network create --internal mapi-sandbox).
  2. Attach the shim to this network, and to no network that routes out.
  3. Set MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=mapi-sandbox.
  4. Declare the network with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED=true. The executor refuses host, bridge and default.

The executor then reports enforced egress and DNS. But the dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on it only after these conditions:

  • The security suite ran against it, and the executor stopped the http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes.
  • That result and a passing conformance run are on record (the shared-tier gate).

Worker isolation in run containers. A run container starts its supervisor as root, with no-new-privileges. All Linux capabilities are dropped, but not the few that the uid split needs. The supervisor then starts the untrusted worker as uid 10001, which has no capabilities. Thus the worker cannot signal the supervisor or write to its event pipe. It also cannot read the environment of the supervisor or of the init process. The executor also sets MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1. With this setting, the supervisor fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION, and it does not run the worker under its own uid.

The two modes are not a multi-tenant boundary. They are single-tenant local stacks. The local-process executor refuses all multi-tenant profiles.

What a local-process run can reach. Each run is a subprocess of mapi-server worker, and it runs as the same uid, 10001. There is no uid split before v0.3. Thus run code (the plugins and the steps that they load) can read all that the orchestrator can read:

  • The control key of the shim (/shim/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json). It gives storage.admin on all buckets. This is sufficient to read or write bundles, datasets and run outputs again, and to mint signed URLs.
  • The bundle-signing key (/var/lib/mapi/keys/). This is sufficient to forge a manifest that the API accepts.
  • The executions directory under /tmp/mapi-data. This includes the pid files that name the nonces of the runs that are in progress.

Thus, in this mode, bundle signatures and the output checks of the finalizer protect against accidents, but not against hostile plugin code. The orchestrator marks itself non-dumpable. Thus run code cannot ptrace it or read its memory. Run code also cannot read its /proc/<pid>/environ (DATABASE_URL with the password). The worker also logs this warning at start-up.

Warning

Run only trusted plugin code under local-process. Other code can read the keys above.

The docker executor does not have this risk. Each attempt runs in its own container, and none of these files are mounted. The /tmp of the worker is the scratch space for local-process runs. Set its size with MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_CPUS in .env.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example). POSTGRES_PASSWORD is necessary. These variables are optional:

  • The MAPI_WORKER_* sizes.
  • The image version (MAPI_VERSION, which the Makefile sets).
  • MAPI_API_UPSTREAM and MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA of the web image.

All the variables are in the configuration reference.

compose.override.example.yml shows the two usual changes: it publishes PostgreSQL on the host, and it changes the worker to the docker executor. To use it, copy it to compose.override.yml. Version control ignores this file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Troubleshooting tells about these problems: a missing Docker daemon, a missing POSTGRES_PASSWORD, an unhealthy api container, a read-only /tmp and ports that are already allocated.

docs.title: Deploy to Google Cloud v0.3
docs.text:
This page tells how to change empty Google Cloud projects into a multi-tenant platform that operates. It applies to an environment (dev, staging or prod). At the end, you have these items:

  • The API and the web app on Cloud Run.
  • Runs that execute as Cloud Run Jobs in a zero-egress sandbox project.
  • Data in private buckets behind a VPC Service Controls perimeter.

All the configuration is in infra/terraform. Four scripts in deploy/gcp operate it.

Status: written, validated and tested offline; not yet applied

The Terraform passes terraform validate for each environment. It also passes a terraform test suite that applies each module against mocked providers (refer to Testing the infrastructure). We have not applied it to a real organisation yet. The cloud adapters of the server (Cloud Run Jobs executor, Cloud Storage, KMS signing, Pub/Sub push verification) are in the same release. We tested them only against fakes. The environment variables that they read are below. Read the next section before you start.

docs.title: Before you start: the [verify M0] checklist
docs.text:
The design depends on cloud behaviours that the Google Cloud documentation suggests. But nobody has confirmed them against a real Cloud Run Jobs execution yet. The plan marks each behaviour [verify M0]. These behaviours do not break a dev environment. But do not admit untrusted tenants until each one has a recorded pass. The full procedure, with the probe for each item, is the M0 verification checklist. The steps that remain after the offline M2 verification are in M2 verification.

Assumption What depends on it If it is not true The Direct VPC egress resolver obeys the DNS response policy (*. to NXDOMAIN, Google APIs to the restricted VIP) DNS exfiltration is stopped. You can set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED to true. Only this setting lets verified and public tenants run Cloud Run Jobs cannot host untrusted code. Keep shared tiers off it. Use GKE Sandbox behind the same executor protocol Deny-all egress and VPC Service Controls apply to Jobs executions Runs cannot connect to the internet or to buckets outside the perimeter The same as above gen2 permits the supervisor/worker uid split with no_new_privs, seccomp and no ptrace The worker cannot read the credentials of the supervisor Runs report DEV_MODE_ISOLATION. The runner images must start the supervisor as root for the split Execution overrides are env-only (no image, resources, service account or network) jobs.run can give only the run id and nonce The role of the dispatcher must have fewer permissions The limits of the in-memory filesystem operate as planned (no ephemeral disk, exit 137 at the limit) Scratch budgets of 3/6/12 GiB for classes S/M/L. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with a retry in the next larger class Fits with large data move to GKE You cannot restore a deleted bootstrap object The nonce in the audit log points at nothing Terraform already sets the soft-delete window of the bootstrap bucket to 0. If you can still restore a copy, examine the bootstrap design again before launch Quotas: 180 jobs.run in each minute and 1,000 running executions in each region The token bucket of the dispatcher (150 a minute by default) and the global limit of 700 concurrent runs Decrease MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE. Divide the work across exec projects The cold start of a base image of about 2.5 GB keeps the p95 of time-to-RUNNING below 90 s The M2 latency target (met offline, only against the fake backend) Smaller images, or warm capacity (planned) The path from the Logging sink to Pub/Sub carries the labels of the execution in some seconds. Pub/Sub can push to an internal-only service Run events and progress Runs still finish (the status of the executor decides if a run is alive), but there is no progress Cloud SQL managed connection pooling works in transaction mode with the driver of the server. The migrate role can grant BYPASSRLS Row-level security for requests. The platform role for the orchestrator Give mapi_orchestrator its own policy-based access (the explicit policy is already there) run.jobs.runWithOverrides works without iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the execution account The least-privilege role of the orchestrator Grant actAs on that one account Cloud Run accepts the image indexes that build-push.sh pushes (with attestations) Deploys Build with --no-attestations

Two more limits of v0.3 are not cloud facts, but they are important on the first day:

  • Browser sign-in uses an OpenID provider with an authorization-code endpoint (Google by default). The server does not accept the tokens of Identity Platform yet. Refer to Authentication.
  • The nightly security suite has no probe Job in Terraform yet (Security suite).

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
One environment has five types of project, one for each trust zone (plan §8.1):

flowchart TB
    users(("browsers ·<br/>clients")) -->|HTTPS| lb["global HTTPS load balancer<br/>app.example.com · plots.example.net"]
    subgraph control["control project (trusted)"]
        lb --> api["api<br/>Cloud Run"]
        lb --> web["web · plots<br/>Cloud Run"]
        events["events<br/>Cloud Run, internal"]
        orch["orchestrator<br/>worker pool"]
        sql[("Cloud SQL<br/>PostgreSQL 16")]
        kms["KMS<br/>bundle signing"]
        topic["Pub/Sub<br/>run events"]
        api --> sql
        orch --> sql
        events --> sql
        topic -->|"push + OIDC"| events
    end
    subgraph perimeter["VPC-SC perimeter"]
        subgraph exec["exec-paid · exec-public (hostile)"]
            jobs["Cloud Run Jobs<br/>3 bases × S/M/L<br/>deny-all egress"]
            sink["Logging sink<br/>mapi_event lines"]
        end
        subgraph data["data project"]
            buckets[("quarantine · bootstrap · runs<br/>bundles · data")]
        end
    end
    subgraph build["build project"]
        ar["Artifact Registry<br/>images · curated PyPI"]
    end
