    orch -->|"jobs.run (env: run id, nonce)"| jobs
    jobs -->|"signed URLs only<br/>(restricted VIP)"| buckets
    jobs --> sink -->|Publish| topic
    jobs -. pull .-> ar
Module Project Creates control control Cloud Run api, events, web, plots. Orchestrator worker pool. migrate job. Cloud SQL (private IP, managed connection pooling). Secret Manager secrets. Pub/Sub topic, push subscription and dead letters. One Logging sink for each exec project. KMS signing key. Identity Platform. Optional load balancer exec each exec project VPC without a default route, deny-all egress firewall, restricted-VIP route and DNS zone, DNS response policy, the Job inventory, the execution service account, the dispatcher role data data The five buckets of plan §8.6 with lifecycle rules, retention, CORS and bucket-level IAM build build Docker repository (immutable tags), curated PyPI remote, Binary Authorization attestor (stub), GitHub Workload Identity Federation perimeter organisation The VPC-SC perimeter around the exec and data projects stack all Connects the modules and enables the APIs

envs/<env>/main.tf holds the policy of each environment, where code review sees it. The policy includes the database size and availability, the deletion protection, the retention lock and the perimeter mode. terraform.tfvars holds only names and ids.

dev staging prod Database Enterprise, 1 vCPU, zonal, no pooler Enterprise Plus, zonal, pooler Enterprise Plus, regional (HA), pooler VPC-SC perimeter dry-run (optional) enforced, necessary enforced, necessary Load balancer + domains optional optional necessary Deletion protection off on on Bundle retention 1 day, unlocked 7 days, unlocked 30 days, locked Signing key software software HSM Minimum instances (api) 0 1 2

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An organisation with an Access Context Manager policy (gcloud access-context-manager policies list --organization ORG_ID). Without a policy, you can deploy only dev, without the perimeter. Each plan then shows a warning.
  • Projects that the project vending of your organisation makes: control, data, build, and one exec project for each pool. The pools are exec-paid, and also exec-public when you have public tenants. Link all projects to billing. Put nothing else in the exec projects.
  • Tools: Terraform ≥ 1.11 (tested with 1.14), gcloud, Docker with buildx, python3 and curl.
  • Permissions for the first run: project owner (or equivalent) on each project, and roles/accesscontextmanager.policyEditor on the organisation policy. Later runs use the CI identities that Terraform makes.
  • An OAuth client (web application) for the app origin, for browser sign-in.

docs.title: 1. Bootstrap the projects
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh --env staging --region europe-west4 \
  --control-project acme-mapi-stg-control --data-project acme-mapi-stg-data \
  --build-project acme-mapi-stg-build \
  --exec-project paid=acme-mapi-stg-exec-paid --exec-project public=acme-mapi-stg-exec-public \
  --state-project acme-mapi-stg-build --dry-run       # read what it will do, then drop --dry-run

The script enables the APIs of each project. It uses the same lists as modules/stack/apis.tf, and a test keeps the lists identical. It makes the state bucket (uniform access, public access prevention, object versioning). Then it writes infra/terraform/envs/staging/backend.hcl.

docs.title: 2. Describe the environment
docs.text:
cp infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars.example infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
$EDITOR infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars

Type these values:

  • The project ids and the region.
  • The bucket location. Use the data residency of your tenants.
  • The exec pools and the access policy id.
  • The domains, the OAuth client id and the GitHub repository.

The file holds no secrets. Do not commit it.

Data residency and the exec region

The dispatcher puts a run only on an executor whose region satisfies the data residency of its tenant. The default residency is the residency that the region of the dispatch pool satisfies: eu for europe-west4. This default applies to the platform tenant and to each tenant that you make without a residency. To change the default, use the default_residency of the control module.

The exec region can be unable to satisfy the residency of a tenant. Then the server refuses its runs at submission (403, "no executor of this platform can run this tenant's work"). The worker also logs a warning for the tenant at start-up. To change the residency of a tenant, use PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{id} (data_residency).

docs.title: 3. Apply the foundation
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging --foundation

A foundation apply makes all resources except the Cloud Run workloads and Jobs, which need images. It makes the registry, networks, DNS policy, database, secrets, buckets, perimeter and CI identities. deploy.sh always shows the plan. Before it applies the plan, it asks you to type the environment name.

During this apply, ephemeral resources make the database passwords, the token pepper and the session key. Write-only arguments write them. They are in Secret Manager only. They are not in the state and not in the plan file.

docs.title: 4. Add the OAuth client secret
docs.text:
export TF_VAR_oidc_client_secret='...'      # from the OAuth client
# in terraform.tfvars: oidc_client_secret_version = 1

The secret is an ephemeral Terraform variable. Terraform writes it to Secret Manager as a new version and never keeps it. When you rotate the secret, increase oidc_client_secret_version. Add the identity providers that you want to Identity Platform. Use the console, or google_identity_platform_*_idp_config resources outside this module.

docs.title: 5. Build and push the images
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/build-push.sh --env staging

The script builds server, web, base-bayes, base-ml, base-forecast and base-dl for linux/amd64. It pushes them as <version>-<git sha>. Tags are immutable in the registry. Thus, if you run the script again for the same commit, it uses the images that are there. The script writes the digests of the images to deploy/gcp/.out/staging/images.tfvars.json. Terraform refuses all images that are not pinned by digest.

docs.title: 6. Deploy the release
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging

The script does these steps:

  1. It does a terraform plan with terraform.tfvars and the images file, and saves the plan to a plan file.
  2. It asks for confirmation. Type the environment name. In automation, --yes skips this step.
  3. Migrations first: it points the mapi-staging-migrate job at the new server image and executes the job (deploy/gcp/migrate.sh). Migrations are expand/contract. Thus the release that serves now continues to work on the new schema. On the first release, the job is not there yet. Thus the migrations run immediately after the apply.
  4. It does a terraform apply of exactly the saved plan.
  5. It records the images file as a release in gs://<state bucket>/mapi/staging/releases/<UTC timestamp>-<release id>.json. The release id is a hash of the images. Thus, if you retry a deploy of the same images, it is the same release.
  6. It does a smoke test. The test does a check of the API /healthz and /readyz, the web app (with a Content-Security-Policy) and the plot sandbox. It also makes sure that the events service refuses requests from the internet.

docs.title: 7. Point DNS at the load balancer
docs.text:
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/envs/staging output lb_ip

Make A records for the two domains. The Google-managed certificate becomes available when DNS resolves. This often takes 15–60 minutes. Until then, run deploy.sh --skip-smoke. Without domains, the services answer on their run.app URLs (terraform output urls).

docs.title: 8. Verify the controls
docs.text:
Before the first production deploy, read the security hardening page and do the M0 verification checklist. When the DNS item has a recorded pass, tell the orchestrator in the main.tf of the environment. Then deploy again:

control = {
  # ...
  extra_env = {
    orchestrator = { MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" }
  }
}

Until then, the executor declares that DNS is not enforced. The dispatcher then does not put verified and public tenants on it (trust tiers).

docs.title: 9. Name the operators and create the first tenant
docs.text:
Platform operators are the persons whose verified e-mail is in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS. Set it on the API. Use only plain values. Never put secrets in extra_env:

control = {
  # ...
  extra_env = {
    api = { MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS = "oncall@acme.example,platform@acme.example" }
  }
}

Run deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging. Then an operator signs in to the web app, or with mapi login --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id <the CLI's client id>. The operator makes the tenant of each organisation with its first admin. The server sends an invitation to the admin by e-mail. The admin becomes tenant admin at the first sign-in:

mapi admin tenants create acme --name "Acme Retail" --tier verified --residency eu \
    --admin-email it@acme.example

After this, the tenant admin makes projects and invites persons (Administration). Monitor the platform with the observability dashboards. Import the alerts before you let users in.

Verified tenants cannot run until DNS enforcement is verified

verified and public tenants need an executor with egress and DNS enforced. verified is the default tier of new tenants (the private beta). A new stack does not set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED and has no suite evidence. Thus the server refuses their runs at submission (INFRA_ERROR, 503). Only internal and self_hosted_trusted tenants run. To open the shared tiers, do these steps:

  1. Pass the DNS red-team gate of the M0 checklist from a Job of this environment.
  2. Set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" for the orchestrator through control.extra_env ({ orchestrator = { MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" } }). Then deploy.
  3. Run the executor conformance suite and the security suite against the deployed executor. Record the two results with PUT /v1/admin/executors/cloudrun-jobs/evidence (the shared-tier gate). Evidence expires after MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S, so record the nightly runs.

docs.title: Continuous deployment
docs.text:
.github/workflows/deploy.yml deploys only on manual dispatch, without service-account keys:

Job GitHub environment Google identity Does build <env>-build mapi-<env>-ci-push build-push.sh. Uploads the images file plan <env>-plan mapi-<env>-planner (read-only) deploy.sh --plan-only. The plan goes to the job summary apply <env> mapi-<env>-deployer deploy.sh --apply-plan: migrations, apply of that plan, release record, smoke test

Do these steps for each environment:

  1. Make the three GitHub environments. Put required reviewers on <env> (the apply).
  2. Restrict <env> to protected branches.
  3. Copy the values of terraform output github into environment variables: GCP_WIF_PROVIDER, GCP_CI_PUSH_SA, GCP_PLANNER_SA, GCP_DEPLOYER_SA.
  4. Also add GCP_IMAGE_REPOSITORY (terraform output image_repository), TF_STATE_BUCKET and TERRAFORM_TFVARS (the contents of the terraform.tfvars of the environment).
  5. Optionally, add OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET as a secret of <env>-plan and <env>. You must give an ephemeral variable to the plan and to the apply.

The workload identity provider accepts tokens only from your repository. Each service account trusts exactly one GitHub environment. Thus a job can never get more permissions than its environment permits. A person runs the first apply of an environment, which makes these identities.

The perimeter is an organisation-level resource. Project-level grants cannot include it. Thus give these roles on the access policy yourself, or use a scoped access policy for the projects of the platform:

  • roles/accesscontextmanager.policyEditor to the deployer.
  • roles/accesscontextmanager.policyReader to the planner.

When the perimeter is enforced, persons outside it need an access level (vpc_sc.access_levels) to run Terraform or to read the logs of the exec projects. The deployer has its own ingress rule.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Bucket names are global. The storage contract names buckets mapi-{env}-{purpose} (mapi_spec.storage.bucket_name). Thus mapi-prod-data must be free in all of Cloud Storage. If a different user has the name, select a more specific environment name as a new envs/ directory. The name must agree with ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,15}$, for example acme-prod.
  • KMS key rings are permanent. If you make a destroyed environment again, you must do a terraform import of its key rings.
  • --traffic-only rollbacks apply only to the HTTP services. To roll back the orchestrator and the Jobs, deploy a release again.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The alert policies in ops/alerts/cloud-monitoring-alerts.yaml and the Cloud Monitoring dashboard read the mapi_* series from Managed Service for Prometheus. Nothing outside an instance can scrape them. The load balancer routes only /v1, /auth/* and the health checks, and the orchestrator has no ingress. Thus each server workload (api, events, orchestrator) runs a collector sidecar.

The sidecar is an OpenTelemetry Collector. It scrapes the /metrics of the workload over 127.0.0.1 each 30 s, with the metrics-token bearer. It writes the series to Managed Service for Prometheus. The orchestrator serves its own series on 127.0.0.1:9464: dispatch latency, finalize outcomes, integrity failures, running executions and jobs.run 429s. The runtime identities already have roles/monitoring.metricWriter.

Copy the collector image from Google into the registry of the build project. Pin it by digest, and set it for each environment:

gcloud artifacts docker images copy \
  us-docker.pkg.dev/cloud-ops-agents-artifacts/google-cloud-opentelemetry-collector/otelcol-google:<version> \
  europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/<build project>/mirror/otelcol-google:<version>
# terraform.tfvars
metrics_collector_image = "europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/<build project>/mirror/otelcol-google@sha256:<digest>"

Without the image, a release still deploys, but Terraform shows a warning (check.metrics_collection). Then no mapi_* series goes to Cloud Monitoring, and the PromQL alerts (integrity failure, STALLED rate, spend caps) can never fire. control.metrics_collector also accepts scrape_interval, cpu and memory. The api and events services get CPU only while they serve requests. Thus the sidecar scrapes an idle instance late. This is satisfactory for alerts that use a period of 5 to 15 minutes.

The security-suite series (mapi_security_probe_unexpected) comes from the nightly workflow. The workflow pushes it to the Pushgateway that the MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL repository secret names (ops/README.md).

docs.title: Day-2 operations
docs.text:
Rollback. There are two procedures:

deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --list            # recorded releases, newest first
deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --previous        # redeploy the release before the deployed one
deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --traffic-only    # seconds: services back to their previous revision

A release rollback goes through deploy.sh (plan, confirmation, apply, smoke test) with --skip-migrate, because schema changes only move forward. The script records it as <UTC timestamp>-<id of the release it redeployed>-rollback.json. --previous reads the records again. A retried deploy counts one time. After a rollback from a bad release, a second --previous goes one more release back. It does not go back to the bad release.

--traffic-only moves traffic with gcloud and does not change Terraform. Use it for incidents. It does not change the orchestrator and the Jobs. The next deploy moves traffic to the newest revision again.

Migrations by themselves. deploy/gcp/migrate.sh --env prod --image <server@sha256:...>.

Rotate secrets. Increase one of these values in the main.tf of the environment:

  • control.database.password_version. All three database roles and their connection URLs change in one apply.
  • control.secret_versions.session_secret. This signs out all users.
  • token_pepper. This makes all API tokens invalid.

New Cloud Run revisions use the latest secret versions.

Rotate the bundle-signing key. Do these steps (refer to ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md):

  1. Make a KMS key version.
  2. Set control.kms_key_version to it.
  3. List the previous version in control.kms_trusted_key_versions.
  4. Deploy.

If you remove a version from the trusted list, each model that it signed fails with INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

Add an exec pool. Add an entry to exec_pools. Run bootstrap.sh for its project, then run deploy.sh. The perimeter, the Logging sink, the image-pull grant and the bootstrap-bucket grant change automatically.

Tear down dev. You cannot delete KMS keys. You can only schedule their versions for destruction. Thus the two signing keys have prevent_destroy. First, remove them from the state. Then destroy. Dev has no deletion protection and lets Terraform empty its buckets. Staging and prod refuse this:

cd infra/terraform/envs/dev
terraform state list | grep 'google_kms_crypto_key\.' | xargs -n1 terraform state rm
terraform destroy

docs.title: Environment of the Cloud Run workloads
docs.text:
This is the deployment contract between Terraform (modules/control/locals.tf) and mapi-server. Each name is a mapi-server setting (refer to the configuration reference). If Terraform sets a variable that the server does not read, tests/infra fails. These are the plain values:

Variable Workloads Value MAPI_ENV all Environment name. Buckets are mapi-{env}-* MAPI_PROFILE all multi-tenant (the local-process executor refuses it) MAPI_OBJECT_STORE all gcs: real Cloud Storage, URLs signed without a key file MAPI_GCP_PROJECT all The project of the Cloud Storage client MAPI_URL_SIGNER all The service account whose signBlob signs URLs (no key file is necessary) MAPI_URL_UPLOADER all The service account whose signBlob signs create-only upload policies (run outputs). It can make objects in runs and quarantine, but it can never delete them MAPI_SIGNER, MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION all kms and …/cryptoKeyVersions/<control.kms_key_version> of the EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE, MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE all mapi_app (row-level security), mapi_orchestrator (the platform role, the only RLS bypass) and mapi_gateway (the look-ups of the API before it knows the tenant, RLS applies) MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY all The residency of the platform tenant and of tenants that you make without a residency. It is the default_residency of the control module. If not set, it is the residency that the region of the dispatch pool satisfies (eu for europe-west4) MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES all 169.254.0.0/16 (the Cloud Run front end), 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22 (Google load balancer front ends) and the address of the load balancer. The API skips these hops when it reads the address of the caller from X-Forwarded-For. After the first deployment, make sure that the audit fingerprint of a sign-up is different between two networks. If your topology has more hops, add them through extra_env MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN all, web Public origins (the API shares the app origin behind the load balancer) MAPI_DATA_DIR all /tmp/mapi (in-memory scratch) MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS api, events The host names that the service answers MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID api Browser sign-in MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS events The values that a valid Pub/Sub push token must contain, and the one subscription that can push MAPI_EXECUTOR orchestrator cloudrun-jobs MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST orchestrator 9464 on 127.0.0.1: the /metrics of the orchestrator (dispatch, reconcile, finalize series), for the collector sidecar MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION orchestrator The exec pool that it dispatches to (control.dispatch_pool, default the first pool that is not public). Its Jobs use the default mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} names MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL Jobs gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce} (set on each Job, read by the runner)

These values come from Secret Manager (references that resolve when a revision starts):

Variable Workloads Secret MAPI_DATABASE_URL api, events db-url-app-direct: mapi_app, direct (the LISTEN that feeds SSE) MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL api, events, orchestrator db-url-app: mapi_app through the pooler (transaction mode). Tenant sessions MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL api, events db-url-gateway: mapi_gateway through the pooler. Sign-in look-ups, operator routes, the routing of pushed events (no RLS bypass) MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL orchestrator db-url-orchestrator: mapi_orchestrator, direct. The loops of the orchestrator. Only the service account of the orchestrator can read this secret (plan §9) MAPI_DATABASE_URL orchestrator db-url-orchestrator (procrastinate needs LISTEN) MAPI_DATABASE_URL migrate db-url-migrate: role mapi_migrate (schema owner), direct MAPI_SERVER_SECRET all The root of the API-token pepper and the audit fingerprint key. If you rotate it (control.secret_versions.server_secret), all API tokens become invalid MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN api, events, orchestrator, collector sidecars The bearer that a scraper sends on GET /metrics (the multi-tenant profile refuses scrapes without it) MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET api Only when a client secret version is available

One orchestrator serves one exec pool, and an environment deploys one orchestrator. Runs go only to control.dispatch_pool. Until tier placement across pools (planned), keep all tenants on that pool. A second pool, for example a separate exec project for public tenants, needs a second orchestrator outside this module.

The two orchestrators must then set MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS with no common tiers. For example, set internal,self-hosted-trusted,verified through control.extra_env.orchestrator here, and public on the other orchestrator. If not, leases do not look at pools. Each orchestrator then takes the queued runs of all tenants, and public-tier code can go into the paid pool. Terraform exec_pools[*].public selects only the default dispatch_pool. The server does not read it.

Each workload can get more plain variables through control.extra_env in the main.tf of the environment. Never put secrets there.

docs.title: Testing the infrastructure
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/infra -q                     # everything below
TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR=~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache uv run pytest tests/infra -q   # reuse providers
  • Static invariants (they always run): deny-all egress with exactly two exceptions, no public buckets or principals, max_retries = 0 and gen2 on each Job, the VPC-SC perimeter and DNS policy, write-only secrets, and digest-pinned images. They also make sure that the infrastructure agrees with the mapi_spec contracts (bucket names, resource class sizes, runner environment, the push endpoint).
  • terraform fmt, terraform validate for each environment (with -backend=false).
  • terraform test for each module. The test applies each module against mocked Google providers. Thus it evaluates each expression and connection, and it asserts the security properties on the result values. It uses no credentials and makes no cloud calls.
  • Deploy scripts: --help, argument checks, the confirmation guard and full dry runs. These tests use stub terraform/gcloud/docker/curl binaries that prove that nothing executes. They run under /bin/bash 3.2 and under the bash on PATH. If shellcheck is installed, it also runs.

If terraform is not installed, the Terraform tests are skipped. The first run downloads the Google providers (about 250 MB). It puts them into a temporary cache, but not if TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR is set.

docs.title: Container images v0.2
docs.text:
The platform has six images (and a worker target). The build makes them from images/<name>/Dockerfile, with the repository root as the build context. The images have three purposes:

  • To run the exact production artifacts locally (Docker Compose).
  • To support the docker executor.
  • To become the Cloud Run Jobs in v0.3.
make docker-build                      # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make docker-build IMAGES="server web"  # a subset
make docker-pin-check                  # every base image pinned by digest?

docs.title: The images
docs.text:
Image Contents Runs as Entry point mapi/base-bayes mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, workflow nodes, mapi-pymc, the mmm.*, tabular.* and sci.* plugins (mapi-plugin-science, which uses SciPy), a C++ compiler for PyTensor 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-ml mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, workflow nodes, mapi-sklearn with the gbm extra (sklearn.* plugins, LightGBM and CatBoost from v0.14) and libgomp1 (for LightGBM). No PyMC. 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-forecast mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, workflow nodes, mapi-pymc with the pathfinder extra, the ts.* plugins (mapi-plugin-ts and mapi-plugin-statsmodels), the causal.* plugins (mapi-plugin-causal) and pymc-extras 10001 mapi-runner mapi/worker base-bayes with the ts.* and causal.* plugins and mapi-server (target worker of the base-bayes Dockerfile). Only for compose 10001 mapi-server worker mapi/server The control plane: mapi-server, mapi-spec, the JSON-only mapi-plots core, the JSON-only mapi-workflows engine, docker-py. No science dependencies. 10001 mapi-server api (or worker, migrate) mapi/gcs-shim The local Cloud Storage emulator 10001 mapi-gcs-shim mapi/web nginx that serves apps/web (port 8080) and apps/plot-sandbox (port 8081) 101 nginx

causal.impact uses the ts.bsts model of mapi-plugin-ts. Thus the causal.* plugins are in mapi/base-forecast, and mapi/base-bayes does not contain them. pymc-extras (state space models and the Pathfinder engine) adds preliz, Numba and Matplotlib. Thus mapi/base-forecast is larger than in v0.12. mapi/base-bayes also contains pymc-extras (the Pathfinder engine).

From v0.14, mapi-runner depends on Pillow (for the image_folder ingest). Thus all runner images contain Pillow. Pillow decodes uploaded images only in the sandboxed ingest run, never in the control plane. LightGBM and CatBoost (about 150 MB) are only in mapi/base-ml. tabular.image_logistic runs in mapi/base-bayes and does not need Pillow.

make docker-build IMAGES="server web" builds a subset. make docker-build builds all images. It also builds mapi/worker when base-bayes is in the set. Each image has the OCI labels title, version, revision (git commit) and created.

docs.title: How the Python images are built
docs.text:
Each Python image uses the same multi-stage pattern:

  1. manifests copies the build context. It deletes all files except the pyproject.toml and uv.lock files. Thus its output changes only when dependencies change.
  2. builder installs the third-party dependencies of the package set of the image. It uses only those manifests (uv sync --frozen --no-install-workspace, one time for each package, into /opt/mapi/venv). BuildKit keeps this layer in a cache. Thus, when you edit source code, the build does not install PyMC again. The builder then copies the sources and installs the workspace packages, non-editable. Each version comes from uv.lock.

  3. runtime starts again from the same python:3.12-slim base. It adds tini (and g++ for the PyMC images) and makes user 10001. Then it copies in only the virtual environment.

    The images that run mapi-server (mapi/server and mapi/worker) also copy uv.lock to /opt/mapi/uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH to it. Its SHA-256 is the image digest. The API and the orchestrator use this digest as the cache key of the step and model catalog. make dev calculates the same value. The build makes the two images from one lock, so api and worker agree.

The package set is the MAPI_PACKAGES build argument. images/common/install_packages.py changes it into uv sync calls. The build never installs the xgboost dependency nvidia-nccl-cu13 (MAPI_NO_INSTALL). This is a 300 MB wheel that only multi-GPU training uses.

docs.title: Build-time guards
docs.text:
If an image is not what it claims to be, the build fails:

  • Package assertions. images/common/assert_dists.py does a check of MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT and MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT against the real environment. For example, base-ml must not contain pymc, pytensor or numba, and must contain pillow, lightgbm and catboost (v0.14). base-bayes and base-forecast must contain pillow and must not contain lightgbm or catboost. server must not contain numpy, xarray, pandas, scipy, pyarrow, PyMC, pillow, lightgbm, catboost, mapi_sdk, mapi_runner or a plugin.
  • Import contracts in the control-plane image. The contracts stage of images/server/Dockerfile installs import-linter (hash-pinned from uv.lock) into a temporary copy of the environment. It runs the contracts of the repository against the packages exactly as they are installed. The runtime stage depends on that stage, so BuildKit cannot skip it.
  • Catalog export. The runner images load each installed step, model and plot plugin. They write /opt/mapi/catalog.json with its digest (/opt/mapi/catalog.digest). If no steps or models are registered, the build fails.

We also prove the same claims without Docker. tests/devops/test_container_invariants.py calculates the dependency closure of each image from uv.lock (scripts/lock_closure.py). Then it does a check of the closure against the assertions.

docs.title: Compile caches and the read-only root filesystem
docs.text:
PyTensor compiles C at run time, and Numba keeps machine code in a cache. During the build, a small hierarchical model compiles and fills the two caches. The build then puts the caches read-only into /opt/mapi/cache. PyTensor needs a writable compile directory, because it takes a lock and adds new modules.

Thus, at start-up, the entry point (images/common/runner-entrypoint.sh) builds a symlink farm of the cache under /tmp/mapi-cache. The farm has real directories, with files that are symlinks to the objects in the cache. This uses some KiB of RAM. This is important on the in-memory filesystem of Cloud Run. PyTensor accepts the moved entries and does not compile them again.

HOME, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR and MPLCONFIGDIR all point under /tmp. The first three are on the worker-environment allow-list of the runner (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST). Thus plugin code sees them after the supervisor removes the other variables from the environment. As a result, each image runs with --read-only and a tmpfs on /tmp.

docker run mapi/base-bayes runs the runner. The image gives arguments that start with - to the runner. All other commands replace the runner (docker run mapi/base-bayes python -c ...).

docs.title: The web image and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
mapi/web builds the two Vite apps with pnpm. It uses --frozen-lockfile and --ignore-scripts, so no package lifecycle scripts run. One unprivileged nginx with two server blocks serves the apps. NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR selects which blocks nginx uses: /etc/nginx/templates/all (the default), web or plots. Origins are runtime settings. At start-up, nginx puts them into the headers.

App (:8080, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) Plot sandbox (:8081, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN) CSP default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' (no unsafe-eval, no inline scripts); frame-src = the plots origin; connect-src = self, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; frame-ancestors 'none' default-src 'none'; scripts, styles and images only from its own origin; connect-src = only its own /topojson/; frame-ancestors = the app origin Other headers X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, COOP and CORP same-origin, Trusted Types in report-only mode nosniff, no-referrer, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * API access nginx sends /v1/ to MAPI_API_UPSTREAM, unbuffered, with a read timeout of one hour for SSE None: no proxy, and the CSP blocks it

The app frames the sandbox documents with sandbox="allow-scripts" and no same-origin access. Thus they have an opaque origin, and the browser gets their module scripts, styles and topojson in CORS mode. For this reason, the sandbox answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The assets are static and public, and there are no cookies. For the same reason, its CSP lists the plots origin explicitly next to 'self'.

MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA (empty by default) adds sources to the script-src of the app. Use it only after a review, for example if a library needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Trusted Types stay in report-only mode until the SPA has its policy.

docs.title: Base images and pinning
docs.text:
Each base image is a build argument with a readable tag and a digest:

ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.12-slim-trixie@sha256:a6e3…11b1

The Dockerfile frontend (# syntax=) and the compose postgres image are pinned in the same way. make docker-pin resolves each tag again through the registry API. It needs no Docker daemon. Examine the diff that it makes as you examine each dependency update. make docker-pin-check fails if an image is not pinned. CI and make release-check also run it.

docs.title: Licences in the images
docs.text: Each image has the licence files of the project and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in /usr/share/doc/mapi/. The notices list each third-party Python and JavaScript package in the image set, with its version and licence. They also contain the NOTICE files, and the licence texts of the JavaScript packages that the build compiles into the web app. When uv.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml changes, run make notices to make the file again. While the file is not current, the test suite and make release-check fail. Refer to Licensing.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml builds each image, and the worker target, on each push and pull request. It uses the GitHub Actions layer cache. CI never pushes the images. A separate job does a check of the digest pins. It also validates the two compose files with docker compose config.

You can do a smoke test when you have built the images and a Docker daemon runs. Then uv run pytest tests/devops/test_compose_smoke.py -m docker starts postgres, gcs-shim, migrate, api and worker under a temporary project name. It publishes no host ports. Then it makes sure that api and worker started. It also makes sure that they agree on the values that bundle verification needs: the image digest and the bundle-signing key.

docs.title: Local, without Docker v0.2
docs.text:
make dev runs the whole platform on your machine without Docker. PostgreSQL comes from the pgserver wheel, and object storage comes from the GCS shim. Thus you need only the uv workspace and, for the web app, Node.js with pnpm.

make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make dev              # start everything; Ctrl-C stops everything
make seed             # in another shell: load the E33 demo data and spec
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

The quickstart tells how to fit, examine and score the demo model from the browser. This page tells what make dev runs, how to work on one component, and where the local state is.

docs.title: Signing in v0.3
docs.text:
make dev runs the servers in the dev profile. This profile is multi-tenant, with a development identity provider in the API. The browser shows a sign-in screen. Select one of the seeded accounts on the page of the provider:

Account Role admin@dev.local Admin of the default tenant and a platform operator (the admin console) analyst@dev.local runner in the default project viewer@dev.local viewer in the default project

make seed and make e2e sign in automatically as admin@dev.local. To change the account, set MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT. The CLI signs in with mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp. Each person who can get access to the API can sign in as each of these accounts. For this reason, the profile is only for local development. MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant make dev gives the v0.2 API without credentials. For more data, refer to Authentication and isolation.

docs.title: Signing up v0.4
docs.text:
Self-service sign-up (POST /auth/signup) is on in the dev profile. The server does not send its e-mails. The dev mailer writes each e-mail to an outbox under MAPI_DATA_DIR/outbox. make outbox prints the newest e-mails with their verification links. TO=<address> shows only the e-mails of one recipient. The API serves the same data at GET /dev/outbox?to=<address>.

A verified sign-up makes a public-tier workspace. To sign in to it, sign up with one of the seeded addresses above, because the development identity provider knows only those addresses. A public workspace runs only built-in models and declarative specs. It runs only on an executor with enforced egress and DNS. Thus the local-process executor of make dev refuses its runs (cut line A, refer to Sign-up and abuse controls).

docs.title: What make dev starts
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py is a small process supervisor. It starts each service in the sequence of its dependencies. It waits until a service is ready before it starts the services that need it. All output goes to one terminal. Each line starts with the name of its service (in colour when the output is a terminal).

flowchart LR
    pg[(postgres<br/>.local/pg)] --> migrate
    shim[gcs-shim<br/>:4443] --> api
    migrate --> api[api<br/>:8000]
    migrate --> worker
    shim --> worker
    api --> web[web<br/>:5173]
    plots[plots<br/>:5174]
Service Command Ready when postgres Embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver), data in .local/pg, unix socket only. Skipped when DATABASE_URL is set. pg_ctl reports that it runs, and the mapi database is there gcs-shim mapi-gcs-shim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4443 --cors-origin <web origin> --root .local/gcs The port accepts connections migrate mapi-server migrate (runs one time) It stops with status 0 api mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 GET /healthz returns 2xx worker mapi-server worker with MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process: dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and the finalizer queue. Each run is a mapi-runner supervisor process that starts its own worker process. Started web pnpm --filter @mapi/web dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort The port accepts connections plots pnpm --filter @mapi/plot-sandbox dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174 --strictPort The port accepts connections

Each service gets the same resolved environment: MAPI_ENV, DATABASE_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN and MAPI_DATA_DIR. The values come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev. The services read the same contract, so they always agree about ports. The configuration reference lists all the variables.

The plot sandbox is a separate origin

Plots show in an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> that comes from MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (port 5174), never from the app origin (port 5173). LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts the two on the same origin.

docs.title: Shutting down
docs.text:
Ctrl+C (or make stop from a different shell) stops the services in the opposite sequence of the start. Each service runs in its own process group. The supervisor sends SIGTERM to that group. If the group still runs after the grace period, the supervisor sends SIGKILL. The grace period is 10 s (change it with --grace). Child processes, for example the esbuild of Vite, stop with their parent. A second Ctrl+C stops all processes immediately. The embedded PostgreSQL stops last, but not if you ran scripts/dev.py up --keep-db.

If a long-running service stops without a command, the supervisor stops the whole stack. The supervisor then stops with a status that is not zero. It never starts a service again without a message. The log above the shutdown shows the reason.

docs.title: The first start
docs.text:
At its first start against a new environment, the worker logs no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. The catalog contains the steps, models and plot recipes in the runner, with their settings schemas and schema effects. A sandboxed describe run of the real runner makes the catalog. The server keeps it in a cache for each digest of the environment: the hash of uv.lock and of the workspace sources (packages/*/src, plugins/*/src). Thus the server builds it again after you change the locked dependencies or the code, when you restart make dev. Until the catalog is ready, spec validation reports that the catalog is not available. This takes some seconds.

Runs use the same isolation as in production, but not the parts that a laptop cannot do. The run event DEV_MODE_ISOLATION tells that the worker process runs as your user, without a uid split or no_new_privs.

Plugin code runs as you, next to the platform's keys

Run only plugin code that you trust in make dev. Without a uid split, run code (plugins and the steps that they load) can read all the files that your user can read. These include the control key of the shim (.local/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json, full access to all buckets), the bundle-signing key (.local/keys/) and the executions directory. Thus a hostile plugin could forge a signed bundle, or change outputs after the finalizer did a check of them. On Linux, the orchestrator makes itself non-dumpable. Thus run code cannot read its environment (DATABASE_URL) or its memory. The worker logs the same warning when it starts.

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text:
Command What it does make dev (or make run) Starts the stack in the foreground make dev ONLY=api Starts api and its dependencies (gcs-shim, migrate) make dev WITHOUT=web,plots Starts all services, but not the two Vite servers (for example, while the web app is not built yet) make stop Stops a stack that runs in a different shell, then its embedded PostgreSQL make status Shows which services operate, and if PostgreSQL runs make migrate Applies database migrations one time. If necessary, it starts the embedded PostgreSQL, and then it stops it again. make db-shell psql on the dev database (the embedded server or DATABASE_URL) make seed Loads the E33 demo datasets and the eu-geo-mmm spec through the HTTP API (make seed SIZE=full for the large variant) make e2e Runs the end-to-end suites against the stack: pytest -m e2e (tests/e2e, through the Python client), then the Playwright @e2e suite (apps/web/e2e, through the browser) make outbox Shows the newest e-mails of the dev mailer and their links (sign-up verification). TO=<address> filters make clean-local Deletes MAPI_DATA_DIR (database, objects, supervisor state). It refuses while a service runs. YES=1 skips the prompt. uv run python scripts/dev.py env Prints the resolved environment as export lines, so that you can run a component manually

make seed uses only the public API. It does these steps:

  1. It makes the datasets eu_media_daily, fx_daily and holidays_eu.
  2. It uploads each table to the signed URL that the API returns.
  3. It waits for the sandboxed ingest runs.
  4. It makes the spec that points at the new dataset versions.

If you run it again, it adds new dataset versions and a new spec revision. It uses the same datasets again. make reads SIZE only from the make command line, because some toolchains (the compilers of conda) export their own SIZE variable.

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/ writes the same tables, the E33 score payloads and the spec as files. You can then upload these files through the web app.

docs.title: Science data v0.9
docs.text:
The sci.* models of mapi-plugin-science use the data of the pymc-challenges case studies. make install installs the plugin with the other workspace packages, so a make dev stack can fit these models. To get a dataset that you can upload, write it to a file with the export command:

export MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA=~/pymc-challenges/data      # the data/ directory of a local copy
uv run python -m mapi_plugin_science.export --list           # the cases that you can export
uv run python -m mapi_plugin_science.export e18 --out .local/science/scotland_lip.nc --spec .local/science/e18.yaml
uv run python -m mapi_plugin_science.export e50 --synthetic --out .local/science/assay.nc
  • --challenges gives the data directory. The default is MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA.
  • --synthetic writes the simulated data of the model. It does not need a copy of pymc-challenges. The cases e51 and e61 do not need a data directory.
  • --spec also writes the suggested spec of the case.
  • The suffix of --out sets the format: .nc, .zarr.zip or .tree.zip.

The tutorials of the case studies upload these files through the web app.

The tests of the plugin that read the real data files run only when MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA is set. If it is not set, these tests skip. MAPI_E21_DRAWS sets the draws for each chain of the real-data fit of sci.network_latent_space (default 300).

make docs-screenshots-science captures the screenshots of the science tutorials and of the Data Explorer on scientific data again from a make dev stack. Before you run it, export the cases e18, e51, e21, e58, e23 and e81b to scotland_lip.nc, heat_plate_e51.nc, lazega_coworkers.nc, unc13_dstorm.nc, primates301.nc and bci_camera_traps.nc in .local/science (or in the folder that MAPI_SCIENCE_DATA gives). To capture only the Data Explorer, run node scripts/docs_screenshots_science.mjs .local/screenshots-science explorer. Refer to the header of scripts/docs_screenshots_science.mjs for the full procedure.

docs.title: End-to-end tests
docs.text:
make e2e does the M1 flow through the stack:

  • It uploads the E33 data, validates and fits the spec, and follows the run over SSE.
  • It does a check of the signed manifest and the bundle.
  • It scores an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals.
  • It probes the security boundaries that are visible from outside. The bootstrap object is gone, the server refuses forged events, and the plot iframe is an opaque origin.

Start make dev first. The two suites read the same MAPI_* variables. Thus, if you moved a port, export the variables in the shell that runs make e2e. The browser suite writes screenshots to apps/web/e2e/screenshots/ (git ignores them).

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010   # only if you moved the API
make dev                                     # shell 1
make e2e                                     # shell 2: about 25 minutes

make e2e also runs the M2 tenancy suite and the M3 suites. The M3 suites are the trust lifecycle and the whole Guided journey to an endpoint, webhooks, embeds, budget optimisation, export and deletion (refer to M3 verification). Two settings make the deletion checks complete:

  • Start the stack with MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S=0 (no grace period).
  • On a new MAPI_DATA_DIR, set MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0 (no retention lock on model bundles).

If not, those checks stop where the platform waits, and the suite skips them. Each run signs up two workspaces. The default sign-up limits are 5 for each address in each hour, and 25 for each dev.local in each day. These limits permit two runs in each hour. Thus, on a stack that you test many times, increase MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR and MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY.

Webhooks can get to receivers on your machine. In the dev profile, make dev writes a temporary CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/. The servers trust the CA and permit the two hosts. Serve HTTPS with cert.pem and key.pem from there. Then register https://127.0.0.1:<port>/....

The mocked Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on port 5173. Thus run it only while make dev is stopped.

docs.title: Working on one component
docs.text:
You can run a component yourself, for example with a debugger or auto-reload. There are two procedures. In the first procedure, exclude the component and start it manually with the same environment:

make dev WITHOUT=api,web           # web depends on api, so exclude it too
eval "$(uv run python scripts/dev.py env)"
mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

In the second procedure, replace its command with MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD. The command is shell-quoted. <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS:

MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000" make dev

The readiness probe still applies. Thus a replacement api must answer GET /healthz.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
make dev reads your shell environment. It does not read .env, which is only for docker compose. If you set nothing, all services use the defaults above. To change a value, export the variable first:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000          # move the API (and its probe) to port 9000
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://me@localhost/mapi  # use your own PostgreSQL instead of pgserver
make dev

Export the same MAPI_* URLs in each shell that connects to the stack (make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client). The configuration reference lists all the variables. This includes the variables that only compose or the images use.

docs.title: Where state lives
docs.text:
All local state is under MAPI_DATA_DIR. The default is .local/ in the repository root, and git ignores it.

.local/
├─ pg/                    PostgreSQL data directory (pgserver); log in pg/log
├─ gcs/                   GCS shim objects (buckets mapi-local-*)
│  └─ _shim/keys/         the shim's principals: control.json (control plane), exec.json (runs)
├─ keys/                  bundle-signing-p256.pem: signs bundle manifests (stands in for KMS)
├─ outbox/                the dev mailer's e-mails (make outbox, GET /dev/outbox)
├─ executions/            per-run scratch of the local executor (removed when a run ends)
└─ dev/supervisor.json    pid of the running supervisor and its services (make stop/status)

Caution

Do not delete keys/. If you delete it, you cannot use the registered model versions. Their manifests do not verify, and the API does not mint download links for them (INTEGRITY_FAILURE).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Troubleshooting tells about these problems: port conflicts, an old supervisor, PostgreSQL that does not start, failed migrations, an API that never becomes ready, and blank plots.

docs.title: M2 verification v0.3
docs.text:
Milestone M2 (cloud and multi-tenant core) has five exit criteria:

  1. 100 concurrent fits without loss.
  2. Chaos and executor conformance green.
  3. The security suite green each night.
  4. p95 time-to-RUNNING below 90 s.
  5. The cost of each run shown in the UI.

This page records how much of each criterion we verified locally. It also tells what still needs a real Google Cloud project. The local run had no Docker daemon and no cloud credentials:

  • Cloud Storage was the GCS shim.
  • Postgres was the embedded pgserver.
  • The Cloud Run Jobs executor ran against its in-memory fake Admin API (FakeCloudRun).
  • Locally signed OIDC tokens simulated the Pub/Sub pushes.
  • We validated the Terraform, but we did not apply it.

We did the verification on 2026-10-15 at commit feat/m2-e2e (v0.3 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Exit criterion Verified locally Result Still needs real GCP 100 concurrent fits without loss make load-test: 100 fits through the real dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and events path on the Cloud Run executor (fake Admin API) and the GCS shim. A second mode keeps all 100 executions live at the same time. A burst of 32 real fits ran on the live dev stack. 100/100 succeeded, with one execution and one attempt for each run. 32/32 real fits succeeded, with one attempt, ledger entry and model version for each run. The same burst on Cloud Run Jobs (real cold starts, real jobs.run quota) Chaos green make chaos 5/5 passed Cloud SQL failover. Pub/Sub redelivery from the real subscription Executor conformance green 12 cases on fake-cloudrun and on local-process, and the gate 24 passed, 3 skipped (documented capabilities that local-process does not have), 0 failed The 12 cases against the real Cloud Run Admin API (there is no live target yet, refer to the text below) Security suite nightly green make security-suite EXECUTOR=local-process. The nightly workflow is written. PASS: all 17 outcomes are acceptable for PROCESS Probes in a gVisor container (needs Docker) and in a Cloud Run Jobs execution (MICROVM) p95 time-to-RUNNING < 90 s Measured in the load test, and on the live stack Fake Cloud Run: p95 45.9–46.5 s (100 fits). Live local stack: p95 3.0 s (16 real fits) and 8.9 s (32) The real cold start of a base image of about 2.5 GB [verify M0] adds more time (refer to the warning below) Per-run cost shown in the UI Playwright against the live stack: the run page, the runs list and the usage page show the metered cost $0.0003 metered on the run page and in the list. The usage totals agree with the ledger The price table against real Cloud Run billing

M2 also adds multi-tenancy. We verified these items from end to end on the live stack:

  • Two users in two tenants, signed in through the development identity provider.
  • The API and row-level security refuse cross-tenant access.
  • Token scopes.
  • Quotas.
  • The spend-cap kill switch, which holds runs at dispatch.
  • The cost of each run.
  • The audit trail.

p95 time-to-RUNNING on real Cloud Run

For a burst of 100 fits, almost all of the 46 s p95 comes from the submit rate. MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE=150 divides 100 submissions over about 40 s. The regional jobs.run quota is 180 a minute ([verify M0]). The fake provisions in 0.3–1.5 s. On Cloud Run, the cold start of each execution adds to that time.

The p95 cold start of a base image can be more than about 40 s. Then a cold burst of 100 fits is longer than the 90 s budget. This is true also when each fit starts quickly. Measure the cold start first (refer to What remains for real GCP). Homogeneous fan-out (sweeps, SBC) uses one execution with taskCount, and thus it does not have this limit. Independent fits cannot do this.

docs.title: Load: 100 concurrent fits
docs.text:
make load-test                                    # default: fits of 0.2–3 s
LOAD_TEST_FIT_MS=40000-60000 make load-test       # 40–60 s fits: all 100 live at once

packages/server/tests/test_load_cloudrun.py submits 100 fits. They go through the production rate limits: the token bucket of the dispatcher and the 150 a minute of the executor. The backend makes errors on purpose:

  • It answers the first jobs.run calls with 429.
  • It loses two responses. This makes orphans that the executor must adopt. The executor must not submit them again.

A synthetic supervisor reads its bootstrap object. It writes its outputs through signed URLs on the real GCS shim. Its events come as OIDC-authenticated Pub/Sub pushes, with random lag and 5 % duplicates.

Mode Runs p50 / p95 / max time-to-RUNNING Most executions live at the same time Pushes (duplicates) Wall default 100/100 succeeded 28.95 / 46.45 / 48.53 s 9 525 (24) 50.5 s LOAD_TEST_FIT_MS=40000-60000 100/100 succeeded 28.47 / 45.93 / 48.09 s 100 525 (24) 105.8 s

The two modes asserted exactly one execution and one attempt for each run (no double dispatch). They also asserted that each run succeeded (no loss).

Real fits on the live stack. This test is opt-in, because each fit is a pair of processes on the host:

make dev   # with the MAPI_* ports below
MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS=32 uv run pytest -q -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py
Burst Result p50 / p95 / max time-to-RUNNING p95 queued → finished 16 real store-demand fits 16/16 succeeded 1.32 / 3.0 / 3.23 s 38.3 s 32 real store-demand fits 32/32 succeeded 3.66 / 8.91 / 9.61 s 82.0 s

For each run, the test made sure of two things. The run has exactly one row in each of run_attempts, cost_ledger and model_versions (counted directly in Postgres). The run registered a different model version.

docs.title: Chaos
docs.text:
make chaos

5/5 passed:

  • The test stopped the worker during PROVISIONING.
  • The test stopped the worker during RUNNING.
  • Event redelivery and a changed sequence of events.
  • A redelivered event with a bad HMAC. This event never moves the run forward.
  • A Postgres restart during a run.

Each case came to the correct terminal state, with no lost or duplicated attempt.

docs.title: Executor conformance
docs.text:
uv run pytest -q -rs packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py

24 passed, 3 skipped. The 12 cases are:

  • Submit.
  • Orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash.
  • Safety of a duplicate submit.
  • Cancel during a run.
  • Timeout.
  • STALLED without a false LOST.
  • Confirmed cancel before retry.
  • Checkpoint resume.
  • OOM classification.
  • Fan-out with taskCount.
  • Generation verification.
  • 429 back-off.

All cases passed on fake-cloudrun. The gate test (test_conformance_report_gates_the_executor) passed for the two backends.

On local-process, the suite skipped three cases. They need capabilities that this executor does not declare: memory_limit, fanout and remote_control_api. The gate needs exactly those skips.

The suite did not select the 12 cases of the docker backend, because there is no Docker daemon.

docs.title: Security suite
docs.text:
make security-suite EXECUTOR=local-process

Result: PASS: all 17 probe outcomes acceptable for this executor. The tests of the suite also passed (9). The outcomes agree with the expected matrix for PROCESS isolation. For this isolation, the suite accepts the two outcomes for the isolation probes. But the executor must stop all platform probes:

Probe Category Outcome metadata_token, http_egress, dns_egress isolation blocked (no metadata server or egress on this host) write_outside_scratch, reuse_foreign_url, pth_injection, fork_bomb, memory_bomb, disk_bomb, log_flood isolation allowed (accepted: PROCESS is not a security boundary) read_proc1_environ, read_supervisor_mem isolation skipped (no procfs on macOS) forged_stdout_event, tampered_manifest, redos_schema, plot_xss_exfil, reuse_foreign_manifest platform blocked

The probes remove what they make. The suite removed the .pth file and the file that it wrote outside scratch.

We repaired two defects in the suite:

  • The docker and gVisor runner ran python -m mapi_security in the runner image, but the runner image never contains the suite. Now the suite is mounted read-only into the probe container.
  • --executor cloud probed the host where it ran. Now it does not run outside a Cloud Run Jobs execution.

.github/workflows/nightly.yml schedules these jobs each night:

  • Chaos.
  • Executor conformance.
  • The two load-test modes.
  • The security suite on local-process.
  • The security suite in gVisor (it installs runsc and builds the worker image).

We did a check of the workflow as YAML here. It has not run on GitHub yet.

docs.title: Multi-tenancy through the live stack
docs.text:
make e2e    # API suites (M1 + M2), then the browser @e2e suites

The M2 API suite, tests/e2e/test_m2_tenancy_stack.py (11 tests, about 2 minutes), does these steps:

  1. The platform operator makes two internal tenants. Each tenant has an invited admin, the dev accounts analyst@dev.local and viewer@dev.local.
  2. Each admin signs in, which accepts the invitation, and makes project growth.
  3. Each admin uploads data under the same dataset names. Each admin fits the scikit-learn store-demand model of the corpus and scores it.

On that state, the suite proves these items.

Sign-in

  • The BFF flow works: /auth/login, the IdP, then /auth/callback, with PKCE S256.
  • A replayed callback gets 401.
  • A cookie mutation without X-CSRF-Token, or from a foreign origin, gets 403.
  • Logout stops the session.
  • ID-token bearers work.
  • API tokens work and are bound to their project. After revocation, they do not work (401).

API isolation. The other tenant always gets 404 or 403, never a 2xx or a 5xx:

  • On 18 project-scoped reads: datasets and versions, the preview, the data artifact, specs, runs, logs, run plots, models, versions, artifacts, ui/ views and plots.
  • On the SSE stream.
  • On 10 writes: cancel, retry, resume, spec revision, dry-run, score, evaluate, fit, upload and new version.
  • On tenant routes: tenant, projects, members, audit and usage.
  • When the caller names the project of the other tenant explicitly.

Lists never show the rows of the other tenant. The same dataset://growth/... ref resolves to the data of each tenant. The lineage dataset hashes are different.

Row-level security, directly in Postgres (as mapi_app)

  • FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is on for each table that we examined.
  • A new connection without a tenant fails closed.
  • With app.tenant_id set, each table shows the rows of the caller and none of the rows of the other tenant.
  • The caller cannot see or update the run of the other tenant by id.
  • If you move a row to a different tenant, this violates the policy.
  • The setting is local to the transaction. After commit, a pooled connection sees nothing.

Scopes

  • A models:read token can read. It gets 403 on fit, score and token minting, and on the project of a different tenant.
  • A runs:create token can fit. The audit log shows that token as the source of the run.

Quotas. These two limits answer 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. They have no effect on the other tenant:

  • A tenant cap of vcpu_seconds_per_day=1.
  • A token vcpu_seconds_budget=1.

Kill switch. This test pauses the worker for a short time (SIGSTOP). Thus a run is always first in the queue. Then:

  • The operator makes the tenant verified and sets global_spend_cap_micros=1.
  • The queued run stays queued across many dispatcher polls. Thus the dispatcher holds it.
  • New runs of that tenant get 429 with the spend-cap message.
  • The dispatcher continues to admit and dispatch an internal tenant.
  • When the tenant is internal again, the dispatcher leases the held run, and the run succeeds.

Cost. For each fit and score:

  • Run.cost is metered (estimated=false, one attempt billed, amount_micros > 0, a price version, and vCPU- and GiB-seconds).
  • There is one actual ledger row for each attempt, in the correct tenant.
  • GET /v1/usage and the tenant usage are equal to the ledger or more.

Audit

  • The tenant log has project.create, run.create, token.create and token.revoke.
  • The platform log has tenant.create, quota.update, kill_switch.update and auth.login.
  • The other tenant cannot read the log.

docs.title: The browser flow
docs.text:
MAPI_E2E=1 pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec playwright test e2e/m2-flow.e2e.spec.ts

Chromium runs the M2 browser flow, apps/web/e2e/m2-flow.e2e.spec.ts (4 tests):

  1. Sign in through the account chooser of the IdP.
  2. Use the tenant switcher. Change to the seeded tenant. The selection stays after a reload.
  3. Fit from the spec editor and wait for succeeded. The run page shows Metered · price table … · 1 attempt billed and cost $0.0003. The runs list and the usage page also show the cost.
  4. Mint a models:read token, then revoke it. Before revocation, the API refuses a fit with it (403). After revocation, the token gets 401.
  5. In the admin console, do these steps:
    1. Make the tenant verified.
    2. Set a spend cap.
    3. The next fit of the tenant admin gets the spend-cap message.
    4. Remove the cap (type REMOVE).
    5. Find kill_switch.update and tenant.update in the audit log.

tests/e2e/m2_browser_seed.py seeds the tenant, and puts the stack back after the test. We examined the screenshots in apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m2-*.png (git ignores them). They caused these fixes:

  • Costs below one cent showed as $0.00. A 3 s ingest cost $0.000047. The spend-cap badge for a 1-micro cap showed "$0.00 per day". Now amounts below $0.0001 keep two significant digits.
  • Session usage showed as "-" in "By token". The group key of the server is -. Now the page shows the label "Signed-in users".
  • Memory showed "0 GiB·h". Now it shows GiB-seconds below one hour.
  • A finished run without output showed "No output captured yet".
  • The project switcher cut tenant and project names short, also on wide screens.

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text:
make tf-validate

87 passed, 1 skipped: shellcheck is not installed. The tests include:

  • terraform fmt.
  • validate of each environment, with -backend=false.
  • Module tests with mocked providers.
  • The HCL invariants (for example digest-pinned images, the deny-all egress, the env-only overrides).
  • The deploy scripts and the deploy workflow.

docs.title: Local stack used
docs.text:
A different process used the default port of the API. Thus the stack ran on other ports, with a new data directory and two more dev accounts:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443 \
       MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174 \
       MAPI_DATA_DIR=$PWD/.local/m2e2e VITE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:18000
make dev                     # dev profile: dev IdP, the default tenant, admin@dev.local as operator
make e2e                     # in another shell, with the same exports

MAPI_E2E_ACCOUNTS selects the two tenant admins of the API suite (default analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local). MAPI_E2E_UI_ACCOUNT selects the tenant admin of the browser flow (default analyst@dev.local). The two suites need a stack in the dev profile. If not, they skip.

docs.title: Full verification set
docs.text: Check Command Result Python suite make test 4141 passed, 11 skipped (optional cloud SDKs not installed, Linux-only prctl, Debian cp, shellcheck, the three documented local-process conformance skips), 45 deselected (docker, cloud, e2e) Lint and import contracts make lint ruff and format clean (569 files). Import contracts: 4 kept, 0 broken Type checks make typecheck mypy clean on each package (--strict for spec, gcs-shim, runner, server, client and cli) Conformance corpus (tiny) make conformance 7/7 fixtures passed (e02, c08, e24, xgb and sklearn store demand, e33 and the model-owns-units MMM fixture) in 77 s Web: lint, typecheck, unit, smoke, build make web-check web: 146 Vitest tests. Plot sandbox: 60. Playwright smoke: 26. The two production builds are OK Docs make docs-build (MkDocs --strict) built with no warnings End to end, M1 and M2, API and browser make e2e API suites: 28 passed, 1 skipped (the opt-in burst): M1 E33 stack, corpus on the stack, the docs walkthroughs, M2 tenancy. Browser @e2e suites: 14 passed: the stack smoke tests, the M1 flow and the M2 flow

docs.title: Known gaps (not cloud-specific)
docs.text:
• An operator records executor evidence manually. Shared tiers need stored conformance and security-suite reports (the shared-tier gate). But no job sends the nightly results to PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence yet.
  • The nightly workflow has not run yet. .github/workflows/nightly.yml has no remote to run on here. Its gVisor job (which installs runsc on the runner) is not tested.

docs.title: What remains for real GCP
docs.text:
All items below need a Google Cloud project. Use a temporary dev environment. Build it as Google Cloud deployment tells. The values below are placeholders from infra/terraform/envs/dev/terraform.tfvars.example:

export ENV=dev REGION=europe-west4
export CONTROL=acme-mapi-dev-control EXEC=acme-mapi-dev-exec DATA=acme-mapi-dev-data
export EXEC_SA=mapi-$ENV-exec@$EXEC.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export NET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid SUBNET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid-jobs

docs.title: 1. Stand the environment up
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh --env $ENV --region $REGION --control-project $CONTROL \
  --data-project $DATA --build-project acme-mapi-dev-build --exec-project paid=$EXEC \
  --state-project acme-mapi-dev-build
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV --foundation
deploy/gcp/build-push.sh --env $ENV
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV            # migrations, apply, smoke test

docs.title: 2. Work through the M0 checklist
docs.text:
The M0 verification checklist lists each [verify M0] item, with its pass condition. The checklist has four areas:

  • DNS response policy: the Direct VPC resolver obeys it, with root wildcard and bypass rules.
  • Network: egress is really denied, and VPC-SC applies on Jobs.
  • Sandbox: gen2 uid split with seccomp, no_new_privs and ptrace denial. Env-only overrides. Ephemeral disk and the in-memory filesystem limits. Bootstrap read-then-delete.
  • Platform:
    • Quotas: 1,000 Jobs and 1,000 running executions in each region, 180 jobs.run a minute.
    • The Logging → Pub/Sub path and its labels.
    • Push to an internal service.
    • Pooled connections.
    • BYPASSRLS on Cloud SQL.
    • runWithOverrides without actAs.
    • Image indexes.

docs.title: 3. Cold start and p95 time-to-RUNNING
docs.text:
Measure one cold execution for each base image. Overrides change only env. Thus this measures exactly what the dispatcher does:

for base in base-bayes base-ml base-forecast; do
  gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-$base-s --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
    --update-env-vars MAPI_RUN_ID=coldstart,MAPI_NONCE=none --wait --format='value(name)'
done
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name:mapi-$ENV-" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='table(timestamp,resource.labels.job_name,textPayload)'

The supervisor stops immediately, because it finds no bootstrap object. The cold start is the time from the createTime of the execution to its first log line. Then run the burst through the deployed API with a token that has the admin scope:

MAPI_API_URL=https://api.$ENV.example.com MAPI_TOKEN=<token> MAPI_PROJECT=<tenant>/<project> \
MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS=100 uv run pytest -q -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py

The test asserts no loss or duplication (through the API) and a p95 time-to-RUNNING below 90 s. It prints the percentiles.

docs.title: 4. Security suite inside a Cloud Run Jobs execution
docs.text:
--executor cloud runs only in a Job execution. The runner images do not contain the suite. Thus build a probe image on the deployed base, and run it as its own Job. Use the same network and identity as the inventory Jobs:

REPO=$(terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/envs/$ENV output -raw image_repository)   # …/mapi-$ENV-images
IMAGE=$REPO/base-bayes@sha256:<digest from deploy/gcp/.out/$ENV/images.tfvars.json>
PROBE=$REPO/security-probe:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
printf 'FROM %s\nCOPY security/src /opt/mapi-security\nENV PYTHONPATH=/opt/mapi-security\n' "$IMAGE" \
  | docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$PROBE" -f - . && docker push "$PROBE"
gcloud run jobs create mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
  --image "$PROBE" --command python --args=-m,mapi_security,run,--executor,cloud \
  --service-account $EXEC_SA --network $NET --subnet $SUBNET --network-tags mapi-exec \
  --vpc-egress all-traffic --execution-environment gen2 --max-retries 0 --task-timeout 15m
gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION --wait
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name=mapi-$ENV-security-probe" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='value(textPayload)'

Pass: PASS: all 17 probe outcomes acceptable for this executor. On MICROVM, each isolation probe must be BLOCKED or SKIPPED. The DNS probe passes only if the authoritative query log of the zone also never sees the name of the probe (checklist, network section). After the test, delete the probe Job. To run this each night, add the probe image to build-push.sh and the Job to infra/terraform/modules/exec. We have not done this yet.

docs.title: 5. Executor conformance against the real Admin API
docs.text:
There is no live conformance target yet. packages/server/tests/mapi_server_testkit/conformance.py operates only fake-cloudrun, local-process and docker. A cloudrun-live target needs a harness that does these actions:

  • It builds CloudRunJobsExecutor from settings (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT=$EXEC, the dev inventory).
  • It causes the faults through real means. It stops an execution with gcloud run jobs executions cancel. It causes an OOM with a run that is larger than class S. It causes a 429 when it sets MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE above the quota.
  • It marks itself cloud.

Until then, run the chaos cases manually against the deployed stack:

# orphan adoption: scale the orchestrator worker pool (manual scaling) to 0 right after a
# submit, then back (`gcloud beta run worker-pools update --help` names the flag of your gcloud)
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 0
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 1
# Cloud SQL failover (regional/HA instance)
gcloud sql instances failover mapi-$ENV-pg --project $CONTROL

After each case, each run that the case affects must come to a terminal state, with exactly one attempt for each execution.

docs.title: 6. Cost
docs.text: Compare the cost_ledger of one day with the billing export for the exec project. If list prices or discounts are different, adjust the price table (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH).

docs.title: M3 verification v0.4
docs.text:
Milestone M3 (Guided mode and integrations) has three exit criteria:

  1. Five non-technical testers complete upload → report → scenario without help in less than 30 minutes.
  2. An external budget optimiser works against an endpoint.
  3. Cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins (untrusted data, trusted code).

This page records how much of each criterion we verified locally, and the measured numbers. It also tells what the runs found and fixed, and what remains. We cannot simulate real testers. Thus we prepared the first criterion, but it is not met. An automated "unaided tester" script measures the minimum of the time budget. We also examined the screens as an analyst who uses them for the first time. The protocol for the five testers below is the work that remains.

We did the verification on 2026-10-16 on branch feat/m3-e2e (v0.4 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS), against a live make dev stack:

  • The API, worker, web app and plot sandbox on ports that are not the defaults (API 18000, GCS shim 14443, web 15173, plot sandbox 15174).
  • The dev profile: the development identity provider and the outbox mailer.
  • The GCS shim in place of Cloud Storage, and the embedded pgserver Postgres.
  • All runs on the local-process executor (no Docker daemon, no cloud project).
  • MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S=0 and MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0, so that we could watch a deletion to the end.
  • Higher MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR and MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY, because each run signs up new workspaces from one address.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Exit criterion Verified locally Result Still needs 5 non-technical testers: upload → report → scenario without help in < 30 min The browser script apps/web/e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts clicks through the whole Guided flow on a realistic spreadsheet, and measures the time of each step. We examined each screen for plain language, next steps and dead ends 135 s of automated wall time. The system used almost all of this time (the beliefs preview, the fit, the exact runs). We found and repaired six usability defects. Two of them were dead ends Five real testers (protocol) An external optimiser works against an endpoint The optimiser adapter of the v0.4 client (removed in v0.5) against the live endpoint. The optimiser uses the protocol of the external framework Under the model, the selected allocation is better than the current one: +0.22 % revenue for next quarter at the same budget. It came from 25 candidate allocations (22 score requests) in 220 s The in-sandbox optimize job (M4) Cut line A A self-service sign-up makes a public workspace. The e-mail is verified, and the server refuses uploaded code (uploaded_code_allowed: false). Built-ins and declarative specs run. Here they ran on an internal workspace that an operator promoted, because the local executor admits only trusted tiers Pass Public workspaces that run on docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs. Shared tiers can use only these executors

tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py (15 tests, 7 minutes) also tested all M3 additions from end to end through the API: 15 passed.
