docs.title: An external optimiser against the live endpoint
docs.text:
An external optimisation framework (a sibling project) has the model and optimiser interfaces. The test registered the endpoint-backed model adapter of the v0.4 client as one of its models. Then it ran an optimiser that uses its protocol. The optimiser moves a step of budget between two channels while this increases the predicted revenue of the endpoint. When no move increases it, the optimiser makes the step half as large. Each candidate is one score request against the live endpoint (inline XrJSON, score:<alias> token).

Search Social TV Predicted revenue (13 weeks) Current plan 16,136 9,737 37,890 929,612 Chosen 19,324 9,737 34,702 931,620 (+0.22 %)

25 candidates used 22 requests (the cache answered the others). The total time was 220 s. Each request is a sandboxed score run, so the wall time is mostly run start-up. You cannot put the markets of a geo MMM into one request (new markets are pooled). For this reason, the in-sandbox optimize job (M4) is the path for longer optimisations.

docs.title: The unaided-tester script
docs.text:
MAPI_E2E=1 pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec playwright test e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts

tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py makes a new project and writes the spreadsheet of the analyst. The script then does the tasks that the five testers will do, without hesitation, as the admin of the default tenant. Screenshots go to apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m3-*.png (git ignores them). The times go to m3-timings.json.

The times below are from the release check of v0.4.0 on the integrated develop branch (2026-10-16, the same laptop and settings). The first run on feat/m3-e2e took 137 s.

Step What the script does Wall time (s) 1. Template Starts where sign-in goes (/) and finds Guided. "What do you want to learn?" → Geo marketing mix 0.7 2. Your data Gives the analysis a name and selects the CSV. Makes sure that each question has the correct answer. Upload and continue (upload, sandboxed check) 4.7 3. What you believe Selects tv, states an ROI of 1.5 to 4, shows a preview of what it means (a sandboxed run) and continues 20.7 4. Fit the model Fit the model. Phases and progress in plain language. See the results 78.5 5. Results Headline numbers, ROI and share for each channel, two charts, the sanity scorecard 0.4 6. What if… Search spend +20 % on the slider (immediate), Run exact, Turn off tv, a 13-week forecast 29.6 Upload → report → scenario 134.6 7. Share The gate explained. The reason of an admin. Approve and go live. An embed link 0.4

The system uses almost all of the 135 s: the beliefs preview, the fit (79 s), the exact run, the channel-off run and the forecast. Clicks, typing and page loads take some seconds. A person reads, hesitates and explores. Thus the 30-minute budget is mostly the time that the testers need to understand each screen. The script shows that the system uses about two and a half minutes of it on this laptop.

The second test goes through the Integrations hub:

  • The overview cards and the endpoint page.
  • Try it (validate, then score: 8.6 s), and a copy of the curl snippet.
  • A score:<alias> token from the shortcut of the snippet.
  • A webhook with its one-time secret.
  • The embed link. It shows read-only in a new page (no button to push). After the hub revokes it, the page shows "This link has expired or was revoked".

docs.title: What the review found and fixed
docs.text:
We read each screenshot as an analyst who uses the app for the first time. We asked these questions: Is the language plain? Is the next step clear? Is there a dead end? Does the app explain each error? We fixed these items on this branch, each with a test:

Finding Where Fix "Run exact" always failed on the live stack ("User or plugin code failed"). The compiled counterfactual named no data What if… POST /v1/guided/requests:compile names the fit dataset in data for what-ifs and presets over the fit window. The server refuses a score request without data with 422 before a run starts "Forecast error on held-back weeks: 83 %" for an error of 0.8 % (mapi_sdk reports MAPE in percent) Results The headline reads the measured fraction of the scorecard Dead end: the fit of the template failed the convergence checks on two years of weekly data. The advice of the checks ("raise target_accept") names settings that Guided screens do not show. Share showed "cannot go live" Results, Share The geo_mmm template (1.1.0) samples longer and more carefully. A convergence check with a warning or failure offers Fit again, more carefully. A blocked Share step links to it Beliefs that the analyst did not state: each channel started selected with an ROI range of 0.5–4 (the true ROI of search was 6.3). But the page says "leave a channel unticked if you have no view" What you believe Channels start not selected. When you select one, it starts from the sensible range "Results without any media: between −164 % and 271 %" Beliefs preview Without a stated baseline: "anything from none to all of your results - the model has no view yet" A revoked embed link continued to show for one minute (Cache-Control: public, max-age=60) Embed page private, no-cache: revocation applies on the next load Jargon: "y_hat" on the axis and caption of the fit chart. "evenly spaced (W-SUN)". "the host did not resolve (gaierror)". "Sampler convergence" first under Share a chart Report, data step, webhook dialog, Share The name of the dataset ("revenue"). "weekly, on Sundays". "no such name". Result charts first

We also fixed this item: mapi_client refused to upload an MFF table (a CSV file) with the mapping of a Guided MFF draft.

We saw these items and left them for later. They do not block the flow, and we noted them for the sessions of the testers:

  • The fit chart showed markets under the dim name geo. The y axis of the forecast chart started at zero, and this made the fan flat. The M3 review fixed the two items: panels use the name of the dataset, and the axis fits the band.
  • The endpoint page showed the user id of the person who promoted a version, not a name. The M3 review fixed this: names come from the members of the project.
  • The header showed Expert mode on the Integrations hub. That test runs in a new browser context, and there the default tenant (not a self-service tenant) started in Expert mode. The browser remembers the selection. Since then, a self-service workspace starts in Guided mode, and Expert navigation and Home link to Guided.
  • The fit takes about 80 s with the stronger settings (30 s before). This is still well in the budget.

docs.title: Protocol for the five non-technical testers
docs.text: The exit criterion needs people. Do this protocol with five testers, one at a time. Use a stack like the stack above (or staging). Record the results on the observation sheet.

docs.title: Who
docs.text:
• Five persons who analyse marketing or sales results in spreadsheets (marketing analysts, media planners, finance business partners). They must have no statistics or programming training, other than spreadsheet formulas. Select them with two questions: "Have you fitted a regression or written Python or R?" (no) and "Do you work with weekly spend and sales by market?" (yes).
  • None of them has seen modeling-api before. Nobody from the team that built it.

docs.title: Setup (before each session)
docs.text:
1. Make a new workspace for the tester. Sign up at /signup with their work address, in a new browser profile. Sign in after the e-mail link. This opens an empty Guided page. A self-service workspace starts in Guided mode on all browsers. If you use an internal tenant that an operator made (a stack without a sandboxed executor), the session starts on Expert Home. Then the tester must find Guided in the sidebar as part of T1.
  2. Put the spreadsheet on the desktop of the tester. uv run python tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py seed --run <id> writes weekly_media_by_region.csv (two years, five regions, three channels). You can also use the anonymised data of the tester in the same shape.
  3. Prepare a screen recorder, a stopwatch and the observation sheet. The facilitator sits next to or behind the tester. The facilitator does not touch the keyboard.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Read this aloud, word for word:

"Thank you for your help. We test the software, not you. If something is difficult, it is our fault. Please think aloud: say what you look for and what you think will occur. I cannot help you during the tasks. If you would stop in real life, tell me, and we go to the next task. You have a maximum of 30 minutes for all tasks."

Then give one task card at a time.

Task Card Success means T1 Upload "Here is last two years' media spend and revenue by region. Load it into the tool so it can explain what each channel brings in." The analysis gets to "What you believe" with correct answers for Revenue, Week, Region, the three spend columns and Avg Price T2 Report "Get the tool to tell you which channel returns the most per euro, and whether you can trust the numbers." The fit finishes. The tester names the best channel and its range, and says in their own words what the scorecard concluded T3 Scenario "Next quarter you could move 20 % more into search. What would it do to revenue? How sure is the tool?" The tester gives the change in revenue with its range (immediate or exact), from the What if… step

The optional "What you believe" step is part of T1 to T2. Testers can skip it.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Unaided: the facilitator answers no question about the product. Permitted: say the task card again, "what would you do if I were not here?", "please keep thinking aloud". All other help is an assist. Record it. A task with an assist is not unaided.
  • Give-up: the tester says that they stop, or 12 minutes go by on one task. Record it and give the next card. A later task can need the result of an earlier task. If this occurs, the facilitator does that step without comment. The time of the later task starts after this step.
  • The time to wait for the fit is part of the 30 minutes (about 1.5 minutes on a laptop).

docs.title: Metrics and pass mark
docs.text:
For each tester and task, record these items:

  • Completion (unaided, assisted or failed).
  • Time on task.
  • The number of errors (a wrong turn that the tester had to undo).
  • The Single Ease Question (1 = very difficult to 7 = very easy) after each task.

After the session, record the System Usability Scale (10 items) and two open questions: "What was most confusing?" and "What would you trust least?".

The criterion is met when all five testers complete T1, T2 and T3 unaided with a total under 30 minutes. Also report the median and maximum total time, the mean SEQ for each task and the mean SUS (target: more than 68). Each assist, give-up or error that occurs again is a defect. Repair it before the public launch, also when the five testers pass.

docs.title: Observation sheet
docs.text:
Copy one sheet for each tester.

Field T1 Upload T2 Report T3 Scenario Start / end (mm:ss) Completed (unaided / assisted / failed) Errors (wrong turns, with the screen) Assists (what was said) Words or screens the tester did not understand Answer given (T2: best channel, trust; T3: change and range) SEQ (1-7) Session Tester (role, years of experience; no name) Total time SUS score Most confusing Would trust least Facilitator notes (quotes, hesitations, where the cursor went first)

docs.title: What remains unverified
docs.text:
• The five testers. We did only the automated minimum and an expert review (above).
  • Real Google Cloud. Cloud Storage (the GCS shim was in its place), Cloud Run Jobs (the local-process executor ran all runs), Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, Identity Platform, Cloud Armor (the policy is Terraform, validated and never applied) and Cloud Logging retention. The cold start of the base images adds time to each fit, exact run and optimiser evaluation.
  • Docker. There is no daemon here. We did not run the images, the docker and docker-gvisor executors or the compose stack. Thus public (shared-tier) workspaces never ran a fit. We did a check of the admission rule of cut line A, but not of its sandbox.
  • Plotly rendering. Static renders and embeds were only Vega-Lite. Plotly needs kaleido and a Chrome in the runner image (MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED). This laptop does not have them.
  • Identity verification by a vendor. Only the fake IdentityVerifier and the manual verification of the operators are available. We did not test a vendor integration.
  • Real e-mail. The dev outbox was in place of SMTP. We did not test deliverability, SPF/DKIM and bounce handling.
  • Webhooks to the internet. Deliveries went to a receiver on 127.0.0.1 through the dev allow-list. Only unit tests include the full SSRF policy for public hosts.
  • Bundle retention. With a retention lock (the default, and 30 days when deployed), a purge stops at the model bundles. It continues when the lock expires. Locally, we did a check only up to the stop, not of the continuation after 30 days. The deletion test of the journey does this check on a stack without MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0.
  • The in-sandbox optimize job came later (v0.5, on mmm-framework). Here the optimiser ran on the client.

docs.title: M3.5 verification v0.5
docs.text:
M3.5 adds these items: workflows, governance policies and validations, the Data and Model Explorers, mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, the statsmodels time-series models, About cards and Help me choose. Each part has unit, integration and mocked-browser tests. This page records the next step. The five journeys below run through the running stack, from outside its processes. Real fits run in the runner, the real orchestrator operates the workflow runs, and the web app sends requests to the real API.

We did the verification on 2026-10-16 on branch fix/m35-e2e (v0.5 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS), against a live make dev stack:

  • The API, worker, web app (Vite dev server) and plot sandbox on ports that are not the defaults (API 18000, GCS shim 14443, web 15173, plot sandbox 15174), with their own MAPI_DATA_DIR.
  • The dev profile: the development identity provider (admin@dev.local submits, analyst@dev.local reviews) and the outbox mailer.
  • The GCS shim in place of Cloud Storage, and the embedded pgserver Postgres.
  • All runs on the local-process executor (no Docker daemon, no cloud project).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Journey Verified through the live stack Result 1. The canonical time-series workflow A weekly KPI with a unit root (a random walk and a price driver with a true effect of -3). It went through the ts_readiness_arimax template. We followed it over server-sent events (API), in the run monitor (browser, Expert) and as a Guided recipe that we started from the Data Explorer ADF (p = 0.62), KPSS, Phillips-Perron and Zivot-Andrews all show that the series wanders. The branch differences it (and skips the seasonal difference), and records the four values that it read. The AIC search selects ARIMA(1, 1, 1). The fitted ARIMAX and the backtest use exactly [1, 1, 1] with price. Six expanding-window folds score ARIMAX and the naive benchmarks for each horizon. ARIMAX is better (MAE 1.45 against naive 1.68), and the workflow selects it. The governance node passes the default forecasting policy. Pass, after two fixes (the workflow graph of the dev server, the first run of a recipe) 2. Governance A project policy that needs null.permutation_target and null.noise_regressors with the approval of a reviewer. ARIMAX fitted on real signal and on pure noise Noise: the shuffled-target test fails (across runs, 13 to 18 of 19 shuffled fits were equally good, p = 0.7-0.95). The validation is checks_failed, and promotion answers 409 NOT_VALIDATED. Signal: p = 0.05 (better than all shuffled fits), and fake drivers get 0.1 % of the result, awaiting_approval. The server refuses promotion until approval. The approval of the submitter gets SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN. The reviewer (an editor with the reviewer capability) approves, and the result is validated. Promotion succeeds. The evidence pack exports as HTML (no script) and JSON (with its digest). Pass, after three fixes (the families of the policy, the reviewer capability in the client, an upload of the same data again) 3. mmm-framework mmm.bayesian (150 tuning steps and draws, 2 chains), pooled over 3 regions, 2 channels, 40 weeks Fitted in about 30 s. The Model Explorer shows the contributions and response curves (they do not decrease when spend increases, for the two channels). A budget plan keeps the total and obeys the 0.5-1.5x bounds of tv. It reports the chance to be better than the plan of today, and a 5-point efficient frontier, in about 10 s. Pass, after one fix 4. Explorers and the chooser The Data Explorer of the unit-root series. A statsmodels VAR(2) on three weekly series. Help me choose for "forecast weekly sales with drivers" Stationarity for each series. Impulse responses with bands, and a variance decomposition whose shares add up to 1. The browser shows the two in the plot sandbox. The chooser now puts ts.sarimax first with four reasons and no caution, and its About card opens. Pass, after two fixes 5. The CLI mapi workflows validate, apply and run --watch on the canonical document of the cookbook, exactly as docs/snippets/cli_v05.sh runs them (with a different project name) 23 nodes are valid. The live board prints each node and decision. The rolling-origin backtest (window 104) and the Diebold-Mariano node run. The exit status is 0, with the reference of the fitted model. Pass

Two suites pass:

  • tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py (5 tests, the API and the CLI, about 5 minutes).
  • apps/web/e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts (7 tests, the browser in Expert and Guided mode, about 3 minutes with a 90-second seed).

The unit-root tests of the canonical run did not change. Thus the cookbook run from the CLI gets them from the cache (cached_from names that run). We also ran the earlier end-to-end suites (M1 to M3) against the same stack. Refer to Full verification set.

docs.title: What the runs found and fixed
docs.text:
The runs found eight defects. The unit, integration and mocked-browser tests could not find them. Each fix has a regression test.

Found in Defect Fix Governance A policy with applies_to: {families: [ts]} applied to no statsmodels model. This policy is the example on all governance pages and in forecast-policy.yaml. The manifests of the statsmodels models declare the family forecast (or ts_multivariate, regime). Thus the checks, approval and promotion gate of the policy never applied, and there was no message. The model fitted on noise got only the default policy. It became validated, and it was promoted. A family agrees with the declared family of a model, or with the namespace of its id (mapi_spec.governance.PolicyMatch). Governance The client could not give a member the reviewer capability (add_member and set_role removed it). Thus you could not set up the second person without raw HTTP. tenants.add_member(..., capabilities=[...]) and tenants.set_capabilities(...), sync and async. Each upload An upload of data that was uploaded before failed its ingest with INTEGRITY_FAILURE ("ui/explore/index.json already holds different content"). This occurred for the same file as the next version, or in a different dataset or project. Ingest outputs are stored under the content hash of the data. Since v0.5, the Data Explorer views that an ingest writes name the dataset version and contain plot timestamps. The explorer views of each ingest are stored under its run (t/<tenant>/datasets/<sha>/runs/<run>/ui/explore/). The data and its sidecars keep the strict same-content check. mmm-framework api.explorations.view(..., "response_curves") (and mapi explore --show) returned the list of plots of the section, not its view. This occurred for each section whose name comes after plots in alphabetical sequence (residuals, response_curves, stationarity, stl...). The code looks for the exact view first. Plot files never agree. Chooser Help me choose put ts.sarimax in position six for "forecast weekly sales with drivers". But it is the only model that agrees with all four answers. Items that did not answer a question also got a score of 1.0, and the difficulty decided ties. The number of answers that an item agrees with explicitly decides ties. Browser On the dev server, the first page that opened a workflow graph crashed with "Invalid hook call" in ReactFlowProvider. A route that loaded while the YAML worker of the spec editor started for the first time failed with "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module". Vite found React Flow and the dependency of the worker late. It optimised them in a second pass and loaded the page again. The dev server pre-bundles the two when it starts (apps/web/dev-prebundle.ts). A test makes sure that the list includes each package that a web worker imports. Production builds were not affected. Data Explorer The overview of the most usual upload, a time dimension with the name time, showed "2 variables over 156 time". The name of the time dimension is now its frequency ("156 weeks"). Guided recipes The first run of a recipe in a project by a Guided user failed with "The recipe did not start: Not Found". The click made the workflow from the template. Then it sent the run to /v1/workflows//runs with the id from when the page was shown. The mock project always had the workflow. A run can name its workflow. The recipe runs the workflow that it made.

docs.title: The earlier journeys, brought up to date
docs.text:
We ran the M1 and M3 journeys against the same stack. Four of their assertions were not correct after M3.5, but the product was correct:

  • The E33 spec on mmm-framework does not have scaling or lag steps now. M1 now does a check of its currency, weekly and holiday steps.
  • Its scores have six components, not five. The M1 browser flow counts the rows.
  • A Guided draft records no units. Thus the test finds the budget plan by the name of its KPI.
  • The M3 webhook receiver verified deliveries some minutes after they came. This was later than the 5-minute signature tolerance. Now it verifies each delivery when it comes, as a real receiver does.

docs.title: An observation, since fixed
docs.text:
We had a project policy that made the shuffled-target test blocking. Under this policy, the ARIMA(1, 1, 1) of the cookbook on the random walk failed the test. 4 of 19 shuffled refits were equally good (p = 0.25). But the model was 25 % better than the naive forecast on the held-out weeks. The null shuffled the target in blocks. This kept most of the persistence that a differenced model uses.

The M3.5 review replaced this null before the release. Now, for a model with drivers, the null shuffles the drivers in blocks and does not change the result. For a model without drivers, the null shuffles the differences and integrates them again. The null test scores each fit by its holdout skill against the null forecast (refer to null tests explained). On the same data, the model of the cookbook is now better than all 20 shuffled fits (p = 0.048).

docs.title: How to rerun
docs.text:
Start a stack on free ports with its own data directory. The variables are those of local development:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174
export VITE_API_BASE=$MAPI_API_URL MAPI_DATA_DIR=$PWD/.local/m35e2e
make dev                    # in one shell; `make stop` with the same variables stops it

Then, in a different shell with the same variables:

uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py -s          # the API and CLI journeys
pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec env MAPI_E2E=1 \
  playwright test e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts                    # the browser journeys
make e2e                                                      # or every end-to-end suite

Each suite makes its own project in the default tenant (m35e2e-<id>, m35ui-<id>). It deletes the project at the end. To keep the project and look at it in the app, set MAPI_E2E_KEEP=1. The suites write the times to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/e2e/m35-timings.json and apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m35-timings.json. The browser suite saves its screens as apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m35-*.png (git ignores them).

docs.title: Timings
docs.text:
These are the wall-clock seconds of the last run, on the laptop above (no Docker, no cold starts):

Step Seconds Upload and ingest of a small dataset (the sandboxed ingest with its Data Explorer views) 8-13 The canonical workflow, 19 nodes, through the orchestrator and the runner 37-40 The cookbook workflow from the CLI, 23 nodes 45 A validation with the null tests (19 shuffled refits and 3 fake drivers) 26 mmm.bayesian, tiny settings, 3 regions x 2 channels x 40 weeks 31-34 A statsmodels VAR(2) fit 13 A Model Explorer request served from the views of the fit 8 A budget plan with a 5-point frontier 10-16

docs.title: Full verification set
docs.text:
On the final tree of fix/m35-e2e:

docs.title: What remains unverified
docs.text:
• Real Google Cloud. Cloud Storage (the GCS shim was in its place), Cloud Run Jobs (each workflow node, fit, governance, explore and optimise run used the local-process executor), Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL and Identity Platform. Each workflow node runs as its own sandboxed run, and the cold starts of the runner images add time to each node. A 19-node workflow starts about 15 of these runs.
  • Docker. There is no daemon here, so we did not build the images. In particular, we did not build base-bayes with mmm-framework, JAX and nutpie, and base-forecast with statsmodels and the workflow runtime. The docker and docker-gvisor executors never ran a workflow, a validation or an optimisation. Thus public (shared-tier) workspaces also never ran them.
  • People. No non-technical user tried the Guided recipes, Help me choose or the About cards. No reviewer used the approval screens on real models. Nobody tried the app with a screen reader. The protocol of the M3 testers applies. Add this task: "run the readiness recipe on your weekly sales and say whether you would trust the forecast".
  • Scale and real fits. Only tiny MCMC settings and small panels ran here. We did not measure the time of full-size mmm-framework fits (4 chains, thousands of draws, dozens of geos), of governance refit budgets on them, or of workflows with hundreds of nodes.
  • Not operated live by these journeys (the integration tests of the server with embedded Postgres include them): schedules and dataset triggers that fire, workflow cancellation, sub-workflows, the workflow.run.* and validation webhooks, tenant-wide policies, deprecation and resubmission. Also the visual workflow editor and the policy editor (only their mocked Playwright specs).

docs.title: Observability v0.3
docs.text:
The API and the worker send three signals:

  • Metrics: Prometheus text at GET /metrics on each API process. The worker records the series of the orchestrator (dispatch, reconciliation, finalization, pipe event ingestion). When MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT is set, the worker serves them on that port.
  • Logs: one JSON object on each line on stderr. Each line has trace_id and span_id, and the request, run and tenant that it is related to.
  • Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for each request, each outgoing HTTP call, and the dispatch and finalization of each run. The server exports spans over OTLP/HTTP only when you configure a collector.

Nothing goes out from inside a sandbox. Each execution gets the traceparent of the dispatching span in MAPI_TRACEPARENT. Thus you can join the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor to the trace of the run, and no telemetry goes out of the exec project.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Effect MAPI_LOG_JSON true JSON logs. false gives a console format that is easy to read for local work MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve GET /metrics MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset The bearer that a scraper must send. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 The address where the worker serves its own /metrics (the same bearer rule) MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Make spans (their ids go into the logs also without a collector) MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset OTLP/HTTP collector (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT also works). Needs the otlp extra of mapi-server

docs.title: Scraping /metrics
docs.text:
The series contain tenant ids and spend. Thus /metrics is not a public route. It authenticates its own bearer, as the Pub/Sub push endpoint does:

# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: mapi-api
    authorization:
      type: Bearer
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/mapi-metrics-token
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["api.internal:8000", "worker.internal:9464"]

In the multi-tenant profile, a server without MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN refuses all scrapes (401). The single-tenant and dev profiles serve /metrics without authentication on their loopback API, if no token is set.

docs.title: The metric set
docs.text:
This table comes from mapi_server.observability.metrics.Metrics. This is the one registry that defines all series. Thus the table always agrees with what /metrics serves. The number of label values is limited on purpose. tenant_id is the only unlimited label, on the two counters that have no meaning without it. HTTP series have the route template as label, never the raw path.

Metric Type Labels Meaning mapi_runs_total counter kind, state Runs that reached a terminal state, by kind and terminal state. mapi_runs_active gauge state Runs currently in a non-terminal state (sampled each reconcile pass). mapi_run_transitions_total counter state Run state transitions, by target state (every edge, terminal or not). mapi_dispatch_latency_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to the executor accepting its submission. mapi_time_to_running_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to its first event (RUNNING). mapi_event_ingestion_lag_seconds histogram — Seconds between a run event's timestamp and its ingestion. mapi_events_ingested_total counter result Run events seen by the ingestor, by result (accepted, duplicate, bad_hmac, ...). mapi_finalize_outcomes_total counter kind, outcome Finalize attempts, by outcome (succeeded, partial, integrity, infra, retry). mapi_integrity_failures_total counter tenant_id Output-integrity verification failures at FINALIZING (a security signal). mapi_sandbox_violations_total counter reason Sandbox violations observed by the control plane, by reason. mapi_quota_rejections_total counter scope, code Requests denied by a quota or rate limit, by scope and error code. mapi_cost_micros_total counter tenant_id Billed compute cost in currency micros, by tenant (cost ledger). mapi_global_spend_micros gauge — Current spend against the global cap, in currency micros (0 until set). mapi_global_spend_cap_micros gauge — The configured global spend cap, in currency micros (0 = no cap set). mapi_sse_clients gauge — Live Server-Sent-Events subscribers connected to this process. mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total counter executor 429 answers from an executor backend to a submission (Cloud Run jobs.run), each one, retried or not. Not the API's own 429s to tenants. mapi_executor_running_executions gauge executor Runs holding a live execution on this executor (fleet-wide, from the run table; each orchestrator reports the same value, so aggregate with max). mapi_http_requests_total counter method, route, status HTTP requests handled by the API, by method, route template and status. mapi_http_request_duration_seconds histogram method, route HTTP request handling time, by method and route template. mapi_endpoint_promotions_total counter outcome Endpoint promotion and rollback decisions, by outcome (allowed, overridden, needs_override, blocked, forbidden, rollback). mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total counter result, inline POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score calls, by result (accepted, replayed, invalid) and whether the payload was inline XrJSON. mapi_webhook_events_total counter type Webhook events written to the outbox, by event type. mapi_webhook_deliveries_total counter status Webhook delivery tries, by resulting status (succeeded, retrying, failed, blocked). mapi_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds histogram — Time of one webhook delivery try (resolution, connection, answer). mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total counter stage Webhook URLs refused by the SSRF policy, by stage (create, update, replay, delivery). mapi_webhooks_disabled_total counter reason Webhooks the platform disabled, by reason (failures, gone).

Monitor these series first:

  • mapi_time_to_running_seconds: the M2 target is a p95 below 90 s.
  • mapi_integrity_failures_total and mapi_sandbox_violations_total: each increase is a security signal, not a reliability signal.
  • mapi_global_spend_micros against mapi_global_spend_cap_micros: the window of the kill switch.
  • mapi_runs_active{state="stalled"}: runs that sent no events for some time. The status of the executor decides what occurs to them, not the absence of events.

The security suite adds one more series from outside the server, mapi_security_probe_unexpected{executor}, through a textfile collector or a Pushgateway (Security suite).

Each response has X-Request-Id. This is the header of the caller if the caller sent one. If not, it is the trace id. When you report a problem, give this id. It finds the log lines and the trace.

docs.title: Dashboards, alerts and runbooks
docs.text: All the files that operators need are in ops/ at the root of the repository. ops/README.md tells how to import each one. The tables below come from those files.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
A Grafana dashboard and a Cloud Monitoring dashboard show the same series:

File Dashboard Sections ops/dashboards/cloud-monitoring-mapi-overview.json Cloud Monitoring: modeling-api — control plane 15 tiles: Running, Stalled, SSE clients, Integrity failures (1h), Active runs by state, Terminal outcomes (rate), Dispatch latency p95, Time to RUNNING p95 (SLO 90s), Event ingestion lag p95, Finalize outcomes (rate), Sandbox violations (rate), Quota rejections (rate), Cost per tenant (micros/s), HTTP requests by status, jobs.run 429 (Cloud Run) ops/dashboards/grafana-mapi-overview.json Grafana: modeling-api — control plane 18 panels in 6 rows: Fleet overview, Runs, Dispatch & time-to-RUNNING, Events & finalize, Security & abuse, HTTP API

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
ops/alerts/prometheus-rules.yml has the Prometheus rules, with recording rules such as mapi:global_spend_ratio. ops/alerts/cloud-monitoring-alerts.yaml has the same policies for Cloud Monitoring. A page alert wakes a person. A ticket alert is for the next working hour. The thresholds are initial values for the private beta.

Alert Severity Fires when Says Runbook MapiIntegrityFailure page increase(mapi_integrity_failures_total[10m]) > 0 Integrity failure finalizing a run (N in 10m) ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiSecurityProbeFailure page max(mapi_security_probe_unexpected) > 0 Security probe had an unexpected outcome on an enforcing executor ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiSandboxViolationSpike ticket mapi:sandbox_violations:rate5m > 0.2 for 10m Sandbox violations () elevated ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md MapiGlobalSpendCap70 ticket mapi:global_spend_ratio >= 0.70 and mapi:global_spend_ratio < 0.90 for 5m Global spend at N % of the cap ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiGlobalSpendCap90 page mapi:global_spend_ratio >= 0.90 for 1m Global spend at N % of the cap ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiJobsRun429 ticket mapi:executor_submit_throttled:rate5m > 0 for 5m 429s on jobs.run from (N/s) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiRunningExecutions70 ticket max by (executor) (mapi_executor_running_executions{executor=~"cloudrun.*"}) > 700 for 10m : N running executions (70 % of the 1,000 quota) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiQuotaRejections ticket sum by (scope) (rate(mapi_quota_rejections_total{code="QUOTA_EXCEEDED"}[15m])) > 0.05 for 15m Quota rejections sustained at the level ops/runbooks/incident-response.md MapiStalledRateHigh page mapi:runs_stalled / clamp_min(mapi:runs_running + mapi:runs_stalled, 1) > 0.2 for 10m N % of live runs are STALLED ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiTimeToRunningSlow ticket histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(mapi_time_to_running_seconds_bucket[30m])) by (le)) > 90 for 15m p95 time-to-RUNNING Ns (> 90s SLO) ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md MapiNoProgressIngested page (sum(rate(mapi_events_ingested_total{result="accepted"}[10m])) or vector(0)) == 0 and sum(mapi_runs_active{state=~"running\|provisioning"}) > 0 for 10m Runs are live but no events are being ingested ops/runbooks/db-failover.md

docs.title: Runbooks
docs.text:
Each alert names the runbook that solves it:

Runbook For Starts with ops/runbooks/db-failover.md database (Postgres) failover / outage Triggered by MapiNoProgressIngested, /readyz reporting postgres: fail, a Cloud SQL failover event, or widespread 5xx. ops/runbooks/incident-response.md incident response (control plane) The general flow for any control-plane incident. ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md rotating the HMAC / signing keys Two long-lived secrets protect run integrity (plan §8.6, §8.7, §9). ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md suspected or confirmed sandbox escape Triggered by MapiIntegrityFailure, MapiSecurityProbeFailure, a MapiSandboxViolationSpike, or any external report of untrusted code reaching something it should not. ops/runbooks/stuck-runs.md stuck runs (STALLED, stuck in a state, jobs.run 429) Triggered by MapiStalledRateHigh, MapiTimeToRunningSlow, MapiJobsRun429, MapiRunningExecutions70, MapiNoProgressIngested, or tenant reports that a run "isn't moving".

The sandbox-escape runbook is the incident response of the plan for a confirmed escape. It has these steps:

  1. Turn off uploaded code with the kill switch.
  2. Rotate the signing and HMAC keys. This makes all signed URLs that are open now invalid.
  3. Put the affected bundles in quarantine.
  4. Tell the tenants.

docs.title: Tests that guard the signals
docs.text:
Command What it checks make chaos A worker that stops during PROVISIONING and RUNNING, Pub/Sub redelivery and a changed sequence, redelivery with a bad HMAC, and a PostgreSQL restart during a run. Each run comes to one outcome, with one attempt and no duplicate execution make load-test 100 concurrent fits through the real dispatcher, reconciler and finalizer on the fake Cloud Run backend, with injected 429s, lost responses and duplicate pushes. No run is lost, and the p95 time-to-RUNNING stays below 90 s make security-suite The sandbox-escape probes (refer to Security suite)

All three run offline, against the embedded PostgreSQL and the in-memory or shim object store.

docs.title: Security hardening on Google Cloud v0.3
docs.text:
Tenants can submit specs (and, from M4, code) that run on the infrastructure of the platform. Thus the cloud deployment assumes that each execution is hostile. This page lists each control of the Google Cloud deployment. For each control, it gives the threat that it stops (plan §9) and its location in infra/terraform. It also tells how to do a check of the control on a live environment. The model at application level (supervisor and worker, signed events, verified outputs) is in Security model.

The last section is the M0 verification checklist. It lists the cloud behaviours that the design depends on, which nobody has confirmed against a real project yet. Do this checklist before production.

docs.title: Executions cannot reach the network
docs.text:
Control Threat Where Check Direct VPC egress with egress = ALL_TRAFFIC on each Job A path around the controls of the VPC modules/exec/jobs.tf gcloud run jobs describe shows the network interface and ALL_TRAFFIC No default route. One route to 199.36.153.4/30 A path to the internet modules/exec/network.tf gcloud compute routes list --filter=network:mapi-<env>-exec-<pool> lists only restricted-vip (and the subnet routes) Firewall: deny all egress (IPv4 and IPv6) at priority 65534, with logs Data exfiltration over IP modules/exec/network.tf Red-team probe: curl https://example.com from a Job fails. The denial shows in the firewall logs Firewall: allow only TCP 443 to the restricted VIP and port 53 to 35.199.192.0/19 The two exceptions that executions need modules/exec/network.tf gcloud compute firewall-rules list shows exactly these two allow rules DNS response policy: *. answered locally (sinkhole). The bypass applies only to googleapis.com, *.googleapis.com and metadata.google.internal DNS exfiltration (queries for <secret>.attacker.example) modules/exec/dns.tf Red-team gate below: the authoritative servers of a zone that you control never see a unique subdomain of that zone Private zone googleapis.com → restricted.googleapis.com (199.36.153.4–7) Access to Google APIs through endpoints without VPC-SC modules/exec/dns.tf From a Job, storage.googleapis.com resolves to 199.36.153.4–7 VPC-SC perimeter around the exec and data projects. All APIs that move data are restricted. The only VPC-accessible service is Cloud Storage Exfiltration through the VIP to a bucket, topic or dataset of an attacker (with all credentials) modules/perimeter Red-team probe: from a Job, a signed PUT URL for a bucket outside the perimeter fails, and a VPC-SC violation shows in the audit logs

Cloud DNS response policies can answer with local data or bypass the policy. They cannot return NXDOMAIN. Thus the "*. → NXDOMAIN" of the plan is a local sinkhole answer (192.0.2.1 / 100::1). The two addresses are non-routable, and the firewall denies them. For exfiltration, the important point is that the resolver answers the query locally and never sends it on.

docs.title: Identities hold only what they use
docs.text:
Identity Can Cannot Execution SA (one for each exec project) storage.objects.get + delete on the bootstrap bucket (custom role, no list) All other actions: no project roles, no secrets, no access to bundles or data Orchestrator Run, list, examine and cancel executions of Jobs that are there (custom role). Write bootstrap objects. Verify, copy and sign outputs (KMS signer) Make or change a Job (image, class, identity). Delete bundles API Read bucket metadata. Mint signed URLs (signBlob only on the URL signer). Read the public key of the signing key Sign manifests. Run Jobs. Read secrets other than its own Events Database (through db-url-app) All other actions URL signer The bucket permissions that signed URLs carry (custom reader/writer roles) No other actions. There is no key file, and nobody can impersonate it (only signBlob) Pub/Sub push SA Invoke the events service All other actions CI: ci-push / planner / deployer Push images / read-only plan / apply. Each is bound to one GitHub environment of one repository Use a long-lived key (there are none)

Where: modules/control/iam.tf, modules/exec/iam.tf, modules/data/iam.tf, modules/build/wif.tf. To do a check, use gcloud projects get-iam-policy <project> --flatten=bindings --format='table(bindings.role,bindings.members)' and gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://mapi-<env>-<bucket>.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Control Threat Where Public access prevention enforced and uniform bucket-level access on each bucket. No ACL resources Public objects, or objects that an ACL makes available modules/data/buckets.tf Bootstrap: 1-day lifecycle, soft delete off The RunSpec (signed URLs, HMAC key of the run) stays after its read-then-delete modules/data/buckets.tf Bundles: retention policy (locked in prod), no delete role for anybody, never force_destroy Artifact swap or replay after verification modules/data/ Quarantine and runs expire (7 and 30 days), soft delete off Tenant data that stays after its purpose modules/data/buckets.tf Optional CMEK (data.kms_key_name) Crypto-shredding for enterprise tenants modules/data/buckets.tf CORS only for the app origin, and only the methods that each bucket needs Cross-origin abuse of signed URLs modules/data/buckets.tf

docs.title: Secrets and signing
docs.text:
• No secret in Terraform state or plans. Ephemeral resources make the database passwords, the root secret of the server and the metrics scrape token. The API-token pepper and the audit key come from the root secret. The OAuth client secret is an ephemeral variable. Terraform writes all of them with write-only arguments (password_wo, secret_data_wo). Cloud Run revisions refer to secrets by name, never by value.
  • Secrets are replicated in one region (the control region), for data residency.
  • KMS signs the bundle manifests (EC P-256 / SHA-256, HSM in prod). Only the orchestrator can sign. The API verifies with the public key before it mints a URL for a bundle (plan §8.6). Key versions are destroyed only after a 30-day schedule.

  • Database: only private IP, TLS necessary, password policy enforced. There are four roles:

    • The migrations own the schema.
    • mapi_app and mapi_gateway (API, events) are not the table owner. Thus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies to them. The gateway sees only identity tables and some metadata columns.
    • Only mapi_orchestrator gets BYPASSRLS from the migrations, and only the orchestrator can read its URL.

    The managed pooler runs in transaction mode. This is safe, because the tenant is set with SET LOCAL for each transaction.

docs.title: Event path and control-plane ingress
docs.text:
• The Logging sink of each exec project routes only the jsonPayload.mapi_event:* lines of the Jobs of this environment. It writes as its own identity, which can only publish to the events topic.
  • The _Default sink of the exec project excludes user output (plan §8.7, modules/exec/logging.tf). The log and progress events of the runner Jobs still go to the events service through the routing sink. But the exec project does not ingest them (or bill them). State changes, warnings, errors, completions and the system logs of Cloud Run stay.
  • The events service is internal-only and protected by IAM. Only the push identity can invoke it. Cloud Run does a check of the signature and audience of the push token before the request goes to the container. The server also does a check of the claims (mapi_spec.auth.check_push_claims) and of the HMAC of each line.
  • After 10 attempts, events that cannot be delivered go to a dead-letter topic. They are not dropped.
  • Behind the load balancer, the API accepts traffic only from the load balancer. TLS 1.2+ (MODERN profile). The plot sandbox has its own host, as plan §10.3 needs. In prod, use a different registrable domain. Each backend has the Cloud Armor policy below.

docs.title: Cloud Armor
docs.text:
modules/control/armor.tf makes a Cloud Armor policy with the load balancer (var.domains). It attaches the policy to the api, web and plots backends (lb.tf). You can give your own policy with security_policy, or turn it off with cloud_armor.enabled = false.

Rule Priority Threat Setting Trusted ranges (CI, office) 100 Your own load tests cause a ban cloud_armor.trusted_ip_ranges (a maximum of 10 CIDRs, never *) OWASP CRS: sqli, xss, lfi, rce, scannerdetection (v3.3 stable) 1000–1004 Injection probes and scanners against the API and the SPA cloud_armor.waf_mode (preview by default), cloud_armor.waf_sensitivity (paranoia level 1–4, default 1) Rate ban for each IP on /auth/signup (and /v1/signup) 2000 Sign-up floods, Sybil farms rate_limits.signup_per_minute (10) Rate ban for each IP on /auth/* 2001 Credential stuffing on sign-in, callback and e-mail verification rate_limits.auth_per_minute (120) Rate ban for each IP on /v1/embeds/* 2002 Scraping of public embed links rate_limits.embed_per_minute (600) Rate ban for each IP on /v1/endpoints/<alias>/score 2003 Denial of wallet through scores rate_limits.score_per_minute (600) Default last allow
  • Preview, then enforce. The OWASP rules start in preview. Cloud Armor logs the matches (jsonPayload.previewSecurityPolicy on the request logs of the load balancer), but it blocks nothing. Do these steps:
    1. Monitor one week of real traffic.
    2. Where a rule matches legitimate requests, add exclusions or decrease the sensitivity. Spec YAML and plot JSON are the most probable matches.
    3. Set waf_mode = "enforce" (in prod: cloud_armor_waf_mode). Enforced matches answer 403.
  • Rate bans are enforced from the start (rate_limit_mode = "enforce"). Above the threshold for each minute, a client gets 429. At three times the threshold in five minutes, Cloud Armor bans the address for ban_duration_sec (600 s). The limits of the API apply behind these bans (sign-up for each address, domain and platform, and token and tenant request rates).
  • Adaptive Protection (Layer 7 DDoS defense) is on. It learns the normal traffic of each backend and sends alerts with a suggested rule. It never blocks automatically.
  • Request bodies. Cloud Armor parses JSON bodies (json_parsing = STANDARD). Thus the rules see field values, not raw text. Cloud Armor examines only the first request_body_inspection_size bytes of a body (8 KB by default, a maximum of 64 KB). It examines larger bodies only partially, and does not block them. Examples are spec documents and inline XrJSON score payloads of up to 5 MB. The API enforces its own body limits. Signed-URL uploads go directly to Cloud Storage and never go through the load balancer.

Do a check on a live environment:

gcloud compute backend-services describe mapi-prod-api --global --format='value(securityPolicy)'
gcloud compute security-policies describe mapi-prod-edge --format='yaml(rules,adaptiveProtectionConfig)'
# a burst against sign-up is banned (expect 429s after the threshold)
for i in $(seq 1 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://app.example.com/auth/signup; done | sort | uniq -c

Logs and tenant deletion. The load balancer logs each request (log_config.sample_rate = 1) into the _Default bucket of the control project. Terraform sets the retention of this bucket explicitly (log_retention_days, 30 days, modules/control/logging.tf). Tenant deletion does not purge logs. The logs hold ids, not content, and they expire with that retention (Deleting data).

docs.title: Supply chain
docs.text:
• You deploy images only by digest. Terraform refuses tags. The tags of the registry are immutable, and nothing is deleted automatically. The digests that live model versions use must stay (plan §12).
  • Builds attach SBOM and provenance attestations (build-push.sh, --no-attestations to skip).
  • A Binary Authorization attestor, note and signing key are available (modules/build/binauthz.tf). Enforcement on the Jobs (binary_authorization = true) starts in a later release, when CI attests each base digest.
  • CI authenticates with Workload Identity Federation. Nobody ever makes a service-account key.

docs.title: M0 verification checklist
docs.text: This checklist has the plan items with the mark [verify M0], and the assumptions that this Terraform adds. Each item needs a temporary environment (dev, perimeter enforced) and a probe Job built from a base image. For each item, record the date, the result and the evidence (log query, screenshot).

docs.title: Network and DNS
docs.text:
• The Direct VPC egress resolver obeys response policies. From a Job, resolve <random>.probe.<zone you control> (A, AAAA and TXT). Pass: the answer is the sinkhole (or NODATA), and the authoritative query logs of the zone never see the name. This is the red-team gate of plan §9. If it fails, Cloud Run Jobs cannot host untrusted code (fallback: GKE Sandbox). Until this item passes, verified and public tenants stay off. After it passes, set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED=true on the orchestrator. Then record the security-suite and conformance evidence (the shared-tier gate). New tenants are verified by default, so the private beta needs this item.
  • Cloud DNS accepts a wildcard rule for the root (*.). Local data for A/AAAA does not send TXT or other record types upstream (the same probe, other types).
  • The bypass rules work: storage.googleapis.com resolves to 199.36.153.4–7, and metadata.google.internal still serves the token of the execution.
  • Egress is really denied: curl to a public IP and to a public name, a raw TCP connect to 8.8.8.8:53 and an ICMP ping all fail. The firewall logs show the denials.
  • VPC-SC applies to Cloud Run Jobs: from a Job, a signed PUT URL for a bucket outside the perimeter fails, and a VPC-SC violation shows in the audit logs.

docs.title: Sandbox
docs.text:
• The supervisor/worker uid split works on gen2: the supervisor can start the worker under uid 10001 with no_new_privs and a seccomp filter. The worker cannot ptrace the supervisor or read /proc/1/environ. Cloud Run runs the USER of the image. Thus the runner images must start the supervisor as root (or with the capabilities to change users) for this item.
  • Execution overrides are env-only: jobs.run with overrides cannot change the image, resources, service account or network. Try each one. All must be refused or impossible.
  • Ephemeral disk: find out if Jobs have a disk in addition to the in-memory filesystem. Find out what occurs at the memory limit (exit 137 → RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, class+1 offered).
  • In-memory filesystem limits: a write of the scratch budget of the class (3/6/12 GiB for S/M/L) succeeds. A larger write stops the execution, and the host continues to operate correctly.
  • Bootstrap read-then-delete: after the supervisor deletes the RunSpec, the object is gone (you cannot restore a soft-deleted copy). The nonce in the audit log points at nothing.

docs.title: Quotas and rates (plan §8.8)
docs.text:
• Jobs for each region: 1,000 (the inventory uses 9 for each exec project).
  • Running executions: 1,000 for each project and region. An alert fires at 70 %.
  • jobs.run rate: 180 each minute for each region. The token bucket of the dispatcher stays below it. A 429 causes an alarm and a back-off (mapi_spec.quotas.backoff_seconds).
  • Regional CPU and memory for the expected fan-out (sweeps, SBC).
  • Cold start of a base image of about 2.5 GB: measure the p50. The p95 of time-to-RUNNING must be below 90 s.

docs.title: Control plane
docs.text:
• Logging → Pub/Sub path: an event line goes to the events service with the labels of the execution (job, execution) in the push payload, in some seconds.
  • Pub/Sub push to an internal-only service works (a subscription in the same project).
  • Managed connection pooling: the pooler port (6432 by default here) and transaction mode work with the driver of the server. LISTEN uses the direct URL.
  • BYPASSRLS: the migrate role can grant it to mapi_orchestrator on Cloud SQL.
  • run.jobs.runWithOverrides without iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the execution service account is sufficient for the orchestrator. If not, grant actAs only on that account.
  • Image indexes: Cloud Run runs the images that build-push.sh pushes with attestations (an OCI index). If not, build with --no-attestations.

docs.title: Red-team probes (security suite, plan §13)
docs.text:
When the platform operates, run these probes each night. Keep them green for two weeks before cut line B:

  • Use of the metadata token for more than the bootstrap object.
  • HTTP and DNS egress.
  • Writes outside signed objects.
  • Use of the URL of a different tenant.
  • Reads of /proc/1.
  • Overlay .pth injection.
  • Fork, memory and disk bombs.
  • Log flood (SANDBOX_VIOLATION).
  • Forged events (bad HMAC, replayed sequence numbers).
  • A tampered manifest (INTEGRITY_FAILURE).
  • ReDoS schemas.
  • Plot XSS and postMessage abuse.

docs.title: Security suite v0.3
docs.text:
The security suite is a set of hostile probes. For each executor, it reports which attacks the executor BLOCKED and which it ALLOWED. It compares the result with the guarantees of the isolation level of that executor. It runs each night in the cloud. It must stay green for two weeks before public code upload (cut line B) can open.

The suite is in security/ at the root of the repository, and it is never installed. security/ is not a uv workspace member, so uv sync --all-packages does not include it. Its malicious plugin is also not registered as a mapi.models entry point. Thus the platform can never find it. The suite runs on the installed environment with security/src on PYTHONPATH. The Make targets do this.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
make security-list                              # the probe corpus
make security-suite                             # EXECUTOR=local-process (always runnable)
make security-suite EXECUTOR=docker-gvisor      # sandbox probes inside a gVisor container

If an outcome is not acceptable for the isolation level of the executor, make security-suite stops with a status that is not zero. It also writes .local/security-<executor>.prom. This file exports mapi_security_probe_unexpected{executor} for a textfile collector or a Pushgateway. The MapiSecurityProbeFailure alert in ops/alerts/ monitors that series. The nightly workflow pushes the file to the Pushgateway that the MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL repository secret names. Without that secret, the alert has no data. Then the failed nightly job is the signal.

docs.title: The probes
docs.text:
Isolation probes test the controls of the operating system and the sandbox. Each probe tries a hostile action, safely and with limits. It reports ALLOWED or BLOCKED:

Probe Attempts metadata_token Get an instance token from the metadata server http_egress, dns_egress Open an outbound connection. Resolve a unique subdomain (DNS exfiltration) write_outside_scratch Write outside the output area of the run reuse_foreign_url Connect to an object-store endpoint. This is the first step to use the signed URL of a different run read_proc1_environ, read_supervisor_mem Read the environment or memory of the supervisor pth_injection Put a .pth or sitecustomize file into site-packages fork_bomb, memory_bomb, disk_bomb Go above the process, memory or scratch limits (all capped) log_flood Write more than the log cap of the run

Platform probes call the real defences of the control plane in mapi_spec and mapi_plots. All executors must stop them (BLOCKED):

Probe Attempts forged_stdout_event A run event with the wrong HMAC tampered_manifest An output object that the signed manifest did not list redos_schema A catastrophic-backtracking regex in a plot spec plot_xss_exfil A plot with an external image URL or a <script> caption reuse_foreign_manifest The signed manifest of one run, sent under the key of a different run

docs.title: What each isolation level must block
docs.text:
Isolation Executors Isolation probes Platform probes PROCESS local-process, docker (runc) The suite accepts the two outcomes, because these are not security boundaries BLOCKED GVISOR docker-gvisor (shared tiers only on a network declared with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED) BLOCKED BLOCKED MICROVM cloud (the cloudrun-jobs executor) BLOCKED BLOCKED

SKIPPED is always acceptable, for example when there is no procfs or no Docker daemon. ERROR is never acceptable. An executor needs two items before it can take verified and public tenants:

  • A passing run of this matrix, recorded for the current caps of the executor.
  • A passing run of the 12-case executor conformance suite (packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py).

Record the two with PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence. Refer to the shared-tier gate. For that gate, the network probes (http_egress, dns_egress, metadata_token) must run, and the executor must stop them.

docs.title: Where the probes run
docs.text:
• local-process: the suite process is the execution environment. Thus the probes run in the process. On a developer machine, most isolation probes are ALLOWED. This is expected and documented.
  • docker, docker-gvisor: the isolation probes run in a locked-down container (--network none, read-only root, non-root user, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, and --runtime runsc for gVisor). Without a Docker daemon, they report SKIPPED. The platform probes still run.
  • cloud: the probes must run inside a Cloud Run Jobs execution of a base image. The suite compares them with the MICROVM row. Thus --executor cloud does not run (exit status 2) where CLOUD_RUN_JOB and CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION are not set. A report from a laptop or a CI runner would describe the wrong sandbox. The base images do not contain the suite yet, and Terraform defines no probe Job. Thus we must still connect the nightly cloud run. Refer to M2 verification. The authoritative DNS-exfiltration check reads the query logs of a zone that we control (security hardening).

security/THREAT-MODEL.md connects each probe to its threat, and to the control that must stop it.

docs.title: Sign-up and abuse controls v0.4
docs.text: With self-service sign-up, each person with an e-mail address can make a public workspace. Public workspaces run untrusted data through trusted code: only built-in models and declarative specs (cut line A). This page is for the person who operates the platform. It tells how sign-up works, what stops abuse, and what operators examine. Each variable on this page is in the configuration reference. The HTTP operations are in the HTTP API reference.

docs.title: How sign-up works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant API as API (/auth)
    participant M as Mailer
    B->>API: POST /auth/signup {email, name, organisation, accepted_terms}
    API->>API: terms, blocklist, bot check, rate limits
    API->>M: verification link (single use, 24 h)
    API-->>B: 202 {"status": "check_email"}
    B->>API: POST /auth/verify-email {token}
    API->>API: create tenant (public), project "default", admin grant; Sybil checks
    API-->>B: 200 {tenant_id, login_url}
    B->>API: GET /auth/login (OpenID sign-in with that address)
  1. POST /auth/signup first refuses requests that can never sign up. These are: terms not accepted (TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED), an address that is malformed or disposable (EMAIL_NOT_ALLOWED), and a failed bot check. Then it applies the rate limits below (RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After).
  2. It keeps the sign-up with an HMAC of a new 200-bit token. It never keeps the token. It sends the link MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL by e-mail. Only the newest link of an address works.
  3. The answer is the same for all addresses, new or already registered. Thus nobody can use sign-up to find out who has an account. If an account that is already there verifies a new sign-up, it gets one more workspace.

  4. POST /auth/verify-email uses the token. In one transaction, it makes these items:

    • The tenant (tier public, with an id from the organisation name).
    • Its default project.
    • The person as tenant admin. This is an invitation that the person gets at the first sign-in with that verified address.
    • The verification record of the tenant.

    A link that is expired, replaced or used answers 410 LINK_EXPIRED.

The audit log records all events: auth.signup, auth.signup_rejected, auth.email_verified, tenant.create and auth.signup_flagged. It records a limited number of auth.signup_rejected events for each client in each minute, because each person can cause them.

docs.title: Mailers
docs.text:
MAPI_MAILER Use Notes smtp Production smtplib with STARTTLS (necessary, never opportunistic) or implicit TLS (MAPI_SMTP_TLS=ssl, port 465). The mailer verifies certificates. Needs MAPI_SMTP_HOST. Credentials in MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME/MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD. No third-party mail API outbox dev profile, end-to-end tests One JSON file for each message (mode 0600) under MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR. The dev profile serves the newest messages at GET /dev/outbox?to=<address>, with the token in tags.token console Single-user installations Logs the message, with the link none Sign-up is off

The multi-tenant profile refuses console and outbox while sign-up is on. With these mailers, each person who can read the logs or the disk could verify all addresses. Without an SMTP host, sign-up is off (POST /auth/signup answers 403). Messages are plain text. The mailer refuses header values with line breaks. Thus nobody can inject a header through the name of a sign-up.

# dev: follow a verification link without a mail server
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/auth/signup -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ana@acme.example","name":"Ana","accepted_terms":true,"terms_version":"2026-10"}'
TOKEN=$(curl -s 'localhost:8000/dev/outbox?to=ana@acme.example' | jq -r '.items[0].tags.token')
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/auth/verify-email -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"token\":\"$TOKEN\"}"

docs.title: Disposable addresses
docs.text: The built-in list (mapi_spec.trust.DEFAULT_DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS) is small on purpose. To add domains, use MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS (comma-separated). You can also point MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH at a file (one domain on each line, # comments). For example, use a public disposable-domain list that your deployment updates. A domain on the list also blocks its subdomains. If a deployment wants a vendor check, it can add a mapi_spec.trust.DisposableEmailPolicy to TrustServices.email_policy.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Limit Default Variable Sign-ups for each client address in each hour 5 MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR Verified sign-ups for each e-mail domain in each day 25 MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY Verified sign-ups on the whole platform in each hour 500 MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR Verification attempts for each client address in each minute 20 MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE

The server counts the limits in Postgres from the sign-ups. Thus the limits apply across API instances. Each request counts toward the limit for each address. This limit stops floods of unverified sign-ups. The domain and platform caps count only sign-ups whose link was opened. If not, a person could send 25 false @gmail.com (or @your-customer.com) addresses. That domain could then not sign up for one day.

Large free-mail domains (MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, by default gmail.com, outlook.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, proton.me and similar domains) have no cap for each domain. Behind the Google Cloud load balancer, Cloud Armor adds rate bans for each IP in front of /auth/signup and /auth/*. These bans apply before a request goes to the API. The server keeps client addresses only as keyed digests.

The client address is the peer that connects, but not if that peer is a trusted proxy (MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES). Then the client address is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy. Thus callers behind one load balancer keep separate limits. A caller cannot forge its address when it sends the header itself. The multi-tenant profile does not start without the setting (use none when clients connect to the API directly).

docs.title: Sybil heuristics and the review queue
docs.text:
When a sign-up is verified, the platform looks back MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS (30) days for workspaces that come from the same signals:

Flag Signal same_ip the same client address (keyed digest) same_device the same browser: a random, HttpOnly mapi_device cookie that the server sets at sign-up same_email the same e-mail address domain_burst many verified sign-ups from one domain in one hour (two times the threshold). Never for the shared free-mail domains

At MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD (3) earlier workspaces, the server flags the new sign-up. The workspace works, and it waits in the review queue (auth.signup_flagged in the audit log). With MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND=true, the server suspends a flagged workspace (read-only) until an operator approves it.

Operators examine flagged sign-ups:

# the queue, newest first
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/admin/signups?review=flagged"
# reject: the workspace is suspended (audited, with the reason)
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/admin/signups/$ID/review" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"decision":"reject","reason":"device farm"}'
# approve: the flag is cleared, and a suspension the review caused is lifted

An approval removes only the suspensions that the review caused. It never removes a suspension that an operator set. If you reject a sign-up that was never verified, its link stops working.

docs.title: Identity verification and cut line A
docs.text:
Each tenant has a verification record. GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification answers email_verified, identity_verified, the method and uploaded_code_allowed, with a reason in plain words. The rule (mapi_spec.trust.uploaded_code_allowed):

Trust tier Uploaded code (plugins with an overlay) internal, self-hosted-trusted allowed verified only after identity verification public never before cut line B (MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED, planned). After cut line B, only with identity verification

The server enforces the rule at run admission. If a tenant cannot run uploaded code, the server refuses its runs of uploaded code with 403 IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED. The audit log records this as a denied run.create. The server always admits built-in models and declarative specs. The plugin upload of M4 calls the same check (mapi_server.services.verification.require_uploaded_code_allowed).

After a check outside the platform (a contract, an invoice), operators record the identity verification:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X PUT \
  "$API/v1/admin/tenants/acme/verification" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"identity_verified":true,"method":"manual","reason":"signed enterprise contract"}'

The request-path database role can only read verification records. Thus no tenant session can mark its own tenant as verified. A card or document provider connects as a mapi_server.services.trust.IdentityVerifier. A deterministic FakeIdentityVerifier is available for tests and drills. No vendor is integrated yet.

docs.title: Bot checks
docs.text: SignupRequest.challenge contains a bot-check token (for example Cloudflare Turnstile). The server asks TrustServices.challenge (mapi_server.services.trust.SignupChallenge). The default accepts all sign-ups. Then the rate limits, Cloud Armor and the Sybil review do the work. A deployment that adds a vendor check implements the protocol.

docs.title: Runbook: a sign-up wave
docs.text:
1. Look at the queue (GET /v1/admin/signups?review=flagged) and the audit log (auth.signup_rejected, auth.signup_flagged).
  2. Decrease the limits (MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR, MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR), or set MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND=true.
  3. Deploy the API again.
  4. Block the domains (MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS).
  5. At the edge, decrease cloud_armor.rate_limits.signup_per_minute in Terraform.
  6. Reject the flagged sign-ups.
  7. Suspend all other workspaces that you must stop with PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{id}. Public workspaces never ran uploaded code, so their runs used only built-in models. The kill switches and the spend cap still limit what they can spend.
  8. To close sign-up fully, set MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED=false.

docs.title: Troubleshooting v0.2
docs.text: Start with make status. It shows which services of a make dev stack operate, and if the embedded PostgreSQL runs. The Settings page of the web app shows the readiness checks of the API. curl -s $MAPI_API_URL/readyz shows the same data from a shell.

docs.title: Port conflicts
docs.text:
If a different process uses a port that make dev needs, make dev does not start:

cannot start - fix these first
  - 127.0.0.1:8000 is already in use

The port can belong to a different make dev (in a different terminal or worktree), a compose stack, or a program that is not related. Find the process. Then stop it, or move the platform:

lsof -iTCP:8000 -sTCP:LISTEN          # who has it?
make stop                              # if it is another make dev of this checkout

To move the platform, export the addresses in each shell that connects to it. Then start again. All components (make dev, make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client, the build of the web app) read the same variables:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174
make dev
Port Variable Service 8000 MAPI_API_URL API 4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT GCS shim (signed URLs point here) 5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Web app 5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Plot sandbox

A state directory is for one stack at a time. To run two stacks at the same time, also give each stack its own MAPI_DATA_DIR. The Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on 5173 and 5174. Thus run it only while make dev is stopped. Docker Compose publishes the same four ports as make dev, on purpose. Run only one of the two.

docs.title: The local stack
docs.text:
cannot start - fix these first

The supervisor does a check of each necessary item before it starts a service. In addition to ports, it can show these errors:

  • module 'mapi_server.__main__' not found: your environment is not current. Run uv sync --all-packages (or make install).
  • exe 'pnpm' not found or run pnpm install first: install pnpm (corepack enable) and the JavaScript dependencies (pnpm install). You can also skip the front end with make dev WITHOUT=web,plots.
already running (supervisor pid N) A previous make dev still runs, possibly in a different terminal. Run make stop. The process can be gone while its state file stays (for example, after kill -9). Then the next start finds the dead pid and ignores the file. plots exited unexpectedly with status 143; stopping the stack A process outside the stack sent SIGTERM to the service (for example a pkill vite). The supervisor never starts services again without a message. It stops all services and stops itself. Start it again. The reconciler recovers the runs that were in progress as a new attempt. postgres | failed to start Read .local/pg/log. If the data directory came from a different PostgreSQL major version, or is corrupt, run make clean-local. This deletes the local database. make stop stops an orphaned server from an earlier crash. migrate exited with status 1 The output of the migration is immediately above this line. Repair the migration, or reset the database with make stop && make clean-local. Then run make dev again. api not ready after 60s The API process runs, but GET /healthz never succeeded. Look at the api | lines. The usual causes are a wrong DATABASE_URL, or a GCS shim that the API cannot connect to. Validation says the catalog is unavailable At the first start against a new environment (and after each change to uv.lock), the worker puts a sandboxed describe run in the queue to export the catalog: no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. This takes some seconds. If it fails, its run page under Runs shows the reason. The server refuses MAPI_PROFILE MAPI_PROFILE is also the config-profile variable of the CLI. If you exported a client profile name, unset it in the shell that runs make dev. The server accepts only single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev. Leftover processes after a crash Each service runs in its own process group. You can find it with ps -o pid,pgid,command. If the supervisor does not respond in 30 s, make stop also stops the process groups in .local/dev/supervisor.json.

docs.title: The web app and plots
docs.text:
API unreachable in the header, or the app cannot load data The app calls the API at the VITE_API_BASE that it started with. make dev sets it from MAPI_API_URL. If you start Vite yourself, also set it. The API must also permit the origin of the app. It permits MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, so the two must agree. Plots stay blank

Make sure of these three conditions:

  • MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN are different origins.
  • The plot sandbox runs (make status).
  • The sandbox permits the origin of the app (VITE_APP_ORIGINS, set by make dev).

The browser console names the blocked origin.

Uploads fail in the browser The browser sends files with PUT directly to MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. The shim must permit the origin of the app (--cors-origin, which make dev sets from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN). The CSP of the app must permit the storage origin (VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS).

docs.title: Runs and scoring
docs.text: A run is stalled No progress came for some time. This is a warning, not a failure. The status of the executor decides if the run is alive. A long PyTensor compile on the first fit of a new machine can cause it. DEV_MODE_ISOLATION on every run This is expected on a laptop. The local executor runs the model code as your own user, without a separate uid or no_new_privs. Refer to the security model. SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE when scoring You must give a side table with score_policy: supplied (in the demo, fx) in the score request (side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}). It must include the scored dates. To skip it, enter the pipeline after the step that uses it (inputs_stage: weekly). MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, … These are typed errors from the static checks. The request asks for an answer that the model cannot give honestly. The detail and the JSON pointer of the problem tell what is wrong. Error codes lists the codes. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED The run did not have sufficient memory or scratch space. Retry on the run page suggests the next resource class. Under compose, increase MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS. INTEGRITY_FAILURE when downloading The signed manifest of the bundle does not verify. Thus the API does not mint download links. Locally, this occurs when somebody deleted .local/keys/. You cannot trust the old model versions after this. Fit again. SCHEMA_INVALID: "the score request has no data" The request has no data, no scenario dataset and no forecast horizon. The server refuses it before a run starts. Give a dataset, a scenario dataset or a horizon. The Score page shows No new data only for Forecast, or when a scenario dataset gives the values. SETTINGS_INVALID before the fit starts The settings of the model break a rule that uses more than one field. The harness reads the settings before it transforms or splits the data, so this error comes early. The message tells which settings to change. For example, sci.storm_localisation refuses a render of more than 50 million values.

docs.title: Workflows and science models v0.9
docs.text: EXPRESSION_ERROR in a branch node The condition could not be calculated. Usually, it compares a value that is null or not there, for example the R-hat of a fit with one chain. Wrap the reference in coalesce(...) or exists(...), or fit two or more chains. PLOT_UNSAFE on a workflow node The plot output of the node did not pass the plot sanitizer, so the node failed. The server does a check of each plot output when it collects it, and again when it serves it. Look at the recipe and the settings of the plot.render node. The tests of the science plugin skip The tests that read the real data of pymc-challenges run only when MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA gives the data/ directory of a local copy. Refer to Science data. make docs-screenshots-science stops at an upload (ENOENT) The script reads scotland_lip.nc, heat_plate_e51.nc, lazega_coworkers.nc, unc13_dstorm.nc, primates301.nc and bci_camera_traps.nc from .local/science, or from the folder that MAPI_SCIENCE_DATA gives.
