Export them first with python -m mapi_plugin_science.export. The recipe monitor screenshot shows Reused make docs-screenshots-science ran before on the same stack. The server used the earlier results of the recipe again. To capture a run in progress, use a new stack (a new MAPI_DATA_DIR).

docs.title: Docker and compose
docs.text:
error: the Docker daemon is not reachable make docker-build and make compose-up first do a check with docker info. Start Docker Desktop, Colima or dockerd. You can also use make dev, which needs no Docker. required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is missing a value Copy .env.example to .env and set POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Compose reads .env from the repository root. image check failed: forbidden distribution 'numpy' is installed (server build) A control-plane dependency now adds a science package. To see the closure, run uv run python scripts/lock_closure.py "mapi-server[docker]" --lacks numpy. Then find the dependency that adds numpy. Contracts: 1 broken in the contracts stage Server code imports a forbidden module. make lint (lint-imports) shows the same failure locally, with the import chain. PyTensor found no C++ compiler (base-bayes / base-forecast build) g++ is missing from MAPI_APT_PACKAGES. The PyMC images also need it at run time. The api container is unhealthy

Run make compose-logs SERVICE=api. These are the usual causes:

  • migrate failed. Look at its logs.
  • The DATABASE_URL password does not agree with the database volume. This occurs after you change POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Then reset with make compose-down VOLUMES=1. This deletes the data.
no bundle-signing key at /var/lib/mapi/keys/... and MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE is off api or worker started before migrate made the key, or without the keys volume. Do a check with make compose-logs SERVICE=migrate. Never point the two services at different keys. If you do, the API refuses each bundle that the worker signs, with INTEGRITY_FAILURE. 400 Invalid host header from the API, or nginx closes the connection The stack answers only known host names (a DNS-rebinding guard). You can connect to it with a name other than 127.0.0.1, localhost or api. Then add that name to MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (the API) and MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (the nginx of the web image). mapi-entrypoint: /tmp/mapi-cache is not writable The container runs with a read-only root filesystem, but without a writable /tmp. Add --tmpfs /tmp (compose already does this). Port already allocated on docker compose up A make dev stack, or a different process, uses 4443, 8000, 5173 or 5174. Stop it with make stop. The two stacks use the same ports on purpose, so that the same URLs work with the two stacks. nginx exits with host not found or invalid number of arguments in "set" MAPI_API_UPSTREAM is empty or malformed. It must be a URL without a path, for example http://api:8000.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes are documented here. The project follows Semantic Versioning; milestone releases are tagged on main.

docs.title: Deep learning and image collections
docs.text: You can now train neural networks on the platform. The new package mapi-jax has three models: a network for tables, an image classifier and a classifier that starts from pretrained weights. The training shows the training and validation curves while it runs, logs images of the predictions, stops early, saves checkpoints and gives draws. Large image sets upload as image collections: the client uploads only the new images, and an upload that stops can continue. A new resource class gives a run one GPU.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Image collections: the dataset layout collection. A version is a manifest (manifest.parquet), a summary (collection.json, CollectionInfo) and packs of images, stored one time for each tenant at t/{tenant}/blobs/packs/{digest}.zip. A version can hold 1 000 000 images of different sizes. The pack address is pack_digest(size, crc32c, md5) over the digests that the store calculated. Each image is identified by its SHA-256, and each read makes sure that the SHA-256 is correct. Contracts in mapi_spec.collection.
  • DatasetVersionCreate.collection (CollectionSource: a manifest upload, up to 64 part uploads, a base version and CollectionOptions). The ingest run reads the parts in ranges, makes sure that each image has the SHA-256 of its name, reads the image headers and writes the explorer views of a sample. The finalizer copies the parts to the shared pack path.
  • Resumable uploads and deduplication: GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id} (UploadSession.received), POST .../uploads/{upload_id}/renew and POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/blobs/missing (BlobQuery, BlobMissing: the images that the base version does not have).
  • Client and CLI: datasets.upload_collection, datasets.missing_images, datasets.get_upload, datasets.renew_upload; mapi datasets upload-images, mapi datasets missing-images and mapi datasets upload-weights. The parts are deterministic zip files, and a state file continues an upload.
  • Web app: the upload step Folder of images (labels from folders or from a manifest column, progress, retry and continue), and the collection summary on the version page.
  • mapi_sdk.collection: Collection, the lazy and seeded CollectionLoader, ArrayImageLoader, ImageLoader, Batch, Augment and to_xarray(max_samples, size). mapi_sdk.images decodes images. mapi_sdk.testing.images makes small test collections.
  • Model hooks fit_batches and score_batches (Capabilities.input = "collection"). The harness gives these models a loader of the rows of the split. Other models get a seeded sample of a collection, as set by data.collection (CollectionRead).
  • Model side tables: ModelManifest.side_table_params, FitContext.side_tables and ResolvedModel.side_tables. A score request never needs a table that only the model reads.
  • The upload format safetensors (WeightsOptions): a file of network weights becomes a weights dataset (weights(param) and the attribute mapi_weights). mapi_sdk.safetensors reads and writes safetensors files with numpy only.
  • mapi-jax (packages/sdk-jax, Apache-2.0) on JAX, Flax (nnx) and Optax: the models dl.mlp, dl.cnn_classifier and dl.finetune_classifier, and the step dl.embed (image features from a frozen pretrained network). The shared trainer logs loss and accuracy (or rmse) with the label split, logs prediction images and the confusion matrix as media, stops early, can be cancelled, is deterministic for a seed, and saves checkpoints every N epochs. The models give draws from a last-layer Laplace approximation or from MC dropout.
  • fit.checkpoint.every_epochs, and file checkpoints (ckpt-<key>.weights.safetensors, ckpt-<key>.opt.safetensors, ckpt-<key>.meta.json) with resume.
  • tabular.image_logistic (model version 1.1.0) takes input: features, for example the output of dl.embed.
  • The resource class GPU (one NVIDIA L4, 8 vCPU, 32 GiB) and the runner image base-dl (mapi-jax[cuda12]). The Cloud Run inventory has the Jobs base-dl × {S, M, L, GPU} (Terraform gpu_jobs, default off). The docker executor asks for a GPU when MAPI_DOCKER_GPUS=true. Otherwise, and with the local-process executor, a GPU run uses the CPU and shows the warning GPU_UNAVAILABLE. The price table has a GPU row with an accelerator price.
  • Plots: ml.training_curves, ml.confusion_epochs and ml.misclassified, with About cards. The fit adds them when the bundle has the training history.
  • About cards for dl.mlp, dl.cnn_classifier, dl.finetune_classifier and dl.embed.
  • Documentation: the guide Deep learning, and the section Large image sets: collections of the guide Image data.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Checkpoint.every_draws is optional. A checkpoint has exactly one of every_draws and every_epochs. Documents with every_draws do not change.
  • Capabilities.input accepts collection. DataLayout and DatasetVersion.layout accept collection. IngestJob takes exactly one of mapping, preset, assembly and collection. IngestFormat has safetensors.
  • ResourceClass has GPU as its last member. next_up() walks the CPU classes only, and quotas with a maximum class below GPU refuse it. ResourceClassSpec has accelerator and accelerators. ClassPrice and ResourceUsage have accelerator fields (left out when zero).
  • validate_spec takes dataset_layout and side_table_layouts: a collection takes no pipeline steps for a model that trains on batches, takes only row splits, and cannot be a side table. Validation refuses a spec that selects GPU for a model that does not use a GPU (the GPU Job runs only these models). It warns when a spec sets every_epochs for a model that cannot save checkpoints.
  • An upload whose file arrived has the status uploaded. It stays usable after its PUT URL expires, so a collection upload that takes more than one hour, or that continues the next day, can make its version. The storage quota counts a pending upload until the housekeeper retires it. The housekeeper deletes an arrived upload that no version used after 7 days. get_upload needs update on dataset, because its answer holds the signed PUT URL. When you renew an expired upload, the server does a check of the storage quota again.
  • The size of a collection version is the size of the packs that it uses, also the images in a part that the manifest does not use.
  • The worker environment allows JAX_PLATFORMS, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
  • The images mapi/base-bayes and mapi/base-ml have mapi-jax for the CPU, so that dl.embed works in front of their models. The import-linter contracts forbid mapi_jax, jax, flax and optax in the control plane and in the supervisor.
  • Upgrade the CLI and mapi-client to v0.15 to upload collections and weights. Older clients ignore the new fields.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• Cloud Run GPU jobs and the base-dl CUDA image are not tested against GCP or on a GPU.
  • Deduplication is only against a base version of the same dataset.
  • The platform keeps packs until the tenant is deleted.
  • There are no thumbnails for each image beyond the gallery sample of the ingest.
  • Collections take no pipeline steps (with a model that trains on batches) and no time splits.
  • Workflows and side tables do not take collections.
  • dl.embed on a collection needs data.collection (a sample). Use dl.finetune_classifier with freeze: backbone for all images.
  • One GPU for each run. There is no training on more than one GPU or more than one machine.
  • Pretrained weights must use the mapi-jax ResNet layout. There is no conversion from PyTorch checkpoints.

docs.title: [0.14.0] — Run comparison, media and image data — 2026-10-20
Run comparison, media, image data and classification
docs.text: You can now compare runs and group them. The runs table shows metrics, params and tags as columns, and you can filter, sort and save the search as a view. The compare page shows 2 to 10 runs side by side. An experiment is a named group of runs. A run can also log images, figures and small tables. You can upload a zip of small images as a dataset, look at the images in a gallery, and classify them. The classification pack adds a multiclass classifier, LightGBM and CatBoost, new GLM families and multiclass plots.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Experiments: a named group of runs in a project (GET/POST /v1/experiments, GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}, POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/runs). A run is in a maximum of one experiment (RunCreate.experiment_id, Run.experiment_id, RunPatch.experiment_id, WorkflowRunCreate.experiment_id). A workflow node run gets the experiment of its workflow run. A retry gets the experiment of the run that it retries. An archived experiment accepts no new runs and no retries. list_runs has the filter experiment_id.
  • Saved views of the runs table (/v1/run-views): a name and a RunViewQuery (the filters, the sort order, the columns, the tags and the other filters of list_runs), shared in the project. A maximum of 200 views in a project.
  • GET /v1/run-compare: the summaries, the metric histories, the params (with differs) and the media of 2 to 10 runs. GET /v1/run-keys: the metric series, param keys and tag keys of the runs of a project or an experiment, with the number of runs that have each.
  • Run media: ctx.log_image, ctx.log_figure and ctx.log_table on the fit, score and node contexts. The supervisor uploads the files through a create-only POST policy on the media/ prefix of the run (RunSpec.media_prefix, output media) and sends a media event. The server downloads each file, does a check of its SHA-256, size and format, and keeps a copy in the bundles bucket. A run can log 1000 items and 256 MiB. GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/media, /media/{media_id}, /media-keys, and POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/media (from a notebook, a maximum of 4 MiB). The tracking frame has the field media.
  • mapi_spec.media: the media kinds and content types, sniff_image (PNG and JPEG headers, no image library), MediaTable, media_name, check_media and the limits. mapi_sdk.media: MediaItem, encode_png (numpy and zlib only) and the optional MediaTracker protocol.
  • Web app: the runs table has a filter bar, a column picker for tracked columns, sort by a column, saved views, and check boxes to compare runs or to add them to an experiment. New pages: Experiments, the page of an experiment, and the compare page (curves, metric bars, param differences, plots side by side, and images with a step slider). The run page has a Media tab. The Notes tab moves the run to an experiment.
  • Client and CLI: runs.media, runs.media_keys, runs.get_media, runs.download_media, runs.log_image, runs.log_table, runs.keys, runs.compare, client.experiments and client.run_views. mapi experiments ..., mapi runs media, mapi runs log-image, mapi runs compare, mapi runs views ..., mapi runs ls --experiment/--view, mapi fit --experiment and mapi workflows run --experiment.
  • Image data, stage 1: the upload format image_folder (a zip of PNG, JPEG or TIFF images and a manifest table, ImageFolderOptions). The ingest writes pixels(image, y, x, channel) with the new dtype uint8, the target label(image) and the manifest columns as coordinates. It can resize the images (stretch, crop or pad). The ingest refuses unsafe paths, images of more than 4096 × 4096 pixels, images with more than 8 bits, and datasets that are too large, with a message that gives the number of images that fit.
  • Data Explorer: the Gallery section (thumbnails of the images, an even sample for each label and split, and the counts of each facet), and colour (RGB) images in Images and fields. A label variable on the frames gives the classes of the mean images.
  • The split kinds column (hold out the rows with a value of a column, for example split = test) and stratified (hold out the same share of each class, at random), with About cards.
  • Classification: sklearn.multiclass_classifier (the probability of each class in y_hat(..., class)), the estimators sklearn.HistGradientBoostingClassifier, lightgbm.LGBMClassifier and catboost.CatBoostClassifier (the extra mapi-sklearn[gbm]), and the metric auc for multiclass predictions (the mean one-vs-rest AUC).
  • tabular.hierarchical_glm (model version 1.1.0) has the families negative_binomial, zero_inflated_poisson, zero_inflated_negative_binomial, beta, gamma and ordinal.
  • tabular.image_logistic: a Bayesian multinomial logistic regression on the main patterns (PCA) of small images. The fit logs the patterns and the class means as images.
  • Help me choose has the goal "Put items or images into classes" (classify) and the data shape "Images (pictures of the same size)" (images).
  • Documentation: the guides Compare runs and use experiments and Image data.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• core.roc_pr and core.confusion accept a binary or a multiclass target. With a class dim on the prediction, or more than two observed classes, core.roc_pr draws one-vs-rest curves for each class with the macro AUC (classes selects the classes), and core.confusion shows a K × K matrix with the accuracy and the macro F1. The binary behaviour does not change.
  • sklearn.tabular_classifier accepts the new classifier estimators.
  • verify_output_objects accepts objects below media/ of the run prefix by default.
  • mapi-runner depends on Pillow. The runner image mapi/base-ml has LightGBM, CatBoost and libgomp1. The other runner images have Pillow, and do not have LightGBM or CatBoost. The mapi/server image has none of them.
  • New audit actions: experiment.create, experiment.update, experiment.delete, run_view.save and run_view.delete. A media write through the API is a run.log event.
  • Upgrade the CLI and mapi-client to v0.14 to use experiments, saved views, comparison and media. Older clients ignore the new fields.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• mapi_spec.expand_sweep and the module mapi_spec.sweep. Nothing called them.
  • New Sweep documents: the server refuses them (422 SCHEMA_INVALID at /kind). Stored Sweep documents still load. Use a workflow with a search.grid node.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• A fit without a run (for example fit_spec in a notebook) keeps no logged media. tracking_media is False, and log_image, log_figure and log_table only check their arguments. To keep the items in memory, give the fit a recorder: FitHooks(tracker=MetricRecorder()). The items are then in MetricRecorder.media.
  • Workflow schedules and triggers start their runs in no experiment. To group such a run, move it with PATCH /v1/runs/{run_id} before it starts its nodes. Node runs that started before the move stay where they are.
  • The platform keeps media until you delete the tenant. There is no retention setting for media.
  • image_folder has no inspect step. Errors about the columns of the manifest come from the ingest run.
  • Images must have 8 bits for each channel and one size for each dataset. A dataset has a maximum of 268 435 456 pixel values. The collection layout of v0.15 removes these limits.
  • Workflow backtests do not make stratified split plans.
  • There is no calibration plot for multiclass predictions.
  • LightGBM and CatBoost are only in the mapi/base-ml runner image.
  • Validation refuses log_score for sklearn.multiclass_classifier, as for the binary classifier, because the plugin gives point predictions. Use brier.

docs.title: [0.13.0] — Causal models and Bayesian state space — 2026-10-20
Causal inference and Bayesian state space
docs.text: The platform can now measure the effect of a campaign, a launch or a test. Three new causal models compare the actual values with a prediction of the values without the change: on one series (causal.impact), in test markets against a mix of the other markets (causal.synthetic_control) and in units with and without a change (causal.did). The result of a geo-lift test becomes a lift test for mmm.bayesian. A new Bayesian structural time series (ts.bsts) forecasts one series from its level, trend, seasonal patterns and drivers. Each fit logs its results with the v0.11 tracking API.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• ts.bsts (mapi-plugin-ts): a Bayesian structural time series on the state-space models of pymc-extras. It has a level, a trend (level, local_linear or smooth), a maximum of three seasonal patterns (one effect for each season, or harmonics) and drivers with one effect for all periods. The fit uses the exact Kalman likelihood. Missing periods are permitted. The bundle keeps a terminal_state group. forecast starts from it, and the filter mode adds new periods without a new fit. The components group shows the level, the seasonal parts and the drivers with core.decomposition.
  • A new plugin package, mapi-plugin-causal (Apache-2.0), with three models. Each model writes the effect to the bundle group impact (actual values, values without the change, the effect in each period and the cumulative effect, in the units of the target):
    • causal.impact: CausalImpact (Brodersen et al. 2015) on the ts.bsts core. The model fits the periods before the change, with optional control series. Without control series, it is an interrupted time series.
    • causal.synthetic_control: a Bayesian synthetic control for geo-lift tests. The weights of the other markets are positive with a sum of 1 (simplex), or have a horseshoe prior. The bundle group donor_weights keeps the weights.
    • causal.did: difference-in-differences and event study (Bayesian two-way fixed effects). The bundle group event_study keeps one coefficient for each period before and after the change. The counterfactual mode sets the treatment to 0.
  • New plot recipes, each with an About card and example data: causal.impact (the actual values against the values without the change, the effect in each period and the cumulative effect), causal.pre_fit (the fit before the change), causal.donor_weights and causal.event_study.
  • The workflow node model.lift_test makes a lift test for mmm.bayesian from the impact group of a causal model version. model.fit has a new parameter calibration.
  • The workflow template geo_lift_mmm: a geo-lift test, its lift test, mmm.bayesian calibrated with the lift test, the plots and a report.
  • Guided templates campaign_impact (Effect of a campaign, causal.impact) and geo_lift (Geo-lift test, causal.synthetic_control), with About cards. The report of geo_lift has a card that makes the lift-test entry for your marketing mix.
  • Help me choose has a new goal: "Measure the effect of a campaign, a launch or a test" (measure_impact). The four new models have About cards.
  • Run tracking: ts.bsts logs its structure (bsts.* params), the noise and the error of the one-step-ahead predictions. The causal models log the total effect with its interval, the relative effect, the probability that the effect is more than zero and the error before the change. Synthetic control also logs the donor weights. DiD also logs the average effect and the event-study coefficients.
  • Conformance fixtures e13_bsts (the plan fixture E13 is no longer deferred), causal_impact, geo_lift and did_event_study.
  • Documentation: the pages Causal models and Bayesian structural time series and Measure the effect of a change.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• pymc-extras is now a declared dependency: of mapi-plugin-ts, and of the new extra mapi-pymc[pathfinder] for the pathfinder engine. The error message for a missing engine names the extra. Pathfinder does not write a progress table to the output.
  • The runner image mapi/base-forecast has pymc-extras and mapi-plugin-causal. The causal.* models run in it. mapi/base-bayes has pymc-extras for Pathfinder.
  • GuidedTemplate.family has the new value causal. Upgrade the CLI and mapi-client to v0.13. A v0.12 client cannot read the list of Guided templates from a v0.13 server (mapi guided templates fails for all templates). From v0.13, a client keeps a family that it does not know as text.
  • The causal.* plot recipes are platform recipes: you can embed them, and the Guided share step offers them. Only the platform distributions can register ids in the causal and choice namespaces.
  • A score output can be a difference (the scored array attr difference_of names the reference output). With output.units: original, the harness changes the level and the reference to the output units, then subtracts them. The effect of causal.impact uses this, thus it is y - y_hat in the units of the data also when the pipeline transforms the target.
  • The Guided steps of campaign_impact and geo_lift do not include the scenarios step (the templates have no tasks). The lift-test card of the geo_lift report uses the test markets of the revision that the last fit used.
  • causal.did scores a payload with only some periods: the periods that the payload does not have take the adoption of the fit. causal.impact refuses periods that are not evenly spaced (SCHEMA_INVALID), as ts.bsts does. An impossible date in intervention_start or intervention_end (for example 2024-02-30) is SETTINGS_INVALID. Two units or donors whose names give the same tracking label get different labels (_2, _3).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• ts.bsts takes one series. Each driver has one effect for all periods. A forecast does not use actual values that you know (use the filter mode). A seasonal pattern with one effect for each season has a maximum period of 24 (use harmonics for longer periods).
  • causal.impact fits the periods before the change only.
  • causal.synthetic_control has no placebo tests and does not design a test (the choice of the markets, the power).
  • A lift test from two or more test markets is national.
  • The time effects of causal.did are fixed, thus the model does not forecast. When the units got the change at different times, the estimates can be wrong.
  • The lift-test card of the Guided report does not write into the MMM spec. Copy the entry.

docs.title: MMM pack
docs.text: The marketing-mix models get two new models, two new kinds of data and the charts that a marketing team asks for. mmm.nested measures effects that go through an intermediate measure, for example visits or awareness. mmm.multivariate measures effects on two or more results at the same time. mmm.bayesian can now have channel effects that change over time, and counts or shares as the result. Each MMM fit logs its return on spend and other summaries with the v0.11 tracking API.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mmm.nested (mmm-framework NestedMMM): a national marketing mix with one or more intermediate measures (mediator dim). Each measure can be measured in some periods only, or not at all (latent: true). Each channel has a direct effect and an indirect effect through each measure. The new derived quantity mediation gives the direct, indirect and total effect of each channel and the part that goes through the measures. Lift tests calibrate the total effect of a channel. The output mediator_hat gives the fitted measures.
  • mmm.multivariate (mmm-framework MultivariateMMM): a national marketing mix of two or more results (outcome dim) with correlated noise. Cross-effects between the results can be halo, cannibalization or unconstrained. Scores, response curves and budget plans use the reduced form, thus a channel that moves one result also moves the results that it acts on. The new derived quantity cross_effects gives each cross-effect. outcomes[].weight gives the value of one unit of each result in the budget plan. The KPI of the plan is then "weighted total of the outcomes", and a note of the plan gives the weights.
  • mmm.bayesian 1.1.0: time-varying channel effects. Put the channels in time_varying.channels. Their effect is a random walk over the fit window. time_varying.forecast sets the effect after the fit window: random_walk (default, the range becomes wider with the horizon), hold_last or mean. A forecast tells you which policy it used.
  • mmm.bayesian 1.1.0: the likelihoods poisson and negative_binomial (counts, log link) and beta (shares between 0 and 1, logit link). media_effect_sigma sets the prior of the channel effects of these likelihoods. The contributions of the channels still add up to y_hat. The trend, the seasonality and the controls are then part of the baseline.
  • New derived quantities for every MMM: adstock (the part of the effect of a unit of spend that comes in each later period, and the mean lag). mmm.bayesian and mmm.frequentist also have effectiveness (the effect for each unit of spend in each period).
  • New plot recipes, each with an About card and example data:
    • mmm.roi: the return on spend of each channel with a range, and the marginal return (mROAS), against a break-even line.
    • mmm.adstock: how the effect of spend decays over the next periods, with a range.
    • mmm.waterfall: the contribution of each component to the total result.
    • mmm.spend_effect: the share of spend against the share of the effect of each channel.
    • mmm.lift_tests: the result of each lift test, with its error bar, next to the estimate of the model.
    • mmm.effectiveness: the effect of a unit of spend over time, for time-varying channels.
    • mmm.mediation: the direct and indirect effect of each channel (mmm.nested).
    • mmm.cross_effects: the effects between the results (mmm.multivariate).
    • core.energy: the energy plot of the sampler and the BFMI of each chain.
    • core.prior_posterior: the prior and the posterior of each parameter, with their overlap.
  • A fit with lift tests keeps the bundle group lift_tests (each test and the estimate of the model for each draw).
  • Run tracking for every MMM: each fit logs the params mmm.framework_version, mmm.n_channels, mmm.n_periods, mmm.n_cells and mmm.link, and the metrics roi, roi_p05, roi_p95, mroi and contribution_share for each channel (label channel) and baseline_share. mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate also send the progress of each chain and the step metrics, as mmm.bayesian does.
  • Guided templates mediated_mmm (Marketing mix with an intermediate measure, mmm.nested) and multi_kpi_mmm (Marketing mix for related products, mmm.multivariate), with About cards. Help me choose recommends the two models and templates for "a few related numbers over time".

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• geo_mmm 2.1.0: the template also keeps adstock and draws mmm.roi.
  • The About cards of mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate now tell what the models can do: national data, no control variables, and cross-effects that are associations. The card of mmm.bayesian tells about time-varying effects, counts and shares.
  • Guided drafts: a question that allows missing values also suggests columns that are mostly empty (for example a monthly survey). The labels of a wide covariate that has its own dim keep their words (site_visits, not site).
  • The Guided report and the shared report show mmm.roi first when the spec draws it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Score plots of mmm.decomposition and mmm.waterfall show one outcome when a score renames the outcome dim to its dataset name. Before, they added all outcomes together.
  • The Guided what-if and the scenario presets of the several-results template use the spend question, not the results question.
  • The mediated template does not ask for channel beliefs, because mmm.nested takes lift tests only.
  • The data-shape hint of the national templates names the mediator or result columns.
  • The mmm.multivariate starter spec does not ask for the cross-effects plot when it sets no cross-effects.
  • A budget plan for one weighted outcome names that outcome and its weight.
  • A very long mmm.* parameter value is cut to 6000 characters, not refused after sampling.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate use national data only and take no control variables.
  • mmm.multivariate has no lift-test calibration and no promotion modulation.
  • The Guided template multi_kpi_mmm sets no weights and no cross-effects. Add them in the spec editor.
  • The likelihoods binomial, beta-binomial and lognormal are not available.
  • A budget plan of a count model (log link) adds the increments of the channels. The removal-based response curves are the correct view of each channel.
  • The approximate fits of mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate do not send their loss while they fit.

docs.title: Run tracking: metrics, parameters, tags and notes
docs.text: Each run now keeps a log of what happened in it: metrics (curves and single values), params, tags, a name, a note and structured log lines. Model code, workflow nodes and you (from a notebook, a script or the command line) can add to this log. You can search runs by their metrics, params and tags. The data that a run comparison needs is stored. The compare page comes in a later release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• A logging API for model code. FitContext, ScoreContext and the workflow NodeContext have log_metric, log_metrics, log_param, log_params, set_tag, set_tags, log_line and chains. The methods do a check of each key and label when you call them, also without a run. They are thread-safe. The new guide Track metrics, params and tags tells how to use them.
  • Metric keys keep the pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$. Labels (a maximum of 8) give the qualifiers, for example loss with {"split": "val"} or step_size with {"chain": "0"}.
  • mapi_spec.tracking: the key and label rules, TrackingLimits, labels_key, param_text and the run search grammar (parse_run_filter, parse_run_order, parse_run_ref).
  • mapi_sdk.tracking: the Tracker protocol, MetricRecorder, TeeTracker, with_labels and spec_params. A fit writes the logged values into the new bundle group /model/metrics_history, and core.loss_curve draws them.
  • Each fit logs the params of its spec: model, fit.*, data.split and settings.*. scikit-learn fits also log the hyperparameters of the estimator as estimator.*.
  • Live chains: PyMC fits (nutpie and the PyMC NUTS sampler) and mmm.bayesian send the progress of each chain. The run page shows one lane for each chain, with its draws, divergences and step size.
  • Step metrics: nutpie logs step_size, num_steps and divergences. The PyMC NUTS sampler (also in mmm.bayesian with nuts_sampler: pymc) also logs tree_depth. For a chain of more than 5000 draws, it logs each k-th draw. These metrics have the label chain. ADVI sends its loss while it optimises. The evaluation fit of evaluate_then_refit adds the label fit=evaluation and the prefix evaluation. to the keys of its params.
  • search.grid logs each grid point in its search run (the first of the child runs of the node): the params trial.<i>.<pointer> and grid.*, the scores with the point number as the step, best_<metric> and the tag grid.best_point. model.backtest logs the metrics of each fold with the label fold.
  • New endpoints: PATCH /v1/runs/{run_id} (name, note and tags), GET and POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/metrics, GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/metrics/{key} (downsampled with LTTB), GET and POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/params. You can log metrics and params to a run after it finished, for example a business KPI after a deployment.
  • GET /v1/runs search: parent_run_id, name, tag, filter (for example metric.rmse < 0.5 or param.fit.engine = nutpie), order_by and column (Run.columns).
  • The SSE stream of a run sends tracking frames when the metrics, the params or the tags change, and a snapshot frame when the name or the note changes.
  • GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs sends the structured user lines only with stream=user or include_user=true, thus older clients continue to read the logs. The v0.11 client, the CLI and the web app send include_user=true.
  • The token scope runs:write and the permission update on run (runner role). The audit actions run.update and run.log.
  • Python client: runs.update, runs.log_metric, runs.log_metrics, runs.log_params, runs.set_tags, runs.track (a context manager that sends points in batches), runs.metrics, runs.metric_history, runs.params, and the search arguments of runs.list.
  • CLI: mapi runs metrics, params, log-metric, log-param, tag, rename and note. mapi runs ls has --filter, --order-by, --column, --tag, --name and --parent. mapi runs watch shows metrics, params, tags and structured log lines.
  • Web app, run page: the tabs Overview, Metrics (a chart for each key, colour by a label, label filters, log scale, live updates), Params, Logs (level filter) and Notes (name, tags and note). The runs list shows the name and the tags of each run.
  • Budgets for each run (RunLimits.tracking): 10 000 points for each series, 500 000 points, 1000 series, 5000 params, 100 tags and 10 000 structured log lines. A run that logs more gets one TRACKING_BUDGET warning. More than 64 MiB of tracking data is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION.
  • The setting MAPI_TRACKING_RETENTION_DAYS. The server deletes the metric points and the structured log lines of old runs. It keeps the summaries, the value of each metric without a step, the params, the tags and the notes. Points that you log later add to the kept summary.
  • Model Explorer: the backtest has the error for each horizon, pooled over the folds (BacktestView.by_horizon), and the chart "Backtest error by horizon". A plan without horizons uses the horizons 1 to the length of the first test window (a maximum of 32).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Run events: the new types metrics, params and tags. The platform writes them to the tracking tables, not to the event list. The log event has the new stream user, with level and fields. ChainProgress has step_size and num_steps.
  • The legacy metric event (for example the holdout rmse at the end of a fit) also becomes a scalar metric series.
  • GET /v1/runs returns 422 SCHEMA_INVALID for a filter, order_by or column that is not correct. GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs has the filter level. Run has name, note and tags. LogLine has level and fields.
  • mmm.bayesian reports the progress of the sampler from 10% to 90%, and you can cancel it while it samples. A cancelled fit makes no model version.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The page that compares runs comes in v0.14. v0.11 stores the data and gives the summaries and the search filters in the API.
  • Runs cannot log images or other media.
  • numpyro and blackjax samplers do not send the progress of each chain.
  • The approximate methods of mmm-framework (ADVI, Pathfinder) do not send their loss while they fit.

docs.title: [0.10.0] — Chart wiring and score plots by output shape — 2026-10-20
Chart wiring and metric correctness
docs.text: More models now get the plots that apply to them, and the metrics that a spec requests are calculated. A classifier gets classifier plots and metrics. A state model gets a state plot. An ADVI fit shows its loss. The run page shows the plots of a run.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• New plot recipes in the core pack, each with an About card and example data:
    • core.roc_pr: the ROC curve and the precision-recall curve of a 0/1 target, with the AUC and the average precision.
    • core.confusion: the 2 × 2 table of actual and predicted classes at a threshold (0.5, or auto), with accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and F1.
    • core.loss_curve: the loss of each step of a fit, raw and smoothed, with a note when the loss still goes down at the end.
    • core.loo_pit: the LOO-PIT check of calibration and the PSIS Pareto k of each observation. It is not a default plot. Add it in the plot builder.
  • Metrics: auc (the Mann-Whitney AUC) and binary brier, log_score and accuracy for a target with two values. mase for a fit with a time holdout: the holdout mae divided by the in-sample error of a seasonal naive forecast.
  • metrics.json keeps the PSIS Pareto k of each observation of elpd_loo (ElpdDetail.pareto_k).
  • An ADVI fit keeps the loss of each step in the bundle group fit_history (loss(step), at most 5,000 steps). The fit run adds core.loss_curve to its plots.
  • Standard plots for more models. The model declares them, and the Insert panel of the spec editor shows them first. A fit draws only the plots in outputs.plots:
    • sklearn regressors (and the quantile, bootstrap and conformal plugins): core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time, ml.feature_importance.
    • sklearn.tabular_classifier: core.calibration, core.roc_pr, core.confusion, ml.feature_importance.
    • ts.gaussian_hmm and the statsmodels Markov switching model: core.state_sequence.
    • The unobserved components model, ETS and ts.hsgp_trend: core.decomposition. ETS and ts.hsgp_trend keep a new components group for it.
  • Default score plots: an areal output gets sci.area_map, an output of probabilities over a state or regime dim gets core.state_sequence, and an evaluate run with a 0/1 target gets core.calibration, core.roc_pr and core.confusion.
  • ScoreSummaryTable.plots: the ids of the rendered plots that draw the output.
  • Score, Results by output: a map of areas and a classification view, made from the plots of the run.
  • Run detail: a Plots card with the plots of a finished run.
  • Compare in the Model Explorer: the card Which version predicts new data best? with the core.model_comparison plot, when two or more versions have elpd_loo (or elpd_waic).
  • Score, quick chart: a Cell picker for a table with more dims than the axis and the colour, for example a grid. The chart shows one cell at a time.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• core.calibration accepts one predicted probability for each row (no draws) for a 0/1 target. Validation now accepts it for a model with point predictions.
  • core.state_sequence reads the hidden_states group (HMM), the regimes group (Markov switching) and a score summary. It finds the state dim (state or regime) itself. When the data has more than one series, it shows the first one and names it in the caption.
  • core.decomposition reads the components group. It does not stack a variable with the attr decomposition: exclude (the trend slope of the UC and ETS models).
  • GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots returns the plots of the newest attempt that has them. Thus partial runs, and failed or cancelled runs with an earlier partial attempt, also show plots.
  • One implementation of the MASE scale (mapi_sdk.metrics.mase_scale) for the SDK, the workflows, the explorer and governance.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The fit calculated no metric for a classifier: metrics.json was empty. The harness did not pair a probability output with its target, because the output declares units. It now pairs an output with meaning: probability with the target.
  • An evaluate run from the Score page did not draw its plots: the runner skipped core.fit_vs_actual because the result had no observed values. The runner now gives the plots the full predictions and the observed values.
  • auc and mase passed validation but the fit did not calculate them.
  • Compare in the Model Explorer showed no holdout metrics of the versions (only the number of parameters). The explore run did not get the metrics.json of each version. The server now gives it to the run with each bundle.
  • Score: the quick chart of a large grid table (for example 864 rows of the LGCP summary) looked blank. The chart drew one line through all the rows, so all the cells of a period were at the same x position: each period was a vertical stroke and the band had no width. Empty cells (outside the study area) also broke the line between the periods. The chart now draws one cell of the grid at a time.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• Validation refuses log_score in evaluate.metrics for a model with point predictions, so a point classifier cannot request it. Use brier.
  • mase is calculated only in the evaluation of a fit. An evaluate run from the Score page skips it, because it does not have the training data.
  • A regression target that has only the values 0 and 1 gets the classifier plots on evaluate.
  • The sci.* models that run the PyMC engine themselves do not keep the ADVI loss history. PyMCModel plugins and ts.gaussian_hmm keep it.
  • sci.area_map on the Score page draws an output with only an area dim. An areal output with more dims is skipped with a warning.

docs.title: Score results by output shape
docs.text: The plots of a score run now follow the shape of each output. A gridded output, for example the intensity of the earthquake model sci.lgcp_grid, shows as a map with a slider over the periods of the forecast, not as a forecast fan of the sum over the grid.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The runner picks the default score plots from the shape of the outputs (predict, forecast and evaluate). A grid output gets sci.field_map, or sci.vector_field when it has a component of size 2, with the frame dim (quarter) as the slider. A time series output that is not a grid (total[period]) gets core.ppc_fan. A model with grid outputs and no such time series gets no fan. A model with no grid outputs keeps the plots of before, and job.plots still replaces the defaults.
  • A predict, forecast or evaluate run of a model with grid outputs writes ui/fields.json (FieldsView, mapi_spec.views.SCORE_FIELDS_VIEW): the same field view as the Model Explorer, made from the predictions.
  • The output variables of a grid in score.zarr.zip carry the attr grid (the GridDecl as JSON, with the dataset names of the dims). Thus a download can be plotted as a map.
  • ScoreSummaryTable has two optional fields: dims (the coordinate columns) and time_dim (the dim that is time). A server that predates them leaves both out.
  • Score in the web app shows a view for each output by its shape: a map with a frame slider for a grid, a line with a band for a time series, intervals for a categorical output and tiles for a scalar. When ui/fields.json is there, the map replaces the sci.field_map and sci.vector_field plots in the plot list.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The KPI of a guided forecast (ui/guided/forecast.json) is an output that is not a grid when there is one, for example total and not the sum of rate over the grid.
  • The summary tables are in the order of their size, so a truncated summary drops a large grid table and keeps total.
  • A model's field map (Score page and Model Explorer) colours the 1% to 99% range of the posterior means when the quantiles and draws reach much wider, so a log-scale intensity does not look flat; the mean, quantiles and draws still share the scale, and "Colours for the full range" shows all of it.

docs.title: Data Explorer for scientific data
docs.text: The Data Explorer now shows graphs of scientific data, not only time series. It finds the structure of the data (images, profiles, maps, networks, trees, directions and points) and shows the sections that apply first.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The explorer finds the shapes of each dataset, and of each node of a tree dataset, from the dims, the coords, the roles and the units. The new section Structure shows the shapes, the role of each dim and how the explorer uses each variable.
  • Seven picture sections in the new group Pictures of the data:
    • Images and fields: the field viewer of the Model Explorer, with the statistics of each frame.
    • Profiles and spectra.
    • Map: areas in colour, neighbours and Moran's I.
    • Network: matrix, node-link graph, degree and homophily.
    • Tree: the tree with the traits and the phylogenetic signal.
    • Directions and times of day: roses and the Rayleigh test.
    • Points: lattice, CIE Lab colours and agreement.
  • The ingest writes structure and each picture section that applies. The explorer index gives the new fields reason, shapes and order. A request takes the new field hints to correct the structure.
  • In Expert mode, All series also shows the Plotly plots sci.area_map, net.graph and sci.rose.
  • Mock datasets for eleven pymc-challenges cases and the E80 lens tree, and screenshots of the new sections. make docs-screenshots-explorers records the profiles, the points and the section list from mock mode. make docs-screenshots-science records the images (E58), the map (E18), the network (E21), the tree (E23) and the roses (E81b) from the real exports.
  • Images and fields: when a few cells are much brighter than the others (E58 camera frames), the colours cover 98% of the values. Colours for the full range shows all the values. The axis of a histogram with a log count has ticks at the powers of ten.
  • Tree: a trait with positive values that go across two orders of magnitude or more (E23 body mass) has a logarithmic axis.
  • Each pymc-challenges tutorial has a step "Explore the data". The guide Explore a dataset (docs/guides/data-explorer.md) has a new part "Scientific data".

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The list of sections shows only the sections that apply to the data, in the sequence that agrees with the structure. The other sections go in the closed list Not for this data. A link to one of these sections continues to open it. Versions from earlier releases keep the thirteen sections.
  • A dim with policy: extend is time only when its coords are numbers that increase and it is not a list of ids. A week, month, quarter, year, day, date, period or time dim with numbers stays time (an MMM panel on the weeks 1 to 104). A list of ids is a sequence when its name tells a step in time (step, t) or media or spend change along it. If your data uses another list of ids as time, give time_dim in the request.
  • Over time adds or averages the cells of an image to make one series. It does not make a series for each cell. The time patterns need a real time dim and 16 periods or more.
  • Group comparison compares only real groups. Correlations, Distributions and Unusual values do not use geometry (borders, neighbours, tree variables, positions). Data quality gives SHORT_HISTORY only for data with a time dim, and has the new warnings GEOMETRY_INVALID, TREE_INVALID, NETWORK_ASYMMETRIC, ANGLE_RANGE and IMAGE_SATURATED.
  • A request can have all 21 sections (before: 13).
  • Map starts with the ratio of the target and the exposure (E18 cases / expected), when the data has this ratio.
  • Unusual values and the OUTLIERS check do not use an indicator (the values 0 and 1, or two values that each occur in 5 % of the rows or more), or a profile or a spectrum (E79 reference_dl). One spike in a constant series continues to be an unusual value.
  • Distributions says "has only the values 0 and 1" for a variable with only 0 and 1. Correlations names the largest pair when no pair has a correlation of 0.7 or more.
  • The tables of the picture sections show counts with all their digits (10,292, not 10,290).
  • The dataset About counts a pair of dims (district, district_) once, and does not add an "s" to a dim name that ends in "s" ("186 species", not "186 speciess"). A name that ends in "ss", "us", "x", "ch" or "sh" gets "es" ("3 classes", "3 statuses").

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The upload page puts the bytes of a file once. Before, Upload and ingest while Preview structure still sent the file failed with "upload failed with HTTP 412".
  • Time-series and tabular data keep the classic sections:
    • A target named y, or a pair of columns such as sales_x and sales_y, is data, not the positions of points. Points need names of positions and, for x and y, integers, units of length or a dim of points (site).
    • An MMM panel with integer geo or channel codes is not an image. Over time gives one series for each geo and channel.
    • hours_open, months_active, a temperature in degrees, and a latitude or a longitude are not directions.
  • Images and fields reads a few frames at a time. A movie of 1,000 frames of 256 × 256 cells needs about 250 MB more memory, not 1.8 GB. The ingest leaves out the images of more than 50,000,000 cells: Run the deeper checks calculates them.
  • IMAGE_SATURATED looks only for a pile-up at the limit of a detector. A heater setting (E51 heater_w) and a noise map (E79 noise_sd) do not get it.
  • Moran's I of a map variable with frames uses the mean over the frames, not the first frame.
  • The server does not reuse an explore run from before this release: the cache key of a request includes the version of the explorer.
  • Group comparison does not compare the layers of a network (E21 covariate).
  • The roses show the bin in the units of the data when the pointer is on a bar ("13–14 h", not "203°"). The plain summary of the roses does not count the rose of all the records as a group.
  • The export plots of a section have different ids (three roses in E81).
  • "has only the values 0 and 1" shows only for a variable with the values 0 and 1, not for any two values between 0 and 1.
  • The counts of frames, ties and dim sizes show all their digits. For a version from an earlier release, the header names the views for scientific data apart from the list.
  • In Network, the Colour by picker stays when a network has no matrix.

docs.title: [0.9.1] — Science gallery docs — 2026-10-19
docs.text: This release updates the documentation for v0.9.0. It has no code changes.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• New page "What's new in 0.9", linked from the home page and the nav.
  • The README, home page, why, use cases and getting started pages describe the science models, the new plots, the new workflow nodes and recipes, and the pymc-challenges tutorials. The counts of models, plots, recipes and nodes agree with the code.
  • The roadmap covers v0.5.1 to v0.9. Plugin upload and the MCP server are "planned"; they are no longer said to come in v0.6. Old M4 to M6 labels for planned work are removed.
  • Concepts, guides and reference pages describe circular and grid outputs, custom samplers, start values, export cases, the new SDK and spec fields, the Score page options, the scorecard missing-values rule and the recovery.simulated check.
  • The conformance guide lists all 26 fixtures. Each science model section in the model reference links to its tutorial.
  • Operations pages list the new environment variables and make docs-screenshots-science. The package READMEs describe the new recipes, nodes and fields.

docs.title: [0.9.0] — Science gallery — 2026-10-19
docs.text: This release adds eleven science models from the pymc-challenges case studies, for images, fields, maps and graphs (15 sci.* models in all), and 14 plot recipes for them: maps, networks, trees, polar charts, image checks, colour swatches and posterior views. New workflow nodes give posterior summaries, posterior predictive checks, stacking weights, score modes and plots inside a workflow. Six workflow recipes use them for model ladders, a convergence-gated Bayesian audit and calibrate-then-design. Each ported case has a tutorial that does the notebook analysis in the web app, and python -m mapi_plugin_science.export turns the pymc-challenges data into datasets to upload.

docs.title: M5 phase 3 — Workflow recipes and tutorials for science models
Added
docs.text:
• sci_spatial_ladder in the workflow gallery. It fits sci.areal_bym2 with iid, ICAR and BYM2 area effects and compares them by elpd_loo and stacking weights. It keeps the best model and gives the range of the covariate effect. When the chains of the best model agree and the effect is clear, it fits the best model again with wider and narrower priors. It draws a risk map and writes a report.
  • sci_network_ladder in the workflow gallery. It fits sci.network_latent_space with covariates, sociality and a latent space and compares them by elpd_loo and stacking weights. It gives the pair effects of the best model, a network plot, simulated networks with their statistics and a report.
  • Two sections in the workflow cookbook, with the documents in docs/snippets/cookbook_sci_{spatial,network}_ladder.yaml. A test makes sure that each document is the same as its gallery template, and slow tests run the two documents.
  • Recipe sci_phylo_signal in the workflow gallery. It fits sci.phylo_regression with four residual kinds (no tree, Brownian motion, Pagel's lambda, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck), ranks them by elpd_loo, gives the stacking weights and selects the best. Then it tests if the range of one slope of the winner excludes zero. A clear effect also gets a predictive check. The report has the three tables and the sci.phylogeny plot. On the 186 primates of the primates301 dataset (E23), lambda wins with an elpd_loo of 129.9 (the notebook gives 130).
  • Recipe sci_calibrate_then_design in the workflow gallery. It fits sci.heat_plate with one calibration run held out, then fits all the runs again. It predicts the field of a new heater layout (model.score, sci.field_map) only if the error on the run held out and R-hat are in their limits. The report has the parameters, the holdout metrics and the sci.image_residuals and sci.field_map plots.
  • Both recipes have a section in the workflow cookbook with the CLI and the Python client. Their cookbook documents are tested against the gallery templates and run with the local runner on the simulated data of the models.
  • model.summary has a new parameter focus and a result field focus. A condition cannot build an entry name from a parameter, so focus names one value (beta[north], or only north). The result gives its mean, sd, HDI bounds, p_positive and excludes_zero.
  • Two gallery templates with About cards, cookbook sections (docs/snippets/cookbook_<id>.yaml) and run tests with the local runner:
  • bayes_workflow_audit: the checks of a careful Bayesian workflow for each model that gives draws (the model parameter). The fit keeps prior draws for the prior plot. A gate on R-hat and the effective sample size controls the posterior predictive check, the prior sensitivity check and the recovery check. The report has the prior, pair, predictive and estimate plots.
  • sci_image_model_check: residual maps and a grid of predicted images next to the observed image for an image model (for example sci.strong_lens or sci.cmb_field), with the posterior predictive check and a report.
  • Tutorials for the pymc-challenges case studies in docs/tutorials/pymc-challenges/: an index and one page for each of the 15 ported cases (E07, E18, E19, E21, E23, E31, E50, E51, E58, E60, E61, E77, E79, E80, E81). Each page exports the data, uploads it, builds and fits the spec in the web app, reads the Model Explorer, scores the model and runs the matching recipe, with the CLI and the Python client as tabs. The numbers come from fits of the real data. E51 and E61 use the data that their notebooks simulate. docs/tutorials/complex-workflows.md shows the patterns of the recipes in the workflow editor: model ladders, gates, predictive checks, governance checks, calibrate-then-design, plots in reports, tree datasets and sub-workflows. The pages are in the navigation and have cards in the tutorials index.
  • The web mocks (workflows.gen.json, explorer.gen.json) have the ten gallery templates.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• evaluate.ppc failed for a model whose output has the name of its canonical target when the dataset binds the target to a different name (for example sci.phylo_regression, with trait bound to brain). The score names outputs in the names of the dataset, and the node now looks for that name.
  • sci.area_map of a fitted sci.areal_bym2 showed no Observed panel: the plot looked for rr in the observed data, and the model keeps the raw SMR as smr. A spec cannot give settings to a plot, so the fit now names the observed counterpart of rr in the attribute mapi_observed, and the plot reads it.
  • The table of a score result on the Score page lost the cells of a grid when a dim had numeric labels (for example y_cm and x_cm of sci.heat_plate, or the lawyer numbers of sci.network_latent_space). The page took the numeric dims for variables and kept one row for each run. The Arrow views now name their dims in the schema metadata mapi.dims, and the page keeps these columns as keys.
  • The science tutorials: the build steps now paste the full spec over the starter template (it has a pipeline, a split and MMM plots), open the closed Datasets section of the Insert panel, click Create dataset before the upload, take the spec name from metadata.name, and point to the Events card (the Logs card stays empty). The E18, E21 and E51 tutorials and complex-workflows.md have eight screenshots from a live dev stack (make docs-screenshots-science).
  • sci_spatial_ladder ignored its own convergence check: the branch clear took the then arm when the chains of the best model did not agree. The branch now needs a convergence check that does not fail, and the report says so.
  • The scorecard check "Few missing values" (data.missing) counted each NaN of the raw dataset. Thus it always failed for E18 (the padding of the outlines ring_x and ring_y) and E51 (the cells without a thermocouple). The check now counts only the variables that contain observations. It does not count the roles constant, index and mask, or the variables that the model declares in the new class attribute CustomModel.structural_missing (sci.heat_plate declares temperature). The expert message names the variables that the check does not count. Gaps in a target, a spend or a covariate count as before, also with missing: allow.
  • The gate of sci_calibrate_then_design stopped the run with EXPRESSION_ERROR when R-hat was null (one chain). The condition now uses coalesce, and the recipe needs two or more chains.
  • The Score page offered No new data for Predict, Simulate and What if. The server refuses such a request when it has no forecast horizon and no scenario dataset ("the score request has no data"). The page now shows No new data only for Forecast, or when a scenario dataset gives the values. For the other modes, a note on the page tells why the option is not there. For a model that has no forecast mode, the note says that the model always needs values to score.
  • Some suggested specs of mapi_plugin_science.export needed changes by hand:
  • E50 lists elpd_loo, but the spec did not keep the log-likelihood, so the fit did not calculate elpd_loo. The spec now has fit.keep: {log_likelihood: true} and the sci.profile_bands plot.
  • E60 listed sci.field_map, which cannot draw the vector output traction. The spec now lists sci.vector_field. It also fits on all of the data (mode: train_only), with no metrics.
  • E80 listed sci.field_map, which draws the parameter e_light and not the image. The spec now lists sci.image_residuals and sci.ppc_image_grid, and fits on all of the pixels (mode: train_only).
  • With --synthetic, the E77 spec held out speakers that the simulated data does not have, and the E79 spec had a bandpower bin that the simulated patch is too small for. These specs now fit the simulated data.

New tests make sure that each suggested spec validates against the schema of its exported file. A slow test fits each spec on the simulated data with few draws and makes sure that each plot of the spec shows, that a map shows an output of the model, and that the fit calculates elpd_loo when the spec lists it. - The score summaries of a circular output (OutputDecl.circular) were calculated on a line, not on the circle. For draws on the two sides of north (350 and 10 degrees), the mean was near 180 degrees and hdi_90 covered almost the full circle. Now the summaries of draws use the circular mean, and each interval (hdi, eti) and quantile is centred on that mean. The values are in [0, period), so an interval with lower more than upper crosses the seam. sd is the circular standard deviation. The difference between a scenario and its baseline (delta/summary, delta/draws) is wrapped to [-period/2, period/2). This is the same rule as the evaluate metrics. A circular output that has no valid period attr, or that is aggregated over a dim, keeps the summary on a line, and the result has a warning. - ScoreSummaryTable (summary.json) has a new field period for a circular output, so that a reader knows that the statistics are on the circle. - sci.circular_regression also declares mean_direction circular, with a period attr. - governance.check with recovery.simulated gave error for sci.lgcp_grid and sci.areal_bym2, and skipped for sci.network_latent_space. The check added residuals to the fitted values, so the simulated counts were not whole numbers and the refits failed. Now a Bayesian model with predictive draws simulates each dataset from its posterior predictive (one posterior draw and the noise of the model). The known values are the values of that draw. A count target without predictive draws gives skipped with the reason. A simulated dataset that the model cannot fit is counted in the evidence (failed_simulations). - The governance checks found no predictions for a model whose output has the name of its canonical target when the dataset binds the target to a different name (tie bound to cowork in sci.network_latent_space). They now look for the dataset name too.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• governance.check with sensitivity.prior cannot find the prior widths of sci.areal_bym2 (intercept_sd, slope_sd, sigma_scale), so the check is skipped. The spatial ladder fits the model again with these widths in its place.
  • The graph check of the network ladder plots the statistics of the simulated networks only. The plot does not mark the statistics of the observed network.
  • core.prior_predictive cannot draw the prior draws of sci.heat_plate (the draws are on the sensor dim, the observed data is on the grid). Some science models (for example sci.cmb_field and sci.phylo_regression) keep no prior draws. The audit then shows a failed prior plot and continues.
  • Only sci_spatial_ladder has run end to end on a live dev stack and in a browser. The six M5 recipes run through the server orchestrator in a slow test (packages/server/tests/test_workflows_m5_templates.py), with small fits.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Eleven science models in mapi-plugin-science, ported from the pymc-challenges case studies. Each has an About card, a section in docs/reference/models.md, a conformance fixture, a data export case and tests against the real data of its notebook:
  • sci.heat_plate (E51): the 2-D steady heat equation of a heated plate, a finite-volume system solved in the model graph; predicts the field of new heater layouts.
  • sci.turing_pattern (E61 part A): Schnakenberg rates from early images of a growing Turing pattern, with the exact Fourier-mode likelihood, the dispersion relation, P(Turing) and simulated patterns.
  • sci.storm_localisation (E58): single-molecule localisation in raw EMCCD STORM frames, with camera calibration, spot detection, a batched pixel-integrated Gaussian PSF fit and a super-resolved render kept in the bundle.
  • sci.ibp_features (E31): latent binary features of small images (truncated Indian buffet process with the patterns summed out).
  • sci.colour_naming (E77): colour naming of one World Color Survey language, pooled or with speaker effects.
  • sci.cmb_field (E79): field-level inference of a masked CMB map with a Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler (sky draws behind the mask and bandpowers).
  • sci.areal_bym2 (E18): disease mapping on a graph of areas with iid, ICAR, proper CAR or BYM2 effects.
  • sci.network_latent_space (E21): ties of a graph from pair covariates, sociality and Procrustes-aligned latent positions.
  • sci.graphical_model (E19): a Gaussian graphical model, dense LKJ or horseshoe neighbourhood selection, with edge probabilities.
  • sci.phylo_regression (E23): regression on a phylogeny with iid, Brownian, Pagel lambda or OU residuals.
  • sci.circular_regression (E81): von Mises, projected normal and regime-mixture regression of angles, and log-Fourier activity densities with overlaps.
  • Export cases e18, e19, e21, e23, e31, e51, e58, e61, e77, e79, e81 (KSBA winds) and e81b (Barro Colorado camera-trap times). A case whose notebook simulates its data (E51, E61) needs no data directory.
  • OutputDecl.circular (mapi-spec): an output that is an angle (a direction, a time of day). The model sets a period attr on the scored array, and the holdout metrics use the circular mean, errors wrapped to half a turn, intervals around the circular mean and an arc-distance CRPS (mape, smape, wape and r2 are skipped). sci.circular_regression declares direction_hat circular.
  • mapi_plugin_science._common: the seeded generators, the quiet PyMC context, the attr cleaning and the draw selection the sci.* modules share (one copy instead of ten).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• BindingMap rewrites the dim names in a variable's grid attr when it renames dims, so the sci.* image recipes find the grid of a score tree after a data.bind.

  • EnginePlan (mapi-pymc) has initvals and jitter: a plugin can start every MCMC chain at one given point (pymc, nutpie and the external NUTS bridges). sci.ibp_features uses it to avoid a start where all its features switch off.

  • The SDK harness parses the model's settings before the data is transformed or split, so a cross-field settings rule (a pydantic model_validator) refuses the fit early. sci.storm_localisation, sci.graphical_model and sci.colour_naming check their settings-only rules there, as the phase 1 models do.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• python -m mapi_plugin_science.export --list lists every case (a case registered after the __main__ guard was missing from the command line).
  • sci.circular_regression evaluate metrics treated angles as numbers: draws around north (350° and 10°) had a mean near 180°, and the MAE of a good fit was about that of a constant guess. They are circular now (see OutputDecl.circular).
  • sci.cmb_field simulate drew the mean of each new patch from the vague 100 µK prior of the fitted patch's mean; it now comes from the spectrum.
  • sci.storm_localisation: render_px_nm is at least 1 nm, and the fit refuses (SETTINGS_INVALID) settings whose render of score_draws draws is over 50 million values (a 0.1 nm render could ask for terabytes).
  • score_bundle refuses a mode the model does not support (MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED) before any mode-specific work: a forecast of a model with text labels on the horizon dim raised an untyped UFuncTypeError, and some models answered ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. A horizon along text labels is COORD_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • sci.graphical_model: score data without a cell dim is SCHEMA_INVALID, not a KeyError (USER_CODE_ERROR).
  • Conformance: e18_areal and e19_ggm pass at --size full (their score expectations fixed the tiny data's district and protein counts; the hooks now check them against the data).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• sci.turing_pattern: the notebook-sized fit takes about 5 min and mixes slowly (r_hat about 1.02, bulk ESS about 180 for rho and g).
  • sci.network_latent_space: the latent-space fit with covariates (model c) warns at 4 × 1000 draws (max r_hat 1.08, bulk ESS 46); it needs more draws or tuning.
  • sci.network_latent_space: evaluate metrics include the diagonal (self-tie) cells.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Core plot recipes (mapi_plots.recipes.extras, Vega-Lite): core.pair (corner plot with divergent draws), core.ridge (one density for each level, with HDI), core.rank_matrix (P(rank = k) and P(row above column)), core.calibration (PIT-ECDF difference with a simultaneous envelope, or a reliability diagram for 0/1 targets) and core.state_sequence (observed series above the state probabilities).
  • Science plot recipes (Plotly): sci.area_map (areas as polygons with mean, sd and exceedance panels), sci.phylogeny (a tree with tip estimates), sci.rose (polar rose or density of angles), sci.image_residuals, sci.ppc_image_grid, sci.swatches (sRGB colour squares, also as a map), sci.power_spectrum and sci.point_pattern (points with error ellipses over a field).
  • Network pack net (entry point mapi.plots: net): net.graph, a node-link drawing and an adjacency matrix of an edge variable (…, node, node_). The catalog shows a "Networks" filter.
  • Each new recipe has an About card, an example in mapi_plots.examples, a gallery image and a row in docs/reference/plots.md.
  • The plot sandbox applies the theme to polar subplots (barpolar, scatterpolar).
  • Workflow nodes: model.summary (posterior summaries, R-hat, ESS, divergences; conditions can read nodes.s.params[...]), evaluate.ppc (coverage, PIT KS distance, Bayesian p-values), compare.stacking (stacking and pseudo-BMA+ weights from the pointwise elpd that model.fit now keeps), model.score (a score mode as a dataset) and plot.render (any catalog recipe as a plot output). The new node kind is plot.
  • model.forecast and evaluate.residuals now give their plot outputs. report.summary has a plots input and plot sections. The web run view draws the plot outputs of nodes and reports.
  • The SDK MetricsReport has an elpd field with the pointwise values (up to 10 000 points). The server reads it from the fit run of a workflow.
  • model.fit and model.backtest take nodes and join, so tree datasets work in workflows. The local runner accepts xr.DataTree inputs. mapi_workflows.testing.science_registry() registers the science plugin.
  • Data export of the science case studies: python -m mapi_plugin_science.export <case> --challenges <data dir> --out <file.nc> (and --list) writes a file that you can upload. Cases e07, e50, e60 and e80.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• mapi-workflows[runtime] depends on mapi-plots[recipes].
  • The server puts the plot outputs of workflow nodes through the plot sanitizer when it collects them (an unsafe plot fails its node with PLOT_UNSAFE) and again when it serves node runs, run outputs and report plot sections.
  • Workflow validation resolves the recipe of plot.render against the bundled recipes and the plot catalog (REF_UNRESOLVED).
  • model.summary computes max_rhat and min_ess over all the values of the selected variables (up to 20 000), not only the 200 values of the table.
  • model.score, model.forecast and plot.render (source: predictions) send a tree input whole and give a tree-input model the tree of that input. plot.render with source: data keeps the groups of a tree input.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• sci.phylogeny matched tips by label when a 0-based tip coord shared a label or two with the node positions by chance; most tips were then empty.
  • sci.image_residuals with log divided log10 residuals by a σ in data units. The normalised residual is now in data units.
  • A non-finite elpd_loo (a log-likelihood of -inf) made the fitted bundle impossible to load. Such an estimate is now left out, and bundles that already hold one load.
  • The pseudo-BMA+ bootstrap of compare.stacking no longer holds a (n_bootstrap, N) matrix (800 MB at the limits).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• A backtest of a tree dataset gives the full tree to each fold. A tree-input model that reads its target from the tree can see the test window. The node shows a warning.
  • search.grid has no nodes parameter.
  • The HTML report does not show plot sections. Only the JSON report and the web run view show them.

docs.title: [0.8.0] — Tree datasets — 2026-10-18
docs.text: This release adds datasets that are trees of groups. A NetCDF-4 or HDF5 file keeps its groups, a raw HDF5 file is mapped to variables after an inspection of its arrays, and a version can combine several files: each file as a node, files stacked along a dim, or files merged on shared coords. A spec selects the nodes that its pipeline reads, and a model can also ask for the whole tree. A guard checks every HDF5 file in the sandbox before it is opened. The catalog also shows each plot recipe as a card with an example picture.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• libhdf5 reads a variable-length text attribute whole before the exact length check. The read is bounded by the run budget, and some rare files with such attributes are refused.
  • The web HDF5 mapper cannot set the description of a variable or the DimSpec of a coord. Use the Python client or the CLI for these.
  • A local mapi fit --data x.tree.zip reads the file as a plain dataset. Only mapi check resolves data.nodes locally.
  • Workflow nodes that fit again on changed flat data, and the ablations of governance checks, do not give a tree to tree-input models.
  • The tree version page shows the preview and profile of the default node only. The Data Explorer shows the other nodes.
  • The web flows for trees ran against the mock API only. The real server and runner path ran in the end-to-end test.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Tree datasets (M4). A dataset version can hold an xr.DataTree (layout tree): one node for each group, with node paths such as / and /instrument/psf. A TreeSchema describes it (one DataSchema for each node; mapi_spec.tree). DatasetVersion has layout, tree_schema and sources. The version stores data.tree.zip and tree_schema.json, and its schema.json is the schema of the root node. Migration 0014_tree_datasets adds the columns. Refer to the new guide Tree datasets, HDF5 and multi-file versions (docs/guides/tree-data.md).
  • NetCDF-4 and HDF5 groups. The ingest opens a NetCDF-4 (or xarray-written HDF5) file with groups as a tree, and a .zarr.zip with nested groups too. Empty groups stay as nodes.
  • Raw HDF5 files (format hdf5, .h5/.hdf5/.he5). IngestMapping.hdf5 (Hdf5Mapping) tells which arrays become which variables of which node, with their dims (Hdf5Var) and coords (Hdf5Coord: an array of the file, a range of numbers or dates, or an integer index). One warning lists the arrays that the mapping does not name.
  • Upload inspection. POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/inspect starts an inspect run, and GET …/inspection gives the UploadInspection: the groups and arrays (path, shape, dtype, chunks, filters, dims hint, small attributes) from the metadata only. 409 NOT_READY while the run is not complete. MAPI_INSPECT_TIMEOUT_S sets its time limit.
  • Versions made from several files. DatasetVersionCreate.assembly (IngestAssembly) combines a maximum of 64 uploads in one ingest run. Each source goes to a node and joins the other sources of that node by node, concat (along a new dim, one label for each file) or merge (on shared coords, with join exact, inner or outer).
  • data.nodes and data.join in specs. A spec selects nodes of a tree (NodeSelect: path, vars, prefix). The platform merges them into the one flat dataset that the pipeline reads. Static validation resolves the merge from the tree_schema of the version. A side table that is a tree reads one node (side_tables.<name>.node).
  • Tree-input models. Capabilities.input = "tree" gives a model the whole bound tree in ctx.tree (fit, score, evaluate, the Model Explorer, governance checks and workflow scoring), next to the flat input. mapi_sdk.tree has select_nodes, infer_tree_schema, validate_tree and read_tree_zip/write_tree_zip. The contract kit has check_tree_model, TreeModelFixture, tree_dataset and the reference model toy.tree_linear. fit_spec and score_bundle accept tree datasets.
  • The Data Explorer shows one node of a tree at a time. Ingest writes the views of each node under ui/explore/nodes/, and a DataExploreRequest takes a node.
  • Python client: datasets.upload takes an xr.DataTree and raw HDF5 files; datasets.upload_files (with AssemblyFile), stage_upload, inspect_upload, upload_inspection, inspect and inspect_file.
  • CLI: mapi datasets upload takes several files with --node, --concat DIM=LABEL, --merge and --join. New commands mapi datasets inspect and mapi datasets ingest.
  • Web app: the upload page takes several files for one version. Each file has a format (from its extension; .h5/.hdf5/.he5 give hdf5), a node path and a combine rule (node, concat with a dim and a label, or merge with a join). The page checks the assembly and shows every problem before the upload. A raw HDF5 file is inspected first; an array browser (path, shape, dtype, dims, filters, warnings) lets you map arrays to variables, with dims, roles, units, a missing-value rule and a coord for each dim (an array of the file, a start and step, or an index). Each problem shows next to the input it is about, in a live region that a screen reader announces. NetCDF and Zarr files can be inspected to preview their groups.
  • Web app: the version page of a tree dataset has a Nodes tab (the node tree, the schema and coords of each node, and the preview of the default node). The Data Explorer takes ?node= and has a node picker. The spec editor completes data.nodes (node keys, paths and vars) from the tree schema, and the Insert panel has a Tree nodes group.
