Their platform lookups (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, routing pushed events) now run as a new mapi_gateway role (migration 0005_gateway_role, MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE). It has no BYPASSRLS, gets explicit policies on identity tables and column privileges on a few run and ledger metadata columns, and cannot read datasets, specs, models, plots, attempts, events or logs. Every API request uses it automatically. Pushed events are written through tenant sessions. Terraform adds the mapi_gateway login and its db-url-gateway secret, and only the orchestrator can read db-url-orchestrator.

docs.title: Fixed (M2 review: executors, cloud and infrastructure)
docs.text:
• infra: the deployed stack can run work at all. Terraform creates a create-only url-uploader account (MAPI_URL_UPLOADER), without which every run failed at dispatch; the server refuses MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs without a distinct uploader.
  • infra: checkpoint policies may overwrite their own checkpoints (conditional storage.objects.delete under .../checkpoints/ only), so PARTIAL bundles and resume see every segment on real GCS.
  • server: verified and public tenants are placed only on an executor with passing, unexpired conformance and security-suite reports for its current caps (PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence, MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S); the admin console, CLI and web show the real state. Runs that no executor can place are refused at submission (503) instead of failing at lease, and the docs say that verified tenants need DNS enforcement verified first.
  • server: docker-gvisor can qualify for shared tiers on a network declared isolated (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED).
  • server: Cloud Run 429s requeue a run without using up an infrastructure retry, leases are renewed while a batch is submitted (for at most ten lease lengths per submit), and Retry-After is capped. The executor's per-process bookkeeping is bounded.
  • sdk: zip artifacts (skops) are no longer rejected as pickles depending on the second they were written.
  • infra: user log and progress events are excluded from the exec projects' _Default log bucket; the API identity only reads the quarantine bucket.
  • deploy: the deploy workflow is valid (no runner context in job env; CI runs actionlint); rollback.sh --previous picks the release before the deployed one (records are named after their images, rollbacks are marked); dry runs no longer claim what they did not do.

docs.title: Fixed (M2 review: CLI, operations and docs)
docs.text:
• server: incident containment can now stop running tenant code. PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name} (audited executor.update, reason required; mapi admin executors disable|enable, a Disable button in Admin → Executors) disables an executor: orchestrators lease nothing onto it and their periodic reports no longer reset enabled to true. The kill-switch update takes cancel_untrusted_runs (with untrusted_execution_enabled=false; mapi admin kill-switches set --cancel-untrusted-runs, "Cancel running uploaded code" in the web app), which moves every unfinished run of uploaded code to cancelling. The sandbox-escape and incident-response runbooks use both.
  • ops: the jobs.run 429 alarm (plan §8.3) watches Cloud Run's 429s. The orchestrator exports mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total{executor} (every 429, retried ones included), and MapiJobsRun429 and the dashboard use it instead of the API's own 429s to tenants on POST /v1/runs. The Cloud Monitoring policy uses serviceruntime.googleapis.com/api/request_count (RunJob, response_code=429). Its old filter named a metric that Cloud Run jobs do not export, and it counted every 4xx.
  • ops: the plan's alert on running executions at 70 % of Cloud Run's 1,000 (§8.8) exists. The orchestrator's report exports mapi_executor_running_executions{executor} from the run table; MapiRunningExecutions70 and a Cloud Monitoring policy on run.googleapis.com/job/running_executions fire above 700.
  • infra: on GCP the mapi_* series reach Cloud Monitoring.
  • The orchestrator serves its own /metrics on 127.0.0.1:9464. Before, the dispatch, reconcile and finalize series had no endpoint in the cloud.
  • api, events and the orchestrator run a collector sidecar (metrics_collector_image, an OpenTelemetry Collector pinned by digest). It scrapes /metrics over loopback with the metrics bearer and writes to Managed Service for Prometheus.
  • Without an image Terraform warns that the alerts and dashboard stay empty.
  • The nightly security jobs push mapi_security_probe_unexpected to the Pushgateway at MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL.
  • gcp-deployment.md has a Metrics section.
  • server: rotating the local bundle-signing key no longer breaks every existing model. MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS lists retired keys (public or private PEM) that still verify. Terraform gains control.kms_trusted_key_versions (MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS on every server workload). The key-rotation runbook now gives the real local and Cloud KMS procedures and the compromise path. It no longer tells GCP operators to rotate a Pub/Sub "internal token": pushes there are OIDC-authenticated.
  • docs: data residency is enforced only on executors that declare regions (Cloud Run Jobs). The self-hosted executors are not checked, and the tenancy page now says so instead of promising a region match everywhere.
  • server: MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS restricts an orchestrator to some trust tiers. Two orchestrators serving different exec pools can no longer lease each other's runs (leasing was not pool-aware, so public-tier code could land in the paid pool). gcp-deployment.md no longer suggests a second orchestrator without it, and says that one environment deploys one pool until M5.
  • ops: three Prometheus rule fixes.
  • MapiQuota70 is now MapiQuotaRejections. It fires on rejections, not at 70 %, and it aggregates by (scope), so its summary names the scope.
  • MapiNoProgressIngested also fires when no event was ever accepted (or vector(0)).
  • Clearing the spend cap now resets mapi_global_spend_micros and mapi_global_spend_cap_micros to 0, both at once and at every admission. The spend ratio ignores a cap of 0, so MapiGlobalSpendCap90 stops firing.
  • cli: mapi logout --revoke revokes the token in the project it is bound to (it was refused with 403 when another project was selected) and forgets the local credentials even when the revocation fails, then exits 1.
  • security: the report writers create their directory, so make security-suite (and both nightly security jobs) no longer fail on a fresh checkout without .local/.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• server: two review branches each added a database role for the API without the row-level-security bypass. One is kept (0005_gateway_role, column-level grants, used for every API request); MAPI_DB_PLATFORM from the other is gone. The executor-disable migration is renumbered 0006_executor_disable and lets the gateway change an executor's enabled and disabled_reason.
  • server: an executor's enabled flag belongs to operators. Missing shared-tier evidence no longer turns it off; it shows in shared_tiers_enabled and the executor's message.
  • server: a submission that no executor can place gets one answer per cause. A residency or resource class no executor serves is refused with 403. A trust tier that no executor can take yet (enforcement not verified, no suite evidence) gets 503.
  • server: as the gateway role, the kill switch's cancel_untrusted_runs cancels each tenant's runs in a session of that tenant. The operators' usage report can read the ledger columns it sums.
  • tests: the end-to-end spend-cap drills use a self-hosted-trusted tenant, which the local executor can still place.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• Nothing has run against real Google Cloud. The Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, KMS and Cloud SQL code paths, the IAM conditions, the logging exclusion, the metrics collector sidecar and the Cloud Monitoring filters are checked with fakes and mocked providers only.
  • No job posts the nightly conformance and security-suite results to the evidence endpoint yet. Until an operator records them (and the M0 DNS check passes), verified and public tenants cannot run on any executor.
  • There is no endpoint to disable a user account. disabled is set in the database, and sign-in keeps it.
  • The gateway role still reads some tables across tenants for the operator console, quota counters and sign-in.
  • A live log tail polls the logs endpoint instead of using the run's event stream.
  • The API's built-in /docs and /redoc pages load assets from a public CDN.

docs.title: [0.2.0] — M1: local vertical slice — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
The platform now runs end to end on one machine. From the Expert web app (or the CLI, the Python client or plain HTTP) you can upload data, write and validate a spec, fit an E33-style hierarchical geo MMM, inspect it, and score it: an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals. Real Cloud Run and multi-tenancy come in M2 (v0.3.0). In summary:

  • server (mapi-server): a single-tenant FastAPI control plane on PostgreSQL with procrastinate. It includes a dispatcher, a level-triggered reconciler, a metadata-only finalizer with signed bundle manifests, HMAC-verified run events, SSE with resume, and local-process and docker executors. It never imports plugin code or array libraries.
  • runner (mapi-runner): a trusted supervisor and an untrusted worker harness for ingest, describe, validate, fit, score, evaluate, derive and render runs. It produces signed events, checkpoints, partial manifests and the ui/ views the web app reads.
  • gcs-shim (mapi-gcs-shim): a local Cloud Storage emulator. It provides generations, server-side CRC32C/MD5, V4 signed URLs and POST policies, per-principal permissions and a write-once bundles bucket.
  • web and plot-sandbox: the Expert web app (YAML editor with live validation, runs with live progress and logs, model inspection, scoring) and a separate-origin, CSP-locked plot renderer.
  • client and cli: a typed sync/async Python client for every v1 endpoint, and mapi for local and remote work.
  • devops: make dev (the whole stack without Docker), digest-pinned images, docker compose, make seed, make e2e and make release-check.
  • conformance: the corpus also runs through the live stack (run --stack URL), and a sklearn conformal fixture is added (7 fixtures in all).
  • docs: a 10-minute quickstart, guides to the web app, CLI, client and HTTP API, a deployment section, an architecture overview and a security model.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.2.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• spec: the M1 shared contracts, so the API, runner, executors, GCS shim, web app and plot sandbox can be built in parallel against one source of truth:
  • mapi_spec.run: the run state machine (RunState, RunTrigger, a pure transition() with owners, failure classes and attempt bumps), the RunSpec bootstrap object, typed event payloads, canonical HMAC-SHA256 event signing, the {"mapi_event": …} stdout format, OutputManifest with metadata-only verification, the signed BundleManifest, RunnerEnv and exit codes.
  • mapi_spec.storage: ObjectMeta, the async ObjectStore protocol, signed GET/PUT and POST policy shapes, GCS-style CRC32C/MD5 helpers, storage errors and the bucket/key naming scheme.
  • mapi_spec.api: REST DTOs for the v1 surface (each with examples), SSE/Prefer/idempotency helpers and M1_ENDPOINTS, the machine-readable endpoint table.
  • mapi_spec.localdev: local ports, origins and environment variable names.
  • spec (additive, contract v0.1): RunKind gains the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign); RunEventType gains checkpoint and metric; RunEvent.ts must be timezone-aware and is normalised to UTC; PlotSpec carries a schema example. The new schemas join export_schemas() and the contract snapshot.
  • docs: the "HTTP API (v1)" and "Run protocol" reference pages (docs/reference/http-api.md, docs/reference/run-protocol.md).
  • gcs-shim: mapi-gcs-shim, a local Cloud Storage emulator. It serves the GCS JSON-API subset the platform uses, with generation and metageneration preconditions, plus V4 signed GET (with Range) and PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix and size range). It adds IAM-lite principals (control, and exec with bootstrap get and delete only), a write-once bundles bucket, lifecycle sweeps, and server-computed CRC32C and MD5 on a crash-safe filesystem backend. ShimObjectStore and the import-guarded GcsObjectStore implement mapi_spec.storage.ObjectStore, and a pytest11 plugin provides the gcs_shim fixture. See docs/reference/gcs-shim.md.
  • runner: mapi-runner, the sandboxed run harness. A trusted supervisor reads and deletes the bootstrap object, starts the untrusted worker with a scrubbed environment (uid 10001 and no-new-privs as root, dev mode otherwise), signs every stdout event, caps logs, events, scratch and outputs, handles SIGTERM/deadline with partial manifests from checkpoints, and uploads outputs plus a signed OutputManifest. The worker runs ingest (CSV/Parquet with a column mapping or the MFF preset, zarr zip, netCDF), describe, validate (dry run), fit (bundle, sidecars, plots, ui/ views, checkpoints), score, evaluate, derive and render through the SDK harness. See docs/reference/runner.md.
  • server: the M1 control plane (mapi-server api|worker|migrate|dev): FastAPI /v1 API covering every M1_ENDPOINTS row plus /v1/me, spec diff, ui/ redirects and :evaluate; SQLAlchemy 2 + Alembic schema (every row carries tenant_id/project_id) with procrastinate on the same Postgres; dispatcher (token bucket, intent row before submit), level-triggered reconciler (executor status is the liveness source of truth, STALLED is a warning, orphan adoption by nonce), metadata-only finalizer with server-side copy and EC P-256 signed bundle manifests verified at URL minting; HMAC-verified event ingestion from the executor pipe and POST /internal/events; SSE with Last-Event-ID resume over one LISTEN connection per process; local-process and docker/docker-gvisor executors; OpenAPI 3.1 export (python -m mapi_server.openapi).
  • web: apps/web, the Expert-mode web app (React 19, TanStack Router/Query/Table, Tailwind + shadcn/ui, Monaco + monaco-yaml with live :validate diagnostics, SSE run progress per chain, dataset upload via signed URLs, model inspection, scoring) and the Guided-mode shell; a pnpm workspace at the repo root.
  • plot-sandbox: apps/plot-sandbox, the separate-origin Vega-Lite/Plotly renderer with a strict CSP and a validated postMessage protocol.
  • devops: containers, local orchestration and developer tooling for M1:
  • images/: base-bayes (with a worker target), base-ml (no PyMC), base-forecast, server (control plane only, checked with import-linter and package assertions at build time), gcs-shim and web (nginx serving the app and the plot sandbox on separate origins with strict CSPs). All are digest-pinned, run as non-root with a read-only root filesystem, and have health checks. The runner images bake the catalog JSON and a warmed PyTensor/Numba cache.
  • docker-compose.yml (postgres 16, gcs-shim, migrate, api, worker with the local-process executor, web, plot-sandbox), compose.override.example.yml and .env.example, which documents every MAPI_* variable.
  • scripts/dev.py (make dev): runs the whole stack without Docker (pgserver PostgreSQL, GCS shim, migrations, api, worker and both Vite servers) with readiness probes, prefixed logs and clean process-group shutdown. Also stop, status, migrate, db-shell and clean.
  • New make targets: dev/run, stop, status, migrate, db-shell, seed (the E33 demo through the API), clean-local, docker-build, docker-pin, compose-up/down/logs, web-build, web-test, test-all, e2e and release-check.
  • CI: a web job, a build-only docker job for every image, and digest-pin and compose checks.
  • Docs: "Local development" and "Containers and docker compose" (Operations), and deploy/README.md.
  • client: mapi-client, the typed Python client (Client, AsyncClient) for every M1_ENDPOINTS row: DTO-typed resources, RFC 7807 errors as MapiError subclasses, idempotency keys and safe retries, lazy pagination, SSE with Last-Event-ID resume, dataset upload through signed URLs, Prefer: wait scoring, CRC32C-checked transfers without the API token. See docs/reference/cli.md.
  • cli: mapi (new, check, fit, score locally or --remote, runs, datasets, catalog, plugin init|test, spec upgrade, serve, config), with --json output and ANSI-stripped untrusted text.
  • spec: mapi_spec.jobs, the run job contract shared by the dispatcher and the runner (IngestJob, DescribeJob, ScoreJob, EvaluateJob, DeriveJob, RenderJob, input and output object names, MetricsSidecar, DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR), and mapi_spec.views, the UI views the web app reads (mapi.preview/v1, mapi.profile/v1, mapi.tree-index/v1).
  • gcs-shim: CORS for the web origin (--cors-origin, default $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) so browsers can use signed URLs, and a wrap hook on ShimServer.
  • server: mapi-server dev (and so mapi serve) starts an embedded GCS shim when nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; the OpenAPI document publishes the run-event payload schemas.
  • docs: "CLI and Python client" and "Web app and plot sandbox" reference pages; the run protocol documents job payloads, object names and UI views.
  • server: GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots (list_run_plots) returns the plots a succeeded run rendered, sanitized on every read; the client has runs.plots().
  • web: the score form takes the input dataset and the spec's side tables (defaulting to the versions the fit used), shows the score run's own plots and pivots the summary by statistic.
  • devops: scripts/seed.py --export DIR writes the E33 demo tables, score payloads and spec as files for the web app.
  • tests: the M1 exit criterion end to end against the running stack: tests/e2e (Python client: fit, SSE, signed manifest and bundle generations, the bundle read back with the corpus' checks, five E33 score requests, bootstrap deletion, forged events) and apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts (the same flow in the browser, plots in the sandbox iframe); a server test proves the finalizer refuses tampered output of the real runner.
  • docs: "Your first model in the web app" guide; the local-development page covers the first start, make e2e and the state under .local/.
  • docs: the M1 documentation set. A landing page with screenshots of the running platform (docs/assets/screenshots/, captured by scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs and shrunk by scripts/optimise_screenshots.py, make docs-screenshots); a validated "zero to first model in 10 minutes" quickstart; guides to every page of the Expert web app, the CLI, the Python client and the HTTP API; an OpenAPI explorer page (a vendored, hash-pinned Redoc bundle over the committed openapi.json, scripts/vendor_redoc.py); a Deployment section (local, Docker Compose, container images, a configuration reference naming every MAPI_* variable, troubleshooting); an architecture overview and a security model; an updated roadmap (M2 cloud and multi-tenant, M3 Guided mode). scripts/gen_docs_reference.py (run by make docs-build and the MkDocs hook) generates the CLI reference from the Typer app, the server settings table from Settings, and copies the OpenAPI document. conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py runs the CLI walkthrough, checks the generated pages, the configuration reference, the Redoc pin and the screenshots, and (under make e2e) runs the client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs against the live stack.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• docs: anchors are validated in strict builds; mermaid is pinned to 11.17.2 instead of Material's moving mermaid@11.
  • server: the object store is ShimObjectStore built from the shim's control key file (MAPI_GCS_ROOT, default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs, or MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE); local executions get the exec token from the same directory unless MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN is set. RunSpec payloads and input names follow mapi_spec.jobs (score data under dataset, side tables under side.<name>, bundle.manifest passed to score runs); evaluate/derive default to the fit dataset and render gets the bundle's plots.json. metrics.json is read as MetricsSidecar.
  • runner: fit writes coords.json and ingest writes summary.json (the control plane's CoordPlan metadata); preview.json, profile.json and ui/tree_index.json follow mapi_spec.views. The runner tests run against the real GCS shim.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are generated from the real server (apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py, checked in CI); the @e2e specs can reuse a running stack on any ports.
  • devops: make dev starts mapi-gcs-shim serve --root … with CORS and passes the resolved URLs to the Vite servers; compose mounts the shim volume read-only into api and worker (MAPI_GCS_ROOT) so they can load the principal keys.
  • sdk: zarr zips record their data-variable order (group attribute _mapi_var_order, removed again on read).
  • devops: make e2e runs the browser @e2e suite (it ran the mocked smoke suite).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• spec: static score validation binds dataset names to canonical names at every inputs_stage, as the runtime does (a weekly EUR plan entering at weekly was refused).
  • server: the dry-run and evaluate endpoints declare their Run response in OpenAPI.
  • seed: make seed ships E33's raw schema with the data, so the fit keeps market: new_levels and new-market scoring works.
  • client: the run event stream decodes the live progress and log frames (sent without an id) as RunLiveFrame; it aborted on the first progress frame of a real fit.
  • server: model lineage records the side-table versions a fit read (it was always empty).
  • sdk: variables come back from a zarr zip in their written order; plot recipes that default to the first variable chose a random one on a bundle read back from storage (mmm.response_curves failed). The response-curve recipe also prefers variables with a channel dim.
  • plot-sandbox: composite Vega-Lite specs (concat, facet) rendered at zero width; they now keep their own size and scroll when wider than the frame.
  • plots: the convergence table's columns no longer overlap; the fan chart draws and captions only the intervals a summary holds.
  • web: a spec opened right after "Save spec" no longer shows unsaved changes (the editor used CRLF for models created empty on Windows user agents), so Fit is enabled; the run page's result column no longer overflows; result tables show dates as dates.
  • devops: make seed ignores a SIZE exported by other toolchains (conda).
  • devops: the compose api and worker containers start. The mapi/server and mapi/worker images bake uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH, so both resolve the same image digest. Before, neither could resolve one and both failed at start-up.
  • devops: compose keeps the bundle-signing key on a keys volume that migrate writes and api/worker mount read-only (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false). Each container used to mint its own key on its tmpfs, so the API rejected every bundle the worker signed, and a restart orphaned every model. mapi-server migrate now creates the key, and concurrent first starts converge on one key.
  • server: mapi-server api|worker|dev make themselves non-dumpable on Linux, so local-process runs (same uid) cannot read their environment or memory. The worker's start-up warning and the operations docs state what such runs can still read.
  • server: a Prefer: wait long-poll stops waiting when its client disconnects.
  • client: models.score() extends the read timeout of each long-poll by its wait and treats a read timeout as "still running", so scores slower than about 90 s no longer raise TransportError. stream_events() counts only connections that deliver nothing towards max_reconnects, so it follows long fits behind proxies that cut connections.
  • cli: run progress and state messages are never parsed as rich markup (no terminal hyperlink injection, no MarkupError aborting mapi fit).
  • devops: .env.example documents every mapi-server setting, and the devops test now derives the list from Settings.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: spec, runner, shim and plots)
docs.text:
• runner: fit runs write ui/preprocess.json (mapi_spec.views.PreprocessView, mapi.preprocess/v1): each step's resolved plugin, learned JSON and small numeric state arrays, so the web app's Preprocessing tab is no longer empty.
  • runner: an INFRA_ERROR reported by the worker fails the run as a user error. Only failures the supervisor sees itself are retried automatically as infrastructure failures.
  • runner: every string the worker sends has ANSI, control and bidi characters stripped. The CLI's strip_control also removes the bidi ranges.
  • server, gcs-shim: the artifacts upload policy is create-only (post_policy(create_only=True) signs x-goog-if-generation-match: 0, and the shim answers 412 for an existing key).
  • plots: recipes draw from mapi_plots.palette, whose dark variants keep at least 3:1 contrast, and the plot sandbox swaps them in dark mode. The decomposition legend is titled "component" when baseline or controls join the channels. Faceted fans and MMM curves give each panel its own axes, in coordinate order.
  • conformance: new sklearn_store_demand fixture. Fixtures not yet ported are listed in DEFERRED with reasons (list --deferred). run --stack URL drives fixtures through the API.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: server)
docs.text:
• GET /v1/runs/{id}/plots and score results are scoped to the caller's tenant and project.
  • Runner JSON is parsed with a nesting limit, and deep nesting is reported as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Bundle inputs are verified again at dispatch and on :retry.
  • The API refuses unexpected Host headers (MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS), nginx answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES and the GCS shim checks hosts too, which guards against DNS rebinding.
  • Ingest and spec validation enforce the per-resource-class data caps (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE).
  • An omitted fit seed is pinned to 0 at submission, so lineage records the seed actually used.
  • Run lifecycle:
  • A cancelled checkpointed fit ends PARTIAL and can be resumed (new CANCELLING --complete--> FINALIZING edge).
  • :cancel on a finalizing run is a no-op.
  • A run stopped at its deadline fails as TIMEOUT or finalizes as PARTIAL.
  • An exit counts only after its event backlog is ingested.
  • A restarted reconciler re-adopts live executions.
  • Stalled finalize jobs are re-queued.
  • Executor cancels no longer block the reconcile pass.
  • SSE reads the run state before its events, and a run never shows another attempt's progress.
  • Docker executor:
  • Each plugin namespace gets its own versioned mapi/base-* image (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES).
  • Run containers join the shim's network namespace; none is refused.
  • The supervisor and the worker run under separate uids (10001 for the worker), and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1 fails a run closed rather than falling back to dev mode.
  • The import-linter contract also forbids plugin packages, plot recipes and columnar libraries in mapi_server.
  • Docs: invalid submissions are refused without a run, and REJECTED is reserved.

docs.title: Fixed (M1 review: web)
docs.text:
• Plots:
  • The plot host accepts a sandbox exported reply only for an export the app requested.
  • Downloading a score output saves a checksum-verified file instead of leaving the app.
  • Run pages:
  • Live progress and log SSE frames, which the server sends without an id, are delivered.
  • The live log view follows the tail.
  • Performance: Monaco and Arrow are no longer in first paint, and routes are lazy-loaded. A build-time budget keeps first-paint JavaScript under 640 KiB (it was 4.26 MB; now about 515 KB).
  • Spec editor:
  • It never replaces unsaved edits when a newer revision appears.
  • Save sends the revision the text came from as parent_revision.
  • Accessibility:
  • No sideways scroll at phone width, and the compact nav shows every page.
  • Status colours and form borders meet WCAG AA.
  • Score form errors are marked on their fields and announced.
  • The Score page resets its form and results when the version changes, and shows a loading state while the version loads.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• tests: a devops docstring no longer names a fake MAPI_ variable that the configuration reference test picked up.
  • web: openapi.json and schema.d.ts are regenerated (the cancel endpoint documents the finalizing no-op).
  • docs: pages written before the review fixes landed now describe the shared compose signing key, ui/preprocess.json, the docker executor's network and images, and the new MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS, MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES, MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES, MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE and MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION settings.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• The docker executor, the compose stack and the new compose smoke test have not run against a real Docker daemon yet.
  • Under the local-process executor, run code shares the orchestrator's uid and can read its key files. The uid split is M2.
  • MAPI_PROFILE means a config profile to the CLI and client, but the deployment profile to the server.
  • The API's built-in /docs and /redoc pages load assets from a public CDN.
  • Conformance fixtures E13, E84-lite, E82-slim and E45 are deferred: they need new plugins or run kinds.

docs.title: [0.1.0] — M0: contract layer — 2026-10-15
docs.text:
First milestone release: the typed contract layer and the in-process xarray runtime, with no platform services yet. In summary:

  • spec (mapi-spec): pure-Pydantic contracts (DataSchema, SchemaEffect, ModelSpec, ScoreRequest, capabilities, representations, PlotSpec envelope, error codes) with static validation and JSON Schema export, frozen as contract v0.1.
  • sdk (mapi-sdk): wire formats, the stage/split/context/replay/inverse pipeline engine, CoordPlan, bundles without pickle, the fit_spec/score_bundle harness, the in-process executor and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit.
  • steps (mapi-steps): 28 built-in core.* preprocessing steps and five split kinds, each with exported static effects.
  • pymc (mapi-pymc) and sklearn (mapi-sklearn): model adapters where an author writes only build() or estimator().
  • plots (mapi-plots): JSON-only Vega-Lite/Plotly sanitizer and the core, mmm and ml recipe catalogs.
  • plugins: mmm.hierarchical_geo, mmm.pymc_marketing, ts.hsgp_trend, ts.gaussian_hmm, tabular.hierarchical_glm and tabular.regressor.
  • conformance (mapi-conformance): the corpus runner and six fixtures (E02, C08, E24, store demand, E33, pymc-marketing), all passing at --size tiny.
  • docs: the MkDocs Material site with tested snippets and generated catalogs.

Every workspace package is versioned 0.1.0. The server, runner, CLI, client and GCS shim packages are still skeletons.

  • Repository scaffold: uv workspace, package skeletons, split Apache-2.0 / AGPLv3+commercial licensing.

docs.title: Contract v0.1 (frozen)
docs.text:
• mapi_spec.CONTRACT_VERSION = "0.1" names the contract the exported JSON Schemas describe; every exported schema carries it as x-mapi-contract-version.
  • The contract is frozen for the v0.1.x line: packages/spec/tests/snapshots/contract.json pins a digest of every exported schema and the drift test fails on any change. Additive changes (new optional fields, new error codes) regenerate the snapshot (MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1); breaking changes bump CONTRACT_VERSION first.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mapi-spec: the pure-Pydantic contract layer.
  • DataSchema, DimSpec and VarSpec, with schema templates.
  • SchemaEffect propagation; ModelSpec, ScoreRequest and the Sweep, Backtest, SBC and Campaign wrappers.
  • A strict YAML 1.2 loader, canonical JSON and spec hashes.
  • Static validation: split stage, LEAKAGE_RISK, dim policies, recursion and the CoordPlan checks.
  • Capabilities, representation rules, the PlotSpec envelope, stable RFC 7807 error codes, the Executor protocol shapes, JSON Schema export and the mapi-spec CLI.
  • mapi-sdk: the xarray runtime.
  • Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips and Arrow IPC.
  • Array-level schema validation; the step contract, pipeline engine and stages.
  • Split and per-group context replay; inverse chains with output-space labels.
  • CoordPlan and coordinate canonicalisation, the representation-aware summariser and metrics.
  • Bundle IO with integrity sidecars and no pickle; the fit_spec/score_bundle harness with evaluate_then_refit.
  • The entry-point registry, the in-process executor, and the mapi_sdk.testing contract kit (check_step, check_model, pytest plugin).
  • mapi-steps: 28 built-in core.* steps (reshape, value, feature, formula, adstock and saturation).
  • Each exports a templated SchemaEffect and a shipped catalog JSON.
  • Catalog entries for the five split kinds.
  • mapi-pymc: PyMCModel, where an author writes only build().
  • BuildContext with hier_effect new levels.
  • Engines: nutpie, pymc, MAP and ADVI, plus guarded numpyro, blackjax and pathfinder.
  • Segmented, resumable sampling with checkpoints; CRN counterfactuals.
  • Convergence diagnostics, FrozenPredictor fast scoring and check_fast_score.
  • mapi-sklearn: SklearnModel with an allow-listed estimator registry (sklearn and xgboost).
  • skops and xgboost-JSON persistence.
  • Point, quantile, bootstrap, conformal and classifier plugins (sklearn.tabular_*).
  • Pooled new levels; exact or zeroing contributions.
  • mapi-plots: a JSON-only PlotSpec sanitizer (pinned Vega-Lite 6.4.1 and plotly.js 4.1.1 schemas, an expression allow-list, HTML stripping) and role-bound templates.
  • The standard core.* recipe catalog, plus the mmm.* and ml.* domain packs.
  • Altair and Plotly converters with named Arrow datasets, and the render_plots batch entry point.
  • mapi-plugin-mmm: marketing-mix model plugins (entry point mapi.models: mmm).
  • mmm.hierarchical_geo 1.3.0, the E33 hierarchical geo MMM: adstock over core.lag_tensor features, logistic/Hill saturation, channel effects partially pooled across geos, new geos from the hyperprior, additive contributions.
  • Fit-cached derived quantities in original units: contributions, per-draw response-curve grids for Guided sliders, marginal cost/ROI; a decision objective for budgets; fast scoring.
  • mmm.pymc_marketing 1.0.0, an adapter around pymc-marketing 1.2's MMM (verified on PyMC 6.3) that owns scaling, carry-over and units and never pickles.
  • Declarative priors in pymc-marketing's dict form, typed per parameter so wrong priors fail static validation; a synthetic E33 simulator with known parameters and a parameter-recovery test.
  • mapi-sdk: outputs.derived with cache: fit is computed on the production fit through the plugin's derive hook; ScoreContext.to_original maps model-stage arrays to the output space.
  • Cross-package conformance suites:
  • the plan's xgboost spec through real steps, models and plots;
  • an E33-shaped core.* pipeline in front of a PyMC model.
  • mapi-plugin-ts: ts.hsgp_trend (C08: HSGP trend + seasonality whose domain comes from the anticipated coords; HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT past max_extension; sentinel months left out of the likelihood) and ts.gaussian_hmm (E24: forward-algorithm HMM over padded tracks with a terminal_state group, forecast and filter modes, relabelling postprocess, LOO declared invalid).
  • mapi-plugin-tabular: tabular.hierarchical_glm (E02: partially pooled GLM in long layout, hyperprior new groups, group-level covariates, four families) and tabular.regressor (plan §6.2 store demand: quantile regression restricted to the registry's quantile-capable estimators).
  • mapi-conformance: the corpus runner python -m mapi_conformance run [--size tiny|full] [--fixture id] (validate, fit, score requests, evaluate, contract kit, plots, expectations; summary table and JSON) with the e02, c08, e24, xgb_store_demand, e33 and pymc_marketing fixtures; pytest -m conformance, make conformance (tiny) and make conformance-full.
  • Score cases can opt out of side tables (side_tables: false, e.g. a weekly EUR plan entering after the FX step).
  • Expectation hooks that declare ctx receive a FixtureContext (seed, size, registry, side tables and earlier score results).
  • Docs: spec format, SDK, built-in steps and plots references; guides for plugins, PyMC, tabular models and plots.
  • Docs: built-in models reference, marketing-mix models guide, forecasting and sequential models guide, conformance corpus guide.
  • Docs: the MkDocs Material site.
  • A landing page, getting started (install, first model, runs and executors), concepts (labelled data, pipelines and stages, representations, bundles, coord plans, capabilities), the "port a model in 15 minutes" guide, licensing, contributing and roadmap pages for v0.2–v0.4.
  • Generated reference pages: steps, models and plot-recipe catalogs, the ModelSpec/ScoreRequest schema and error codes (scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py, run by an MkDocs hook and make docs-catalog); API reference via mkdocstrings.
  • Every Python example lives in docs/snippets/ and is executed by conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py (make docs-test).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The workspace runs numpy 2.4 (pymc-marketing 1.2 requires numpy < 2.5).
  • make typecheck also covers plugins/mmm, plugins/ts, plugins/tabular and conformance.
  • Score requests that name a pinned side table now fail validation. Score outputs along time and extend dims come back sorted. validate_spec emits an INFO issue when the model's target role overrides a declared role.
  • Plugin-raised error text now appears in untrusted_text, not in detail.

docs.title: Fixed (integration)
docs.text:
• The plan's xgboost example names the real quantile plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles). A new ml.feature_importance recipe covers its plot list.
  • core.fit_vs_actual and core.residuals_over_time compare quantile and interval summaries cell by cell instead of refusing them.
  • The contract kit flags step settings whose defaults are missing from the exported JSON Schema (default_factory), and finds reverse-bound outputs when checking units.
  • Holdout metrics no longer invert the predictions of models that own inverse_units a second time.
  • Score outputs that declare their own units (e.g. state probabilities) no longer go through the target's inverse transforms.
  • The contract kit runs its shuffled, subset and new-level checks on long layouts (index variables are remapped) and shifts calendar-frequency time coords by whole periods.
  • The in-process executor no longer resolves a score request's side-table refs when the run payload already supplies those tables.
  • The contract kit's score requests name the spec's score_policy: supplied side tables, so models with supplied tables (E33's FX) pass the scoring checks.
  • The E33 and pymc-marketing fixtures use the corpus runner's fixture layout and run in python -m mapi_conformance run.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: spec and SDK)
docs.text:
• Counterfactuals: score_bundle takes a baseline data payload and a separate scenario payload, and scores the scenario's interventions against the baseline. A scenario without baseline data, or a named scenario that was not supplied, is SCHEMA_INVALID.
  • owns is enforced: catalog steps declare provides (scaling, carryover), and validate_spec rejects such a step on the target, media or spend variables of a model that owns that preprocessing (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • Target dependence follows the model template's target roles, even with an inferred raw schema, so RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED fires reliably. The recursion and future-covariate checks measure how far the payload extends past the fit, not only horizon.
  • No target leakage into evaluation lags for dynamic or cell-level splits. as_of gap periods stay in the holdout with masked targets and are excluded from metrics.
  • Pinned side tables always replay the fit-time version; a request that names one fails with SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE.
  • Score payloads are sorted along ordered/extend dims before the pipeline; duplicate labels are COORD_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • Chained look-back steps (adstock then lag) replay with fit-time history. A score window that starts inside the fitted range and loses look-back history gets a WARNING.
  • Long-layout per-group context works end to end.
  • Inverses: steps declare additive inverses, and decompositions along component only go through additive steps (otherwise they stay at the blocking stage, with a WARNING). Smearing residuals come only from target-shaped outputs. The moments sd uses the delta method.
  • Model-owned outputs are labelled per variable with their units and output_space.
  • Derived quantities named in output.vars come back from the fit cache. An uncached one is refused.
  • PyMC CRN counterfactuals give identical draws in untouched cells for Poisson, negative binomial and binomial likelihoods (crn_ppf).
  • Wire and bundle hardening: XrJSON budgets decoded bytes (max_decoded_bytes), caps declared dim sizes and accepts only ISO-8601 dates. Zarr-zip decoding is bounded by declared shapes, string lengths and an expansion ratio. Pickle is detected by opcode stream, in object .npy and inside archives. The evaluation sub-bundle is verified and never kept stale. Entry points can no longer replace registered or built-in plugin ids.
  • Spec parsing rejects non-finite floats and reports oversized JSON integers as SpecParseError.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: models and steps)
docs.text:
• core.formula: scalar ~ is logical not; overflow and division by zero give inf/nan, and other arithmetic errors are reported as SCHEMA_INVALID rather than escaping.
  • PyMC checkpoints: the codec rebuilds only classes defined in PyMC step-method modules (plus pymc.util and mapi_pymc), at exactly the encoded module:qualname.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: plots, conformance and tooling)
docs.text:
• Plot sanitizer (Plotly): updatemenus/sliders method args are checked in the positional [attr, value] form and inside nested frame/trace objects, so external image sources, href/url paths, tile-map subplots and tile-map trace types can no longer hide there.
  • Plot sanitizer (Vega-Lite): select.toggle strings and bind.legend event filters are checked as expressions, event['view'] is rejected like event.view, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected.
  • from_plotly strips HTML from (and scans) the strings it moves into Arrow datasets, which the JSON sanitizer never decodes.
  • Plugin-originated error text stays out of trusted fields: render_plots and the step/model wrappers (Pipeline, harness fit/score/derive) move a plugin MapiError's detail into untrusted_text and keep its code only when plugin code may raise it (mapi_spec.errors.from_plugin_error, PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES).
  • Contract kit, check_step: effect_matches_output also compares each dim's kind and frequency and each variable's units; the toy FX and scale steps now set the units they declare.
  • Contract kit, check_model: new horizon_exceeds_fit, missing_future_covariate, recursive_unsupported, fast_score_matches_exact (plugin check_fast_score hook, provided by PyMCModel), plots_sanitize and outputs_match_manifest checks; extend_typed_errors covers integer extend dims; output_space_and_units covers outputs that inherit the target implicitly.
  • OutputDecl.dims_of (additive) lets a manifest declare settings-dependent data dims; the sklearn models (and so tabular.regressor) and mmm.pymc_marketing use it, so their static output dims match what score returns.

docs.text:
make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make help             # every developer entry point
Command What it does make test Runs the default test suite (all tests, but not the Docker, cloud and end-to-end tests) make test-fast Runs only the unit tests. It does not run the slow MCMC tests make lint Runs ruff, the ruff format check and the import-linter contracts make typecheck Runs mypy on each package that has type checks make conformance Runs the conformance corpus at size tiny (FIXTURE=e33 for one fixture) make docs-serve Shows this site and loads it again when a page changes make docs-build Makes the generated reference pages again and builds the site in strict mode make docs-test Runs all the documentation snippets and the checks of the docs make dev Runs the whole stack locally without Docker (Local, without Docker) make docker-build / make compose-up Builds the images / runs the compose stack (Docker Compose) make release-check Does a check of version consistency, the changelog entry, plan files (there must be none), pinned images and current third-party notices make notices Makes THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md again after a change to uv.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml (Licensing)

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
We use git flow with two permanent branches, main and develop.

gitGraph
    commit id: "v0.1.0" tag: "v0.1.0"
    branch develop
    checkout develop
    commit id: "integration"
    branch feat/m1-runner
    checkout feat/m1-runner
    commit id: "feat(runner): …"
    commit id: "test(runner): …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-runner
    branch feat/m1-docs
    checkout feat/m1-docs
    commit id: "docs: …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-docs
    checkout main
    merge develop tag: "v0.2.0"
Branch Purpose main Releases only. We merge each milestone from develop and tag it vX.Y.Z. Nobody commits to main directly. develop Integration. We merge feature branches here with --no-ff. feat/<milestone>-<topic> One unit of work. Make the branch from the latest develop. 
git checkout -B feat/m1-my-change develop
# ... small, logical commits ...
make fmt lint typecheck test

Do not rebase or rewrite develop or main. Keep changes to shared files small, and only add to them. The shared files are the root pyproject.toml, the Makefile, uv.lock and CI. Tell about these changes in your pull request.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text: Write all text for users in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. This includes the documentation, the text in the web app, and the messages that the server sends for the app to show. The rules are in Writing style.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Use Conventional commits, with the package as the scope:

feat(sdk): replay context tails at each step's input stage
fix(server): reject score requests whose horizon exceeds the fit
docs: add the porting guide
test(conformance): add the e24 filter fixture
chore: bump ruff

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Use Python 3.12 and ruff (line length 100). Use type hints in all code. Use mypy strict for the core packages.
  • Tests are in tests/ in each package. PyMC fits in tests use very small settings (tune: 50–150, draws: 50–150, chains: 2). If a test takes more than about ten seconds, mark it slow.
  • Write short docstrings (Google style). The contract tests are the executable documentation.
  • mapi_spec must not import numpy, xarray or pandas. The server must not import plugin code or array code. make lint makes sure of the two rules.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site uses MkDocs Material. mkdocs.yml is at the repository root, and the pages are in docs/.

  • The tests run all Python examples. The examples are in docs/snippets/*.py. Pages include them with --8<-- "file.py:section". conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py
  • Platform examples run against a live stack. make e2e runs the client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs (docs/snippets/client_tour.py, http_tour.sh, cli_remote.sh). The default suite runs the local CLI walkthrough (cli_local.sh) in conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py. Shell snippets use the same section markers.
  • Scripts make the reference pages. scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py writes the pages for the steps, models, plot recipes, spec schema and error codes. scripts/gen_docs_reference.py writes the CLI reference, the server settings and a copy of apps/web/openapi.json. The two scripts write into docs/reference/generated/, which git ignores. An MkDocs hook runs the two scripts before each build.
  • New MAPI_* variables go into the configuration reference (docs/operations/configuration.md). A test looks for these variables in the source tree.

  • Screenshots are in docs/assets/screenshots/. Each screenshot must be 300 KB or less, and a page must use it. make docs-screenshots captures them again from a stack that runs and has seed data. Other targets capture one set each:

    • from a make dev stack: docs-screenshots-admin and docs-screenshots-science (the science tutorials, with the datasets of Science data);
    • from the web app in mock mode: docs-screenshots-guided, docs-screenshots-integrations, docs-screenshots-tutorials, docs-screenshots-explorers and docs-screenshots-workflows.

    The configuration reference lists the variables that these scripts read. - The cookbook documents are tested. conformance/tests/test_docs_v05.py makes sure that each docs/snippets/cookbook_*.yaml is a valid workflow. It also makes sure that the documents of the six M5 recipes (cookbook_sci_*.yaml and cookbook_bayes_workflow_audit.yaml) are the same as their gallery templates. If you change one of these templates, change its document too. - make docs-build must pass (mkdocs build --strict, with anchor validation). - Write for two types of readers. An analyst wants to know what a feature does for them. A data scientist wants to know exactly how it works.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text:
modeling-api uses a split licence. The copyleft licence does not apply to persons who write models and integrations. The copyleft licence protects the hosted platform.

Component Where Licence SDK and contracts: mapi-spec, mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc, mapi-sklearn, mapi-jax packages/spec, packages/sdk, packages/sdk-pymc, packages/sdk-sklearn, packages/sdk-jax Apache-2.0 Built-ins: steps, plots, model plugins, workflow runtime, conformance corpus packages/steps-core, packages/plots-core, plugins/*, packages/workflows, conformance/ Apache-2.0 Tools: CLI, Python client, GCS emulator packages/cli, packages/client, packages/gcs-shim Apache-2.0 Platform: API server, run harness, web apps, images, infrastructure packages/server, packages/runner, apps/*, images/, infra/, ops/, security/ AGPLv3 or a commercial licence Documentation docs/ CC BY 4.0

Each package gives its SPDX expression in its pyproject.toml (Apache-2.0, or AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-mapi-commercial). Each package also has its own LICENSE file. The full texts are in the repository root: LICENSE.md, LICENSE-APACHE.txt, LICENSE-AGPL.txt and COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md.

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text:
Plugins you write are yours

A step, model or plot recipe that you write with mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc or mapi-sklearn uses Apache-2.0 libraries. You can use the licence that you want for it, and a proprietary licence is also possible.

Applications that call the platform are not derivative works

Your application can call the platform over HTTP, with the Python or TypeScript client, through webhooks or through MCP. These calls do not make your application subject to the AGPL.

If you modify and host the platform

If you modify the platform components (server, runner, apps) and offer them as a network service, the AGPLv3 says that you must publish your modifications. This does not apply if you hold a commercial licence. For commercial terms, send an email to mattreda@mattreda.pro.

docs.title: Third-party libraries
docs.text:
The SDK uses xarray, numpy, pandas, zarr and Pydantic. The model packages use PyMC, ArviZ, scikit-learn, xgboost and skops. The marketing-mix models run on mmm-framework (Apache-2.0). mmm-framework adds NumPyro and JAX (Apache-2.0) and nutpie (MIT). The time-series models (ts.sarimax, ts.var, ts.ets and the other time-series models) run on statsmodels (BSD-3-Clause). The plot recipes use Altair and Plotly. From v0.15, the deep learning models (mapi-jax) use JAX, Flax and Optax (Apache-2.0). The base-dl image also has the NVIDIA CUDA runtime wheels from pip, which have the NVIDIA licence (NVIDIA Software License Agreement). THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md lists them.

The visual workflow builder in the web app uses @xyflow/react (MIT). The API server connects to PostgreSQL through psycopg (LGPL-3.0). The server uses psycopg without modification, as a library that you install separately. Each library keeps its own licence.

THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the repository root is the full list. It gives each Python and JavaScript package in the container images, with its version and SPDX licence. It also contains the NOTICE files of Apache-2.0 packages. It also contains the licence texts of the JavaScript packages that the build compiles into the web app and the plot sandbox.

A script makes this file from uv.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml. After you change a lock file, run make notices. If the file is not current, make release-check and the test suite fail. Each image contains this file and the licence files above, in /usr/share/doc/mapi/.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: The project accepts contributions under the Contributor Licence Agreement (CONTRIBUTOR-LICENSE.md). With this agreement, the project can continue to offer the platform under the two licences. Refer to Contributing.

docs.title: Writing style: Simplified Technical English
docs.text:
All text for users in this project is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (STE). STE makes instructions clear and short. It also makes them easy to read for persons who do not speak English as a first language, and easy to translate.

This page gives the rules that we use. It does not replace the ASD-STE100 specification. When you are not sure, read the specification (Issue 9), section 1 (words) and section 2 (writing rules).

docs.title: Where these rules apply
docs.text: Text Rules Documentation (docs/) Yes, all pages. Procedures and descriptions. Text in the web app Yes: labels, buttons, hints, help text, empty states, errors and tooltips. Text that the server sends for the app to show Yes: About cards, scorecard messages, suggested actions and plain-language error messages. New CHANGELOG entries Yes. Older entries stay as they are. Code, identifiers, API field names and log text for developers No. Keep the names that the code uses. Code comments, docstrings and commit messages No.

docs.title: Words
docs.text:
1. Use approved words from the STE dictionary. Use each word only with its approved meaning and its approved part of speech. For example, "test" is a noun and a verb, but "check" is a noun only. Use "do a check of" or "make sure that".
  2. You can use technical names and technical verbs (see the project word list). Use a technical name only as a noun or an adjective.
  3. Use one word for one thing. Do not use synonyms. For example, always write "dataset", not "data set", "table" or "file" for the same thing.
  4. Do not use the "-ing" form of a verb as a noun or as an adjective, except in a technical name. Write "when you score a model", not "when scoring a model".
  5. Use "the", "a" or "an" before nouns where possible.
  6. Do not make noun clusters of more than three words. Write "the input table of the model", not "model input table layout".

docs.title: Words to replace
docs.text: Do not write Write ensure make sure utilize, leverage use perform, carry out do obtain, retrieve get require, requirement need, necessary prior to before in order to to via through, with approximately about assist help may (possibility) can, possibly e.g. for example etc. (give the full list) i.e. that is simply, just, easily, please (remove the word) allows you to you can in the event that if a number of some, many (or give the number)

docs.title: Verbs
docs.text:
1. Use only these tenses: the simple present, the simple past and the simple future ("shows", "showed", "will show").
  2. Use the active voice in procedures. Use the active voice as much as possible in descriptions. Write "The server checks the request", not "The request is checked".
  3. Use the imperative in instructions: "Select the model".
  4. Do not use "-ing" forms after a verb. Write "Start to type", not "Start typing".

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
1. Write a maximum of 20 words in a procedural sentence.
  2. Write a maximum of 25 words in a descriptive sentence.
  3. Write about one topic in each sentence.
  4. Do not use semicolons to join sentences. Write two sentences.
  5. Use a vertical list when there are more than three items.

docs.title: Procedures
docs.text:
1. Write one instruction in each sentence. You can write two instructions in one sentence only when you do them at the same time.
  2. Write the instructions in the sequence that the user does them.
  3. Put a condition before the instruction: "If the model forecasts, type the periods."
  4. Use numbered steps for a sequence. Use a bulleted list for items that have no sequence.
  5. Use a note to give information that is not an instruction. Do not put an instruction in a note.

docs.title: Descriptions
docs.text:
1. Start each paragraph with a topic sentence.
  2. Write a maximum of six sentences in a paragraph.
  3. Give the most important information first.

docs.title: Warnings and cautions
docs.text:
1. Start with a clear command: "Do not delete the dataset."
  2. Then give the risk: "Model versions that use it will not score."
  3. A warning tells about a risk to persons or to security. A caution tells about a risk to data or to equipment.

docs.title: Text in the app
docs.text: Element Rule Example Button A verb and, if necessary, an object "Save spec", "Add a row" Field hint One or two short sentences. Tell what to type, then the limits. "Type the number of periods. The maximum is 200." Empty state Tell what is missing, then what to do "This project has no datasets. Upload a CSV file to start." Error Tell what is wrong, then what to do "The YAML is not correct. Correct the line that shows in red." Tooltip One sentence "Shows the inputs that the model needs." Confirmation Tell the result of the action "Delete the dataset? You cannot undo this."

docs.title: Project technical names and verbs
docs.text:
You can use these words as technical names (nouns) or technical verbs in this project.

Technical names: actual, adstock, API, argument, artifact, backtest, band, binding, bundle, catalog, channel, coordinate, counterfactual, covariate, CSV file, dashboard, dataset, dimension (dim), draw, driver, endpoint, evidence pack, forecast, governance, horizon, input table, intervention, JSON, level, market, metric, mode, model, model version, node, payload, period, pipeline, plot, plugin, posterior, prior, project, quantile, revision, run, sandbox, scenario, scorecard, side table, spec, stage, step, summary, target, tenant, token, variable, webhook, workflow, YAML.

Technical verbs: click, deploy, download, fit, forecast, log in, log out, paste, promote, roll back, score, select, sign in, type, upload.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Not STE STE Ensure that the dataset has been uploaded prior to scoring. Upload the dataset before you score the model. The form only offers what this model supports, and the fitted preprocessing is replayed exactly: nothing is refitted. The form shows only the modes that the model can do. The server uses the same preprocessing as the fit. It does not fit the model again. Clicking Save will create a new revision. Click Save revision. The app makes a new revision. You may want to check the scorecard. Look at the scorecard.

docs.title: CLI and Python client v0.5
docs.text:
Two Apache-2.0 packages send requests to the /v1 HTTP API:

  • mapi-client (mapi_client): a typed Python client. It has a sync and an async version. It uses httpx.
  • mapi-cli (mapi): the command line. It uses the client, and the SDK for local runs.

The two packages use the Pydantic DTOs from mapi_spec.api for each request and response. For errors, they raise mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses. They make these subclasses from RFC 7807 problem documents.

This page is a short summary. The guides give tested examples for each package (command line, Python client). The CLI reference shows the --help text of each command. The installed CLI makes that page.

docs.title: Python client
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

with Client() as api:  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_TOKEN / ~/.config/mapi/config.toml / 127.0.0.1:8000
    version = api.datasets.upload("eu_media.zarr.zip", dataset="eu_media_daily")
    rev = api.specs.upsert(open("spec.yaml").read())
    run = api.runs.fit(rev.spec_id, rev.revision)
    for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE, resumes with Last-Event-ID
        print(item)
    run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
    result = api.models.score(
        model_id,
        1,
        {
            "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
            "mode": "forecast",
            "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        },
    )
    result.tree  # xr.DataTree with the `xarray` extra
Resource Calls projects list, get catalog get, models, model, steps, plots, schema datasets create, list, get, find, ensure, create_upload, create_version, versions, version, wait_version, upload, artifact, download specs validate, create, list, get, find, revise, upsert, revisions, revision, dry_run runs create, fit, get, list, wait, stream_events, events, logs, plots, cancel, resume, retry runs tracking (v0.11) update, log_metric, log_metrics, log_params, set_tags, track, metrics, metric_history, params; list also takes parent_run_id, name, tags, filters, order_by and columns models list, get, versions, version, artifact, download, score plots list, get, validate tenants (v0.3) list, get, rename, projects, create_project, update_project, delete_project, members, add_member, set_role, remove_member, usage, audit tokens (v0.3) list, create, get, revoke usage (v0.3) get (the project), tenant admin (v0.3, operators) tenants, tenant, create_tenant, update_tenant, quotas, set_quota, delete_quota, kill_switches, set_kill_switches, executors, executor, audit; v0.4: signups, review_signup, set_verification, retry_deletion guided (v0.4) templates, template, detect_roles, draft, compile, translate_priors, prior_translation, wait_prior_translation, preview_priors endpoints (v0.4) list, get, promote, delete, history, rollback, schema, validate, submit, score, snippets webhooks (v0.4) list, create, get, update, delete, rotate_secret, deliveries, replay plots sharing (v0.4) save, saved, get_saved, delete_saved, render, render_status, render_output, download_render, create_embed, embeds, revoke_embed, embed tenants trust (v0.4) verification, request_deletion, deletion, cancel_deletion, export, export_status, wait_export, download_export catalog About cards (v0.5) abouts, about, chooser, recommend, workflow_nodes, workflow_node, governance_checks datasets About and explorer (v0.5) about, describe, explore models explorers and plans (v0.5) explore, compare, optimize, optimization, validate, validations explorations (v0.5) get, wait, link, view workflows (v0.5) list, find, create, validate, get, update, delete, revisions, revision, revise, upsert, run, runs, get_run, wait, cancel, stream_events, events, nodes, node, output_link, download_output, schedules, schedule, update_schedule, delete_schedule, triggers, trigger, delete_trigger, templates, template governance (v0.5) checks, policies, policy, create_policy, update_policy, retire_policy, policy_versions (tenant_id= for tenant-wide policies) validations (v0.5) request, list, for_model, get, wait, evidence, cancel, resubmit, decide, approve, reject, deprecate, evidence_pack, download_evidence_pack

v0.4. api.endpoint(alias) is a RemoteEndpoint (schema(), validate(ds), score(ds) -> xr.Dataset with inline XrJSON). api.signup() and api.verify_email() are public calls. The client sends them without credentials. mapi_client.webhooks.verify(headers, body, secret) does a check of the Mapi-Signature of a delivery (Receiving webhooks). mapi_client.xrjson encodes and decodes inline payloads. The platform optimises budgets (Optimise a budget). Each operation in the endpoint table has a request builder. The tests of the client do a check of each builder against the contract.

v0.5. api.workflows.stream_events(run_id) follows the server-sent events of a workflow run. It gives these items:

  • WorkflowSnapshot: the run with all its nodes. It is the first item on each connection.
  • WorkflowEventFrame: workflow.node.*, workflow.branch.decided and other events. Its id is the seq of the event.
  • WorkflowEnd.

If the connection stops, the client continues with Last-Event-ID. It does not give an event two times.

The client accepts a workflow document as a WorkflowSpec, a mapping, YAML text or a file path (api.workflows.validate(Path("wf.yaml"))). upsert adds a revision only when the hash of the document changed. models.optimize sends a keyed Prefer: wait request again until the plan is ready. datasets.explore, models.explore and models.compare wait for the explore run. explorations.view(exploration, section) downloads one view.

catalog.recommend(goal=..., data_shape=[...]) does a check of the answers against the questions of the chooser before it sends them. The client does not send validations.decide (and approve, reject) again after a lost response. Reviewers sign in (mapi login), because an API token cannot approve. If a workflow run fails, wait and run(wait=True) raise the error of the node that failed. With raise_on_failure=False, they return the run.

  • AsyncClient has the same resources with await and async for.
  • List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor.
  • If a call accepts an Idempotency-Key and you do not give one, the client makes a new UUID. The client tries idempotent calls again after 502, 503, 504 and connection errors. It obeys Retry-After.
  • For 429 RATE_LIMITED, the client waits (Retry-After, then exponential back-off). Then it sends the request again, for all methods. This is safe because the server refused the request before it did an action. After RetryPolicy.rate_limit_retries attempts, the client raises RateLimited.
  • 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED raises QuotaExceeded immediately. retry_after_of(exc) gives the number of seconds until the quota resets (v0.3).
  • api.tokens.create returns the secret of the token one time (TokenCreated.secret). The secret is not in the repr. The client does not send the call again after a lost response. Thus it cannot make two tokens.
  • datasets.upload accepts a path, bytes or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). It makes the dataset if necessary. Then it PUTs the file to the signed URL and starts the ingest run. Then it waits until the version is ready. If a dataset has its raw schema in the mapi_schema attribute, the dataset keeps its dim policies and roles.
  • runs.stream_events gives RunSnapshot, RunEventFrame (persisted events, with an id), RunLiveFrame (live progress and log frames, without an id) and at the end RunEnd.
  • models.score sends Prefer: wait=N. While the run continues, the client sends the same request again with the same Idempotency-Key. The idempotent replay of the server returns the completed ScoreCallResult with new output links.
  • The client gets signed storage URLs without the Authorization header of the API. It does a check of each transfer against the CRC32C and size that the storage calculated.

Configuration. The client uses the first value that it finds in this sequence:

  1. Arguments.
  2. MAPI_URL (fallback MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN, MAPI_PROJECT and MAPI_PROFILE.
  3. A profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME).
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.

The client does not send a token over plain HTTP to a host that is not a loopback host. v0.2 has no authentication.

Credentials and project (v0.3). The client authenticates with an API token (argument, MAPI_TOKEN or the token of the profile). If there is no token, the client uses the OpenID Connect sign-in from mapi login. mapi login keeps this sign-in for the profile in credentials.json (mode 0600, next to the config file, or $MAPI_CREDENTIALS). The client uses a stored sign-in only for the API URL of that sign-in. The client renews the ID token with the refresh token a short time before it expires, and after a 401.

The client sends project (Client(project=…), MAPI_PROJECT, the project of the profile) as X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project>. It sends this header only on project-scoped requests. It does not send it on identity, tenant and operator routes, or when the path names the project.

File Mode Holds ~/.config/mapi/config.toml 0600 when mapi writes it Profiles: url, project, token, timeout, max_retries, verify, oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id, oidc_client_secret ~/.config/mapi/credentials.json 0600 For each profile: the API URL, issuer, client id, ID token, refresh token and expiry of a mapi login sign-in

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
mapi new geo-mmm -o spec.yaml --with-data   # template + tiny sample data (needs mapi-conformance)
mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip   # full static validation against installed plugins
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip \
    --side-table fx=fx.zarr.zip --side-table holidays=holidays.zarr.zip   # in-process fit
mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/geo-mmm --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip

mapi serve                                  # the local stack in one process (see below)
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --remote @   # upload, create/revise spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --state running | get RUN | logs RUN | watch RUN | cancel RUN | retry RUN
mapi datasets ls | upload file.csv --name sales --mapping mapping.yaml
mapi score request.yaml --remote @ --model MODEL_ID --version 1 -o result.zarr.zip
mapi catalog [models|steps|plots] [--remote @]

mapi plugin init acme-demand && mapi plugin test acme-demand   # scaffold + contract kit
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check
mapi config show | path | set KEY VALUE | unset KEY

Multi-tenant commands (v0.3). Authentication and Administration show these commands step by step. The test suite runs the two guides:

mapi login [--device | --no-browser | --with-token] [--issuer URL --client-id ID]
mapi whoami
mapi use [TENANT/PROJECT | --unset]          # --project / MAPI_PROJECT for one command
mapi logout [--revoke]
mapi tokens ls [--all] | get TOKEN | create NAME -s SCOPE... [--save] | revoke TOKEN
mapi usage [--period day|month] [--start DATE] [--group-by KEY] [--tenant TENANT]
mapi admin tenants ls | get | create | update     # operators; changes ask first (--yes)
mapi admin quotas ls | set SCOPE SUBJECT --LIMIT... | rm SCOPE SUBJECT
mapi admin kill-switches get | set --reason TEXT [--untrusted-code on|off] [--spend-cap N]
                                  [--cancel-untrusted-runs]  # with --untrusted-code off
mapi admin executors ls | get NAME | disable NAME --reason TEXT | enable NAME --reason TEXT
mapi admin audit [--tenant] [--action] [--since] ...
Command Notes login Browser sign-in: authorization code + PKCE (S256) with a loopback redirect to 127.0.0.1:<port>/callback. The CLI does a check of state and nonce. --device: the device authorization grant. --with-token: an API token from stdin. The CLI does a check of its checksum and verifies it with GET /v1/me. The CLI saves --url, --issuer and --client-id in the profile whoami GET /v1/me: the principal, how you signed in, the operator flag, and the tenants and projects with roles use Does a check of membership with GET /v1/me. If only one tenant has a bare project id, the CLI adds the tenant to it. The CLI saves project in the profile. A token acts only in its own project logout Removes the sign-in and token of the profile. It also revokes the refresh token at the identity provider. --revoke also revokes the token on the server tokens create Prints the secret one time, alone on stdout. With --save, the CLI keeps it in the profile. --json includes it, because you asked for it usage The exact cost (micro-units, with the name of the price table), vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds, groups, and the use and reset time of each quota runs get, runs ls Show the metered cost of the run (~ while it is an estimate) admin ... Each change prints a before/after table on stderr and asks you to confirm. --yes skips this step. quotas set replaces the full policy

Guided mode and integrations (v0.4). The command-line guide shows these commands step by step:

mapi endpoints ls | get ALIAS | history ALIAS | schema ALIAS [--example] | snippets ALIAS [-l LANG]
mapi endpoints promote ALIAS MODEL_REF [--override --reason TEXT] [--expected-revision N]
mapi endpoints rollback ALIAS --reason TEXT [--to-revision N]
mapi endpoints score ALIAS [CALL.json | --example] [--mode M] [--periods N] [--data FILE|REF] [-o OUT]
mapi webhooks ls | get ID | create URL -e EVENT... [--inactive] | rotate ID | deliveries ID [--status S]

mapi webhooks replay ID DELIVERY_ID | rm ID

mapi plots embed PLOT_ID [--expires-in-days N] [--allow-origin URL] | embeds PLOT_ID | revoke PLOT_ID EMBED_ID
mapi guided templates [ID] | detect ID (--csv FILE | --dataset REF) | draft ID --name N --dataset D ...
mapi priors preview --beliefs FILE (--spec ID --revision N | --document FILE) [--lift-tests FILE]
mapi signup --email E --name N [--accept-terms] | verify-email TOKEN
mapi tenant status | export [-o FILE] | delete [--confirm TENANT] [--cancel]
Command Notes endpoints promote, endpoints rollback Show the current version and ask you first (--yes skips this step). --override needs --reason webhooks create, webhooks rotate Print the signing secret one time, alone on stdout. rotate and rm ask you first webhooks update --enable turns on a webhook that is paused or that the server disabled. It also sets the failure count to zero. -e replaces the event list plots embed Prints the embed URL one time. The URL contains the token. revoke asks you first guided detect, guided draft --csv Profile the CSV file locally and send only summaries of the columns signup, verify-email Public calls. The CLI sends no credentials tenant delete Shows the data that the server purges and the data that it keeps. Then it asks you to type the tenant id (--confirm TENANT in scripts)

Workflows, governance, explorers and the chooser (v0.5). The command-line guide and the workflow cookbook show these commands step by step:

mapi workflows templates | template ID [--expert] | init ID [--name N] [--into PROJECT] [-o FILE] [--offline]
mapi workflows validate FILE | apply FILE [-m MSG] | create [FILE | --template ID] | ls [--archived]

mapi workflows watch RUN [--from N] | status RUN | runs WF [--status S] | nodes RUN | node RUN NODE
mapi workflows output RUN NODE PORT -o FILE | cancel RUN | nodes-catalog [--kind K] [--about ID]
mapi workflows schedules ls WF | add WF CRON [--tz TZ] [-i ...] [-p ...] | pause | resume | rm WF ID

mapi governance policies create FILE [--tenant T] | update ID FILE [--expected-version N] | retire ID

mapi validations ls [--queue | --status S] | get ID | evidence ID | cancel ID | resubmit ID
mapi validations deprecate ID --reason TEXT | pack ID -o evidence.html|evidence.json
mapi approve VALIDATION [--reject] [--comment TEXT] [--yes]
mapi explore dataset REF [-s SECTION]... [--kpi V] [--facet-by D] [--max-lag N] [-o DIR] [--show S]
mapi explore model REF [-s SECTION]... [--horizon N] [--compare-with REF] [-o DIR] [--show S]
mapi explore compare REF REF... [--horizon N] | get RUN

              [--frontier N] [--by-geo] [--request FILE]
