mapi about ID [--kind K] [--expert]
Command Notes workflows run --watch, workflows watch Shows a live board of the nodes. The SSE stream supplies the data. On a terminal, the CLI draws the board again for each change. Otherwise, it prints one line for each change. Then it prints the summary. The exit status is 1 if the run failed or was cancelled. --json: one JSON event on each line workflows apply Makes the workflow that metadata.name names, or saves the file as the next revision. If the file did not change, the CLI adds nothing workflows init Writes a gallery template as YAML with your name and project. --offline uses the templates that come with the CLI -i, -p name=value. If a -p value parses as JSON, the CLI uses it as JSON (-p 'horizons=[1,4]') validate model MODEL_REF is model://project/name@vN, name@vN, name with -v N, or a model id. The CLI waits for the checks. Then it prints each result with its plain message and suggested action. The exit status is 1 on checks_failed or rejected approve Shows the validation and asks you first (--yes skips this step). --reject needs --comment. The server refuses the submitter (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and API tokens governance policies retire, validations deprecate, workflows rm Ask you first (--yes skips this step) explore … Waits for the explore run. --out DIR writes each view as JSON. --show SECTION prints one view optimize Prints the plan (the current spend and the recommended spend, the return of the next unit, notes), the uplift and its probability, and the frontier choose Asks the questions of the chooser, or uses the -a answers and asks nothing. Then it prints the ranking with reasons, cautions and the top About cards

Run tracking (v0.11). Track metrics, params and tags shows these commands with examples:

mapi runs ls [--filter EXPR]... [--order-by REF] [--column REF]... [--tag K[=V]]... [--name TEXT] [--parent RUN]
mapi runs metrics RUN [--key KEY] [--points N]
mapi runs params RUN [--prefix TEXT]
mapi runs logs RUN [--stream user] [--level warning]
mapi runs log-metric RUN KEY VALUE [--step N] [--label K=V]...
mapi runs log-param RUN KEY VALUE [--text]
mapi runs tag RUN K=V... [--delete KEY]...
mapi runs rename RUN NAME
mapi runs note RUN (TEXT | -)
Command Notes runs ls --filter (-f, a maximum of 8) and --order-by use the search grammar, for example -f 'metric.rmse < 12'. Each --column (-c, a maximum of 16) adds a column to the table. The table has a name column runs metrics Without --key: one row for each series (key, labels, last, min, max, count). With --key: the downsampled points of that key (--points, the default is 1000) runs logs --level shows the lines at that level or higher (debug, info, warning, error). Lines without a level count as info runs log-param The CLI reads VALUE as a number, true or false when it can. --text keeps it as text runs log-metric, runs log-param, runs tag, runs rename, runs note Need the runner role (a token needs runs:write). runs note RUN - reads the note from stdin. runs rename RUN "" removes the name runs watch, fit --remote Show a maximum of one metrics line each 5 seconds (the newest values of a maximum of 4 series), one params line and one tags line when they change, and user log lines as [level] text. The stream only tells that the params or the tags changed. The CLI then reads them and shows the changed values

Errors: for QUOTA_EXCEEDED and RATE_LIMITED, the CLI prints when to try again (retry after 1h 30m). With --json, the error document contains retry_after_seconds. No command prints a token. Tokens show as mapi_<prefix>_….

Template (mapi new) What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Geo marketing-mix model on mmm-framework (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend + seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02
  • --remote @ means "the configured API". --remote URL overrides it for one command.
  • --json prints one JSON document on stdout. runs watch --json prints one JSON event on each line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1. Usage errors have exit status 2.
  • Local fit and score run plugins in the same process (isolation NONE). Use them only with code and data that you trust.
  • The CLI removes ANSI sequences, control sequences and bidi overrides from server, plugin and log text before it prints the text.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev. This command runs the database migrations. Then it runs the API and the orchestrator (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and event pump) in one process. If DATABASE_URL is not set, Postgres is the embedded pgserver. If nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, the command starts the GCS shim in the same process. Runs use the local-process executor with the real mapi-runner. To also run the web app, use make dev (Local development).

docs.title: Export the data of a science case study v0.9
docs.text:
mapi-plugin-science has its own command. It writes the dataset of a pymc-challenges case study to a file that you can upload (mapi datasets upload, or Datasets → New dataset in the web app). It is not a mapi command:

python -m mapi_plugin_science.export --list
python -m mapi_plugin_science.export CASE [--challenges DIR] [--out FILE] [--spec FILE] [--synthetic]
Option Default Meaning CASE — The case id, for example e07, e81 or e81b. Upper case is also correct --list — Print each case (model, dataset or tree, title, notebook, data files and the suggested dataset), then stop --challenges DIR $MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA The data/ directory of a local copy of pymc-challenges. A case without a data file (e51, e61) does not need it --out FILE <dataset>.nc The file to write. The suffix sets the format: .nc (NetCDF-4), .zarr.zip (a plain dataset) or .tree.zip (a tree dataset) --spec FILE — Also write the suggested spec (YAML). It reads dataset://<project>/<dataset>@latest --synthetic off Write the simulated data of the model. You do not need pymc-challenges

There are 16 cases: e07, e50, e60, e80, e51, e61, e58, e31, e77, e79, e18, e21, e19, e23, e81 (the wind directions at Santa Barbara airport) and e81b (the camera-trap times at Barro Colorado). The case table gives the model, the data files and the suggested dataset of each case.

The command prints the file that it wrote and the dataset name to use for the upload. The exit status is 0 on success and 1 if a data file is missing or the data is not correct. It is 2 for a usage error, for example an unknown case, or a case that needs data without --challenges and without --synthetic.

docs.title: GCS shim (local Cloud Storage)
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim is a local emulator of the parts of Google Cloud Storage that the platform uses. The local stack, the test suites and the runner use it instead of real GCS. It implements:

  • object generations and metagenerations, with generation preconditions
  • CRC32C and MD5 that the server calculates, in the GCS wire forms (base64)
  • V4 signed URLs: GET with HTTP Range, and PUT
  • V4 POST policies that limit uploads to a key prefix and a content-length-range
  • IAM-lite: tokens and keys for each principal, with role bindings for each bucket
  • a retention lock (write-once buckets) and lifecycle (delete after an age).

The control plane uses ShimObjectStore to communicate with the shim. ShimObjectStore implements the ObjectStore protocol from mapi_spec.storage. GcsObjectStore implements the same protocol on real GCS.

docs.title: Start the shim
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim                                   # serve .local/gcs on 127.0.0.1:4443
python -m mapi_gcs_shim --root .local/gcs --port 4443
mapi-gcs-shim init --root .local/gcs            # write config + key files, then exit
mapi-gcs-shim key exec --field token            # print the exec principal's bearer token

The defaults come from the local-dev variables:

  • MAPI_DATA_DIR: the root is $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs.
  • MAPI_ENV: the bucket names are mapi-{env}-*.
  • MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT: the host and the port.

--port 0 selects a free port. The server stops correctly on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Only one server can serve a root at a time. A lock file controls this.

docs.title: State on disk
docs.text:
Path Content _shim/config.json Buckets and principals, with their secrets. Mode 0600. _shim/keys/{principal}.json One key file for each principal: email, bearer token, HMAC secret and endpoint. Mode 0600. buckets/{bucket}/bucket.json The retention and lifecycle policies of the bucket. buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.json The metadata of the live generation, where h = sha256(object name). buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.{generation}.bin The bytes of the object. tmp/ The staging area for uploads.

An object name never becomes a filesystem path. The shim hashes the names. Bucket names must agree with the GCS bucket grammar. The shim rejects some names with 400: names with empty, . or .. segments, a leading / or control characters. This rule applies to the JSON API, the XML API and the key of a POST policy.

The shim writes data safely, also if it crashes:

  1. It streams the bytes into tmp/ and calculates the CRC32C and the MD5 during the stream.
  2. It renames the data file into its final location.
  3. It replaces the metadata sidecar atomically. This is the commit point.

When the shim starts, it deletes the staging files that stay from before. It also deletes all data files that it did not commit. The shim keeps only the live generation, as in a bucket without object versioning. Thus, if you read a superseded generation, the shim returns 404.

docs.title: Buckets and principals
docs.text:
By default, init makes the five buckets from the storage layout of the plan:

Bucket Policy mapi-{env}-quarantine Lifecycle: the shim deletes objects after 7 days. mapi-{env}-bootstrap Lifecycle: the shim deletes objects after 1 day. mapi-{env}-runs No policy. mapi-{env}-bundles Locked retention of about 100 years. Nobody can overwrite or delete objects, also not an admin. --bundle-retention-days N (default $MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS) locks it for N days instead, as the deployed bucket does (30). 0 sets no retention. Thus the tenant deletions of a test stack finish immediately. The shim uses this value when it makes the root. A root that exists keeps its policy. mapi-{env}-data No policy.

It also makes two principals:

Principal Bindings control (control@mapi-{env}.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/storage.admin on all buckets. The control plane and the finalizer use it. exec (exec@…) storage.objects.get and storage.objects.delete on the bootstrap bucket only. It cannot list that bucket. It has no access to the bundles bucket. Its token is the MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN of the local executor.

You can add principals and bindings to config.json. The predefined roles are:

  • roles/storage.admin
  • roles/storage.objectAdmin
  • roles/storage.objectUser
  • roles/storage.objectViewer
  • roles/storage.objectCreator
  • roles/storage.legacyBucketReader

A binding applies to one bucket, or to all buckets with "*".

The shim does a check of the permissions as follows:

  • JSON-API calls: the shim uses the bearer token of the caller. If the token is missing or unknown, the shim returns 401. If a permission is missing, it returns 403.
  • Signed URLs and POST policies: these have the authority of the signer. The shim does the check when a client uses the URL. The shim refuses a URL that exec signed for the runs bucket.
  • Overwrite of an object that exists: this also needs storage.objects.delete, as in GCS.

docs.title: JSON API
docs.text:
All JSON-API requests need Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Method and path Operation GET /storage/v1/b List buckets. Needs storage.buckets.list. POST /storage/v1/b Make a bucket. The body can set retentionPolicy and lifecycle (Delete with an age condition). GET or DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket} Get a bucket, or delete it if it is empty. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o List objects. Accepts prefix, delimiter, pageToken, maxResults, startOffset and endOffset. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Get metadata. With alt=media, it returns the content. With Range, it returns 206. PATCH /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Update contentType or metadata. This increases metageneration. DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Delete an object. Accepts generation. POST /storage/v1/b/{b}/o/{o}/rewriteTo/b/{b2}/o/{o2} Server-side copy. Also available as copyTo. Accepts sourceGeneration. POST /upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o Upload with uploadType=media or multipart. Resumable uploads return 501. GET /download/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Download the content.

All object operations accept the preconditions ifGenerationMatch, ifGenerationNotMatch, ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch. A rewrite also accepts the ifSource… forms.

  • On writes, a failed precondition returns 412.
  • On reads, a failed …NotMatch returns 304.
  • ifGenerationMatch=0 means "the object must not exist yet".

Errors use the GCS JSON shape: {"error": {"code", "message", "errors": [{"reason"}]}}.

docs.title: Signed URLs (XML style)
docs.text:
Method and path Operation GET /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Download. With Range, it returns 206 with Content-Range. If the shim cannot satisfy the range, it returns 416. PUT /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Upload. POST /{bucket} (multipart/form-data) Upload through a V4 POST policy. The file field must be the last field.

The signature uses GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 with an HMAC key for each principal:

  • Canonical request: the method, the path, all query parameters except X-Goog-Signature, the signed headers (always with host) and UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD.
  • Signed values: X-Goog-Expires (maximum 7 days) and X-Goog-Date. The expiry is strict. But X-Goog-Date can be a maximum of 5 minutes in the future, because clocks can have small differences.
  • Bound to the signature: the method, the path, the host, the query (for example generation) and the values of the signed headers. If you change one of them, the shim returns 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.
  • Unsigned headers: an x-goog-* header that is not signed returns 400. The exception is x-goog-hash.
  • Expiry: a URL that expired returns 400 ExpiredToken.

Signed GET URLs from sign_get are pinned to a generation. If a client overwrites the object, the URL returns 404. The URL never serves the new bytes without an error.

Signed PUT URLs from sign_put sign these headers. The uploader must send them with no change:

  • content-type
  • x-goog-if-generation-match: 0. Thus the object is write-once by default.
  • x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max>.

The uploader can also send Content-MD5 or x-goog-hash: crc32c=…,md5=…. If a value does not agree, the shim returns 400 BadDigest and keeps nothing.

POST policies from post_policy are a base64 JSON document of conditions. They have an HMAC signature on the document. The conditions are:

  • {"bucket": …}
  • ["starts-with", "$key", prefix]
  • ["starts-with", "$content-type", ""]
  • ["content-length-range", min, max]
  • the x-goog-* credential fields
  • with create_only=True, {"x-goog-if-generation-match": "0"} (the client also sends it as a form field).

When a client uses the policy, the shim enforces these rules:

  • The signature and the expiration must be valid.
  • All conditions must be true.
  • A condition must cover each form field. The exceptions are x-goog-signature, policy, file and x-ignore-*.
  • The size must be in the range. The shim rejects a body that is too large during the stream.
  • An x-goog-if-generation-match form field is a precondition. Thus a create-only policy returns 412 for a key that exists. This occurs also if the signer has permission to delete.

Real GCS does not accept a generation precondition in a POST form. Thus GcsObjectStore signs create-only policies with uploader_credentials instead. This is a principal without storage.objects.delete, which GCS needs for an overwrite.

success_action_status (200, 201 with an XML PostResponse, or 204 by default) and ${filename} in key operate as in GCS.

docs.title: Shim-only endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /_shim/healthz: no authentication.
  • POST /_shim/v1/lifecycle:sweep?now=<iso>: needs shim.admin. It applies the lifecycle rules now. It never deletes objects that have retention.

The server also applies the lifecycle rules at each --sweep-interval seconds. The default is 300.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta
from mapi_gcs_shim import ShimObjectStore

async with ShimObjectStore.from_root(".local/gcs", "control") as store:
    meta = await store.put("mapi-local-runs", "t/default/runs/r1/a1/x.json", b"{}",
                           content_type="application/json", if_generation_match=0)
    url = await store.sign_get("mapi-local-runs", meta.name, expires_in=timedelta(minutes=15))

ShimObjectStore has three constructors:

  • ShimObjectStore(endpoint, credentials, public_endpoint=None). public_endpoint is the host that the shim writes into signed URLs. Thus a sandbox can get access to the shim with a different name. The host is signed.
  • .from_root(root, principal).
  • .from_local_dev(LocalDev).

It has the protocol methods. It also has create_bucket, get_bucket and sweep_lifecycle. Errors map to NotFound, PreconditionFailed, AccessDenied, InvalidRange and StorageError:

  • get(max_bytes=…) raises PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE before it reads the body.
  • A full read with a CRC32C that does not agree raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

mapi_gcs_shim.transfer has helpers for a client that has a URL:

  • download_signed
  • upload_signed_put
  • upload_post_policy.

They use only GCS XML semantics. Thus they also operate with real GCS.

docs.title: Real Cloud Storage
docs.text:
GcsObjectStore (install mapi-gcs-shim[gcp]) implements the same protocol with google-cloud-storage. The tests use only a fake client. Nobody tested it with live GCP.

  • Signatures. If you give a BlobSigner (blob_signer=), mapi_gcs_shim.gcs_signing makes the signed GET/PUT URLs and the POST policies. It uses GOOG4-RSA-SHA256, and the result is byte-identical to the V4 signer of the library. Only the string to sign goes to the signer. IamSignBlobSigner signs with the IAM Credentials signBlob API. It uses a token provider that refreshes the token (google_token_provider()), and it retries on 429/5xx. GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run(service_account_email=..., uploader_service_account_email=...) connects the two accounts. The control account signs URLs. The uploader account (create, but no delete) signs create-only POST policies.
  • Integrity. If the CRC32C, MD5 or size that the server calculates is different from the bytes that it got, the store deletes that write (that generation only). Then it raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE. A copy pins the source generation (ifSourceGenerationMatch). It compares the size and the CRC32C of the destination with the source.
  • Preconditions. Signed GETs are pinned to a generation. Signed PUTs have a signed x-goog-if-generation-match (0, write-once, by default). put, copy and delete send if_generation_match to GCS.

docs.title: pytest fixtures
docs.text:
The package registers a pytest11 plugin. Thus all workspace tests can use these fixtures:

async def test_something(gcs_shim):            # a fresh shim per test, on a free port
    async with gcs_shim.store() as store:       # the control principal; store("exec") also works
        await store.put(gcs_shim.buckets.runs, "t/default/x", b"...")
    headers = gcs_shim.auth_headers("exec")     # for raw httpx calls

gcs_shim_session gives one shim for the full session. To use the shim outside pytest, use ShimServer(root). It is a context manager that runs the shim on a background thread.

docs.title: Differences from real GCS
docs.text:
• There is no object versioning. The shim keeps only the live generation.
  • The shim does not implement resumable uploads (uploadType=resumable). Use media or multipart uploads, or a signed PUT.
  • The signatures use HMAC keys (GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256), not the RSA keys of a service account (GOOG4-RSA-SHA256). GcsObjectStore signs RSA URLs itself through a BlobSigner (IAM signBlob on Cloud Run). If it has no BlobSigner, it uses the signatures of the library.
  • There are no ACLs, CMEK, storage classes, notifications or bucket PATCH. You set bucket policies when you make the bucket, or in config.json.
  • A signed URL is valid only for the method that it was signed for. A HEAD request needs its own signature, as in GCS.

docs.title: HTTP API (v1) v0.2
docs.text:
This page describes the platform API of v0.2 (milestone M1, the local vertical slice). Each request body and each response body is a Pydantic model in mapi_spec.api. The server serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document that it makes from those models. Each model has examples. The endpoint table on this page agrees with mapi_spec.api.M1_ENDPOINTS. If the two are different, a test fails.

See also OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, which you can browse, with all schemas and examples (full screen) HTTP API guide The main flow with curl and jq: upload, validate, fit, follow, score Python client The same flow with mapi_client

M1 is single-tenant

A local installation has one tenant and one project. Their names are default. Each resource has a tenant_id and a project_id, and each storage key starts with t/{tenant}/. Thus, the multi-tenancy of v0.3 adds row-level security and does not change the schema. M1 has no authentication. The API listens only on 127.0.0.1. Multi-tenant API describes the tenants, sign-in, tokens and quotas that v0.3 adds.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Topic Rule Base URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 locally. Resource paths start with /v1. Bodies application/json (UTF-8). The spec text is a string field (yaml) in the JSON. Unknown fields Request bodies reject unknown fields (SCHEMA_INVALID). Clients ignore unknown response fields. Thus, the server can add fields and not make a new version. Timestamps RFC 3339, with a timezone, in UTC (2026-10-15T09:30:00Z). Ids <prefix>_<26 lowercase Crockford base32>, with the ULID layout. You can sort them by the time of creation (run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0). The prefixes are ds, upl, spc, run, mdl and mv. Projects and tenants use slugs (default). Durations "45m", "1h30m", "90s". Actions Actions that are not CRUD use a colon suffix: POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel. Untrusted text Log lines, tracebacks and plugin messages occur only in untrusted_text or LogLine.line. Render them as text. Do not render them as HTML or markdown.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Each error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json, model mapi_spec.Problem). It has a stable code:

{
  "type": "urn:mapi:error:LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "title": "A stateful step runs before the split",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "detail": "validation failed with 1 error; first at /pipeline/2: …",
  "errors": [
    {"code": "LEAKAGE_RISK", "severity": "error", "pointer": "/pipeline/2",
     "message": "stateful step 'scale_y' runs before the split"}
  ]
}
  • Incorrect request bodies, path parameters and query parameters return 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. Each problem goes in errors[], with an RFC 6901 pointer into the request (/body/kind, /query/limit).
  • All endpoints can also return RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500) and INFRA_ERROR (503). The table does not show these codes again.
  • Error codes has the full list of codes and their HTTP statuses.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
List endpoints return Page[T]:

{"items": [ … ], "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6InJ1bl8wMWphZiJ9"}
  • To get the next page, send ?limit= (default 50, maximum 200) and ?cursor=<next_cursor>. A null cursor tells you that the current page is the last page.
  • Cursors are opaque. A cursor is valid only for the same list and the same filters.
  • The items are in order of id, with the newest item first.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
POST /v1/runs, …:score, …:retry, …:dry-run and POST …/versions (ingest) accept an Idempotency-Key header. The key has 1–255 printable ASCII characters. Its scope is the project, and the server keeps it for 24 hours:

Situation Response First request with the key The usual response, for example 201 Created with the Run Same key, same body (the bytes are equal after canonical JSON) 200 OK with the resource that the first request made. The server does not make a second run. Same key, different body 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT Same key while the first request is in progress 409 CONFLICT. Try again later.

Clients must make one key for each user intent, for example a UUIDv4 when the user clicks Fit. They must use that key again on each network retry.

docs.title: Long-running work and Prefer: wait
docs.text:
Runs are asynchronous. When you make a run, the response gives the Run immediately, in the state created or queued. POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score also obeys the RFC 7240 header Prefer: wait=N. The maximum value of N is 60 seconds:

  • If the score run gets to a terminal state in N seconds, the response is 200 with ScoreCallResult{done: true, run, outputs: [ArtifactLink…]}.
  • If not, the response is 202 with done: false and the run. Follow the run with GET /v1/runs/{run_id} or with its event stream.
  • The response header Preference-Applied: wait=N gives the wait time that the server used.

docs.title: Forecasts with actuals
docs.text:
A forecast request (on a model version or on an endpoint) can send actuals. Actuals are target values for periods after the fit, or new values for the last periods of the fit. The request can also send the periods to forecast, with an empty target. The model uses its fitted parameters to update its state with the actuals. Then it forecasts from the last actual. The model does not estimate its parameters again. Forecasts with actuals gives the rules, the plugin hook and examples.

  • The model forecasts exactly the periods after the last actual that have an empty target. When the payload ends with an actual, the model adds horizon.periods periods after it.
  • ScoreCallResult.summary.conditioning (ForecastConditioning) tells what the model used to condition each forecast. It has fit_end, conditioned, n_actuals, actuals_through, revised, horizon_source (rows or horizon), details for each series and a plain message.
  • A model without capabilities.conditions_on_actuals refuses actuals with 422 ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. The suggested action is to fit again with the new data, or to keep the target empty.
  • Gaps that the model cannot filter, and actuals without their drivers, give 422 ACTUALS_INVALID.
  • EndpointSchema.actuals_example is a forecast call that you can use immediately. It has inline data for the periods after the fit, and all values are empty. Endpoints have this example only when their model conditions on actuals.

docs.title: Run events (server-sent events)
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events has two representations:

  • Accept: text/event-stream: a live SSE stream.
  • All other Accept values: a JSON Page[RunEventView] of the persisted events. To read the events after a given id, send ?after=<id>.

The stream sends these frames, in this order:

  1. event: snapshot with the full Run JSON. It is the first frame on each connection. It has no id:.
  2. A replay of the persisted events that have an id greater than the request header Last-Event-ID. If the request has no header, the replay starts from the start. Each replayed frame has id: <RunEventView.id>. The ids increase for each run. Thus, a client that connects again continues exactly where it stopped. This is also true after the 60-minute request limit on Cloud Run.
  3. Live frames when the events occur: state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete and error. The data: of each frame is one line of compact JSON (RunEventView). From v0.11, the stream also sends tracking frames (see Run tracking).
  4. event: end when the run is terminal (data: the final Run). Then the server closes the stream. A client that gets end must not connect again.

When the state, the name or the note of the run changes, the server also sends a new event: snapshot (no id:). Thus, a client can show the latest Run again and does not have to assemble it from events. The server does not persist progress and log frames. It sends them live without an id: (data: {run_id, attempt, seq, ts, type, payload}) and does not replay them. Last-Event-ID applies only to persisted events. From v0.11, the payload of a log frame also has level and fields when the line has stream user.

Between events, the server writes a heartbeat comment (: keepalive) each 15 seconds. The first frame also has retry: 3000.

An open stream does a check of the credential of its caller again each minute (MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S). The server closes the stream without end in these conditions:

  • The token is revoked or expired.
  • The session has ended.
  • The caller does not have access to the project now.

Then the new connection gets 401 or 403. Clients must stop at that point and not try again.

The server combines progress frames into a maximum of one frame each 2–5 seconds. The server persists only state changes, warnings, diagnostics, checkpoints, metrics and terminal events. Only these events can replay. A client that connects again gets the latest progress from the snapshot frame. To get the log lines in pages, use GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs.

retry: 3000
event: snapshot
data: {"id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"running", …}

id: 17
event: state
data: {"id":17,"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","attempt":1,"seq":3,"type":"state", …}

: keepalive

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: The columns: Request and Response are DTO names in mapi_spec.api, but some are catalog or plot models from mapi_spec. Errors lists the codes that are special to the endpoint. This table does not show the common codes from the Errors section again.

docs.title: Health
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /healthz The process is live — Health 200 — GET /readyz The API can connect to Postgres and the object store. If not, it sends 503 with the same body — Health 200 —

docs.title: Projects and catalog
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/projects List the projects — Page[Project] 200 — GET /v1/projects/{project_id} Get a project — Project 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/catalog The full catalog with its digest — CatalogResponse 200 — GET /v1/catalog/models Model plugins — Page[ModelCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/catalog/models/{model_id}/{version} One plugin version (manifest, sanitized schemas, schema template) — ModelCatalogEntry 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/catalog/steps Steps — Page[StepCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/catalog/plots Plot recipes — Page[PlotCatalogEntry] 200 — GET /v1/catalog/plots/{plot_id}/{version}/example The recipe drawn on synthetic example data (datasets inline), made by the describe run — PlotSpec 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/schemas/{name} An exported JSON Schema, for example modelspec.json. Monaco and JSON Forms use it — JSON Schema 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Data goes into the platform in three steps:

  1. Create the dataset.
  2. PUT the file to the signed URL from an upload session. The URL points into the quarantine bucket. The API does not see the bytes.
  3. Create a version. A sandboxed ingest run parses the upload and validates it. Then it writes the content-addressed data.zarr.zip with its schema, profile and preview.
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/datasets Create a dataset DatasetCreate Dataset 201 CONFLICT (the name is in use) GET /v1/datasets List the datasets — Page[Dataset] 200 — GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id} Get a dataset — Dataset 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads Get a signed PUT URL into quarantine UploadCreate UploadSession 201 NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions Ingest an upload as a new version. This starts an ingest run. From v0.8, assembly makes one version from several uploads (tree datasets). From v0.15, collection makes an image collection. Accepts Idempotency-Key. DatasetVersionCreate DatasetVersion (status ingesting) 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the upload is not complete, or a version already uses it), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (the uploads of an assembly are larger than 5 GB together) GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions List the versions — Page[DatasetVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version} Schema, summary, and references to the profile and the preview — DatasetVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for data.zarr.zip, schema.json, profile.json or preview.json. A tree version (v0.8) has data.tree.zip and tree_schema.json — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Specs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/specs:validate Synchronous static validation. It returns all issues at one time with JSON pointers. It also returns the schema at each pipeline stage. ValidateRequest ValidateResponse 200 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID POST /v1/specs Create a spec and its revision 1 SpecCreate SpecDoc 201 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT GET /v1/specs List the specs — Page[SpecDoc] 200 — GET /v1/specs/{spec_id} Get a spec with its latest revision — SpecDoc 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions Add an immutable revision SpecRevisionCreate SpecRevision 201 NOT_FOUND, SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (the parent_revision is not the latest) GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions List the revisions — Page[SpecRevision] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision} Get one revision — SpecRevision 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision}:dry-run An explicit sandboxed dry run. It is the same as POST /v1/runs with kind: validate. Accepts Idempotency-Key. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, QUOTA_EXCEEDED

How validation gives its results:

  • POST /v1/specs:validate returns 200 also when the document is not valid. The result is in ValidateResponse.valid and issues.
  • The API uses the statuses that are not 2xx only for requests that it cannot validate. These are YAML that it cannot parse, a document that is too large, and a request body that is not correct.
  • When you create a spec or a revision, the API also stores revisions that are not valid. They have valid: false and their issues. Thus, the editor can save work that is not complete.
  • POST /v1/runs refuses revisions that are not valid. It uses the code of the first error. Examples: LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/runs Submit a run. It returns 200 on an idempotent replay. Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunCreate Run 201 NOT_FOUND, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED GET /v1/runs List the runs. Filters: kind, state, spec_id. From v0.11 also parent_run_id, name, tag, filter, order_by and column (see Search runs) — Page[Run] 200 SCHEMA_INVALID (a filter, order_by or column value that is not correct) GET /v1/runs/{run_id} Get a run: state, failure class and problem, attempt, progress snapshot and cost. The cost has placeholders in v0.2. From v0.3, the platform meters it — Run 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events An SSE stream or a JSON page of the persisted events (see Run events). Accepts Last-Event-ID. — Page[RunEventView] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs The captured log lines. Filters: attempt, stream and, from v0.11, level (the minimum level) and include_user (see Log levels) — Page[LogLine] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots The plots that a run rendered (plots.json: forecast fans, counterfactual bands, classifier plots). The response comes from the newest attempt that has a verified plots.json. Thus succeeded and partial runs have plots, and so do failed or cancelled runs with an earlier partial attempt that wrote plots (v0.10). The plot sanitizer does a check of them at each read. The response does not include rejected plots. The list is empty while no attempt has plots, for example while the run is active. — Page[PlotSpec] 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel Request cancellation. It is idempotent. It returns the run in cancelling, or in its terminal state if the run is already complete. The API does not change a finalizing run and returns it as it is, because its execution is already complete. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:resume Resume a partial run from its checkpoints (new attempt) — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the run is not partial) POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:retry Start a new run from a failed run. For example, use the next larger resource class after RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunRetry Run 201 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the run did not fail, or it is a workflow, workflow node or governance run. For these, start the workflow again or submit the validation again)

The fields that RunCreate needs change with kind:

kind Required Not permitted fit, validate (sandboxed dry run) spec_id, revision model_version_id, request score model_version_id, request (a ScoreRequest document) spec_id, revision evaluate, derive, render model_version_id (params is optional) spec_id, revision, request

POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions creates the ingest runs. In v0.2, you cannot create describe runs, optimize runs or the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign). Run protocol lists the run states and the transitions between them.

docs.title: Models and scoring
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/models List the models — Page[Model] 200 — GET /v1/models/{model_id} Get a model — Model 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions List the versions — Page[ModelVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version} Signed bundle manifest, diagnostics, scorecard, lineage, metrics — ModelVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for a bundle object or a ui/… view. name can contain / — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score Score with replayed preprocessing. Accepts Prefer: wait=N (200 if the run is complete, if not 202) and Idempotency-Key. inline holds data/scenario that you type in (XrJSON, maximum 5 MB each). The API does a check of them against the inputs of the version. ScoreCall ScoreCallResult 200 NOT_FOUND, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED, ACTUALS_INVALID, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/inputs The data that a score call can send. This is the input contract (canonical names, variables that the future needs, fitted coordinates) and the input table. Use ?periods=N (1-200) for the number of periods after the fit — ModelInputSchema 200 NOT_FOUND, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED

Score summaries. When a score run succeeds, ScoreCallResult.summary (ScoreSummary) holds the requested summary as plain tables (the summary.json of the run). Each ScoreSummaryTable has the coordinate columns (one for each dim), then one column for each statistic. dims names the coordinate columns, and time_dim names the dim that is time when there is one. A server that predates these two fields leaves them out. The tables are in the order of their size. If the summary has more than 100 000 cells, truncated is true. Use the score.zarr.zip output for all the values. From v0.9, the table of a circular output (OutputDecl.circular, for example a direction) has the field period (one turn, in the units of the output). The statistics are then on the circle:

  • mean is the circular mean, and the intervals are centred on it.
  • The mean, the median, the quantiles and the interval bounds are in [0, period). An interval with lower more than upper crosses the seam (from 350 to 10 degrees).
  • sd is the circular standard deviation.

Other tables do not have the field. Refer to Circular outputs.

A score call needs data. If the request has no data, no inline values, no scenario and no horizon, the API refuses it with 422 SCHEMA_INVALID at /data ("the score request has no data"). A mode that the model does not support gives 422 MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED.

The API makes artifact links only after two checks are satisfactory:

  1. The authorization check.
  2. The verification of the signed bundle manifest of the model version. The tenant, model version, digests and object generations must all agree.

If the second check fails, the response is INTEGRITY_FAILURE and the API gives no URL. Each link is pinned to an object generation. It expires after 15 minutes. It supports HTTP Range requests.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/plots The plots of a model version — Page[PlotListItem] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/plots/{plot_id} A sanitized PlotSpec. Render it only in the plot-sandbox iframe, which has its own origin. — PlotSpec 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/plots:validate Run the server-side plot sanitizer on a spec that a user wrote PlotSpec PlotValidateResponse 200 SCHEMA_INVALID

docs.title: Multi-tenant API v0.3
docs.text:
v0.3 (milestone M2) adds tenants, projects, members, API tokens, quotas, cost and an operator console. The models are in these modules:

  • mapi_spec.api
  • mapi_spec.tenancy
  • mapi_spec.tokens
  • mapi_spec.quotas
  • mapi_spec.cost
  • mapi_spec.audit
  • mapi_spec.admin
  • mapi_spec.auth

The endpoint table below agrees with mapi_spec.api.M2_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives each operation its scope and the permission that it checks. This includes the v0.2 operations. If the code, this page and the server are different, tests fail. Tenancy and authentication explains roles, tokens and scopes. Quotas and cost explains limits and prices.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Caller Credential Notes Browser (the web app) Session cookie __Host-mapi_session (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/). GET /auth/callback sets it OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce. The API runs the flow as a backend-for-frontend. The browser does not hold an OAuth token. Programs, SDKs, CLI Authorization: Bearer mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum> An API token. It acts as its owner, with only its scopes, in the one project that it is bound to. Google Pub/Sub A Google-signed OIDC ID token on POST /internal/events The API does a check of the audience, the issuer and the push service account. No data in the body gives authentication.

Responses for authentication and authorization:

Situation Response No credential, or an expired session, on a route that is not public 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A token that is not correctly formed, or a token with a bad checksum 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. The API does not show the value in the response. A revoked or expired token 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A resource in a project or tenant that the caller cannot see 404 NOT_FOUND, the same as for a resource that does not exist. Thus, callers cannot find ids by tests The caller can see the resource, but the role or the token scopes do not permit the action 403 FORBIDDEN A token used outside the project that it is bound to 403 FORBIDDEN The tenant is suspended Reads work. All other requests return 403 FORBIDDEN.

docs.title: Selecting the project
docs.text:
Each v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) is part of a project. From v0.3, a request identifies its project in one of these ways. The list order is the order of precedence:

  1. Path parameters, on routes under /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}.
  2. The X-Mapi-Project header: X-Mapi-Project: <tenant_id>/<project_id>, for example X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth. The API also accepts only the project, for example X-Mapi-Project: growth, when the tenant is clear. This is when the caller is a member of one tenant, or uses a token.
  3. The token binding. A token always acts in its own project. Thus, token clients do not have to send the header. A header that identifies a different project returns 403 FORBIDDEN.
  4. The deployment default, only in the single-tenant local profile (default/default, as in v0.2).

If no rule applies, or the path and the header are different, the request fails with 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope implements these rules.

The scope of each v0.2 endpoint (by operation id) and the permission that the API checks:

Scope Operations Permission Public health, ready, get_schema None Authenticated list_projects, get_catalog, list_catalog_models, get_catalog_model, list_catalog_steps, list_catalog_plots All signed-in callers. The lists show only what the caller can see. Project get_project read project Project create_dataset / create_upload, create_dataset_version create / update dataset (editor) Project list_datasets, get_dataset, list_dataset_versions, get_dataset_version, get_dataset_artifact read dataset Project validate_spec, list_specs, get_spec, list_spec_revisions, get_spec_revision read spec Project create_spec / create_spec_revision create / update spec (editor) Project create_run, dry_run_spec, resume_run, retry_run create run (runner). Runs on a model version also need run model. Project cancel_run cancel run (runner) Project list_runs, get_run, run_events, run_logs, list_run_plots read run Project list_run_metrics, get_metric_history, list_run_params (v0.11) read run Project update_run, log_run_metrics, log_run_params (v0.11) update run (runner). A token needs the runs:write scope. Project list_models, get_model, list_model_versions, get_model_version, get_model_artifact read model Project score_model run model (runner) Project list_plots, get_plot, validate_plot read plot

In v0.2, the storage keys and rows already had the tenant and the project (t/{tenant}/…). Thus, the change needs no data migration. Postgres enforces the boundary with row-level security on tenant_id in all tables.

docs.title: Identity, tenants and projects
docs.text: Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/me The caller (Principal), with their tenants, projects and roles. For a token, the response also includes the token — Me 200 UNAUTHENTICATED GET /v1/tenants The tenants that the caller is a member of — Page[Tenant] 200 — GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Get a tenant — Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Change the name of a tenant (tenant admin) TenantUpdate Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects The projects of the tenant that the caller can see — Page[Project] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects Create a project (tenant admin) ProjectCreate Project 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (the id is in use) PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Change the name or the description of a project (project admin) ProjectUpdate Project 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Delete an empty project (tenant admin) — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (the project still has data)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
A membership gives one role. A tenant-wide membership gives the role on the tenant and on all projects in it. A project membership gives the role only on that project. The effective role in a project is the higher of the two. Add a member by principal_id. To invite a person who did not sign in before, add the member by email. At the first sign-in with that verified e-mail, the person gets the invitation. If you remove or demote the last admin, the API returns 409 CONFLICT.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members Tenant-wide members — Page[Membership] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members Give a tenant-wide role (tenant admin) MembershipCreate Membership 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members/{principal_id} Change a tenant-wide role MembershipUpdate Membership 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/members/{principal_id} Remove a tenant-wide role — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members Project members, with the tenant-wide grants — Page[Membership] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members Give a project role (project admin) MembershipCreate Membership 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members/{principal_id} Change a project role MembershipUpdate Membership 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}/members/{principal_id} Remove a project role — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Tokens are part of the project that X-Mapi-Project selects. POST /v1/tokens returns the full token one time, in TokenCreated.secret. The API cannot show it again. Lists show the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_…. Each member can mint, list and revoke their own tokens. To list the tokens of all members (?all=true) or to revoke the token of a different person, you need manage on token (project admin).

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/tokens The tokens of the caller. Filters: all, status — Page[ApiToken] 200 — POST /v1/tokens Mint a token with scopes and an expiry.   • price_version identifies the price table that the platform used.

docs.title: Browser session (backend-for-frontend)
docs.text:
These routes have no version. They are at the root, next to the web app.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /auth/login Start the sign-in. It redirects to the identity provider with response_type=code, a PKCE code_challenge (S256), state and nonce. ?return_to= must be a path on the same origin. If it is not, the API uses /. — — 302 — GET /auth/callback Do a check of state. Exchange the code with the PKCE verifier. Verify the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry). Set the session cookie and redirect to return_to — — 302 UNAUTHENTICATED POST /auth/logout End the session and clear the cookies. It works without a valid session. With a valid session, it needs X-CSRF-Token. — — 204 — GET /auth/session Tells if the browser is signed in, the identity, and the expiry time. authenticated: false is a 200, not a 401. — SessionInfo 200 —

The server keeps the login transaction (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) for 10 minutes. A __Host-mapi_login cookie with SameSite=Lax refers to it. The cookie uses this setting because the redirect back from the identity provider is a cross-site navigation, and that navigation does not send a Strict cookie. Sessions expire after 2 hours with no activity or after 12 hours in total. Each API route that changes state accepts only JSON. A cross-site form cannot send JSON without a CORS preflight. The session cookie is SameSite=Strict, thus cross-site requests never send it.

Also, each cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE must send the CSRF token of the session in an X-CSRF-Token header. This includes POST /auth/logout when a session is live. The API refuses the request (403 FORBIDDEN) in these conditions:

  • Its Origin is not the web app or the API.
  • It has Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site.

The web app reads the token from the __Host-mapi_csrf cookie (readable, SameSite=Strict) or from the X-CSRF-Token header of GET /auth/session. Requests with an API token do not need a CSRF token.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /internal/events Pub/Sub push of run events from the Cloud Logging sink PubSubPushEnvelope Ingest result 200 UNAUTHENTICATED, SCHEMA_INVALID

The push envelope is {message: {data, attributes, messageId, publishTime}, subscription, deliveryAttempt}. message.data is a base64 Cloud Logging entry. Its jsonPayload.mapi_event is one HMAC-signed run event (see Run protocol). The request must have Authorization: Bearer <Google-signed ID token>. After the server verifies the signature, it does a check of the claims with mapi_spec.auth.check_push_claims:

  • The issuer is https://accounts.google.com.
  • The audience is the configured audience.
  • The verified e-mail is the e-mail of the push service account.
  • The token is not expired.

If an event fails its HMAC, the server acknowledges it with 200, because a new delivery cannot help. The server records it in the audit log as event.rejected.

docs.title: Quotas and rate limits on every endpoint
docs.text:
The platform does a check of requests and submissions against three levels of quota: token, tenant and global (see Quotas and cost).

  • If a request goes above a requests-per-minute limit, the API returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header. Try again after that number of seconds.
  • If a submission goes above a compute, concurrency, fan-out, resource-class, storage or egress limit, the API returns 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The API sets Retry-After when the limit resets with a window (the UTC day or month). The detail of the problem gives the level and the limit.
  • The platform kill switches (uploaded code paused, global spend cap reached) also return QUOTA_EXCEEDED, at the global level.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
v0.4 (milestone M3) adds the contracts for Guided mode and for the connection of other applications. These contracts are:

  • Guided templates and drafts.
  • Business priors and lift tests.
  • What-if scenarios.
  • Endpoints and aliases.
  • Code snippets.
  • Webhooks.
  • Saved and rendered plots, with embed links.
  • The trust lifecycle (sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and export).

The endpoint table agrees with mapi_spec.api.M3_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives the scope and the permission of each operation. mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the full v0.4 surface (M1, M2 and M3). The route-table test of the server makes sure that the server serves each row. Guided mode and Integrations explain the ideas.

Project-scoped M3 routes get the project from X-Mapi-Project, as all v0.3 routes do.

docs.title: Guided mode
docs.text:
GET /v1/guided/templates lists the built-in templates (GuidedTemplate). Each template has these items:

  • Questions in plain language.
  • The built-in plugin that the questions are for.
  • A ModelSpec template with {{placeholder}} strings.
  • Default settings.
  • The scorecard checks that apply.
  • x-ui-level hints.

Role detection (POST /v1/guided/detect-roles) ranks the columns of an upload for each question. It uses ColumnProfiles that the browser calculates. It can also use a stored dataset version: the columns.json of its ingest, or else its schema and summary. It returns RoleSuggestions. Each candidate has a confidence and a reason_plain.

A draft (POST /v1/guided/drafts) changes GuidedAnswers into an IngestMapping for the upload, a ModelSpec document and its YAML ("View as YAML"). It does not store anything. The findings of the static validator are in issues. To save the draft, use POST /v1/specs.

A sandboxed translate_priors run changes business priors into model-space priors (PriorTranslationRequest → PriorTranslation). The result of the translation is a PriorTranslationResult, with a prior-predictive preview in business units.

POST /v1/guided/requests:compile changes a what-if scenario, a forecast or an intervention preset (GuidedCompile) into the equivalent ScoreRequest. Thus, "Run exact" sends a real score run.

The persona lock is Project.guided_locked. To change it, use PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} (ProjectUpdate.guided_locked). In a locked project, members below admin get 403 FORBIDDEN from POST /v1/specs and POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions. The only exception is Guided specs that keep the advanced and hidden fields of their template.

This release serves the templates, role detection, drafts and the lock (see From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft).

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text:
An endpoint is a stable alias (endpoint://<project>/<alias>) for one model version. PUT promotes a version. The promotion gate (PromotionGateDecision) does a check of the scorecard:

  • If the scorecard passes, the gate permits the promotion.
  • If the scorecard has a warning, the gate asks for override: true with a reason from a signed-in project admin (409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED). The audit log records the override as endpoint.promote_override.
  • If the scorecard fails, the gate blocks the promotion (409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED).

By default, the EvaluationPolicy of the endpoint needs evaluate_then_refit fits. It also blocks changes to the input schema that would break callers.

POST …/score takes an EndpointScoreCall. This is a score request without model. Its data and scenario can be inline XrJSON datasets of up to 5 MB. The answer is the same as for …:score on a model version. With Prefer: wait=60, you get 200 with the result if the run completes in time. If not, you get 202 with the run.

A score:<alias> token can read the endpoint, its schema, history and snippets, and can score it. endpoints:promote tokens can promote and roll back, but they cannot override the gate.

The scorecard is the gate. It does not run the call EndpointScoreCall EndpointValidation 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/rollback Set the alias back to the version of an earlier revision (audited) EndpointRollback Endpoint 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT, NOT_VALIDATED GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script and notebook code for the endpoint — SnippetSet 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Saved plots, rendering and embeds
docs.text:
A SavedPlot keeps a plot of a model version or a PlotSpec that a user wrote. Rendering (PlotRenderRequest → PlotRender) makes PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox. Embed links (PlotEmbedCreate → PlotEmbedCreated, listed as PlotEmbed) have tokens, are read-only and expire. You can embed only plots of platform recipes (422 EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED).

The public GET /v1/embeds/{embed_token} returns an EmbedView with all datasets inline, or 410 LINK_EXPIRED. It does not read credentials. It answers cross-origin reads only from the plot sandbox origin. See Sharing plots.

docs.title: Sign-up, verification, deletion and export
docs.text:
Self-service sign-up (SignupRequest → SignupAccepted) gives the same answer for new and known addresses. Verification of the e-mail (EmailVerify → VerificationResult) creates a public-tier tenant.

VerificationStatus tells if the tenant can upload code. Public tenants cannot upload code before cut line B. After cut line B, they can upload code only after identity verification. Operators record the identity verification with VerificationUpdate.

Deletion starts after a grace period (TenantDeletionRequest → TenantDeletion, with the progress for each store). During the grace period, the tenant is suspended and can cancel the deletion. A GDPR export (GdprExportRequest → GdprExport) puts all the data that the tenant stored into a package.

This creates a public-tier tenant EmailVerify VerificationResult 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, LINK_EXPIRED, RATE_LIMITED GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification E-mail and identity verification, and if code upload is permitted — VerificationStatus 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/verification Record identity verification (operators, audited) VerificationUpdate VerificationStatus 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Schedule deletion of the full tenant (grace period, then purge) TenantDeletionRequest TenantDeletion 202 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Deletion state and progress for each store — TenantDeletion 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion Cancel a scheduled deletion (during the grace period) — TenantDeletion 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports GDPR export of all the data that the tenant stored GdprExportRequest GdprExport 202 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, QUOTA_EXCEEDED GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports The GDPR exports of the tenant, newest first (GET one export to get its download link) — Page[GdprExport] 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports/{export_id} An export. docs.title: Workflows, governance, explorers and About cards v0.5
docs.text:
v0.5 (milestone M3.5) adds the contracts for these items:

  • Automated workflows: statistical tests, data processing, splits, searches and models in one versioned DAG.
  • Model governance: policies, checks with evidence, validation and approval.
  • The Data Explorer and the Model Explorer.
  • Budget optimisation with mmm-framework.
  • The plain-language About cards, with the Help me choose chooser.

The endpoint table agrees with mapi_spec.api.M35_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the full v0.5 surface (V04_ENDPOINTS + M35_ENDPOINTS). ROUTE_ACCESS gives the scope and the permission of each operation. Workflows, Governance and About cards and choosing explain the ideas.

v0.5 also removes an importer route of v0.4, its ingest preset and one snippet language (see the CHANGELOG). Thus, mmm-framework is the only MMM engine. The contract version is 0.2.

Permissions. These rules apply:

  • Viewers read workflows. Editors write them. Runners run and schedule them. Admins delete them.
  • Project admins manage project policies. Tenant admins manage tenant-wide policies. All members of the project can read the policies.
  • To submit a model version for validation, you need run rights (validate on model).
  • To approve or reject, you need the reviewer capability (Membership.capabilities, given with MembershipUpdate). Project admins have this capability automatically.
  • The person who submitted a model version cannot approve or reject it (403 SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN).
  • No API token can approve.

The new token scopes are workflows:write, workflows:run, models:validate and policies:manage.

Long-running work. A workflow run, an explore run and an optimize run are the same as other runs (Idempotency-Key, the quota checks, cost). POST …:optimize obeys Prefer: wait=N. Workflow runs stream their node events on GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}/events (SSE with Last-Event-ID, event types in WorkflowEventType). The terminal events also go to webhooks (workflow.run.succeeded, workflow.run.failed). These events also go to webhooks: validation transitions (model.validated, model.rejected, ...), dataset.version.created and optimize.completed.

Plot outputs (v0.9). The node kind plot is new. The nodes plot.render, model.forecast and evaluate.residuals give plot outputs, and a report.summary can have plot sections. The server sends each plot output through the plot sanitizer two times:

  1. When it collects the outputs of a node. An unsafe plot fails the node with PLOT_UNSAFE.
  2. When it serves node runs, run outputs and the plot sections of reports. If a stored plot is not safe, the response has null in its place.

Workflow validation finds the recipe of plot.render in the bundled recipes and in the plot catalog. If it does not find the recipe, it reports REF_UNRESOLVED at /nodes/<i>/with/recipe.

Promotion. A governance policy that applies to a model can set require_validated_for_promotion. In this case, PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} refuses a version if its validation status is not validated (409 NOT_VALIDATED). No override can pass this check.
