docs.title: Tree datasets and multi-file versions v0.8
docs.text:
A dataset version can hold an xr.DataTree (layout tree) instead of one xr.Dataset (layout dataset, the default). DatasetVersion then has layout: "tree", the tree_schema (a TreeSchema: one DataSchema per node such as / or /instrument/psf) and the sources it was built from, and data_schema is the schema of the root node.

  • Several files in one version. DatasetVersionCreate takes either upload_id + mapping (one file, as before) or assembly (an IngestAssembly): each source names its upload, its own IngestMapping, the node it goes to and how it joins the other sources of that node: node (the only source), concat (along concat_dim, one concat_label per file) or merge (variables on shared coords, aligned per join).
  • Raw HDF5. Format hdf5 needs mapping.hdf5 (an Hdf5Mapping): which HDF5 dataset becomes which variable of which node, with its dims (Hdf5Var) and coords (Hdf5Coord). To see what is in a file first, inspect the upload (below). NetCDF and xarray-written HDF5 files keep format netcdf; their groups become nodes.
  • Inspection. An inspect run reads only the metadata of an upload (after the HDF5 safety checks) and lists its groups and arrays. It is idempotent per upload: while an inspection runs, or after it succeeded, the server returns that run. If the run failed or was cancelled, a new request starts a new run. The run has the resource class that an ingest of the upload would get (the smallest class that holds the upload, so S, M or L), interactive priority and the timeout MAPI_INSPECT_TIMEOUT_S (300 s).
  • Assemblies. The server checks every upload of an assembly before it uses any of them: each upload belongs to the dataset, is complete, is used one time and is not in another version. Otherwise it answers 409 CONFLICT with a pointer to the source (/body/assembly/sources/<i>/upload_id), and all the uploads stay available. The uploads of one version are a maximum of 5 GB together (413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE). One ingest run reads them all.
  • Unsafe files. If the HDF5 guard refuses a file, the ingest or inspect run fails with INGEST_UNSAFE_FILE (422) in its problem, and the version becomes failed.

The full guide, with examples, is Tree datasets, HDF5 and multi-file versions.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/inspect List the groups and arrays of an upload (an inspect run). The server returns the current run, or the run of a finished inspection. Accepts Idempotency-Key. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the file did not arrive, the upload expired, or a version used the upload before an inspection), QUOTA_EXCEEDED GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/inspection What the inspect run found — UploadInspection 200 NOT_FOUND (never inspected, or the run ended without an inspection: the problem of the run tells why), NOT_READY (409, the run has not finished)

docs.title: Run tracking v0.11
docs.text:
A run keeps a log of what happened in it. The log has these parts:

  • Metrics. A metric is a series of points. A series has a key (for example loss) and labels (for example {"chain": "0"}). A point has a value, a time and, if it is part of a curve, a step. A point without a step is a scalar. For a scalar, the newest value is kept.
  • Params. A param is a key and a value that does not change: the first value is kept. The runner logs the params of the spec (model, fit.*, settings.*) automatically.
  • Tags. A tag is a key and a text value that you can change at any time. Tag keys that start with mapi. are for the platform only.
  • The name and the note. A run can have a display name (a maximum of 200 characters) and a note (free text, a maximum of 20 000 characters).
  • Structured log lines. Model code can write log lines with a level (debug, info, warning or error) and fields. These lines have stream user in LogLine.

Metric keys must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$. Do not write qualifiers such as train/loss in the key. Use labels: key loss with labels={"split": "train"}. Label keys match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$, label values match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{1,63}$, and a series has a maximum of 8 labels. Param keys and tag keys can have ., - and /. The guide Track metrics, params and tags shows how to log from model code, workflow nodes and notebooks.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors PATCH /v1/runs/{run_id} Set the name, the note or the tags of a run. This is a merge patch: a field that is not in the body does not change. null clears the name or the note. A tag with the value null is deleted. A run has a maximum of 100 tags. The labels of a run do not change. From v0.14, experiment_id moves the run to an experiment (null takes it out of its experiment). RunPatch Run 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/metrics The metric series of a run, with a summary of each (count, last, last_step, min, max). The order is key, then labels. Filters: key, attempt — Page[MetricSeries] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/metrics/{key} The points of one metric key, for each series (a maximum of 64 series). The server downsamples each series to max_points (10 to 10 000, default 1000) with LTTB and keeps the first and the last point. Filters: attempt, label (k:v, repeatable, all must match) — MetricHistory 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/metrics Log metric points to a run. The run can be in any state, thus you can log a KPI after the run finished. A maximum of 1000 points for each request. A point that repeats a stored (series, step) is ignored and counted in duplicates. MetricsWrite MetricsWriteResult 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID, QUOTA_EXCEEDED (the tracking budget of the run is full) GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/params The params of a run, in key order. Filter: prefix — Page[RunParam] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/params Log params to a run (a maximum of 500 for each request). A param that has the same value again is unchanged. ParamsWrite ParamsWriteResult 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (a key has a different stored value: the server writes nothing and names a maximum of 10 keys), QUOTA_EXCEEDED

The write endpoints need update on run (the runner role or higher). An API token needs the runs:write scope: runs:create does not give it. Each write makes an audit event: run.update for PATCH (the changed fields and the number of tags, never the note text), and run.log for metric and param writes (the number of points or params).

Run has the fields name, note and tags (v0.11). MetricSeries gives the newest attempt that logged the series. MetricHistorySeries has three lists of equal length: steps, values and ts. A scalar series has one point with the step null. MetricPointIn has key, value (a finite number), step (optional, 0 or more), ts (optional, the default is the time of the request) and labels.

docs.title: Search runs
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs has these query parameters for search (v0.11):

Parameter Value parent_run_id Only the child runs of this run (for example, the node runs of a workflow run). experiment_id v0.14: only the runs of this experiment. name The runs whose name contains this text (case-insensitive). tag key (the run has the tag) or key:value (exact value). Repeatable: all must match. filter A comparison, for example metric.rmse < 0.5. Repeatable, a maximum of 8: all must match. order_by One ref. A - before the ref gives descending order. The default is -created_at. column A ref whose value the server adds to Run.columns. Repeatable, a maximum of 16.

A ref has one of these forms:

metric.KEY[{label=value,...}][.AGG]     AGG: last (default), min, max, count
param.KEY
tag.KEY
name
created_at                              (only in order_by and column)

A filter is ref OP value. The operators are <, <=, >, >=, =, != and ~. ~ finds text that contains the value (case-insensitive).

Ref Operators Value metric.… < <= > >= = != A number. The server compares it with the summary of that exact series. metric.loss is the series without labels. metric.loss{split=val} is the series with exactly that label. param.… = != ~ Text, compared with the text form of the param. param.… < <= > >= A number, compared with the numeric value of the param. tag.… = != ~ Text. name = ~ Text.

A run that does not have the series, the param or the tag does not match the filter. This is also true for !=. Runs that do not have the value of order_by come last. Equal values sort by run id (descending). When order_by is a param, the server sorts by the numeric value of the param first, then by its text. Run.columns uses the canonical text of each ref as its key (labels in key order, .last left out), for example metric.loss{chain=0,split=val}. The server returns 422 SCHEMA_INVALID for a value that does not have this grammar. mapi_spec.tracking.parse_run_filter, parse_run_order and parse_run_ref implement the grammar. The Python client and the CLI use them to do a check of the values before they send the request.

curl -G "$MAPI/v1/runs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=metric.rmse < 12' \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=param.fit.engine = nutpie' \
  --data-urlencode 'order_by=metric.rmse' \
  --data-urlencode 'column=metric.rmse' --data-urlencode 'column=param.settings.adstock.l_max'

docs.title: Log levels
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs?level=warning returns the lines with the level warning or error. The order of the levels is debug, info, warning, error. A line without a level (stdout, stderr and system lines) counts as info. LogLine has level and fields only for stream user.

The server sends the lines of stream user only when the request has stream=user or include_user=true. A client before v0.11 knows only the streams stdout, stderr and system, thus it continues to read the logs of all runs. The v0.11 Python client, the CLI and the web app send include_user=true.

docs.title: The tracking frame
docs.text:
The event stream (GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events, SSE) sends event: tracking when the metrics, the params or the tags of the run change. The data: is a TrackingFrame:

  • series: the MetricSeries summaries that changed after the last frame (a maximum of 200).
  • params and tags: true if the params or the tags changed. Get them again.
  • media (v0.14): true if the run logged images or tables. Get them again from GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/media-keys.

A tracking frame has no id:, and the server does not replay it. A client that connects again gets the current values from the endpoints above. The run events metrics, params and tags (see Run protocol) are not persisted as events. Thus, they are not in Page[RunEventView] and have no frame name of their own.

event: tracking
data: {"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","series":[{"key":"step_size","labels":{"chain":"0"},"attempt":1,"count":1400,"last":0.31,"last_step":1400, …}],"params":false,"tags":false}

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: The setting MAPI_TRACKING_RETENTION_DAYS (no default: keep all) deletes the metric points and the user log lines of runs that finished more days ago than the setting. The server keeps the summaries, the params, the tags, the name and the note. Thus, search and comparison of old runs continue to work. See Configuration. The setting does not delete media (v0.14).

docs.title: Media, comparison, experiments and saved views v0.14
docs.text:
v0.14 adds these parts to run tracking:

  • Media. A run can log images (PNG or JPEG) and small tables (JSON). The runner uploads them during the run (see Run protocol: Media). You can also log them through the API, also after the run finished.
  • Comparison. One request gets the summaries, the metric histories, the params and the media of 2 to 10 runs.
  • Experiments. An experiment is a named group of runs. A run is in a maximum of one experiment.
  • Saved views. A saved view is a list_runs query with a name, shared in the project.

The guide Compare runs and use experiments shows the web app, the client and the CLI.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/media The media of a run. The order is key, labels, step. Filters: key, kind, attempt. With links (default true), each item has a signed url and expires_at. — Page[RunMedia] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/media/{media_id} One media item, always with a signed url — RunMedia 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/media Log one image or table to a run (any state). data is the standard base64 of the bytes, a maximum of 4 MiB after decoding. The server checks Content-Length before it reads the body. MediaWrite RunMedia 201 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID (bad base64, the bytes are not the content type, an image side is more than 4096), QUOTA_EXCEEDED (the media budget of the run is full), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/media-keys The media series of a run (key and labels), with the number of items and the first and last step. Filter: attempt — Page[MediaKeySummary] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/run-compare Compare runs. run (repeatable, 2 to 10, no duplicates), key (a maximum of 12 metric keys; the default is the 12 keys that most of the runs have), media_key (a maximum of 4), max_points (10 to 2000, default 300), params (default true) — RunCompare 200 NOT_FOUND (a run is not in the project), SCHEMA_INVALID GET /v1/run-keys The metric series, the param keys and the tag keys of the runs of the project, or of one experiment (experiment_id), with the number of runs that have each. prefix keeps the keys that start with the text. — RunKeys 200 SCHEMA_INVALID GET /v1/experiments The experiments of the project, newest first. Filters: name (contains, case-insensitive), archived — Page[Experiment] 200 — POST /v1/experiments Make an experiment. Names are unique in a project (case is ignored). ExperimentCreate Experiment 201 SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (the name is in use) GET /v1/experiments/{experiment_id} One experiment, with run_count and last_run_at — Experiment 200 NOT_FOUND PATCH /v1/experiments/{experiment_id} Rename, describe, archive or unarchive (merge patch) ExperimentPatch Experiment 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/experiments/{experiment_id} Delete an experiment. Its runs stay, with no experiment. Its saved views are deleted. — — 204 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/experiments/{experiment_id}/runs Move runs into the experiment (add) or out of it (remove), a maximum of 200 ids each. A run that is added leaves its earlier experiment. missing lists the ids that are not runs of the project. ExperimentRunsWrite ExperimentRunsResult 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (the experiment is archived) GET /v1/run-views The saved views of the project, in name order. Filter: experiment_id — Page[RunView] 200 — POST /v1/run-views Save a view. Names are unique for each project and experiment (case is ignored). A project has a maximum of 200 views. RunViewCreate RunView 201 SCHEMA_INVALID (a filter, an order or a column is not valid: the pointer is /query/filters/<i>), CONFLICT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED PATCH /v1/run-views/{view_id} Rename a view or change its query RunViewPatch RunView 200 NOT_FOUND, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT DELETE /v1/run-views/{view_id} Delete a saved view — — 204 NOT_FOUND

All these endpoints need the X-Mapi-Project header (or a project in the token). Reads need read on run (a viewer can read). Writes need update on run (the runner role or higher, or an API token with the runs:write scope). The writes make audit events: experiment.create, experiment.update (also bulk moves, with the numbers added and removed), experiment.delete, run_view.save (create and update) and run_view.delete. A media write through the API is a run.log event. A PATCH of a run that moves it is a run.update event with experiment_id in the fields.

RunCreate and PATCH /v1/runs/{run_id} take experiment_id. An unknown experiment is 422 SCHEMA_INVALID with the pointer /experiment_id. An archived experiment is 409 CONFLICT. Run has the field experiment_id. A workflow node run gets the experiment of its workflow run. A retry gets the experiment of the run that it retries.

docs.title: The DTOs
docs.text:
• RunMedia: id (rm_…), run_id, attempt, key, labels, step, kind (image or table), content_type (image/png, image/jpeg or application/json), size, sha256 (sha256:<hex>), crc32c, width and height (images), caption (untrusted text), source (runner or api), created_at, and with links url and expires_at. Do a check of size and crc32c after the download.
  • MediaKeySummary: key, labels, kind, count, first_step, last_step, last_created_at.
  • MediaWrite: key, kind, content_type, data (base64), step, labels, caption (a maximum of 500 characters). A table is UTF-8 JSON of a MediaTable (mapi_spec.media): {"columns": [...], "rows": [[...], ...]}.
  • Experiment: id (exp_…), name, description, archived, created_by, created_at, updated_at, run_count, last_run_at. ExperimentCreate has name (1 to 200 characters, no control characters) and description (a maximum of 20 000 characters). ExperimentPatch has name, description (null clears it) and archived.
  • ExperimentRunsWrite: add and remove (a minimum of one id in all, no id in both). ExperimentRunsResult: added, removed, missing.
  • RunView: id (rv_…), name, experiment_id, query, created_by, created_at, updated_at. RunViewCreate has name, experiment_id and query. RunViewPatch has name or query.
  • RunViewQuery: the query of list_runs: kind, state, name, spec_id, experiment_id, parent_run_id, tags (key or key:value, a maximum of 16), filters (a maximum of 8), order_by and columns (a maximum of 16). The search grammar applies.
  • RunKeys: metrics (a maximum of 500), params (a maximum of 500) and tags (a maximum of 200), each a list of RunKeyCount (key, labels, runs), most common first. truncated is true when a list is cut.
  • RunCompare: runs (in the order of the run values), summaries (CompareSummary: a MetricSeries with run_id; a maximum of 1000), metrics (CompareMetric: key and series, a list of CompareSeries with run_id, labels, attempt, count, downsampled, steps and values; a maximum of 16 series for each run and key), params (CompareParam: key, values (run id to text, null when the run did not log it) and differs; a maximum of 2000), media (CompareMedia: run_id, key, labels, kind and items, a maximum of 50 RunMedia with links for each series, thinned evenly, the last item kept) and truncated (summaries, series, params or media when cut).
curl -G "$MAPI/v1/run-compare" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Mapi-Project: growth" \
  --data-urlencode run=run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0 \
  --data-urlencode run=run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d1 \
  --data-urlencode key=loss --data-urlencode media_key=samples

docs.title: Resumable uploads and image collections v0.15
docs.text:
v0.15 adds these parts to the dataset API:

  • Resumable uploads. get_upload tells you if the file of an upload arrived. renew_upload signs a fresh PUT URL for an upload whose URL expired. An upload whose file arrived has the status uploaded. You can use it in a version also after its PUT URL expired. If no version uses it, the server deletes it 7 days after its PUT URL expired. When you renew an expired upload, the server does a check of the storage quota again.
  • Image collections. A collection version is made from a manifest upload and image part uploads (DatasetVersionCreate.collection). find_missing_images tells you which images a base version does not have, so you upload only these images.

The guide Image data: collections shows the CLI, the client and the web app.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id} An upload and whether its file arrived (received). upload is the current signed PUT. — UploadSession 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads/{upload_id}/renew Sign a fresh PUT URL (TTL 1 h) for an upload whose file did not arrive. received is false. — UploadSession 200 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (a version used the upload, or the file arrived) POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/blobs/missing Which images (by SHA-256) the base version does not have BlobQuery BlobMissing 200 NOT_FOUND (the base version), SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (the base version is not a ready collection)

All three need the X-Mapi-Project header (or a project in the token). find_missing_images needs read on dataset, as get_dataset. get_upload and renew_upload need update on dataset, as create_upload, because their answer holds a signed PUT URL. A user who can only read the dataset cannot write its uploads.

POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions takes collection (a CollectionSource) in place of upload_id + mapping or assembly. The server:

  • makes sure that the manifest upload has a maximum of 256 MB and each part a maximum of 2 GB − 64 MB, and that each part has an MD5 (else 409, pointer /body/collection/part_upload_ids/<i>);
  • finds the base version: with base_version set, the version must exist, be ready and have the layout collection (else 409); with null, the latest ready collection version (or none); with 0, no base;
  • starts a collection ingest run of class M. The run reads the parts in ranges, so the class does not depend on the size of the upload.

get_dataset_artifact also gives manifest.parquet and collection.json of a collection version.

docs.title: The DTOs
docs.text:
• UploadSession gains received (only in the answers of get_upload and renew_upload).
  • DatasetVersionCreate gains collection (a CollectionSource). Give exactly one of upload_id + mapping, assembly or collection. upload_ids is the manifest, then the parts.
  • CollectionSource (mapi_spec.collection): manifest_upload_id, part_upload_ids (a maximum of 64, unique, not the manifest), base_version (null: the latest ready collection version; 0: none) and options (a CollectionOptions).
  • CollectionOptions (mapi_spec.collection): sha256_column (default sha256), id_column, path_column (default path), label_column, split_column, columns (a maximum of 64; not the reserved names of manifest.parquet), var (pixels), dim (image), mode (auto, gray or rgb), size (height, width), resize (stretch, crop or pad) and max_images (default 100 000, a maximum of 1 000 000).
  • DatasetVersion.layout can be collection. DatasetVersion.collection is then a CollectionInfo (mapi_spec.collection): n_images, dim, var, label, split, classes (a maximum of 1000 ClassCount, by count), other_classes, splits, mode, size, min_size, max_size, formats, total_bytes, packs (PackInfo: digest, size, crc32c, md5, entries, images, source (upload or base) and input), new_images, reused_images, base_version, columns and manifest_sha256.
  • BlobQuery: sha256 (1 to 5000 unique lowercase hex digests) and base_version (null: the latest ready collection version; 0: none, so all images are missing).
  • BlobMissing: base_version (the version compared with, or null), missing (in the order of the query) and present (the number of the other digests).
curl -X POST "$MAPI/v1/datasets/$DATASET/blobs/missing" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Mapi-Project: growth" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sha256": ["'"$(sha256sum photo.jpg | cut -c1-64)"'"]}'

docs.title: Built-in models
docs.text:
These model plugins come with the platform (tier T0). They register through the mapi.models entry point. Thus default_registry() and the control-plane catalog show them without configuration. Each plugin passes the contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model). Each plugin also has a conformance fixture (see Conformance corpus). From v0.5, the marketing-mix models run on mmm-framework. This is the only marketing-mix engine of the platform.

Calibration (M3, the calibration block of the spec, Guided task 3): each plugin declares it in Capabilities.calibration. A spec can have calibration data for a plugin that does not declare it. Such a spec fails static validation with CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED:

Plugin Business priors Lift tests mmm.bayesian yes - log-normal ROI priors for each channel (priors.roi) and the intercept yes - mmm-framework experiment likelihoods (marginal ROAS or contribution) mmm.frequentist no no mmm.nested no yes - the total effect of a channel (marginal ROAS or contribution) mmm.multivariate no no

Guided modelling gives the math of the translation and of each lift likelihood.

Every setting, generated

The platform makes the models catalog from the installed manifests. It shows the capabilities, outputs and derived quantities. It also shows each setting with its default and Guided-mode level, and the contract for the input data.

docs.title: mmm.bayesian: marketing mix on mmm-framework
docs.text:
This plugin uses the BayesianMMM of mmm-framework. It has these parts:

  • Adstock (geometric, delayed, Weibull) and saturation (logistic, Hill, Michaelis-Menten, tanh, root) for each channel.
  • A trend (none, linear, piecewise, spline, GP).
  • Fourier seasonality.
  • Baselines with partial pooling across geos and products. Channel effects for each geo are optional.
  • Channel effects as returns on spend.
  • Channel effects that change over time (time_varying) v0.12.
  • The likelihoods normal, student_t, poisson, negative_binomial (counts) and beta (shares) v0.12.

The model owns scaling, carry-over and units (owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units]). Thus the pipeline only converts currencies and resamples. With outputs.derived, the fit caches contributions, response curves for each draw and marginal costs. The mmm-framework planning optimises budgets (POST …:optimize). The model declares a decision objective.

Inputs. y(*panel, time), spend(*panel, channel, time), and other numeric variables over time as controls. The panel dims are hierarchy.pool_over (geo, product). New panel levels follow new_levels (pooled by default). channel is fixed. time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(*panel, time) and contributions(component, *panel, time). The components are one for each channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and one for each control. Their sum is y_hat.

Marketing-mix models on mmm-framework tells how the settings map to mmm-framework. It also tells about priors, lift tests and optimisation. For a complete analysis, read the marketing-mix guide.

docs.title: mmm.nested: marketing mix with an intermediate measure v0.12
docs.text:
This plugin uses the NestedMMM of mmm-framework (mmm_extensions). Channels act on one or more mediators (for example visits or awareness), and the mediators act on the KPI. The channels can also act on the KPI directly. A measured mediator can have empty periods. A latent mediator has no data.

Inputs. National data only: y(time), spend(channel, time) and mediators(mediator, time) (missing values allowed). There are no control variables. channel and mediator are fixed. time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(time), contributions(component, time) (each channel with its total effect, baseline, trend, seasonality; their sum is y_hat) and mediator_hat(mediator, time). Derived: contributions, response_curves, marginal_cost, adstock and mediation (direct, indirect and total effect of each channel). Lift tests calibrate the total effect of a channel.

docs.title: mmm.multivariate: marketing mix for several results v0.12
docs.text:
This plugin uses the MultivariateMMM of mmm-framework (mmm_extensions). Each outcome has its own equation. The noise of the outcomes is correlated (LKJ prior). Cross-effects (halo, cannibalization, unconstrained) link the outcomes. They are associations, not causes. Scores and budget plans use the reduced form. Thus, a channel that moves one outcome also moves the outcomes that it links to.

Inputs. National data only: y(outcome, time) and spend(channel, time). There are no control variables. channel and outcome are fixed. time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(outcome, time) and contributions(component, outcome, time). Their sum is y_hat for each outcome. Derived: contributions, response_curves (the weighted total of the outcomes, and each outcome), marginal_cost, adstock and cross_effects. There is no lift-test calibration.

Marketing-mix models on mmm-framework gives the settings of the two models.

docs.title: mmm.frequentist: fast marketing mix
docs.text: This plugin uses the ridge estimator of mmm-framework. An out-of-sample search selects the adstock and saturation. The channel effects are not negative. The bootstrap gives confidence intervals (the replicates are the draws). The data contract and outputs are the same as mmm.bayesian. There are no priors, no lift tests and no convergence diagnostics. The same seed gives the same result, and a fit takes seconds.

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend — smooth trend with seasonality
docs.text:
This plugin has a Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) trend, an optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality. It is for one series with regular spaces between periods (CO2 as at Mauna Loa, sales, traffic).

Inputs. t (time, policy extend) and the target y(t). Missing months are permitted. Replace sentinel codes with core.replace_sentinel. The likelihood then does not use these months, but the model interpolates them. Put core.standardize on y. The priors are on the standardised scale, and the model changes the outputs back to your units.

Forecast horizon. max_extension (default 24 periods) is part of the input schema of the model. At fit time, the model sets the size of the HSGP domain from the anticipated coordinates. These are the fitted range plus max_extension periods. Thus each forecast up to that horizon evaluates exactly the fitted functions. The server rejects a longer horizon with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (HTTP 409) before it starts to compute. Fit again with a larger max_extension.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 24 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach without a new fit kernel expquad expquad, matern52 or matern32 m, c 30, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation lengthscale_mu, lengthscale_sigma 0.4, 0.5 Log-normal lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] eta_sigma 1.0 Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude linear_trend true Adds intercept + slope * t season_period, season_order 12, 3 Fourier seasonality (periods of t, order) noise_sigma 0.5 Half-normal scale of the observation noise

Outputs. y_hat(t) (the expected value or a predictive draw) and trend(t). trend(t) is the long-term component without seasonality. The two outputs are in the units of the target.

data:
  bind: {dims: {t: date}, vars: {y: co2}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 12}
pipeline:
  - {id: clean, use: core.replace_sentinel@^1, with: {vars: [y], below: 0}}
  - {id: scale, use: core.standardize@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [t]}}
model:
  use: ts.hsgp_trend@^1
  settings: {max_extension: 24, season_order: 2}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: pymc, seed: 11}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm — hidden states with a terminal state
docs.text:
This plugin is a Gaussian hidden Markov model with K states. It uses many sequences at the same time (animal tracks, machine regimes, customer phases). The forward algorithm sums out the hidden states. Thus the sampler is fast and exact.

Inputs. A padded layout with these items: animal (the sequence dim, new_levels with strategy pooled), step (extend), y(animal, step) with NaN padding, and a boolean mask(animal, step).

Terminal state. After the fit, the bundle keeps the filtered state distribution at the last fitted step. It is the terminal_state group of the bundle, alpha_T(chain, draw, animal, state).

  • predict / evaluate use the one-step-ahead state distribution of the fit in the fitted range. After the fitted range, they use alpha_T, propagated by the transition matrix. They do not use targets in the payload.
  • forecast propagates alpha_T over the horizon.
  • filter runs the forward filter over new observations that continue the fitted steps. It returns an updated terminal_state group with the filtered state_prob.
  • New animals start from the initial distribution pi at the first fitted step.

After the sampler stops, the model gives new labels to the draws so that the state means increase (label switching). identification: ordered uses an ordered prior instead. The manifest declares pointwise LOO as not valid, because the steps in a track are dependent. Validation rejects elpd_loo.

Setting Default Meaning n_states 2 Number of hidden states mu_center, mu_sigma 0.0, 2.0 Normal prior of the state means sigma_scale 1.0 Half-normal scale of the sds for each state stickiness 2.0 Additional Dirichlet weight to stay in the same state pi_concentration 1.0 Dirichlet weight of the initial distribution identification relabel relabel (sort the draws by mean) or ordered

Outputs. y_hat(animal, step) in your units, and state_prob(animal, step, state). The units of state_prob are probability. The model does not inverse-transform it.

docs.title: ts.bsts and the causal models v0.13
docs.text:
ts.bsts is a Bayesian structural time series on the state-space models of pymc-extras: a level, a trend, seasonal patterns and drivers with one effect for all periods. Like ts.gaussian_hmm, it keeps a terminal_state group. forecast starts from it and filter updates it. The manifest declares pointwise LOO as not valid.

causal.impact (CausalImpact on the ts.bsts core), causal.synthetic_control (a Bayesian synthetic control for geo-lift tests) and causal.did (difference-in-differences and event study) write the effect of a change to the impact group. See Causal models and Bayesian structural time series for the inputs, the settings and the groups, and Measure the effect of a change for the procedures.

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm — partial pooling in long layout
docs.text:
This plugin has intercepts that change by group, and optionally slopes that change by group. It has group-level predictors. Examples are the radon model and many similar models (schools, stores, clinics).

Inputs. A long layout with these items:

  • Rows along obs (extend).
  • A group dim (group_dim, default county, new_levels with strategy hyperprior).
  • The index <group_dim>_idx(obs).
  • The target y(obs).
  • Observation-level covariates and group-level group_covariates.

Covariates are part of the input schema. Thus, if a spec names a covariate that is missing, the spec fails validation.

New groups. For a county that the model did not see, the model draws its effect from the fitted hyperprior for each posterior draw. Its group-level covariates move its prior mean in the same way as for fitted counties. Score payloads can list counties in any sequence. The platform maps county_idx again.

Setting Default Meaning group_dim county The grouping dim family normal normal, student_t, poisson (log link) or bernoulli (logit). From v0.14 (model version 1.1.0) also the families in the table below. n_categories none v0.14: the number of ordered categories (2 to 50). Necessary for ordinal. covariates [] Predictors over obs varying_slopes [] Covariates whose slope varies by group group_covariates [] Predictors over the group dim centered false Use centred group effects

Families of v0.14. mu is the expected value of y.

Family Link Extra parameter Data negative_binomial log alpha ~ HalfNormal (dispersion) Counts: whole numbers, 0 or more zero_inflated_poisson log psi ~ Beta(2, 2): the probability of the count process. mu = psi · exp(eta). Counts with many zeros zero_inflated_negative_binomial log alpha and psi Counts with many zeros and a large spread beta logit kappa ~ HalfNormal(50) (precision) Shares strictly between 0 and 1 gamma log alpha ~ HalfNormal(5) (shape) Positive amounts, more than 0 ordinal cumulative logit cutpoints: n_categories − 1 sorted values. The intercept is 0. mu = Σ k · p_k. Whole numbers from 0 to n_categories − 1

If the target does not agree with the family (for example a negative count, or a share of exactly 0 or 1 for beta), the fit stops with a clear message.

docs.title: tabular.image_logistic — classify small images v0.14
docs.text:
This plugin classifies small images, for example the images of an image folder upload. It is a Bayesian multinomial logistic regression on the main patterns of the pixels.

Inputs. pixels(image, y, x, channel) with the dtype uint8 (role covariate) and the target label(image) as text (role target, missing values allowed). image is categorical with new_levels (strategy pooled). y and x are integer dims and channel is a categorical dim, all fixed.

Model. The pixels are divided by 255. With downsample more than 1, the model takes the mean of blocks of pixels. With features: pca (the default), the model calculates the first n_components principal components of the training images and uses their standardised scores. With features: pixels, it uses the pixels (a maximum of max_features values). Then: alpha ~ ZeroSumNormal(2) over the classes, beta ~ ZeroSumNormal(prior_sigma) over the features and the classes, and label ~ Categorical(softmax(alpha + Z · beta)). The default engine is nutpie.

Outputs. y_hat(chain, draw, image, class): the probability of each class (a maximum of 500 draws), with the attribute meaning: class_probability. The bundle keeps the PCA basis in the group features. The fit logs the params image.features, image.n_components, image.height and image.width, the metric explained_variance, and the images pca_components and class_means (the Media tab). The plots are core.roc_pr, core.confusion and core.convergence. loo is not valid for this model.

Setting Default Meaning pixels, target, image_dim pixels, label, image The names of the inputs features pca pca or pixels n_components 16 The number of components (2 to 64, a maximum of the training images − 1) downsample 1 The size of the pixel blocks (1 to 16) max_features 256 pixels: the maximum of (height / downsample) × (width / downsample) × channels prior_sigma 1.0 The prior scale of beta (more than 0, a maximum of 10) class_order none The classes in a fixed sequence (a maximum of 50) input pixels v0.15: pixels or features (image features such as embedding(image, feature)) feature_dim feature v0.15: the feature dim when input is features

mapi_plugin_tabular.image_data.shapes_dataset() makes a small example dataset (circles, squares and crosses, 16 × 16 pixels, with a split coordinate).

Features input (v1.1, v0.15). With input: features, the model reads image features, for example embedding(image, feature) from the step dl.embed. Set pixels to the name of the feature variable and feature_dim (default feature) to its dim. The model standardises the features. It uses PCA only when there are more than max_features features. See Deep learning: image features and a simple head.

docs.title: Deep learning (mapi-jax) v0.15
docs.text:
The package mapi-jax has three models and one step. They use JAX, Flax (nnx) and Optax. The models train with the shared trainer of mapi_jax.trainer. All have the capabilities: inference custom, representation draws (chain = 1), score modes predict and evaluate, checkpointable, deterministic_given_seed, and loo_valid: false ("a network trained by gradient descent has no pointwise log likelihood").

Model Input Resources Outputs dl.mlp dataset S, no GPU y_hat(chain, draw, *rows) (regression) or y_hat(chain, draw, *rows, class) with meaning: class_probability dl.cnn_classifier collection (also plain image datasets) minimum S, default M, GPU y_hat(chain, draw, image, class) dl.finetune_classifier collection (also plain image datasets) minimum S, default M, GPU y_hat(chain, draw, image, class). Reads the side table pretrained.

The image models use a small ResNet with GroupNorm and global average pooling. The bundle has:

  • the group training: train_loss, val_loss, train_accuracy (or train_rmse), val_accuracy (or val_rmse) and lr along epoch, and confusion(epoch, true_class, pred_class) for classifiers with validation data;
  • the group misclassified: up to 32 small validation images that the network classifies incorrectly, with true_label, pred_label and prob;
  • the native objects weights.safetensors and, for the Laplace draws, laplace.safetensors.

The plots are ml.training_curves, ml.confusion_epochs, ml.misclassified, core.roc_pr and core.confusion (dl.mlp: ml.training_curves). The step dl.embed writes embedding(image, feature) from a frozen pretrained backbone.

Deep learning gives the settings, the training, the draws, the checkpoints, the GPU class and examples.

docs.title: tabular.regressor — quantile regression for panels
docs.text:
This plugin is the store-demand model of the plan. The model stacks rows from labelled dims (store × sku × week). The coordinates become categorical features. An estimator from the allow list predicts conditional quantiles. The estimator setting accepts only the estimators of the registry that can predict quantiles. These are xgboost, the gradient boosting and histogram boosting of scikit-learn, and quantile regression. Validation rejects other estimators.

  • Defaults: xgboost (300 trees, depth 5, learning rate 0.05) and quantiles [0.1, 0.5, 0.9].
  • The model pools new stores (new_levels: pooled).
  • The forecast is direct. Thus you must supply the future covariates that have the future_required mark. If you do not, the error is MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE.
  • Quantiles are for each cell. The server refuses to aggregate them across stores (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • The manifest lists core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time and ml.feature_importance.

All other settings are the settings of mapi_sklearn (see Tabular models).

docs.title: choice.multinomial_logit — which product customers pick
docs.text:
This plugin is the built-in model of the Guided customer choice template (household panels as in E84). On each shopping trip, a household selects one product. Price and promotions change the choice.

Inputs. A dense hh × trip panel, with the alternatives along product (categorical, fixed). hh is categorical, with new_levels with strategy hyperprior. trip is index and extend. The target y(hh, trip) is text: the product that the household selected. It is empty when a household made no trip (ragged panels are permitted). Covariates are variables for each alternative along product, for example price(hh, trip, product) and promo(hh, trip, product). By default, each numeric variable with the product dim is a covariate. If the covariates of a product are missing on a trip, that product was not available on that trip (not on the shelf).

Model. A conditional logit with product intercepts for each household: U[h, t, j] = asc[j] + Σ_k beta[k]·x_k[h, t, j] + u[h, j]. The choice probabilities are a softmax over the available products. u[h, j] ~ Normal(0, effect_sd) (a random-intercept logit). The fit uses penalised maximum likelihood, that is, the posterior mode of that model.

Uncertainty comes from the Bayesian bootstrap. Each of the fit.draws draws is a new fit with Dirichlet weights on households. Thus each household keeps its own effect in each draw, and the draws are joint. In the draws representation, shares, counterfactual deltas and sums over trips are valid. There is no pointwise log-likelihood, so LOO is not available.

Scoring. y_hat(hh, trip, product) is the choice probability (expected), or one sampled choice for each draw (predictive, one-hot). The fit did not see some households. For each draw, the model draws their preferences from Normal(0, sd). sd is the spread of the fitted effects in that draw. A trip that the household did not make has probability 0 for all products. Thus sums over trips count the expected purchases.

Price scenarios are interventions, for example {var: price, sel: {product: cola}, multiply: 1.1} in a counterfactual request. To match choice values to product labels, the model changes them to lower case and replaces punctuation with _.

Setting Default Meaning covariates each numeric variable along product Covariates for each alternative random_effects [hh] Household product intercepts ([]: none) effect_sd 1.0 Prior sd of the household effects (a smaller value pools more) coef_sd 10.0 Prior sd of the product intercepts and coefficients reference the first product The product whose intercept is fixed at 0 max_iter 500 Iterations of each L-BFGS fit

fit.draws (default 100, maximum 2000) sets the number of bootstrap draws. With fit.seed, you get the same draws each time. The CHOICE_HIT_RATE diagnostic gives the in-sample hit rate.

Holdout metrics. A text target with one score probability for each product gets the categorical metrics of evaluate.metrics:

  • accuracy: the hit rate of the most likely product.
  • accuracy_naive: the hit rate if you always select the most common product of the holdout.
  • accuracy_lift: the difference between the two.
  • log_score: the mean log probability of the product that the household bought.
  • brier: the multi-class Brier score.

The Guided customer_choice template evaluates all five on the last trip of each household. Its scorecard runs holdout.hit_rate. For a text target, the server skips numeric metrics, for example mape.

docs.title: Scientific models (mapi-plugin-science)
docs.text:
These plugins come from the case studies of pymc-challenges. Most of their data are maps, images and fields on a regular grid. Some read other shapes: the areas of a map (sci.areal_bym2), a graph of nodes (sci.network_latent_space), a network of variables (sci.graphical_model), a phylogeny (sci.phylo_regression) or angles (sci.circular_regression). Their outputs have a range for each cell, area or node. Each output that is a field declares a grid (OutputDecl.grid: the row dim y, the column dim x, an optional frame dim and an optional component dim for a vector field). The platform then shows the output in two places:

  • The Fields section of the Model Explorer. It shows the mean, the sd, mean ÷ sd, the 5% and 95% maps and single draws, with a frame slider and a draw player.
  • The sci.* plot recipes (see Plot recipes).

An output that is an angle (a direction or a time of day) declares circular (OutputDecl.circular). Its metrics and score summaries are then on the circle (see Circular outputs).

The runner images of base-bayes contain these plugins (namespace sci).

Tutorials

The pymc-challenges tutorials have one page for each case study. Each page exports the data, fits the model in the web app, reads the results, scores the model and runs a workflow recipe. The complex workflows tutorial and the workflow cookbook show the six workflow recipes for these models.

Real data

Each data module has a from_challenges(path) function. It reads the real data file of the case study from a local copy of pymc-challenges. To run the tests that use the real files, set MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA to the data/ directory of that copy. Without it, these tests are skipped.

docs.title: Export the data of a case study
docs.text:
mapi_plugin_science.export writes the dataset of a case study to a file. You can then upload the file in the web app (Datasets → New dataset), with the CLI or with the Python client. The file contains the raw schema of the model (the mapi_schema attribute). Thus the ingest gives the correct role to each variable, for example target and mask.

# the cases that you can export
python -m mapi_plugin_science.export --list
# the real data, from a local copy of pymc-challenges, and the suggested spec
python -m mapi_plugin_science.export e07 \
    --challenges ~/pymc-challenges/data --out quakes.nc --spec quakes.yaml
# the simulated data of the model (you do not need pymc-challenges)
python -m mapi_plugin_science.export e50 --synthetic --out assay.nc

--challenges is the data/ directory of pymc-challenges. If you do not give it, the command uses MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA. A case without a data file (e51, e61) needs neither. The suffix of --out sets the format:

Suffix Format .nc NetCDF-4 (h5netcdf). A tree dataset has one HDF5 group for each node .zarr.zip A zarr zip of a plain dataset (the data.zarr.zip wire format) .tree.zip A tree dataset (the data.tree.zip wire format)

If you do not give --out, the file is <dataset>.nc. With --spec, the command also writes the suggested spec. That spec reads the suggested dataset name (dataset://<project>/<dataset>@latest). Use that name when you upload the file.

Case Model Data file in data/ Suggested dataset e07 sci.lgcp_grid oklahoma_quakes.csv geoscience/oklahoma_quakes_grid e18 sci.areal_bym2 scotland_lip.geojson epidemiology/scotland_lip_cancer e50 sci.fisher_kpp scratch_assay_pc3.csv biology/scratch_assay_pc3 e60 sci.traction_force pytfm_colony_ko04.npz biophysics/pytfm_colony_ko04 e80 sci.strong_lens slacs_j1627_f814w.npz astronomy/slacs_j1627_f814w e51 sci.heat_plate none (the notebook simulates the data) engineering/heat_plate_e51 e61 sci.turing_pattern none (the notebook simulates its images) biology/e61_turing_early_images e58 sci.storm_localisation dannhauser2022_unc13_dstorm_roi.npz microscopy/dannhauser2022_unc13_dstorm e31 sci.ibp_features optdigits_train.csv, optdigits_test.csv vision/optdigits_e31 e77 sci.colour_naming wcs_naming.npz, wcs_terms.csv, wcs_chips.csv, wcs_languages.csv linguistics/wcs_nafaanra e79 sci.cmb_field planck_smica_patches.npz, planck_theory_tt.txt astronomy/planck_smica_lmc e21 sci.network_latent_space lazega_cowork.txt, lazega_attributes.txt sociology/lazega_coworkers e19 sci.graphical_model sachs2005.txt, sachs2005_consensus.txt biology/sachs_cd3cd28 e23 sci.phylo_regression primates301.csv, primates301_tree.rda biology/primates301 e81 sci.circular_regression asos_ksba_2021_2023.csv.gz meteorology/ksba_wind_2021_2023 e81b sci.circular_regression bci_camera_trap_times.csv ecology/bci_camera_traps

In Python, export_case("e07", "quakes.nc", data_dir=...) does the same work, and write_export(data, path, schema=...) writes any dataset or tree. To add a case, add one ExportCase entry to EXPORTS (the docstring of the module shows an example).

docs.title: sci.lgcp_grid — event counts on a map over time (E07)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E07 from start to end.

A log-Gaussian Cox process on a space-time grid. The total for each period follows a random walk. The share of each cell comes from a 2-D Hilbert-space GP (Matérn 5/2) whose map changes from one era (a group of periods) to the next.

Inputs. period (time, policy extend), row and col (integer, fixed) and the target count(period, row, col). Row 0 is the south edge of the grid.

Outputs. rate(period, row, col) (a field with a frame for each period, log colour scale) and total(period). The sum of rate over the cells is equal to total.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 8 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach without a new fit era_periods 4 The number of periods in one era. The map changes from era to era field era_walk era_walk (a new map for each era) or static (one map) cell_km 25 The width of one cell in km m_row, m_col, c 10, 14, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation ell_lower_km, ell_upper_km 15, 100 The 5% and 95% quantiles of the lengthscale prior likelihood negbin negbin or poisson

from_challenges puts the Oklahoma earthquake catalogue into 12 × 9 cells of 25 km for each quarter from 2009 to 2019. A fit on 2009–2017 takes approximately one minute with nutpie.

docs.title: sci.areal_bym2 — disease risk on a map of areas (E18)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E18 from start to end.

A disease map for counts in areas (districts, counties). The count of each area is Poisson around its expected count times a relative risk rr. The log of rr is an intercept, plus a covariate effect, plus an area effect u. The kind setting selects the prior of u:

kind Area effect u poisson No area effect iid Independent effects with sd sigma icar An intrinsic CAR (ICAR) on the graph of neighbours: each effect is close to the mean of its neighbours car A proper CAR with alpha ~ Uniform(0, 1). alpha is often near 1, and then the intercept mixes slowly bym2 A scaled ICAR plus independent effects. sigma is the total sd and rho is the share that follows the map

For bym2, the model divides the ICAR by the square root of the scaling factor s of the graph (the geometric mean of the diagonal of the generalised inverse of the graph Laplacian). Thus sigma and rho have the same meaning on every map. The fit always keeps the log-likelihood of each area, so elpd_loo compares the kinds. Many Pareto k values are high, because each area has its own effect.

Inputs. area and area_ (categorical, fixed: the same areas twice), vertex (integer, fixed), the target cases(area) (missing values are permitted), expected(area) (the expected count, for example age-standardised), one covariate(area), adjacency(area, area_) (1 for neighbours) and the polygon outlines ring_x(area, vertex) and ring_y(area, vertex) (NaN padded; a NaN inside a row starts a new ring).

Islands. An area without neighbours makes the BYM2 scaling factor undefined, and under an ICAR its effect gets no information from other areas. The islands setting selects what happens:

  • link_nearest (default): the model links each such area to the area with the closest polygon vertex. Then it links each remaining separate piece of the graph in the same way. The links are in learned["links"].
  • isolate: the graph stays as it is. Only iid and icar accept this.
  • error: a graph with more than one piece stops the fit with SCHEMA_INVALID.

Outputs. cases(area) (the expected count expected × rr, or a Poisson draw), rr(area) (the relative risk), p_exceed(area) (1 when rr is more than exceed_threshold in a draw, so its mean is the probability) and effect(area) (u). The bundle keeps the map for the plots in constant_data: ring_x, ring_y, adjacency (the graph that the model used, with the links), centroid(area, xy) and smr(area) (observed ÷ expected). Thus sci.area_map draws the maps (use observed: smr for the raw ratio) and net.graph draws the graph at the centroids.

Score modes. A score needs only the area labels. expected and covariate come from the fit when the payload does not give them. A payload can change them (for example, a different covariate). simulate draws a new map of area effects for each draw from the fitted sigma, rho and alpha, and then new counts. A hand-written sampler draws the ICAR, because pm.ICAR cannot draw values. Areas that are not in the fit stop the score with UNSEEN_LEVELS.

Leave-areas-out. A mask_block split over area removes the counts of the held-out areas from the likelihood, but the areas stay in the graph. The model then predicts them from their neighbours.

Setting Default Meaning kind bym2 poisson, iid, icar, car or bym2 islands link_nearest link_nearest, isolate or error covariate_scale 10 The model divides the centred covariate by this value. b1 is the effect of one unit center_covariate true Subtract the mean of the covariate intercept_sd, slope_sd 1, 1 Prior sd of b0 and b1 sigma_scale 1 Half-normal scale of sigma rho_alpha, rho_beta 1, 1 Beta prior of rho (bym2) exceed_threshold 1 The threshold of p_exceed

from_challenges reads scotland_lip.geojson: the 56 districts of Scotland with the lip cancer cases from 1975 to 1980, the expected cases and aff (the percentage of workers in agriculture, fishing and forestry). The adjacency is queen contiguity from the polygons (117 edges), as in the notebook. Orkney, Shetland and the Western Isles have no neighbours, and link_nearest links them to Caithness, Orkney and Ross-Cromarty. Use graph="rook" for shared border segments, or graph="published" for the hand-edited WinBUGS list of scotland_lip_adjacency.csv. With kind: bym2 the AFF effect b1 is 0.41 (0.67 with iid), rho is about 0.8, and 19 districts have P(rr > 1) > 0.95. The fit takes a few seconds.

Typed errors: SETTINGS_INVALID for bym2 or car on a graph with more than one piece, and for simulate of an ICAR with isolated areas. SCHEMA_INVALID for counts that are not whole non-negative numbers, for an expected count that is not more than zero, and for a graph with islands when islands is error.

docs.title: sci.fisher_kpp — a reaction-diffusion PDE (E50)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E50 from start to end.

The Fisher-KPP equation du/dt = D d²u/dx² + lam u (1 - u) moves and grows cells into a scratch wound. The model solves the equation in the model graph (explicit Euler in pytensor.scan, zero flux at the edges). The counts are Poisson. With delay: true, the movement and the growth start slowly after the scratch (tanh(beta t)).

Inputs. t (integer hours, policy extend), x (float positions in µm, equal spaces, fixed) and the target count(t, x). The first time is the initial condition. The likelihood does not use it. Each time after the first must be on the Euler grid.

Outputs. density(t, x) (a field: time on the rows, position on the columns) and the scalar wave_speed (2 sqrt(D lam), µm/h). A forecast continues the PDE to later times.

Setting Default Meaning steps_per_hour 10 Euler steps for each hour delay true Multiply the movement and the growth by tanh(beta t) max_extension 4 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach diffusivity_median, growth_median 1000, 0.05 Prior medians of D (µm²/h) and lam (1/h) capacity_mu, capacity_sigma 122, 15 Prior of the capacity K (cells for each column) cfl_quantile 0.99 The prior quantile of D that must keep the Euler steps stable

If the Euler steps are not stable at the cfl_quantile of the prior of D, the model stops with SETTINGS_INVALID. The message gives the smallest steps_per_hour that is stable.

docs.title: sci.traction_force — cell forces from gel movement (E60)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E60 from start to end.

Fourier-transform traction cytometry as a Gaussian inverse problem. The data are a displacement field of a soft gel. The output is the traction field that the cells apply. NUTS samples only the noise sd and the prior spectrum. The model integrates the field out, with one closed-form likelihood for each Fourier mode. At score time, the model draws each traction field exactly with two FFTs for each posterior draw.

Inputs. component (categorical x, y), row and col (integer, fixed) and the target displacement(component, row, col) in µm. The raster must have no missing pixels. Thus the model has no split: evaluate it in sample. With force_mask: true, the data also has a force_mask(row, col).

Outputs. traction(component, row, col) (a vector field, Pa), displacement_hat, and the scalars strain_energy (fJ) and contractility (µN).

Setting Default Meaning grid_um, young_pa, poisson 1, 10000, 0.49 Grid spacing (µm), Young's modulus (Pa) and Poisson ratio of the gel young_cv 0 Relative uncertainty of Young's modulus (0 = known) prior matern white (Tikhonov), smooth or matern field_draws 100 The number of traction fields to draw for each score force_mask false Sum the strain energy and the contractility inside force_mask only

The NOISE_SPECTRUM_MISMATCH diagnostic compares the power of the data in the finest modes with the model. Correlated noise from overlapping PIV windows causes it, and then the ranges are too narrow. challenges_settings(ds) gives the settings for the real pyTFM colony of from_challenges.

docs.title: sci.strong_lens — a galaxy-scale strong lens (E80)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E80 from start to end.

A pixel forward model of a strong gravitational lens in a telescope image. The mass is a singular isothermal ellipsoid with an optional external shear. Rays from each pixel (and from sub-pixels) go back to the source plane. The source and the lens light are Sérsic profiles, and the model applies the PSF of the image. The model integrates the linear light amplitudes out in closed form. A staged search for the mode starts the sampler, and NUTS samples near that mode with a Laplace preconditioner.

Inputs. row and col (integer, fixed, row 0 at the bottom), the target image(row, col), the inverse variance weight(row, col) (0 leaves a pixel out) and a constant psf(psf_row, psf_col) with odd sides. With use_mask: true, the data also has a bool mask(row, col). The model also reads tree datasets (capabilities.input is tree): select the image node in data.nodes. When the tree has a /psf node with psf(psf_row, psf_col), the fit uses that PSF. Otherwise it uses the flat psf. With psf_source: tree, the flat input needs no psf and the /psf node is required.

Outputs. model_image(row, col) (a field, grey scale), source(source_row, source_col) (the source on a source-plane grid), the scalar einstein_radius (arcsec) and, when z_lens and z_source are set, einstein_mass (solar masses). The fit keeps the critical curve, the caustic and the cut of each posterior draw as the derived group critical_curves. In simulate mode, the model makes new noisy images from the posterior.

Setting Default Meaning pixel_scale 0.05 Pixel size (arcsec) subsample 2 Rays for each pixel along each axis lens_light_components 2 Sérsic profiles of the lens galaxy light (0 to 2) external_shear true Add an external shear to the mass noise_correlation 0 Correlation of the noise between neighbour pixels (drizzled images) theta_e_median, theta_e_log_sd 1.0, 0.5 Log-normal prior of the Einstein radius n_starts 5 Starts of the search for the mode source_grid, source_half_width 30, 0.45 Size of the source-plane grid (pixels, arcsec) curve_draws 100 Posterior draws with critical curves psf_source auto auto: the /psf node of a tree dataset, else the flat psf; tree: only the /psf node

The model has no LOO (loo_valid is false). from_challenges reads the HST F814W image of SDSS J1627-0053 (an 81 × 81 cutout and a PSF from the star stamps). On that image the posterior Einstein radius is 1.223 ± 0.001 arcsec. The fit takes approximately 5 to 7 minutes.

docs.title: sci.heat_plate — temperature of a heated plate (E51)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E51 from start to end.

The 2-D steady heat equation of a thin plate. Heat moves in the plane of the plate (conductivity k) and goes out through the two faces (h) and the outer edges (h_edge). A part eta of the heater power goes into the plate. The model divides the plate into square cells (finite volumes). This gives a linear system A(θ) u = eta q for the rise u above the room. The model solves the system for each run in the model graph (pytensor.tensor.linalg.solve). The readings are Normal around T_room + u with the noise sigma.

The field is linear in the heater powers. Thus one fit predicts the field of any new heater layout. To do this, score a payload with new run labels and their heater_power.

Inputs. run (categorical, policy new_levels), y and x (float cell centres in cm, equal steps, square cells, fixed), the input heater_power(run, y, x) in W and the target temperature(run, y, x) in °C. Cells without a sensor have no value (NaN). The fit uses only the cells with a value. The model declares these NaN in structural_missing, so the scorecard check data.missing does not count them. With use_insulation: true, the data also has a bool insulation(y, x): True where the back face of the cell has insulation.

Outputs. field(run, y, x) (a field with a frame for each run, in °C) and the scalar spread_length (sqrt(k δ / 2h), cm). predict gives the steady field. simulate gives simulated sensor readings in all cells (the field plus the noise). The pointwise log-likelihood has one value for each reading. Thus elpd_loo works when the spec keeps it (keep: {log_likelihood: true}).

Setting Default Meaning thickness_mm 5 Thickness of the plate (mm) room_temperature 20 Temperature of the room (°C) use_insulation false The data has insulation(y, x) insulated_back_loss 0.1 Back-face loss under insulation, as a part of the loss without insulation k_median, k_log_sd 50, 0.5 Log-normal prior of the conductivity k (W/m/K) h_median, h_log_sd 10, 0.5 Log-normal prior of the face coefficient h (W/m²/K) h_edge_median, h_edge_log_sd 10, 0.7 Log-normal prior of the edge coefficient h_edge eta_alpha, eta_beta 40, 4 Beta prior of the heater efficiency eta sigma_scale 0.5 Half-normal scale of the sensor noise sd (°C)

The notebook simulates its data, so E51 has no data file. from_challenges() makes the calibration experiment of the notebook again with the same generator and seed: a 40 × 20 cm plate on 24 × 12 cells, three runs with one 10 W heater each and twelve sensors. The readings are the same as in the notebook. On these data, E51_SPEC_YAML (4 × 1000 draws, nutpie) gives k = 59.1 ± 2.7, h = 9.05 ± 0.42, eta = 0.910 ± 0.040 and a spread length of 12.8 cm in approximately 45 s. These values are the same as in the notebook. h_edge stays near its prior (6.9 ± 3.7; the true value is 15): few sensors are near an edge.

The model stops with SCHEMA_INVALID when the cells are not square, when the positions do not have equal steps, when the fit data has no reading or when use_insulation is set and the data has no insulation. A new layout without heater_power gives MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE. Cells that are not on the fitted plate give UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.title: sci.turing_pattern — Turing patterns from early images (E61)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E61 from start to end.

The Schnakenberg activator-substrate system makes spots or stripes (a Turing pattern). The model gets its rates from images of the activator that you take while the pattern starts to grow. In this phase the growth is linear. Thus each Fourier mode of the images is a complex Gaussian, and the modes are independent. The model groups the modes by their integer |k|² and uses a Woodbury identity. Thus the likelihood needs only 2 × 2 algebra for each wavenumber, and it is exact for the linear dynamics. The model finds the mode first, and NUTS samples near that mode with a Laplace preconditioner.

The units have no dimensions. Lengths are in units where the activator diffuses at a rate of 1. The parameters are the supply s = a + b, the activator share rho = a / s, the diffusion ratio d, the reaction scale g, the initial noise s0 and the camera noise sigma. The priors are those of the notebook.

Inputs. t (float, extend: the time since the start of the pattern, t > 0), y and x (integer, fixed) and the target activator(t, y, x). The raster must be square, with an even number of pixels on each side, and must have no missing pixels. The model treats the square as periodic.

Outputs.

  • pattern(t, y, x): a field with a frame for each time. In predict and evaluate, it is a draw of the activator at the requested times, given the fitted images. In simulate, it is a new pattern from the nonlinear spectral solver, with camera noise.
  • settled(y, x): only in simulate. The pattern of each run at settle_time.
  • growth(wavenumber): the dispersion relation (the growth rate of each wavenumber).
  • p_turing: 1 when the draw meets the Turing conditions, else 0. Its mean is the probability.
  • wavelength: the wavelength 2π / k_m of the fastest-growing mode.
  • turing_space(b_supply, a_supply): a field. Its mean is P(Turing) for each pair of supply rates.

The posterior also has a, b, wavelength, max_growth and p_turing. With fit.keep.log_likelihood: true, the bundle keeps the log-likelihood of each Fourier mode (log_likelihood/activator(chain, draw, mode)). The modes are independent, thus elpd_loo over the modes is valid.

Setting Default Meaning box_length 100 The side of the square in the length unit of the model k2_max 1.5 Use only the Fourier modes with a squared wavenumber less than this value max_extension 2 Image times after the fit that a prediction can go to d_median, d_log_sd 10, 1 Log-normal prior of the diffusion ratio initial_noise_median, camera_noise_median 0.001, 0.001 Prior medians of s0 and sigma field_draws 40 Posterior draws for each score simulate_draws 4 Nonlinear runs for each simulate score simulate_dt auto Time step of the spectral solver (default min(0.025, 0.1 / (g (1 + s²)))) settle_time 300 Time of the settled pattern in simulate wavenumber_max, wavenumber_points 1.2, 120 Largest wavenumber and points of the growth(wavenumber) output a_max, b_max, supply_points 0.6, 3, 60 Largest supply rates and grid points of the turing_space(b_supply, a_supply) output precondition true Sample near the mode with a Laplace preconditioner (the model does not change)

E61 part A has no data file: the notebook simulates its four 128 × 128 images (t = 4, 8, 12, 16). from_challenges and notebook_dataset() do the same simulation, and NOTEBOOK_SPEC_YAML fits it with the sampler settings of the notebook. The 89% intervals are d 17.7–24.6, g 0.90–1.07, b 0.85–1.04 and a 0.057–0.130 (the notebook gives 17.7–25.2, 0.90–1.08, 0.84–1.04 and 0.054–0.133). The truth is 20, 1, 0.9 and 0.1.

Typed errors: SCHEMA_INVALID for missing pixels, a raster that is not square or times that are not after the start. SETTINGS_INVALID when no mode has |k|² less than k2_max, or when the spectral solver diverges in simulate (set a smaller simulate_dt). forecast and counterfactual give MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED. To predict later images, use predict with the next times. The NONLINEAR_REGIME diagnostic shows when the images are more than 10% from their mean, because then the linear likelihood is not correct.

docs.title: sci.storm_localisation — molecule positions in STORM frames (E58)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E58 from start to end.

Single-molecule localisation microscopy (STORM, PALM, dSTORM). The data are the raw frames of an EMCCD camera. The model finds isolated spots and gives the position of each molecule with an error bar in nm. Detection, camera calibration and the patches use NumPy and scipy.ndimage at fit time. Then NUTS fits all patches in one model. Each patch has one emitter with its own position, photons, background and PSF sd. The image of the emitter is a Gaussian PSF that is integrated over each pixel (erf). The counts are Poisson.

Camera. An EMCCD at high gain doubles the variance of the photon counts. The effective counts z = round((ADU - offset_adu) / scale_adu) are Poisson with a mean of half the photons. scale_adu is twice the EM gain. Set offset_adu and scale_adu together. If you do not set them, the model fits the photon-transfer curve of the frames: the robust temporal variance of each pixel against its median, without the brightest 10 % of the pixels. This calibration needs pixels with a range of background brightness. A small crop over one bright structure is not sufficient. For such data, calibrate on a larger field and set the two values.

Detection. The model subtracts the per-pixel time median from each frame, smooths with a Gaussian (smooth_px) and keeps the connected regions above threshold_sd robust noise sds. A blob is isolated when no other blob is in its patch_px × patch_px patch and it has min_blob_px to max_blob_px pixels. The fit uses max_spots isolated blobs, evenly spaced in frame order.

Inputs. frame, row and col (integer, fixed; rows and columns are consecutive pixel numbers) and the target frames(frame, row, col) (int32, ADU). The frames must have no missing values. Thus the model has no split: evaluate it in sample.

Outputs.

  • x, y (spot): the position in nm. It is the column (row) number times pixel_nm.
  • photons, background (photons per pixel) and psf_sd (nm) of each spot.
  • render(render_y, render_x): the super-resolution image (a field). Each draw puts each spot at its drawn position as a small Gaussian. The mean of the draws is the usual image where each localisation is a Gaussian with its own error.
  • patch_fit(spot, py, px): the effective counts of each patch (a field with a frame for each spot). With kind: predictive, these are Poisson draws.
  • frames_hat(frame, row, col): the camera image in ADU. Inside a fitted patch it is offset_adu + scale_adu × patch_fit. Outside the patches it is the per-pixel time median. evaluate compares it with the frames. Spots that the model did not fit count as misfit.

The bundle also keeps posterior_predictive/patch_fit (ppc_draws draws) and observed_data/patch_fit. Thus sci.image_residuals shows the data, the fit and the residuals of each spot. The bundle keeps predictions/render (score_draws draws) as well, so sci.point_pattern (the positions with error ellipses over render) and sci.field_map draw the super-resolved image from the fit alone. A whole long movie, such as the 2,000 real frames, is too large for the in-sample evaluate (see PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE below).

Setting Default Meaning pixel_nm 100 Size of a camera pixel in the sample (nm) kind flat Background in each patch: flat, or plane (a log-linear slope in x and y) offset_adu, scale_adu unset Camera offset (ADU) and ADU per effective count; unset: from the frames max_spots 200 Isolated spots to fit threshold_sd, smooth_px 5, 1 Detection threshold (robust sds) and smoothing (px) patch_px 11 Side of each patch (odd, px) min_blob_px, max_blob_px 13, 39 Size limits of a fitted blob (px) amplitude_band 0, 1 Quantile band of the blob amplitude to fit photons_median, photons_log_sd 1500, 1 Log-normal prior of the photons psf_sd_px, psf_log_sd 1, 0.2 Log-normal prior of the PSF sd (px) position_sd_px 2 Prior sd of the position around the blob centre (px) background_photons, background_log_sd unset, 0.5 Log-normal prior of the background; unset: twice the median effective count gradient_sd 0.05 Prior sd of the background slopes (kind: plane) score_draws, ppc_draws 40, 20 Posterior draws in a score, and predictive patch draws in the bundle render_px_nm 16 Pixel size of render (nm, at least 1)

To compare flat and plane by elpd_loo, fit both with fit.keep.log_likelihood: true. The pointwise values are per patch pixel, and the two kinds use the same patches. The PATCH_MISFIT diagnostic warns when the Pearson χ² per patch pixel at the posterior mean is more than 1.5.

Typed errors:

  • SETTINGS_INVALID: only one of offset_adu and scale_adu, an even patch_px, min_blob_px > max_blob_px, or a bad amplitude_band (refused when the settings are parsed, before the data is read); a render of score_draws draws at render_px_nm with more than 50 million values (refused at the start of the fit).
  • SCHEMA_INVALID: missing frames or pixels, rows or columns that are not consecutive, fewer than 3 frames, frames smaller than a patch, no spot above the threshold, no isolated spot, or frames that cannot calibrate the camera.
  • UNSEEN_LEVELS: a score with frames, rows or columns that the fit did not have.
  • PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE: frames_hat for the scored frames has more than 50 million values. Score fewer frames, for example the frames with a fitted spot (constant_data/spot_frame).
  • MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED: forecast, counterfactual, simulate and filter.

from_challenges reads dannhauser2022_unc13_dstorm_roi.npz: 2,000 frames of 40 × 40 pixels (127 nm) of a dSTORM recording of Unc-13 at a Drosophila synapse. Its attributes keep the camera calibration of the notebook (offset 457 ADU, 13.86 ADU per effective count), from the photon-transfer curve of the full 200 × 200 field. challenges_settings(ds) gives these values as settings. The detector finds 4,192 blobs, as in the notebook. With amplitude_band: [0.45, 0.55] and max_spots: 1, the fit is the spot of the notebook (blob 12, frame 5): x = 4.46 ± 0.05 px, about 2,160 photons, a PSF sd of 125 nm and a position error of 7 nm. 200 spots take approximately one minute with nutpie (4 chains of 1,000 draws). On these frames, kind: plane has more than one mode for approximately 8 % of the spots (spots at the edge of the crop, or near a bright spot outside the patch). Then the chains do not agree. Use flat for these frames. The model does not do the multi-emitter selection, the Laplace fits for the full movie or the blink counting of the notebook.

docs.title: sci.ibp_features — shared parts of small images (E31)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E31 from start to end.

A latent feature model for small images, for example handwritten digits. Each image is the average image plus the features that it owns, plus Gaussian noise: x = mu + z A + e. Each z is 0 or 1. The prior of z is an Indian buffet process (stick-breaking, truncated at K = n_features): alpha ~ Gamma, nu_k ~ Beta(alpha, 1), pi_k = nu_1 ... nu_k. The model sums z out exactly over the 2^K patterns of each image (a pm.Potential). Thus NUTS samples only the feature images A, the sticks, alpha and sigma_A. Each extra feature doubles the time, so n_features is 10 or less.

Inputs. digit (categorical, fixed), y and x (integer, fixed, row 0 at the top) and the target ink(digit, y, x) from 0 (blank) to 1 (full ink). An empty value is a pixel that the model does not see. With shown_mask: true, the data also has a bool shown(digit, y, x). The fit does not use a pixel where shown is false, but the bundle keeps its value for comparison. The average image mu is the mean of the images with no hidden pixels.

Outputs. ink_hat(digit, y, x) (a field for each digit, grey scale): the expected image given the seen pixels. Where the model did not see a pixel, this is the completion. The predictive kind draws a pattern and the noise. features(feature, y, x) (a field for each feature, diverging scale) gives the change of ink that each feature adds to the average image. feature_prob(feature) gives pi_k, and owns(digit, feature) gives the probability that each image owns each feature. A score uses only the pixels that the bundle keeps, never the target values in the score data. Thus a held-out pixel cannot get into its own prediction.

Setting Default Meaning n_features 8 Truncation K (1 to 10). Each image sums over 2^K patterns kind fixed_noise fixed_noise: the pixel noise is noise_sd; free_noise: the model learns it (HalfNormal(1) prior) noise_sd 0.25 Pixel noise sigma_X. It sets the level of detail: a smaller value makes more features useful alpha_shape, alpha_rate 1, 1 Gamma prior of the IBP mass alpha feature_scale_sd 1 HalfNormal scale of sigma_A, the scale of the feature images start digits digits: all chains start, without jitter, at half of K random images with nu = 0.8; default: the jittered start of the engine score_draws 200 Posterior draws for each score shown_mask false Read shown(digit, y, x) and hide the pixels where it is false truncation_warn 0.05 Warn when the mean of the last pi_K is more than this value

Start. From the default start, some chains can go to a trap: all pi_k go to zero and the images use no features. Then no feature gets a gradient again. The digits start prevents this (the notebook does the same). The engines pymc, nutpie and the external NUTS bridges use the start point with no jitter (EnginePlan.initvals and jitter=False).

Diagnostics. The posterior of A has many modes, as in a mixture model. Chains usually find different features, so expect r-hat and ESS warnings for logpi and sigma_A. The predictions of the chains are almost the same. TRUNCATION_BINDS warns when the last pi_K is not small: more features would be used. FEATURES_COLLAPSED warns when a chain has no features.

Splits and comparisons. digit is fixed: a score can use only the digits of the fit. To complete a new image, add it to the data with its unseen pixels empty, and fit again. To hold out halves of images, use a mask_block split over [digit, y] with block: {y: 4}. With fit.keep.log_likelihood: true, the bundle keeps the log-likelihood of each image. Then elpd_loo compares n_features, noise_sd and kind. With fit.keep.posterior_predictive, the bundle keeps replicate images for sci.ppc_image_grid and sci.image_residuals.

from_challenges reads the UCI optdigits of pymc-challenges as the E31 notebook does: 30 training digits for each class and 20 test digits for each class by 13 other writers, 8 × 6 pixels, ink from 0 to 1. The visible mask hides the bottom half of each test digit.
