The learned.heldout field of the fit gives the completion score of those halves (the mean log predictive density for each digit and the RMSE). The E31 spec of the export (K = 8, noise_sd = 0.25, 4 chains of 1000 draws, all 500 digits with the test bottom halves hidden by the mask) completes the test halves with an RMSE of 0.284 and −0.70 nats for each digit. The fit takes approximately 10 minutes with the pymc engine, and the convergence checks warn, as the notebook predicts. The notebook fits the 300 training digits only and gives 0.283 and −0.3. The export spec also fits the top halves of the test digits, so its log density differs. A separate fit on the 300 training digits only, as in the notebook, gives 0.283 and −0.34 nats in approximately 4 minutes.

docs.title: sci.colour_naming — how the speakers of a language name colours (E77)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E77 from start to end.

The World Color Survey asked the speakers of 110 languages to name 330 colour chips. This model fits the naming of one language. The probability that a speaker gives term t to chip c is a softmax over the terms. The logit of each term is a quadratic surface in CIELAB colour space: a multinomial logistic regression on 10 standardised features (1, L, a, b, L², a², b², ab, La, Lb). The weights W are zero-sum over the terms (ZeroSumNormal(w_sd)).

  • kind: pooled gives all speakers the same naming. The likelihood uses the chip × term counts.
  • kind: hierarchical gives each speaker an intercept and linear weights (L, a, b) of their own, around the weights of the language: W_s = W + sd z_s, with sd ~ HalfNormal(sd_scale) and z ~ ZeroSumNormal(1). A term that only some speakers use gets a large sd on its intercept.
  • features: grid_line and features: grid_circle use the place of the chip on the printed palette (row and hue column) instead of its colour. grid_line treats the hue as a line, and grid_circle treats it as a circle. Fit the variants with elpd_loo in a workflow to compare them.

Inputs. speaker (categorical, policy new_levels, strategy hyperprior), chip (integer, fixed) and the target naming(speaker, chip). The target holds the term labels as text. An empty cell is a speaker who gave no answer. The chip variables are lab_l, lab_a, lab_b (the CIELAB colour) and grid_row, grid_col (the place on the palette; WCS rows A to J are 0 to 9 and the greys are in column 0). The model orders the terms from the most used to the least used.

Outputs.

  • p_name(speaker, chip, term): the probability that the speaker gives the term to the chip. A fitted speaker keeps their own effects. A new speaker gets new effects in each draw, so the mean over the draws is the prediction for a new speaker. With kind: predictive, each draw holds one sampled term (one-hot). The evaluate mode always uses the probabilities.
  • p_term(term, lightness, hue): the share of the speakers of the language who give the term to the chip, on the palette grid (a field with one frame for each term). The fit averages new_speakers simulated speakers in each draw. A grid cell without a chip is empty in the fitted model and 0 in a score.
  • mode_term_rgb(chip, rgb): each chip in the display colour of its most probable term in the draw. The display colour of a term is the CIELAB mean of the chips where the term is most probable. The row and col coords put the chips on the palette for sci.swatches. The observed panel paints each chip with the term that most speakers gave.
  • p_top(chip): the share of speakers who give the chip its most probable term.
  • k_eff_speaker and k_eff_language: the effective number of colour categories of one speaker and of the language, exp of the mutual information between chip and term.

The fitted model keeps these language-level outputs for every draw. Thus the fit-time plots (sci.field_map, sci.swatches) show them without a score. The pointwise log-likelihood has one value for each chip (the sum over its speakers). Thus elpd_loo is leave-one-chip-out, and the variants have the same points. Use the categorical metrics (log_score, accuracy, accuracy_lift, brier) with a leave_group_out split on speaker: they score the held-out speakers as new speakers.

Setting Default Meaning kind hierarchical hierarchical (speaker effects) or pooled features cielab cielab, grid_line or grid_circle w_sd 3 Prior sd of the zero-sum weights sd_scale 1 Half-normal scale of the sds between speakers n_random 4 The number of leading features with speaker effects (the intercept and L, a, b) hue_columns the largest grid_col The number of hue columns around the circle (grid_circle) new_speakers 20 Simulated new speakers in each draw for the language-level shares score_draws 200 Posterior draws that one score uses

from_challenges(path) reads wcs_naming.npz and the three WCS tables next to it. It takes one language (language=77, Nafaanra) and keeps the major terms (used by at least a third of the speakers). All other terms become other. NAFAANRA_SPEC_YAML holds out the same 9 speakers as the notebook. On Nafaanra the pooled fit scores the held-out speakers at -0.392 nats for each answer, and the hierarchical fit gives 1.92 effective categories for one speaker and 1.84 for the language.

The model stops with SCHEMA_INVALID when the naming has fewer than 2 or more than 40 terms, a chip has no CIELAB colour, or two chips have the same palette place. It stops with SETTINGS_INVALID when kind: hierarchical has only one speaker, or n_random is larger than the number of features (refused when the settings are parsed). Chips that are not in the fit give UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.title: sci.cmb_field — the CMB sky behind a mask (E79)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E79 from start to end.

Field-level inference of a temperature map of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Each pixel of the sky is a parameter. The model samples the sky together with the power spectrum in bins (bandpowers). Masked pixels have no data term, and each pixel has its own noise level. Thus the model needs no correction for the mask, as a simple spectrum estimate does.

The sky is a Gaussian random field on a flat, periodic torus. The torus is the map plus a border of border pixels without data on each side, because a real patch does not repeat at its edges. The prior power of each Fourier (Hartley) mode is the reference spectrum after the beam, the pixel windows and aliasing, times exp(q_b) for bin b. q_b has a flat prior.

The sampler is not NUTS. It is the Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler of the notebook, in NumPy:

  1. A constrained realisation of the sky for the current bandpowers. Preconditioned conjugate gradients (CG) solve one linear system. The preconditioner is dense below ell_dense and diagonal above it.
  2. A draw of each bandpower from its inverse-gamma distribution, given the sky.
  3. A rescaling move for each bin (Metropolis). It helps in the bins where the noise is larger than the signal.

tune sets the burn-in iterations and draws the kept iterations of each chain. All chains run together. The fit is deterministic for a given seed.

Inputs. row and col (integer, fixed, row 0 at the bottom) and multipole (integer, fixed, 0, 1, 2, ...). The target temperature(row, col) is in µK, with NaN where the mask removes a pixel. noise_sd(row, col) is the noise sd of each pixel (µK). reference_dl(multipole) is the reference spectrum D_ℓ = ℓ(ℓ+1)C_ℓ/2π in µK². With pixel_window: true, the data also has pixel_window(multipole), the pixel window of the source map (for example HEALPix).

Outputs. sky(row, col) and temperature_hat(row, col) are fields (diverging colours). sky is a sky map for each of field_draws posterior draws. temperature_hat is the same map, plus noise with noise_sd for kind: predictive. bandpower(bin) (µK²) and bandpower_ratio(bin) have the coords ell, ell_low and ell_high on bin. The scalars log_amplitude and tilt compare the bandpowers with the reference: they come from the exact Gaussian posterior of q_b = log A + tilt · log(ℓ_b / tilt_pivot), with the bins below tilt_max_ell. The fit keeps the mean and the sd of each pixel over all kept Gibbs draws as the derived group sky_moments. In simulate mode, the model makes skies of a new patch with the spectrum of each posterior draw, plus noise. The mean of a new patch comes from the spectrum too (a few µK), not from the vague mean_prior_sd prior of the fitted patch's mean.

Setting Default Meaning pixel_arcmin, beam_fwhm_arcmin 7.5, 5 Pixel side and FWHM of the Gaussian beam (arcmin) pixel_subsamples 8 Point samples along each side that a map pixel is the mean of (1: no box window) pixel_window false The data has pixel_window(multipole) bin_edges the 26 bins of the notebook Multipole edges of the bandpower bins projection gnomonic gnomonic: correct the multipoles for the mean stretch of a tangent-plane map; flat: no correction border 8 Pixels without data around the map on the torus ell_dense 300 Modes below this multipole get the dense preconditioner cg_tol, cg_max_iter 1e-5, 5000 Stop rule of CG rescale true Use the rescaling move tilt_pivot, tilt_max_ell, tilt_prior_sd 500, 1450, 0.5 The amplitude-and-tilt summary field_draws 40 The number of sky maps to draw for each score n_alias 3 Aliased replicas folded into the prior power of each mode mean_prior_sd 100 Prior sd of the patch mean (µK) in the fit q_init_sd 0.3 Sd of the dispersed chain starts of the log bandpowers

The model has no LOO (loo_valid is false), because all pixels share one latent field. To compare projection: gnomonic with flat, compare the bandpowers, the amplitude and the tilt. The diagnostic CG_NOT_CONVERGED shows that a solve stopped at cg_max_iter. Then the large-scale bandpowers can be too low.

Typed errors: SCHEMA_INVALID when a variable or a dim is missing, when all pixels are masked, when noise_sd is not positive at an unmasked pixel, when reference_dl is negative or all zero, or when the map is smaller than 8 × 8 pixels. SETTINGS_INVALID when a bin has no mode on the torus, when the torus has more than 512 × 512 pixels, or when ell_dense puts more than 2,500 modes in the dense preconditioner.

from_challenges(path, patch="lmc") reads the Planck 2018 SMICA patch around the Large Magellanic Cloud (or patch="north") from planck_smica_patches.npz and the Planck best-fit spectrum from planck_theory_tt.txt. It prepares the map as the notebook does: 128 × 128 pixels of 7.5 arcmin, a pixel is usable only if all its samples are inside the common mask (16.5% of the pixels are masked), and the noise sd is the local rms of the half-mission half-difference map. PLANCK_SPEC_YAML is the notebook fit (4 chains of 80 iterations, the first 16 are burn-in). It takes approximately one minute. On this patch, the log amplitude is −0.017 ± 0.022 and the tilt is −0.001 ± 0.028 (the notebook: −0.014 ± 0.023 and −0.009 ± 0.030). The pixel sd is 2.5 µK where there are data, 32 µK in the small holes and 89 µK in the hole of the LMC.

docs.title: sci.network_latent_space — who works with whom (E21)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E21 from start to end.

A model of an undirected graph. Each pair of nodes i < j has a tie or not (Bernoulli, logit link). The log odds have three parts:

  • alpha + x_ij beta: the pair covariates (homophily), for example the same office.
  • s_i + s_j: the sociality of the two nodes (how many ties each node has).
  • -||z_i - z_j||: the distance between the latent positions of the two nodes.

The kind setting selects the parts: covariates (the first part), sociality (the first two) or latent_space (all three). With covariates: false, the model has no pair covariates. kind: covariates with covariates: false is the Erdős-Rényi graph.

The distances do not change when the positions turn, flip or move together. Thus the raw positions z_raw do not converge, but each distance does. After the fit, the model aligns each draw to one reference with Procrustes analysis. The aligned draws are the posterior variable position. The reference is constant_data/position_ref. The fit then drops the raw draws z_raw and s_raw from the posterior (position and sociality hold them, with the same distances). Thus the convergence diagnostics and the plots core.convergence and core.posterior_forest use only identified quantities: alpha, beta, sigma_s, sigma_z, sociality, position and tie_prob, in that order.

Inputs. node and node_ (the same labels, fixed) and the target tie(node, node_): 1 for a tie, 0 for no tie, and a missing value when you do not know. The matrix must be symmetric. The likelihood uses a pair only when its two cells are not missing. With covariates: true, the data has dyad_cov(node, node_, cov) (cov is categorical, fixed). With node_groups: true, the data has node_group(node), an integer code for the colours of the plots.

Outputs.

  • tie_prob(node, node_): the probability of a tie (a field, 0 on the diagonal).
  • tie(node, node_): the probability, or a simulated graph with kind: predictive and in simulate mode. The graphs are symmetric. The random numbers belong to the pair, so a subset of the nodes gets the same ties.
  • degree(node): the ties of each node with the scored nodes (the node_ labels of the score data), expected or in a simulated graph. Score all the nodes for the degree in the graph: on a subset, degree counts only the ties inside the subset.
  • sociality(node) and position(node, latent_dim), when the kind has them.
  • graph_stat(statistic): statistics of each simulated graph (density, sd_degree, max_degree, isolates, triangles, transitivity, esp0, mean_geodesic, unreachable). esp0 is the number of ties whose two nodes have no shared neighbour. Compare them with the statistics of the data (posterior predictive checks). The statistics need simulated graphs of all the nodes of the fit. A request that names graph_stat in output.vars for a subset of the nodes, or for expected probabilities, fails with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED.

The posterior also keeps tie_prob (float32) for the plots of the fit, and constant_data/adjacency keeps the observed matrix. The fit always keeps the log-likelihood of each observed pair (dim dyad; the pairs are in constant_data/dyad_i and dyad_j). Thus elpd_loo is leave-one-pair-out, and the kinds of a workflow ladder use the same pairs in the same order. A mask_block split over [node, node_] holds out random cells. A pair is out of the fit when one of its two cells is held out.

Setting Default Meaning kind latent_space covariates, sociality or latent_space covariates true Use dyad_cov node_groups false The data has node_group latent_dims 2 Dimensions of the latent space (1 to 3) alpha_mu, alpha_sigma -2, 2 Normal prior of the intercept beta_sigma 1 Normal prior sd of each covariate effect sociality_scale, latent_scale 1, 2 Half-normal priors of sigma_s and sigma_z procrustes_iters 10 Passes of the Procrustes alignment

from_challenges reads the coworker network of the 71 lawyers of the Lazega firm (378 ties) and makes the six pair covariates of the notebook: same office, practice, status, gender and law school, and the gap in years with the firm ÷ 10. office is the node group. With 4 chains of 1000 draws, the fit takes approximately 15 s (sociality) to 45 s (latent_space). elpd_loo is -1060 (Erdős-Rényi), -894 (covariates), -764 (sociality), -795 (latent_space without covariates) and -761 (latent_space), as in the notebook.

A score with fewer covariates than the fit stops with MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE. A node that the fit did not see stops with UNSEEN_LEVELS. The model has no forecast and no counterfactual mode. The mixed-membership block models of the notebook are not part of the model.

docs.title: sci.graphical_model — direct links between variables (E19)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E19 from start to end.

A Gaussian graphical model. The model measures the partial correlation of each pair of variables: the correlation that stays when all the other variables are held constant. A zero partial correlation means that the two variables have no direct link. A link (an edge) is present when |partial correlation| > threshold, and the model gives the probability of each edge. The model centres and scales each variable with the mean and the sd of the fit data.

There are two kinds:

  • dense (default): one multivariate normal with an LKJ prior on the correlations (eta = 2) and an Exponential(1) prior on the sds. The precision matrix comes from a triangular solve. This kind also predicts and simulates new samples.
  • neighbourhood: a sparse (regularised horseshoe) regression of each variable on all the others, in one model. The edge_rule setting makes the two coefficients of a pair into one edge: and (both pass the threshold), or (one passes) or rho (their symmetric combination). This kind conditions on the other variables of each sample. Thus it does not predict, simulate or evaluate new samples, and a spec with this kind has no split.

Inputs. cell (integer, policy new_levels with the pooled strategy: the samples are exchangeable, so new samples can be scored), var (categorical, fixed: the variables) and the target value(cell, var). With reference: true, the data also has a known network reference(var, var_) (1 = edge, constant). The fit keeps it in constant_data, and net.graph draws it below the learned edges.

Outputs. pcor(var, var_) (the partial correlations, a field with a diverging colour scale), edge_prob(var, var_) (the edge indicator of each draw: its mean is the edge probability) and, for kind dense, value(cell, var). With kind expected, value is the mean of each variable. With kind predictive or in simulate mode, it is a new sample from the model. The fit also keeps the posterior precision(var, var_) and the learned values edges (the pairs with a probability above 0.5), undecided_pairs (between 0.2 and 0.8) and pcor_sd_mean.

Setting Default Meaning kind dense dense (LKJ multivariate normal) or neighbourhood (horseshoe regressions) threshold 0.1 An edge is a partial correlation larger than this value (in absolute value) reference false The data has a known network reference(var, var_) standardise true Centre and scale each variable with the fit data log_likelihood auto The log-likelihood that the fit keeps for elpd_loo: joint (dense only) or conditional. auto is joint for dense and conditional for neighbourhood lkj_eta, sd_rate, mean_sd 2, 1, 1 dense: the LKJ shape, the rate of the sd prior and the sd of the mean prior expected_neighbours 2 neighbourhood: the prior guess of the links of each variable slab_alpha, slab_beta 2, 2 neighbourhood: the slab prior c² ~ InvGamma(alpha, beta) edge_rule and neighbourhood: and, or or rho

The fit keeps one log-likelihood value for each sample when fit.keep.log_likelihood is true. To compare a dense fit and a neighbourhood fit with elpd_loo, set log_likelihood: conditional on both. Then both values are the sum of the log densities of each variable given the other variables of the same sample.

Typed errors: SETTINGS_INVALID for log_likelihood: joint with kind neighbourhood (when the settings are parsed), or expected_neighbours that is not smaller than the number of other variables; SCHEMA_INVALID for score data without a cell dim, missing values, a variable with no variation, fewer than two variables, or reference: true without a reference variable; MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED for simulate, evaluate or predictive outputs with kind neighbourhood, and for forecast and counterfactual.

from_challenges reads the Sachs et al. (2005) flow cytometry data: the 853 cells with only the CD3/CD28 stimulus and 11 proteins (log of the intensity + 10). When sachs2005_consensus.txt is in the same directory, it adds the 20 edges of the consensus network as consensus. With observational=False, it reads all 7466 cells of the nine conditions (the notebook shows why you must not pool them). On the 853 cells, the dense model finds 8 edges with a probability above 0.5. Seven of them are in the consensus network. The fit takes approximately 40 seconds with nutpie. The neighbourhood model finds 6 edges, all in the consensus network, in approximately 2 minutes.

docs.title: sci.phylo_regression — traits of related species on a tree (E23)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E23 from start to end.

A regression of one trait of species on other traits. Related species are alike because they share ancestors, so the residuals are correlated by a phylogeny (a tree with branch lengths). The model reads the correlation from the shared branch length of two species. On standardised log values it is trait ~ MvNormal(intercept + X slope, K). The kind setting selects K:

kind Residual correlation iid None: sigma² I (the tree is not used) brownian Brownian motion along the branches: sigma² R (R = shared length ÷ tree depth) lambda Pagel's lambda: sigma² (lam R + (1 - lam) I), a tree part and a species part ou Ornstein-Uhlenbeck: eta2 exp(-rho D / 2T) on the distance D through the tree (T = tree depth)

For ou, the data identify only the Brownian rate rate = eta2 rho. Thus the default prior is on rate (ou_parameterisation: rate). This removes the ridge of the (eta2, rho) posterior.

Inputs. species (categorical, fixed) and node (integer, fixed). The target is trait(species); missing values are permitted. Each name in predictors is a variable on species with no missing values. The tree is four variables on node: parent (the position of the parent node, -1 at the root), branch_length (the branch above the node), is_tip and tip_label (the species name of each tip). Each species label must be a tip label. The tree can have unary nodes.

Outputs. trait(species): the trait of each species, predicted from the other species by Gaussian conditioning, in the units of the target. For a fitted species, the prediction leaves that species out. For a species without a trait value, it uses all fitted species. With log_target, the expected value is the conditional median. slope(predictor): the slopes. If the score data changes a fitted species' predictors, its prediction moves by the change in its regression mean. The fit also keeps posterior_predictive/trait(species) (the same predictions as conditional means, beside observed_data/trait for the sci.phylogeny plot) and the tree in constant_data.

Score modes. predict and evaluate predict each requested species from its relatives. simulate draws new traits for the requested species from the fitted parameters, without the observed traits. Use a mask_block split on species to hold out species: the model predicts them from the species that remain.

LOO. log_likelihood/trait holds the leave-one-out conditional density of each observed species, log p(y_i | y_-i), from Q = K⁻¹. Thus elpd_loo compares the four kinds correctly (a workflow can fit each kind and compare them). The marginal density of each species gives the opposite ranking.

Setting Default Meaning kind lambda iid, brownian, lambda or ou predictors [body, group_size] The predictor variables on species log_target, log_predictors true, true Take the log first (the values must be positive) standardise true Centre and scale by the fitted species intercept_sd, slope_sd 1, 0.5 Normal prior sd of the intercept and of each slope sigma_rate 1 Rate of the exponential prior of sigma lambda_alpha, lambda_beta 1, 1 Beta prior of lam ou_parameterisation rate rate: prior on eta2 rho; variance: priors on eta2 and rho rate_sd, rho_sd, eta2_sd 1, 5, 5 Half-normal prior sd for the ou parameters jitter 1e-6 ou: added to the diagonal of K

from_challenges reads primates301.csv and the tree primates301_tree.rda (an R ape::phylo object). It reads the R file without R. read_tree also reads Newick files. The dataset has the 186 species with a body mass and a group size; 151 of them have a brain volume. The tree is pruned to these species. With the notebook settings (4 chains of 1000 draws), the lambda fit gives a group-size slope of 0.027 ± 0.020 and lam = 0.954. The iid fit gives 0.123. elpd_loo is about 130 for lambda, 91 for brownian and ou, and 15 for iid.

Typed errors. SCHEMA_INVALID when a species has no tip of the same label, the tree has no single root or has a cycle, a predictor has missing values, a value is not positive for a log, or fewer than 3 species have a trait value. UNSEEN_LEVELS when a score requests a species that the fit did not see.

docs.title: sci.circular_regression — directions and times of day (E81)
docs.text:
Tutorial: E81 from start to end.

The data are angles: the direction that a wind comes from, or the time of day of a photograph. 359 degrees is next to 1 degree, and 23:59 is next to 00:01. Thus the model uses densities on the circle, as the E81 case study does. It has four kinds:

  • von_mises (default). The hour of the day and the day of the year are features: an intercept, cos and sin of k 2π h / 24 and of k 2π d / 365.25, and the products of the first daily harmonics with the first annual harmonic. The defaults give 19 features F. The natural parameters of a von Mises are η = F B (the canonical link). The mean direction is atan2(η₂, η₁) and the concentration is |η|. This model has one mode. It has no wrapped prior and no seam at ±π.
  • projected_normal. The angle of a vector z ~ N(F B, I).
  • regime_mixture. Two von Mises regimes (for example the easterly night wind and the westerly sea breeze). Each regime uses fewer features. A logistic gate on all features gives the probability of the second regime. The prior directions of the regimes keep their labels.
  • activity. A log-Fourier density for each group (species): log f(θ) = Σ aₖ cos kθ + bₖ sin kθ − log Z, with the prior aₖ, bₖ ~ N(0, (τ/k)²). The model uses only the sums of cos kθ and sin kθ for each group.

The priors of von_mises and projected_normal are N(0, intercept_sd = 2) on the intercepts and N(0, coef_sd = 1) on the other coefficients. regime_mixture does not use intercept_sd, as in the notebook. The intercept of regime r has the prior N(regime_strength (cos μᵣ, sin μᵣ), 1), with μᵣ from regime_directions_deg. The gate intercept has the prior N(0, gate_intercept_sd = 1.5). The other coefficients of the regimes and of the gate have the prior N(0, coef_sd). NUTS samples the coefficients. With fit.keep.log_likelihood: true, the bundle keeps the log density of each row (per radian). Thus elpd_loo compares the kinds on the same rows, for example in a workflow ladder von_mises → projected_normal → regime_mixture.

Inputs. obs (integer, policy extend, one row for each report) and the target direction(obs) in units. The regression kinds also need hour(obs) (hours since midnight, 0 to 24) and day(obs) (days since 1 January). The kind activity needs a categorical dim (group_dim, fixed) and the index <group_dim>_idx(obs). Remove rows with no direction (a calm wind has no direction) before the fit.

Outputs.

  • direction_hat(obs): the mean direction of the row, in units from 0 to one turn. With kind: predictive and in simulate mode, it is one simulated angle.
  • resultant(obs): the mean resultant length of the row (1: one direction, 0: no preferred direction).
  • density(frame, angle): the density per unit of units on angle_points angles (a field: frames on the rows, angles on the columns). For the regression kinds, a frame is a block of 24 / frames hours. Its density is the mean of the densities of up to rows_per_frame fit rows in that block (the rose diagram of the model). For activity, a frame is a group.
  • mean_direction(frame) and resultant_length(frame): the mean resultant vector of each frame.
  • activity only: activity_level(frame) (1 / (2π max f), the part of the day that the group is active) and overlap(frame, frame_) (the area under the lower of two densities, a field).

The fit also keeps the fields density(frame, angle) and, for activity, overlap(frame, frame_) in the posterior. They have the same values as in a score. Thus sci.field_map and sci.profile_bands show the densities (and, with var: overlap, the overlaps) in the plots of a fit run.

With fit.keep.posterior_predictive, the bundle keeps simulated angles theta (radians, 0 to 2π) and the observed theta in observed_data. sci.rose uses them in its default settings: it shows the observed rose with the range of the model. The default settings use the orientation of mathematics: 0 is at the right (east) and the angles increase anticlockwise. Thus a wind from the west (270°) is at the bottom. For a compass or a clock (0 at the top, clockwise), pass clockwise: true to sci.rose in a plot.render step or in the plots request. For the density of each frame, use sci.rose with var: density, frame: frame and units set to the units of the data. The default rose of a score result reads direction_hat, which is in the units of the data, as radians. Pass var: direction_hat and units set to the units of the data.

Setting Default Meaning kind von_mises von_mises, projected_normal, regime_mixture or activity units degrees Units of the direction: degrees, radians or hours daily_harmonics, annual_harmonics 3, 2 Harmonics of the hour and of the day of the year interaction_harmonics 2 Daily harmonics multiplied by the first annual harmonic intercept_sd, coef_sd 2, 1 Prior sd of the intercepts (not for regime_mixture) and of the other coefficients regime_directions_deg, regime_names [90, 250], [easterly, westerly] regime_mixture: prior directions and names of the two regimes regime_daily_harmonics, regime_annual_harmonics 2, 1 regime_mixture: features of each regime regime_strength 2 regime_mixture: prior mean concentration of each regime (the length of the prior mean of its intercept) gate_intercept_sd 1.5 regime_mixture: prior sd of the gate intercept group_dim group activity: the dim of the groups harmonics, tau_sd, grid_points 16, 2, 256 activity: Fourier terms, prior scale of τ, angles of the sum for Z frames, angle_points, rows_per_frame 8, 72, 200 Blocks of the day, angles and fit rows of the density output score_draws 400 Posterior draws for each score

from_challenges reads the hourly wind reports of Santa Barbara airport (2021–2023). It removes the calm reports and uses Pacific standard time (UTC − 8). ksba_spec_yaml(ds) holds out 2023 as the notebook does. On the 12,023 reports of 2021–2022, elpd_loo is −17,385 (the notebook: −17,385). The mean log score of 2023 is −1.517 for each report (the notebook: −1.517). from_challenges_activity reads the camera-trap times of Barro Colorado Island for the ocelot and five species that it hunts. With BCI_SPEC_YAML, the overlap of the ocelot and the agouti is 0.30 (the notebook: 0.30).

direction_hat and mean_direction are circular outputs (OutputDecl.circular, with their period attr: 360, 2π or 24). Their score summaries are on the circle: the circular mean, and intervals centred on it in [0, period). The holdout metrics of evaluate are circular: the point is the circular mean of the draws, mae, rmse and bias use the error wrapped to half a turn (359° against 1° is an error of 2°), coverage_<p> and interval_width_<p> use central intervals of the draws around the circular mean (an interval may cross 0), and crps uses the arc distance. mape, smape, wape and r2 are skipped. For a proper score of the whole density, use elpd_loo, or CircularRegressionModel().holdout_log_score(bundle.model, ds) for the log score of held-out rows. Errors: SCHEMA_INVALID for a missing direction, an hour out of range or a bad group index; MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE when the score data have no hour or day; SETTINGS_INVALID for more interaction harmonics than daily harmonics.

docs.title: OpenAPI explorer v0.2
docs.text:
This page shows the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the /v1 API. Redoc renders the document. The document is the committed file apps/web/openapi.json. A script makes it from the FastAPI app of the server and the mapi_spec.api models (uv run python apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py). CI fails when the file is different from the server. A running API serves the same document at /openapi.json.

Open full screen Download openapi.json

The explorer loads nothing from outside this site. The script scripts/vendor_redoc.py copies the Redoc bundle (version 2.5.4) into the repository. The script does a check of the integrity of the npm tarball and pins the SHA-256 of the bundle. A Content-Security-Policy on the page permits scripts, styles, images and requests from this site only.

For descriptions of the conventions, idempotency, server-sent events and the errors of each endpoint, read the HTTP API reference. For a full example, read the HTTP API guide.

docs.title: Plots reference (mapi-plots)
docs.text:
mapi-plots has two parts. Each part has different dependencies:

Install Modules Imports Runs in mapi-plots mapi_plots.sanitize, mapi_plots.templates mapi-spec, jsonschema (JSON only) API server, runner, notebooks mapi-plots[recipes] mapi_plots.convert, mapi_plots.recipes, mapi_plots.packs, mapi_plots.examples + altair, plotly, numpy, pandas, pyarrow, xarray runner images, notebooks

An import-linter contract makes sure that the sanitizer and the templates do not import numpy, pandas, xarray, pyarrow, altair, plotly or mapi_sdk. import mapi_plots loads no large modules, because the exports are lazy.

docs.title: The PlotSpec envelope
docs.text:
The contract package mapi_spec.plots defines the envelope:

id: core.ppc_fan                    # [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}
title: Fit and forecast
kind: vega-lite                     # or plotly
spec: {...}                         # Vega-Lite JSON, or Plotly {data, layout, frames, config}
datasets:                           # referenced BY NAME only
  fan: {kind: inline_arrow, data: <base64 Arrow IPC stream>, rows: 84}
  big: {kind: data_ref, path: ui/plotdata/fan.arrow, format: arrow}
bindings: {x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}   # templates only
schema_version: v6.4.1
persona: both                       # guided | expert | both
caption_plain: "The line is the model's median estimate ..."
provenance: {recipe: core.ppc_fan@1.0.0, bundle_id: ..., generated_at: ...}
  • Vega-Lite references data with {"data": {"name": "fan"}}.
  • Plotly references a column with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"} in a data-array attribute. It also uses this reference in arrayOk attributes, for example marker.color. The part before the first . is the dataset. The remaining part is the column (trace0.marker.color → dataset trace0, column marker.color). The JSON Schema of the reference is mapi_plots.sanitize.PLOTLY_REF_SCHEMA. It is also in the file mapi_plots/sanitize/schemas/plotly-ref.schema.json:
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "urn:mapi:schema:plotly-dataset-ref:v1",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {"$ref": {"type": "string",
    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{0,63}\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]{0,127}$"}},
  "required": ["$ref"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • The maximum size of each inline Arrow dataset is 2 MiB of base64. Recipes write datasets in a compact format (float32, int32, dictionary-encoded strings). Timestamps are UTC milliseconds.

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot, check_plot, sanitize_spec, SanitizeLimits

result = sanitize_plot(doc)            # PlotSpec | dict | JSON str | bytes
result.plot                            # validated, sanitized PlotSpec
result.changes                         # list[Issue] (severity info): HTML stripped, $schema pinned ...

issues = check_plot(doc)               # errors + changes, never raises
spec, changes = sanitize_spec("plotly", figure_dict)   # bare spec, no envelope

SanitizeError is a MapiError. err.issues lists all violations, up to max_issues. Each violation has these items:

  • An RFC 6901 pointer.
  • A message that the platform wrote.
  • The rule, in context["rule"].
  • Text from the user, if there is some. This text is only in untrusted_text.

err.rules is the set of rules that fired. The error code is the most severe code that is present:

Code HTTP Rules PLOT_UNSAFE 422 url_data, href, external_image, tile_map, proto_key, script_url, css_url, expression, format_type, config PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 too_large, too_deep, too_many_nodes, string_too_long, array_too_long SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 parse (JSON that is not valid, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity) SCHEMA_INVALID 422 schema, envelope, dataset_ref, typed_array

Changes use the rules html_stripped, schema_url and template_pruned. Changes are not errors.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: SanitizeLimits field Default max_document_bytes 16 MiB (the full PlotSpec, with the inline Arrow data) max_spec_bytes 2 MiB (the spec member) max_depth 48 max_nodes 200 000 max_string_bytes 64 KiB (the envelope sets the limit for inline Arrow payloads) max_array_items 100 000 max_expr_chars 2 000 max_typed_array_bytes 8 MiB max_issues 50

docs.title: Vega-Lite rules
docs.text:
1. $schema must be an official Vega-Lite v5 or v6 URL, or not present. The sanitizer sets it to v6.4.1.
  2. The spec must be valid against the vendored Vega-Lite v6.4.1 JSON Schema (draft-07, local $refs only).
  3. Do not use these items: a url key at any location, href, and the image mark. formatType can only be number, time or utc. Do not enable config.customFormatTypes.

  4. Expressions must use only Vega functions from the allow list. Expressions are:

    • expr, calculate and filter/test strings, and their and/or/not compositions.
    • Each …Expr key, for example labelExpr.
    • Filters in brackets in selection event streams.

    The sanitizer rejects these items: method calls, this/new, assignment, statements, template and regex literals, and \u/\x escapes. It also rejects non-ASCII characters outside strings, and computed member access with a key that is not a literal. It also rejects browser globals (window, document, fetch, globalThis …) and event.view.

docs.title: Plotly rules
docs.text:
1. The top level has only data, layout, frames and config.
  2. The sanitizer does a check of trace types, attribute names and value types against a table. This table comes from the official plotly.js 4.1.1 plot-schema.json. It has enumerations, flag lists, subplot ids, colour scales and info arrays. It also has subplot keys of the xaxis2 type, and template keys of the annotationdefaults type.
  3. Unknown attributes are errors. In layout.template, the sanitizer removes unknown attributes and tile-map sections, and reports them.
  4. Data arrays are inline lists, dataset references or plotly.py typed arrays ({dtype: i1|u1|u1c|i2|u2|i4|u4|f4|f8, bdata, shape?}). The sanitizer does a check of the base64, length and shape of typed arrays.
  5. The sanitizer rejects these items:
    • Tile-map traces and subplots.
    • Image sources that are not data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64. This rule also applies in the relayout arguments of updatemenus/sliders.
    • url/href/topojsonURL keys.
    • Network config options.
  6. Strings can keep only <b> <i> <br> <sub> <sup>. The sanitizer removes attributes and escapes a stray <. <extra> stays in hover templates.

docs.title: Vendored schemas
docs.text: File Source Regenerate vega-lite-v6.4.1.json https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.4.1.json (byte-for-byte) scripts/vendor_schemas.py --download plotly-structure-v4.1.1.json made from plotly.js@v4.1.1/dist/plot-schema.json same VENDORED.json source URLs and SHA-256 digests (a unit test does a check of them) same

docs.title: Templates (mapi_plots.templates)
docs.text:
resolve_bindings(bindings, schema, *, optional=()) -> dict[channel, BoundField | list[BoundField]]
apply_template(plot, schema, *, optional=(), title=None) -> PlotSpec
template_issues(plot, schema, *, optional=()) -> list[Issue]
Binding Resolves to Vega-Lite type dim:<name> a dim of the schema time → temporal, numeric → quantitative, ordered/index → ordinal, other → nominal role:<role> the one variable with that role (lists for tooltip) from the dtype var:<name> that variable from the dtype coord:<name> a coordinate (dim or not) from the dim, or nominal if it is not a dim stat:<name> a summary statistic column (mean, hdi_90_lower, q5 …) quantitative

render_template(template, data, schema=None, *, group=None, value=None, optional=()) (extra recipes) also makes the dataset from an xr.Dataset or a tree group. The default schema is attrs["mapi_schema"]. If that is not available, the function infers the schema. It gets the roles from the role attribute of each variable.

docs.title: Recipes (mapi_plots.recipes)
docs.text:
get_recipe(id) -> Recipe                 # bundled recipes (core + packs)
standard_recipes() -> list[Recipe]       # entry point  mapi.plots: core
mapi_plots.packs.mmm.mmm_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: mmm
mapi_plots.packs.ml.ml_recipes()         # entry point  mapi.plots: ml
mapi_plots.packs.sci.sci_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: sci (Plotly)
mapi_plots.packs.net.net_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: net (Plotly)
mapi_plots.packs.causal.causal_recipes() # entry point  mapi.plots: causal (v0.13)
Recipe.render(data, **settings) -> PlotSpec       # also Recipe(data, **settings)
Recipe.catalog_entry() -> PlotCatalogEntry        # id, version, persona, required groups/representation

# what the runner calls for outputs.plots: never raises for a single bad plot
report = render_plots(tree, ["core.ppc_fan", "mmm.response_curves@^1"],
                      registry=None, options={"core.ppc_fan": {"facet": "market"}})
report.plots          # sanitized PlotSpecs
report.issues         # skipped plots: REF_UNRESOLVED / SCHEMA_INVALID / USER_CODE_ERROR
                      # (warnings) and PLOT_UNSAFE (error)
report.to_json()      # plots.json sidecar body

To write your own recipe, use the decorator. The result works with Registry.register and the mapi.plots entry-point group:

import altair as alt
from mapi_plots.recipes import Figure, RecipeSettings, named, recipe


class Settings(RecipeSettings):
    var: str = "y_hat"


@recipe("acme.weekly_total", title="Weekly total", settings=Settings, persona="guided")
def weekly_total(inp, s: Settings) -> Figure:
    ds = inp.require("summary")
    frame = ds[s.var].sel(stat="mean").sum("market").to_dataframe().reset_index()
    chart = alt.Chart(named("weekly")).mark_line().encode(x="date:T", y=f"{s.var}:Q")
    return Figure(chart, {"weekly": frame}, caption=f"Total {s.var} per week.")

A recipe can also return a Plotly figure (plotly.graph_objects.Figure or a {data, layout, frames} dict) in Figure.chart. Recipe.render then sends it through from_plotly with the same title, caption, persona and provenance. The recipe can also give its own DataFrames in Figure.datasets. The traces then refer to their columns with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"}. The function plotly_plot applies the inline-text rules to the string columns of these DataFrames.

docs.title: Extra core recipes
docs.text:
These recipes are in the core pack (mapi_plots.recipes.extras, classification, training and loo, Vega-Lite):

Recipe What it shows core.pair A corner plot of up to max_params scalar parameter elements. Below the diagonal: thinned draws of each pair. On the diagonal: a histogram of each parameter. Red points are divergent transitions (sample_stats.diverging). core.ridge One density for each level of dim, sorted by the mean, with a dot for the mean and a bar for the HDI. Each curve has the same peak height. core.rank_matrix P(rank = k) for each item, sorted by the expected rank, and the matrix of P(row above column). Input: draws (…, item). core.calibration Continuous targets: the PIT-ECDF difference with a simultaneous envelope (simulated). Targets with values 0 and 1: a reliability diagram with a binomial band for each bin and a histogram of the predicted probabilities. A point prediction (no draws, values from 0 to 1) uses the reliability diagram. A point prediction of a target that is not 0/1 gives an error, because the PIT check needs draws. core.state_sequence The observed series (points coloured by the most likely state) above the stacked state probabilities. Input: probabilities (…, state, time) with or without draws, a score summary with a stat dim (the plot uses mean), or integer state draws (chain, draw, time). The default variable is smoothed_prob, state_prob or filtered_prob. Without select, the plot fixes each other dim at its first level and the caption names that level. core.roc_pr Two panels: the ROC curve with the diagonal of a random guess, and the precision-recall curve with the base rate. The titles give the AUC and the average precision. With draws, the caption gives the 90% interval of the AUC (up to 500 draws). Multiclass (v0.14): one-vs-rest curves in a colour for each class, the macro AUC in the title, and the number of classes that are not drawn in the caption. core.confusion The 2 × 2 table of the actual class and the predicted class at the threshold, as counts or as the share of each actual class. The caption gives the accuracy, the precision, the recall, the specificity, the F1 score and the threshold. Multiclass (v0.14): a K × K table of the most probable class (a maximum of 30 classes; the other classes are (other)), with the accuracy and the macro F1. core.loss_curve The raw loss (light) and a rolling mean (dark) over the steps, one line for each level of an extra dim (at most 8). The caption gives the first and the last smoothed value and the change over the last 10% of the steps. core.loo_pit The LOO-PIT ECDF difference with a simultaneous envelope (when posterior_predictive and observed_data are present), and the PSIS Pareto k of each observation with lines at 0.5 and k_threshold.

The recipes core.calibration, core.roc_pr and core.confusion share one input rule. They look for the prediction in the posterior_predictive, predictions and draws groups (with draws, or one probability for each cell), then in summary (stat mean, point or median). The actual values come from observed_data or observed. The two arrays are aligned on their shared cells, and cells with NaN are left out. For a binary target, the target must have two values. The larger value is the positive class unless you set positive. The predictions must be from 0 to 1. From v0.14, core.roc_pr and core.confusion change to multiclass when the prediction has a class dim (meaning: class_probability, the probabilities of the classes add up to 1) or when the actual target has more than two values. The actual classes can be text or whole numbers (3.0 is the class 3).

docs.title: Marketing-mix recipes of v0.12
docs.text:
All of these recipes accept draws with a sample dim or with chain and draw dims. A recipe that does not find its group or variable raises RecipeDataError. The runner then skips only that plot.

Recipe Input What it shows core.energy sample_stats.energy(chain, draw) The centred marginal energy and the energy transitions (two histograms), and the BFMI of each chain, mean(diff(E)²) / var(E). The caption names the chains below bfmi_threshold. core.prior_posterior variables with chain/draw dims in prior and in posterior A density of the prior and of the posterior for each parameter cell, ranked by |Δmean| / sd(prior). The caption gives the overlap of each panel. An overlap above little (0.8) means that the data adds little. mmm.roi response_curves: contribution at multiplier 1 divided by current_spend (other dims summed). marginal_cost.marginal_roi_total, else a central difference on the grid around 1 A forest of the ROI of each channel (median and HDI), the mROAS next to it, and a break-even line mmm.adstock adstock: weight(sample, channel, lag), optional mean_lag The weight of each lag with an HDI band, one line for each channel (or one panel with facet) mmm.waterfall contributions: channel_contribution and every other variable as a component The total of each component over the fit window as steps to the total result mmm.spend_effect response_curves: contribution at multiplier 1 for each draw and current_spend The share of spend and the share of effect of each channel side by side mmm.lift_tests the lift_tests group: observed(test), observed_sd(test), model(chain, draw, test) and the coords channel, estimand, start, end, geo Each test (value ± z standard errors) next to the model estimate (HDI) mmm.effectiveness effectiveness(sample, channel, time), time_varying(channel) The effect of one unit of spend in each period with an HDI band mmm.mediation mediation: direct(sample, channel), indirect(sample, channel, mediator) Stacked direct and indirect effects of each channel, with the share that the mediators carry mmm.cross_effects cross_effects: psi(sample, pair) and the coords source, target, kind A forest of each cross-effect with its kind

docs.title: Causal pack (causal.*) v0.13
docs.text:
The causal models (causal.impact, causal.synthetic_control, causal.did) write their results to bundle groups that these recipes read. See Causal models. All recipes accept draws with a sample dim or with chain and draw dims. A recipe that does not find its group raises RecipeDataError. The runner then skips only that plot. The recipes send medians and intervals for each period to the sanitizer, not the draws.

Recipe Input Settings What it shows causal.impact impact: actual, counterfactual, effect, cumulative_effect, post hdi_prob (0.9), unit (none: the sum over the unit dim), panels (series, pointwise, cumulative) Three panels on one time axis: the actual values with the median and HDI band of the values without the change, the effect in each period, and the cumulative effect in the effect window. A rule marks the start (and the end). The caption gives the total effect with its interval, the relative effect and the probability that the effect is more than zero. causal.pre_fit impact (the cells before the start) hdi_prob (0.9), unit The actual values against the band of the model before the change, with the RMSE, the MAPE and the part of the actual values in the band. The caption flags a part below 80%. causal.donor_weights donor_weights: weight(sample, unit, donor) hdi_prob (0.9), top (15), unit (none: one panel for each treated unit up to 4, else the first unit) Horizontal bars of the mean weight of each donor with HDI rules, sorted. The other donors are summed as "other donors". causal.event_study event_study: coef(sample, event_time), att, attrs reference hdi_prob (0.9) A point and an HDI rule for each event time, a zero line and a dashed rule between -1 and 0. The reference period is marked. The caption gives the average effect after the change and tells if the coefficients before the change include zero.

docs.title: Scientific-model pack (sci.*)
docs.text:
The sci.* recipes make Plotly figures for models with gridded outputs, vector fields, profiles and trajectories. They read draws (chain/draw or sample dims) from posterior, predictions or posterior_predictive. They read the actual values from observed_data.

Recipe What it shows sci.field_map One heatmap panel for each statistic of a gridded output. A slider and a Play button show one frame at a time. sci.vector_field The length of a vector as colours, arrows of the mean vector, and the sd of the length. sci.profile_bands The median and the 50% and 90% bands along along, one curve for each level of by, and the actual values. A slider shows one level with its bands. sci.ensemble Some draws as thin lines, the 90% band of all draws, the median and the actual values. sci.area_map A map of areas (polygons) coloured by the observed value, the mean, the sd and the probability that the value is above threshold. A cross marks each area where this probability is above mark_above. sci.phylogeny A tree of the tips (species) next to a strip with the estimate and its interval for each tip, and the observed values. sci.rose A polar chart of angles: a rose of the observed angles with the 90% range of simulated data in each sector, or a curve around the circle with its limits. sci.image_residuals The observed image, the model mean, the residual and the normalised residual (obs - mean) / sqrt(sd² + σ²), with a histogram of the normalised residuals against N(0, 1). sci.ppc_image_grid The observed image next to n_draws images from the model on one colour scale. With shuffle, the panels are in a random order and the caption names the real one. sci.swatches Squares in the colours of an sRGB output (…, item, rgb) in [0, 1]: observed, mean and some draws. A map when the item dim has row and col coords. sci.power_spectrum A binned spectrum (…, bin) against a coord such as ell: median, 50% and 90% bands, a theory curve and the observed values with error bars. sci.point_pattern One dot for each point (localisation, event) at its mean position, an error ellipse for each point, and an optional image or intensity field below the points.

Data for the map, tree and polar recipes:

  • sci.area_map reads the outlines of the areas from ring_x(area, vertex) and ring_y(area, vertex). Fill the unused vertices with NaN. A NaN between points starts a new ring, for example an island. The first dim is the area dim. The optional adjacency(area, area_) matrix (not zero for neighbours) gives the lines of show_edges. The recipe finds these variables in observed_data, constant_data, a geometry group, the group of the output or the root. It draws the areas as filled shapes on axes with equal scales. It does not use a geographic projection or a base map. If the outlines have too many points, the recipe uses fewer points.
  • The Observed panel of sci.area_map reads observed, else the variable with the name of the output in observed_data. If there is none, the recipe reads the variable that the attr mapi_observed of the output names. A model sets this attr when it keeps the observed value under a different name. For example, sci.areal_bym2 keeps the raw SMR as smr for its output rr.
  • sci.phylogeny reads the tree from parent(node): the position of the parent node, or -1 for the root. The optional variables are branch_length(node) (default 1), is_tip(node) (default: the nodes that are not a parent) and tip_label(node). The tips match the levels of the output by label. If there are no labels, tip k (in node order) is level k.
  • sci.rose reads angles in units. One turn is 2π radians, 360 degrees, 24 hours or 365.25 days, or period. If the output has an angle dim (angle_dim, or a dim called angle, direction, hour and so on), the recipe draws a curve. Otherwise it counts the angles in bins sectors.

Notes on the image and spectrum recipes (mapi_plots.packs.sci_images):

  • sci.image_residuals and sci.ppc_image_grid need the observed image in observed_data, with the grid dims of the output. The recipe uses the variable with the same name, the observed_var setting or the only observed variable.
  • Draws from posterior_predictive already hold the noise of the data, so sci.image_residuals adds no σ to them. For a noise-free output (posterior or predictions), it uses sigma or a variable named sigma.
  • With log, sci.image_residuals shows the observed, mean and residual panels as log10. It computes the normalised residual and its histogram in the data's units, because σ is in those units.
  • sci.swatches writes the colours as #rrggbb text in the dataset. The plot sandbox does not change these colours in dark mode, because they are data.
  • Colours that a recipe takes from a colour scale (the groups of net.graph and sci.point_pattern, the classes of sci.area_map, the curves of sci.profile_bands) are also data. They do not change in dark mode, as a colour scale does not. All other colours come from the palette and have a dark variant.

Statistics of sci.field_map:

  • mean, median: the average value and the middle value of the draws.
  • sd: the uncertainty. A high sd shows where the data do not fix the value.
  • z: the mean divided by the sd. Values far from zero are clear.
  • q05, q95: the limits of the 90% interval.
  • draws: n_draws possible fields from the model.

The grid dims come from the settings. If you do not set them, the recipe uses the grid of the output (OutputDecl.grid). It reads the grid from the grid attribute of the variable or from the model manifest in the bundle. The colormap, log and origin settings also come from the grid when you do not set them. If the output has more dims than the plot uses, use select to pick one level of each, for example select: {species: 0}.

The size of a field plot has limits:

  • All the cells of a plot are in one dataset: x, y and one column for each statistic and frame. The recipe keeps this dataset below the inline Arrow limit (2 MB).
  • If the field has too many cells, the recipe calculates the average of each block of k × k cells. A cell with no value (NaN) stays empty. The caption tells the block size.
  • A field of 189 × 193 cells with six panels and one frame has its full resolution.
  • max_frames sets the maximum number of frames. The slider shows frames at equal intervals.

sci.point_pattern reads the variables x and y with one value for each level of the point dim. Draws give the posterior mean and an ellipse from the 2 × 2 covariance of the draws. A score summary gives its point statistic and an ellipse from its sd. Plain values use the sd_x and sd_y variables (or a radius variable, drawn as a circle) when they exist. The ellipse holds the position with probability level. The field is a gridded output (by default the first output with a grid), drawn below the points in the same units.

docs.title: Network pack (net.*)
docs.text:
Recipe What it shows net.graph A node-link drawing of the links above threshold (line width shows the value, blue and red show the sign, arrows show the direction) and a heatmap of the full matrix. Dotted lines and open squares show the known or observed links.

net.graph reads an edge variable with two node dims: the second dim has the name of the first plus _, for example (node, node_) or (var, var_). The values can be draws (the recipe uses the posterior mean), a score summary (its point statistic) or plain values. They can be probabilities, weights or partial correlations.

  • positions: a variable (node, latent_dim), for example the latent positions of a latent space model. The recipe uses the posterior mean of the first two coordinates. Without it, the recipe calculates a layout from the mean weights (a spectral start and seeded Fruchterman–Reingold steps). The layout puts strongly linked nodes near each other.
  • group: a variable with one value for each node (by default node_group or group). Categories get one colour each and a legend. Continuous values get a colour scale.
  • truth: a known or observed adjacency (node, node_). By default the recipe uses one from observed_data or constant_data.
  • threshold: by default 0.5 for values in [0, 1], else 10% of the largest absolute value. With draws, the tooltip at the middle of a link shows the share of draws above the threshold.

The plot sandbox shows the Plotly frames, sliders and updatemenus of these plots. In dark mode, it changes the palette colours of the traces to their dark variants, the same as for Vega-Lite. It also applies the theme to each polar subplot (barpolar, scatterpolar), for example in sci.rose.

The convergence diagnostics are rank-normalised split R-hat and bulk/tail ESS (Vehtari et al. 2021). The package calculates them with numpy. Tests make sure that the values agree exactly with ArviZ.

docs.title: Run protocol v0.2
docs.text:
This page tells how a run moves from the API to a sandbox and back. It gives:

  • the state machine of the run
  • the bootstrap object and the environment that an execution gets
  • the event stream that the runner writes
  • the output manifest, the checks on it at finalisation, and the signed bundle manifest
  • the storage layout
  • the ports and the environment variables of a local installation.

Each shape on this page is a Pydantic model or a constant in mapi_spec.run, mapi_spec.storage or mapi_spec.localdev. The API server, the executors, the runner and the tests all import them from these modules.

sequenceDiagram
    participant API
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant S as Object store
    participant X as Executor
    participant R as Supervisor (runner)
    participant W as Worker (plugin code)
    API->>API: CREATED → QUEUED (static validation, quota)
    D->>D: lease → DISPATCHING, intent row (run, attempt, nonce)
    D->>S: PUT bootstrap/{nonce} (RunSpec: signed URLs, HMAC key)
    D->>X: submit(env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE)
    X->>R: start execution → PROVISIONING
    R->>S: GET + DELETE bootstrap/{nonce}
    R->>W: spawn with scrubbed env (socketpair)
    R-->>API: stdout {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC per line) → RUNNING
    W->>R: progress / results
    R->>S: signed POST/PUT outputs + manifest.json
    R-->>API: "complete" event, exit 0
    API->>S: stat + list (metadata only), server-side copy → bundles
    API->>API: FINALIZING → SUCCEEDED, signed BundleManifest

docs.title: Run states
docs.text:
RunState values are in lower case on the wire. This page writes them in upper case.

State Meaning CREATED The API accepted the run. The static validation and the quota check are not complete yet. REJECTED Terminal. This state is for submissions that the static validation or the quota refuses. The current server does not make such runs. Refer to the note below the transition table. QUEUED The run waits for the dispatcher. DISPATCHING The dispatcher has the lease and wrote the intent row. The call to the executor is in progress. PROVISIONING The executor accepted the execution. No event came yet. RUNNING Minimum one verified event came. STALLED No event came for K × the progress interval. This is a warning, not a failure. The status API of the executor is the source of truth about the execution. FINALIZING The execution is complete. The control plane does a check of the outputs and copies them. SUCCEEDED Terminal. A verified bundle exists. PARTIAL Terminal, but you can resume the run. A verified partial bundle exists. The runner wrote it from checkpoints after a SIGTERM or at the deadline. FAILED Terminal, with one of these failure classes: user, resource_exhausted, infra, integrity, timeout or sandbox CANCELLING The user asked to cancel the run. The run waits for the executor to confirm. CANCELLED Terminal

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
mapi_spec.run.transition(state, trigger, actor=...) is a pure function. It returns the rule that matches, or it raises IllegalTransition. IllegalTransition maps to 409 CONFLICT. Callers save rule.target with a compare-and-set on the old state. If rule.new_attempt is set, callers also increase attempt and make a new nonce. A test compares the table below with the code for all 13 × 19 pairs of state and trigger.

From Trigger To Owner Failure class New attempt CREATED accept QUEUED api CREATED reject REJECTED api QUEUED lease DISPATCHING dispatcher DISPATCHING submitted PROVISIONING dispatcher, reconciler (orphan adoption) DISPATCHING infra_retry QUEUED dispatcher, reconciler yes DISPATCHING fail_infra FAILED dispatcher, reconciler infra PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED event RUNNING events PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED complete FINALIZING reconciler PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED infra_retry QUEUED reconciler yes PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED fail_user / fail_resource_exhausted / fail_infra / fail_timeout / fail_sandbox FAILED reconciler user / resource_exhausted / infra / timeout / sandbox RUNNING silence STALLED reconciler STALLED silence STALLED (no-op) reconciler FINALIZING event FINALIZING (no-op) events FINALIZING verified SUCCEEDED finalizer FINALIZING verified_partial PARTIAL finalizer FINALIZING fail_integrity FAILED finalizer integrity FINALIZING fail_infra FAILED finalizer infra every non-terminal state except CANCELLING cancel CANCELLING api CANCELLING cancel / event CANCELLING (no-op) api / events CANCELLING cancel_confirmed CANCELLED reconciler CANCELLING complete FINALIZING reconciler PARTIAL resume QUEUED api yes

A submission that is not valid makes no run. POST /v1/runs and the model :score action do the static validation before a run row exists. If the validation finds an error, the server refuses the request with a 4xx problem. The code of the problem is the code of the first error. The errors list gives each issue with its JSON pointer. The server keeps nothing, thus there is no REJECTED run and no run history for the request.

CREATED → reject → REJECTED stays in the table for a later server that records refused submissions.

All components obey these rules:

  • Events only move a run to RUNNING. All other transitions during the execution come from the reconciler. The reconciler is level-triggered and reads the status of the executor.
  • complete occurs when the executor reports exit code 0 or 16 and the complete event came. Then the finalizer reads OutputManifest.status and starts verified or verified_partial.
  • infra_retry occurs only after the control plane confirms that the old execution stopped. The cost limits the automatic retries (MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR times the estimate). A count also limits them (MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES). If a run used more than 30 minutes, there is no automatic retry without the consent of the user.
  • Late events. The events service ignores verified events for runs that are already terminal. All terminal states reject event.
  • A cancel of a FINALIZING run has no effect at the API. The table permits the transition, but POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel returns the run with no change. The execution is already complete. The finalizer can possibly have a version number already. It can also have copied write-once bundle objects.

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
The executor does not send credentials, URLs or keys through argv or the environment. The only values for each execution are MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE.

  1. The dispatcher writes an intent row (run, attempt, nonce). The nonce is 256 random bits, written as 64 lowercase hex characters (new_nonce()).
  2. The dispatcher writes a RunSpec to gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce} (mapi_spec.run.RunSpec, schema runspec.json).
  3. The dispatcher calls Executor.submit(RunSubmit, nonce). For all out-of-process executors, RunSubmit.payload stays empty. The executor sees only the run id, the attempt, the kind, the resource class, the timeout and the labels. All secret values go in the RunSpec.
  4. The supervisor resolves MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL, GETs the object, and deletes it immediately. Then it validates the object as a RunSpec. It starts the worker with worker_environ(), an allow-listed environment that has no MAPI_* variable. If the object is missing or not valid, the supervisor exits with code 2 CONFIG_ERROR.
RunSpec field Meaning schema_version mapi.runspec/v1 run_id, attempt, nonce, kind The identity of the run. Parent kinds (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign) never execute. tenant_id, project_id Always present (default in M1) spec, spec_hash, catalog_digest The resolved spec JSON (with pinned use: ranges), its canonical hash, and the catalog snapshot that the server used to resolve it inputs name → SignedGet{url, expires_at, generation, size, crc32c, md5_hash?}. The well-known names are dataset and bundle. Each URL is pinned to a generation and supports HTTP Range. The runner does a check of the size and the CRC32C after the download. If they do not agree, it exits with 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR. outputs name → SignedPut \| PostPolicy. manifest is a necessary write-once signed PUT for {prefix}manifest.json. artifacts is a create-only V4 POST policy on the attempt prefix with a content_length_range. It cannot replace an object that exists. Thus it cannot overwrite the manifest or replace an output after the runner wrote it. checkpoints is a POST policy on checkpoint_prefix. It is present only for runs that can write checkpoints. media (v0.14) is a create-only POST policy on media_prefix for the images and tables that the run logs. resume The checkpoint objects of the newest earlier attempt that wrote checkpoints, as SignedGets. The server ignores an attempt that stopped before its first checkpoint. checkpoint_prefix {attempt prefix}checkpoints/, or null media_prefix v0.14: {attempt prefix}media/, or absent. When outputs has media, its prefix must be media_prefix. hmac_key The event HMAC key of the run (new_hmac_key()), in base64. It has a minimum of 32 random bytes. The logs never show it: RunSpec.redacted() removes it and all URLs. limits RunLimits: log_line_bytes (4096), log_total_bytes (20 MiB), max_event_bytes (64 KiB), progress_interval_s (2 s), max_output_bytes and scratch_bytes (from the resource class), max_output_objects (10 000), and from v0.11 tracking (a TrackingLimits, see Tracking budgets) resource_class, deadline, created_at, labels The class (S/M/L/XL, and from v0.15 GPU), a hard UTC deadline, and metadata input_layouts v0.8: name → layout for dataset inputs that are not a plain dataset: tree (a data.tree.zip) or, from v0.15, collection (an image collection, see Image collections). An input that is not in the map is a dataset.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Variable Set by Value MAPI_RUN_ID executor, for each execution The run id MAPI_NONCE executor, for each execution 64 hex characters MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL executor, static for each Job or backend A template with exactly one {nonce}. Cloud: gs://mapi-prod-bootstrap/{nonce}. The execution service account reads it. This account can get and delete, but it cannot list. Local: http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}. MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN local executor only The bearer token of the exec principal of the GCS shim. This principal can get and delete in the bootstrap bucket. Never set in the cloud.

The worker gets only the variables of WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST. From v0.15 the list also has JAX_PLATFORMS, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, for the networks of mapi-jax.

RunnerEnv.from_environ() parses these variables and gives the name of each missing variable. RunnerEnv.resolved_bootstrap_url() puts the nonce into the template.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The worker cannot write to the real stdout. It sends reports to the supervisor through a socketpair. The supervisor captures the stdout and the stderr of the worker. It removes ANSI and control sequences. Then it writes one JSON object on each line to its own stdout:

{"mapi_event":{"attempt":1,"hmac":"5f0c…","payload":{"chains":[],"fraction":0.4,"phase":"sample"},"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","seq":12,"ts":"2026-10-15T09:31:00.123456Z","type":"progress"}}

Cloud Logging keeps each line as the jsonPayload of a log entry. The sink filter is jsonPayload.mapi_event:*. The platform compares the identity of the run with the label of the execution. The local executor reads the same lines from the stdout pipe of the supervisor. encode_event_line() and decode_event_line() implement the wire format:

  • A line that is not JSON, or JSON without mapi_event, is not an event. The platform ignores it.
  • A mapi_event object that is not valid, or a line of more than 64 KiB, raises InvalidEvent. This is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION.

Each event has these fields:

Field Rule run_id, attempt Must agree with the run and its current attempt seq Starts at 0 for each attempt and increases by 1 for each line. The receiver removes duplicates on (run_id, attempt, seq). Gaps are permitted, because the logs can lose entries. ts Has a timezone and is normalised to UTC type state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, metrics, params, tags, media (v0.14), complete or error payload Validated against the payload model for type. Refer to the table below. hmac Lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 with the hmac_key of the run

The data that the HMAC signs:

"mapi.run-event.v1" 0x00 ‖ canonical JSON of the event without "hmac"

Canonical JSON (canonical_bytes()) has these rules:

  • The model is dumped in JSON mode with the defaults.
  • The keys are sorted.
  • There is no whitespace.
  • The text is UTF-8 with no ASCII escapes.
  • Floats with integral values are written as integers.
  • NaN and Infinity are not permitted.

The verification uses a constant-time comparison (verify_event()). If an event fails the verification, the platform ignores it and counts a sandbox violation for that run. Such an event never changes the state of the run. Output manifests use the context tag mapi.output-manifest.v1. Bundle manifests use mapi.bundle-manifest.v1. Thus a signature from one domain is never valid in a different domain.

type Payload model Notes state StatePayload{phase, message?} The runner phases: bootstrap, load_inputs, validate, preprocess, fit, sample, score, evaluate, derive, plots, upload, done progress ProgressPayload{phase, fraction?, message?, eta_seconds?, chains[]} Maximum one in each limits.progress_interval_s. The platform writes it into one run_progress row (upsert). From v0.11, samplers fill chains (ChainProgress{chain, draws_done, draws_total, tuning, divergences, step_size?, num_steps?}). log LogPayload{stream, line, truncated, level?, fields?} One line, maximum log_line_bytes. After log_total_bytes, the run fails with SANDBOX_VIOLATION (log flood). The streams are stdout, stderr, system and, from v0.11, user. Only user lines have level and fields. diagnostic Diagnostic (mapi_spec) Goes into the scorecard warning WarningPayload{code, message, untrusted_text?} v0.15: GPU_UNAVAILABLE when a run of the GPU class sees no NVIDIA device. The run continues on the CPU. checkpoint CheckpointPayload{name, size, crc32c, segment, draws_done?} name is relative to checkpoint_prefix metric MetricPayload{name, value, step?, labels} One scalar, for example a holdout metric at the end of a fit. From v0.11, the platform also keeps it as a point of the metric series name. metrics MetricBatchPayload{t0, series[]} v0.11. Points of metric series. See Tracking events. params ParamsPayload{params[]} v0.11. Run params. The first value of a key is kept. tags TagsPayload{tags[]} v0.11. Run tags. The last value of a key is kept. media MediaPayload{key, kind, content_type, name, sha256, size, crc32c, step?, labels, width?, height?, caption?} v0.14. An image or a table that the supervisor uploaded below media_prefix. See Media. complete CompletePayload{status, manifest_name, manifest_crc32c, objects, total_bytes} The last event of a successful attempt (complete) or of an attempt with checkpoints (partial) error ErrorPayload{code, failure_class, message, untrusted_text?} code must be equal to failure_class.error_code

make_event(run_id, attempt, seq, payload, key=...) gets type from the payload model and signs the event.

docs.title: Tracking events v0.11
docs.text:
The events metrics, params and tags carry the tracking data of a run. The platform writes them into the tracking tables (metric points, series summaries, params and tags). It does not keep them in the event list. Thus, GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events does not return them. The event stream sends a tracking frame when they change (see HTTP API).

A metrics payload groups its points by series. A series is one metric key and one set of labels. The point lists are columns of equal length:

{"t0": "2026-10-15T09:31:00Z",
 "series": [{"key": "step_size", "labels": {"chain": "0"},
             "steps": [399, 400], "values": [0.32, 0.31], "ts_ms": [0, 250]}]}
Field Rule t0 A time with a timezone. The time of a point is t0 + ts_ms milliseconds. series 1 to 64 MetricSeriesBatch items key A metric key: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$. Use labels for qualifiers. labels A maximum of 8. Key: ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$. Value: ^[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{1,63}$. steps An integer (0 or more) for each point, or null for a scalar point values Finite numbers only. NaN and infinity are not valid. ts_ms An integer (0 or more) for each point

One metrics event has a maximum of 1000 points (MAX_POINTS_PER_EVENT). One params event has a maximum of 200 items, and one tags event has a maximum of 100 items. A param value is a boolean, an integer, a float or a text of a maximum of 6000 characters. A tag value is a text of a maximum of 1000 characters. A tag key that starts with mapi. is not valid.

An event line must not be more than max_event_bytes. split_for_events(payload, max_event_bytes) divides a payload into parts that each fit in one line. It divides by series first, then by points or items, and it keeps the sequence. Each part keeps 2048 bytes for the envelope of the event.

docs.title: Worker messages
docs.text:
The worker sends tracking data to the supervisor through the socketpair, with these messages (mapi_runner.channel):

Message Payload Rule metrics MetricBatchPayload The worker collects points for each series and sends them each flush_interval_s (1 s), or when 1000 points wait params ParamsPayload Sent with the next flush tags TagsPayload Sent with the next flush user_log LogPayload with stream user Sent immediately. Another stream is a protocol error.

The worker sends the last points before its result or error message. StartMessage gives the worker the TrackingLimits of the run.

docs.title: Tracking budgets
docs.text:
RunLimits.tracking (TrackingLimits) gives the budgets of each run. The worker, the supervisor and the server use the same budgets.

Field Default Meaning metric_points_per_series 10 000 Points in one series metric_points_total 500 000 Points in all the series of the run metric_series 1000 Different (key, labels) series params 5000 Params tags 100 Tags (also the maximum) log_lines 10 000 user log lines log_bytes 2 MiB Bytes of user log lines tracking_bytes 64 MiB Bytes of all tracking messages flush_interval_s 1.0 Seconds between two flushes of the worker (0.1 to 30)

When a run logs more than a budget, the worker and the supervisor do not keep the points or the items that are more than the budget. They count them. At the end of the run, the run gets one warning with the code TRACKING_BUDGET. The warning gives the reasons and the series with the most dropped points. The run does not fail.

tracking_bytes is a hard limit. If the worker sends more bytes of tracking messages than this limit, the supervisor stops the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION (tracking flood), like a log flood.

From v0.14, TrackingLimits also has the budgets of the media of a run:

Field Default Meaning media_items 1000 Different media items (key, labels and step) media_bytes 256 MiB Bytes of all media items of the run media_item_bytes 8 MiB Bytes of one media item (1024 to 8 MiB)

docs.title: Media v0.14
docs.text:
The media event tells the server that the supervisor uploaded an image or a table of the run. Like the tracking events, the server does not keep it in the event list. It writes a row of run_media, and the event stream sends a tracking frame with media: true.

A media item goes through these steps:

  1. The worker encodes the item (ctx.log_image, log_figure or log_table). It writes the bytes to {scratch}/media/<sha256>.<ext> (create-only) and sends a media message to the supervisor. StartMessage.media is false when the run has no media policy. Then the worker does not write files.
  2. The supervisor opens the file with O_NOFOLLOW (a regular file only), with the size limit media_item_bytes. It reads the bytes and deletes the file. It calculates the SHA-256 and calls check_media(kind, content_type, data).
  3. The supervisor uploads the bytes through the media POST policy to {media_prefix}<sha256>.<ext>. An item with the same SHA-256 in the same attempt is not uploaded again.
  4. The supervisor sends a media event with a MediaPayload.
  5. The server downloads the object from the runs bucket (a maximum of 8 MiB). It calculates the SHA-256 again, and does a check of the size, the format and the image size.
