It writes the bytes create-only to the bundles bucket at t/{tenant}/run-media/{run}/<sha256>.<ext> (run_media_store_key). Then it writes the row.

The sandbox never writes to a shared path. The runs bucket deletes run objects after 30 days. The copy in the bundles bucket stays until the tenant is deleted.

MediaPayload:

Field Rule key A metric key. Use labels for qualifiers. kind image or table content_type image/png or image/jpeg (kind image), application/json (kind table) name <sha256>.<ext> (.png, .jpg or .json): the object name below media_prefix. It must agree with sha256 and content_type. sha256 64 lowercase hex characters size, crc32c 1 to 8 MiB. The CRC32C that the store calculated for the upload. step, labels As for a metric point width, height Necessary for an image (1 to 4096). Not valid for a table. caption A maximum of 500 characters. It is untrusted text.

check_media (mapi_spec.media) accepts:

  • A PNG or a JPEG image of a maximum of 8 MiB, with a maximum of 4096 pixels on each side. sniff_image reads the size from the PNG IHDR chunk, or from the first JPEG frame header in the first MiB. It does not decode the pixels. GIF, SVG, WebP and other data are not valid.
  • A table: UTF-8 JSON of a maximum of 1 MiB that validates as a MediaTable (columns, and rows of equal length; a maximum of 10 000 rows, 64 columns and 200 000 cells; cells are numbers, booleans, text of a maximum of 1000 characters, or null).

The worker messages and the warnings for media:

Message or warning Meaning media (worker message, MediaMessage) file (<sha256>.<ext>), key, kind, content_type, step, labels and caption. One message for each item. MEDIA_IGNORED (warning) The run has no media policy. The supervisor ignores the media of the run (one warning). MEDIA_BUDGET (warning) The run logged more than media_items or media_bytes. The supervisor counts the items of the attempt. The server counts the items of all attempts and the items logged through the API. Each one drops the extra items and writes one warning for the attempt. MEDIA_INVALID (warning) The file is not a regular file, is too large, or check_media refused it. The text of the worker is in untrusted_text. MEDIA_UPLOAD_FAILED (warning) The upload failed. The run continues. MEDIA_REJECTED (warning, server) The server checks failed: the object is missing, or its SHA-256, size or format does not agree with the event. The server writes no row.

docs.title: Image collections v0.15
docs.text:
A run that reads an image collection gets more than one input for the dataset. For the dataset input dataset:

Input Object dataset manifest.parquet of the version dataset.info collection.json (CollectionInfo) dataset.pack.0000, dataset.pack.0001 … The packs, in the order of CollectionInfo.packs (pack_input(i)) schema schema.json, when present

RunSpec.input_layouts["dataset"] is collection. The server sets it for each input whose object name ends with /manifest.parquet. mapi_spec.collection has the names: info_input(prefix), pack_input(i, prefix) and part_input(i).

A pack is a zip file. Each entry is named <sha256>.<ext>. Its address is pack_digest(size, crc32c, md5): the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the store's own size, CRC32C and MD5 of the object. This is the same basis as the address of a dataset version. The runner calculates the digest of each signed pack URL again before it reads the pack. A pack without an MD5 or with a different digest stops the run with INTEGRITY_FAILURE. The runner reads the packs in ranges (HTTP Range), and it makes sure that each image has the SHA-256 of its name.

The finalizer of a collection ingest:

  1. reads and validates collection.json and schema.json;
  2. for each pack with source: upload, gets the stored size, CRC32C and MD5 of the pinned generation of its part.<i> input, calculates pack_digest again and compares it with the digest of the pack;
  3. copies the part to t/{tenant}/blobs/packs/{digest}.zip (create-only, the generation pinned);
  4. for each pack with source: base, makes sure that the base version has it.

The sandbox never writes to the shared pack path.

docs.title: Checkpoints of networks
docs.text:
From v0.15, a model that trains in epochs saves checkpoints as files (FileCheckpointSink). The names in checkpoint_prefix are:

Name Contents ckpt-<key>.weights.safetensors The weights of the network ckpt-<key>.opt.safetensors The state of the optimizer ckpt-<key>.meta.json The epoch, the step, the early-stopping state and the history

<key> has 16 to 64 lowercase hex characters (the fit key). The checkpoint event has segment = the epochs done and no draws_done. The samplers keep the names ckpt-<key>.draws.zarr.zip and ckpt-<key>.meta.json. The supervisor uploads .safetensors files with the content type application/octet-stream.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The supervisor exits with 0 only after it uploads the manifest and sends the complete event. failure_class_for_exit() gives the failure class of the code. All other non-zero codes are infra, for example 1 from a supervisor that crashed.

Code Name Failure class 0 OK — (success) 2 CONFIG_ERROR infra: the environment is bad, or the bootstrap is missing or not valid 10 USER_ERROR user: plugin code or user code raised an exception, or made output that is not valid 11 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED resource_exhausted: MemoryError, or the run used more than the scratch budget 12 INFRA_ERROR infra: the uploads or downloads of the supervisor failed after retries. (An INFRA_ERROR that the worker reports exits with 10.) 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR integrity: the size or the CRC32C of an input was not correct 14 TIMEOUT timeout: the run got to the deadline with no checkpoint to flush 15 SANDBOX_VIOLATION sandbox: log flood, output caps exceeded, or forged or oversized events 16 PARTIAL — (SIGTERM or deadline. The runner flushed a checkpoint and uploaded a partial manifest.) 137 KILLED resource_exhausted: SIGKILL, usually from the OOM killer. The platform offers "retry at class + 1" to the user. 143 TERMINATED timeout: the runner did not stop in the permitted time after SIGTERM

When the user cancels a run, the run is already in CANCELLING. Thus the exit code does not set the result, with one exception. A fit that writes checkpoints can get the SIGTERM. Then it flushes its last checkpoint, uploads a partial manifest, sends a partial complete event and exits with 16. The reconciler then starts complete from CANCELLING, and the finalizer verifies the partial bundle. Thus the run ends in PARTIAL, and you can resume it. All other exits end in CANCELLED.

docs.title: Outputs and finalisation
docs.text:
The runner uploads all outputs below its attempt prefix t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{attempt}/ in the runs bucket. It uses the artifacts POST policy. It streams each object and calculates CRC32C and MD5 during the stream. Last, it PUTs manifest.json, an OutputManifest that it signs with the HMAC key of the run:

{
  "schema_version": "mapi.output-manifest/v1",
  "tenant_id": "default", "project_id": "default",
  "run_id": "run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0", "attempt": 1, "kind": "fit",
  "status": "complete",
  "prefix": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/",
  "spec_hash": "sha256:…", "catalog_digest": "sha256:…",
  "inputs": {"dataset": {"generation": 3, "size": 1048576, "crc32c": "4waSgw=="}},
  "objects": {
    "bundle.zarr.zip": {"key": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/bundle.zarr.zip",
                        "size": 2097152, "crc32c": "AAAAAA==", "md5": "1B2M2Y8AsgTpgAmY7PhCfg=="}
  },
  "runner_version": "0.2.0", "created_at": "2026-10-15T10:20:00Z", "hmac": "…"
}

The key of each object must be equal to prefix + name. Names must not have empty, . or .. segments. The manifest must not list itself.

The hashes use the GCS conventions:

  • CRC32C is the base64 encoding of the 4-byte big-endian value (crc32c_to_base64()).
  • MD5 is the base64 encoding of the 16-byte digest.

The manifest is a claim. The control plane verifies it in the FINALIZING state. It does not read the content of the objects:

  1. Metadata only. The control plane lists the attempt prefix and does a stat of the objects. This gives the size, crc32c, md5Hash and generation that the server calculated.

  2. Compare. verify_output_objects(manifest, listing, expected_prefix=…) needs these conditions:

    • Each object in the manifest exists with the same size, CRC32C and MD5.
    • No unexpected object exists below the prefix. manifest.json, checkpoints/… and (v0.14) media/… are permitted.

    Each difference is an INTEGRITY_FAILURE issue. The run moves to FAILED(integrity), and the platform raises a security alert. 3. Validate sidecars. The control plane reads the JSON sidecars with size caps and validates them with Pydantic. The sidecars are diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json and coords.json, schema.json and summary.json for ingest, and catalog.json for describe. It also sanitizes the plots. 4. Server-side copy. The control plane copies each verified object into the bundles bucket below t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/. The copy pins source_generation to the verified generation and uses if_generation_match=0. Thus bundle objects are write-once. The execution service account has no access to this bucket. 5. Sign. The platform writes a BundleManifest and signs it. The manifest binds the tenant, the run, the base image, the overlay hash, the spec hash, the data hash, the catalog digest and each destination generation. The signature is: - M1 (local): KMS-EC-P256-SHA256 with a local P-256 key. The server keeps the key below MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/. This is an emulation of the KMS signer. Thus you can replace it with a real KMS key, and the signed bytes do not change. The server refuses bundles with the HS256 signature when it makes URLs. - v0.3 (M2): a Cloud KMS asymmetric signature on the same bytes.

    The control plane makes URLs to the bundle only after verify_bundle_manifest() is successful.

docs.title: Job payloads and object names
docs.text:
mapi_spec.jobs is the contract between the dispatcher and the runner. The dispatcher writes RunSpec.spec and gives the names of the inputs. The runner reads them and gives the names of the outputs. The two sides import the module. Thus, if you change the name of an input or change a payload, the type checks and the tests fail on the two sides.

Kind RunSpec.spec Inputs Outputs that the control plane reads ingest IngestJob (a mapping or the MFF preset. dataset and source are only for information.) upload data.zarr.zip, schema.json (DataSchema), summary.json (DataSummary), profile.json, preview.json ingest of a collection (v0.15) IngestJob with collection (CollectionIngest) manifest, part.0000 …, and with a base version base.manifest, base.info, base.pack.0000 … manifest.parquet, collection.json (CollectionInfo), members.bin, schema.json, summary.json, profile.json, preview.json, columns.json (optional), ui/explore/…. No data.zarr.zip. describe DescribeJob (image_digest) none catalog.json (Catalog) validate the resolved ModelSpec dataset, side.<name> validation.json fit the resolved ModelSpec (with pinned use: and dataset references) dataset, side.<name> bundle.zarr.zip, diagnostics.json, metrics.json (MetricsSidecar), plots.json, coords.json (ScoreMetadata.fit_coords), ui/… score the ScoreRequest bundle, bundle.manifest, dataset (the data of the request), scenario, side.<name>, history (v0.4: the fit dataset, for forecasts with future_covariates set to carry_last or seasonal_naive), inline.data / inline.scenario (v0.4: the inline XrJSON of an endpoint call, for use when dataset / scenario is not present) score.zarr.zip, result.json, summary.json (ScoreSummary, which the API puts in ScoreCallResult.summary), plots.json, ui/summary.arrow. Also ui/guided/forecast.json or ui/guided/counterfactual.json (v0.4). Also ui/fields.json (FieldsView) for the grid outputs of a predict, forecast or evaluate run. The default plots follow the shape of the outputs (see Runner), and grid outputs carry the attr grid evaluate / derive / render EvaluateJob / DeriveJob / RenderJob from the params of the run bundle, dataset (default: the fit dataset), side.<name>. plots for render. as the runner reference shows

side_table_input(name) makes side.<name>. SCORE_INPUTS maps the data and scenario fields of a ScoreRequest to their input names. A *.zarr.zip dataset can contain its raw DataSchema as JSON in the root attribute DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR (mapi_schema). Ingest writes this attribute. If an upload has this attribute, the upload keeps its dim policies, roles and units. The platform does not infer a schema for it.

inline.data and inline.scenario (mapi_spec.endpoints.INPUT_INLINE_DATA and INPUT_INLINE_SCENARIO) contain the XrJsonDataset JSON of an endpoint score call. The API keeps them in the quarantine bucket. The worker decodes them with the caps of the wire format: strict JSON, no NaN or Infinity, and a maximum of 5 MB. The worker gives each dim coordinate the type from the raw schema of the bundle:

  • dates from ISO strings
  • whole numbers for integer and index dims
  • text for categorical dims.

If the worker cannot read a value, the run fails with SCHEMA_INVALID.

docs.title: UI views
docs.text:
Small JSON views for the browser go next to datasets and bundles. The control plane never decodes them. The web app gets them through signed URLs. mapi_spec.views defines them, and each view has a format tag:

Object format Model preview.json mapi.preview/v1 PreviewView: the dim columns, then the variable columns, the first rows, and total_rows profile.json mapi.profile/v1 ProfileView: the statistics for each variable, and a grid of missing values along the time-like dim (maximum 1,000 binned columns) ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 TreeIndexView: the dims, coordinates (with values for small coordinates), variables and scalar attributes of each DataTree node. It has no arrays. ui/summary.arrow, ui/grids/*.arrow Arrow IPC Tidy tables (mapi_sdk.wire.to_arrow_table): one column for each dim, then one column for each variable. The schema metadata mapi.attrs holds the attrs as JSON. From v0.9, the schema metadata mapi.dims holds the names of the dim columns as a JSON list ui/fields.json mapi.model-explorer.fields/v1 FieldsView: the maps of the grid outputs of a score run, with the frames, bands and draws. It is the same view as the field section of the Model Explorer ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 PreprocessView: each pipeline step in sequence (id, resolved use, kind, stateful). For each step, it gives the learned JSON (maximum 16 KB, learned_truncated). It also gives the numeric state arrays with their labels, if they have a maximum of two dims and 10,000 cells. omitted gives the names of larger arrays.

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
mapi_spec.storage makes each key on the server from validated ids (check_segment). User input never becomes a path.

Bucket (Buckets(env)) Keys Access mapi-{env}-quarantine t/{tenant}/uploads/{upload_id} Signed PUT from the browser. 7-day lifecycle. mapi-{env}-bootstrap {nonce} The execution identity can get and delete, but it cannot list. 1-day lifecycle. mapi-{env}-runs t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{n}/[tasks/{i}/], with checkpoints/ and (v0.14) media/ in it Written only through signed URLs mapi-{env}-bundles t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/: bundle.zarr.zip, manifest.json, manifest.sig, diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json, ui/…. From v0.14 also t/{tenant}/run-media/{run}/<sha256>.<ext> (the verified media of the runs). Control plane only. Write-once. mapi-{env}-data t/{tenant}/datasets/{sha256}/: data.zarr.zip, schema.json, summary.json, profile.json, preview.json. A collection version (v0.15) has manifest.parquet, collection.json and members.bin in place of data.zarr.zip. From v0.15 also t/{tenant}/blobs/packs/{digest}.zip (the packs of image collections, shared by the versions of the tenant) Content-addressed

The control plane gets access to storage only through the async ObjectStore protocol:

  • read and write: put, get (with byte ranges and a max_bytes cap), stat (metadata only), list, delete and copy
  • sign: sign_get (pinned to a generation), sign_put (write-once by default) and post_policy.

if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist yet". Failures raise NotFound, PreconditionFailed or AccessDenied.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Component Address Override API (FastAPI) http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_API_URL GCS shim (local Cloud Storage emulator) http://127.0.0.1:4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT Web app (Vite dev server) http://127.0.0.1:5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Plot sandbox http://127.0.0.1:5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Postgres 16 Embedded pgserver, with its data in MAPI_DATA_DIR (default .local/) DATABASE_URL (any postgresql:// URL)

The plot sandbox must have an origin that is different from the web app. The reason is that plots render in a sandbox="allow-scripts" iframe with no same-origin access. LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts the two on the same origin.

Other environment variables and helpers:

  • MAPI_ENV (default local) selects the bucket names, for example mapi-local-runs.
  • LocalDev.from_environ(os.environ) resolves the full configuration.
  • LocalDev.bootstrap_url_template() gives the MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL value for the local executor.

You do not need a Docker daemon. Postgres comes from pgserver, and storage comes from the GCS shim.

docs.title: Runner v0.2
docs.text:
mapi-runner executes one run in a sandbox. It implements the side of the execution in the run protocol. Two processes are part of a run:

  • The supervisor is trusted. It has the HMAC key of the run and the signed URLs. It is the only process that writes to the stdout of the execution.
  • The worker is not trusted. It runs the platform harness (mapi_sdk) together with plugin code. It does not get the key or a URL that can write.
sequenceDiagram
    participant X as Executor
    participant S as Supervisor
    participant G as Object store
    participant W as Worker
    X->>S: start (env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE, MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL)
    S->>G: GET bootstrap/{nonce}, then DELETE that generation
    S->>W: spawn (scrubbed env, uid 10001), start message over a socketpair
    W->>G: range-read inputs (signed GET)
    W-->>S: state / progress / diagnostic / metric / checkpoint messages
    W-->>S: metrics / params / tags / user_log messages (v0.11)
    W-->>S: stdout + stderr (pipes, captured as log lines)
    S-->>X: stdout: {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC + seq per line)
    S->>G: POST outputs (policy), PUT manifest.json
    S-->>X: "complete" event, exit 0

docs.title: Start a run
docs.text:
MAPI_RUN_ID=run_01… MAPI_NONCE=<64 hex> \
MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL='http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}' \
MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN=<local shim exec token> \
mapi-runner

All the configuration of the run comes from the environment. The command-line options tell only about the image. They never contain secrets:

Option Default Meaning --worker-python PATH this interpreter, or MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The interpreter of the worker environment (the site-packages of the base image and all overlays) --worker-registry MODULE:CALLABLE entry points The factory of the plugin registry for the worker --scratch-dir DIR $TMPDIR The parent directory of the scratch space of the run --keep-scratch off Keep the scratch directory after the run, for debug --term-grace SECONDS 5 The time that the worker gets to stop after SIGTERM. After this time, the supervisor kills the worker. --deadline-reserve SECONDS 15 The time before the deadline for the checkpoint flush and a partial manifest --base-image NAME MAPI_BASE_IMAGE Recorded in the output manifest

docs.title: What the supervisor guarantees
docs.text:
• The supervisor deletes the bootstrap object before code that is not trusted runs. The supervisor reads the object. Then it deletes exactly the generation that it read. If the delete fails, the run stops with exit code 2.
  • Only signed events go to stdout. The supervisor keeps a private copy of the stdout descriptor for its event writer. It points fd 1 at stderr. All text that the worker prints goes into the line of a log event. This is also true for text that looks like an event. Each line has seq and an HMAC with the key of the run.

  • The worker gets a scrubbed environment. Only WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST goes through. Thus no MAPI_* variable gets to the worker. The worker starts with python -I -u in a new session, with TMPDIR set to its scratch directory. If the supervisor runs as root (Cloud Run, docker), these rules also apply:

    • The worker runs as uid/gid 10001 with no supplementary groups.
    • The worker has no_new_privs and no core dumps.
    • The supervisor marks itself non-dumpable.

    In all other conditions (macOS, a non-root shell), the run continues in dev mode. The supervisor reports a DEV_MODE_ISOLATION warning event. Dev mode is not a security boundary. An executor that promises the split sets MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1 (the docker executor does this). Then the supervisor does not go into dev mode. It fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION. - The supervisor validates worker messages. Each message is a JSON frame with a length prefix and a maximum size of 256 KiB. It must agree with its Pydantic model. These are a SANDBOX_VIOLATION: a malformed frame, an unknown type, or a message after the final result. - Logs have caps. The supervisor removes ANSI escapes, control characters and bidi overrides. It cuts lines at limits.log_line_bytes (4 KB) and flags them truncated. More than limits.log_total_bytes (20 MB) of worker output is SANDBOX_VIOLATION (log_flood). - The supervisor cleans worker text. It removes the same characters from all other strings that the worker sends. These strings are state and progress messages, warnings, diagnostics, metric labels, and error and issue messages. Line breaks become spaces, except in untrusted_text. - The supervisor coalesces progress. It sends a maximum of one progress event in each limits.progress_interval_s (2 s). The newest value wins. - Tracking data has budgets (v0.11). The supervisor counts each metrics, params, tags and user_log message against limits.tracking (TrackingLimits). It does not keep points or items that are more than a budget, and it counts them. At the end of the run, it sends one TRACKING_BUDGET warning. More than tracking_bytes (64 MiB) of tracking messages is SANDBOX_VIOLATION (tracking flood). The supervisor cleans the strings of each message. It divides each payload with split_for_events, thus no event is larger than limits.max_event_bytes. Tracking messages do not go through the progress coalescer. - The supervisor uploads outputs only from regular files. It opens each file with O_NOFOLLOW, relative to directories that it opened before. A symlink, FIFO or device in the outputs tree is a violation. The reserved names manifest.json and checkpoints/ are also violations. The object caps and byte caps from limits apply. The supervisor selects the content type of each object from its extension. - The manifest tells exactly which bytes the supervisor sent. The supervisor calculates CRC32C and MD5 while it streams each file through the POST policy. It signs the OutputManifest with the key of the run and PUTs it last. The complete event comes after the manifest. - The supervisor enforces the scratch budget. It measures the scratch directory each 2 s. The worker refuses all inputs that are larger than the remaining space. If the run uses more than limits.scratch_bytes, the result is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

docs.title: Tracking in the worker v0.11
docs.text:
The worker gives a tracker to the model code (WorkerContext.tracker, a WorkerTracker). The harness puts it on FitContext.tracker, ScoreContext.tracker and, for workflow node runs, on NodeContext.tracker. The tracker has these properties:

  • It is thread-safe. A sampler callback on a different thread can log points.
  • It collects points for each series. A background thread sends them each flush_interval_s (1 s). When 1000 points wait, the tracker sends them immediately.
  • It does the same budget checks as the supervisor, thus a correct worker never gets to the limits of the supervisor.
  • It sends params and tags with the next flush. It sends a user log line immediately.
  • chains() keeps the newest per-chain progress. The next progress message has it in chains.

Before the worker sends its result or error message, it closes the tracker. Thus the last points are sent. When the tracker did not keep some points, it sends one TRACKING_BUDGET warning. The end-of-run metrics (metric events, for example the holdout rmse) are also kept as scalar series. The guide Track metrics, params and tags shows the API that model code uses.

docs.title: SIGTERM, the deadline and checkpoints
docs.text:
The supervisor does these steps on SIGTERM, or when the time gets to the deadline minus the reserve:

  1. It sends a RUN_TERMINATING warning event and sends SIGTERM to the session of the worker.
  2. It waits for the worker to stop. The worker cooperates when it cancels. Samplers do a check for cancellation after some draws. The segmented sampler of PyMC writes a final checkpoint before it stops. After --term-grace, the supervisor kills the worker.
  3. It waits for the checkpoint uploads that did not finish.
  4. If checkpoints exist, it uploads a manifest with status: partial that lists the checkpoint objects. Then it exits with 16 PARTIAL. If no checkpoints exist, it exits with 143 (SIGTERM) or 14 (deadline).

The worker writes checkpoints to {scratch}/checkpoints/ as two flat files for each fit key: ckpt-<key>.draws.zarr.zip and ckpt-<key>.meta.json. The supervisor uploads the two files with the checkpoints POST policy. It sends a checkpoint event for each file. A resumed attempt gets the same names in RunSpec.resume: the resume names are equal to the object names relative to the checkpoint prefix. The runner downloads them before the fit starts, and the engine continues from them.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Exit When 0 The supervisor uploaded the outputs and the manifest, and sent the complete event 2 The environment is bad, the bootstrap is missing or not valid, or the supervisor cannot use outputs. (There are no events if the supervisor could not read the RunSpec.) 10 The worker reported a user, spec or data error, crashed, or exited without a result 11 Out of memory (MemoryError, or SIGKILL killed the worker), or the run used more than the scratch budget 12 The uploads or downloads of the supervisor failed after retries 13 The size, CRC32C or MD5 of an input was not correct, or a bundle did not agree with its manifest 14 The run got to the deadline without a checkpoint 15 Sandbox violation: log flood, malformed messages, unsafe outputs, oversized events or output caps 16 Partial: the worker flushed a checkpoint after SIGTERM or at the deadline 143 SIGTERM with no checkpoint to flush

The supervisor always reports a failure in an error event. The supervisor writes the message of this event. Text from the worker or from a plugin goes in untrusted_text. The supervisor also sends typed issues from the worker as diagnostic events, for example MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE.

The supervisor accepts only three failure classes from the worker: resource_exhausted, integrity and sandbox. If the worker reports INFRA_ERROR, the run fails as user. An example is a failed input download. The reason is that the infra exit makes the platform retry the full run automatically. Thus only failures that the supervisor sees itself can use infra. All other failures that the worker reports become user.

docs.title: What RunSpec.spec holds, per kind
docs.text:
The dispatcher writes these documents, and the runner reads them. The two sides import the models and the names of the inputs and outputs from mapi_spec.jobs. Refer to the run protocol. The runner reads inputs with HTTP range requests. Each dataset is one object: *.zarr.zip, or data.tree.zip for a tree dataset (v0.8). A tree input can come with a tree_schema input (the tree_schema.json of its version). The runner selects the nodes of data.nodes and merges them into the flat input of the pipeline. A tree-input model also gets the whole tree. The raw schema of a plain dataset comes from one of these sources, in this sequence:

  1. the schema input, if there is one
  2. the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (mapi_spec.jobs.DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR). Ingest writes this attribute, and uploads can contain it.
  3. a schema that the runner infers.
Kind spec Inputs Outputs (relative to the attempt prefix) ingest IngestMapping, or IngestJob ({"mapping": …}, {"preset": "mff", "mff": {…}} or, from v0.8, {"assembly": …}, and also dataset and source, which are only for information) upload, or upload.0, upload.1, … (one for each source of an assembly) data.zarr.zip, schema.json, summary.json (DataSummary), profile.json (mapi.profile/v1, with the sha256 and size_bytes of the data), preview.json (mapi.preview/v1). A tree version (v0.8) writes data.tree.zip and tree_schema.json (TreeSchema) in place of data.zarr.zip. Its schema.json is the schema of the root node, summary.json adds a summary for each node under nodes, and the explorer views of each node are under ui/explore/nodes/<slug>/ with an index inspect InspectJob (v0.8: format, and caps for arrays, HDF5 objects, dims and attributes) upload inspection.json (UploadInspection). The run reads only metadata, after the HDF5 guard describe DescribeJob ({"image_digest": …?}) none catalog.json (Catalog), describe.json (catalog_digest, versions) validate a ModelSpec dataset, optional schema, side.<name> validation.json (ValidateResponse with the stages that a dry run resolved) fit a ModelSpec dataset, optional schema, side.<name> bundle.zarr.zip, bundle.manifest.json, diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json (MetricsReport. v0.9: elpd has the elpd_loo/elpd_waic estimates with their pointwise values), coords.json ({stage: {dim: CoordSummary}}), scorecard.json (Scorecard, v0.4), evaluation/…, ui/thin.zarr.zip, ui/summaries.json, ui/tree_index.json (mapi.tree-index/v1), ui/preprocess.json (mapi.preprocess/v1), ui/grids/*.arrow, ui/grids/response_curves.json (mapi.response-grid/v1, v0.4), ui/plotdata/*.arrow score a ScoreRequest, or {"request": …, "plots": […], "max_draws": n} bundle, optional bundle.manifest, dataset (payload), scenario, side.<name>, history (v0.4) score.zarr.zip, result.json, summary.json (ScoreSummary: the summary as tables, at most 100 000 cells. v0.9: a circular output has period), ui/summary.arrow, plots.json. Forecasts add ui/guided/forecast.json (mapi.forecast/v1). Counterfactuals add ui/guided/counterfactual.json (mapi.counterfactual/v1) (v0.4). Predict, forecast and evaluate add ui/fields.json (FieldsView) for a model with grid outputs evaluate {"request": …?, "metrics": […]?} bundle, dataset, side.<name> the score outputs and also metrics.json derive {"names": […], "draws": n?, "data": "dataset://…"?} bundle, dataset, side.<name> derived.zarr.zip, ui/grids/<name>.arrow, result.json render {"plots": […]?, "format": "png" \| "svg", "scale": 2} plots (a plots.json) renders/<plot id>.<format> translate_priors PriorTranslationJob ({"spec": …, "business_priors": …, "lift_tests": […], "draws": n, "seed": s}, v0.4) dataset, optional schema, side.<name> priors.json (PriorTranslationResult), plots.json (mmm.prior_beliefs, core.prior_predictive)

At the top level of the attempt prefix, manifest.json is the OutputManifest of the runner. Thus the runner uploads the manifest of the SDK bundle as bundle.manifest.json. The evaluation sub-bundle keeps the SDK layout (evaluation/manifest.json).

In plots.json, the runner moves inline Arrow datasets that are larger than 64 KiB to ui/plotdata/<plot>.<dataset>.arrow. The plot refers to them as data_ref, with their size and CRC32C.

The Arrow views (ui/summary.arrow, ui/grids/*.arrow) are tidy tables from mapi_sdk.wire.to_arrow_table. From v0.9, the schema metadata mapi.dims gives the names of the dim columns as a JSON list. Thus the web app keeps a numeric dim, for example a grid position in cm, as a key column and not as a value.

A score run picks its default plots from the shape of the outputs, when the job does not give plots:

Output (manifest declaration, result dims) Default plot A grid output (y and x in the result) sci.field_map, with var, y, x and the frame dim (when it is in the result) as options. The frame dim is the slider. A grid output with a component of size 2 sci.vector_field, with the same options An output on the areas of ring_x/ring_y (v0.10) sci.area_map (var). The polygons come from the bundle. Probabilities over a dim with the name state or regime (v0.10): each cell has a sum of 1 core.state_sequence (var, state_dim) Evaluate: a binary output (observed values 0/1, predictions from 0 to 1) (v0.10) core.calibration, core.roc_pr, core.confusion (var, observed_var) An output that is not a grid, over time, with at most one other dim of size more than 1 core.ppc_fan (var), for predict and forecast

Each mode except counterfactual starts from the plots of before (DEFAULT_PLOTS). A counterfactual keeps core.counterfactual. A model with grid outputs or area outputs gets the fan only when it also has an output over time. A fan of a map adds the values of all cells. Evaluate draws core.fit_vs_actual. It adds core.residuals_over_time only when an output is over time. A binary output replaces the two plots with the three classifier plots (BINARY_EVALUATE_PLOTS). There is at most one plot for each recipe, so each recipe draws one output. The map draws the first grid output with a frame, else the first grid output. The other recipes draw the first areal, state or binary output in the sequence of the manifest.

A state output must have a dim with the name state or regime (not only a name that contains the word, such as us_state). Its values must also be probabilities over that dim. Thus a panel output such as sales(time, state) for the states of a country does not get the state plot.

The map draws from /predictions, so the runner keeps the full predictions of a grid model until the plots are done. From v0.10, the runner also keeps them for a model with area outputs and for each evaluate run. Thus the evaluate plots get /predictions and /observed. score.zarr.zip does not keep the two groups. The summary.json table of an output gives plots (v0.10): the ids of the rendered plots that draw it.

A fit run adds core.loss_curve to the plots of a fit that has a fit_history group (an ADVI fit, v0.10).

The output variables of a grid carry the attr grid (the GridDecl as JSON, with the dims renamed to the names of the result). summary.json gives dims and time_dim for each table, and orders the tables by size.

scorecard.json does the data checks on the raw dataset. The check data.missing (v0.9) does not count these variables:

  • the variables with the role constant, index or mask in the raw schema or in the schema of the model stage
  • the canonical variables that the model lists in CustomModel.structural_missing. The runner gets them from the plugin registry. If it cannot find the plugin, the list is empty.

The message of the check names the variables that it does not count.

A workflow_node run gets a tree dataset input as its root node, and keeps the full tree (v0.9). Thus the nodes parameter of a model node can select other nodes of the tree.

docs.title: MFF preset
docs.text: The preset reads a long table with the columns Period, VariableName and VariableValue. Period becomes the time dim (date, policy extend, inferred frequency). Each key column (Geography, Product, Campaign, Outlet, Creative) becomes a categorical dim only if it has more than one distinct value. Each VariableName becomes a variable. You can override roles, units and column names in mff.

docs.title: Not implemented yet
docs.text:
• optimize runs. They fail with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. The runner reports this as exit 10.
  • render needs vl-convert-python (Vega-Lite) or kaleido (Plotly) in the image. If the image does not have them, the run fails with a clear message. The runner does not render plots with data_ref datasets.

docs.title: HDF5 and NetCDF-4 v0.8
docs.text:
h5py and h5netcdf are explicit dependencies of mapi-runner. Thus each runner image can read NetCDF-4 and HDF5 uploads. The runner reads NetCDF-3 files with SciPy.

Before xarray or h5py opens an HDF5 file, the HDF5 guard (mapi_runner.worker.hdf5_guard) walks the file with the low-level API of h5py and refuses unsafe files with INGEST_UNSAFE_FILE. The supervisor sets HDF5_PLUGIN_PATH to an empty directory and HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE in the environment of the worker. Thus libhdf5 cannot load a filter plugin. Refer to the HDF5 guard.

docs.title: Python SDK (mapi-sdk)
docs.text:
mapi-sdk is the runtime that operates on your arrays. It runs in runner images and in your notebook. It never runs in the API server. It does all the work between a spec and a fitted model that you can score:

  • binding
  • preprocessing with fitted state
  • the train and holdout split
  • the model plugin
  • the coordinates at score time
  • inverse transforms
  • summaries and bundles
uv add mapi-sdk          # or: pip install mapi-sdk

docs.title: Fit and score in a notebook
docs.text:
The first-model walkthrough shows these steps one by one. The short version is below. It uses spec, data and schema from that page:

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

For a model with the draws representation, add draws: 50 to output. Then the tree also has a draws group. This group has 50 joint draws from the thinning index of the bundle.

score_bundle returns an xr.DataTree. Its root attributes record these items:

  • The representation.
  • The output kind (expected or predictive).
  • The output space of each variable, for example weekly. Inverse transforms stop at the last reshape step.
  • The retransformation labels for point models.
  • All warnings.

Counterfactual requests add baseline/ and delta/ groups.

docs.title: How the fit works
docs.text:
fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit (the default) does these steps:

  1. Parse the settings of the model (plugin.parse_settings). A settings rule that the JSON Schema cannot give (a pydantic model_validator) refuses the fit here with SETTINGS_INVALID, before the SDK changes the data.
  2. Bind the dataset names to canonical names. Do a check of the data against its schema.
  3. Run the stateless prefix of the pipeline on all the data, up to the split stage.
  4. Split the data. Fit the remaining steps and the model on train.
  5. Score the holdout through the usual score path (with context rows from train). Calculate evaluate.metrics.
  6. Fit each step and the model again on all the data. Thus, forecasts start from the latest context tails and the latest terminal state. The lineage of the production bundle has a link to the evaluation bundle.

train_only stops after step 5 and keeps the fit on train.

When BindingMap changes the name of a dim, it also changes that name in the grid attr of each variable (the keys y, x, frame and component). Thus a plot recipe finds the grid of an output after a data.bind.

docs.title: How the score works
docs.text: Phase What occurs Mode score_bundle refuses a mode that the fitted model does not support (MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, with the supported modes in context). This check comes before all work for a mode. For example, a forecast never starts on a model that cannot forecast CoordPlan The SDK finds typed errors early from the metadata: UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (409), MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, ... Horizon A forecast makes the labels of the horizon after the last fitted label. A horizon along a dim with text labels gives COORD_NOT_ALLOWED at /horizon/dim, because text labels have no sequence. The labels must be numbers or dates Entry The data goes in at inputs_stage (default raw). The SDK skips the steps before this stage and their side tables. Replay The SDK applies the stored state of each step. Some steps look back (lags). For these steps, the SDK first does a contiguity check. Then it puts the stored context rows of each group before the data. Canonical coords The SDK puts the model-stage data in the fit order and pads it to the full fit set. It adds new levels at the end with a <dim>__is_new flag. Model plugin.score(...) returns the predictions group in the representation of the plugin. Back to you The SDK removes the context rows and selects the requested coords. It inverts the outputs to the output space. It aggregates them (only if this is statistically valid) and makes summaries. Then it binds the names back to your dataset names.

docs.title: Run tracking v0.11
docs.text:
FitContext, ScoreContext and the NodeContext of workflow nodes have the same logging methods (mapi_sdk.tracking.TrackingMixin):

Method What it does log_metric(key, value, step=None, labels=None) One metric point. Without step, the point is a scalar and the newest value is kept. log_metrics(values, step=None, labels=None) Some metrics with one step and one label set. log_metrics({}) does nothing. log_param(key, value), log_params(params) Params. The same value again does nothing. A different value raises ValueError. set_tag(key, value), set_tags(tags) Tags. The last value is kept. log_line(message, level="info", fields=None) A structured log line (stream user). The SDK cuts the message at 4096 characters. A maximum of 16 fields. chains(chains) The progress of each chain, a list of mapi_spec.run.ChainProgress tracking True when a tracker records the values log_image(key, image, step=None, labels=None, caption=None) v0.14. An image: a numpy array (gray, RGB or RGBA), PNG or JPEG bytes, a Pillow image or a DataArray log_figure(key, figure, step=None, labels=None, caption=None) v0.14. A matplotlib figure, saved as PNG log_table(key, table, step=None, labels=None, caption=None) v0.14. A DataFrame, a dict of columns or a list of records tracking_media v0.14. True when the tracker records media (MediaTracker)

Each method does a check of its input, also when no tracker is attached. A bad key, a bad label, a negative step or a bad level raises ValueError at the call. The SDK ignores non-finite metric values. The key and label rules are in mapi_spec.tracking (check_metric_key, check_labels, check_param_key, check_tag_key).

The values go to a Tracker (mapi_sdk.Tracker, a protocol). All implementations are thread-safe:

Tracker Use MetricRecorder(limits=None) Keeps all values in memory, with the budgets of TrackingLimits. history() gives the metrics_history dataset (or None). params, tags, lines, last_chains and dropped (the count for each reason) show what it kept and what it did not keep. TeeTracker(*trackers) Sends each call to all the trackers that are not None with_labels(tracker, labels, *, param_prefix="") Adds labels to each metric call. The labels of the call have priority. param_prefix goes before each param key (a key that becomes too long is not sent). WorkerTracker (mapi_runner) Inside a run: sends the values to the platform each second

docs.title: Media v0.14
docs.text:
Media use a separate, optional protocol: mapi_sdk.MediaTracker (one method, log_media(item: MediaItem)). A Tracker that does not have it does not get media. Thus the trackers of earlier releases continue to work. log_image, log_figure and log_table always do a check of the key, the labels, the step and the caption. They encode the item only when the tracker is a MediaTracker.

Name What it does MediaItem A frozen item: key, kind, content_type, data, sha256, step, labels, caption, width, height. name is <sha256>.<ext>. encode_png(array) (png_bytes, width, height) of an array of shape (H, W), (H, W, 1), (H, W, 3) or (H, W, 4). uint8 as is, booleans as 0 and 255, other integers in 0 to 255, floats in 0 to 1 (scaled by 255, NaN becomes 0). Other values raise ValueError. The same array always gives the same bytes. It uses numpy and zlib only. mapi_sdk.media.image_item, figure_item, table_item Make a MediaItem. They raise ValueError for bad input or an item above the limits of mapi_spec.media.

MetricRecorder.media keeps the items in memory, within media_items and media_bytes. The items are not written into the bundle. TeeTracker and with_labels send media to the trackers that are MediaTrackers (with_labels adds its labels, and the labels of the call have priority).

The harness connects the trackers:

  • FitHooks(tracker=...) gets the values of the fit and the params of the spec (spec_params: model, fit.*, data.split, settings.*). The values of the evaluation fit of evaluate_then_refit get the label fit=evaluation.
  • fit_spec(..., record_metrics=True) (the default) also records each fit in a MetricRecorder, and writes /model/metrics_history into the bundle (see Bundles). With record_metrics=False, the bundle has no such group.
  • score_bundle gives hooks.tracker to ScoreContext.tracker.
from mapi_sdk import FitHooks, MetricRecorder, fit_spec

rec = MetricRecorder()
bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, hooks=FitHooks(tracker=rec))
rec.params["model"]                         # 'mmm.bayesian@1.2.0'
bundle.model.groups["metrics_history"]      # when the model logged stepped metrics

For the full guide, see Track metrics, params and tags.

docs.title: Image collections, loaders and weights v0.15
docs.text:
mapi_sdk.collection reads image collections lazily. mapi_sdk.images decodes images. mapi_sdk.safetensors and mapi_sdk.checkpoints save network weights. All of them are exported from mapi_sdk.

Name What it does Collection A collection: info (CollectionInfo), manifest (a DataFrame, one row for each image), source (a BlobSource) and schema. Collection.open(info, manifest, source) validates the columns, the ids, the digests and the packs. manifest_dataset() gives the manifest as a 1-D dataset along the image dim. loader(ids=None) gives a CollectionLoader. ImageLoader The protocol of a loader: n, dim, ids, labels, classes, size, channels, manifest(), subset(), with_classes(), with_size(), with_mode(), split(), batches() and to_xarray() ArrayImageLoader An ImageLoader over an in-memory image dataset (pixels(image, y, x, channel)). Pixels can be uint8, or floats in 0 to 1 or 0 to 255. CollectionLoader An ImageLoader that reads the images from the packs while you iterate. Each read makes sure that the SHA-256 is correct. Batch ids, pixels (B, H, W, C) uint8, labels, codes (int32, −1 for a missing label or an unknown class) and index Augment Random changes for each training image: flip_x, flip_y, rotate90, crop_pad, brightness, contrast, noise. Models put it in their settings. BlobSource, LocalPackSource Where the packs are. The runner gives a source that reads the signed pack URLs in ranges. LocalPackSource({digest: path}) reads local files. read_safetensors, write_safetensors Read and write safetensors files with numpy only. The writer gives the same bytes for the same tensors. weights_dataset, tensors_from_dataset Change tensors into the weights dataset (weights(param) and the attribute mapi_weights) and back FileCheckpoint, FileCheckpointSink Checkpoints as files (weights, optimizer state, meta). MemoryFileCheckpointSink keeps them in memory for tests. requested_positions(ds, dim) The positions of the rows that a score request asked for (it skips the padded rows of a new_levels dim)

The order of batches(batch_size, epoch=e, shuffle=True, seed=s) is a function of the seed and the epoch only. The loader reads blocks of up to 64 images of one pack, puts the blocks in a random sequence and shuffles the images in windows of 8 blocks. The random changes of Augment use a generator for each image, from the seed, the epoch and the position. Thus the batches are the same for each number of threads. shard=(i, n) gives every n-th block to shard i.

to_xarray(max_samples, size, seed=..., stratify="label") gives the v0.14 image layout: pixels(image, y, x, channel) uint8 with label(image). When the loader has more than max_samples images, it keeps a seeded share of each label.

from mapi_sdk import Augment
from mapi_sdk.testing.images import local_collection

collection = local_collection(tmp_path, n_per_class=8, size=12)
loader = collection.loader().with_size((12, 12))
train, val = loader.split(0.25, seed=0)
for batch in train.batches(16, epoch=0, shuffle=True, seed=0, augment=Augment(flip_x=True)):
    print(batch.pixels.shape, batch.codes)

fit_spec(spec, collection) and score_bundle(bundle, request, collection) take a Collection in place of a dataset. A model with capabilities.input: collection gets a loader in fit_batches and score_batches. Any other model gets collection_read(collection, spec.data.collection, seed=...). Read Train on batches.

docs.title: Representations and summaries
docs.text:
Representation Shape Summaries Aggregation draws (chain, draw, …) mean, sd, median, hdi_<p>, eti_<p>, q<p> All (for each draw) quantiles (quantile, …) median, q<p>, eti_<p> (interpolated, never extrapolated) None interval (bound, …) interval, point None point (…) mean, point sum/mean, flagged moments (moment, …) mean, sd, eti_<p> None

If you ask for something that is not valid, the request fails with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. For example, you cannot add quantiles together, or get draws from a point model. The SDK does not return a number that can cause an incorrect decision.

docs.title: Circular outputs
docs.text:
An output can be an angle, for example a direction or a time of day. The model declares it with OutputDecl.circular: true (the default is false). It also sets a period attr (one turn, in the units of the output, for example 360, 2π or 24) on the scored array. sci.circular_regression declares direction_hat and mean_direction circular.

For the draws representation, summarise(..., periods={var: period}) calculates the summaries on the circle:

  • mean is the circular mean. sd is the circular standard deviation, sqrt(-2 ln R) converted to the units of the output.
  • median, q<p>, eti_<p> and hdi_<p> come from the wrapped differences between the draws and the circular mean. Thus each interval is centred on the circular mean.
  • The mean, the median, the quantiles and the interval bounds are in [0, period). An interval with lower more than upper crosses the seam, for example from 350 to 10 degrees.
  • The difference between a scenario and its baseline (delta/summary, delta/draws) is wrapped to [-period/2, period/2) (signed=True). Thus 10 − 350 degrees is 20, not −340.

The summary variable has the attr circular_period (mapi_sdk.summarise.CIRCULAR_ATTR). If the output has no valid period attr, or if the request aggregates it over a dim, the summary stays on a line. The result then has a CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED warning at /output/summary.

The holdout metrics of a circular output use the same rules (compute_metrics(..., period=...)):

  • The point is the circular mean of the draws.
  • mae, rmse and bias use the error wrapped to half a turn. Thus 359 degrees against 1 degree is an error of −2 degrees, not 358.
  • coverage_<p> and interval_width_<p> use central intervals of the draws around the circular mean.
  • crps uses the arc distance.
  • The SDK skips mape, smape, wape and r2, because they have no meaning on a circle. It also skips all metrics if the representation is not draws or the period is not valid. skipped gives the reason.

docs.title: Data on the wire
docs.text:
mapi_sdk.wire reads and writes the formats of the platform. The readers think that each payload can be hostile.

  • XrJSON (to_xrjson / from_xrjson): The xr.Dataset.to_dict() shape with explicit dtypes and null for missing values. It has limits on elements, dims and string length. Use it for small payloads and for curl.
  • zarr zip (write_zarr_zip / read_zarr_zip, write_datatree_zip / read_datatree_zip): zarr v3 archives in one object. These rules apply:
    • Strings are vlen-utf8.
    • Datetimes are int64 nanoseconds with explicit units.
    • The reader accepts only zstd/blosc compression.
    • The writer resets MultiIndexes, and the reader restores them.
    • The bytes are deterministic.
  • Rows (stack_rows / unstack_rows): These functions stack dims into rows and remove empty rows. Later, they restore the rows from the recorded row mask.
  • Arrow IPC (to_arrow_table, write_arrow_ipc): Tidy tables for UI views. One column for each dim coordinate, then one column for each variable. The schema metadata mapi.attrs holds the attrs of the variables and of the dataset as JSON. The schema metadata mapi.dims holds the names of the dim columns as a JSON list. A reader uses it to find the key columns. The type of a column does not tell this, for example for a numeric dim such as a grid position in cm.

The SDK never uses pickle.

docs.title: Data checks in plain language
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from mapi_sdk import infer_schema, validate_dataset
from mapi_spec import DimPolicy

days = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=28, freq="D")
markets = ["DE", "FR", "UK"]
channels = ["tv", "search"]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
media = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "revenue": (("market", "date"), rng.gamma(50.0, 20.0, (3, 28))),
        "spend": (("market", "channel", "date"), rng.gamma(5.0, 100.0, (3, 2, 28))),
    },
    coords={"market": markets, "channel": channels, "date": days},
)

schema = infer_schema(
    media,
    targets=["revenue"],
    policies={"market": "new_levels"},
    units={"revenue": "EUR", "spend": "EUR"},
)
print(schema.dims["date"].policy, schema.dims["date"].freq)  # extend D
print(schema.dims["channel"].policy)  # fixed
print(schema.vars["revenue"].role)  # target

broken = media.copy(deep=True)
broken["revenue"].loc[{"market": ["FR", "UK"], "date": days[10:12]}] = np.nan

for issue in validate_dataset(schema, broken):
    print(issue.severity, issue.code, "-", issue.message)
# error SCHEMA_INVALID - 2 markets are missing 2 days of revenue in March 2026

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text:
A bundle directory contains bundle.zarr.zip and the files manifest.json, diagnostics.json, plots.json and metrics.json. bundle.zarr.zip contains these items:

  • the spec, the schemas and the binding
  • the state and the context of each step
  • the groups of the model, with ArviZ names
  • native artifacts
  • the fit coordinates of each stage
  • pinned side tables
  • the thinning index

The manifest records CRC32C and MD5 (in the form that GCS reports) and SHA-256 for each file. Bundle.read verifies them.

metrics.json is a MetricsReport. It has these fields:

Field Meaning values The holdout metrics. null if a metric has no finite value skipped The metrics that the SDK did not calculate, with the reason n_holdout The number of holdout values that count split, evaluation_bundle, output_space The split, the link to the evaluation bundle and the output space of the metrics elpd {name: ElpdDetail} for elpd_loo and elpd_waic (v0.9)

The SDK calculates elpd_loo and elpd_waic only when evaluate.metrics lists them and the bundle has a log_likelihood group. For example, a PyMC model needs fit.keep: {log_likelihood: true}. An ElpdDetail (mapi_sdk.bundle) has these fields:

  • elpd: the estimate.
  • se: its standard error.
  • p: the effective number of parameters.
  • n: the number of data points.
  • pointwise: the value for each point, in the order of the flattened log_likelihood variable. The field is null above 10 000 points (mapi_sdk.metrics.MAX_POINTWISE_ELPD).

The workflow node compare.stacking uses the pointwise values. If the estimate is not finite (a log-likelihood of -inf), the SDK keeps no elpd entry for it. A bundle that has a null entry from an earlier version still loads.

docs.title: Missing values by design
docs.text:
Some datasets have NaN that are correct, for example the cells of a grid that have no sensor. A CustomModel lists these canonical variables in the class attribute structural_missing (the default is empty). The scorecard check data.missing (Few missing values) does not count their missing values. sci.heat_plate declares temperature.

The check also does not count the variables with the role constant, index or mask. The message of the check names the variables that it does not count. Gaps in a target, a spend or a covariate count as before, also with missing: allow.

docs.title: Run work with an executor
docs.text:
InprocExecutor implements the Executor protocol of the platform in your own process. Use it for notebooks and tests. Never use it for untrusted code:

import asyncio

from mapi_plugin_tabular.datasets import (
    STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA,
    STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
    store_demand_dataset,
)
from mapi_sdk import InprocExecutor
from mapi_spec.executor import ExecState, RunEventType, RunKind, RunSubmit

history = store_demand_dataset(stores=4, skus=2, weeks=60, seed=1)
recent = history.isel(week=slice(-8, None))  # a window of fitted weeks to re-score

executor = InprocExecutor(
    # dataset refs in specs and requests resolve to in-memory datasets
    resolver={
        "dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest": history,
        "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1": recent,
    },
)
print(executor.caps().isolation.name)  # NONE: your own code, in your own process

async def main() -> None:
    fit = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="fit-001",
            kind=RunKind.FIT,
            payload={
                "spec": STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
                "raw_schema": STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-fit-0001",  # resubmitting the same nonce returns the same run
    )
    status = await executor.wait(fit, timeout=300)
    print(status.state)  # succeeded
    for event in executor.events(fit):  # the same event stream a cloud run will produce
        if event.type is RunEventType.PROGRESS:
            print(event.seq, event.payload.get("message"))  # 2 validated the spec and the data

    executor.put_bundle("store-demand@1", executor.result(fit))
    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

See Runs and executors.

docs.title: Error codes that you can see
docs.text:
Each error is a MapiError with a stable code. Where it is useful, the error also has a JSON pointer. Text from your data or from a plugin goes in untrusted_text, separate from the message. These are the error types:

  • StepError (USER_CODE_ERROR) contains failures in steps.
  • SchemaValidationError (SCHEMA_INVALID) reports problems in the data.
  • BundleError (INTEGRITY_FAILURE) reports bundles that are damaged or that someone changed.
  • RunCancelled (CANCELLED) reports a cooperative cancellation.

docs.title: Spec format reference
docs.text:
Each model on modeling-api starts as a ModelSpec. This is a small YAML (or JSON) file. It gives your dataset, the preprocessing pipeline and the model plugin. It also tells how to fit and evaluate the model. The Guided wizard, the Expert editor, the CLI and the API all use the same file.

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: eu-geo-mmm, project: growth}

data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/eu_media_daily@latest
  side_tables:
    fx: {ref: dataset://growth/fx_daily@latest, score_policy: supplied}
  bind:
    dims: {geo: market, channel: channel, time: date}   # canonical name: dataset name
    vars: {y: revenue_local, spend: spend_local}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8, after_step: weekly}

pipeline:
  - {id: to_eur, use: core.fx_convert@^1, with: {vars: [y, spend], table: fx, to: EUR}}
  - {id: weekly, use: core.resample@^1,   with: {dim: time, freq: W-SUN, how: sum}}

model:
  use: mmm.bayesian@^1              # mmm-framework scales and carries spend over itself
  settings:
    hierarchy: {pool_over: [geo]}
    dim_policies: {geo: fixed}      # may only tighten the plugin's policy
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, draws: 1000, chains: 4, seed: 7}

evaluate: {metrics: [elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape]}
execution: {resource_class: M, timeout: 45m}

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Section Purpose metadata name and project (lowercase slugs). Optional: labels and description data.dataset dataset://<project>/<name>@latest|vN|sha256:<hex> — The API pins it to an exact version when you submit data.side_tables Small constant datasets (FX, holidays). score_policy is pinned, latest or supplied. A side table that is a tree dataset reads one node: node: /fx (v0.8). From v0.15 a model can read a side table too (side_table_params in its manifest, for example the pretrained weights of dl.finetune_classifier). A score request never needs a table that only the model reads data.nodes v0.8, tree datasets only. The nodes whose variables make the flat input of the pipeline: {key: {path, vars?, prefix?}}, a maximum of 64 entries. Refer to Tree datasets in a spec data.join v0.8, used only with data.nodes (a value other than exact without them is an error). How the labels of the selected nodes align: exact (the default), inner or outer data.bind Maps canonical names (the names that plugins and steps use) to dataset names. By default, the outputs get the dataset names again. When a dim gets a new name, the grid attr of each variable gets the new name too (v0.9) data.split time_holdout, last_per_group, as_of, leave_group_out, mask_block, and from v0.14 column or stratified (see Column and stratified splits). The split occurs at after_step data.collection v0.15, image collections only. How a model that reads datasets sees the collection: a seeded sample as pixels(image, y, x, channel). Refer to Image collections in a spec pipeline Steps in sequence: {id, use: <id>@<semver range>, with: {...}} model The plugin use, its settings and the fit block outputs Derived quantities, plot recipes and the number of draws that the UI keeps evaluate Holdout metrics (elpd_loo, coverage_90, mape, rmse, auc, mase and more). elpd_loo and elpd_waic need a log_likelihood group, for example model.fit.keep: {log_likelihood: true}. If not, metrics.json gives the reason in skipped. A circular output gets circular metrics and skips mape, smape, wape and r2 execution The resource class (S, M, L, XL, and from v0.15 GPU) and the timeout (45m, 1h30m). Each class has a limit for the input data that a run reads (dataset plus side tables): S 0.5 GB, M 2 GB, L 5 GB, XL 50 GB, GPU 50 GB. If the data is larger, validation reports PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE at /execution/resource_class. The message gives the class that fits. Ingest runs select the smallest CPU class that holds the upload. An image collection is read in parts while the model trains, so its size does not count. Refer to Resource classes

docs.title: Metrics in evaluate v0.10
docs.text:
evaluate.metrics names the metrics that the fit calculates on the holdout data. The fit writes them in metrics.json. If the fit cannot calculate a metric, metrics.json gives the metric and the reason in skipped. The fit does not fail.

Metric What it measures Needs mape, smape, wape, rmse, mae, r2, bias The error of the point prediction (the mean or the median) Actual values on the holdout mase mae divided by the mean absolute error of a seasonal naive forecast on the training data A fit with a time holdout. The season length comes from the frequency of the time dim. crps, coverage_N, interval_width_N, log_score The quality of the predicted distribution Draws, quantiles or intervals elpd_loo, elpd_waic The expected log predictive density A log_likelihood group auc, brier, log_score, accuracy The quality of a 0/1 prediction (see below) A 0/1 target and a predicted probability accuracy_naive, accuracy_lift The accuracy of the most frequent class, and the gain of the model over it A categorical target

Targets with two values. If the target has exactly two values and the prediction is a probability from 0 to 1, the fit uses these definitions. The larger target value is the positive class.

Metric Definition auc The area under the ROC curve (the Mann-Whitney statistic, with the average rank for ties) brier mean((p - y)^2). For two classes, the categorical Brier score is two times larger, because it adds the error of the two classes. log_score mean(log(p_y)), where p_y is the probability that the model gave to the actual class (minimum 1e-12) accuracy The share of rows where p >= 0.5 agrees with the target

A prediction with draws uses the mean of the draws as p. A classifier that gives one probability for each row (for example sklearn.tabular_classifier) also gets rmse, mae and the other point metrics on the probability. rmse is then the root of the Brier score.

Reasons in skipped. metrics.json gives these texts:

  • auc on a target that is not 0/1: "AUC needs a 0/1 target and predicted probabilities in [0, 1]".
  • auc when the holdout has only one of the two classes: "AUC needs both classes in the holdout".
  • mase without the training data: "MASE needs the in-sample naive error of the training data (a fit with a time holdout)". Only the evaluation of a fit has the training data. Thus an evaluate run from the Score page skips mase.
  • brier, log_score and accuracy on a target that is not 0/1 or categorical: "defined for categorical targets only".

A known limit

Validation refuses log_score for a model that gives only point predictions, because the metric usually needs uncertainty. Thus a point classifier cannot request log_score in v0.10. Use brier or auc.

docs.title: Tree datasets in a spec v0.8
docs.text:
A tree dataset has nodes, for example /sales and /media. Steps and most models read one flat dataset. data.nodes selects the nodes, and the platform merges their variables before the pipeline:

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: sales-tree, project: growth}
data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/sales_tree@latest
  nodes:                                  # these nodes make the flat input of the pipeline
    sales: {path: /sales}                 # all the variables of /sales
    media: {path: /media, vars: [spend]}  # only 'spend' from /media
    plan: {path: /plan, prefix: plan_}    # /plan 'spend' becomes 'plan_spend'
  join: exact                             # the default: the labels must be equal
  bind:
    dims: {geo: market, time: date}
    vars: {y: revenue}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 4}
pipeline: []
model:
  use: toy.tree_linear@^1                 # test-only reference model (mapi_sdk.testing.toy)
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, seed: 3}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse]}

The model of this example

toy.tree_linear is a reference model of the SDK test kit (mapi_sdk.testing.toy). The documentation tests use it to check and fit this spec. The platform and the CLI catalog do not have it, so mapi check reports REF_UNRESOLVED for it. Put a model of your platform in model.use (mapi catalog lists them).

Field of an entry Meaning path The node path (/ is the root) vars The variables to read from the node. Default: all prefix Text before each variable name of the node (1 to 32 characters, starts with a letter or _). Use it when two nodes have variables with the same name
  • Dims keep their names. A dim that two selected nodes use must have the same DimSpec.
  • A variable name can come from one entry only. Validation reports a clash and tells you to add a prefix.
  • data.bind and the pipeline use the merged names (for example plan_spend).
  • Without data.nodes, a spec on a tree dataset reads the root node. If the root has no variables, validation reports SCHEMA_INVALID ("this dataset is a tree: pick nodes in data.nodes").
  • data.nodes on a plain dataset is an error. So is a data.join other than exact without data.nodes (exact is the default and has no effect without nodes).

Static validation uses the tree_schema of the dataset version. Thus it finds these problems before a run starts.

docs.title: Column and stratified splits v0.14
docs.text:
These two split kinds are for data without a time order, for example images or customers. Both cut whole rows along dim. They do not mask cells.

split: {kind: column, dim: image, column: split, holdout: [test]}
split: {kind: column, dim: image, column: split, holdout: [test], train: [train]}
split: {kind: stratified, dim: image, by: label, fraction: 0.25, seed: 7}
Kind Field Meaning column dim The dim of the rows column A coordinate or a 1-D variable along dim with the assignment of each row holdout The values of the holdout rows (default [test], a maximum of 64). The values compare as text: 1 and "1" are the same. train The values of the training rows (a maximum of 64). Rows with a value in neither list are not used. The default (none) trains on all other rows. A value cannot be in holdout and in train. stratified dim The dim of the rows by A coordinate or a 1-D variable along dim with the class of each row fraction The share of each class to hold out (more than 0, less than 1) seed The random seed (default: the seed of the fit)

stratified holds out round(n × fraction) rows of each class, with a maximum of n − 1. A class with one row stays in training. Rows with an empty or missing class stay in training. The same seed gives the same split. If the split gives no holdout rows or no training rows, the fit stops with an error.

Validation does a check of column and by when the schema of the split stage has the variable: it must be on dim only (SPLIT_INVALID). A coordinate that is not a dim is not in the schema. Then validation gives an information message, and the fit does the check.

Do not use these splits for a time series forecast. Use time_holdout or as_of.

docs.title: Image folders v0.14
docs.text:
An upload of the format image_folder is a zip of images and a manifest table. The mapping has only format and images (an ImageFolderOptions), not dims, vars, wide or a preset. images can be left out: then the defaults apply. An image_folder upload must be the only source of a dataset version.

format: image_folder
images:
  manifest: manifest.csv        # .csv, .tsv or .parquet, a relative path in the zip
  path_column: path
  id_column: id                 # optional: unique labels of the image dim
  label_column: label           # optional: the variable label(image), role target
  split_column: split           # optional: the coordinate split(image)
  columns: null                 # the other columns to keep (null: all)
  var: pixels
  dim: image                    # not sample, chain, draw, quantile, bound, moment, y, x or channel
  mode: auto                    # auto, gray or rgb
  size: [32, 32]                # optional (height, width), each 1 to 4096
  resize: crop                  # stretch, crop or pad (only with size)
  max_images: 20000             # 1 to 100 000

The ingest writes pixels(image, y, x, channel) with the dtype uint8. uint8 is a numeric dtype of the schema (v0.14), for values from 0 to 255. For the full layout and the limits, see Image data.

docs.title: Resource classes
docs.text:
Class vCPU Memory Scratch Input data Bundle Accelerator S 2 8 GiB 3 GiB 0.5 GB 1 GB — M 4 16 GiB 6 GiB 2 GB 4 GB — L 8 32 GiB 12 GiB 5 GB 8 GB — XL (GKE) (GKE) (GKE) 50 GB 50 GB — GPU (v0.15) 8 32 GiB 12 GiB 50 GB 8 GB 1 NVIDIA L4

The classes are in this sequence: S < M < L < XL < GPU. A quota with a maximum class below GPU refuses the GPU class. After RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, the platform offers the next CPU class only (the GPU class is never offered). Validation refuses a spec that selects GPU for a model that does not use a GPU (resources.gpu in its manifest). It shows a note when a model can use the GPU and the spec selects a CPU class. Refer to Deep learning.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
model.fit.checkpoint saves resumable checkpoints during a fit. Give exactly one of:

Field For Meaning every_draws Samplers (PyMC) Save a checkpoint every N draws (1 to 1 000 000) every_epochs Networks (v0.15, dl.*) Save a checkpoint every N epochs (1 to 10 000) 
model:
  fit:
    checkpoint: {every_epochs: 2}

If the model cannot save checkpoints (capabilities.checkpointable is false), validation shows a warning at /model/fit/checkpoint/every_epochs and the run ignores the setting.

docs.title: Image collections in a spec v0.15
docs.text:
An image collection is a dataset version with the layout collection (see Image data). A model reads it in one of two ways:

  • A model with capabilities.input: collection (dl.cnn_classifier, dl.finetune_classifier) trains on batches of all images. The spec takes no pipeline steps (SCHEMA_INVALID at /pipeline).
  • Any other model reads a seeded sample as pixels(image, y, x, channel), as set by data.collection (a CollectionRead). Validation shows a note at /data/collection.
data:
  dataset: dataset://default/product_photos@v5
  collection:
    max_samples: 5000   # 1 to 100 000
    size: [32, 32]      # (height, width); default: the size of the collection
    resize: stretch     # stretch, crop or pad
    mode: auto          # auto, gray or rgb
    stratify: label     # a variable or coordinate along the image dim; null: uniform
    seed: 7             # default: the fit seed

When the collection has no common size and size is not set, the run fails with SCHEMA_INVALID at /data/collection/size. data.collection on a dataset that is not a collection gives a warning, and the run ignores it.

The other rules for a collection:

  • data.split must be a row split: column, stratified or leave_group_out (SPLIT_INVALID at /data/split/kind).
  • A side table must be a dataset, not a collection.

docs.title: Collection options
docs.text:
The options of a collection version (CollectionOptions, the options of DatasetVersionCreate.collection):

Option Default Meaning sha256_column sha256 The column with the lowercase hex SHA-256 of each image id_column none Unique ids of the image dim. Default: the path, else the SHA-256. path_column path Kept as the coordinate path. A missing default column is ignored. label_column none The class: the text variable label(image), role target split_column none The text coordinate split(image) columns all others The other columns to keep as coordinates (a maximum of 64). They cannot use the names of the fixed columns of manifest.parquet (image_id, sha256, pack, offset, stored, method, crc32, nbytes, format, width, height, mode). var, dim pixels, image The names of the virtual pixel variable and of the image dim mode auto gray, rgb or auto (rgb when an image has colour) size none The size (height, width) for samples and model defaults, each 1 to 4096 resize stretch stretch, crop or pad max_images 100 000 1 to 1 000 000

docs.title: Pretrained weights: the safetensors format v0.15
docs.text:
An upload of the format safetensors is a file of network weights. The mapping has only format and, optionally, weights (a WeightsOptions). A safetensors upload must be the only source of a dataset version.

format: safetensors
weights:
  arch: {kind: resnet, channels: 3, widths: [16, 32, 64], blocks: [1, 1, 1]}  # optional
  max_parameters: 200000000   # 1 to 500 000 000

arch is necessary only when the __metadata__ of the file has no mapi_arch key. Its JSON can have a maximum of 64 KiB. The ingest writes a weights dataset:

Name Dims Type Contents weights param float32 All tensors, flattened, role constant attribute mapi_weights JSON tensors (name, shape, source dtype, offset), metadata, arch, sha256 of the file and parameters

The ingest accepts the dtypes F64, F32, F16, BF16, I64, I32, I16, I8, U8 and BOOL, a maximum of 4096 tensors and a header of a maximum of 8 MiB. Use the weights dataset as a side table of a model or a step (see Deep learning).

docs.title: Retired documents
docs.text: The Sweep document is retired in v0.14. Stored Sweep documents still load, but the server does not accept new ones (422 SCHEMA_INVALID at /kind). Use a workflow with a search.grid node.

docs.title: Versions in use:
docs.text: use: takes a semver range in the npm style: ^1 (all 1.x), ~1.2 (1.2.x), >=1.2 <2, 1.x, an exact 1.2.3, or *. When you submit, the API selects the highest version that matches and is not yanked. The run records this version. Thus, you can run a revision again and get the same result.

docs.title: Where the split happens
docs.text: Some dims exist only after preprocessing. For example, a resample step can change daily data to weeks. Thus, the split occurs at a named stage (after_step). If you do not give a stage, the split occurs immediately after the first steps that learn nothing from the data. Examples are unit conversion and resample steps. A step that learns from the data (scale, encode, seasonality fit) can run before the split. Then validation reports LEAKAGE_RISK, because the step learns its state from the holdout.

docs.title: Validation messages
docs.text:
mapi check and POST /v1/specs:validate return all the problems at the same time. Each problem has a stable code and a JSON pointer to the incorrect field:
