Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): ranking (array), best (string).

docs.title: compare.stacking — Weigh models by their predictions
docs.text:
Gives each candidate model a weight from how well it predicts each data point that it did not see. A mix of the models with these weights predicts best.

Runs in a sandboxed workflow_node run. Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: You fitted several Bayesian models of the same data and none is clearly best; You want to average the predictions of the models, not select one of them.

Avoid it when: The models used different data (the scores are not comparable).

Example: Weights: bym2 0.71, icar 0.29, iid 0.00.

Inputs: candidates (metrics, several).

Outputs: table (table).

Parameter Type Default Meaning metric elpd_loo \ elpd_waic "elpd_loo" method stacking \ pseudo_bma_plus "stacking" n_bootstrap integer 1000 Bootstrap draws for pseudo-BMA+

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): weights (object), pseudo_bma (object), best (string), method (string), note_plain (string).

Expert detail

Stacking maximises sum_i log sum_k w_k exp(elpd_loo_ik) over the simplex (Yao, Vehtari, Simpson & Gelman 2018), from the pointwise PSIS-LOO values that model.fit stores for data of at most 10 000 points. pseudo_bma (always reported) is pseudo-BMA+: softmax weights averaged over a Bayesian bootstrap of the pointwise elpd. Without pointwise values the weights are pseudo-BMA from elpd ± se (method pseudo_bma_se) or from elpd alone (pseudo_bma), and note_plain says so.

docs.title: Selection (select)
docs.text: Selects the winner, or all candidates that pass a limit.

docs.title: select.best — Select the best model
docs.text:
Selects the model with the best score from a comparison. It can also make sure that the model is better than the simple benchmarks.

Runs in the orchestrator (no data; computed from earlier results). Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: instant.

Use it when: The end of a bake-off between candidates.

Avoid it when: Only one candidate.

Example: Select the lowest RMSE, but only if it is 5% better than seasonal naive.

Inputs: table (table), models (model_version, several, optional).

Outputs: model (model_version).

Parameter Type Default Meaning metric string "rmse" direction min \ max "min" must_beat array The benchmark ids that the winner must be better than margin number 0.0 The necessary relative improvement over must_beat

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): selected (string), selected_model (string), score (number), beats_baselines (boolean), reason_plain (string).

docs.title: select.threshold — Keep models that pass a limit
docs.text:
Keeps only the models with a score that passes a limit that you set, for example an error below 10%.

Runs in the orchestrator (no data; computed from earlier results). Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: instant.

Use it when: You need all models that are good enough, not only the best.

Avoid it when: You need one winner only.

Example: Keep all models with a MAPE below 10%.

Inputs: table (table).

Outputs: table (table).

Parameter Type Default Meaning metric string required max number Upper limit min number Lower limit

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): passed (array), n_passed (integer).

docs.title: Governance (governance)
docs.text: Runs the checks that a model must pass before you can validate it. It stores the evidence.

docs.title: governance.check — Run one governance check
docs.text:
Runs one check from the governance catalog on a model, for example the shuffled-result test.

Runs in its own child run (a fit run for model.fit, else a workflow_node run). Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: minutes.

Use it when: You want to try a check before you add it to a policy.

Avoid it when: Formal validation (run the full policy).

Example: The noise-channel check gives the fake channel a 2% share. The check passes.

Inputs: model (model_version), data (dataset, optional).

Outputs: evidence (evidence).

Parameter Type Default Meaning check string required Check id (governance catalog) params object Check parameters warn number Warn threshold fail number Fail threshold

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): status (string), value (number).

docs.title: governance.policy — Run the governance checks
docs.text:
Runs on a model all the checks that the policy of your organisation needs, and records the evidence. For example, the model must be better than random noise and a simple benchmark.

Runs in its own child run (a fit run for model.fit, else a workflow_node run). Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: long. Never cached (its result depends on more than its inputs).

Use it when: Before you validate and promote a model.

Avoid it when: Exploratory work that nobody will use.

Example: Seven checks pass and the placebo check fails, so the model is not validated.

Inputs: model (model_version), data (dataset, optional).

Outputs: evidence (evidence).

Parameter Type Default Meaning policy string The policy id (default: the policy that is in force) submit boolean false Submit the result for approval when the checks pass

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): passed (boolean), failed_checks (array), status (string).

docs.title: Report (report)
docs.text: Changes the results of the workflow into a report that is easy to read, or into an evidence pack.

docs.title: report.evidence_pack — Evidence pack
docs.text:
Puts the governance evidence, decisions and approvals of a model into one document for auditors, as HTML and JSON.

Runs in its own child run (a fit run for model.fit, else a workflow_node run). Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: An audit, a model risk review or an approval.

Avoid it when: Before the governance checks run.

Example: A pack with 9 checks, 2 approvals and the lineage of model v7.

Inputs: model (model_version), evidence (evidence, optional).

Outputs: report (report).

Parameter Type Default Meaning format html \ json "html"

docs.title: report.summary — Plain-language report
docs.text:
Writes a short report of the workflow results: the test verdicts, the decisions, the selected model and how good it is.

Runs in the orchestrator (no data; computed from earlier results). Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: instant.

Use it when: At the end of a workflow that you share with other persons.

Avoid it when: You only need the raw numbers.

Example: Sales wander, so the workflow applied a difference. ARIMAX(2,1,1) was 30% better than seasonal naive.

Inputs: items (table, several, optional), tests (test_result, several, optional), metrics (metrics, several, optional), model (model_version, optional), plots (plot, several, optional).

Outputs: report (report).

Parameter Type Default Meaning title string sections array Node ids to include (default: all)

docs.title: Plot (plot)
docs.text: Draws a plot from the plot catalog in the run, for the run view and the report.

docs.title: plot.render — Draw a plot
docs.text:
Draws a plot from the plot catalog with a model or a dataset of earlier steps. The run shows the plot, and a report can include it.

Runs in a sandboxed workflow_node run. Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: You want a chart of a model or of predictions in the run and in the report.

Avoid it when: The Model Explorer already shows the chart that you need.

Example: Draw sci.field_map of the fitted heat plate model.

Inputs: model (model_version, optional), data (dataset, optional).

Outputs: plot (plot).

Parameter Type Default Meaning recipe string required Plot recipe ref (id or id@range), for example core.ppc_fan settings object The settings of the recipe source auto \ data \ model \ title string The title of the plot (default: the recipe title)

Result fields (nodes.<id>.<field> in conditions): recipe (string), kind (string), source (string), bytes (integer).

Expert detail

The node renders the recipe with mapi_plots.recipes.render_plots and the sanitizer. With 'source: auto' it tries the dataset, the model bundle and then the in-sample predictions of the model with the observed values.

docs.title: Sub-workflow (subworkflow)
docs.text: Runs another saved workflow as one step.

docs.title: subworkflow.run — Run another workflow
docs.text:
Runs a saved workflow as one step of this workflow. You write common sequences, for example data readiness checks, one time and use them again.

Runs in its own child run (a fit run for model.fit, else a workflow_node run). Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: minutes.

Use it when: Several workflows use the same sequence of steps.

Avoid it when: Only this workflow uses the steps.

Example: Use 'time-series readiness' again before three different model workflows.

Parameter Type Default Meaning workflow string required workflow:///@ params object The parameters to give to the other workflow

docs.title: mapi_client
docs.text: This page shows the Python client for the /v1 HTTP API. For tested procedures, read the Python client guide. For a summary of each resource, read CLI and Python client. The text on this page comes from the docstrings. AsyncClient has the same resources, but you use await with them.

docs.title: Clients
docs.text:
Python client for the modeling-api /v1 HTTP API.

  • :class:Client / :class:AsyncClient - typed with the mapi_spec.api DTOs; resources projects, catalog, datasets, specs, runs, models and plots, and from v0.3 tenants, tokens, usage and admin (plus :meth:Client.me);
  • credentials: an API token (MAPI_TOKEN, config profile) or the OIDC sign-in stored by mapi login (:mod:mapi_client.oidc), renewed automatically;
  • project selection: Client(project="acme/growth") / MAPI_PROJECT / the profile's project is sent as X-Mapi-Project on project-scoped requests;
  • 429 handling: RATE_LIMITED is waited out (Retry-After) and resent; QUOTA_EXCEEDED raises :class:~mapi_spec.errors.QuotaExceeded with :func:retry_after_of (see :class:RetryPolicy);
  • errors are :class:mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses rebuilt from RFC 7807 problems (see :mod:mapi_client.errors);
  • list endpoints return lazy :class:Paginator / :class:AsyncPaginator iterators;
  • runs.stream_events follows the SSE stream and resumes with Last-Event-ID;
  • datasets.upload and models.score handle signed URLs, waiting and CRC32C checks; xr.Dataset uploads and xr.DataTree results need the xarray extra;
  • from v0.4 guided, endpoints (and Client.endpoint(alias), a :class:RemoteEndpoint whose score(ds) returns an xr.Dataset), webhooks, saved plots, renders and embeds on plots, sign-up (:meth:Client.signup) and the trust lifecycle on tenants/admin; :mod:mapi_client.webhooks verifies deliveries and :mod:mapi_client.xrjson encodes inline payloads;
  • from v0.5 workflows (documents, revisions, runs with :meth:stream_events - an SSE iterator of :class:WorkflowSnapshot, :class:WorkflowEventFrame and :class:WorkflowEnd - node outputs, schedules, triggers, the template gallery), governance (check catalog, project and tenant policies), validations (requests, the review queue, approvals, evidence packs), explorations and the Data/Model Explorer, comparison and budget optimisation (models.optimize) methods, and About cards with Help me choose on catalog (abouts, chooser, recommend);
  • from v0.11 run tracking on runs: update (name, note, tags), log_metric(s), log_params, set_tags, metrics, metric_history, params, run search in list (filters, order_by, columns, tags) and :meth:Runs.track, a buffered :class:RunTracker; stream_events yields :class:RunTrackingFrame;
  • from v0.14 run media on runs (media, media_keys, get_media, download_media - size, CRC32C and sha256 checked - log_image, log_table), runs.compare and runs.keys, list(experiment_id=...), and the resources experiments (named groups of runs) and run_views (saved runs-table searches).

from mapi_client import Client # doctest: +SKIP with Client("http://127.0.0.1:8000") as api: ... version = api.datasets.upload("eu_media.zarr.zip", dataset="eu_media_daily")

docs.title: RetryPolicy
docs.text:
RetryPolicy(
    max_retries: int = 2,
    base_delay: float = 0.5,
    max_delay: float = 30.0,
    rate_limit_retries: int = 4,
    max_rate_limit_wait: float = 120.0,
    max_quota_wait: float = 0.0,
    jitter: float = 0.1,
)

When and how long to wait before resending a request.

  • Transport errors and 502/503/504: idempotent calls only (safe methods, Idempotency-Key, or by definition), max_retries times, exponential backoff with full jitter, honouring Retry-After (capped at max_delay).
  • 429 RATE_LIMITED: the server refused the request before acting on it (:mod:mapi_spec.quotas runs before any handler), so every method is resent, up to rate_limit_retries times, after max(Retry-After, base·2^n) plus a little jitter. A Retry-After longer than max_rate_limit_wait is not waited out: the error is raised with :func:~mapi_client.errors.retry_after_of set.
  • 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED: raised at once, unless the quota resets within max_quota_wait seconds (default 0: never wait for a quota window).
  • A bare 429 without a problem document (a proxy) is treated like RATE_LIMITED for idempotent calls only.

docs.title: Workflow run events (v0.5)
docs.text:
Server-sent events: a WHATWG-conformant line decoder and typed run-stream items.

GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events (Accept: text/event-stream) sends snapshot (the full :class:~mapi_spec.api.Run, no id) first on every connection, then the persisted run events (id: = :attr:RunEventView.id) after Last-Event-ID, then live events, and finally end (the final run) before closing. : keepalive comments are heartbeats. progress and log frames are live and unpersisted: they carry no id: and are never replayed after a reconnect (:class:RunLiveFrame). tracking frames (v0.11, no id) tell which metric series changed and whether params or tags changed (:class:RunTrackingFrame).

GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}/events follows the same pattern for workflow runs (v0.5): snapshot (the :class:~mapi_spec.workflow.WorkflowRun with every node), one frame per :class:~mapi_spec.workflow.WorkflowEvent (event: is its type, id: its seq) and end (the run id and its final status), decoded by :func:to_workflow_stream_item.

forecast(
    alias: str,
    rows: Table | None = None,
    *,
    actuals: Table | None = None,
    future: Table | Sequence[Any] | int | None = None,
    periods: int | None = None,
    future_covariates: str = "carry_last",
    output: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    schema: EndpointSchema | None = None,
    **options: Any,
) -> ScoreResult

Forecast with your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (the model is not refitted: it updates its state with the actuals and forecasts from the last one).

rows is a long table in the endpoint's input layout (schema.input_table: the time column, the target, the drivers) - a DataFrame or a list of row mappings: rows whose target holds a value are actuals, rows after them with it empty are forecast. Or split it: actuals= (rows with the target) and future= (the dates, rows with driver values, or a number of periods to append). Empty driver values on the future rows follow future_covariates (carried forward by default). Models that cannot use actuals refuse them (ActualsNotSupported) rather than ignore them.

The result's :attr:ScoreResult.conditioning says what the forecast was conditioned on. options are those of :meth:score (wait, timeout, download...).

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
The JSON-only PlotSpec sanitizer (plan §10.3, step 1).

This is the control-plane half of plot safety. It depends only on mapi-spec and jsonschema and never imports numpy, pandas, altair or plotly (enforced by import-linter and a subprocess test), so mapi_server can run it on every plot it stores or serves.

from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot result = sanitize_plot(plot_json) # PlotSpec | dict | str | bytes result.plot # the sanitized PlotSpec result.changes # what was rewritten (HTML stripped, ...)

Anything unsafe raises :class:SanitizeError (a MapiError) whose issues carry the JSON pointer, the :class:SanitizeRule (in context["rule"]) and any user-supplied text in untrusted_text. :func:check_plot returns the same issues without raising (for editors).

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Role/dim-bound plot templates (plan §10.1).

A template is an ordinary :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec whose bindings say what to plot in schema terms ({x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}) instead of naming one bundle's variables. :func:apply_template resolves the bindings against a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema and fills the placeholders in the spec, so one user-authored "fan chart of the target over time, faceted by geo" applies to every model of a family. This module is JSON-only (it runs in the control plane).

Placeholders inside spec:

  • {"$bind": "y"} - replaced by a Vega-Lite field definition {"field": ..., "type": ..., "title": ...}; dropped entirely when the channel is optional and unresolved (so encoding.facet simply disappears for a model without geo);
  • "{{y}}" - the bound name; "{{y.field}}" - the name escaped for Vega-Lite field access (dots); "{{y.type}}" - the Vega-Lite type; "{{y.title}}" - name plus units. Placeholders may be embedded in longer strings (titles, captions).

docs.text:
Build :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec envelopes from Altair charts and Plotly figures.

Extra recipes only (needs altair, plotly, numpy, pandas and pyarrow).

  • :func:from_plotly decodes plotly.py 6 typed arrays ({dtype, bdata, shape}) and inline data arrays into named Arrow datasets, one per trace (and array length), and binds them with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"}. String columns get the inline-text rules here (HTML stripped to the Plotly allow-list, script/CSS URLs rejected) because the control-plane sanitizer never decodes Arrow; the plot iframe must still re-strip dataset strings.

Both run the result through the sanitizer unless sanitize=False. Datasets are base64 Arrow IPC streams (:class:~mapi_spec.plots.InlineArrow); datetimes are stored as UTC millisecond timestamps, which JavaScript reads as numbers.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
The standard plot recipe catalog (plan §10.2). Extra recipes only.

Every recipe is a function (DataTree-like, settings) -> PlotSpec with its data in named Arrow datasets (never URLs), a persona and a plain-language caption. They are generated in the runner from a fitted bundle or a score output, so every plugin gets them for free:

============================ ========================================================== core.data_overview series per variable, missingness heatmap, group sizes core.prior_predictive prior predictive densities (+ fan over time) core.convergence R-hat / ESS per parameter, worst-parameter table, trace, rank core.posterior_forest point, 50% and 94% HDI per parameter core.ppc predictive density overlay, PIT histogram, coverage core.ppc_fan fit + forecast fan with the split line core.fit_vs_actual predicted against actual core.residuals_over_time actual minus predicted over time core.decomposition stacked contributions and totals core.model_comparison elpd forest (precomputed LOO table, or WAIC) core.counterfactual scenario vs baseline band + total-change distribution core.decision_distribution scalar decision objective per option core.pair corner plot of a few parameters, divergences highlighted core.ridge one density per level of a dim, ordered by mean core.rank_matrix P(rank = k) per item and pairwise P(i above j) core.calibration PIT-ECDF difference with an envelope, or a reliability diagram core.state_sequence observed series above stacked state probabilities core.roc_pr ROC and precision-recall curves of a binary classifier core.confusion 2 x 2 confusion matrix at a probability threshold core.loss_curve loss of an iterative fit (ADVI) per step, moving average core.loo_pit LOO-PIT calibration and the PSIS Pareto k per observation core.energy marginal energy vs energy transitions, E-BFMI per chain core.prior_posterior prior and posterior densities per parameter, ranked by shift ============================ ==========================================================

The MMM domain pack lives in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.mmm and the tabular-ML pack (ml.feature_importance) in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.ml, and the scientific-model pack (sci.field_map, sci.vector_field, sci.profile_bands, sci.ensemble; Plotly) in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.sci, with the map, tree and polar recipes in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.sci_maps, the image and spectrum recipes in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.sci_images and sci.point_pattern in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.sci_points, the network pack (net.graph; Plotly) in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.net, and the causal pack (causal.impact, causal.pre_fit, causal.donor_weights, causal.event_study) in :mod:mapi_plots.packs.causal. All are exposed through the mapi.plots entry-point group, so mapi_sdk.registry.default_registry() finds them.

docs.title: mapi_pymc
docs.text: This package is for PyMC models. You write build(). The package gives engines, diagnostics, new levels and counterfactuals.

docs.title: The base class
docs.text:
PyMCModel: authors write build(); the platform fits, predicts and checkpoints (§5).

.. code-block:: python

class Radon(PyMCModel[RadonSettings]):
    id = "demo.radon"
    version = "1.0.0"
    Settings = RadonSettings
    schema_template = {...}
    outputs = {"y": {"dims": ["obs"], "units_of": "y"}}
    expected = {"y": "mu"}             # output -> Deterministic holding E[y]

    def build(self, ds, s, ctx):
        with pm.Model(coords=ctx.coords()) as m:
            floor = ctx.data("floor")
            county = ctx.data("county_idx")
            a = ctx.hier_effect("a", "county")
            b = pm.Normal("b", 0, 1)
            mu = pm.Deterministic("mu", a[county] + b * floor, dims="obs")
            pm.Normal("y", mu, pm.HalfNormal("sigma", 1), observed=ctx.observed("y"),
                      dims="obs")
        return m

fit dispatches to the engine in fit.engine (see :mod:mapi_pymc.engines), adds the opt-in groups (prior/prior_predictive, log_likelihood, a thinned posterior_predictive) and turns r-hat, ESS and divergences into diagnostics.

score rebuilds the model on the canonicalised score data and runs pm.sample_posterior_predictive(..., predictions=True) against the posterior:

  • output.kind = expected returns the Deterministic named in :attr:PyMCModel.expected (no observation noise; counterfactual deltas on it are exact per draw);
  • output.kind = predictive returns draws of the observed variable through icdf(dist, U) with frozen uniforms U seeded by (seed, name, shape). A counterfactual's scenario and baseline therefore share their noise (common random numbers) and the delta's variance is not inflated. Discrete distributions without a symbolic inverse CDF (Poisson, negative binomial, binomial) sample their parameters and push the same frozen uniforms through a numeric inverse CDF (noise = crn_ppf), so a change in one cell's mean never reshuffles the noise of the others. Only distributions with neither fall back to the seeded sampler stream (seeded_stream), whose draws in unchanged cells can still differ between a scenario and its baseline - prefer kind: expected deltas for those.

docs.title: PyMCModel
docs.text:
Bases: CustomModel[SettingsT]

Base class for PyMC plugins: implement :meth:build; declare outputs and expected.

Class attributes beyond :class:~mapi_sdk.models.CustomModel:

  • expected - {output: Deterministic name} for kind=expected predictions;
  • predictive - {output: observed RV name} (default: the output's own name);
  • default_engine - engine when the spec names none (default nutpie, else pymc);
  • fast_score_spec - a :class:~mapi_pymc.frozen.FrozenPredictorSpec enabling :meth:frozen_predictor (the manifest then declares fast_score);
  • prior_overlap_vars - free parameters whose prior draws (prior_overlap_draws, forward sampling only, so cheap) are kept as the prior group when the spec keeps no prior itself, so the sanity scorecard can measure how much the data moved them (M3, plausibility.prior_overlap). Empty (the default) keeps nothing.

docs.title: Build context
docs.text:
BuildContext: what a PyMC model's build() uses instead of raw coordinates (plan §5).

build(ds, settings, ctx) runs twice in a model's life: at fit on the training data, and at score on canonicalised score data (fit levels in fit order, then new levels, padded extend dims). The helpers hide the differences so the same build serves both:

  • :meth:BuildContext.coords - the pm.Model(coords=...) mapping; adds <dim>__fit and <dim>__new when the score data holds unseen levels;
  • :meth:BuildContext.data - pm.Data over the current values (rebuild-and-predict);
  • :meth:BuildContext.observed - the target at fit, a shape-only placeholder at score;
  • :meth:BuildContext.hier_effect - a hierarchical effect over a new_levels dim whose new levels are filled according to the dim's strategy (hyperprior draws them from the fitted hyperprior during prediction, with frozen noise so scenario and baseline agree);
  • :meth:BuildContext.position / :attr:BuildContext.anticipated_coords - stable positions along extend dims, so trends and HSGPs see the same axis at fit and at forecast time.

BuildContext.tree (M4) is the bound tree dataset for models whose capabilities declare input="tree" (FitContext.tree / ScoreContext.tree), else None.

docs.title: hier_effect
docs.text:
hier_effect(
    name: str,
    dim: str,
    *,
    mu: Any = None,
    sigma: Any = None,
    centered: bool = False,
    mu_sigma: float = 1.0,
    sigma_scale: float = 1.0,
) -> TensorVariable

A partially pooled effect over dim: name[dim] ~ Normal(mu, sigma).

Creates name (dims dim) - non-centred by default via name__offset - plus hyperpriors name__mu ~ Normal(0, mu_sigma) and name__sigma ~ HalfNormal (sigma_scale) unless mu/sigma are given (mu may be a scalar or a vector over the full dim). When the score data holds unseen levels, name__new covers them according to the dim's new-level strategy:

  • hyperprior - mu + sigma * z with z frozen standard-normal noise, i.e. a fresh level drawn from the fitted hyperprior for every posterior draw;
  • pooled - the population mean mu;
  • zero - 0;
  • error - raises UNSEEN_LEVELS.

Returns the effect over the full current dim (fit levels, then new levels).

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
Inference engines for :class:~mapi_pymc.PyMCModel (plan §5).

fit.engine picks one of:

============== ========================================================================== nutpie nutpie NUTS (default when installed). Fast, parallel chains. Not bit-for-bit reproducible from a seed. Checkpoints are snapshots (draws so far): nutpie cannot export its adaptation, so a retry samples again from the start. pymc PyMC NUTS with segmented sampling: tune once, then draw in chunks of fit.checkpoint.every_draws. After each chunk a resumable checkpoint holds the draws, every chain's position and the full sampler state; a retry resumes exactly where the last chunk ended. Chains run in this process one after another (models with discrete variables fall back to pm.sample without segments). numpyro PyMC's external NUTS bridges, when the library is installed. No segments. blackjax map pm.find_MAP - one "draw" (chain 1, draw 1). advi mean-field ADVI; fit.tune is the number of optimisation steps (default 10,000) and fit.draws the number of draws from the approximation. pathfinder pymc-extras' Pathfinder when pymc-extras is installed (extra pathfinder: mapi-pymc[pathfinder]). One chain; no progress table on stdout. ============== ==========================================================================

Every engine reports progress through one callback (fraction, message) where the message names the chain ("chain 2/4: sampling 150/500, 0 divergences").

Tracking. When :attr:EngineHooks.tracker is set (:meth:EngineHooks.for_context sets it when the run records metrics), the engines also report every chain's progress (nutpie, pymc) and step metrics: step_size, num_steps and cumulative divergences per chain (label chain; step = draws done, tuning included; the pymc engine adds tree_depth and logs every k-th draw so that a chain has at most :data:MAX_HISTORY_POINTS points per metric), and the ADVI loss (negative ELBO) at most :data:MAX_HISTORY_POINTS times per fit. :func:pymc_draw_callback gives the same for a library that calls pm.sample itself. numpyro, blackjax, map and pathfinder report progress only.

Start points. By default every MCMC chain starts at the model's initial point with a random jitter. A plugin whose posterior has a trap near the default start (a mixture whose components all switch off) sets :attr:EnginePlan.initvals (values on the constrained scale, by free variable name, as pm.sample(initvals=...)) and jitter=False with dataclasses.replace(plan, ...): every chain then starts at exactly that point (pymc, nutpie and the external NUTS bridges; map, advi and pathfinder ignore both).

docs.title: Fast scoring
docs.text:
FrozenPredictor: one compiled PyTensor function for fast posterior predictions (plan §5).

Ported from pymc-model-interactivity/frozen_predictor.py to PyMC 6 / PyTensor 3 and ArviZ 1.x (posteriors are xr.DataTree / xr.Dataset). Given a model, posterior samples, response expressions and the pm.Data inputs to vary, it compiles a single function vectorised over posterior samples and scenarios:

  • only the free random variables that are ancestors of the responses are bound, to constant posterior samples (so compilation stays small);
  • observed random variables upstream of a response are replaced by their observed values when they do not depend on the inputs, and by icdf(dist, U) with frozen uniform quantiles U (one per sample) when they do - common random numbers across scenarios;
  • SpecifyShape constraints on dims that only the inputs use are removed, so inputs may change length (dims shared with other model variables stay fixed).

Inputs may have the data variable's own shape (one scenario) or an extra leading scenario axis. Outputs have shape (sample, [scenario,] *dims) before the optional reducer.

The plan's FrozenPredictorSpec(response_exprs, input_vars, reducer) is the JSON form a plugin declares when capabilities.fast_score is true.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
Checkpoints for segmented sampling (plan §5, §8.3).

A long MCMC fit tunes once and then draws in chunks. After each chunk the engine hands a :class:SamplingCheckpoint to a :class:CheckpointSink; a retried run with the same fit key resumes from the last checkpoint instead of starting again.

Two kinds of checkpoint exist:

  • resumable (engine pymc): the draws so far, every chain's current position and the full NUTS sampling state (adapted step size, mass matrix, RNG state). Resuming continues the same chains exactly; the result equals an uninterrupted run with the same seed.
  • snapshot (engine nutpie): the draws so far only. nutpie cannot export or restore its adaptation state, so a snapshot feeds a PARTIAL bundle but a retry starts again.

Nothing here pickles. Sampling states are encoded to JSON by :func:encode_state; arrays travel base64-encoded and dataclasses are rebuilt only from classes defined in an allow-list of PyMC step-method modules (and this package).

docs.title: Supervisor <-> worker channel
docs.text:
The supervisor <-> worker message channel (a socketpair; plan §8.7).

Frames are a 4-byte big-endian length followed by one UTF-8 JSON object. Every message is validated against the models below; the worker is untrusted, so anything malformed, oversized or of an unknown type is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION on the supervisor side.

Supervisor -> worker: exactly one :class:StartMessage (no HMAC key, no output URLs). Worker -> supervisor: state, progress, diagnostic, warning, metric, checkpoint, the tracking messages metrics (batched metric points), params, tags and user_log (structured log lines, stream user), media (v0.14: one file the worker wrote under {scratch}/media/), then exactly one terminal result or error. The supervisor accounts every tracking message against StartMessage.tracking (the run's :class:~mapi_spec.tracking.TrackingLimits).

docs.title: Supervisor
docs.text:
The trusted supervisor (plan §8.1, §8.5, §8.7).

One supervisor runs per execution. It:

  1. reads MAPI_RUN_ID/MAPI_NONCE/MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL, fetches the RunSpec bootstrap object and deletes it before anything else happens;
  2. starts the untrusted worker (python -I -u -m mapi_runner.worker) as a child with a scrubbed environment, a socketpair for messages and pipes for stdout/stderr - as uid 10001 with no-new-privs when it runs as root, in dev mode otherwise;
  3. validates every worker message, turns them and the captured output into HMAC-signed events on its own stdout (the only thing ever written there), enforces the log, event, tracking, scratch and output caps, and coalesces progress;
  4. handles SIGTERM and the run deadline (forward to the worker, wait for the checkpoint flush, upload a partial manifest);
  5. uploads the media the worker logs (v0.14: each file under {scratch}/media/ is read safely, hashed and checked by the supervisor, then sent through the run's media POST policy) and emits one media event per item;
  6. uploads outputs with the signed POST policy (streaming, hashing as it goes), writes the signed :class:~mapi_spec.run.OutputManifest with the signed PUT and exits with a :class:~mapi_spec.run.RunnerExit code.

The supervisor never imports plugin code, the SDK, numpy or xarray.

docs.title: Fit and score
docs.text:
The fit/score harness: the platform side of every run (plan §4.2).

:func:fit_spec implements fit.mode:

  • bind the data, validate it, fit the stateless prefix on all data up to the split stage;
  • split; fit the remaining step states and the model on train (the evaluation fit);
  • evaluate the holdout through the score path (context from train) - never a separate code path - and compute the spec's metrics;
  • evaluate_then_refit: refit states and model on train ∪ holdout so the context tails and terminal state come from the full data; the production bundle links the evaluation bundle and its metrics. train_only keeps the train fit as the result.
  • derived quantities the spec requests (outputs.derived) whose manifest declaration says cache: fit are computed on the production fit by the plugin's derive hook, over the first outputs.ui_draws draws of the thinning index, with ScoreContext.to_original mapping them to the output space.

:func:score_bundle implements scoring: CoordPlan checks, binding, interventions, entry at inputs_stage, context replay, canonical coords, model.score, context removal, selection, inverse transforms to the output space, aggregation, summaries, thinned draws and reverse binding. It returns an xr.DataTree.

Tree datasets (M4): both accept an xr.DataTree wherever they take the dataset. The nodes the spec's data.nodes selects are merged into one flat dataset first (:func:mapi_sdk.tree.select_nodes, aligned per data.join) and everything else runs on it exactly as for a plain dataset. A model whose capabilities declare input="tree" also gets the whole tree, bound per node, as FitContext.tree / ScoreContext.tree.

Image collections (v0.15): both accept a :class:~mapi_sdk.collection.Collection as the dataset. A model that reads datasets gets a seeded sample as the v0.14 image dataset (:func:~mapi_sdk.collection.collection_read, per data.collection). A model whose capabilities declare input="collection" runs on the manifest dataset (one row per image, no pixels; binding, schema checks, row splits, metrics and bundles as usual) and only the model call changes: fit_batches/score_batches receive a loader of the images of the rows that reached the model.

docs.title: fit_spec
docs.text:
fit_spec(
    spec: ModelSpec | str,
    data: Dataset | DataTree | Collection,
    side_tables: Mapping[str, Dataset] | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
    *,
    raw_schema: DataSchema | None = None,
    hooks: FitHooks | None = None,
    keep_evaluation_bundle: bool = True,
    hash_data: bool = True,
    tree_schema: TreeSchema | None = None,
    tree: DataTree | None = None,
    record_metrics: bool = True,
) -> Bundle

Fit spec on data and return the production :class:~mapi_sdk.bundle.Bundle.

raw_schema describes data under its dataset names; when omitted it is read from data.attrs["mapi_schema"] or inferred (variables bound to the model's targets are marked as targets). side_tables maps data.side_tables names to datasets.

data may be a tree dataset (M4): the nodes spec.data.nodes selects are merged into the flat dataset the pipeline reads (:func:mapi_sdk.tree.select_nodes); tree_schema describes the tree (inferred when omitted) and raw_schema, if given, the merged flat dataset. A tree-input model also gets the bound tree (ctx.tree); tree (dataset names) stands in for it when data was already selected from a tree (a refit on modified flat data). With a data.split the evaluation fit and the holdout score see only their part of the tree.

Run tracking (v0.11): the spec params (:func:mapi_sdk.tracking.spec_params) go to hooks.tracker once; what the model logs goes to hooks.tracker (an evaluation fit's metrics with the label fit=evaluation) and, with record_metrics, into each bundle's metrics_history model group.

data may be an image collection (v0.15, see the module docstring): the pipeline must then be empty for an input="collection" model, and only row splits are taken.

docs.title: score_bundle
docs.text:
score_bundle(
    bundle: Bundle,
    request: ScoreRequest | str,
    data: Dataset | DataTree | Collection | None = None,
    *,
    scenario: Dataset | DataTree | None = None,
    side_tables: Mapping[str, Dataset] | None = None,
    registry: Registry | None = None,
    max_draws: int | None = None,
    return_full: bool = False,
    metrics: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    metric_mask: DataArray | None = None,
    hooks: FitHooks | None = None,
    observed: Dataset | DataTree | None = None,
    history: Dataset | DataTree | None = None,
    tree: DataTree | None = None,
    metric_history: Dataset | None = None,
    collection: Collection | None = None,
) -> DataTree

Score a fitted bundle; returns a DataTree.

data is the request's data payload and scenario its scenario payload. Outside counterfactuals a scenario simply is the payload. A counterfactual scores the scenario (or the data, when no scenario is given) with the interventions applied against the baseline data; a scenario without baseline data is rejected.

Groups: summary (stats along a stat dim), draws (when requested; joint, from the bundle thinning index), predictions (full representation, when return_full), and for counterfactuals baseline/... and delta/.... Root attrs carry the representation, output kind, units/output space, retransformation labels, non-error issues and - in evaluate mode - the metrics. observed (evaluation of cell-level splits) gives the observed targets for metrics when data has them masked. history (M3) is the fitted dataset (dataset names): forecasts whose future_covariates policy is carry_last or seasonal_naive extend the covariates the payload lacks from it (:mod:mapi_sdk.future).

Tree datasets (M4): data, scenario, observed and history may be xr.DataTree versions entering at the raw stage; the nodes the bundle's data.nodes selects are merged into the flat payload first. A model whose capabilities declare input="tree" gets the payload's tree, bound, as ScoreContext.tree; tree (dataset names) stands in for it when the payload is already flat (the evaluation of a fit from a tree dataset).

metric_history (v0.10) is the training data at req.inputs_stage (any names) of an evaluation; mase takes its scale from it (:func:mapi_sdk.metrics.mase_scale). Its targets go through the pipeline to the model stage and back to the output space exactly like the observed values (or stay at the model stage for a model that owns inverse_units), so the naive error is in the units of the error it divides. Without it, mase is skipped.

data may be an image collection (v0.15): a model that reads datasets scores a seeded sample (data.collection of the fit spec); an input="collection" model scores the manifest dataset with score_batches on the requested images. A manifest payload (a subset of the collection's manifest dataset, such as the evaluation holdout) names its collection instead.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
The preprocessing step contract: Step, StepState and StepContext.

A step is a class with static metadata (id, version, kind, a Pydantic Settings model, an optional State model) and four methods::

fit(ds, settings, ctx) -> State           # learn on train data only
transform(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds # never learns; must tolerate an absent target
inverse(ds, settings, state, ctx) -> ds   # invertible VALUE steps only

Rules the contract kit (:mod:mapi_sdk.testing) enforces:

  • transform(train, fit(train)) equals the fit-time output exactly, and transform is deterministic and does not mutate its input;
  • reductions name the dims they reduce over; the state stays labelled by the rest;
  • group-local operations take along/within and declare a :class:ContextNeed;
  • unseen levels go through :meth:StepContext.align_state;
  • the static :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect (effect_template) matches the real output schema.

The static metadata is exported as a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.StepCatalogEntry, so the control plane validates specs without importing step code.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
The model plugin contract (plan §5).

A plugin turns a model-stage xr.Dataset into a :class:FitOutput and, later, scores a canonicalised dataset into an xr.DataTree whose predictions group holds the declared outputs in the plugin's :class:~mapi_spec.capabilities.Representation::

draws      (chain, draw, *dims)
quantiles  (quantile, *dims)       quantile coords in (0, 1)
interval   (bound, *dims)          bound coords include "lower", "upper" (+ "point")
point      (*dims)
moments    (moment, *dims)         moment coords ["mean", "sd"]

The platform owns everything around that: binding, CoordPlan, context, canonical coords, inverse transforms, reverse binding and summaries. :class:CustomModel is the base class for hand-written plugins; mapi_pymc.PyMCModel and mapi_sklearn.SklearnModel build on the same protocol.

Optional hooks: :meth:diagnostics, :meth:postprocess, :meth:derive, :meth:objective, :meth:recommend, :meth:translate_priors, :meth:optimize, :meth:forecast_with_actuals (with capabilities.conditions_on_actuals), :meth:fit_batches/:meth:score_batches (with capabilities.input="collection"). Set pad_extend = False if the model does not index time positionally (scoring then skips padding extend dims to the fit range). List in structural_missing the canonical variables whose NaN are part of the design of the data (not gaps), so that the scorecard check data.missing does not count them.

    fitted: Fitted,
    ds: Dataset,
    actuals: ForecastActuals,
    req: ScoreRequest,
    ctx: ScoreContext,
) -> DataTree

A forecast conditioned on actuals (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals): plugins that declare capabilities.conditions_on_actuals override it; the harness calls it instead of :meth:score whenever a forecast payload carries actuals.

ds is the canonicalised model-stage payload (actuals, periods to forecast and their drivers); actuals says which periods are which per series (:class:~mapi_sdk.actuals.ForecastActuals). Update the model's state with the actuals using the fitted parameters - never re-estimate - and return the predictions group over every period of ds, as :meth:score does: the conditioned multi-step forecast on actuals.future, one-step-ahead predictions elsewhere. Supplied actuals inside the fitted range replace the fitted values.

The default refuses (ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED), so a model never ignores actuals.

Everything a plugin's fit may use besides data, settings and fit config.

schema is the model's resolved input schema (its template); stage_schema is the schema of the pipeline stage the data comes from, with every variable and its role.

checkpoint_sink is an engine-specific sink for segmented fits (for example mapi_pymc.CheckpointSink); the runner supplies one that writes to the run prefix. None disables checkpointing.

tree (M4) is the whole tree dataset, binding renames applied per node (:meth:~mapi_sdk.binding.BindingMap.apply_tree), for models whose capabilities declare input="tree" and were fitted from a tree dataset; None otherwise. ds is still the flat pipeline output (the nodes data.nodes selects, preprocessed).

tracker (v0.11) receives what the plugin logs with the :class:~mapi_sdk.tracking.TrackingMixin methods (log_metric, log_params, set_tag, log_line, chains); the harness attaches one that records the bundle's metrics_history group and forwards to the runner. None: validate only.

docs.title: Pipelines
docs.text:
The pipeline engine: stages, fitting, score-time replay and the inverse chain (plan §4.2).

A stage is the dataset after a named step (raw is the bound input before any step). :meth:Pipeline.fit fits and transforms a range of stages, recording each step's state and its per-group context tail at the step's input stage. :meth:Pipeline.transform replays stored states over a range of stages, prepending each step's context before it runs (:mod:mapi_sdk.context). :meth:Pipeline.inverse_outputs maps model outputs back through invertible VALUE steps up to the last RESHAPE step and labels the output space.

docs.title: inverse_outputs
docs.text:
inverse_outputs(
    ds: Dataset,
    states: Mapping[str, StepState],
    var_sources: Mapping[str, str],
    *,
    to_stage: str | None = None,
    from_stage: str | None = None,
    representation: Representation = DRAWS,
    retransform: Retransform = "median",
    residuals: Mapping[str, DataArray] | None = None,
    side_tables: Mapping[str, Dataset] | None = None,
    decompositions: Collection[str] = (),
) -> InverseResult

Map output variables back to their output space.

var_sources maps each output variable to the input variable whose transforms it inherits (y_hat -> y). Inversion stops at to_stage (default: the last RESHAPE stage) or at the first non-invertible step that touched the variable. Point outputs through a non-linear inverse are labelled median (plain inverse) or use Duan's smearing over stored model-space residuals; moments use the first-order delta method (g(mu), |g'(mu)| sd with a central difference).

decompositions name additive decompositions (contributions(component, ...)). They are inverted component by component only through additive steps (Step.additive); through any other inverse (expm1, x * sd + mean) the components would no longer sum to the inverted prediction, so inversion stops right after that step and :attr:InverseResult.kept says why.

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text:
Fitted-model bundles: one bundle.zarr.zip DataTree plus JSON sidecars (plan §8.6).

Layout of bundle.zarr.zip::

/                       attrs: format, bundle_id, role
/spec                   attrs: spec (canonical JSON), resolved (ResolvedSpec JSON)
/schema/raw             attrs: json (dataset-named raw DataSchema)
/schema/model           attrs: json (model input schema, effective policies)
/binding                attrs: json
/preprocess/<step_id>   attrs: state (JSON); children: arrays, context
/model                  attrs: manifest, settings, fit_config, learned (JSON)
/model/<group>          ArviZ-named groups (posterior, sample_stats, log_likelihood ...)
/terminal_state         plugin-owned state for sequential models
/native                 uint8 arrays of safe native artifacts (skops, xgb json, ...)
/derived/<name>         derived quantities cached at fit
/fit_coords/<stage>     coordinates of the fitted data at every stage
/side_tables/<name>     pinned side tables used at fit
/residuals              model-space residuals (point models, smearing)
/thin                   the bundle-wide draw thinning index

Sidecars: manifest.json (content hashes of every file: size, CRC32C and MD5 in the GCS base64 form, SHA-256), diagnostics.json, plots.json and metrics.json. An evaluate_then_refit bundle keeps its train-only evaluation bundle under evaluation/. Pickle is never written and is rejected on read.

docs.text:
CoordPlan checks, coordinate canonicalisation and horizon coordinates (plan §4.2-4.3).

  • :class:CoordPlan runs the static checks of :func:mapi_spec.validate.validate_score_request against the bundle's fit coordinates and the actual score payload, raising typed errors (UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, ...).
  • :func:canonicalise_coords reorders model-stage score data to the fit order, pads requested subsets to the full fit set, appends unseen levels (flagged by <dim>__is_new) and returns a :class:CanonicalPlan that selects the requested coords back afterwards.

  • fixed dims: labels must be fit labels (UNSEEN_LEVELS); data is reindexed to the full fit set (padding unrequested labels);
  • new_levels dims: fit labels in fit order, then unseen labels appended (the <dim>__is_new coordinate flags them; strategy error raises);
  • extend dims: labels may not start before the fit range (COORD_NOT_ALLOWED), must continue it without gaps (NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION) and may not exceed max_extension (HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT); with pad_extend the full fit range is included so positional models see a contiguous axis.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
Representation-aware summaries, aggregation and draw thinning (plan §5).

Outputs come in one of five representations (see :mod:mapi_sdk.models). Which summaries and aggregations are valid depends on the representation; the rules live in :data:mapi_spec.capabilities.REPRESENTATION_RULES and are enforced here:

  • draws: every summary; any aggregation (applied per draw);
  • quantiles: median/quantiles/ETI (interpolated on the stored quantile grid, never extrapolated); no aggregation;
  • interval: the interval and its point; no aggregation;
  • point: mean/point; linear aggregation only, flagged;
  • moments: mean/sd and normal ETIs; no aggregation.

Summaries are returned as one variable per output with a leading stat dim whose labels read like mean, hdi_90_lower, hdi_90_upper, q5 ... HDIs are computed in numpy (narrowest window over sorted draws).

Circular outputs (OutputDecl.circular, periods of :func:summarise): angles that wrap at period (one turn). Draw summaries are then taken on the circle: mean is the circular mean, sd the circular standard deviation sqrt(-2 ln R), and the median, quantiles, ETIs and HDIs come from the draws' wrapped deviations from the circular mean, so an interval is centred on the mean and may cross the seam. Every value is wrapped into [0, period) ([-period/2, period/2) for a difference, signed); an interval with lower > upper crosses the seam. This matches the evaluate metrics of :mod:mapi_sdk.metrics.

docs.title: In-process executor
docs.text:
In-process executor (isolation NONE) for notebooks, tests and mapi fit on own code.

Implements the :class:mapi_spec.executor.Executor protocol: submit starts the run in a worker thread, status is the source of truth, cancel is cooperative (checked between pipeline phases) and event_source yields :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent objects. Payloads are JSON only; dataset references are resolved by a resolver.

Supported run kinds: fit (payload spec, data, optional side_tables and raw_schema) and score/evaluate (payload request, bundle - a bundle directory or a key registered with :meth:InprocExecutor.put_bundle - and optional data/scenario/side_tables; otherwise the request's data/scenario refs are used). A counterfactual resolves data as the baseline and scenario as the scenario.

What the model logs through the tracking API (v0.11) is emitted as metrics, params and tags events (I-2 payload dicts; metric points batched per second) and log events with stream user.

Never use this executor for untrusted code: it runs plugins in the caller's process.

docs.title: Wire formats
docs.text:
Wire formats: XrJSON, single-object zarr v3 zips, DataTree zips, stacking and Arrow IPC.

Encoding rules (plan §3.2), applied by every writer here:

  • any pandas.MultiIndex is reset before persisting (and recorded so readers restore it);
  • string coords and variables are zarr v3 vlen-utf8 (data type string);
  • datetimes are int64 nanoseconds with explicit units and calendar attrs;
  • only the zstd and blosc compressors are written or accepted;
  • :func:stack_rows drops empty rows and records a row mask so :func:unstack_rows restores them.

Pickle (and joblib/cloudpickle) is never used for anything. Readers treat every payload as hostile: zip entries, zarr metadata, codecs, dtypes and sizes are checked before any array is decoded.

docs.title: stack_rows
docs.text:
stack_rows(
    ds: Dataset,
    dims: Sequence[str],
    new_dim: str = "row",
    *,
    drop: Literal["all", "any", "none"] = "all",
    mask_var: str | None = None,
) -> Dataset

Stack dims into one new_dim and drop empty rows, recording a row mask.

A row is dropped when all (drop="all") or any ("any") of the variables that use every stacked dim are missing there (lower-rank variables, which are broadcast, only decide when no variable is full-rank), or where mask_var is false. The result has no MultiIndex: the component coords are plain coords along new_dim and the boolean <new_dim>__rowmask variable (over the original dims, with their full coords) says which rows were kept, so :func:unstack_rows can restore the dropped rows as missing.

docs.text:
Contract-kit checks for step and model authors (plan §13).

:func:check_step and :func:check_model run every contract check that is possible without a sandbox and return a :class:ContractReport (raising :class:ContractViolation by default when any check fails). Each check is independent: one failure never hides the others.

M3.5: both also check the item's plain-language About card (about): an incomplete card always fails; a missing one fails with require_about=True (what the catalog requires) and is skipped otherwise. :func:check_about checks cards on their own.

docs.title: check_model
docs.text:
check_model(
    plugin: type[Any],
    fixture: ModelFixture,
    *,
    raise_on_failure: bool = True,
    checks: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    require_about: bool = False,
    collection: Collection | None = None,
) -> ContractReport

Run the model contract checks: fit, bundle round trip, coordinate handling, typed errors for every dim policy (unseen levels; gaps and out-of-range coords on datetime and integer extend dims; horizons past max_extension; forecasts missing a future-required covariate; horizons longer than a target lag), forecasts with actuals (refused without conditions_on_actuals; with it, the fitted values as actuals reproduce the plain forecast and a new actual moves it), unsupported modes, context-window equivalence, evaluate path == score path, output space, aggregation legality, additive contributions, no pickle, seed determinism, fast scoring == exact scoring within MCSE (via the plugin's check_fast_score hook) and that the manifest's plots sanitize.

collection (v0.15): for a model that declares input="collection", the batch path runs once - fit_batches on the collection with the fixture spec, then score_batches on a few images - and must give the outputs the dataset path gives (same variables and dims), only for the requested images.

docs.title: mapi_sklearn
docs.text: This package is for scikit-learn and xgboost models. You write estimator(). The package gives stacking, safe persistence and uncertainty.

docs.title: Base classes
docs.text:
SklearnModel: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators on labelled data (plan §5).

A plugin author implements only :meth:SklearnModel.estimator, returning an allow-listed estimator (a choice from :data:~mapi_sklearn.estimators.ESTIMATORS, a {kind, params} mapping, or an instance of an allow-listed class). The platform:

  1. stacks the rows dims of the model-stage dataset into samples and builds the design matrix from the selected variables and coordinate features (:mod:mapi_sklearn.design), dropping incomplete rows through the SDK row mask;
  2. fits one or more estimators for the plugin's uncertainty kind;
  3. persists them with skops or xgboost JSON (never pickle);
  4. at score time rebuilds the same columns, handles unseen levels (:mod:mapi_sklearn.levels), predicts and unstacks back to labelled arrays in the plugin's representation:

================= ===================== ========================================== base class representation predictions group ================= ===================== ========================================== SklearnModel point y_hat(*rows) (+ contributions) SklearnQuantile quantiles y_hat(quantile, *rows) SklearnBootstrap draws y_hat(chain, draw, *rows) SklearnConformal interval y_hat(bound=[lower, upper, point], *rows) SklearnClassifier point y_hat(*rows) = P(target == positive) SklearnMulticlass point y_hat(*rows, class) = P(target == class) ================= ===================== ==========================================

Forecasting is direct only: future features must be supplied (or produced by the pipeline from coordinates); forecast_strategy: recursive raises RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED.

docs.title: SklearnQuantileModel
docs.text:
SklearnQuantileModel()

Bases: SklearnModel[SettingsT]

Conditional quantiles (representation quantiles).

xgboost fits one native multi-quantile model (reg:quantileerror); quantile-capable sklearn estimators (QuantileRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor, HistGradientBoostingRegressor) fit one model per level.

docs.title: SklearnBootstrapModel
docs.text:
SklearnBootstrapModel()

Bases: SklearnModel[SettingsT]

Bootstrap ensemble (representation draws: chain=1, one draw per replicate).

expected outputs are the replicate predictions (uncertainty of the fitted mean); predictive outputs add an out-of-bag residual drawn per cell, approximating the predictive distribution. Draws are joint across cells, so every aggregation is valid.

docs.title: SklearnConformalModel
docs.text:
SklearnConformalModel()

Bases: SklearnModel[SettingsT]

Split-conformal prediction intervals (representation interval, never draws).

y_hat(bound=[lower, upper, point], ...) with attribute alpha: each interval covers the observed value with probability at least 1 - alpha for data exchangeable with the calibration rows. Intervals have per-cell coverage only and cannot be summed.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings of the scikit-learn / xgboost model plugins.

A spec's model.settings for sklearn.* plugins looks like::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}
rows: [store, sku, time]               # dims stacked into samples
time_dim: time                         # the row dim that extends at forecast time
columns: {roles: [covariate]}          # which variables become feature columns
coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
uncertainty: {kind: quantile, quantiles: [0.05, 0.5, 0.95]}
forecast_strategy: direct
retransform: median

The uncertainty kind fixes the output representation, so each kind is its own plugin (sklearn.tabular_quantiles accepts only kind: quantile and so on).

docs.title: Estimator registry
docs.text:
The allow-listed estimator registry.

Plugins never import arbitrary classes. An estimator is chosen by kind from :data:ESTIMATORS, and its hyper-parameters are validated by that kind's Pydantic params model (extra="forbid", bounded values). The platform then builds the estimator with every parameter passed explicitly, so behaviour does not drift when a library changes a default. Parameters the platform owns (seeds, threads, categorical handling and the loss/objective an uncertainty kind needs) are not part of the params models.

In a spec::

estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 600, max_depth: 6}}

LightGBM and CatBoost (v0.14) are an optional extra (mapi-sklearn[gbm]) and are imported only when an estimator of theirs is built or loaded; without them those kinds raise SETTINGS_INVALID.

EstimatorEntry(
    kind: str,
    module: str,
    name: str,
    params: type[Params],
    choice: type[_Choice],
    task: Task,
    persistence: Literal[
        "skops", "xgboost", "lightgbm", "catboost"
    ] = "skops",
    linear: bool = False,
    native_nan: bool = False,
    native_categorical: Literal["xgboost", "sklearn_hist"]
    | None = None,
    quantile: QuantileMode | None = None,
    quantile_setter: Callable[
        [dict[str, Any], float], dict[str, Any]

    | None = None,
    loss_param: str | None = None,
    quantile_loss: str | None = None,
    seed_param: str | None = "random_state",
    n_jobs_param: str | None = None,

    fixed: Mapping[str, Any] = dict(),
    description: str = "",
)

Static facts about one allow-listed estimator.

linear estimators expose coef_/intercept_ (exact additive contributions); native_nan ones accept missing feature values; native_categorical says how integer-coded categorical columns are declared (xgboost feature types or the categorical_features of sklearn's histogram boosting). quantile says how a quantile model is built: one native multi-quantile model, or one model per level with quantile_setter. loss_param/loss_default/quantile_loss name the loss or objective the quantile mode manages. trusted lists the extra types skops may load. fixed holds platform-owned constructor arguments (quiet logging, no files written).

The built-in sklearn.* model plugins (registered through the mapi.models entry point).

Each plugin takes its estimator from settings.estimator; the uncertainty kind, and so the output representation, is fixed by the plugin:

========================== ============= ================================================== plugin representation uncertainty ========================== ============= ================================================== sklearn.tabular_regressor point none (contributions, retransform) sklearn.tabular_quantiles quantiles {kind: quantile, quantiles: [...]} sklearn.tabular_bootstrap draws {kind: bootstrap, n: 50, by: store} sklearn.tabular_conformal interval {kind: conformal, alpha: 0.1, calibration: 0.2} sklearn.tabular_classifier point binary class probability sklearn.multiclass_classifier point one probability per class (y_hat(..., class)) ========================== ============= ==================================================

docs.text: This package has contracts that use only Pydantic. It does not use numpy, xarray or pandas, because the control plane depends on this package.

docs.title: Data schema
docs.text:
Data contract primitives: dims, variables, ragged structure and dataset schemas.

A :class:DataSchema describes an xr.Dataset without any arrays: its dims (each with a :class:DimPolicy saying what may happen to it at score time), its variables (with a :class:Role, dtype, units and missingness) and its ragged structure.

A :class:DataSchemaTemplate is a static JSON function of enumerated settings: plugins export one per model so the control plane can compute the required input schema for given settings without running plugin code.

docs.title: DataBlock
docs.text:

The dataset, side tables, binding to canonical names and the split.

For a tree dataset (M4), nodes picks the nodes whose variables are merged into the ONE flat dataset the pipeline sees (:meth:mapi_spec.tree.TreeSchema.flat), aligned per join. Without nodes a tree dataset's root node is read (when it has variables). nodes on a plain dataset is an error. The binding applies to the merged names.

docs.title: Loading and hashing
docs.text:
Strict YAML 1.2 / JSON loading, apiVersion upgrades, canonical JSON and spec hashing.

The loader is safe for hostile input:

  • size ≤ 256 KB, nesting depth ≤ 32, ≤ 10 000 nodes (all configurable via :class:Limits);
  • YAML anchors, aliases, explicit tags (!foo, !!python/...), %TAG directives and multiple documents are rejected;
  • plain scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema (yes/on/0777/dates stay strings), NaN/Infinity are rejected, duplicate keys are rejected and every mapping key must be a string;
  • JSON input is parsed with the same limits.

:func:load_document returns a typed document (discriminated on kind) after running the apiVersion upgrade chain (the API accepts N and N-1). :func:canonical_json and :func:spec_hash give a normalised, deterministic serialisation for immutable revisions.

The :class:Representation of a model's output decides which aggregations and summaries are statistically valid. docs.title: Schema effects and stages
docs.text:
Step kinds, SchemaEffects, context needs and static schema propagation.

A :class:SchemaEffect is a data-free description of how a preprocessing step changes a :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DataSchema. Step authors export it as JSON (per image digest); the control plane evaluates it with :func:propagate and never imports step code.

Effects may be templates: strings can reference the step's settings with the :mod:~mapi_spec.template placeholder syntax ("{dim}", "{*vars as v}"). Every referenced setting must be listed in template_params. :func:resolve_effect renders a template with concrete settings into a plain :class:SchemaEffect.

Within one effect, operations apply in this order: renames → drops → transforms_dims → stacks → unstacks → updates → derives → adds.

docs.title: Static validation
docs.text:
Static (JSON-only) validation of ModelSpecs and ScoreRequests.

:func:validate_spec checks a :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ModelSpec against a :class:~mapi_spec.catalog.Catalog and the dataset's raw :class:DataSchema:

  1. binding references exist and do not collide;
  2. every use: resolves to a non-yanked version (semver range);
  3. step and model settings validate against their JSON Schemas;
  4. side-table references exist;
  5. the schema is propagated through every step's SchemaEffect, with per-step input checks;
  6. the split stage is resolved (default: end of the stateless prefix), its dims exist there, and LEAKAGE_RISK is raised if a stateful step precedes it;
  7. the model's schema template is resolved and compared with the final stage; spec dim policies may only tighten the plugin's;
  8. recursive forecasting (a target-dependent lag feeding a longer holdout) is rejected unless the model owns recursion; outputs, plots, metrics and resource class are checked;
  9. (v0.15) the model's side tables exist; an image collection dataset takes no pipeline steps for a model that trains on batches and only row splits; GPU class and epoch checkpoints match the model.

:func:validate_score_request runs the static CoordPlan checks for a ScoreRequest from metadata only (resolved spec + fit coordinate summaries + dim policies).

Every finding is an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer into the document.

validate_spec(
    spec: ModelSpec,
    catalog: Catalog,
    raw_schema: DataSchema,
    *,
    tree_schema: TreeSchema | None = None,
    dataset_layout: DataLayout = "dataset",
    side_table_layouts: Mapping[str, DataLayout]
    | None = None,

Statically validate spec against catalog and the dataset's raw_schema.

For a tree dataset (M4) pass its tree_schema too (raw_schema is then its root node's schema and is not used): the pipeline input is resolved from data.nodes by :func:resolve_input_schema. For an image collection (v0.15) pass dataset_layout="collection" (raw_schema is the collection's schema, with the virtual pixels variable); side_table_layouts (name → layout) lets the check refuse side tables that are collections.

docs.title: validate_score_request
docs.text:
validate_score_request(
    req: ScoreRequest,
    meta: ScoreMetadata,
    inputs: DataSummary | None = None,
    *,
    max_draws: int | None = None,
    live_capabilities: Capabilities | None = None,
) -> list[Issue]

Static CoordPlan checks for req against a fitted model's metadata.

inputs summarises the payload (data or scenario) as it enters at req.inputs_stage; dataset names are mapped through the binding at every stage, as the runtime does. When it says where the targets hold values (inputs.observed), a forecast's actuals are checked (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals). live_capabilities are those of the plugin build that will score, which may have gained score-time features (conditions_on_actuals) since the fit; the fitted ones are used otherwise.

docs.text:
mapi_spec.run exports the executor shapes again with no changes.

Executor protocol shapes (plan §8.4), shared by the control plane and the runtimes.

The control plane drives every backend (in-process, local process, docker, Cloud Run Jobs, ...) through one :class:Executor protocol. Identifiers travel in the environment only; the executor's status API is the liveness source of truth and events are advisory progress. These are pure Pydantic shapes: no numpy, xarray or plugin code.

docs.title: Run protocol
docs.text:
For the full description, read Run protocol.

The run protocol (plan §8.1, §8.3–§8.7): state machine, bootstrap, events, manifests.

Everything a control plane, an executor and a runner must agree on lives here, as pure Pydantic / stdlib code:

  • :class:RunState, :class:RunTrigger and the transition table :data:TRANSITIONS, with the pure function :func:transition used by the API, dispatcher, events service, reconciler, finalizer and tests;
  • :class:RunSpec — the bootstrap object written to bootstrap/<nonce> before an execution starts (signed URLs, a per-run HMAC key, limits, deadline);
  • :class:~mapi_spec.executor.RunEvent payload models, canonical HMAC-SHA256 signing and verification, and the stdout JSONL wire format ({"mapi_event": {...}} per line);
  • :class:OutputManifest (the runner's claim), metadata-only verification against server-computed hashes, and the platform-signed :class:BundleManifest;
  • the runner invocation contract: environment (:class:RunnerEnv) and exit codes (:class:RunnerExit).

Executor-facing shapes (:class:Isolation, :class:ExecutorCaps, :class:Handle, :class:ExecStatus, :class:RunKind, :class:RunEvent, ...) are defined in :mod:mapi_spec.executor and re-exported here unchanged, so both import paths name the same classes.

docs.title: Job payloads
docs.text:
See Job payloads and object names.

Run job payloads: what RunSpec.spec holds for each run kind, plus the input and output object names shared by the control plane (which writes RunSpecs and reads outputs) and the runner (which reads RunSpecs and writes outputs).

========== ============================================ ====================================== kind RunSpec.spec inputs (RunSpec.inputs names) ========== ============================================ ====================================== ingest :class:IngestJob (a bare IngestMapping upload (the raw file; dataset is also accepted) is accepted as a fallback); M4 assemblies: upload.<i> per source inspect :class:InspectJob (M4) upload; output inspection.json describe :class:DescribeJob none validate a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> fit a ModelSpec document dataset, optional schema, side.<name> score a ScoreRequest document, or bundle, optional :class:ScoreJob bundle.manifest, dataset (the request's data), scenario, side.<name>, history (M3: the fit dataset, for carry_last / seasonal_naive future covariates) evaluate :class:EvaluateJob bundle, dataset, ... derive :class:DeriveJob bundle, dataset, side.<name> render :class:RenderJob plots (a plots.json) translate_ :class:~mapi_spec.calibration.Prior- ``dataset``, optional ``schema``, priors TranslationJob (M3) side.<name>; output priors.json workflow_ :class:~mapi_spec.workflow.WorkflowNode- ``in.<port>.<k>`` (each bound input); node Job (M3.5) output node_result.json explore :class:~mapi_spec.explore.ExploreJob dataset (+ schema) or (M3.5) bundle, bundle.manifest, compare.<k>; output ui/explore/ optimize :class:~mapi_spec.optimize.OptimizeJob bundle, bundle.manifest; output (M3.5) optimize.json governance :class:~mapi_spec.governance.Governance- ``bundle``, ``bundle.manifest``, Job (M3.5) dataset, optional evaluation (+ evaluation.manifest); output governance.json ========== ============================================ ======================================

workflow runs are parents (the orchestrator walks the DAG) and never execute.

Datasets are single-object *.zarr.zip files (M4: a tree dataset is a data.tree.zip with a tree_schema.json; see :mod:mapi_spec.tree). A dataset's raw schema comes from the schema input, else the zarr root attribute mapi_schema (written by ingest), else it is inferred. bundle is the bundle.zarr.zip of a fit and bundle.manifest the SDK bundle manifest that the fit uploaded as bundle.manifest.json.

This module is pure Pydantic (no numpy/xarray): the control plane imports it.

docs.title: MffOptions
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

The MFF ("model feature format") long-table preset.

One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; VariableName values become data variables. The rest follows mmm-framework's MFF semantics (its MFFLoader), so both read a file the same way:

  • Geography and Product become dims when they hold more than one level. A blank label (or National, Total, All) is the coarser level: a variable given only there (national TV) is spread across the levels - equal weights, or the KPI's share of each level (allocation; mmm-framework's defaults: geographies equally, products by sales). A variable may not mix the two levels.
  • Campaign, Outlet and Creative are breakdowns: rows that differ only there are summed, unless the column is listed in split (then it becomes a dim).

combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

docs.title: Object storage
docs.text:
Object storage contracts (plan §8.6): metadata, the ObjectStore protocol, signed URLs, integrity hashes and the bucket/key naming scheme.

The control plane talks to object storage only through :class:ObjectStore. Two implementations exist outside this package: ShimObjectStore (the local GCS emulator in mapi_gcs_shim) and GcsObjectStore (google-cloud-storage). Both expose GCS semantics:

  • every write creates a new generation; if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist" (write-once);
  • the server computes CRC32C (base64 of the big-endian 4-byte value) and MD5 (base64 of the 16-byte digest) — uploader-supplied hashes are never evidence;
  • signed GET URLs are pinned to a generation and honour HTTP Range; signed PUT URLs and V4 POST policies (key prefix + content-length-range) are how sandboxes write, so the executor never holds storage credentials.

Object keys are always built server-side from validated IDs with the helpers at the bottom of this module (never from user-supplied paths).

docs.title: ObjectStore
docs.text:
Bases: Protocol

Async object-store driver used by the control plane (GCS semantics).

Conventions shared by every method:

  • generation pins the source generation to read (None = live generation);
  • if_generation_match is a precondition on the target: 0 means "must not exist", n means "live generation must be n"; a failed precondition raises :class:PreconditionFailed;
  • missing buckets/objects raise :class:NotFound; denied operations raise :class:AccessDenied.

A generation-pinned signed GET URL plus the server-computed facts about its object.

The URL honours HTTP Range, so zarr zip readers can range-read one object. A reader verifies size/crc32c after a full download (corruption check only — integrity is enforced by the control plane).

docs.title: SignedPut
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A signed PUT URL for exactly one object name.

headers must be sent verbatim (they are part of the signature): typically content-type, x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 (write-once) and x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max_bytes>.

docs.title: PostPolicy
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A V4 POST policy: multipart form uploads of any key under prefix.

The uploader posts multipart/form-data to url with every entry of fields, then key (which must start with prefix), then the file part last. The storage service rejects bodies outside content_length_range and keys outside the prefix.

A create_only policy cannot replace an existing object (its signed conditions carry x-goog-if-generation-match: 0), so the holder can neither overwrite the write-once manifest nor swap an output after it was written.

docs.title: REST DTOs
docs.text:
For the endpoint tables and the conventions, read HTTP API (v1). Also read the multi-tenant additions of v0.3.

REST DTOs for the HTTP API (/v1; plan §8.2): M1 (v0.2), M2 (v0.3) and the M3 (v0.4) contracts.

Conventions shared by every endpoint (see docs/reference/http-api.md):

  • Requests reject unknown fields (extra="forbid"); responses ignore unknown fields when parsed by a client, so older clients keep working when the server adds fields.
  • Every resource carries tenant_id and project_id. M1 is single-tenant: both are :data:DEFAULT_TENANT_ID / :data:DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID, but the identity is in every row and key so M2 can add row-level security without migrations churn.
  • Lists return :class:Page (items + opaque next_cursor); errors are RFC 7807 :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Problem documents with stable codes.
  • Timestamps are timezone-aware RFC 3339 strings in UTC.

:data:M1_ENDPOINTS, :data:M2_ENDPOINTS (v0.3), :data:M3_ENDPOINTS (guided mode and integrations, v0.4), :data:M35_ENDPOINTS (workflows, governance, explorers, optimisation and About cards, v0.5), :data:M4_ENDPOINTS (tree datasets) and :data:V011_ENDPOINTS (run tracking, v0.11) and :data:V014_ENDPOINTS (media, run comparison, experiments and saved views, v0.14) and :data:V015_ENDPOINTS (resumable uploads and image collections, v0.15) are the machine-readable endpoint tables; :data:ENDPOINTS (= :data:ALL_ENDPOINTS) is all of them. The server's route table and the reference docs are tested against them. :data:ROUTE_ACCESS gives every operation its tenant/project scope and the permission it checks. From v0.3 every M1 resource is project-scoped: the project comes from the path or the X-Mapi-Project header (:func:mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope).

Acting on other principals' tokens (list_tokens?all=true, revoking someone else's token) additionally needs manage on token. A create_run for a model version (score, evaluate, derive, render) additionally needs run on model. A promote_endpoint with override=true additionally needs manage on endpoint, which no token scope grants (a signed-in admin decides, audited with the reason).
