docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Every mapi command with its --help, generated from the installed CLI by scripts/gen_docs_reference.py. The command-line guide shows them in use. Global options (--url, --token, --profile, --json) go before the command: mapi --json runs ls.

Command What it does mapi new Scaffold a ModelSpec YAML from a template (geo-mmm, forecast, tabular, glm). mapi check Statically validate a spec (exit status 1 when it has errors). mapi fit Fit a spec locally (in-process) or on the API (--remote). mapi score Score a fitted bundle locally, or a model version on the API (--remote). mapi catalog Show the catalog of the locally installed plugins (or the API's with --remote). mapi login Sign in to the API (browser OIDC, device code, or an API token). mapi logout Forget the stored sign-in and API token of the profile. mapi whoami Who you are, how you are signed in, and the projects you can use. mapi use Select the project commands act in (sent as X-Mapi-Project), or show it. mapi usage Cost and quota use of the selected project (or --tenant) for a UTC day or month. mapi signup Create a workspace: sends a verification e-mail (valid 24 hours). mapi verify-email Redeem a verification token: creates your workspace and its default project. mapi serve Start the local development stack (API, embedded Postgres, GCS shim). mapi approve Approve (or --reject) a validated model version as a reviewer. mapi optimize Split a marketing budget across channels with a fitted marketing-mix model. mapi choose Help me choose: a few questions about your goal and data, then the best fits. mapi about The About card of anything a user can pick: what it does in plain words, when to use it and when not, what it needs, assumes and gives. mapi runs Inspect and control runs on the API. mapi runs ls List runs, newest first. Use filters to find runs by metric, param, tag or name. mapi runs get Show one run (state, failure, cost, problem). mapi runs logs Print captured log lines (untrusted text, control characters stripped). mapi runs watch Follow a run's live events until it ends (--json: one JSON event per line). mapi runs cancel Request cancellation (idempotent). mapi runs retry Start a new run from a failed one (e.g. one resource class up). mapi runs metrics Show the metrics of a run: one row for each series, or the points of one metric. mapi runs params Show the params of a run. mapi runs log-metric Add a metric point to a run. You can also do this after the run ends. mapi runs log-param Add a param to a run. A param cannot change after you set it. mapi runs tag Set or remove tags of a run. mapi runs rename Set the name of a run. mapi runs note Set the note of a run. An empty note removes the note. mapi runs media Show the images and tables that a run logged. You can also download them. mapi runs log-image Add an image to a run. You can also do this after the run ends. mapi runs compare Compare runs: a table of metric values, then the params that are different. mapi runs views Save, list and delete run views (a saved search of the runs table). mapi runs views ls List the saved run views of the project. mapi runs views save Save a search of the runs table as a view. A view with the same name is replaced. mapi runs views rm Delete a saved run view. The runs do not change. mapi experiments Make and change experiments (named groups of runs). mapi experiments ls List the experiments of the project, newest first. mapi experiments create Make an experiment. mapi experiments show Show one experiment. mapi experiments rename Change the name of an experiment. mapi experiments archive Archive an experiment. An archived experiment does not accept new runs. mapi experiments unarchive Make an archived experiment active again. mapi experiments rm Delete an experiment. Its runs stay, without an experiment. Its saved views are deleted. mapi experiments add Add runs to an experiment. A run moves out of its previous experiment. mapi experiments remove Remove runs from an experiment. The runs stay, without an experiment. mapi datasets Datasets on the API. mapi datasets ls List datasets. mapi datasets upload Upload one or more files as a new dataset version (signed PUT + sandboxed ingest run). mapi datasets ingest Ingest an already uploaded file as a new dataset version, e.g. a raw HDF5 file after 'mapi datasets inspect' showed which arrays to map. mapi datasets inspect List the groups and arrays of an upload (path, shape, dtype, dims hint) without ingesting it - what a raw-HDF5 mapping needs. A local file is uploaded first; ingest it later with 'mapi datasets ingest DATASET UPLOAD_ID --mapping FILE'. mapi datasets upload-images Upload a folder of images as a new image collection version. mapi datasets missing-images Show how many images of a folder the dataset does not have yet (nothing is uploaded). mapi datasets upload-weights Upload pretrained network weights (a .safetensors file) as a new dataset version. A model reads the version as a side table. mapi plugin Plugin authoring: scaffold and test model plugins. mapi plugin init Scaffold a plugin package (model, entry point and contract-kit tests). mapi plugin test Run the plugin's tests (contract kit) with this interpreter; extra args go to pytest. mapi spec Spec document tools. mapi spec upgrade Upgrade a document through the registered converters (N-1 → N). mapi config Client configuration (~/.config/mapi/config.toml). mapi config show Resolved settings and where each came from (secrets are never shown). mapi config path Print the config file location. mapi config set Set a key of the profile (--profile, MAPI_PROFILE, else the default profile). mapi config unset Remove a key from the profile (token too: prefer mapi logout). mapi tokens API tokens of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation). mapi tokens ls List tokens (yours, or everyone's with --all). mapi tokens get Show one token (never its secret). mapi tokens create Mint a token in the selected project. Its secret is shown once. mapi tokens revoke Revoke a token: programs using it stop working at once. mapi admin Platform operator commands: tenants, quotas, kill switches, executors, audit. mapi admin audit The platform audit log, newest first (times in UTC). mapi admin tenants All tenants (create, change tier/status/residency). mapi admin tenants ls List all tenants. mapi admin tenants get Show one tenant. mapi admin tenants create Create a tenant. mapi admin tenants update Change a tenant's name, trust tier, status or data residency. mapi admin quotas Quota policies per token, tenant or the platform. mapi admin quotas ls List quota policies. mapi admin quotas set Create or REPLACE the policy of (scope, subject): limits left out are removed. mapi admin quotas rm Remove a policy (the tier default applies again). mapi admin kill-switches Platform-wide emergency controls (audited). mapi admin kill-switches get Show the kill switches. mapi admin kill-switches set Flip kill switches (confirmation shows the change; the server audits it). mapi admin executors Executor health, capacity and conformance. mapi admin executors ls Executor health, load and conformance. mapi admin executors get One executor. mapi admin executors disable Disable an executor: no new run is placed on it (incident containment). mapi admin executors enable Enable an executor again. mapi endpoints Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (promote, score, snippets). mapi endpoints ls List the project's endpoints. mapi endpoints get Show an endpoint, the version it serves and its promotion gate. mapi endpoints history Promotions and rollbacks, newest first. mapi endpoints promote Point an alias at a model version, through the scorecard promotion gate. mapi endpoints rollback Point the alias back at an earlier revision's version. mapi endpoints schema What to send: the input schema frozen at promotion and an example payload. mapi endpoints score Score the endpoint's current version and wait for the result. mapi endpoints forecast Forecast with your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (no refit). mapi endpoints snippets Ready-to-run code that scores the endpoint (reads the token from MAPI_TOKEN). mapi webhooks Webhooks of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation). mapi webhooks ls List webhooks (never their secrets). mapi webhooks get Show one webhook (never its secret). mapi webhooks create Add a webhook. Its signing secret is printed once. mapi webhooks update Change a webhook: switch it back on after it was paused or disabled automatically, or change its events, URL or description. The secret is unchanged. mapi webhooks rotate New signing secret (printed once); the current one keeps signing for 24 hours. mapi webhooks deliveries The delivery log, newest first. mapi webhooks replay Send a delivery's event again (a new delivery). mapi webhooks rm Delete a webhook and its delivery log. mapi plots Render plots to files and share them as embed links. mapi plots render Render one plot to a PNG, SVG or PDF file. mapi plots embed Create a read-only embed link for a saved plot. Its URL is printed once. mapi plots embeds List a saved plot's embed links (redacted). mapi plots revoke Revoke an embed link: dashboards showing it stop at once. mapi guided Guided mode: templates, column detection and drafts (stores nothing). mapi guided templates List the guided templates, or one template's questions. mapi guided detect Suggest which column answers each question of a template. mapi guided draft Answers -> the ingest mapping and the ModelSpec YAML (nothing is stored). mapi priors Business priors: translate beliefs into model priors. mapi priors preview Translate beliefs into priors in the sandbox and preview them. mapi tenant Your workspace (tenant): verification status, GDPR export and deletion. mapi tenant status Verification (e-mail, identity, code upload) and any deletion of the tenant. mapi tenant export GDPR export: everything the tenant stored, as one zip archive. mapi tenant delete Schedule deletion of the whole tenant (cancellable during the grace period). mapi workflows Workflows: validate, save, run and watch DAGs of tests, transforms and models. mapi workflows validate Check a workflow file on the server (nothing is saved): unknown nodes, parameters, ports, conditions and cycles, each with a JSON pointer. mapi workflows apply Create the workflow named in the file, or save the file as its next revision (an unchanged file adds nothing). mapi workflows create Create a workflow from a file or a gallery template (revision 1). mapi workflows ls List the project's workflows. mapi workflows get Show a workflow (and with --yaml its document at the latest or a given revision). mapi workflows revisions Revisions, newest first, and whether each can run. mapi workflows archive Archive a workflow (it can no longer run) or bring it back with --undo. mapi workflows rm Delete a workflow with its runs, schedules and triggers. mapi workflows templates The gallery of ready-made workflows, each in plain words. mapi workflows template One template's About card and its nodes. mapi workflows init Write a gallery template as a YAML file to edit, validate and apply. mapi workflows run Start a run (inputs are pinned to exact versions when it starts). mapi workflows watch Follow a run live: every node's status, branch decisions, then the summary (--json: one JSON event per line). mapi workflows status A run's status, nodes, decisions and outputs. mapi workflows runs Runs of a workflow, newest first. mapi workflows nodes The nodes of a run with what each found. mapi workflows node One node in full: resolved parameters, result, outputs and child runs. mapi workflows output Download a node output's file (a derived dataset, a fitted bundle), verified. mapi workflows cancel Cancel a run and its running children. mapi workflows nodes-catalog The node implementations a workflow can use, in plain words. mapi workflows schedules Cron schedules of a workflow. mapi workflows schedules ls A workflow's schedules. mapi workflows schedules add Run the workflow on a schedule (at most every 15 minutes). mapi workflows schedules pause Pause a schedule. mapi workflows schedules resume Resume a paused schedule. mapi workflows schedules rm Delete a schedule. mapi workflows triggers Run a workflow when a dataset gets a new version. mapi workflows triggers ls A workflow's dataset triggers. mapi workflows triggers add Run the workflow whenever the dataset gets a new version. mapi workflows triggers rm Delete a trigger. mapi governance Governance: the check catalog and the policies models must pass. mapi governance checks The checks a policy can require, in plain words. mapi governance policies Project and tenant-wide governance policies. mapi governance policies ls Policies in force in the project (tenant-wide first), or a tenant's. mapi governance policies get A policy's latest version with every check and threshold. mapi governance policies create Add a policy from a file (name, applies_to, checks, require_approval, ...). mapi governance policies update Save the file as the policy's next version. mapi governance policies retire Retire a policy (its versions stay for audit). mapi governance policies versions Every version of a project policy, newest first. mapi validate Validate a model version against the governance policies (or a workflow file). mapi validate model Run the governance checks on a model version and show every result. mapi validate workflow Check a workflow file on the server (same as mapi workflows validate). mapi validations Validations: the review queue, evidence, resubmission, deprecation, evidence packs. mapi validations ls Validations of the project, most recently changed first. mapi validations get A validation: status, every result, approvals and history. mapi validations evidence Every check result with its evidence (numbers, tables). mapi validations cancel Stop running checks (back to draft). mapi validations resubmit Run the checks again after a failure or a rejection. mapi validations deprecate Retire a validated model version (audited with the reason). mapi validations pack Export the evidence pack for an auditor (self-contained HTML, or JSON). mapi explore Explore a dataset or a model (sections computed in the sandbox), compare models. mapi explore dataset Explore a dataset version: profile, distributions, time plots, missingness, outliers, correlations, cross-correlation with the KPI, ACF/PACF, stationarity, STL, VIF, group comparisons and data-quality warnings. mapi explore model Explore a model version: parameters, diagnostics, fit vs actual, residual tests, decomposition, response curves, IRF/FEVD, forecasts, backtests and comparisons. mapi explore compare Compare model versions on their shared holdout: metrics, ranking and pairwise Diebold-Mariano tests (is the difference more than luck?). mapi explore get An exploration's sections (and with --out its views).

docs.title: mapi
docs.text:
Usage: mapi [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  The modeling-api command line.

  Local commands (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec) need no server. Remote commands
  (runs, datasets, tokens, usage, admin, endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors, tenant,
  signup, workflows, governance, validate, validations, approve, explore, optimize, choose,
  about, --remote) use the API from --url, MAPI_URL or a profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml,
  signed in with `mapi login` (or --token / MAPI_TOKEN), in the project chosen with `mapi use`
  (or --project / MAPI_PROJECT). --json prints machine-readable output on stdout.

Options:
  --url <str>           API base URL (default: MAPI_URL, profile, local)
  --token <str>         Bearer token (default: MAPI_TOKEN, profile)
  --profile <str>       Config profile (default: MAPI_PROFILE)
  --project <str>       <tenant>/<project> to act in (default: MAPI_PROJECT, mapi use)
  --json                Machine-readable JSON on stdout
  --version             Show the version
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the
                        installation.
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  new           Scaffold a ModelSpec YAML from a template (geo-mmm, forecast, tabular, glm).
  check         Statically validate a spec (exit status 1 when it has errors).
  fit           Fit a spec locally (in-process) or on the API (--remote).
  score         Score a fitted bundle locally, or a model version on the API (--remote).
  catalog       Show the catalog of the locally installed plugins (or the API's with...
  login         Sign in to the API (browser OIDC, device code, or an API token).
  logout        Forget the stored sign-in and API token of the profile.
  whoami        Who you are, how you are signed in, and the projects you can use.
  use           Select the project commands act in (sent as X-Mapi-Project), or show it.
  usage         Cost and quota use of the selected project (or --tenant) for a UTC day or...
  signup        Create a workspace: sends a verification e-mail (valid 24 hours).
  verify-email  Redeem a verification token: creates your workspace and its default project.
  serve         Start the local development stack (API, embedded Postgres, GCS shim).
  approve       Approve (or --reject) a validated model version as a reviewer.
  optimize      Split a marketing budget across channels with a fitted marketing-mix model.
  choose        Help me choose: a few questions about your goal and data, then the best fits.
  about         The About card of anything a user can pick: what it does in plain words,...
  runs          Inspect and control runs on the API.
  experiments   Make and change experiments (named groups of runs).
  datasets      Datasets on the API.
  plugin        Plugin authoring: scaffold and test model plugins.
  spec          Spec document tools.
  config        Client configuration (~/.config/mapi/config.toml).
  tokens        API tokens of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation).
  admin         Platform operator commands: tenants, quotas, kill switches, executors, audit.
  endpoints     Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (promote, score,...
  webhooks      Webhooks of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation).
  plots         Render plots to files and share them as embed links.
  guided        Guided mode: templates, column detection and drafts (stores nothing).
  priors        Business priors: translate beliefs into model priors.
  tenant        Your workspace (tenant): verification status, GDPR export and deletion.
  workflows     Workflows: validate, save, run and watch DAGs of tests, transforms and models.
  governance    Governance: the check catalog and the policies models must pass.
  validate      Validate a model version against the governance policies (or a workflow file).
  validations   Validations: the review queue, evidence, resubmission, deprecation,...
  explore       Explore a dataset or a model (sections computed in the sandbox), compare...

Usage: mapi runs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Inspect and control runs on the API.

Options:
  -h, --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  ls          List runs, newest first.

  watch       Follow a run's live events until it ends (--json: one JSON event per line).
  cancel      Request cancellation (idempotent).

docs.title: mapi runs ls
docs.text:
Usage: mapi runs ls [OPTIONS]

  List runs, newest first. Use filters to find runs by metric, param, tag or name.

Options:
  --kind <ingest|describe|validate|fit|score|evaluate|derive|render|optimize|sweep|backtest|sbc|campaign|translate_priors|workflow|workflow_node|explore|governance|inspect>
                                  Filter by kind
  --state <created|rejected|queued|dispatching|provisioning|running|stalled|finalizing|succeeded|partial|failed|cancelling|cancelled>
                                  Filter by state
  --spec <str>                    Filter by spec id
  --parent <str>                  Show only the child runs of this run
  --name <str>                    Show only runs with this text in the name
  --tag <str>                     Show only runs with this tag: KEY or KEY=VALUE. You can use
                                  the option more than one time.
  -f, --filter <str>              Show only runs that agree with this filter, for example
                                  'metric.rmse < 0.5' or 'param.fit.draws >= 1000'. You can use
                                  the option more than one time.
  --order-by <str>                Sort the runs by this value, for example '-metric.rmse' (a '-'
                                  sorts from high to low). The default is '-created_at'.
  -c, --column <str>              Add a column with this value, for example 'metric.rmse' or
                                  'param.fit.draws'. You can use the option more than one time.
  -e, --experiment <str>          Show only the runs of this experiment
  --view <str>                    Use the search of this saved view. Other options add to the

docs.title: mapi datasets upload
docs.text:
Usage: mapi datasets upload [OPTIONS] {files}...

  Upload one or more files as a new dataset version (signed PUT + sandboxed ingest run).

  One FILE without --node/--concat/--merge is a plain single-file upload. Several files (or any
  of those flags) make ONE version from all of them:

    mapi datasets upload 2024.nc 2025.nc --name cubes --concat year=2024,2025
    mapi datasets upload a.nc b.nc --name obs --merge --join outer
    mapi datasets upload img.nc psf.nc --name lens --node / --node /instrument

  --node PATH: where a file goes in the tree, once (every file) or once per file in file order
  (default /). Files that share a node are combined by --concat DIM=LABEL (one label per
  combined file in file order: repeat the flag or list LABEL,LABEL,...; numeric labels are
  numbers) or by --merge (variables on shared coords); --join exact|inner|outer aligns their
  coords. --mapping is given once (every file it can read) or once per file. Raw HDF5
  (.h5/.hdf5/.he5) needs a mapping with an 'hdf5' section: see 'mapi datasets inspect'.

Arguments:
  files...  .zarr.zip, .nc, .h5/.hdf5/.he5, .csv or .parquet (several: one version)  [required]

Options:
  --name <str>                Dataset name (created when missing)  [required]
  --mapping <path>            IngestMapping YAML/JSON (required for csv/parquet/raw HDF5); once
                              or per file
  --node <str>                Tree node of the files (once) or of each file (in order)
  --concat DIM=LABEL          Stack the files sharing a node along DIM, one label per file (or
                              DIM=L1,L2)
  --merge                     Merge the variables of the files sharing a node
  --join <exact|inner|outer>  Coord alignment for --concat/--merge (default exact)
  -m, --message <str>
  --wait / --no-wait          Wait for the ingest run  [default: wait]
  --timeout <float>
  -h, --help                  Show this message and exit.

docs.title: mapi datasets upload-images
docs.text:
Usage: mapi datasets upload-images [OPTIONS] {dataset} {directory}

  Upload a folder of images as a new image collection version.

  The command calculates the sha256 of each image, asks the server which images the base version
  does not have, and uploads only those, in zip parts. With --state, an interrupted upload
  continues from where it stopped: run the same command again.

    mapi datasets upload-images pets ./pets --label-from-folder --wait
    mapi datasets upload-images scans ./scans --manifest labels.csv --label-column class

Arguments:
  dataset    Dataset name (created when missing) or id  [required]
  directory  The folder with the images  [required]

Options:
  --manifest <file>            A CSV, TSV or Parquet table with one row per image (column path:
                               the file)
  --label-from-folder          Use the first folder of each path as its label
  --id-column <str>            The manifest column with image ids
  --label-column <str>         The manifest column with labels
  --split-column <str>         The manifest column with train/test values
  --path-column <str>          The manifest column with the file paths  [default: path]
  --size HxW                   The image size for samples and models
  --resize <stretch|crop|pad>  How images get the --size  [default: stretch]
  --mode <auto|gray|rgb>       The image channels  [default: auto]
  --base-version <int range>   Compare with this version (default: the latest image collection
                               version)  [x>=1]
  --no-base                    Upload all images (do not compare with a version)
  --part-size <str>            Maximum size of one zip part (for example 256MB)
  --state <path>               A file that records the upload, to continue it later
  -m, --message <str>
  --wait                       Wait for the ingest run
  --timeout <float>
  -h, --help                   Show this message and exit.

docs.title: mapi endpoints forecast
docs.text:
Usage: mapi endpoints forecast [OPTIONS] {alias} [table]

  Forecast with your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (no refit).

  The table has the columns of `mapi endpoints schema ALIAS` (Input table): the time column, the
  target and any drivers. Rows with the target filled are actuals: the model updates its state
  with them using its fitted parameters and forecasts from the last one. Rows after them with
  the target empty are forecast; without such rows, --periods (default 8) are appended. The
  answer says what the forecast was conditioned on.

Arguments:
  alias  Endpoint alias  [required]
  table  CSV (header row) or JSON rows in the endpoint's input layout: actuals with the target
         filled, dates to forecast with it empty ('-' = stdin)

Options:
  --actuals <path>           Rows with the target filled (CSV/JSON)
  --future <str>             A date to forecast (repeatable), or a CSV/JSON file of future rows
                             with their driver values
  --periods <int range>      Periods to append after the last actual  [x>=1]
  --future-covariates <str>  Empty future drivers: carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero or supplied
                             [default: carry_last]
  --wait <int range>         Prefer: wait=N  [default: 60; 0<=x<=60]
  --timeout <float>          Give up after N seconds
  --dry-run                  Print the call body (JSON) and send nothing
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: Every error is a MapiError with one of these stable codes. Over HTTP it becomes an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json) whose type ends in the code. Anything your data or a plugin said is returned separately, as untrusted_text.

docs.title: Spec and static validation
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable SCHEMA_INVALID 422 The document does not match its schema – SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 The document could not be parsed – PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 The document exceeds a size limit – UNSUPPORTED_API_VERSION 422 Unsupported apiVersion – REF_UNRESOLVED 422 A reference could not be resolved – SETTINGS_INVALID 422 Settings do not match their schema – BINDING_INVALID 422 The data binding is invalid – SPLIT_INVALID 422 The train/holdout split is invalid – LEAKAGE_RISK 422 A stateful step runs before the split – DIM_POLICY_LOOSENED 422 A dim policy can only become stricter – SCHEMA_DYNAMIC 422 Schema needs a dry-run to resolve – SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE 422 A side table is not available – PLOT_UNSAFE 422 The plot spec violates the plot safety policy – GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID 422 The guided answers do not fit the template – BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID 422 The business priors are inconsistent – IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED 422 The imported model uses an unsupported feature – ABOUT_INCOMPLETE 422 A catalog item has no complete About card – WORKFLOW_INVALID 422 The workflow is not valid – EXPRESSION_INVALID 422 A branch condition is not a valid expression – NODE_UNKNOWN 422 A workflow node names an unknown implementation – SCHEDULE_INVALID 422 The schedule or trigger is not valid – POLICY_INVALID 422 The governance policy is not valid – EXPLORE_INVALID 422 The explorer request is not valid –

docs.title: Score-time coordinate checks (CoordPlan)
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable UNSEEN_LEVELS 422 Unseen levels on a dim that forbids them – COORD_NOT_ALLOWED 422 Coordinates not allowed by dim policy – HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT 409 Horizon exceeds the fitted range – MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE 422 A future covariate is missing – NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION 422 Extension is not contiguous – CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 422 The model lacks this capability – RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED 422 Recursive forecasting unsupported – ACTUALS_INVALID 422 The supplied actuals cannot be used for this forecast –

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 Score mode not supported – CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED 422 The model cannot use this calibration data – SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE 422 The scenario is outside the precomputed grid – OPTIMIZE_INFEASIBLE 422 The budget constraints cannot all be met – ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 The model cannot update its forecast with supplied actuals –

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable QUOTA_EXCEEDED 429 Quota exceeded – RATE_LIMITED 429 Too many requests yes

docs.title: API
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable UNAUTHENTICATED 401 Authentication required – FORBIDDEN 403 Not allowed – NOT_FOUND 404 Not found – CONFLICT 409 Conflict – IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT 409 Idempotency key reused – PRECONDITION_FAILED 412 Precondition failed – PROMOTION_BLOCKED 409 The scorecard blocks the promotion – OVERRIDE_REQUIRED 409 Promotion needs an administrator override with a reason – WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED 422 The egress policy does not allow the webhook URL – WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID 401 Webhook signature invalid – EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED 422 Only platform plot recipes can be embedded – LINK_EXPIRED 410 The link has expired or was revoked – EMAIL_NOT_ALLOWED 422 This e-mail address cannot sign up – TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED 422 The terms of service were not accepted – EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED 403 The e-mail address is not verified – IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED 403 Identity verification is necessary – CHOOSER_ANSWER_INVALID 422 A chooser answer is not valid – WORKFLOW_NOT_RUNNABLE 409 The workflow revision cannot be run (it has errors) – VALIDATION_TRANSITION_INVALID 409 The model's validation status does not allow this – SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN 403 Approver and submitter must be different people – NOT_VALIDATED 409 The governance policy needs a validated model – NOT_READY 409 The result is not ready yet yes

docs.title: Run failures
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable USER_CODE_ERROR 422 User or plugin code failed – RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED 507 Run exhausted its resources – INFRA_ERROR 503 Infrastructure error yes INTEGRITY_FAILURE 500 Output integrity check failed – TIMEOUT 504 Run timed out – SANDBOX_VIOLATION 422 Sandbox policy violated – CANCELLED 409 Run was cancelled – EXPRESSION_ERROR 422 A branch condition could not be evaluated – INGEST_UNSAFE_FILE 422 The upload was refused: it is unsafe to read –

docs.title: Internal
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable INTERNAL_ERROR 500 Internal error yes

docs.title: Governance checks
docs.text:
Every check a governance policy can require, generated from mapi_spec.governance.GOVERNANCE_CHECKS (the catalog behind GET /v1/catalog/governance-checks, mapi governance checks and the web app's Check catalog). Each entry starts with its plain-language About card. Can you trust this model? explains the null tests in plain words and in statistics.

A policy may set a check's severity (blocking, warning, info), its own warn and fail limits (never looser than the order below allows) and its parameters. A check whose requirement does not hold for a model is reported as skipped with the reason; one that cannot be computed is error, which fails a blocking check.

Check Title Measures Default limits Needs baseline.beats_naive Better than simple benchmarks relative_skill pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0, fail below holdout, time_series convergence The fit is complete and stable r_hat_max pass at ≤ 1.01, warn up to 1.05, fail above – data.quality The data is good enough data_issue_count pass at ≤ 0, warn up to 2, fail above – holdout.accuracy Accurate on test data holdout_error pass at ≤ 0.15, warn up to 0.3, fail above holdout null.noise_regressors No effect from false drivers noise_effect_share pass at ≤ 0.02, warn up to 0.05, fail above – null.permutation_target Better than shuffled data permutation_p_value pass at ≤ 0.05, warn up to 0.1, fail above holdout null.placebo_time_shift No effect after a time shift placebo_effect_ratio pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above time_series plausibility.signs Effects have the correct direction wrong_sign_share pass at ≤ 0.1, warn up to 0.25, fail above – recovery.simulated Finds known values recovery_coverage pass within 0.1 of 0.9, warn within 0.25, fail further away – residuals.whiteness No pattern in the errors ljung_box_p_value pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0.01, fail below residuals, time_series sensitivity.prior The results come from the data prior_sensitivity pass at ≤ 0.2, warn up to 0.5, fail above bayesian stability.rolling_params Estimates are stable over time param_variation pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above time_series

docs.title: baseline.beats_naive - Better than simple benchmarks
docs.text:
Compares the error of the model on the test periods with very simple forecasts, for example 'same as last week' or 'same as last year'. The model must be better.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each forecast model.

Avoid it when: Models that do not forecast over time.

It needs: The test periods of the model and the history before them.

It assumes: The check scores the benchmarks on the same periods.

You get: The skill against the best benchmark (1 - model error / benchmark error).

Example: The error of the model is 30% lower than 'same as last year': skill 0.30, pass.

Related: evaluate.baseline, holdout.accuracy.

Expert detail

Relative skill 1 - L(model)/min_b L(b) on the holdout or backtest folds; MASE-style scaling by the in-sample seasonal-naive error is reported as well. References: Hyndman & Koehler (2006), Another look at measures of forecast accuracy.

Category baseline Metric relative_skill Default limits pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0, fail below Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again); the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description methods list of naive or seasonal_naive or mean or drift ["naive", "seasonal_naive"] metric string mae

docs.title: convergence - The fit is complete and stable
docs.text:
Makes sure that the fit procedure found a stable answer. If you fit the model again, you get the same result.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Every model.

Avoid it when: Models that you fit outside the platform, without diagnostics.

It needs: The diagnostics of the fit.

It assumes: The fit recorded its diagnostics.

You get: R-hat, effective draws and divergences (Bayesian) or the optimiser status.

Example: All chains agree (R-hat 1.003): pass.

Related: recovery.simulated.

Expert detail

Bayesian: max split R-hat (rank-normalised), with ESS and divergences as evidence; frequentist: optimiser convergence flag (value 1.0 when converged, inf otherwise).

Category convergence Metric r_hat_max Default limits pass at ≤ 1.01, warn up to 1.05, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

docs.title: data.quality - The data is good enough
docs.text:
Makes sure that the data is good before you trust the model. The data must have few gaps, enough history, no constant columns and no impossible values.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Every model.

Avoid it when: Synthetic data that you made yourself.

It needs: The dataset that the model fit used.

It assumes: The limits are correct for your data.

You get: The data problems that the check found, each in plain words.

Example: No gaps, 3 years of history, each driver changes: pass.

Related: convergence.

Category data Metric data_issue_count Default limits pass at ≤ 0, warn up to 2, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description max_missing number 0.05 ≥ 0, ≤ 1 min_history_periods integer 52 ≥ 1

docs.title: holdout.accuracy - Accurate on test data
docs.text:
Makes sure that the error of the model on periods that the fit did not use stays below the limit of your organisation.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each model that you use for forecasts or what-ifs.

Avoid it when: Models without a test period.

It needs: A test period or a backtest.

It assumes: The test periods are similar to future use.

You get: The selected error metric on the test data.

Example: MAPE 9% against a limit of 15%: pass.

Related: baseline.beats_naive, evaluate.metrics.

Category holdout Metric holdout_error Default limits pass at ≤ 0.15, warn up to 0.3, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again) Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description metric mape or smape or mase or rmse or mae mape

docs.title: null.noise_regressors - No effect from false drivers
docs.text:
Adds some false drivers that are only noise and fits the model again. A model that you can trust gives them almost no effect.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Marketing mix models and other models that divide a result between drivers.

Avoid it when: Forecast models that have no drivers.

It needs: The data and the settings of the model.

It assumes: The false drivers look like real drivers, but they have no signal.

You get: The largest share of the effect of the real drivers that goes to a false driver; If a false driver is clearly above the limit.

Example: Three false channels get 0.4%, 0.1% and 0.9% of the media effect: pass.

Related: null.permutation_target, plausibility.signs.

Expert detail

Placebo regressors drawn as Gaussian noise or as a driver shuffled in blocks, with the model's default prior (never a real channel's prior or calibration); the statistic is the largest placebo share of the real drivers' total effect (by ablation through the score path). Bayesian: flagged when P(share > warn limit) >= 0.9 over the posterior (practical equivalence, valid for sign-constrained effects); frequentist: placebo p-values with Holm's correction.

Category null_test Metric noise_effect_share Default limits pass at ≤ 0.02, warn up to 0.05, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_noise integer 3 ≥ 1, ≤ 10 kind gaussian or shuffled_driver shuffled_driver seed integer 0 ≥ 0

docs.title: null.permutation_target - Better than shuffled data
docs.text:
Fits the model again on copies of the data where the drivers have a random time order. A real model must be clearly better on the true data than on the shuffled copies.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Each model whose accuracy you use to make decisions.

Avoid it when: Models without a test period (there is nothing to compare).

It needs: The data and the settings of the model, and a test period.

It assumes: A random order of the drivers removes each real link between the drivers and the result; The trend, the season and the result stay as they are; For a model without drivers, the check shuffles the ups and downs of the result.

You get: The fraction of shuffled fits that were as good as the real fit (a p-value); The distribution of the shuffled scores.

Example: The real model forecasts better than all 19 shuffled fits: p = 0.05, pass.

Related: null.noise_regressors, baseline.beats_naive.

Expert detail

Permutation (randomisation) test on a scale-free statistic: holdout skill 1 - L(model) / L(null forecast) on each dataset (the null forecast is the last training value of an integrated series, else its mean). Null: models with drivers keep the result and get their drivers block-permuted jointly (so trend, season and controls cannot pass on their own; a model that ignores its drivers is tested as one without); models without drivers get the d-th differences of the result permuted i.i.d. and re-integrated from the original start (d from the ARIMA order or ADF/KPSS), which keeps the integration order and the increments' distribution but destroys predictable dynamics. Without a time order the result is permuted across rows and the statistic is the holdout error. p = (1 + #{perm >= real}) / (K + 1). References: Ojala & Garriga (2010), Permutation tests for studying classifier performance.

Category null_test Metric permutation_p_value Default limits pass at ≤ 0.05, warn up to 0.1, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again) Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_permutations integer 20 ≥ 5, ≤ 200 metric rmse or mae or mape or smape or crps rmse block integer – Periods of the drivers shuffled together (default: a twentieth of the series) (≥ 1, ≤ 520)

docs.title: null.placebo_time_shift - No effect after a time shift
docs.text:
Moves the drivers some months away from their real dates and fits the model again. The effects must become much smaller, or else the model finds time patterns, not real effects.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Models that divide results between drivers over time (marketing mix, regressions).

Avoid it when: Very short series (after the shift, the overlap is too small).

It needs: The data and the settings of the model over time.

It assumes: A real effect has a connection to the date of the driver.

You get: The placebo effect as a share of the real effect, for each shift.

Example: A shift of the spend by half a year keeps only 8% of the effect: pass.

Related: null.noise_regressors.

Expert detail

Time-shift placebo (leads/lags beyond any plausible carry-over); ratio of the placebo total effect to the real one, maximised over shifts.

Category null_test Metric placebo_effect_ratio Default limits pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description shifts list of integer [-26, 26] min items 1, max items 6

docs.title: plausibility.signs - Effects have the correct direction
docs.text:
Makes sure that each effect has the direction that business sense expects. For example, advertising must not decrease sales, and higher prices must not increase demand.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each model with effects that you can explain.

Avoid it when: Models that only forecast.

It needs: The estimates of the model and the expected directions.

It assumes: The expected directions are correct.

You get: The share of the estimate (or of the uncertainty) on the wrong side, for each effect.

Example: The effect of radio is negative with a probability of 40%: fail.

Related: null.noise_regressors, test.vif.

Category plausibility Metric wrong_sign_share Default limits pass at ≤ 0.1, warn up to 0.25, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description expected map of positive or negative – Parameter -> expected sign (default: media positive)

docs.title: recovery.simulated - Finds known values
docs.text:
Simulates data from the model with known true values and fits the model again. Then it makes sure that the 90% ranges of the model contain the true values about 90% of the time.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: New models, or models with many changes; Before you trust a complex Bayesian model.

Avoid it when: Models that cannot simulate data.

It needs: The settings of the model and the shape of the data.

It assumes: The simulated data is similar to the real data.

You get: How often the 90% ranges contained the true values.

Example: The true values were in the 90% ranges 88% of the time: pass.

Related: sensitivity.prior, convergence.

Expert detail

Simulation-based calibration lite: N simulate-fit cycles; coverage of central 90% intervals and rank uniformity per parameter. References: Talts et al. (2018), Validating Bayesian inference algorithms with simulation-based calibration.

Category recovery Metric recovery_coverage Default limits pass within 0.1 of 0.9, warn within 0.25, fail further away Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_sims integer 20 ≥ 5, ≤ 100 params list of string –

docs.title: residuals.whiteness - No pattern in the errors
docs.text:
Makes sure that the errors of the model look like random noise over time. If a pattern stays in the errors, the model does not use all of the information in the data.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Time-series and regression models.

Avoid it when: Models without residuals.

It needs: The in-sample errors of the model.

It assumes: The time steps are regular.

You get: The Ljung-Box p-value and the autocorrelations of the errors.

Example: Ljung-Box p = 0.38 at 10 lags: pass.

Related: test.ljung_box, evaluate.residuals.

Expert detail

Ljung-Box Q on residuals (model_df adjusted for ARMA terms); the minimum p-value over series for panels.

Category residuals Metric ljung_box_p_value Default limits pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0.01, fail below Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no residuals; the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description lags integer 10 ≥ 1, ≤ 200

docs.title: sensitivity.prior - The results come from the data
docs.text:
Fits a Bayesian model again with wider and narrower starting assumptions. The key answers must change very little, so that you know that they come from the data.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Bayesian models, mainly models with business priors.

Avoid it when: Models that are not Bayesian.

It needs: The data, the settings and the priors of the model.

It assumes: The scales that the check tries include all reasonable prior changes.

You get: The largest relative change of a key estimate.

Example: Prior widths that are two times larger move the return of TV by 6%: pass.

Related: plausibility.signs, recovery.simulated.

Expert detail

Power-scaling or refit-based prior sensitivity: relative change of posterior means of key quantities under scaled prior widths. References: Kallioinen et al. (2023), Detecting and diagnosing prior and likelihood sensitivity with power-scaling.

Category sensitivity Metric prior_sensitivity Default limits pass at ≤ 0.2, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when only Bayesian models have priors that the check can change Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description scales list of number [0.5, 2.0] Prior widths tried

docs.title: stability.rolling_params - Estimates are stable over time
docs.text:
Fits the model again on rolling windows of history. Then it makes sure that the key estimates do not change much from one window to the next.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Models with estimates that you use for decisions (effects, returns).

Avoid it when: Short histories (the windows are then too small).

It needs: The data over time and the settings of the model.

It assumes: The true effects change slowly.

You get: How much each key estimate changes between windows.

Example: The return of TV changes by 12% between windows: pass.

Related: test.cusum.

Expert detail

Coefficient of variation (or max relative deviation from the full-sample estimate) of each watched parameter across rolling-window refits; maximum over parameters.

Category stability Metric param_variation Default limits pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description window integer – Periods per window (≥ 8) step integer 4 ≥ 1 params list of string – Parameters to watch (default: the key effects)

docs.title: causal.impact
docs.text:
CausalImpact / interrupted time series: a Bayesian structural time series fitted on the periods before an intervention, with control series as regressors, predicts the series without the intervention; the effect is actual minus that counterfactual.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns scaling LOO invalid: the Kalman likelihood is a sum over the whole series; steps depend on each other, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots causal.impact, causal.pre_fit, core.decomposition, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

docs.title: causal.synthetic_control
docs.text:

docs.title: Augment
docs.text:
Random per-image transforms a loader applies to training batches. Flips and 90-degree turns (only half turns for non-square images) keep the pixels; crop_pad pads by n pixels (edge values) and crops back to the size at a random offset; brightness/contrast add or scale by a random amount up to the value (in units of the 0..255 range); noise adds Gaussian noise with that standard deviation.

Field Type Default Description flip_x boolean false Mirror left-right with probability 0.5 flip_y boolean false Mirror top-bottom with probability 0.5 rotate90 boolean false Turn by a random multiple of 90 degrees crop_pad integer 0 Pad by n pixels, then crop at random (≥ 0, ≤ 64) brightness number 0 Largest brightness change (≥ 0, ≤ 1) contrast number 0 Largest relative contrast change (≥ 0, ≤ 1) noise number 0 Gaussian noise sd (0..1 units) (≥ 0, ≤ 0.5)

docs.title: EarlyStopping
docs.text:

docs.title: TrainConfig

docs.title: Augment
docs.text:
Random per-image transforms a loader applies to training batches. Flips and 90-degree turns (only half turns for non-square images) keep the pixels; crop_pad pads by n pixels (edge values) and crops back to the size at a random offset; brightness/contrast add or scale by a random amount up to the value (in units of the 0..255 range); noise adds Gaussian noise with that standard deviation.

Field Type Default Description flip_x boolean false Mirror left-right with probability 0.5 flip_y boolean false Mirror top-bottom with probability 0.5 rotate90 boolean false Turn by a random multiple of 90 degrees crop_pad integer 0 Pad by n pixels, then crop at random (≥ 0, ≤ 64) brightness number 0 Largest brightness change (≥ 0, ≤ 1) contrast number 0 Largest relative contrast change (≥ 0, ≤ 1) noise number 0 Gaussian noise sd (0..1 units) (≥ 0, ≤ 0.5)

docs.title: mmm.bayesian
docs.text:
mmm-framework's Bayesian marketing-mix model: adstock and saturation per channel, trend and seasonality, national or hierarchical over geos and products, channel effects stated as returns on spend, business priors and lift tests as calibration, budget optimisation with mmm-framework planning.

Version 1.1.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions additive Decision objective yes Fast scoring – Owns carryover, inverse_units, scaling LOO valid Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.energy, core.posterior_forest, core.prior_posterior, mmm.decomposition, mmm.waterfall, mmm.response_curves, mmm.marginal_cost, mmm.roi, mmm.spend_effect, mmm.adstock, mmm.lift_tests, mmm.effectiveness Resources class M (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (time) of y Expected (or predictive) KPI over the panel dims and time contributions (component, time) of y Every channel, the baseline, trend, seasonality and each control; they sum to y_hat

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description contributions (sample, channel, time) target fit Channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and control contributions over the fit window per thinned draw (panel dims included) response_curves (sample, channel, multiplier) target fit Total contribution per spend multiplier and channel (and geo) per thinned draw (Guided-mode slider grids, budget optimisation) marginal_cost (sample, channel) spend per target fit Extra spend per extra unit of the KPI at current spend adstock (sample, channel, lag) share fit Share of a unit of spend's total effect that lands each number of periods after the spend, per thinned draw (carry-over shape) effectiveness (sample, channel, time) target per spend fit KPI per unit of spend at the average spend level with the channel effect of each period (changes over time only for time-varying channels)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": 8, "normalize": true} basic saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic channels map of ChannelSettings – advanced Per-channel adstock/saturation overrides (channel label -> settings) trend TrendSettings {"kind": "linear", "n_changepoints": 10, "changepoint_range… basic seasonality SeasonalitySettings {"yearly_order": 2, "monthly_order": null, "weekly_order": … basic hierarchy HierarchySettings {"pool_over": [], "media_by_geo": false, "media_geo_sigma":… basic controls list of string (optional) null advanced Control variables (default: every other numeric variable over time) frequency W or D or M (optional) null advanced Data frequency: W (weekly), D (daily) or M (monthly); default: read from the time labels new_levels pooled or hyperprior or zero or error pooled advanced How a geo or product unseen at fit is scored: pooled (the overall level and average channel effects), hyperprior (a level drawn from the fitted spread, so its range is wider), zero (no channel effects) or error (refuse) grid GridSettings {"max_multiplier": 2.5, "points": 26, "marginal_step": 0.01} advanced media_prior roi or coefficient roi advanced Parameterise channel effects by their return on spend (priors are stated in ROI, comparable across channels) or by a standardised coefficient priors PriorSettings {"roi": {}, "roi_default": null, "intercept": null} advanced Prior overrides (written by business-prior translation) likelihood normal or student_t or poisson or negative_binomial or beta normal advanced Observation model of the KPI: normal, student_t (heavy-tailed outliers), poisson or negative_binomial (counts, log link) or beta (shares between 0 and 1, logit link) media_effect_sigma number 0.5 advanced Count and share likelihoods only: prior scale (half-normal) of a channel's largest effect on the link scale (> 0, ≤ 5) time_varying TimeVaryingSettings {"channels": [], "innovation_sigma": 0.15, "forecast": "ran… advanced Channels whose effect changes over time Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "panel": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "path": "hierarchy.pool_over",
      "default": []
    },
    "strategy": {
      "type": "string",
      "path": "new_levels",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "hyperprior",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "time": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "channel": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "{*panel as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{strategy}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*panel}",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "spend": {
        "dims": [
          "{*panel}",
          "channel",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "spend",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "strategy": "error"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{*panel as d}": {
            "policy": "fixed"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: AdstockSettings
docs.text:
Carry-over of spend into later periods (mmm-framework AdstockConfig).

Field Type Default Description kind geometric or delayed or weibull or none geometric geometric: decays from the spend period; delayed: peaks a few periods later; weibull: a flexible shape; none: no carry-over l_max integer 8 How many periods an effect can last (the kernel length) (≥ 1, ≤ 52) normalize boolean true Normalise the lag weights to sum to one (the effect size stays in the channel coefficient)

docs.title: ChannelSettings
docs.text:
Per-channel overrides of the shared adstock and saturation settings.

Field Type Default Description adstock AdstockSettings (optional) null saturation SaturationSettings (optional) null

docs.title: GridSettings
docs.text:
Response-curve grids cached per thinned draw (Guided-mode sliders, optimisation).

Field Type Default Description max_multiplier number 2.5 Largest spend multiplier on the grid (1 = spend over the fit window, which the grid always holds) (≥ 1, ≤ 20) points integer 26 Grid points from 0 to max_multiplier (plus 1, today's spend, when the spacing skips it) (≥ 3, ≤ 201) marginal_step number 0.01 Relative spend change used for marginal cost (central difference) (> 0, ≤ 0.25)

docs.title: HierarchySettings
docs.text:
Panel structure: the dims the KPI varies over besides time. pool_over lists the panel dims of the data (geo and/or product). Every level gets its own baseline, partially pooled towards the overall level (HierarchicalConfig.pool_across_geo/product); with media_by_geo each geo also gets its own channel effects, partially pooled across geos.

Field Type Default Description pool_over list of geo or product – Panel dims of the data (geo, product); empty for one national series (max items 2) media_by_geo boolean false Let channel effects differ by geo (partially pooled) media_geo_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of the geo deviations of log channel effects (> 0, ≤ 5)

docs.title: NormalPrior
docs.text:
Normal(mu, sigma) on the standardised KPI scale (KPI standard deviations).

Field Type Default Description mu number required ≥ -50, ≤ 50 sigma number required > 0, ≤ 50

docs.title: PriorSettings
docs.text:
Prior overrides; business-prior translation (translate_priors) writes them. * roi - per channel, a log-normal prior on the return on spend (mmm-framework's ROI-parameterised channel effect, roi_prior_mu/roi_prior_sigma); * roi_default - the log-normal ROI prior of channels not listed (default LogNormal(0, 1): median break-even); * intercept - the baseline level in KPI standard deviations from the mean.

Field Type Default Description roi map of RoiPrior – Per-channel log-normal ROI priors (channel label -> {mu, sigma}) roi_default RoiPrior (optional) null intercept NormalPrior (optional) null

docs.title: RoiPrior
docs.text:
A log-normal prior on a channel's return on spend (KPI per unit of spend over the fit window): roi ~ LogNormal(mu, sigma), so exp(mu) is the median ROI.

Field Type Default Description mu number required Log of the median ROI (≥ -20, ≤ 20) sigma number required Spread on the log scale (> 0, ≤ 10)

docs.title: SaturationSettings
docs.text:
Diminishing returns of (carried-over) spend (mmm-framework SaturationConfig).

Field Type Default Description kind logistic or hill or michaelis_menten or tanh or root or none logistic logistic (default, most stable), hill (S-shaped), michaelis_menten, tanh, root (power curve) or none (a straight line)

docs.title: SeasonalitySettings
docs.text:
Fourier seasonality (mmm-framework SeasonalityConfig).

Field Type Default Description yearly_order integer (optional) 2 Fourier pairs of the yearly cycle (0 or null: none) monthly_order integer (optional) null weekly_order integer (optional) null Daily data only prior_sigma number 0.3 Prior sd of each Fourier coefficient, in KPI standard deviations (raise it for strongly seasonal categories) (> 0, ≤ 5)

docs.title: TimeVaryingSettings
docs.text:
Channels whose effect drifts over time (mmm-framework's time-varying coefficient: a random walk on the log of the channel coefficient, one step per period).

Field Type Default Description channels list of string – Channels whose effect may change over time (creative wear-out, changes in the market) (max items 64) innovation_sigma number 0.15 Prior scale of the change in the log effect from one period to the next (smaller: closer to a constant effect) (> 0, ≤ 2) forecast random_walk or hold_last or mean random_walk The effect after the fit window: random_walk (continue the random walk, so the range widens with the horizon), hold_last (the last fitted value) or mean (the average over the fit window)

docs.title: TrendSettings
docs.text:
The slow-moving baseline (mmm-framework TrendConfig).

Field Type Default Description kind none or linear or piecewise or spline or gp linear none, linear (default), piecewise (Prophet-style changepoints), spline or gp (a smooth Gaussian-process curve). Forecasts hold flexible trends at their last fitted level; a linear trend is extrapolated. n_changepoints integer 10 ≥ 1, ≤ 50 changepoint_range number 0.8 > 0, ≤ 1 n_knots integer 10 ≥ 3, ≤ 50 growth_prior_sigma number 0.5 Prior sd of the linear slope, in KPI standard deviations over the whole history (> 0, ≤ 10)

docs.title: sci.areal_bym2
docs.text:
Counts of a disease in areas (districts, counties) against their expected counts, with a covariate and area effects that borrow strength from neighbouring areas: an ICAR, a proper CAR, BYM2 (a scaled ICAR mixed with independent noise) or iid effects. Outputs the smoothed relative risk of each area, the probability that it is above 1, and the expected counts. The polygons and the graph go into the bundle for the maps.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.area_map, net.graph, core.ridge Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description cases (area) of cases Cases in each area: the expected count expected * rr, or a Poisson draw rr (area) 1 Relative risk of each area (1 = the reference rate) p_exceed (area) probability 1 when rr is above exceed_threshold in a draw, else 0: the mean over draws is the probability P(rr > threshold) effect (area) 1 The area effect u on the log relative risk (what the covariate does not explain)

Field Type Default Level Description kind poisson or iid or icar or car or bym2 bym2 – Prior of the area effects: poisson (none), iid, icar, car (proper CAR) or bym2 (ICAR plus iid with a mixing share rho) (x-ui-level: basic) islands link_nearest or isolate or error link_nearest – Areas without neighbours: link_nearest links each to the area with the closest boundary; isolate keeps them alone (iid and icar only); error stops (x-ui-level: basic) covariate_scale number 10.0 – Divide the centred covariate by this (b1 is the effect of one unit) (> 0) center_covariate boolean true – Subtract the mean of the covariate intercept_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the intercept b0 (> 0) slope_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the covariate effect b1 (> 0) sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of sigma, the sd of the area effects (> 0) rho_alpha number 1.0 – Beta prior of rho (bym2): first shape (> 0) rho_beta number 1.0 – Beta prior of rho (bym2): second shape (> 0) exceed_threshold number 1.0 – p_exceed is the probability that rr is above this value (> 0) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: sci.circular_regression
docs.text:
Angles (wind directions, times of day) on the circle. Regression kinds put the hour of day and the day of year into harmonic features and use a von Mises with a canonical link (or a projected normal, or a mixture of two regimes with a gate); kind activity fits a log-Fourier density per group (camera-trap times) with activity levels and overlaps. Outputs are mean directions, resultant lengths and predictive densities by block of the day or by group.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.rose, sci.profile_bands, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description direction_hat (obs) of direction Mean direction of the row's predictive distribution (expected), or a simulated angle (predictive), from 0 to one turn resultant (obs) 1 Mean resultant length of the row's predictive distribution (1: one direction, 0: no preferred direction) density (frame, angle) 1/unit Predictive density per unit of the direction on a grid of angles, for each block of the day (regression) or group (activity) mean_direction (frame) of direction Direction of the mean resultant vector of each frame resultant_length (frame) 1 Length of the mean resultant vector of each frame activity_level (frame) 1 kind activity: fraction of the day the group is active, 1 / (2 pi max f) overlap (frame, frame_) 1 kind activity: coefficient of overlap of the activity densities of two groups

Field Type Default Level Description kind von_mises or projected_normal or regime_mixture or activity von_mises – von_mises (canonical link), projected_normal, regime_mixture (two von Mises regimes with a gate), or activity (a log-Fourier density per group) (x-ui-level: basic) units degrees or radians or hours degrees – Units of the direction: degrees, radians or hours (a time of day) (x-ui-level: basic) group_dim string group – kind activity: the dim of the groups (species); the index variable is _idx daily_harmonics integer 3 – Harmonics of the hour of day (≥ 0, ≤ 8) annual_harmonics integer 2 – Harmonics of the day of year (≥ 0, ≤ 6) interaction_harmonics integer 2 – Daily harmonics multiplied by the first annual harmonic (the daily cycle changes with the season) (≥ 0, ≤ 8) intercept_sd number 2.0 – Prior sd of the intercepts (not used by regime_mixture) (> 0) coef_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the other coefficients (> 0) regime_directions_deg list of number – – regime_mixture: prior mean direction of each regime (degrees, in the units' own orientation) (min items 2, max items 2) regime_names list of string – – regime_mixture: names of the two regimes (min items 2, max items 2) regime_strength number 2.0 – regime_mixture: prior mean concentration of each regime (> 0) regime_daily_harmonics integer 2 – ≥ 0, ≤ 8 regime_annual_harmonics integer 1 – ≥ 0, ≤ 6 gate_intercept_sd number 1.5 – Prior sd of the gate intercept (> 0) harmonics integer 16 – activity: Fourier harmonics (≥ 1, ≤ 64) tau_sd number 2.0 – activity: half-normal scale of tau (> 0) grid_points integer 256 – activity: angles of the normalising sum (≥ 32, ≤ 4096) frames integer 8 – Regression kinds: blocks of the day for density and mean_direction (8: three hours each) (≥ 1, ≤ 48) angle_points integer 72 – Angles of the density output (≥ 8, ≤ 720) rows_per_frame integer 200 – Scored rows averaged per frame for the density (≥ 1, ≤ 20000) score_draws integer 400 – Posterior draws kept per score (evenly spaced) (≥ 1, ≤ 20000) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: sci.cmb_field
docs.text:
Field-level inference of a masked CMB temperature map: every pixel of the sky on a periodic flat patch is sampled jointly with the bandpowers by a Wandelt-Eriksen Gibbs sampler (constrained realisations by preconditioned conjugate gradients, an inverse-gamma bandpower step and a rescaling move). Gives the Wiener-filtered map, sky draws behind the mask, a per-pixel sd and the bandpowers.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: every pixel depends on one latent sky field with tens of thousands of parameters, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined; compare variants by their bandpowers, amplitude and tilt Default plots core.convergence, sci.power_spectrum, sci.field_map, sci.image_residuals, sci.ppc_image_grid Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description sky (row, col) uK Posterior draws of the beamed sky (constrained realisations; unconstrained skies with the posterior spectrum for simulate) temperature_hat (row, col) of temperature The sky draw (expected), plus noise with noise_sd (predictive) bandpower (bin) uK^2 Bandpower D_ell of each bin bandpower_ratio (bin) 1 Bandpower over the reference bandpower, exp(q) log_amplitude () 1 Log amplitude of the bandpowers relative to the reference tilt () 1 Tilt of the bandpowers relative to the reference, at tilt_pivot

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description sky_moments (stat, row, col) uK fit Posterior mean (the Wiener filter averaged over the spectrum) and sd of each pixel over every kept Gibbs draw

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description pixel_arcmin number 7.5 – Side of a map pixel (arcmin) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0, ≤ 600) beam_fwhm_arcmin number 5.0 – FWHM of the Gaussian beam of the map (arcmin) (≥ 0, ≤ 600) pixel_subsamples integer 8 – Point samples per pixel side that the map pixels average (box window; 1 = none) (≥ 1, ≤ 64) pixel_window boolean false – The data has a pixel_window(multipole) variable (for example the HEALPix window of the source map) bin_edges list of number – – Multipole edges of the bandpower bins (x-ui-level: basic) (min items 2, max items 101) projection gnomonic or flat gnomonic – gnomonic: correct the multipoles for the mean stretch of a tangent-plane projection; flat: no correction (x-ui-level: basic) border integer 8 – Unobserved pixels around the raster on the periodic torus (≥ 0, ≤ 128) ell_dense number 300.0 – Modes below this multipole get the dense CG preconditioner (≥ 0) n_alias integer 3 – Aliased replicas folded into the prior power (≥ 0, ≤ 6) mean_prior_sd number 100.0 – Prior sd of the patch mean (uK) (> 0) cg_tol number 1e-05 – Relative residual that stops CG (> 0, ≤ 0.1) cg_max_iter integer 5000 – Most CG iterations per solve (≥ 10, ≤ 100000) rescale boolean true – Use the non-centred rescaling move q_init_sd number 0.3 – Sd of the dispersed chain starts (≥ 0, ≤ 3) tilt_pivot number 500.0 – Pivot multipole of the tilt (> 0) tilt_max_ell number 1450.0 – Bins with a centre at or above this are left out of the tilt (> 0) tilt_prior_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of log amplitude and tilt (> 0) field_draws integer 40 – Sky maps drawn per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) Input data contract (schema template)

    "pixel_window": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {

        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Map rows (bottom up)"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Map columns"
      },
      "multipole": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Multipole ell = 0, 1, 2, ... of the reference spectrum"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "temperature": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",

docs.title: sci.colour_naming
docs.text:
Colour naming in one language (World Color Survey): the probability that a speaker gives each term to each colour chip, as a softmax over quadratic CIELAB logits with zero-sum weights, pooled or with speaker-level intercepts and linear weights. Predicts new speakers and maps each term's share of speakers on the chip palette.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.swatches, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)
