docs.title: sci.fisher_kpp
docs.text:
Cell counts across a closing wound (a scratch assay) as a Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion equation: cells move with diffusivity D, divide logistically at rate lam up to a capacity K, optionally after a start-up delay. The PDE runs inside the model from the counts at the first time; outputs are the expected density field (a kymograph over time and position) and the front speed 2 sqrt(D lam).

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.profile_bands, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description density (t, x) of count Cells per column: the expected count K u(x, t), or a Poisson draw wave_speed () um/h Speed of the travelling invasion front, 2 sqrt(D lam)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description steps_per_hour integer 10 – Explicit Euler steps per hour; more steps are slower but stable for a larger diffusivity (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) delay boolean true – Multiply movement and growth by tanh(beta t): the cells start slowly after the scratch (x-ui-level: basic) max_extension integer 4 – Observation periods a forecast may reach past the last fitted time (≥ 0, ≤ 1000) diffusivity_median number 1000.0 – Prior median of D (um^2/h) (> 0) diffusivity_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of D (> 0) growth_median number 0.05 – Prior median of lam (1/h) (> 0) growth_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of lam (> 0) capacity_mu number 122.0 – Prior mean of K (cells per column) (> 0) capacity_sigma number 15.0 – Prior sd of K (> 0) delay_rate_median number 0.1 – Prior median of beta (1/h) (> 0) delay_rate_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of beta (> 0) initial_floor number 0.1 – Smallest initial count, so an empty column can still fill (> 0) cfl_quantile number 0.99 – Quantile of the prior of D that must satisfy D dt / dx^2 <= 1/2 (> 0.5, < 1.0) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 4
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}",
        "description": "Hours since the start of the assay"
      },
      "x": {
        "kind": "float",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Centre of each column across the wound (um, equal spacing)"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "count": {
        "dims": [
          "t",
          "x"
        ],
        "dtype": "int64",
        "role": "target",
        "units": "cells",
        "bounds": [
          0,
          null
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: sci.graphical_model
docs.text:
Learns which variables are directly linked: partial correlations (the correlation of two variables given all the others) and the probability of an edge, P(|rho| > threshold). kind dense is a multivariate normal with an LKJ prior on the correlations (it also predicts and simulates new samples); kind neighbourhood is a sparse horseshoe regression of each variable on the others with AND/OR symmetrisation.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, net.graph, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description pcor (var, var_) 1 Partial correlation of each pair of variables given all the others (unit diagonal) edge_prob (var, var_) 1 Edge indicator per draw (|partial correlation| > threshold); its mean over the draws is the edge probability value (cell, var) of value dense only: the values of each cell (a draw from the model with kind predictive or mode simulate)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description kind dense or neighbourhood dense – dense: one multivariate normal with an LKJ prior (predicts and simulates cells); neighbourhood: sparse horseshoe regressions of each variable on the others (x-ui-level: basic) threshold number 0.1 – Relevance threshold delta: an edge is |partial correlation| > delta (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0, < 1) standardise boolean true – Centre and scale each variable with the mean and sd of the fit data reference boolean false – The data has a known network reference(var, var_) (1 = edge) that the plots compare with (x-ui-level: basic) log_likelihood auto or joint or conditional auto – Pointwise log-likelihood kept for elpd_loo: joint (dense only) or conditional (each variable given the others; both kinds). auto: joint for dense, conditional for neighbourhood lkj_eta number 2.0 – dense: LKJ shape of the correlation prior (> 0) sd_rate number 1.0 – dense: rate of the Exponential prior of the standardised sds (> 0) mean_sd number 1.0 – dense: sd of the Normal prior of the means (> 0) expected_neighbours number 2.0 – neighbourhood: prior guess p0 of the neighbours of each variable (sets the global horseshoe scale) (> 0) slab_alpha number 2.0 – neighbourhood: c^2 ~ InvGamma(alpha, beta) (> 0) slab_beta number 2.0 – neighbourhood: c^2 ~ InvGamma(alpha, beta) (> 0) edge_rule and or or or rho and – neighbourhood: an edge when both coefficients pass the threshold (and), either one (or), or their symmetric combination (rho) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "reference": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "cell": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "pooled",
        "description": "Exchangeable samples (cells); new ones may be scored"
      },
      "var": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "The measured variables: the nodes of the graph"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "value": {
        "dims": [
          "cell",
          "var"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "description": "The measured value of each variable in each cell"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "reference": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "var_": {
            "kind": "categorical",
            "policy": "fixed",
            "description": "The variables again (the second node of a pair)"
          }
        },
        "vars": {
          "reference": {
            "dims": [
              "var",
              "var_"
            ],
            "dtype": "int64",
            "role": "constant",
            "description": "A known network to compare with (1 = edge)"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: sci.heat_plate

Thermocouple readings of a heated plate as the 2-D steady heat equation: conduction k, face loss h, edge loss h_edge and heater efficiency eta, with a finite-volume linear system solved inside the model for each run. Outputs are the temperature field of each run (or of any new heater layout) and the heat-spreading length sqrt(k delta / 2h).

docs.title: sci.ibp_features
docs.text:
Latent binary features of small images (handwritten digits): every image is the average image plus the features it owns. A stick-breaking Indian buffet process truncated at K features, with every image's binary pattern summed out over 2^K patterns, so NUTS samples the feature images and their probabilities. Outputs are the feature images, which images own them, and completions of unseen pixels.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map, sci.ppc_image_grid, sci.image_residuals Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description ink_hat (digit, y, x) of ink Expected image given the seen pixels (completion where unseen), or a draw of pattern and noise features (feature, y, x) ink Feature images: the ink a feature adds to (or removes from) the average image feature_prob (feature) 1 Probability pi_k that an image owns feature k owns (digit, feature) 1 Probability that each image owns each feature, given its seen pixels

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description n_features integer 8 – Truncation K: the largest number of features. Each image sums over 2^K patterns, so each extra feature doubles the cost (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 10) kind fixed_noise or free_noise fixed_noise – fixed_noise keeps the pixel noise at noise_sd (the notebook); free_noise learns it (x-ui-level: basic) noise_sd number 0.25 – Pixel noise sigma_X (ink units). It sets the resolution: a smaller value makes more features worth keeping (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0) alpha_shape number 1.0 – Gamma shape of the IBP mass alpha (> 0) alpha_rate number 1.0 – Gamma rate of the IBP mass alpha (> 0) feature_scale_sd number 1.0 – HalfNormal scale of sigma_A (> 0) start digits or default digits – digits: every chain starts at half of K random images with nu = 0.8 and no jitter (avoids the 'no features' trap); default: the jittered platform start score_draws integer 200 – Posterior draws (spread over the chains) per score (≥ 1, ≤ 4000) shown_mask boolean false – The data has a shown(digit, y, x) mask: pixels where it is False are hidden from the fit (held-out halves) truncation_warn number 0.05 – Warn when the posterior mean of the last feature probability is above this (> 0, < 1) Input data contract (schema template)

        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel row (top = 0)"
      },

        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel column"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "ink": {
        "dims": [
          "digit",

        ],

        "role": "target",
        "units": "ink",

docs.title: sci.lgcp_grid
docs.text:
A log-Gaussian Cox process for event counts on a regular space-time grid: a random-walk total per period times a smooth 2-D map (Matérn-5/2 HSGP) that can change from era to era, with negative-binomial counts. Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, core.ppc_fan, sci.field_map, sci.ensemble Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description rate (period, row, col) of count Events per cell and period: the expected intensity, or a predictive count draw total (period) of count Expected events per period in the whole grid

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description max_extension integer 8 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 400) era_periods integer 4 – Periods in one era: the spatial field changes from era to era (4 quarters = one map per year) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) field era_walk or static era_walk – era_walk: a new map each era (a random walk of maps); static: one map for all periods (the separable model) anchor busiest or first or last busiest – The era whose map gets the marginal prior; the other eras walk away from it (busiest = the fit era with the most events) likelihood negbin or poisson negbin – cell_km number 25.0 – Width of one grid cell in km (> 0) m_row integer 10 – HSGP basis functions along rows (≥ 2, ≤ 60) m_col integer 14 – HSGP basis functions along columns (≥ 2, ≤ 60) c number 1.5 – HSGP boundary factor (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0) ell_lower_km number 15.0 – 5% quantile of the lengthscale prior (> 0) ell_upper_km number 100.0 – 95% quantile of the lengthscale prior (> 0) alpha_sigma number 1.5 – Sd of the log total per period (centred on the fit mean) (> 0) sigma_g_scale number 0.5 – Half-normal scale of the RW step (> 0) eta0_scale number 2.0 – Half-normal scale of the anchor map (> 0) eta_d_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the era increments (> 0) inv_phi_rate number 1.0 – Exponential rate of 1/phi (0 = Poisson) (> 0) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: sci.network_latent_space
docs.text:
An undirected graph (who works with whom) as one Bernoulli tie for each pair of nodes. The log odds add pair covariates (homophily), a sociality effect per node and, for kind latent_space, minus the distance between latent positions. Outputs are the tie probability of every pair, the positions (aligned by Procrustes), the sociality, simulated graphs and their statistics.

docs.title: sci.phylo_regression
docs.text:
A regression of one trait of species on other traits whose residuals are correlated by a phylogeny: i.i.d., Brownian motion, Pagel's lambda or Ornstein-Uhlenbeck on the shared branch length of the tree. Predicts a missing trait from relatives and stores the leave-one-out conditional log density for elpd_loo.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.phylogeny Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description trait (species) of trait The trait of each species predicted from its relatives (Gaussian conditioning on the other species; the median when the trait is logged), or a draw with the conditional noise slope (predictor) 1 Slope of each predictor (sd of the trait per sd of the predictor when standardised)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description kind iid or brownian or lambda or ou lambda – Residual correlation: iid (no tree), brownian (Brownian motion on the tree), lambda (Pagel's lambda: tree part plus a species part) or ou (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck) (x-ui-level: basic) predictors list of string – – Names of the predictor variables on the species dim (x-ui-level: basic) (max items 16) log_target boolean true – Take the log of the trait (it must be positive) log_predictors boolean true – Take the log of each predictor (they must be positive) standardise boolean true – Centre and scale the trait and the predictors by the fitted species (the slopes are then in sd of the trait per sd of the predictor) intercept_sd number 1.0 – Prior sd of the intercept (> 0) slope_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of each slope (> 0) sigma_rate number 1.0 – Rate of the exponential prior of sigma (> 0) lambda_alpha number 1.0 – Beta prior of lambda: first shape (> 0) lambda_beta number 1.0 – Beta prior of lambda: second shape (> 0) ou_parameterisation rate or variance rate – ou: put the prior on the Brownian rate eta2*rho (rate, recommended) or on eta2 and rho (variance) rate_sd number 1.0 – ou (rate): HalfNormal sd of eta2*rho (> 0) rho_sd number 5.0 – ou: HalfNormal sd of rho (pull to the optimum) (> 0) eta2_sd number 5.0 – ou (variance): HalfNormal sd of eta2 (> 0) jitter number 1e-06 – ou: added to the diagonal of K (≥ 0, ≤ 0.01) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: sci.storm_localisation
docs.text:
Single-molecule localisation microscopy (STORM/PALM): finds isolated spots in raw EMCCD frames and fits each with a pixel-integrated Gaussian PSF on a background, with Poisson counts after the camera's photon-transfer calibration. Outputs are positions with nm error bars, photons, the PSF width, a super-resolved render and the fitted patches.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, sci.point_pattern, sci.image_residuals, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description x (spot) nm Column position of each spot y (spot) nm Row position of each spot photons (spot) photons Photons that each molecule emitted into the frame background (spot) photons/px Background at the centre of each patch psf_sd (spot) nm PSF sd of each spot render (render_y, render_x) localisations Super-resolved image: the spots at the drawn positions, blurred by half a render pixel patch_fit (spot, py, px) counts Expected effective counts (photons / 2) of each fitted patch, or Poisson draws frames_hat (frame, row, col) of frames Camera image (ADU): the fitted spots on the background

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description pixel_nm number 100.0 – Size of one camera pixel in the sample (nm) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0) kind flat or plane flat – Background in each patch: flat (one value) or plane (a value and a slope in x and y) (x-ui-level: basic) offset_adu number (optional) null – Camera offset (ADU). Set it with scale_adu; unset, both come from the photon-transfer curve of the frames scale_adu number (optional) null – ADU per effective count: twice the EM gain (the photon-transfer slope) max_spots integer 200 – Isolated spots fitted, evenly spaced in frame order (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 5000) threshold_sd number 5.0 – Detection threshold (robust noise sds) (> 0) smooth_px number 1.0 – Gaussian smoothing before detection (px) (> 0) patch_px integer 11 – Side of each fitted patch (odd, px) (≥ 5, ≤ 31) min_blob_px integer 13 – Fewest pixels of a fitted blob (≥ 1) max_blob_px integer 39 – Most pixels of a fitted blob (≥ 1) amplitude_band list of any [0.0, 1.0] – Quantile band of blob amplitude that is fitted (0, 1: every isolated blob) (min items 2, max items 2) photons_median number 1500.0 – Prior median of the photons per spot (> 0) photons_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale prior sd of the photons (> 0) psf_sd_px number 1.0 – Prior median of the PSF sd (px) (> 0) psf_log_sd number 0.2 – Log-scale prior sd of the PSF sd (> 0) position_sd_px number 2.0 – Prior sd of the position around the blob centre (px) (> 0) background_photons number (optional) null – Prior median of the background (photons per pixel); unset: twice the median effective count of the movie background_log_sd number 0.5 – Log-scale prior sd of the background (> 0) gradient_sd number 0.05 – Prior sd of the background slopes (log per px; kind plane) (> 0) score_draws integer 40 – Posterior draws in each score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) ppc_draws integer 20 – Predictive patch draws kept in the bundle (0: none) (≥ 0, ≤ 200) render_px_nm number 16.0 – Pixel size of the super-resolved render (nm; the render of score_draws draws must stay within 50,000,000 values) (≥ 1.0) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "frame": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Camera frame"
      },
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel row"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel column"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "frames": {
        "dims": [
          "frame",
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "int32",
        "role": "target",
        "units": "ADU",
        "bounds": [
          0,
          null
        ],
        "description": "Raw camera counts of each frame"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: sci.strong_lens
docs.text:
A pixel forward model of a galaxy-scale strong gravitational lens: a singular isothermal ellipsoid with external shear traces every pixel to a Sersic source; the lens light, a PSF and correlated noise are modelled; the light amplitudes are integrated out. Gives the Einstein radius, the unlensed source and critical curves. Reads plain or tree datasets (the PSF from a /psf node).

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the light amplitudes are integrated out over all pixels and the whitened noise couples neighbouring pixels, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map Resources class M (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description model_image (row, col) of image Expected image (lens light, lensed source, sky, PSF), or a simulated observation with noise source (source_row, source_col) of image The unlensed source (parametric Sersic of each draw) on a source-plane grid einstein_radius () arcsec Einstein radius of the isothermal ellipsoid einstein_mass () solar_mass Mass inside the Einstein radius (needs z_lens and z_source)

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description critical_curves (sample, curve_point) arcsec fit Tangential critical curve (image plane), its caustic and the cut (source plane) for posterior draws, in arcsec and grid pixel indices

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description pixel_scale number 0.05 – Pixel size in arcsec (> 0, ≤ 10) subsample integer 2 – Rays per pixel along each axis (sub-pixel sampling) (≥ 1, ≤ 4) lens_light_components integer 2 – Concentric Sersic profiles for the lens galaxy's light (≥ 0, ≤ 2) external_shear boolean true – Add an external shear to the lens noise_correlation number 0.0 – Lag-one correlation of the noise between neighbouring pixels (separable rows x columns; drizzled images have about 0.2). 0 treats pixels as independent (≥ 0.0, < 0.45) fit_noise_scale boolean true – Scale the noise map by a free factor use_mask boolean false – The data has a bool mask(row, col) of pixels psf_tolerance number 0.001 – Relative error allowed in the separable PSF expansion (> 0, < 1) psf_max_rank integer 12 – Most separable PSF terms (≥ 1, ≤ 40) psf_source auto or tree auto – Where the PSF comes from: 'auto' uses the /psf node of a tree dataset when there is one, else the flat psf variable (which the input then needs); 'tree' reads it only from the /psf node, so the flat input needs no psf theta_e_median number 1.0 – Prior median of the Einstein radius (> 0) theta_e_log_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of log Einstein radius (> 0) mass_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the mass centre (> 0) light_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the light centre (> 0) ellipticity_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of ellipticity components (> 0) shear_sd number 0.05 – Prior sd of the shear components (> 0) light_size_medians list of any [0.5, 1.5] – Prior medians of the lens-light half-light radii (min items 2, max items 2) source_size_median number 0.2 – Prior median source radius (> 0) source_offset_sd number 0.3 – Prior sd of the source position (> 0) noise_scale_log_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of log noise scale (> 0) theta_e_start number (optional) null – Start the optimisation at this Einstein radius instead of the radius of the ring found in the light-subtracted image n_starts integer 5 – Starts of the full-model optimisation (source positions) (≥ 1, ≤ 9) max_iter integer 3000 – Iterations per optimisation (≥ 10, ≤ 100000) source_grid integer 30 – Source-plane grid side (pixels) (≥ 4, ≤ 128) source_half_width number 0.45 – Half-width of the source-plane grid (arcsec) (> 0) curve_points integer 128 – Points per critical curve (≥ 16, ≤ 2048) curve_draws integer 100 – Posterior draws with cached critical curves (≥ 1, ≤ 2000) z_lens number (optional) null – Lens redshift (for the mass) z_source number (optional) null – Source redshift (for the mass) h0 number 70.0 – Hubble constant (km/s/Mpc) (> 0) omega_m number 0.3 – Matter density (flat LCDM) (> 0, < 1) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "use_mask": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    },
    "psf_source": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "auto",
        "tree"
      ],
      "default": "auto"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "description": "Image rows (row 0 at the bottom)"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "description": "Image columns"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "image": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow",
        "description": "Surface brightness of each pixel (for example electrons/s)"
      },
      "weight": {
        "dims": [
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "weight",
        "description": "Inverse variance of each pixel; 0 leaves the pixel out"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "psf_source": "auto"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "psf_row": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "description": "Rows of the PSF kernel"
          },
          "psf_col": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "description": "Columns of the PSF kernel"
          }
        },
        "vars": {
          "psf": {
            "dims": [
              "psf_row",
              "psf_col"
            ],
            "dtype": "float64",
            "role": "constant",
            "description": "The point-spread function (odd sides, centred)"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "use_mask": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "vars": {
          "mask": {
            "dims": [
              "row",
              "col"
            ],
            "dtype": "bool",
            "role": "mask",
            "description": "True where the pixel is used in the fit"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: sci.traction_force
docs.text:
Traction force microscopy: recovers the 2-D traction field under a cell from the displacement field of the gel. A Gaussian prior in Fourier space (white, squared exponential or Matern spectrum); NUTS on the hyperparameters with the field integrated out, then exact posterior draws of the field.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the likelihood is a potential over Fourier modes of the whole raster; pixels are not conditionally independent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.vector_field Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description traction (component, row, col) Pa Joint posterior draws of the traction field displacement_hat (component, row, col) of displacement Displacement of each traction draw (expected), plus noise (predictive) strain_energy () fJ Elastic energy the cell put into the gel, inside the force mask contractility () uN Sum of the forces towards the force epicentre, inside the mask

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description grid_um number 1.0 – Grid spacing of the displacement raster (um) (> 0) young_pa number 10000.0 – Young's modulus of the gel (Pa) (> 0) poisson number 0.49 – Poisson ratio of the gel (≥ 0, < 0.5) young_cv number 0.0 – Relative uncertainty of Young's modulus (lognormal sd); 0 = known exactly (≥ 0, ≤ 1) prior white or smooth or matern matern – Prior spectrum of the tractions: white (Tikhonov), smooth (squared exponential) or matern ((1 + k^2 l^2)^-alpha) noise_um number 0.01 – Prior median of the noise sd (um) (> 0) traction_pa number 300.0 – Prior median of the traction scale (Pa) (> 0) lengthscale_um number 5.0 – Prior median of the length scale (um; smooth and matern) (> 0) field_draws integer 100 – Traction fields drawn per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) force_mask boolean false – The data has a force_mask(row, col) variable: strain energy and contractility are summed inside it (else over the whole grid) Input data contract (schema template)

  "params": {
    "force_mask": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "component": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "displacement": {
        "dims": [
          "component",
          "row",
          "col"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "description": "Displacement of the gel surface (x and y components)"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "force_mask": true
      },
      "merge": {
        "vars": {
          "force_mask": {
            "dims": [
              "row",
              "col"
            ],
            "dtype": "bool",
            "role": "mask",
            "description": "Region that strain energy and contractility cover"

docs.title: sci.turing_pattern
docs.text:
Turing patterns: recovers the reaction and diffusion rates of a Schnakenberg activator-substrate system from early images of a growing pattern. The likelihood is exact for the linearised dynamics (independent complex Gaussian Fourier modes, a Woodbury identity per wavenumber). Gives the dispersion relation, the pattern wavelength, P(Turing conditions hold) and simulated patterns from a spectral solver.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map, sci.ppc_image_grid, sci.profile_bands Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description pattern (t, y, x) of activator Activator field at the requested times: a draw given the fitted images (predict), or a new pattern from the nonlinear solver (simulate) settled (y, x) of activator Simulate only: the pattern of each run at settle_time growth (wavenumber) 1/time Dispersion relation: growth rate Re lambda(k) of a mode with wavenumber k p_turing () probability 1 when the Turing conditions hold for the draw (the mean is the probability) wavelength () length Wavelength 2 pi / k_m of the fastest-growing mode turing_space (b_supply, a_supply) probability 1 where the supply rates (a, b) are Turing unstable at the draw's diffusion ratio (the mean is P(Turing))

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description box_length number 100.0 – Side of the square image in the length unit of the model (the activator diffuses with D = 1 in these units) (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0) k2_max number 1.5 – Use only the Fourier modes with |k|^2 below this value; faster modes have decayed below the camera noise (x-ui-level: basic) (> 0) max_extension integer 2 – Image times a prediction may reach past the last fitted time (the linear theory holds only while the pattern is small) (≥ 0, ≤ 100) d_median number 10.0 – Prior median of the diffusion ratio d (> 0) d_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of d (> 0) initial_noise_median number 0.001 – Prior median of the initial noise sd s0 (> 0) camera_noise_median number 0.001 – Prior median of the camera noise sd sigma (> 0) field_draws integer 40 – Posterior draws per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) simulate_draws integer 4 – Nonlinear simulations per simulate score (each one is a full PDE run) (≥ 1, ≤ 200) simulate_dt number (optional) null – Time step of the spectral solver in simulate (default: min(0.025, 0.1 / (g (1 + s^2)))) settle_time number 300.0 – Time of the settled pattern in simulate (> 0, ≤ 5000.0) wavenumber_max number 1.2 – Largest wavenumber of the dispersion relation output (> 0) wavenumber_points integer 120 – Points of the dispersion relation output (≥ 10, ≤ 2000) a_max number 0.6 – Largest supply rate a of the Turing-space map (> 0) b_max number 3.0 – Largest supply rate b of the Turing-space map (> 0) supply_points integer 60 – Grid points along a and b of the Turing-space map (≥ 5, ≤ 300) precondition boolean true – Sample a parameterisation whitened at the posterior mode (Laplace approximation); the model is the same. False samples the notebook's parameters directly (needs a long warm-up, for example tune 1500) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 2
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "float",
        "policy": "extend",
        "ordered": true,
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}",
        "description": "Time since the uniform state was perturbed"
      },
      "y": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel row"
      },
      "x": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Pixel column"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "activator": {
        "dims": [
          "t",
          "y",
          "x"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "description": "Activator concentration in each pixel (early, small pattern)"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: sklearn.tabular_bootstrap
docs.text:
Tabular regression with a bootstrap ensemble: one joint draw per replicate, so any aggregation is valid.

Version 1.0.0 Inference bootstrap Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators provide no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time, ml.feature_importance Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (chain, draw) – Bootstrap draws of the prediction over the row dims contributions (chain, draw, component) – Per-replicate feature contributions, in model space

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description estimator LinearRegressionChoice or RidgeChoice or LassoChoice or ElasticNetChoice or QuantileRegressorChoice or LogisticRegressionChoice or RandomForestRegressorChoice or RandomForestClassifierChoice or GradientBoostingRegressorChoice or HistGradientBoostingRegressorChoice or XGBRegressorChoice or XGBClassifierChoice or HistGradientBoostingClassifierChoice or LGBMClassifierChoice or CatBoostClassifierChoice required – target string y – rows list of string required – min items 1, max items 8 time_dim string time – time_kind time or integer or index or none time – columns ColumnsSettings – – coord_features map of category or onehot or ordinal or numeric – – new_levels pooled or zero or error pooled – pooled_max_levels integer 256 – ≥ 1, ≤ 10000 weight string (optional) null – mask string (optional) null – forecast_strategy direct or recursive direct – retransform median or smearing median – n_jobs integer 1 – ≥ 1, ≤ 64 uncertainty BootstrapUncertainty – – contributions none or auto or exact or zeroing auto – Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "index"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "index",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: ConformalUncertainty
docs.text:
Split-conformal prediction intervals (representation interval, never draws). A calibration fraction of the training rows is held out (the most recent periods of time_dim for calibration_by: last, a seeded random subset for random); the interval is point ± q where q is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest absolute calibration residual. refit refits the point model on all rows afterwards (sharper, but the finite-sample guarantee then only holds approximately).

docs.title: sklearn.tabular_regressor
docs.text:
Tabular regression with an allow-listed scikit-learn or xgboost estimator: rows are stacked from labelled dims, predictions are point estimates (with exact linear or counterfactual-zeroing contributions).

Version 1.0.0 Inference point Representation point Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators provide no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time, ml.feature_importance Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat () – Prediction of the target over the row dims (settings.rows) contributions (component) – Per-feature contributions (exact for linear estimators, counterfactual zeroing otherwise), in model space

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description estimator LinearRegressionChoice or RidgeChoice or LassoChoice or ElasticNetChoice or QuantileRegressorChoice or LogisticRegressionChoice or RandomForestRegressorChoice or RandomForestClassifierChoice or GradientBoostingRegressorChoice or HistGradientBoostingRegressorChoice or XGBRegressorChoice or XGBClassifierChoice or HistGradientBoostingClassifierChoice or LGBMClassifierChoice or CatBoostClassifierChoice required – target string y – rows list of string required – min items 1, max items 8 time_dim string time – time_kind time or integer or index or none time – columns ColumnsSettings – – coord_features map of category or onehot or ordinal or numeric – – new_levels pooled or zero or error pooled – pooled_max_levels integer 256 – ≥ 1, ≤ 10000 weight string (optional) null – mask string (optional) null – forecast_strategy direct or recursive direct – retransform median or smearing median – n_jobs integer 1 – ≥ 1, ≤ 64 uncertainty NoUncertainty – – contributions none or auto or exact or zeroing auto – Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template)

      "type": "string",

      "type": "string",

A hierarchical generalised linear model in long layout: group intercepts (and optional slopes) partially pooled towards a population mean that may depend on group-level covariates. Unseen groups are drawn from the fitted hyperprior.

statsmodels VECM (Johansen maximum likelihood) for trending series tied together in the long run; the cointegration rank comes from the Johansen trace or max-eigenvalue test unless set; stores alpha/beta, the rank test table, impulse responses, FEVD and Granger tests.

Version 1.0.0 Inference point Representation quantiles Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: statsmodels estimates are maximum-likelihood or least-squares point estimates without posterior draws; use holdout or backtest metrics instead of LOO Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (t) of y Prediction-interval quantiles of y: one-step-ahead inside the fitted range, a multi-step forecast after it

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description exog list of string – basic Driver variables (prices, promotions, holidays) whose future values are supplied for forecasts (max items 64) series_dims list of string – basic Panel dims (geo, product, ...): one model per series cell. Empty for a single series. (max items 4) quantiles list of number – advanced Quantiles of the prediction intervals (must include 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95) (min items 3, max items 16) time_kind time or integer time advanced Whether the time index holds dates ('time') or period numbers ('integer') irf_horizon integer 12 – Periods of the impulse responses and the variance decomposition (≥ 1, ≤ 60) k_ar_diff integer 1 – Lagged differences in each equation (≥ 0, ≤ 12) coint_rank integer (optional) null – Number of long-run relationships; leave empty to take it from the Johansen test rank_test trace or maxeig trace – Johansen test statistic rank_signif number 0.05 – Significance of the rank test: 0.01, 0.05 or 0.1 deterministic n or co or ci or lo or li or cili or colo ci – Constant/trend: n none, co outside / ci inside the long-run relation, lo/li linear trend outside/inside, combinations Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "series_dims": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "exog": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{*series_dims as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "variable": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "variable",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "forbid"
      },
      "{*exog as x}": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "t": {
            "kind": "integer"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The authorization rules of the platform, generated from mapi_spec.tenancy and mapi_spec.tokens by scripts/gen_docs_platform.py. Every component (the API, the web app through OpenAPI, the tests) checks the same table. The Administration guide explains how to use it.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Roles are ordered viewer < editor < runner < admin; each includes the one before it. tenant-wide means only a tenant-wide membership grants it; otherwise the effective role in the project counts (the higher of the tenant-wide and the project grant). A pair that is not listed is denied to everyone.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Platform operators (verified e-mails in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in; never through an API token) hold exactly these permissions, on every tenant: audit read, billing read, catalog read, executor read, executor update, kill_switch read, kill_switch update, member read, project read, quota delete, quota read, quota update, run read, tenant_deletion manage, tenant_deletion read, tenant_member read, tenant create, tenant delete, tenant manage, tenant read, token read, usage read. None of them reads tenant content: datasets, specs, models or plots.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A capability is granted on top of a role, per project membership; project admins hold every capability implicitly. A rule that needs one says so in the roles table ("✓ with reviewer").

Capability Needed for What it allows reviewer model approve Approve or reject model validations that wait for a second person (POST /v1/validations/{id}/approvals), never the member's own submissions (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and never through an API token. Granted per project membership (capabilities on the membership, or the Reviewer column of Members); viewers cannot hold it.

docs.title: Token scopes
docs.text:
A token acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes: both the owner's role and a scope must allow an action. admin covers everything the owner's role allows; score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:* every endpoint of the project).

docs.title: Plot recipes catalog
docs.text:
Generated from every recipe installed through the mapi.plots entry point. Name them in a spec's outputs.plots. See Plots for how to use them. Each picture is the recipe drawn on synthetic example data, as the app's catalog shows it.

Recipe Version Title What it shows Persona Needs groups Needs representation causal.donor_weights 1.0.0 Donor weights Shows which markets the model uses to make a copy of each treated market. A large weight means that the copy follows that market closely. both donor_weights any causal.event_study 1.0.0 Effect by period since the start Shows the effect in each period before and after the start. Before the start the effects must be near zero, else the comparison groups were already different. both event_study any causal.impact 1.0.0 Effect of the intervention Shows the actual values beside the values that the model expects without the campaign, launch or test. The difference is the effect, per period and in total. both impact any causal.pre_fit 1.0.0 Fit before the intervention Shows how well the model follows the actual values before the start. If it does not follow them, do not trust the effect after the start. both impact any core.calibration 1.0.0 Calibration Checks if the ranges and probabilities that the model predicts agree with how often things happen in your data. A line inside the band, or dots on the diagonal, show a well-calibrated model. expert observed_data draws, point core.confusion 1.0.0 Confusion matrix Counts the cases that the model classifies correctly and incorrectly, for a binary or multiclass target. For yes/no, the four boxes are the true and false positives and the true and false negatives at one probability threshold. both – draws, point core.convergence 1.0.0 Sampler convergence Checks that the fitting method found stable answers for each model parameter. Red points and a 'check' status show the parameters that you must not trust yet. expert posterior draws core.counterfactual 1.0.0 Scenario vs baseline Compares a 'what if' scenario with the baseline over time. It also shows how sure the model is about the total difference. both – any core.data_overview 1.0.0 Data overview Shows each column of your data over time, where values are missing and how much data each group has. Use it before you fit a model. both – any core.decision_distribution 1.0.0 Decision outcome Shows the range of results for each option of a decision. It also gives the probability that each option is the best. both – draws core.decomposition 1.0.0 Decomposition Splits the outcome into the parts that the model adds together, such as a baseline and each driver. It shows each part over time and its total share. both contributions any core.energy 1.0.0 Sampler energy Checks if the fitting method can move through all of the possible values of the model, including the extreme ones. A red bar shows a chain with a problem. expert sample_stats draws core.fit_vs_actual 1.0.0 Predicted vs actual Puts each prediction of the model next to the actual value in a scatter plot. Dots on the dashed diagonal line are perfect predictions. both – any core.loo_pit 1.0.0 LOO-PIT and Pareto k Checks each actual value against the predictions of the model when that value is left out of the fit. It also finds the values that have too much effect for this check to be reliable. expert log_likelihood draws core.loss_curve 1.0.0 Loss curve Shows the loss of a fit that runs in steps, such as ADVI, at each step. A flat curve at the end shows that more steps will not make the fit better. expert – any core.model_comparison 1.0.0 Model comparison Ranks two or more models by how well they are expected to predict new data. It shows how far each model is from the best one and how sure that difference is. expert – any core.pair 1.0.0 Pair plot Shows the draws of each pair of model parameters as a cloud of points, with a histogram of each parameter. Red points mark draws where the fitting method had problems. expert posterior draws core.posterior_forest 1.0.0 Posterior forest Shows the estimate and the range of each model parameter as a row with a dot and two lines. Rows whose range does not include zero have a clear direction. expert posterior draws core.ppc 1.0.0 Posterior predictive check Compares data that the fitted model makes with your actual data. It shows if the ranges of the model are too narrow, too wide or shifted. expert posterior_predictive, observed_data draws core.ppc_fan 1.0.0 Fit and forecast Shows the model's estimate over time as a line with shaded ranges, and the actual values as dots. A dashed line marks where the training data ends and the forecast starts. both – any core.prior_posterior 1.0.0 Prior and posterior Shows, for each parameter, the values that the model allowed before it saw the data and the values after the fit. Parameters that the data moved most come first. expert prior, posterior draws core.prior_predictive 1.0.0 Prior predictive check Shows data that the model can make before it sees your data, next to your data. Use it to check that your starting assumptions give values of the right size. expert prior_predictive any core.rank_matrix 1.0.0 Rank matrix Shows how likely each item is to have each place in a ranking, and how likely each item is to be above each other item. Use it when the order of items matters more than their values. both – draws core.residuals_over_time 1.0.0 Residuals over time Shows the error of the model (actual minus predicted) for each point in time. The errors should stay near the zero line with no pattern. expert – any core.ridge 1.0.0 Ridgeline Shows a curve of the possible values for each group, such as each school or each region, one above the other and sorted by the average. Use it to compare many groups at once. both – draws core.roc_pr 1.0.0 ROC and precision-recall curves Shows how well the predicted probabilities separate the yes cases from the no cases at all thresholds, for a binary or multiclass target. A curve near the top-left corner (ROC) or the top-right corner (precision-recall) shows a good separation. both – draws, point core.state_sequence 1.0.0 State sequence Shows your data over time above the probability of each hidden state, such as a calm or a busy period. Use it to see when the state changes and how sure the model is. both – any ml.confusion_epochs 1.0.0 Confusion matrix over epochs Shows the confusion matrix of the validation data at some epochs of the training. You can see which classes the network learns first and which classes it confuses to the end. expert – any ml.feature_importance 1.0.0 Feature importance Ranks the inputs that a tabular model uses most. For a linear model it shows the size and the direction of each input's effect. expert – any ml.misclassified 1.0.0 Wrong validation images Shows the validation images that the network classifies incorrectly, with the true class, the predicted class and its probability. Look at them to find wrong labels or classes that look the same. both – any ml.training_curves 1.0.0 Training curves Shows the loss and the accuracy of a neural network on the training data and on the validation data while it learns. When the validation loss goes up and the training loss goes down, the network starts to overfit. both – any mmm.adstock 1.0.0 Carry-over of the effect Shows how the effect of one unit of spend spreads over the weeks after the spend, for each channel. It also shows the average delay of the effect. both adstock any mmm.budget_plans 1.0.0 Budget plan comparison Compares budget plans side by side: how each plan splits the spend and what outcome each plan is expected to bring. It also shows the change from a reference plan. both plans draws mmm.cross_effects 1.0.0 Effects between outcomes Shows how a change in one outcome goes with a change in another outcome, for each pair that the model links. For example, more sales of a premium product can go with more sales of a basic product. both cross_effects any mmm.decomposition 1.0.0 Contribution by component Splits sales (or another KPI) into the baseline and the part from each marketing channel. It shows each part over time and its total share. both contributions any mmm.effectiveness 1.0.0 Effect of spend over time Shows the effect of one unit of spend in each period, for the channels whose effect can change over time. Use it to see if a channel becomes stronger or weaker. both effectiveness any mmm.lift_tests 1.0.0 Lift tests and the model Compares the result of each lift test with the value that the calibrated model gives for the same channel, period and market. It shows the tests that the model does not agree with. both lift_tests any mmm.marginal_cost 1.0.0 Marginal cost Shows what the next unit of outcome costs in each channel at each level of spend. It can also show the return of the next unit of spend. both response_curves any mmm.mediation 1.0.0 Direct and mediated effects Shows how much of the effect of each channel comes directly and how much comes through a mediator, such as site visits or brand awareness. both mediation any mmm.prior_beliefs 1.0.0 Your beliefs and the priors Compares the range that you gave for each channel with the values that the model allows before it sees your sales. Use it to check that the model understood your beliefs. guided prior_beliefs any mmm.response_curves 1.0.0 Response curves Shows how much outcome each channel brings for each level of spend. A curve that becomes flat shows that more spend in that channel adds little. both response_curves any mmm.roi 1.0.0 ROI and marginal ROI Shows the return of each channel for each unit of its current spend, and the return of the next unit of spend. A dashed line marks the point where a channel pays back its spend. both response_curves any mmm.spend_effect 1.0.0 Share of spend and share of effect Compares the share of the media budget that each channel gets with its share of the effect of all channels. A channel with a larger share of effect than of spend returns more than the average channel. both response_curves any mmm.waterfall 1.0.0 Contribution waterfall Shows how the baseline and each channel add up, step by step, to the total KPI of the period. The last bar is the total. both contributions any net.graph 1.0.0 Network graph Shows a network as dots joined by lines, where thick lines are strong links. A second panel shows every pair of nodes as a grid of colours. both – any sci.area_map 1.0.0 Area map Shows a map of areas, such as districts, coloured by the model's estimate for each area. Other panels show the uncertainty and how likely it is that the value is above a limit. both – any sci.ensemble 1.0.0 Ensemble of draws Shows many possible paths from the model as thin lines, with a shaded range and the actual values. Use it to see what single outcomes can look like, not only the average. both – any sci.field_map 1.0.0 Field map Shows a map of a value that the model estimates on a grid, such as a density over an area. One panel shows the average and another panel shows where the model is not sure. both – any sci.image_residuals 1.0.0 Image residuals Shows the observed image, the image that the model expects and the difference between them. A pattern in the difference shows something that the model misses. both observed_data any sci.phylogeny 1.0.0 Phylogeny with tip estimates Shows a family tree of species next to the model's estimate for each species. Close relatives sit side by side, so you can see if related species have similar values. both – any sci.point_pattern 1.0.0 Point pattern Shows points, such as events or light sources, at their positions on a map or an image. A ring around each point shows where its true position can be. both – any sci.power_spectrum 1.0.0 Power spectrum Shows how much signal there is at each scale or frequency, as the model sees it, with shaded ranges and the measured points. expert – any sci.ppc_image_grid 1.0.0 Predictive image grid Shows the observed image next to a few images that the model makes. If the model fits, it is difficult to tell which image is the real one. both observed_data any sci.profile_bands 1.0.0 Profiles with bands Shows the model's estimate along one dimension, such as distance, with shaded ranges. It draws one curve for each level of a second dimension, such as time. both – any sci.rose 1.0.0 Rose of angles Shows directions or times of day on a circle. Bars show how often each direction occurs, with the range that the model expects for each sector. both – any sci.swatches 1.0.0 Colour swatches Shows squares in the colours that the model gives to each item, next to the measured colours. Squares that change from draw to draw show where the model is not sure. both – any sci.vector_field 1.0.0 Vector field Shows a field of arrows, such as forces or flows, on a grid. Colours show the length of the arrow in each cell and a second panel shows where the length is not certain. both – any

docs.title: Donor weights
docs.text:
causal.donor_weights@1.0.0

Shows which markets the model uses to make a copy of each treated market. A large weight means that the copy follows that market closely.

How to read it. The copy of geo_03 uses three donors: geo_00 (39%), geo_04 (30%) and geo_06 (17%). The other donors have small weights. If geo_00 had a campaign of its own, the copy is not correct.

Use it when

  • You ran a geo test and want to know which markets make the comparison
  • A result looks strange and you want to find a donor that is not a good match

Avoid it when

  • The model is not a synthetic control
  • You want to see the effect (use Effect of the intervention)

What it needs

  • A donor_weights group from causal.synthetic_control: the weight of each donor for each treated unit as draws

What is on the chart

  • One bar for each donor with the mean weight, from the largest to the smallest
  • A line for the 90% range of each weight
  • One row for the donors that are not in the top 15, added together
  • One panel for each treated unit, up to 4 units
For experts

Reads weight(sample, unit, donor) (or chain/draw) and pre_rmse(unit), attr prior (simplex: Dirichlet; horseshoe: unconstrained). Bars are posterior means, rules HDIs at hdi_prob (0.9). Donors are ranked by |mean|; the first top (15) are shown and the rest are summed per draw. unit selects one treated unit; without it up to 4 units get a panel each, else the first unit is shown.

docs.title: Effect by period since the start
docs.text:
causal.event_study@1.0.0

Shows the effect in each period before and after the start. Before the start the effects must be near zero, else the comparison groups were already different.

How to read it. The effect is near zero in the four periods before the start, so there is no sign of different trends. After the start it grows from +2 to +5 units. The average effect after the start is +3.6 (90% interval 3.3 to 4.0).

Use it when

  • Stores or markets started the treatment at different times
  • You want to see if the effect grows, stays or goes away after the start
  • You want to do a check of the trends before the start

Avoid it when

  • The model is not a difference-in-differences model
  • Only one unit got the treatment (use a synthetic control)

What it needs

  • An event_study group from causal.did: the effect of each period relative to the start as draws, and the average effect after the start

What is on the chart

  • A dot for the median effect in each period and a line for its 90% range
  • A zero line and a dashed red line at the start
  • A caption with the average effect after the start and a check of the trends before the start
For experts

Reads coef(sample, event_time) (the reference period is exactly 0), n_cells(event_time) and att(sample), attrs reference (-1), binned and design (did: event times -1 and 0 only). Dots are medians and rules HDIs at hdi_prob (0.9). The pre-trend check flags each lead whose HDI excludes 0. With staggered adoption a two-way fixed effects event study can mix the effects of early and late units (Goodman-Bacon 2021; Sun and Abraham 2021).

docs.title: Effect of the intervention
docs.text:
causal.impact@1.0.0

Shows the actual values beside the values that the model expects without the campaign, launch or test. The difference is the effect, per period and in total.

How to read it. In the 4 weeks of the campaign the total effect is +28 units (90% interval 19 to 36). This is +7% of the sales without the campaign. The probability that the effect is above zero is 100%, so you can report the effect.

Use it when

  • You ran a campaign, a launch or a test and want to know what it added
  • You want to show the effect and its range to other people
  • You want to see when the effect started and if it stopped after the end

Avoid it when

  • The model did not follow the period before the start (look at Fit before the intervention first)
  • Other changes started at the same time as the intervention

What it needs

  • An impact group from a causal model (causal.impact, causal.synthetic_control or causal.did): the actual values, the values without the intervention as draws, and the cells of the effect window

What is on the chart

  • Three panels with the same time axis: the actual values and the values without the intervention with their 90% range, the effect per period, and the cumulative effect in the effect window
  • A red line at the start and a dashed red line at the end
  • A caption with the total effect, its range, the relative effect and the probability that the effect is above zero
For experts

Reads the impact group: actual([unit,] time), counterfactual(sample, [unit,] time) (predictive draws, observation noise included), effect and post([unit,] time), with attrs intervention_start and intervention_end. Lines are medians and bands HDIs at hdi_prob (0.9). unit selects one treated unit; without it the draws are summed over units. The cumulative effect is recomputed per draw as the cumulative sum of effect over the post cells (per unit for staggered adoption). The total is its last value, the relative effect the total divided by the summed counterfactual of the post cells. panels selects series, pointwise and cumulative.

docs.title: Fit before the intervention
docs.text:
causal.pre_fit@1.0.0

Shows how well the model follows the actual values before the start. If it does not follow them, do not trust the effect after the start.

How to read it. Before the start, the typical difference is 1.9 units and 100% of the actual values are inside the band. The model follows the history, so you can use it after the start. With 60% inside, add controls or use a longer history.

Use it when

  • You want to know if you can trust the effect of a campaign or a test
  • You want to compare two sets of controls or donors

Avoid it when

  • The data has no period before the start
  • You want to see the effect itself (use Effect of the intervention)

What it needs

  • An impact group from a causal model with some periods before the start

What is on the chart

  • The actual values before the start as dots (red when they are outside the band)
  • The median and the 90% range of the model without the intervention
  • A caption with the typical difference (RMSE), the mean percentage error (MAPE) and the share of actual values inside the band
For experts

The pre-period is the cells before the first post cell that are in no effect window. RMSE and MAPE compare actual with the mean of counterfactual per period. Coverage is the share of finite actual values inside the HDI at hdi_prob (0.9); the caption flags coverage below 80%. For causal.impact the pre-period values are one-step-ahead predictions, for synthetic control the synthetic copy and for DiD the fitted values without the treatment terms. unit as in causal.impact.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
core.calibration@1.0.0

Checks if the ranges and probabilities that the model predicts agree with how often things happen in your data. A line inside the band, or dots on the diagonal, show a well-calibrated model.

How to read it. The line goes above the band near 0 and below it near 1: too many actual values are in the tails. The predicted ranges of the model are too narrow.

Use it when

  • You want a sharper check of the predicted ranges than the PIT histogram
  • You predict a yes/no outcome and want to know if a 70% prediction comes true about 70% of the time
  • You fitted a classifier that gives one probability for each row, without draws

Avoid it when

  • You have no actual values to compare with
  • You have only a few observations (fewer than about 30)

What it needs

  • Predictions with draws (posterior_predictive or predictions group), or one predicted probability for each cell for a yes/no outcome
  • The actual values (observed_data or observed group)

What is on the chart

  • For numbers: the PIT-ECDF difference with a 95% band that holds at all points together
  • For yes/no outcomes: a reliability diagram with a band for each group and a histogram of the predicted probabilities
  • Red points where the line or a group is outside its band
  • A caption with the verdict, and the Brier score for yes/no outcomes
For experts

Continuous: PIT = P(ŷ < y) + ½ P(ŷ = y); the line is ECDF(z) − z on a grid of min(max(n, 20), 200) points. The simultaneous envelope at prob (0.95) is ±c·sqrt(z(1−z)/n) with c the prob quantile of the largest standardised deviation over the grid in n_sim (1000) simulated uniform samples (cumulative multinomial counts, seed). Binary (auto when y ∈ {0, 1} and the draws are in [0, 1]): bins (10) equal-width bins of the mean prediction; each band is the binomial range p ± z·sqrt(p(1−p)/n_bin); the expected calibration error weights |observed − predicted| by bin size. A point prediction (no sample dims, values in [0, 1], for example the y_hat of an sklearn classifier) takes the binary path with the probability as the mean; var and observed_var pick the pair. A point prediction of a target that is not 0/1 is an error, because the PIT check needs draws.

docs.title: Confusion matrix
docs.text:
core.confusion@1.0.0

Counts the cases that the model classifies correctly and incorrectly, for a binary or multiclass target. For yes/no, the four boxes are the true and false positives and the true and false negatives at one probability threshold.

How to read it. At the threshold 0.5, the model finds 62 of the 80 positive cases (recall 0.78). 25 of its 87 alarms are false (precision 0.71). With the threshold auto, the threshold goes down to 0.31. The recall goes up to 0.9 and the precision goes down to 0.6.

Use it when

  • You must change the probabilities into yes/no decisions and want to see the errors
  • You want the precision, the recall and the specificity at one threshold
  • You want to explain the errors of a classifier to people who do not read models

Avoid it when

  • You want to see all thresholds (use ROC and precision-recall curves)

What it needs

  • Predicted probabilities of the positive class, with draws or one value for each cell (posterior_predictive, predictions or draws group, or a score summary)
  • The actual 0/1 values (observed_data or observed group)

What is on the chart

  • A 2 × 2 matrix of the actual class against the predicted class, with counts or with the share of each actual class
  • For a multiclass target: a K × K matrix of the most probable class (up to 30 classes; the other classes are put together), with the accuracy and the macro F1
  • A caption with the accuracy, the precision, the recall (sensitivity), the specificity, the F1 score and the threshold
For experts

threshold is a number (default 0.5) or 'auto': the threshold that maximises Youden's J = TPR − FPR over the distinct predicted probabilities. normalize='true' divides each row (actual class) by its count; 'none' shows counts. Precision = TP/(TP+FP), recall = TP/(TP+FN), specificity = TN/(TN+FP), F1 = 2PR/(P+R). positive, var and observed_var work as in ROC and precision-recall curves. Multiclass: the predicted class is the argmax of the class probabilities; threshold and positive are not used (the caption says so).

docs.title: Sampler convergence
docs.text:
core.convergence@1.0.0

Checks that the fitting method found stable answers for each model parameter. Red points and a 'check' status show the parameters that you must not trust yet.

How to read it. beta[tv] has R-hat 1.8 and its two trace lines stay at different levels: the chains disagree. The rank plot is not flat. Run the sampler longer or change the model before you use beta[tv]. The caption also reports 3 divergent transitions.

Use it when

  • You fitted a Bayesian model and want to know if you can use it
  • Results change from run to run

Avoid it when

  • The model is not fitted with draws (such as a least-squares model)
  • You want to know if the model is correct (a converged model can still be wrong)

What it needs

  • A fitted Bayesian model with draws in chains (the posterior group)
  • Optional: sample_stats with the divergence flags

What is on the chart

  • A dot for R-hat of each parameter with a red limit line
  • A dot for the effective sample size of each parameter with a limit line
  • A table of the worst parameters
  • Trace lines and rank plots of the worst parameters
  • A caption with the number of problems and divergent transitions
For experts

Rank-normalised split R-hat (max of bulk and folded), bulk and tail ESS, per parameter element. A row is 'check' when R-hat > rhat_threshold (default 1.01) or min(bulk, tail ESS) < ess_per_chain × chains (default 100 per chain). Sorted by R-hat; max_parameters (40) dots, table_rows (15) table rows, max_traces (6) traces and rank histograms (bins, default 20; flat = well mixed). max_elements (2000) caps the elements checked. Divergences come from sample_stats.diverging.

docs.title: Scenario vs baseline
docs.text:
core.counterfactual@1.0.0

Compares a 'what if' scenario with the baseline over time. It also shows how sure the model is about the total difference.

How to read it. The scenario line is above the baseline every week. The histogram of the total change is from 40 to 80, all above zero. The caption says that the probability of an increase is 100%.

Use it when

  • You changed an input, such as spend or price, and want to see the effect
  • You want the probability that the scenario does better

Avoid it when

  • You compare more than one scenario (use Decision outcome)
  • The scenario is far outside the data that the model saw

What it needs

  • A scenario score: scenario draws (or summary) and baseline draws (or summary)
  • Optional: delta draws (scenario minus baseline) for the total difference

What is on the chart

  • Two lines with 90% bands: the scenario and the baseline
  • A histogram of the total change, with its mean and a 90% range
  • A caption with the change and the probability of an increase
For experts

Bands are equal-tailed quantiles of the draws summed over hidden dims; summary inputs use their interval statistics. The total change sums the delta draws over all dims (or scenario − baseline when both have draws); the histogram uses bins (default 30) and the range is an HDI at hdi_prob. When only summaries exist, the chart shows the difference of the means with no uncertainty.

docs.title: Data overview
docs.text:
core.data_overview@1.0.0

Shows each column of your data over time, where values are missing and how much data each group has. Use it before you fit a model.

How to read it. The revenue panel has a gap in week 4 for 'north'. The heatmap shows that search spend is missing for the first four weeks in 'east'. Fix or fill these values before you fit the model.

Use it when

  • You uploaded a dataset and want a first look
  • You want to find gaps, spikes or groups with little data

Avoid it when

  • Your data has no numeric columns
  • You want a plot of model results

What it needs

  • A dataset, or the observed_data, data or constant_data group of a run

What is on the chart

  • One panel for each column with a line for each group
  • A heatmap of the share of missing values over time
  • Bars of the number of values in each group
  • A caption with the column that has most missing values
For experts

The time dim is detected (or along); the colour dim is a small categorical dim (facet, at most max_levels levels). Other dims are summed with min_count=1. The heatmap is the mean of isnull() over the other dims. Group sizes count non-null values of the first variable. vars and max_vars pick columns; above max_rows the x values are thinned evenly.

docs.title: Decision outcome
docs.text:
core.decision_distribution@1.0.0

Shows the range of results for each option of a decision. It also gives the probability that each option is the best.

How to read it. 'shift_tv' has the highest curve and a 64% probability to be the best. Its range overlaps with 'cut_search', so the choice is not certain. 'keep' is best in only 8% of the draws.

Use it when

  • You choose between a few options, such as budget splits
  • You want to see the risk of each option, not only its average

Avoid it when

  • The result has more than one value for each option (sum it first)
  • You have no draws, only averages

What it needs

  • A decision group with draws of one result for each option (an option dimension)

What is on the chart

  • Smooth curves of the results of each option
  • A dot and a 90% range for each option
  • Bars of the probability that each option is the best
  • A caption that names the best option
For experts

Needs sample draws (chain/draw or sample). Densities are KDEs on a shared grid from the 0.5th to the 99.5th percentile; ranges are HDIs at hdi_prob. P(best) is the share of draws where the option has the highest (or lowest, with higher_is_better false) value, which needs the options to share draws. candidate names the option dim (default: the only extra dim); max_candidates caps it at 12.

docs.title: Decomposition
docs.text:
core.decomposition@1.0.0

Splits the outcome into the parts that the model adds together, such as a baseline and each driver. It shows each part over time and its total share.

How to read it. The baseline gives 85% of revenue, TV 10% and search 5%. The 90% range of search includes zero, so the model is not sure that search adds anything.

Use it when

  • You want to know how much each part of the model explains
  • You want to explain the result to people who do not read models

Avoid it when

  • Your model does not add its parts together
  • Some parts are negative and large (a stacked area is then hard to read)

What it needs

  • A contributions, decomposition or components group with one variable or label for each part, over time

What is on the chart

  • Stacked areas of each part over time
  • Bars of the total contribution of each part with a 90% range
  • A caption with the share of the top parts, and the parts that can be zero
For experts

Components are the labels of a component dim (component, default the first of component/channel/contribution/term/effect) plus whole variables without it. The area uses the mean over draws per time; the bar uses the mean of each draw's total with an HDI at hdi_prob (default 0.9). Shares are of the summed means. max_components caps the parts (default 20). Groups: contributions, decomposition, then components (the unobserved-components and ETS states, the HSGP trend and seasonality). A variable with attr decomposition='exclude' (the UC and ETS slope state, which is a rate and not an additive part) is skipped unless vars names it.

docs.title: Sampler energy
docs.text:
core.energy@1.0.0

Checks if the fitting method can move through all of the possible values of the model, including the extreme ones. A red bar shows a chain with a problem.

How to read it. The E-BFMI of chain 1 is 0.19, below 0.3. The blue histogram is much narrower than the grey one. The sampler does not reach the tails, so make the priors narrower or change the parameterisation.

Use it when

  • You fitted a Bayesian model with NUTS or HMC and want to check the sampler
  • The convergence check is good, but you do not trust the extreme values

Avoid it when

  • The model is not fitted with NUTS or HMC (there is no energy)
  • You want to know if the model is correct

What it needs

  • A sample_stats group with the energy of each draw in each chain

What is on the chart

  • Two histograms: the energy (grey) and its change from one draw to the next (blue)
  • A bar for the E-BFMI of each chain with a dashed limit line
  • A caption that names the chains below the limit
For experts

E-BFMI per chain = mean(diff(E)²) / var(E) (ArviZ bfmi, Betancourt 2016). The histograms pool the chains: marginal energy E − mean(E) per chain, transitions diff(E) − its mean per chain, on shared bins (40) between the 0.5% and 99.5% points. bfmi_threshold (0.3) sets the limit.

docs.title: Predicted vs actual
docs.text:
core.fit_vs_actual@1.0.0

Puts each prediction of the model next to the actual value in a scatter plot. Dots on the dashed diagonal line are perfect predictions.

How to read it. Most dots are near the diagonal and the caption says R² = 0.85. The dots for 'south' are all below the line, so the model predicts too low for that market.

Use it when

  • You want a quick view of how accurate the model is
  • You want to find the cells where the model is far wrong
  • Your data has no time dimension

Avoid it when

  • You want to see when the errors happen (use Residuals over time)
  • You need to see the range of the predictions (this chart shows only the middle value)

What it needs

  • Predictions with draws (posterior_predictive, predictions or draws group), or a score summary with interval statistics
  • The actual values (observed_data or observed group)

What is on the chart

  • A dot for each cell: the actual value across, the prediction up
  • A dashed diagonal line for perfect predictions
  • Colours for each market or product when there is a group dimension
  • A caption with R² and the typical error in percent (MAPE)
For experts

Point = median or mean of the draws (or the summary's point statistic). With draws, hidden dims are summed; with a score summary, the extra dims are kept as cells. R² = 1 − SS_res / SS_tot on the plotted cells (not a held-out score). MAPE skips cells where the actual value is zero. The chart is the same for train and test cells: filter the input to judge the forecast.

docs.title: LOO-PIT and Pareto k
docs.text:
core.loo_pit@1.0.0

Checks each actual value against the predictions of the model when that value is left out of the fit. It also finds the values that have too much effect for this check to be reliable.

How to read it. 3 of 120 values (2.5%) have a Pareto k of more than 0.7. All three are in the week of the holiday sale, which the model does not know about. The PIT line stays in the band, so the other predictions are well calibrated.

Use it when

  • You want a calibration check that does not use each actual value two times (one time to fit and one time to check)
  • You want to find values that have a large effect on the model, such as outliers
