the invitation is claimed at first sign-in) MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS list (computed) Accounts of the development identity provider (MAPI_PROFILE=dev only) MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH Path \| None unset JSON PriceTable (default: mapi_spec.cost.DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE) MAPI_ESTIMATE_WALL_S dict (computed) MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED bool True MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES int 500 Queued runs the fair-share planner considers MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT int 50 At most this many of them per tenant (a tenant whose runs are held cannot fill the window) MAPI_EXECUTOR_REPORT_INTERVAL_S float 10.0 MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S float 259200.0 How long a recorded conformance or security-suite report lets an executor take verified and public tenants (the nightly suites renew it) MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S float 15.0 MAPI_SSE_POLL_S float 5.0 Fallback poll when no NOTIFY arrives MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S float 60.0 How often an open event stream re-checks its caller's credential (a revoked token, an expired session or a lost membership closes the stream) MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES int 8388608 MAPI_LOG_LEVEL debug | info | warning | error info MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S int 300 Wall-clock limit of a POST /v1/plots:render run (the sandbox kills it) MAPI_INSPECT_TIMEOUT_S int 300 Wall-clock limit of an upload inspect run (M4; it reads only metadata) MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED bool False Accept Plotly plots in POST /v1/plots:render. Plotly static export needs kaleido and a Chrome/Chromium in the runner image, which the base images do not ship; while off, Plotly renders are refused with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE int 300 Public embed views per minute and embed link (429 beyond) MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE int 120 Public embed requests per minute and client address, valid or not MAPI_EMBED_CACHE_S float 60.0 How long an API instance reuses an embed's resolved plot (revocation and expiry are still checked on every request; responses are never cached by browsers or shared caches, so a revoked link stops rendering on the next load) MAPI_EMBED_IMAGE_URL_TTL_S int 900 Lifetime of the PNG fallback's signed URL MAPI_LOG_JSON bool True Emit JSON logs (structlog); off gives a human console renderer MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES list[str] \| None unset Addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of the API (load balancer, Cloud Run front end, the web container's /v1/ proxy), comma-separated. A request from one of them takes the right-most untrusted X-Forwarded-For hop as the client address (per-address limits, Sybil checks, audit). 'none': clients reach the API directly and X-Forwarded-For is ignored. Required in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED bool True Mount GET /metrics (Prometheus) MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT int \| None unset Serve GET /metrics of the worker (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer, events) on this port; unset: the worker exposes no metrics MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST str 127.0.0.1 Bind address of the worker's metrics endpoint MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN str \| None unset Bearer a scraper must present on GET /metrics; required in the multi-tenant profile (the series carry tenant ids and spend) MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED bool True Install the OpenTelemetry tracer provider MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT str \| None unset OTLP/HTTP collector base URL for span export (also read from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT); unset means spans are created but not exported MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP bool False Development only: allow http:// webhook URLs, for the hosts in MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST only (refused in the multi-tenant profile) MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST list (computed) Development only: webhook host names (comma-separated) exempt from the SSRF address and port checks, e.g. a receiver on localhost (refused in the multi-tenant profile) MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE Path \| None unset Extra PEM CA bundle trusted for webhook receivers (a private CA); the system trust store is always used MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S float 2.0 How often the worker looks for due webhook deliveries MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS int 8 Tries per delivery (the retry schedule allows up to 8) MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER int 20 Disable a webhook after this many consecutive events failed MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_PER_PROJECT int 25 MAPI_WEBHOOK_RETENTION_DAYS int 30 Days webhook events and their delivery logs are kept MAPI_WORKFLOW_TICK_S float 1.0 How often the orchestrator advances active workflow runs MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS int 20 Workflow runs a project may have going at once, sub-workflow runs included MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_SCHEDULES int 20 Active cron schedules per project MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_TRIGGERS int 20 Active dataset triggers per project MAPI_WORKFLOW_NODE_TIMEOUT_S int 1800 Timeout of a node without its own timeout MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_JSON_OUTPUT_BYTES int 1048576 Largest JSON output of a node MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED bool \| None unset Self-service sign-up at POST /auth/signup (default: on in the dev and multi-tenant profiles when a mailer is configured, off single-tenant) MAPI_MAILER MailerKind \| None unset How e-mail is sent: console, outbox, smtp or none (default: outbox in dev, console single-tenant, smtp multi-tenant) MAPI_MAIL_FROM str modeling-api <no-reply@mapi.localhost> From: header of the e-mails the server sends MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR Path \| None unset Where the outbox mailer writes messages (default: data_dir/outbox) MAPI_SMTP_HOST str \| None unset SMTP server (MAPI_MAILER=smtp) MAPI_SMTP_PORT int 587 MAPI_SMTP_TLS starttls | ssl starttls starttls (port 587) or ssl (implicit TLS, port 465) MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME str \| None unset MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD str \| None unset MAPI_SMTP_TIMEOUT_S float 10.0 MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL str \| None unset Verification link template with {token} (default: /verify-email?token={token}) MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS list (computed) E-mail domains refused at sign-up besides the built-in disposable list (comma-separated; subdomains included) MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH Path \| None unset A file of disposable e-mail domains (one per line, # comments), e.g. a maintained public list, added to the built-in one MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR int 5 Sign-ups accepted per client address and hour MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY int 25 Verified sign-ups per e-mail domain and day (shared free-mail domains are exempt) MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR int 500 Verified sign-ups per hour on the whole platform MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS list (computed) Free-mail domains shared by unrelated people (comma-separated; replaces the built-in list): no per-domain sign-up cap and no domain-burst Sybil flag MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE int 20 E-mail verification attempts per client address and minute MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS int 30 Look-back of the Sybil heuristics (same address, browser, e-mail) MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD int 3 Workspaces created from one address, browser or e-mail within the window before a new one is flagged for review MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND bool False Suspend a flagged sign-up's tenant until an operator approves it (default: it works and waits in the review queue) MAPI_SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS int 30 Unverified sign-ups (with their e-mail) are deleted after this MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED bool False Cut line B: let identity-verified public tenants run uploaded code (off through M4: public tenants run built-ins and declarative specs only) MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S float 604800.0 Grace period of a tenant deletion: the tenant is suspended and may cancel MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S float \| None unset Also require a sign-in at most this old to request a deletion (re-auth); unset: the confirmation phrase alone MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S float 3600.0 How long a purge waits for the tenant's cancelled runs to stop MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS int 8 Automatic retries of a failed purge before operators must retry MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS int 30 The bundles bucket's retention period (Terraform bundle_retention_days): when a purge may retry objects a retention lock refused MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S float 15.0 Cadence of the deletion and export scheduler (orchestrator) MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES int 268435456 Dataset bytes a GDPR export archive includes; larger exports list the remaining objects (with sizes and hashes) instead MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S float 604800.0 How long a GDPR export archive is kept MAPI_EXPORT_LINK_TTL_S float 900.0 Lifetime of an export's signed download link MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY int 3 GDPR exports a tenant may request per day MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES int 268435456 Bytes of metadata rows (runs, logs, events, audit, ...) a GDPR export archive includes; the tables cut short are listed in its manifest MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S float 3600.0 How long one GDPR export build may take; a build still marked running 5 minutes after that (its process died) is built again once, then failed

docs.title: ModelSpec
docs.text:
The declarative modelling file.

Field Type Default Description apiVersion mapi/v1 required kind ModelSpec required metadata Metadata required data DataBlock required pipeline list of StepCall – max items 64 model ModelBlock required outputs OutputsBlock – evaluate EvaluateBlock – execution ExecutionBlock – calibration Calibration (optional) null Business priors and lift tests the model should respect (M3); needs a model whose capabilities declare them

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The plain-language card of one catalog item. Every field except the expert ones is required, so an About that validates is structurally complete; :func:about_issues adds the editorial rules (one or two sentences, no jargon in the summary, known chooser tags, related ids that exist).

Field Type Default Description title string required A human name summary_plain string required One or two sentences without jargon: what it does for you use_when list of string required min items 1, max items 10 avoid_when list of string required min items 1, max items 10 data_needs list of string required min items 1, max items 10 assumptions list of string required min items 1, max items 10 outputs list of string required min items 1, max items 10 difficulty Difficulty required typical_runtime TypicalRuntime required example string required A tiny example related list of string – Ids of related catalog items (models, steps, nodes, checks, templates) (max items 16) references list of AboutReference – max items 10 expert_notes string (optional) null Maths, estimator details, caveats for experts fits map of list of string – Chooser tags: question id -> the answers this item suits

docs.title: AboutReference
docs.text:
A source for the expert detail (a paper, a book chapter, library documentation).

Field Type Default Description title string required url string (optional) null

docs.title: AsOfSplit
docs.text:
Train on coords up to and including as_of; hold out the rest (optionally gap).

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind as_of required dim string required as_of string or integer or number or boolean required gap integer 0 ≥ 0

docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
Canonical name → dataset name, for dims and variables (geo: market). Names that are not bound keep their dataset name. The binding is stored in the bundle and reversed on every output by default.

Field Type Default Description dims map of string – vars map of string –

docs.title: BusinessPriors
docs.text:
Beliefs in business units, per channel (keys are channel labels as in the data), and/or about the baseline. At least one belief is stated: a baseline belief alone is fine (channels without a belief keep the model's default priors).

Field Type Default Description channels map of ChannelBelief – baseline_share ShareBelief (optional) null kpi_units string (optional) null spend_units string (optional) null

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The calibration block of a ModelSpec: beliefs and experiment results the model should respect. prior_translation_run records which translate_priors run produced the priors in model.settings.priors (lineage only).

Field Type Default Description business_priors BusinessPriors (optional) null lift_tests list of LiftTest – max items 500 prior_translation_run string (optional) null

docs.title: ChannelBelief
docs.text:
What the user believes about one channel: exactly one of roi or contribution_share, held with credibility. * roi: KPI units gained per spend unit over the fit window ([1.5, 4] = "every euro returns between 1.5 and 4 euros of revenue"); * contribution_share: the channel's share of the KPI over the fit window.

Field Type Default Description roi list of any (optional) null contribution_share list of any (optional) null credibility number 0.8 Probability that the true value lies inside the range (0.8 = 'I am 80% sure') (≥ 0.5, ≤ 0.99)

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Resumable checkpoints: every N draws (samplers) or every N epochs (v0.15: networks). Exactly one is set. The model must be checkpointable; otherwise validation warns and the run ignores it.

Field Type Default Description every_draws integer (optional) null every_epochs integer (optional) null v0.15: networks trained in epochs

docs.title: CollectionRead
docs.text:
How a model that reads datasets sees a collection: a seeded sample as pixels(image, y, x, channel) (ModelSpec data.collection).

Field Type Default Description max_samples integer 5000 ≥ 1, ≤ 100000 size list of any (optional) null (height, width); default: the collection's size (needed when it has none) resize stretch or crop or pad stretch mode auto or gray or rgb auto stratify string (optional) label Keep the share of each level of this var or coord (none: uniform) seed integer (optional) null Default: the fit seed

docs.title: ColumnSplit
docs.text:
Hold out the rows whose value in column is one of holdout (a fixed split read from the data, v0.14). column is a coord or a 1-D data variable along dim. Values compare as text, so holdout: [1] matches a stored 1 or "1". With train set, rows in neither list are dropped; else every other row trains.

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind column required dim string required column string required holdout list of string or integer or number or boolean – min items 1, max items 64 train list of string or integer or number or boolean (optional) null

docs.title: DataBlock
docs.text:
The dataset, side tables, binding to canonical names and the split. For a tree dataset (M4), nodes picks the nodes whose variables are merged into the ONE flat dataset the pipeline sees (:meth:mapi_spec.tree.TreeSchema.flat), aligned per join. Without nodes a tree dataset's root node is read (when it has variables). nodes on a plain dataset is an error. The binding applies to the merged names. For an image collection (v0.15), collection says how a model that reads datasets sees it (a seeded sample); a model that trains on batches reads every image.

Field Type Default Description dataset string required Dataset reference dataset://project/name@version side_tables map of SideTable – bind Binding – split TimeHoldoutSplit or LastPerGroupSplit or AsOfSplit or LeaveGroupOutSplit or MaskBlockSplit or ColumnSplit or StratifiedSplit (optional) null nodes map of NodeSelect (optional) null M4: tree datasets: the nodes merged into the pipeline input join exact or inner or outer exact M4: how the coords of the selected nodes align (xarray merge join) collection CollectionRead (optional) null v0.15: an image collection read by a model that reads datasets: a seeded sample as pixels(image, y, x, channel)

docs.title: LiftTest
docs.text:
One experiment: spend_delta extra spend on channel (optionally in one geo) from start to end (inclusive) caused kpi_delta incremental KPI. Give the measurement's uncertainty as a standard error se or a confidence interval ci at ci_level. A holdout ("turn the channel off") is a negative spend_delta with (usually) a negative kpi_delta.

Field Type Default Description id string (optional) null channel string required geo string (optional) null start string required end string required spend_delta number required Extra spend during the test (spend units) kpi_delta number required Measured incremental KPI (KPI units) se number (optional) null Standard error of kpi_delta ci list of any (optional) null Confidence interval of kpi_delta ci_level number 0.9 ≥ 0.5, ≤ 0.999 description string (optional) null

docs.title: NodeSelect
docs.text:
One node a spec reads from a tree dataset (an entry of data.nodes). Its variables (all, or vars) are merged into the flat pipeline input, renamed prefix + name when prefix is given (so two nodes with the same variable names can both be read). Dims are never renamed: a dim shared by several selected nodes must be the same dim (equal :class:~mapi_spec.schema.DimSpec).

Field Type Default Description path string required vars list of string (optional) null Default: every variable of the node prefix string (optional) null Prepended to the node's variable names in the flat dataset

docs.title: FutureCovariates
docs.text:
Where future values of future_required covariates come from in a forecast (M3). supplied (default) needs them in the request's data or scenario (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE otherwise). The other policies let the runner extend them over the horizon, per series, inside the sandbox: carry_last repeats the last observed value, seasonal_naive repeats the value one season earlier (the time dim's yearly period), zero sets them to zero (e.g. "no spend planned").

One of supplied, carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero.

docs.title: Built-in steps catalog
docs.text:
Generated from the step catalog export (python -m mapi_steps.catalog and the steps of the installed plugins): the same static JSON the control plane uses to validate specs without importing step code. For how the steps behave together, read Built-in steps.

Step Kind Learns state Invertible Looks back Summary core.calendar feature – – – Calendar features (day of week, month, ISO week, ...) core.encode_levels feature yes – – Integer codes for categorical levels core.formula feature – – – Derived variable from an arithmetic expression core.fourier feature yes – – Fourier seasonality features core.holidays feature – – – Holiday indicators per period from a side table core.lag feature – – yes Lagged copies of variables within groups core.lag_tensor feature – – yes Lag tensor (lags 0 .. l_max-1) for in-model carry-over core.missing_indicator feature – – – Indicators of missing values core.one_hot feature yes – – One-hot indicators of categorical variables core.trend feature yes – – Polynomial time trend dl.embed feature yes – – Image features from a frozen pretrained network core.count_events reshape – – – Count events per period on a dense grid core.filter_coords reshape – – – Select labels of a dim core.resample reshape – – – Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency core.stack reshape – – – Stack dims into one core.to_long reshape – – – Padded ragged data to long form core.to_padded reshape – – – Long ragged data to padded form with a mask core.unstack reshape – – – Unstack a dim into several core.adstock value – – yes Adstock (carry-over) with fixed parameters core.clip value – – – Clip values to bounds core.fx_convert value – yes – Currency conversion with per-period rates from a side table core.impute value yes – – Fill missing values (mean, median, constant or forward fill) core.log1p value – yes – log(1 + x) of the named variables core.logit value – yes – Logit of proportions core.max_abs_scale value yes yes – Divide by the maximum absolute value over the named dims core.mean_scale value yes yes – Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims core.replace_sentinel value – – – Turn sentinel codes into missing values core.saturation value – – – Saturation curve with fixed parameters core.standardize value yes yes – Standardise to zero mean and unit variance over the named dims

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
modeling-api ships as three products, in this sequence:

  1. A typed modelling runtime.
  2. A job platform around the runtime.
  3. A hosted platform for many users.

Some rules make the hosted platform safe. These rules are in the code from the first release: no pickle, contracts in JSON only, static validation, sanitized plots, and sandboxed runs with verified outputs.

timeline
    title Releases
    v0.1 · M0 · contract layer : SDK, specs and schemas : 28 steps, PyMC and sklearn base classes : 11 built-in models, plots, sanitizer : conformance corpus
    v0.2 · M1 · local platform : HTTP API, queue, sandboxed runner : GCS shim, signed bundles : Expert web app, CLI, Python client : make dev and Docker Compose
    v0.3 · M2 · cloud and multi-tenant : tenants, OIDC sign-in, tokens, row-level security : quotas, fair share, cost ledger, kill switches : Cloud Run Jobs executor, Terraform : observability, security suite, chaos
    v0.4 · M3 · Guided mode and integrations : templates, question flow, business priors : scorecard, what-if, forecasts : endpoints, snippets, webhooks, embeds : sign-up, deletion, GDPR export
    v0.5 · M3.5 · workflows and governance : workflows of tests, transforms and models : governance policies and null tests : Data and Model Explorers : mmm-framework and statsmodels : About cards, Help me choose
    v0.5.1 · forecasts with actuals : forecasts from the last actual : no refit
    v0.6 · spec builder : completions from the catalog : Insert panel : Visual view
    v0.7 · scientific models : four sci models : outputs on a grid : Fields in the Model Explorer
    v0.8 · M4 · tree datasets : NetCDF-4 and HDF5 groups : versions from several files : data.nodes and tree-input models
    v0.9 · M5 · science gallery : 15 sci models in all : 14 plot recipes : Bayesian workflow nodes and six recipes : tutorials for the case studies
    planned · expert plugins and MCP : plugin upload for allow-listed experts : curated MCP server : SBC as parent runs
Release Milestone Theme Status v0.1 M0 The contract layer: specs, the xarray runtime, steps, models, plots and the conformance corpus. All of it runs in your own Python process. available v0.2 M1 The local platform: the same work as API calls and sandboxed runs, with the Expert web app. It runs on a laptop or on one Docker host. available v0.3 M2 Cloud and multi-tenant core: tenants, sign-in, tokens, quotas and cost. Each run gets one new sandbox on Cloud Run. This release is a private beta. available v0.4 M3 Guided mode and integrations: analysts go from a spreadsheet to a report and a scenario. Other apps get endpoints, webhooks and embeds. This release is the first public launch. available v0.5 M3.5 Workflows, governance, explorers, mmm-framework and statsmodels: automated, versioned analyses. Models must pass null tests and get the approval of a second person. Also budget plans, About cards and Help me choose. available v0.5.1 Forecasts with actuals: a forecast starts from the actuals that came after the fit. The model does not fit again. available v0.6 The spec builder in the web app: completions and hover text from the catalog of the tenant, an Insert panel and a Visual view. available v0.7 Scientific models: four sci.* plugins with data on a map, an image or a grid. Outputs on a grid show in the Fields section of the Model Explorer. available v0.8 M4 Tree datasets: NetCDF-4 and HDF5 files with groups, raw HDF5 files, and versions made from several files. A spec selects the nodes that it reads. available v0.9 M5 Science gallery: 15 sci.* models in all, 14 plot recipes, workflow nodes for Bayesian checks and plots, six workflow recipes and a tutorial for each case study. available Not set Expert plugins and MCP: plugin upload for allow-listed experts, a curated MCP server for AI agents, and SBC as parent runs. planned

Milestone names

The plan before v0.5 gave the names M4 and M5 to plugin upload and to public code upload. The releases used these names for tree datasets (M4) and the science gallery (M5). Plugin upload, the MCP server and public code upload are not done. They have no release number yet.

docs.title: What v0.9 contains
docs.text:
• Eleven new science models from the pymc-challenges case studies, 15 sci.* models in all. They are for images, fields, maps, graphs, trees of species and angles (models reference).
  • 14 plot recipes: maps, networks (net.graph), trees, polar charts, image checks, colour swatches and posterior views (core.pair, core.ridge, core.rank_matrix, core.calibration, core.state_sequence) (plot reference).
  • Workflow nodes for Bayesian models: model.summary, evaluate.ppc, compare.stacking, model.score and plot.render. Plots also go into reports (Bayesian models in a workflow).
  • Tree datasets in workflows: model.fit and model.backtest take nodes and join (Tree datasets in a workflow).
  • Six workflow recipes: model ladders (sci_spatial_ladder, sci_network_ladder, sci_phylo_signal), sci_calibrate_then_design, bayes_workflow_audit and sci_image_model_check (workflow cookbook).
  • Circular outputs (OutputDecl.circular): the holdout metrics and the score summaries of an angle are on the circle (Circular outputs).
  • Tutorials for the 15 case studies, and the complex workflows tutorial. The command python -m mapi_plugin_science.export makes datasets that you can upload from the data of pymc-challenges.

We did the steps of the E18, E51 and E21 tutorials on a live dev stack, in a browser. Only sci_spatial_ladder ran end to end on a live dev stack. The six recipes run through the server orchestrator in a slow test, with small fits. The same as for v0.5, no part of v0.9 ran on real Google Cloud or in Docker. These items are not done yet:

  • governance.check with sensitivity.prior cannot find the prior widths of sci.areal_bym2, so the check is skipped.
  • The graph check of the network ladder does not mark the statistics of the observed network.
  • core.prior_predictive cannot draw the prior draws of sci.heat_plate. Some science models keep no prior draws.
  • A backtest of a tree dataset gives the full tree to each fold. search.grid has no nodes parameter.
  • The HTML report does not show plot sections.
  • Some fits mix slowly: sci.turing_pattern at the size of the notebook, and the latent-space fit of sci.network_latent_space with covariates.

Read the changelog for the full list. Some of the case studies of pymc-challenges are not ported yet.

docs.title: What v0.5.1 to v0.8 contain
docs.text:
• v0.5.1, forecasts with actuals. All twelve statsmodels models can forecast from actuals with their fitted parameters. Other models refuse with ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED (Forecasts with actuals).
  • v0.6, the spec builder. Completions, hover text and settings checks in the YAML editor come from the catalog of the tenant. The Insert panel and the Visual view edit the same document. This release changed only the web app.
  • v0.7, scientific models. sci.lgcp_grid, sci.fisher_kpp, sci.traction_force and sci.strong_lens. OutputDecl.grid declares an output on a grid (Capabilities). The Score page guides each request in steps.
  • v0.8 (M4), tree datasets. A dataset version can hold an xr.DataTree. A guard does a check of each HDF5 file in the sandbox before it opens the file. A model can declare input: tree to get the full tree (Tree datasets). The catalog shows each plot recipe as a card with an example picture.

The web flows for trees ran against the mock API only. The real server and runner path ran in the end-to-end test. The v0.6 spec builder ran in the unit and Playwright smoke tests against the mock API.

docs.title: What v0.5 contains
docs.text:
• Workflows: versioned DAGs of statistical tests, transforms, branches, split plans, order searches, model fits, evaluations, comparisons, governance and reports. Also live events, a cache, schedules and dataset triggers (cookbook).
  • Governance: versioned project and tenant policies and twelve checks. The checks include null tests against shuffled targets and placebo regressors. Also second-person approval, evidence packs and promotion that needs validation (null tests explained).
  • Data and Model Explorers, with side-by-side comparisons and Diebold-Mariano tests
  • mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, with budget optimisation in the sandbox
  • Twelve statsmodels time-series models
  • About cards on each item that you can select, and Help me choose (choosing a model)
  • The Python client and the CLI for all of these items
  • The screens of the web app for all of these items: the visual workflow builder, the run monitor, Guided recipes, the policy editor, the review queue, the explorers, About cards and the chooser, and budget plans

We verified these items end to end on a live local stack (M3.5 verification):

  • the canonical workflow
  • governance with a second person
  • mmm-framework with a budget plan
  • the explorers and the chooser
  • the CLI.

Some work is not done yet, the same as for v0.4. It includes a real Google Cloud project, Docker-isolated executors, and the sessions with five non-technical testers.

docs.title: What v0.4 contains
docs.text:
• Guided mode: four templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice). Also a question flow with role detection, drafts with "View as YAML", and the persona lock (tutorial).
  • Sandboxed ingest of CSV, Parquet, MFF and Meridian-shaped tables. Refusals are in plain language.
  • Business priors as ROI or share ranges. A sandbox translates them and shows a prior-predictive preview. Also lift tests as calibration (Guided modelling).
  • The sanity scorecard that each fit writes, and the promotion gate that uses it
  • What-if sliders over response grids for each draw, "Run exact", and forecast and counterfactual views
  • Endpoints and aliases, score:<alias> tokens, snippets in seven languages, and a Google Sheets card (Connect Google Sheets)
  • Signed webhooks with an outbox, retries, a delivery log, replays and an SSRF guard (Receive webhooks)
  • Saved plots, static renders and embed links (Embed a chart)
  • The endpoints of the Python client, and new CLI commands
  • Sign-up with e-mail verification and abuse controls, tenant deletion, the GDPR export, and a Cloud Armor policy
  • The Integrations hub, trust pages and admin additions in the web app

We verified these items end to end on a laptop (M3 verification). The exit of M3 also needs the sessions with five non-technical testers. These sessions are not done yet. Some work against a real Google Cloud project is not done yet, the same as for v0.3:

  • the [verify M0] checklist
  • cold-start measurements
  • public workspaces on an executor that enforces egress and DNS.

docs.title: Planned: expert plugins and MCP
docs.text:
Plugin upload for allow-listed experts. Experts upload their own model plugins. The platform builds them into hash-pinned overlays, with native wheels from a curated mirror. The contract kit checks each plugin on upload. Also fast dev overlays and a vetted tier of ported sibling models.

An MCP server gives AI assistants and agents a small, curated set of tools that are safe from injection. The tools list and describe models, score an endpoint, read a run and get a plot.

Budget optimisations already run as in-sandbox optimize jobs, and backtests run as workflow nodes (v0.5). Sweeps are workflows with a search.grid node (v0.14 retired the Sweep document). SBC runs as one parent. More.

docs.title: After expert plugins
docs.text:
This is the planned sequence:

  1. Public code upload: uploaded plugins for all tenants. This release needs these controls:

    • a separate execution project
    • signed base images
    • verification before code runs
    • Sybil controls
    • a takedown process
    • a rehearsed kill-switch drill
    • an external penetration test.

    The security suite must first be green for two weeks. 2. Scale and depth. Each item comes when real usage needs it: - warm scorers for exact answers in less than one second - GPU and large-data executors - other clouds - recursive forecasting - chained models (full-funnel and KPI graphs) - a plugin marketplace with a consent model.

Dates

We cut a release when it passes its exit criteria, not on a calendar date. Read the changelog to see the changes that we released.

docs.title: Cloud and multi-tenant core v0.3
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.3 (milestone M2), a private beta

v0.3 makes the platform multi-tenant. It also gives the platform a cloud execution backend: each run gets one new sandbox on Cloud Run Jobs. The run protocol (bootstrap object, signed events, verified outputs, signed bundle manifests) did not change from v0.2. v0.3 adds the cloud versions of the local parts. All multi-tenant functions also run on a laptop (make dev). We tested the cloud parts against fakes. A short checklist of cloud behaviours waits for a real project. For instructions, read Administration, Authentication and Deploy to Google Cloud.

docs.title: One sandbox per run
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph SB["Fresh sandbox (one per run)"]
        direction LR
        SUP["Supervisor<br/><i>trusted · holds credentials</i>"] -->|"inputs"| W["Worker<br/><i>separate uid · runs the plugin</i>"]
        W -->|"outputs (claims)"| SUP
    end
    SUP -->|"signed upload"| OBJ[("Object store")]
    SUP -->|"HMAC-signed events"| EV["Events service"]
    OBJ -->|"server-computed hashes"| FIN["Finalizer<br/>verifies, then publishes"]
  • Isolation. Each run gets a new micro-VM sandbox (Cloud Run Jobs, gen2). A trusted supervisor holds the short-lived credentials of the run. An untrusted worker runs the harness and the plugin under a different user. The worker has no credentials and no network.
  • No egress. Sandboxes cannot connect to the internet, and they cannot use DNS. Data comes in and results go out only through signed URLs for one object.
  • Outputs are claims. The finalizer checks each artifact against the hashes and the object generation that the store calculated. Then it copies the artifact to a location where the sandbox cannot write. If a manifest does not agree, the finalizer rejects it as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Progress you can trust. Only the supervisor writes events. Each line has an HMAC signature and a sequence number. The status from the executor tells if a run is alive.
  • Long fits can resume. Segmented PyMC sampling writes checkpoints to the prefix of the run. Thus a preempted fit resumes where it stopped. (Checkpoints, partial runs and resume already work locally in v0.2.)
Local (make dev, Compose) On Google Cloud in v0.3 local-process / docker executor Cloud Run Jobs, a fixed inventory of base image × resource class Worker as your user (DEV_MODE_ISOLATION) Worker under its own uid, no_new_privs, in a microVM GCS shim with emulated principals Cloud Storage with IAM, VPC Service Controls Events from the supervisor's stdout pipe Cloud Logging → Pub/Sub push → POST /internal/events EC P-256 key in .local/keys/ Cloud KMS asymmetric signatures, same bytes The development IdP, 127.0.0.1 only OIDC for people, scoped tokens for programs

docs.title: Multi-tenant core
docs.text:
• Tenants and projects with role-based access. Postgres applies row-level security on each table. (In v0.2, each row and storage key already has tenant_id and project_id.)
  • Scoped API tokens with their own budgets, and quotas for each tenant in vCPU-seconds. Interactive and batch priority classes stop one big sweep from blocking the scoring of all other users.
  • A cost ledger for each run, which shows in the UI.
  • We already published the contracts for all of these functions. See Tenancy and authentication, Quotas and cost and the multi-tenant HTTP API.
  • Other backends connect through the same Executor protocol. Each backend must pass an executor conformance suite.
  • The infrastructure is code. Terraform sets up the control, exec, data and build projects and the VPC Service Controls perimeter. There are also deploy scripts and a GitHub Actions workflow. See Deploy to Google Cloud and Security hardening on Google Cloud.

Cloud Run Jobs executor describes the Cloud Run executor, the authenticated Pub/Sub event path, KMS manifest signing and the hardened Cloud Storage driver. We tested these parts against fakes. They did not run on a live cloud yet.

docs.title: What it means for plugins
docs.text: You do not change your code. The contract kit already checks the properties that the cloud needs: no pickle, deterministic bundles, typed errors, and the evaluate path is the same as the score path. If a plugin passes check_model now, it is ready for sandboxed execution.

docs.title: Expert plugins and MCP planned
docs.text:
Status: planned, no release number yet

v0.4 opened the hosted platform to declarative specs and built-in models. v0.5 added workflows, governance, the explorers and budget optimisation in the sandbox (what's new). The plan before v0.5 put this work in v0.6 (M4). The releases v0.6 to v0.9 gave other features: the spec builder, scientific models, tree datasets (M4) and the science gallery (M5). Thus the items on this page are not done yet. With them, allow-listed experts can upload their own model plugins. AI assistants and agents also get a curated MCP server. Simulation-based calibration becomes a single parent run. Sweeps are workflows with a search.grid node (v0.14 retired the Sweep document). Public code upload for all users comes after these items, with its own controls (see the roadmap).

docs.title: Plugin upload for allow-listed experts
docs.text:
Now, a data scientist can run their own PyMCModel or SklearnModel only on a deployment that they control. They install it into the environment of the runner. This work makes it a product feature of a shared deployment. It is available to tenants that an operator put on the allow list:

flowchart LR
    A["mapi plugin push<br/>(your package)"] --> B["Overlay build<br/>source + pre-resolved wheels,<br/>pinned by hash"]
    B --> C["Describe run<br/>catalog entry, schema sanitizer,<br/>contract kit report"]
    C --> D{{"Kit passes?"}}
    D -->|yes| E["Runnable in your project<br/>on the pinned base image"]
    D -->|no| F["Readable report<br/>of what to fix"]
  • Overlays, not images. The platform builds a plugin into a hash-pinned overlay on top of one base-image version. The overlay has the source and wheels that were resolved before, including native wheels from a curated mirror. Runs never install software.
  • The contract kit runs on upload. The kit does the same checks as mapi plugin test on your computer. These checks decide if a version becomes runnable. The platform keeps the report with the version, next to its SBOM.
  • Schema sanitizer. The platform sanitizes the settings schemas of a plugin before the web app makes forms from them.
  • Dev overlays for fast iteration. The target is less than five minutes from push to a runnable version.
  • A vetted tier. We will port the sibling marketing-mix and HMM models as plugins. They will show that real models agree with the contract.

docs.title: An MCP server for agents
docs.text: The MCP server gives a curated set of tools to AI assistants and agents. For example, the tools list and describe models, score an endpoint, read a run and get a plot. The server returns each string from a user or a plugin as clearly delimited untrusted text. Thus a model name cannot put hidden instructions into an agent. Tokens and scopes work the same as for other clients.

docs.title: Sweeps, SBC and what is already delivered
docs.text:
• optimize runs (delivered in v0.5). The sandbox optimises budgets next to the model with the planning module of mmm-framework. It uses the response curves of the posterior (Optimise a budget).
  • Backtests (delivered in v0.5) run as workflow nodes on rolling-origin and expanding-window plans (cookbook).
  • Sweeps (delivered). The search.grid workflow node runs each point of a grid and logs the scores of each point as metrics. v0.14 retired the Sweep document: the server does not accept new ones. To compare sweeps, use the compare page.
  • SBC as one parent run that fans out and aggregates the results, for example the simulation-based calibration of a new plugin. (The governance of v0.5 has a parametric-bootstrap version, recovery.simulated.)
  • Bayesian checks in a workflow (delivered in v0.9). The recipe bayes_workflow_audit does a convergence gate, a posterior predictive check, a prior sensitivity check and a recovery check in one workflow run. Since v0.9, recovery.simulated simulates each dataset of a Bayesian model with predictive draws from its posterior predictive. sci_spatial_ladder fits its best model again with wider and narrower priors (Bayesian models in a workflow). These checks run as nodes of the workflow, not as one parent run.

docs.title: Exit criteria
docs.text:
• Three sibling models are packaged as plugins and pass the contract kit.
  • A dev overlay is pushed and becomes runnable in less than five minutes.
  • An SBC of a new plugin runs as a single parent.

We cut a release when it passes its exit criteria. Read the changelog.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.4 (milestone M3), the first public launch

v0.4 builds on the multi-tenant core of v0.3. With v0.4, analysts go from a spreadsheet to a trustworthy report and a what-if scenario. They do not write YAML. Other applications can call fitted models through stable endpoints. v0.4 is the first public launch, cut line A. All persons can sign up and run declarative specs and the built-in models on their own data. Only trusted tiers can upload code. For instructions, read the Guided tutorial, the Integrations hub and Tutorials.

docs.title: Guided mode: organised around tasks
docs.text:
The app has two modes over the same ModelSpec. A toggle in the header changes between Guided and Expert. Each Guided screen has "View as YAML". Edits in Expert mode go back to Guided mode.

journey

    section Set up
      Choose "Geo marketing mix": 5: Analyst

    section Run

    section Decide
      Read the report and the sanity scorecard: 5: Analyst

Shipped Where to read about it Four templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice) and a question flow with role detection Your first analysis in Guided mode Sandboxed ingest of CSV, Parquet, MFF and Meridian-shaped tables From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft Business priors (ROI or share ranges) translated in a sandbox, lift tests as calibration Guided modelling The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate Guided mode, Integrations What-if sliders over per-draw response grids, "Run exact", forecast and counterfactual views What if… The persona lock: projects that stay Guided-only The persona lock

docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Endpoints and aliases with history, rollback and a frozen input contract; score:<alias> tokens Endpoints and webhooks Generated snippets: Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, a notebook cell The Integrations hub, Connect Google Sheets Signed webhooks with an outbox, retries, a delivery log, replays and an SSRF guard Receive webhooks Saved plots, PNG/SVG/PDF renders in the sandbox and expiring embed links Embed a chart, Sharing plots The Python client's endpoints; the CLI's endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors and tenant commands Optimise a budget, The Python client

docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Self-service sign-up with e-mail verification, disposable-domain blocking, rate limits and Sybil flags for operators to review Sign-up and abuse controls Identity verification and cut line A at run admission Sign-up and abuse controls Tenant deletion that purges every store, and the GDPR export Deleting and exporting data A Cloud Armor policy on every load-balancer backend Security hardening

docs.title: The exit criteria
docs.text:
Criterion Where it stands Five non-technical testers go from upload to report to scenario without help in less than 30 minutes Prepared. An automated run takes 135 s of system time. We repaired the six usability defects that it found. We wrote the protocol for the testers. The sessions are not done yet. An external optimiser works against an endpoint Met on a laptop: +0.22 % revenue at the same budget against the live endpoint (details). From v0.5, the platform optimises budgets next to the model, in a sandboxed optimize run on mmm-framework planning (Optimise a budget). We removed the external-optimiser adapter. Cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins Met for admission. Sign-up workspaces are public, and the platform refuses uploaded code. Public runs need an executor that enforces egress and DNS (docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs). This laptop could not run these executors.

We verified all items locally. M3 verification gives the numbers. It also tells which items still need real persons, Docker or Google Cloud.

docs.title: The local platform v0.2
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.2 (milestone M1)

v0.1 defined the documents that the platform accepts (ModelSpec, ScoreRequest). It also defined the error codes that the platform returns and the executor protocol that it controls. v0.2 puts an HTTP API, a job queue, a sandboxed runner, a local object store and the Expert web app around them. All of it runs on one machine. Start with the quickstart.

docs.title: What changed for you
docs.text:
Each thing that you do in a notebook is also an API call. The work runs in a sandbox, not in your process:

In your process (v0.1) On the platform (v0.2) validate_spec(spec, catalog, schema) POST /v1/specs:validate, all problems at one time with JSON pointers, and the live squiggles in the editor fit_spec(spec, data, ...) POST /v1/runs with kind: fit. Progress comes as server-sent events. score_bundle(bundle, request, data) POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score with Prefer: wait A bundle directory A model version in a registry, with lineage, metrics, a scorecard, plots and a signed manifest InprocExecutor local-process and docker executors behind the same protocol 
flowchart LR
    C["Web app · CLI ·<br/>Python client · curl"] -->|"/v1 JSON"| API["API<br/>(validates from static JSON)"]
    API --> Q[("PostgreSQL<br/>runs · queue · events")]
    Q --> D["Dispatcher"]
    D --> X["Executor<br/>(local process / Docker)"]
    X --> R["Runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    R -->|"outputs + manifest"| S[("GCS shim")]
    R -->|"signed events"| API

docs.title: Design commitments, kept
docs.text:
• The API never imports plugin code and never decodes your arrays. It validates specs and score requests from the exported catalog JSON and stored metadata. An import-linter contract keeps numpy, xarray and all plugins out of the server. The build of the server image checks this contract against the installed packages.
  • Runs are idempotent and observable. Submissions have idempotency keys. The status from the executor is the source of truth. Events control progress bars. They never decide if a run is alive.
  • Errors are RFC 7807 problems with the same stable codes that you see in Python.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 describes each endpoint. CI checks the generated clients for drift.
  • Outputs are verified. The platform checks the outputs of a run against the checksums and generations of the object store. Then it copies the outputs to a location where runs cannot write, and signs them.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• The Expert web app, the CLI, the Python client and the HTTP API
  • Architecture overview and the security model
  • Deployment: make dev and Docker Compose

docs.title: Workflows, governance and explorers v0.5
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.5 (milestone M3.5)

v0.4 made one model easy to fit, read and share. v0.5 makes the analysis around the model repeatable and defensible. v0.5 has these parts:

  • workflows that run the statistics that a careful analyst runs
  • governance policies that make each model pass null tests before a person uses it
  • Data and Model Explorers
  • mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, with budget optimisation
  • twelve statsmodels time-series models
  • an About card on each item that a user can select.

For instructions, read What's new in 0.5, the workflow cookbook and Can you trust this model?.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Shipped Where to read about it Versioned WorkflowSpec DAGs with typed ports, parameters, alternatives, branch gating and sub-workflows, validated with JSON pointers before anything runs Workflows 51 nodes: 17 statistical tests, 6 transforms, 7 train/test plans, 5 searches, fits, backtests, forecasts, evaluations, comparisons with Diebold-Mariano, selection, governance, reports Workflow node reference A safe condition language for branches and computed parameters (mapi_spec.expr, never eval) Conditions Server orchestration: per-node status, server-sent events, retries, caching of unchanged nodes, child runs, cost Where nodes run Cron schedules and dataset triggers Schedules and triggers A gallery: readiness to ARIMAX, VAR/VECM cointegration, governed MMM, forecast bake-off Workflow cookbook A visual workflow builder, a live run monitor and Guided recipes in the web app In the web app

Added after v0.5

  • v0.9 (M5): five new nodes, 56 in all. model.summary, evaluate.ppc, compare.stacking, model.score and plot.render give posterior summaries, posterior predictive checks, stacking weights, scores and plots in a workflow. The new node kind is plot, and reports have plot sections.
  • v0.9 (M5): model.fit and model.backtest read the tree datasets of v0.8 (the parameters nodes and join). The local runner accepts xr.DataTree inputs.
  • v0.9 (M5): six new recipes, ten in the gallery in all: sci_spatial_ladder, sci_network_ladder, sci_phylo_signal, sci_calibrate_then_design, bayes_workflow_audit and sci_image_model_check.

Read Bayesian models in a workflow and the gallery.
